### `SiegeEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Marker for the Siege mechanic (the March-of-the-Machine "Battle — Siege" subtype). Recorded on a `StaticAbility` whose `Reminder` carries the verbatim standalone Siege type-reminder parenthetical ("(As a Siege enters, choose an opponent to protect it. You and others can attack it. When it's defeated, exile it, then cast it transformed.)").

- **Effect discriminator:** `siege`

[Source](AST/Effects/Battle/SiegeEffect.cs)

## `/AST/Effects/CardFlow/`

### `AbundanceRevealEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Abundance's "choose land or nonland and reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a card of the chosen kind. Put that card into your hand and put all other cards revealed this way on the bottom of your library in any order."

This is a single atomic action specific to the Abundance draw-replacement family: the controller first declares whether they want a land or nonland card, then reveals cards from the top of their library one at a time until the first card of the chosen kind is found. That card goes to the controller's hand; all other revealed cards go to the bottom of the library in player-chosen order (any order, not a random order).

"In any order" (player-chosen ordering of the remainder) distinguishes this from `RevealUntilEffect` (which always places the remainder on the bottom in a random order, per CR 400.4). The two shapes are distinct oracle templates and must not be collapsed.

The "choose land or nonland" step is baked into this effect's discriminator: the binary land/nonland choice is the only dimension of the filter, and it is made by the controller at resolution — unlike `RevealUntilEffect`, where the filter is a static `ObjectFilter` printed on the card. MAST records the instruction to choose, not the chosen value (descriptive-not-engine, ADR 0004).

The two-sentence oracle text is one coupled action — "a card of the chosen kind" and "all other cards revealed this way" in the second sentence are back-references to the first. This MUST NOT be decomposed into separate effects.

CR 614.11 (draw replacement effects); CR 701.12 (reveal); CR 400.4 (random order), compared with the Abundance template which says "in any order" (player-chosen).

- **Effect discriminator:** `abundanceReveal`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/AbundanceRevealEffect.cs)

### `AdditionalCastCostEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You may pay an additional [cost] [any number of times] as you cast this spell" — the shared permission a CR-static additional-cost keyword grants: Kicker (CR 702.33), Multikicker (702.33c), Buyback (702.27), Entwine (702.42), Escalate (702.120), and the repeatable copy/token keywords Squad / Replicate / Conspire (the cost half). (CR numbers verified against rules-structure.json — 702.32 is Fading, 702.121 is Melee.)

These keywords are static abilities per their CR, so the keyword combinator emits a `StaticAbility` carrying this effect with its `KeywordSource` label — NOT a card-level `AdditionalCostsAttribute`, which loses the keyword identity and so cannot express the production/reference duality ADR 0003 requires ("Kicker abilities cost {1} less"). Sibling of `AlternativeCastEffect` (alternative cost) on the additional-cost side.

Riders keyed to whether/how-many-times the cost was paid (Buyback's return-to-hand replacement, Conspire/Replicate's copy, Squad's ETB tokens) are SEPARATE abilities on the card — they reference "if the [keyword] cost was paid", and the topology of two abilities is faithful (ADR 0004). This effect models only the additional cost itself.

- **Effect discriminator:** `additionalCastCost`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/AdditionalCastCostEffect.cs)

### `AlternativeCastEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You may cast this card from [zone] by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost" — the shared permission a CR-static alternative-cast keyword grants: Flashback (CR 702.34, from graveyard), Escape (702.139), Aftermath, Jump-start, Retrace; Madness (702.35, from exile); and the cast-from-hand conditional family Surge, Spectacle, Freerunning.

These keywords are static abilities (per their CR), so the keyword combinator emits a `StaticAbility` carrying this effect — not a card-level attribute — which keeps keyword identity on a correctly-categorized ability and is testable through the keyword-expansion harness.

The alternative `Cost` is the shared polymorphic `Cost` primitive, so a keyword that pays by exiling or discarding filtered cards reuses the existing cost vocabulary: Escape's "exile N other cards from your graveyard" is a `CompositeCost` bundling the mana cost with an `ExileCost`{Filter, FromZone, Quantity}; Jump-start's "discard a card" a `DiscardCost`. The card itself is the implicit subject ("this card"); the zone it is cast from is `FromZone`. The post-cast exile (Flashback) and stack/zone bookkeeping are engine territory (ADR 0003/0004 describe-not-execute).

- **Effect discriminator:** `alternativeCast`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/AlternativeCastEffect.cs)

### `CantDrawCardsEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

A global draw lock — a continuous static effect that stops a player (or players) from drawing cards. e.g. "Players can't draw cards." (Maralen of the Mornsong). A rules-of-the-game-modifying continuous effect (CR 611.1) — written as a plain static statement (CR 604.1: "Static abilities do something all the time rather than being activated or triggered. They are written as statements, and they're simply true.").

- **Effect discriminator:** `cantDrawCards`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/CantDrawCardsEffect.cs)

### `ConniveEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Connive (Rule 701.50a). "Certain spells and abilities instruct a permanent to connive. To do so, that permanent's controller draws a card, then discards a card. If a nonland card is discarded this way, that player puts a +1/+1 counter on the conniving permanent."

MAST records the keyword action's invocation and the conniving subject; the draw / discard / conditional-+1/+1-counter sequence is engine territory per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine (mirroring the SurveilEffect pattern — Surveil similarly records only the keyword and count, not the look/put-into- graveyard machinery).

Filed under `CardFlow` alongside `SurveilEffect` and `ExploreEffect`: the keyword's primary descriptive axis is draw-then-discard, with the +1/+1 counter being a conditional fallback path. The Counter directory hosts effects whose <em>primary</em> shape is counter placement; here that is conditional and secondary.

- **Effect discriminator:** `connive`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/ConniveEffect.cs)

### `DiscardCardsEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"discard [count] cards"

The discarding player is `Player`; the optional `Filter` narrows which card(s) may be discarded ("a nonland card"). CR 701.9a: "To discard a card, move it from its owner's hand to that player's graveyard."

The targeted reveal-choose-discard family (Thoughtseize / Coercion / Thought Erasure — "Target opponent reveals their hand. You choose a nonland card from it. That player discards that card.") is ONE coupled game action, not three independent sentences: the chosen card from the reveal is the very card discarded. It is modeled here as a single effect with three distinct structured axes —

`Player` — the discarder ("that player", i.e. the targeted opponent); `Chooser` — who selects the card ("you"), distinct from the discarder; `Filter` — which card qualifies ("a nonland card").

The preceding hand reveal is the disclosure that makes the choice possible; it is recorded by `RevealHand` rather than as a separate decomposed effect, so the coupling between "what is revealed" and "what is chosen and discarded" is not lost.

- **Effect discriminator:** `discardCards`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/DiscardCardsEffect.cs)

### `DrawCardsEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"draw [count] cards"

- **Effect discriminator:** `drawCards`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/DrawCardsEffect.cs)

### `ExploreEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Explore (Rule 701.44a). "[Permanent] explores. (Reveal the top card of your library. Put that card into your hand if it's a land. Otherwise, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature, then put the card back or put it into your graveyard.)"

MAST records the keyword action's invocation and the exploring subject; the reveal / land-to-hand / +1/+1-counter / graveyard sequence is engine territory per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine (mirroring the SurveilEffect pattern — Surveil similarly records only the keyword and count, not the look/put-into-graveyard machinery).

Filed under `CardFlow` alongside `SurveilEffect`: the keyword's primary descriptive axis is library-reveal followed by put-into- zone, with the +1/+1 counter being a fallback path. The Counter directory hosts effects whose <em>primary</em> shape is counter placement; here that is conditional and secondary.

- **Effect discriminator:** `explore`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/ExploreEffect.cs)

### `ImpulseEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

"Look at the top N cards of your library. Put one of them into your hand and the rest into [RestDestination]." Models the Impulse/Strategic Planning family: a single atomic action where the controller looks at the top N cards, chooses one to keep in hand, and the remaining cards go to a fixed destination. Rule 701.12 (look).

The two-sentence oracle text is a single game action — "the rest" in the second sentence is a back-reference to the cards revealed by the first. This must not be decomposed into a flat [lookAtCards, …] list; a single ImpulseEffect preserves that semantic coupling.

Variants by RestDestination:

`Graveyard` — Strategic Planning, Rummage `BottomOfLibrary` — Impulse (Visions), Anticipate

- **Effect discriminator:** `impulse`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/ImpulseEffect.cs)

### `LookAtCardsEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Look at the top N cards of your library" or "Look at target player's hand"

- **Effect discriminator:** `lookAtCards`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/LookAtCardsEffect.cs)

### `LookAtTopCardAnyTimeEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You may look at the top card of your library any time." A continuous static permission that lets the controller inspect the top card of their library whenever they choose, rather than only at times when they could cast or play something. This is a persistent visibility grant, not a one-shot look or a triggered look.

MAST records this as a static ability (the permission persists as long as the source is on the battlefield — Rule 604.2). The "You may" preamble makes the effect permissive (`IsOptional` = `true`); the controller is never forced to look. There are no parameters: the subject is always "You" (the controller), the zone is always the top of the library, and the timing grant is "any time" — all of which are captured by the discriminator alone.

- **Effect discriminator:** `lookAtTopCardAnyTime`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/LookAtTopCardAnyTimeEffect.cs)

### `LookAtTopMayRevealMatchingRestToBottomEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Look at the top N cards of your library. You may reveal a [filter] card from among them and put it into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order." — Dragonologist's ETB pattern.

This is a single coupled atomic action: the controller privately LOOKS (looking at cards is a general game instruction, not one of the CR 701 keyword actions) at a FIXED number of cards from the top of their library — unlike the sibling `RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardEffect` and `RevealTopMayPutSharesCreatureTypeRestToBottomEffect` families, this pile is never shown to any other player. The controller MAY then reveal (CR 701.20a: "to reveal a card means to show it to all players") UP TO ONE of the looked-at cards matching `Filter` and put it into their hand — an optional, player-chosen selection, not "all matching" — and every remaining looked-at card goes to the bottom of the library in a RANDOM order without ever having been shown to anyone. CR 401.4: cards placed at a specific position in a library "in a random order" are shuffled among themselves before being placed.

The three-sentence oracle text is one coupled action — "from among them" and "the rest" are back-references to the look in the first sentence. This MUST NOT be decomposed into separate look + reveal + zone-change effects.

A DISTINCT shape from the neighbouring look/reveal families — do not collapse:

`RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardEffect` — REVEALS (not merely looks at) the whole pile up front to every player, and the non-kept remainder goes to the GRAVEYARD, not the bottom of the library. `RevealTopMayPutSharesCreatureTypeRestToBottomEffect` — also REVEALS the whole pile up front (public information), and the hand-eligible filter is a relational `SharesCreatureTypeWith` predicate rather than a static `ObjectFilter`. `ImpulseEffect` — LOOKS (matching this effect), but keeps EXACTLY ONE card with NO type filter (a free choice among all N), and sends the rest to a fixed `ImpulseRestDestination` (never "random order"). `RevealUntilEffect` — reveals UNTIL the first match (not a fixed count), and the match is MANDATORY (not "you may").

This effect instead LOOKS PRIVATELY at a fixed count, OPTIONALLY reveals and keeps up to one card matching a static `ObjectFilter`, and sends the non-kept remainder to the BOTTOM of the library in a RANDOM order — a disposition baked into this discriminator's meaning, following the minimal-fields precedent of `RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardEffect`.

- **Effect discriminator:** `lookAtTopMayRevealMatchingRestToBottom`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/LookAtTopMayRevealMatchingRestToBottomEffect.cs)

### `MayCastTargetFromGraveyardEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You may cast [target] from your graveyard [paying its mana cost]." — a one-shot permission granted by an activated ability that allows the controller to cast a targeted card from their graveyard, paying its normal mana cost.

Distinct from `MayPlayFromGraveyardEffect` (a continuous static permission for lands) and `CastWithoutPayingEffect` (which waives the mana cost). This effect is a one-shot permission — it grants the option to cast the targeted card at its printed mana cost from the graveyard.

CR 601.3e: "Some rules and effects state that an alternative set of characteristics or a subset of characteristics are considered to determine if a card or copy of a card is legal to cast…" Here the permission grants a zone exception — graveyard rather than hand — without altering the cost. MAST describes the permission; the engine handles the legality check, zone-change, and stack placement (ADR 0003/0004 describe-not-execute).

- **Effect discriminator:** `mayCastTargetFromGraveyard`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/MayCastTargetFromGraveyardEffect.cs)

### `MayPlayFromExileEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"[During your turn,] you may [play|cast] cards exiled with [object] [as though they had flash]. [Mana of any type can be spent to cast those spells.]" — a static permission to play cards from exile (Azula, Cunning Usurper).

The permission is the linked second ability of a CR 406.6 pair: it refers to "cards exiled with [object]" via the `Cards` filter's `ExiledWith` reference, NOT by threading a binding from the exile ability (ADR 0004 "reference not resolution"). It is a separate static ability rather than a one-shot bundled inside the exile trigger (ADR 0004 "topology not annotation").

- **Effect discriminator:** `mayPlayFromExile`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/MayPlayFromExileEffect.cs)

### `MayPlayFromGraveyardEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You may play [lands/cards] from your graveyard." — a static permission that allows the controller to play cards matching `Cards` from their graveyard (Crucible of Worlds, Ramunap Excavator).

CR 305.1: "A player who has priority may play a land card from their hand during a main phase of their turn when the stack is empty. Playing a land is a special action; it doesn't use the stack." This ability extends that permission so the eligible land cards may come from the graveyard rather than (or in addition to) the hand. MAST describes the permission; when and whether the player actually plays a land is engine territory (ADR 0003/0004 describe-not-execute).

- **Effect discriminator:** `mayPlayFromGraveyard`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/MayPlayFromGraveyardEffect.cs)

### `MayPlayFromLibraryEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You may cast [filter] spells from the top of your library." — a static permission that allows the controller to cast matching spells from the top of their library (Mystic Forge: "artifact spells and colorless spells"; Bolas's Citadel: "nonland cards").

This is a continuous static ability (CR 604.2): the permission persists as long as the source permanent is on the battlefield. MAST models what the oracle text says — which cards may be cast and from which zone — not the execution (when the player actually casts, the engine handles priority, timing restrictions, etc.). The `Cards` filter identifies which subset of the library's top card qualifies; Zone=Library is implied by the effect type.

CR 604.2: "Static abilities create continuous effects, some of which are prevention effects or replacement effects. These effects are active as long as the permanent with the ability remains on the battlefield and has the ability, or as long as the object with the ability remains in the appropriate zone …"

- **Effect discriminator:** `mayPlayFromLibrary`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/MayPlayFromLibraryEffect.cs)

### `MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You may play lands and cast spells from the top of your library." — a static permission allowing the controller to play cards from the top of their library rather than from hand, optionally with an alternative cost for spells cast this way.

Bolas's Citadel (WAR) grants this permission with an attached alternative cost: "If you cast a spell this way, pay life equal to its mana value rather than pay its mana cost." (CR 118.9b: paying life is an alternative cost; CR 202.3: a spell's mana value is the total cost of its mana symbols.) The `SpellAltCost` field records the alternative cost kind for spells cast this way — null when no alternative cost applies.

MAST describes the permission as written: the controller may play lands and/or cast spells from the top of their library. What "the top" means and when the controller may exercise this permission are engine territory (CR 305.1 for playing lands, CR 601.2 for casting spells). The effect's `Actions` list records which permissions are granted (play lands, cast spells, or both). Describing, not executing (ADR 0003).

- **Effect discriminator:** `mayPlayFromTopOfLibrary`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryEffect.cs)

### `MayPlayTargetFromExileEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

"You may play that card from exile [this turn]." — a one-shot permission to play a SPECIFIC, previously-referenced card while it sits in exile, bounded by a stated duration (Norin, Swift Survivalist: "Whenever a creature you control becomes blocked, you may exile it. You may play that card from exile this turn.").

Distinct from `MayPlayFromExileEffect` (a continuous static permission over a FILTERED set of cards, keyed by `ExiledWith` — CR 406.6 "reference not resolution" topology) and from `MayCastTargetFromGraveyardEffect` (the graveyard analogue of THIS node — same one-shot/Target shape, different zone and verb). Here the referenced object is a single card named by pronoun back-reference (the "it" exiled by a sibling effect earlier in the SAME ability), not a filter — so `Target` carries an `It` reference rather than a zone filter (ADR 0004 "reference not resolution").

CR 701.13a (exile) places the card in the exile zone; this effect is the separate permission grant that lets the controller play it from there (CR 305.1 "play a land"/601.2 "cast a spell" normally require hand). The stated window ("this turn") is carried on the inherited `Duration` (`UntilTimeDuration.EndOfTurn`), matching the identical "you may play that card this turn" surface already modelled with an end-of-turn `Duration` on `ImpulseEffect` (Count on Luck). MAST describes the permission; the engine handles the legality check, zone-change, and stack placement (ADR 0003/0004 describe-not-execute).

- **Effect discriminator:** `mayPlayTargetFromExile`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/MayPlayTargetFromExileEffect.cs)

### `OracleTopLookEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Look at the top N cards of your library. Put up to one of them on top of your library and the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order." — the Thassa's Oracle / oracle-look family.

Semantics: the controller looks at N cards from the top of their library, then chooses up to one card to remain on top, and the remaining cards are placed on the bottom of the library in a random (unordered) arrangement. CR 701.12 (look); CR 701.14 (in a random order, the owner randomizes the placement).

This is a single atomic action — the "put up to one on top" clause and the "rest on the bottom in a random order" clause back-reference the same looked-at pile. It must not be decomposed into separate look + move effects; the coupling between the two dispositions (the chosen one to top, the unchosen to random-bottom) is part of the action's meaning.

- **Effect discriminator:** `oracleTopLook`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/OracleTopLookEffect.cs)

### `PlayWithHandsRevealedEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Players play with their hands revealed." (Revelation) / "Your opponents play with their hands revealed." (Telepathy) — a continuous static effect that requires the affected player(s) to keep every card in their hand face-up and visible to all players at all times while the source permanent is on the battlefield.

CR 701.20a (verbatim): "To reveal a card, show that card to all players for a brief time. If an effect causes a card to be revealed, it remains revealed for as long as necessary to complete the parts of the effect that card is relevant to. If the cost to cast a spell or activate an ability includes revealing a card, or if a card is revealed because an ability is activated from a hidden zone (see rule 602.2a), the card remains revealed from the time the spell or ability is announced until the time it leaves the stack. If revealing a card causes a triggered ability to trigger, the card remains revealed until that triggered ability leaves the stack. If that ability isn't put onto the stack the next time a player would receive priority, the card ceases to be revealed." The CR 701.20 rule text itself uses Telepathy as its worked example of this exact "play with their hands revealed" phrasing.

MAST encodes this as a continuous static effect (no `Duration` stated — the effect persists as long as the source permanent is on the battlefield, per CR 604.2), mirroring the sibling library-transparency effect `PlayWithTopRevealedEffect`. The imperative "Players play with …" / "Your opponents play with …" form is NOT optional: the affected player(s) have no choice. No `OptionalEffect` wrapper is applied.

`Player` generalizes the player scope so this one node covers both printed shapes: "Players play with their hands revealed" (Revelation) → `{ Kind: EachPlayer }`; "Your opponents play with their hands revealed" (Telepathy) → `{ Kind: EachOpponent }`.

- **Effect discriminator:** `playWithHandsRevealed`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/PlayWithHandsRevealedEffect.cs)

### `PlayWithTopRevealedEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Play with the top card of your library revealed." — a continuous static effect that requires the controller to keep the top card of their library face-up and visible to all players at all times while the source permanent is on the battlefield.

CR 401.5: "Some effects tell a player to play with the top card of their library revealed … If the top card of the player's library changes while a spell is being cast, the new top card won't be revealed and can't be looked at until the spell becomes cast." CR 401.6: "If an effect causes a player to play with the top card of their library revealed, and that particular card stops being revealed for any length of time before being revealed again, it becomes a new object." CR 701.18c: "Some effects instruct a player to 'play' with a certain aspect of the game changed, such as 'Play with the top card of your library revealed.' 'Play' in this sense means to play the Magic game."

MAST encodes this as a continuous static effect (no `Duration` stated — the effect persists as long as the source permanent is on the battlefield, per CR 604.2). The imperative "Play with …" form is NOT optional: the controller has no choice. No `OptionalEffect` wrapper is applied. There are no parameters; the discriminator alone carries the full meaning (subject = You, zone = top of library, visibility = revealed to all). Covers Oracle of Mul Daya and similar library-transparency effects.

- **Effect discriminator:** `playWithTopRevealed`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/PlayWithTopRevealedEffect.cs)

### `RevealCardsEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Reveal [count] [cards] in [zone]" — a player shows cards matching a filter from a zone to all players (the Scent of Nightshade family: "Reveal any number of black cards in your hand"). Distinct from the specialized library-reveal effects (`RevealUntilEffect`, `RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect`, etc.): this is the general "reveal a chosen set of cards you already hold" action whose `Count` often defines a later variable ("where X is the number of cards revealed this way" — see `CardsRevealedThisWayQuantity`).

CR 701.20a (verbatim): "To reveal a card, show that card to all players for a brief time. If an effect causes a card to be revealed, it remains revealed for as long as necessary to complete the parts of the effect that card is relevant to."

- **Effect discriminator:** `revealCards`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/RevealCardsEffect.cs)

### `RevealTopCardMatchToBattlefieldElseGraveyardEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Reveal the top card of your library. If it's a [filter] card, put it onto the battlefield. Otherwise, put it into your graveyard." — the Call of the Wild reveal-top-card-and-partition family.

This is a single coupled atomic action: the controller reveals the SINGLE top card of their library (CR 701.20 — Reveal: "To show a card to all players for a brief time"), and that same revealed card is then routed to exactly one of two destinations by whether it matches `Filter` — if it matches it is put onto the battlefield (CR 400.7, the card changes zones and becomes a new object), otherwise it is put into the controller's graveyard (CR 404.1, a graveyard is the discard pile).

The three-sentence oracle text is one coupled action — "it" in the second and third sentences back-references the single card revealed in the first. This MUST NOT be decomposed into separate reveal + conditional zone-change effects (the "it" binding would dangle), mirroring the coupled precedent of the neighbouring reveal-top families (`RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect`, `RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardEffect`, `TopLookPutOntoBattlefieldEffect`).

A DISTINCT shape from those neighbours — do not collapse:

`RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect` / `RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardEffect` reveal a FIXED count of N cards and PARTITION the pile by filter (matching set → hand, remainder → bottom/graveyard). `TopLookPutOntoBattlefieldEffect` LOOKS (doesn't reveal), keeps an optional up-to-one matching card, rest to the bottom.

This effect instead REVEALS the SINGLE top card and routes THAT card by a static `ObjectFilter` to either the battlefield (match) or the graveyard (non-match) — both dispositions baked into this discriminator's meaning, following the minimal-fields precedent of the sibling reveal-top effects (no destination enum is added to the record).

- **Effect discriminator:** `revealTopCardMatchToBattlefieldElseGraveyard`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/RevealTopCardMatchToBattlefieldElseGraveyardEffect.cs)

### `RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Reveal the top N cards of your library. You may put a [filter] card from among them into your hand. Put the rest into your graveyard." — the Grisly Salvage / Scout the Borders / Commune with the Gods reveal-then-dredge family.

This is a single coupled atomic action (CR 701.20 — Reveal: "To show a card to all players for a brief time"): the controller reveals a FIXED number of cards from the top of their library, MAY put UP TO ONE of the revealed cards matching `Filter` into their hand (an optional, player-chosen selection — not "all matching", not "until" the first match), and every remaining revealed card goes to the controller's graveyard. CR 404.1 (a graveyard is the discard pile); CR 404.3: "If an effect or rule puts two or more cards into the same graveyard at the same time, the owner of those cards may arrange them in any order."

The three-sentence oracle text is one coupled action — "from among them" and "the rest" are back-references to the reveal in the first sentence. This MUST NOT be decomposed into separate reveal + zone-change effects (mirroring the coupled precedent of `RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect`).

A DISTINCT shape from the neighbouring reveal/look families — do not collapse:

`RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect` — puts ALL matching cards to hand (not an optional up-to-one) and the remainder on the BOTTOM of the library in any order (Sylvan Messenger). `ImpulseEffect` — LOOKS (doesn't reveal), keeps EXACTLY ONE card with NO type filter, and sends the rest to a `ImpulseRestDestination` (Strategic Planning). `RevealUntilEffect` — reveals UNTIL the first match, keeps exactly one, rest to bottom in a random order.

This effect instead REVEALS a fixed count, OPTIONALLY keeps up to one card matching a static `ObjectFilter`, and sends the non-kept remainder to the controller's GRAVEYARD — a disposition baked into this discriminator's meaning (following the minimal-fields precedent of `RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect`, which likewise bakes its bottom-of-library disposition into the discriminator rather than adding a destination enum).

- **Effect discriminator:** `revealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyard`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardEffect.cs)

### `RevealTopMayPutSharesCreatureTypeRestToBottomEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Reveal the top N cards of your library. You may put a card that shares a creature type with it from among them into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order." — the Tajuru Paragon kicked-ETB reveal family.

This is a single coupled atomic action (CR 701.20 — Reveal): the controller reveals a FIXED number of cards from the top of their library, MAY put UP TO ONE of the revealed cards that shares a creature type with the source object (`SharesCreatureTypeWith`, CR 205.3m) into their hand — an optional, player-chosen selection, not "all matching" — and every remaining revealed card goes to the bottom of the controller's library in a RANDOM order. CR 401.4: cards placed at a specific position in a library "in a random order" are shuffled among themselves before being placed.

The three-sentence oracle text is one coupled action — "from among them" and "the rest" are back-references to the reveal in the first sentence. This MUST NOT be decomposed into separate reveal + zone-change effects (mirroring the coupled precedent of `RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect` and `RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardEffect`).

A DISTINCT shape from the neighbouring reveal families — do not collapse:

`RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardEffect` — the non-matching remainder goes to the GRAVEYARD, and the hand-eligible filter is a static `ObjectFilter` (not a relational share-predicate). `RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect` — puts ALL matching cards to hand (not an optional up-to-one), and the remainder goes to the bottom in ANY (player-chosen) order, not a random one. `RevealUntilEffect` — reveals UNTIL the first match (not a fixed count), and the match is MANDATORY (not "you may").

This effect instead REVEALS a fixed count, OPTIONALLY keeps up to one card sharing a creature type with the referenced object, and sends the non-kept remainder to the BOTTOM of the library in a RANDOM order — a disposition baked into this discriminator's meaning, following the minimal-fields precedent of `RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect`.

- **Effect discriminator:** `revealTopMayPutSharesCreatureTypeRestToBottom`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/RevealTopMayPutSharesCreatureTypeRestToBottomEffect.cs)

### `RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Reveal the top N cards of your library. Put all [filter] cards revealed this way into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in any order." — the Sylvan Messenger ETB reveal-and-partition family.

This is a single coupled atomic action (CR 701.20 — Reveal: "To show a card to all players for a brief time"): the controller reveals a FIXED number of cards from the top of their library, ALL of the revealed cards matching `Filter` go to the controller's hand (zero, some, or all of the revealed cards may match), and the remaining (non-matching) cards go to the bottom of the library in an order the controller chooses. CR 401.4: "If an effect puts two or more cards in a specific position in a library at the same time, the owner of those cards may arrange them in any order. That library's owner doesn't reveal the order in which the cards go into the library."

The two-sentence oracle text is one coupled action — "revealed this way" and "the rest" in the second sentence are back-references to the reveal in the first. This MUST NOT be decomposed into separate reveal + zone-change effects.

This is a DISTINCT shape from the other three-and-four reveal/look families and must not be collapsed into any of them:

`RevealUntilEffect` — reveals UNTIL the first match (not a fixed count), puts exactly ONE card to hand, and the rest go to the bottom in a RANDOM order (CR 400.4). `AbundanceRevealEffect` — reveals until a land/nonland choice is met, puts exactly ONE card to hand, rest to bottom in any order. `OracleTopLookEffect` — LOOKS (doesn't reveal) at a fixed count, puts UP TO ONE card back on TOP, rest to bottom in a RANDOM order. `ImpulseEffect` — LOOKS at a fixed count, puts exactly ONE (controller's free choice) to hand, rest to graveyard or bottom.

This effect instead REVEALS a fixed count, puts ALL cards matching a static `ObjectFilter` to hand (not a free choice, not "until" the first match), and puts the non-matching remainder on the bottom in a player-chosen (any) order — a disposition baked into this discriminator's meaning, following the minimal-fields precedent of `AbundanceRevealEffect` (no separate destination enum is added to the record).

- **Effect discriminator:** `revealTopPutMatchingToHand`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect.cs)

### `RevealUntilEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a [filter] card. Put that card into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order."

This is a single atomic action (CR 701.12 — look/reveal): the controller reveals cards one at a time from the top of their library until they find the first card matching `Filter`, which then goes to their hand. All other revealed cards are placed on the bottom of the library in a random (shuffled) order.

The two-sentence oracle text is one game action — "that card" in the second sentence is a back-reference to the matching card found in the first. This MUST NOT be decomposed into separate reveal + zone-change effects; the coupling between the found card and the rest is part of the action's meaning (mirroring the coupling in `ImpulseEffect` and `TopLookPutOntoBattlefieldEffect`).

CR 701.12 (look/reveal from library); CR 400.4 (random order on the bottom).

- **Effect discriminator:** `revealUntil`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/RevealUntilEffect.cs)

### `ScryEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"scry [count]"

- **Effect discriminator:** `scry`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/ScryEffect.cs)

### `SurveilEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Surveil N" - look at top N cards, put any number into graveyard, rest on top in any order. Rule 701.42

- **Effect discriminator:** `surveil`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/SurveilEffect.cs)

### `TopLookPutOntoBattlefieldEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Look at the top N cards of your library. You may put a [filter] card from among them onto the battlefield. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order." — the Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy activated ability family.

This is a single atomic action: the controller looks at the top N cards, optionally chooses one matching `CardFilter` to put onto the battlefield, and then the remaining cards go to the bottom of the library in a random order. The "from among them" back-references the same looked-at pile; the action must not be decomposed into separate look + zone-change effects.

Structural position: similar to `ImpulseEffect` (look top N, keep one, rest elsewhere) but with distinct semantics:

The kept card goes to the battlefield (not hand). The kept card must match `CardFilter` (e.g. non-Human creature). The choice is optional ("You may"). The rest go to the bottom in a random order (not any order).

CR 701.12 (look); CR 400.7 (putting a card onto the battlefield); CR 400.4 (random order).

- **Effect discriminator:** `topLookPutOntoBattlefield`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/TopLookPutOntoBattlefieldEffect.cs)

### `WishEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You may reveal a [filter] card you own from outside the game or choose a face-up [filter] card you own in exile. Put that card into your hand." — the Karn, the Great Creator −2 / Glittering Wish / Mastermind's Acquisition family. The controller retrieves a card matching `CardFilter` from either outside the game (sideboard) or exile and puts it into their hand.

CR 400.11: "Some effects bring cards into a game from outside the game. Those cards remain in the game until the game ends, their owner leaves the game, or a rule or effect removes them from the game, whichever comes first." The two source zones (outside game and exile) are stated explicitly on the card; this node records both as the `Sources` list. MAST records what the oracle text says (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004) — which sources are available and which filter qualifies the card — not the runtime evaluation.

The "You may" optionality is encoded by an `OptionalEffect` wrapper around this node at the parse level (ADR 0005: clause-level modifiers are composition). The `WishSource` enum records the legal retrieval zones so a consumer can distinguish the broad form (outside game + exile) from a narrower form (outside game only, or exile only).

"Face-up" qualifies the exile-zone source: only face-up exiled cards may be chosen (Karn can't retrieve face-down morphs or other hidden cards). This is captured by `FaceUpOnly` on the exile branch.

- **Effect discriminator:** `wish`

[Source](AST/Effects/CardFlow/WishEffect.cs)

### `AllMustBlockEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

"All creatures able to block [Target] do so." — Lure-type forcing requirement. Rule 509.1c (block requirements that the defending player must satisfy when possible).

### `AssignDamageAsToughnessEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

Combat damage assignment substitution: creatures assign combat damage equal to their toughness rather than their power. Rule 510.1a (verbatim): "Each attacking creature and each blocking creature assigns combat damage equal to its power." This effect records the static replacement that substitutes toughness for power when assigning combat damage — the High Alert / Doran, the Siege Tower family.

- **Effect discriminator:** `assignDamageAsToughness`

[Source](AST/Effects/Combat/AssignDamageAsToughnessEffect.cs)

### `AssignDamageAsUnblockedEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

Combat damage-assignment substitution (attacker-side): oracle text states that a blocked creature may "assign its combat damage as though it weren't blocked." Rule 510.1c (combat-damage step; a blocked creature normally assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it — "If exactly one creature is blocking it, it assigns all its combat damage to that creature. If two or more creatures are blocking it, its controller divides that creature's combat damage…"). This effect records the substitution that lets the creature instead assign that damage as though no creature were blocking it (i.e., to the player or planeswalker it is attacking).

- **Effect discriminator:** `assignDamageAsUnblocked`

[Source](AST/Effects/Combat/AssignDamageAsUnblockedEffect.cs)

### `BlockAdditionalEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Combat-block permission (blocker-side): oracle text states that a creature "can block an additional creature each combat" or "can block any number of creatures." Rule 509.1a (the defending player may declare more than one blocker for the same or additional attackers when an effect explicitly grants the extra-blocker permission).

- **Effect discriminator:** `blockAdditional`

[Source](AST/Effects/Combat/BlockAdditionalEffect.cs)

### `CanAttackIgnoringDefenderEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

Permission for creatures to attack as though they did not have the Defender keyword ability. Rule 702.3b (verbatim): "A creature with defender can't attack." This effect records the static override that removes the can't-attack restriction normally imposed by Defender — the High Alert / Assault Formation family.

### `CanBlockOnlyEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Combat-block restriction (blocker-side): oracle text states that a creature "can block only [filter]." Rule 509.1c (declare-blockers step; blocking restrictions constrain the set of legal blocker declarations the defending player can make).

- **Effect discriminator:** `canBlockOnly`

[Source](AST/Effects/Combat/CanBlockOnlyEffect.cs)

### `CantAttackEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

Combat-attack restriction (attacker-side): oracle text states that a creature "can't attack." Rule 508.1c (declare-attackers step; attacking restrictions constrain the set of legal attacker declarations the active player can make).

- **Effect discriminator:** `cantAttack`

[Source](AST/Effects/Combat/CantAttackEffect.cs)

### `CantBeBlockedEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

Combat-block evasion (attacker-side): oracle text states that a creature "can't be blocked" (unconditionally), "can't be blocked by [filter]" (color-/power-restricted), or "can't be blocked by more than one creature" (blocker-count restriction). Rule 509.1b (declare-blockers step; evasion abilities constrain the set of legal blocker declarations the defending player can make against the named object).

### `CantBlockEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

### `ExertEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You may exert [this creature] as it attacks." — the optional cost to attack that defines the Exert mechanic (CR 701.43d).

CR 701.43d (verbatim): "'You may exert [this creature] as it attacks' is an optional cost to attack (see rule 508.1g). Some objects with this static ability have a triggered ability that triggers 'when you do' printed in the same paragraph. These abilities are linked. (See rule 607.2h.)"

CR 701.43a: "To exert a permanent, you choose to have it not untap during your next untap step." The untap consequence is engine-side; MAST records the oracle text's mechanic, not the enforcement.

This is a parameterless marker — the subject is always the source creature itself (Self). It sits on a `StaticAbility` whose `KeywordSource` is "Exert" and pairs with a linked `TriggeredAbility` (Event: Exerted) that fires "When you do" — i.e., when the controller pays the optional exert cost.

- **Effect discriminator:** `exert`

[Source](AST/Effects/Combat/ExertEffect.cs)

### `FightEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Fight keyword action (CR 701.14): "Target creature you control fights target creature you don't control." MAST records the two participants as target references and does not model the mutual-damage exchange — that is engine territory per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine. Each creature deals damage equal to its power to the other; MAST describes <em>who fights whom</em>, not the resulting damage events.

- **Effect discriminator:** `fight`

A goaded creature attacks each combat if able and attacks a player other than the controller of the permanent, spell, or ability that caused it to be goaded if able. Goaded is neither an ability nor part of the permanent's copiable values."

### `NoCombatDamageEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Records that a source assigns no combat damage this combat: "[Source] assigns no combat damage this combat."

Rule 510.1: "Each attacking creature and each blocking creature assigns combat damage." This effect records that the named source is explicitly excluded from assigning combat damage for the remainder of the current combat, overriding the default rule. Descriptive only — MAST records what the oracle text says; the zero-damage assignment is engine territory.

Canonical use: Master of Cruelties — after triggering its life-total-setting ability, the clause "This creature assigns no combat damage this combat" prevents the creature from also dealing normal combat damage that turn. This effect accompanies the `SetLifeTotalEffect` in the same triggered ability.

Records only the pairing action and its partner reference. The shared abilities a paired pair grants are expressed elsewhere over `BothPaired` (the consumer side, already present); maintaining the pairing while control persists is engine territory.

## `/AST/Effects/Core/`

### `CompositeEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Multiple effects combined.

- **Effect discriminator:** `composite`

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/CompositeEffect.cs)

### `ConditionalEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"If [condition], [effect]." — an in-ability conditional gate where a condition is checked mid-ability-resolution and an effect fires only if it is true.

Distinct from `InterveningIf` (CR 603.4), which gates whether a TRIGGERED ABILITY fires at all: `ConditionalEffect` is an effect-level gate that fires AFTER the preceding effects in the same ability have already resolved, e.g. "If X is greater than or equal to the number of cards in your library, you win the game." after the look on Thassa's Oracle.

MAST describes, does not execute (ADR 0004): the engine evaluates `Condition` and conditionally applies `Then`; MAST simply records that the oracle text has an if-then structure.

- **Effect discriminator:** `conditional`

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/ConditionalEffect.cs)

### `CreateDelayedTriggerEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

An effect that, on resolution, creates a `DelayedTriggeredAbility` (CR 603.7) — the structured home for "…at the beginning of the next end step", "Whenever you cast a creature spell this turn, …", etc. Replaces the former practice of hanging an `AtBeginningOfNext*` duration on a one-shot effect: a delayed trigger is an ability that fires later, not a duration on the effect that set it up (ADR 0002/0004).

- **Effect discriminator:** `createDelayedTrigger`

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/CreateDelayedTriggerEffect.cs)

### `EffectWrap` — *static class*

Conditional clause-modifier wrapping (ADR 0005). Producers that detect a "you may" / "unless [player] pays" clause wrap their effect through these so a wrapper is emitted only when the clause is actually present — keeping the modifier off the effect node itself.

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/EffectWrap.cs)

### `ModalEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

An effect that wraps a modal choice inside another ability's resolution. Used when oracle text inserts a "choose one —" preamble inside a triggered or activated ability's effect stream, e.g.: <code> When [self] dies, choose one — • [option A] • [option B] </code> The ability's `Effects` list carries a single `ModalEffect` whose `Modes` mirror the spell-level `ModalAbility` shape: each option is its own `Ability` (typically a `SpellAbility`) wrapped in a `ModalOption`. Rule 700.2b — modal triggered abilities. The controller chooses the mode(s) as part of putting that ability on the stack. (See also Rule 700.2 for modal mechanics generally.)

- **Effect discriminator:** `modal`

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/ModalEffect.cs)

### `OptionalEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You may [Inner]. If you do, [IfYouDo] / if you don't, [IfYouDoNot]." (CR 118.12 — "[A player] may [do something]. If [that player] [does, doesn't, or can't], [effect]"). Wrapper presence is the "you may" — no bool. One-shot action effects only (ADR 0005).

The chooser defaults to the ability's controller ("you"), so `Chooser` is `null` for the overwhelming majority of "you may …" cards and is omitted from their JSON. It is set only when the oracle names a DIFFERENT decision-maker — "any opponent may have it deal 5 damage to them" (Longhorn Firebeast): the OPPONENT, not the controller, decides whether `Inner` happens. This is load-bearing (CR 118.12 keys the "If [that player] does" branch on the choosing player), so who chooses cannot be inferred from `Inner`'s references when the inner action's source/target are other objects (here the source is "it"/the creature and the recipient is the opponent).

- **Effect discriminator:** `optional`

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/OptionalEffect.cs)

### `PreventableEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"[Inner] unless [player] pays [cost]." (Mana Leak, Rhystic Study). A distinct clause shape from `OptionalEffect`; nests with it in the rare co-occurrence. One-shot action effects only (ADR 0005).

- **Effect discriminator:** `preventable`

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/PreventableEffect.cs)

### `RepeatEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Repeat this process [N] more times." — a loop-repeat instruction that names a previously stated base process (`Inner`) and the number of <b>additional</b> repetitions (`AdditionalTimes`). The total execution count is `AdditionalTimes + 1` (the initial occurrence plus the stated extra iterations).

Example: Professor Onyx's −8: "Each opponent may discard a card. If they don't, they lose 3 life. Repeat this process six more times." → `AdditionalTimes` = 6; total iterations = 7.

MAST describes, does not execute (ADR 0004): the engine evaluates `Inner` the stated total number of times; MAST records that oracle text requests a fixed-count repetition of the given process.

CR 701 (game actions); CR 608.2 (effects resolve once on resolution, unless the text explicitly directs a repetition — as here). Cluster axis: any card with "repeat this process N more times" maps to this node keyed on the count, making the repeat count queryable without re-parsing raw text.

- **Effect discriminator:** `repeat`

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/RepeatEffect.cs)

### `UnparsedEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect, IUnparsed

An effect that couldn't be parsed.

- **Effect discriminator:** `unparsed`

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/UnparsedEffect.cs)

### `UnstructuredEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect, IResidual

L1 residual — an effect POSITION the parser recognised (it sits inside a classified ability shell, i.e. an already-parsed trigger/cost) but whose interior it has not yet structured.

This is the keystone of the fidelity ladder. Unlike `UnparsedEffect` — an `IUnparsed` hole that fails triage and is banned from gold fixtures — `UnstructuredEffect` is an `IResidual` under the free-text doctrine (ADR 0001): the loss is <b>accounted for</b> (its `Text` is counted in residual debt, and it is permitted in golds via the free-text whitelist), not a silent drop. A clause that would otherwise collapse to a whole-ability `UnparsedAbility` (fidelity L0) instead lands as its real shell — a `TriggeredAbility` with its parsed trigger, an `ActivatedAbility` with its parsed cost — carrying this node for the unstructured interior, which is fidelity L1: structurally anchored, interior deferred, zero silent loss.

- **Effect discriminator:** `unstructured`

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/UnstructuredEffect.cs)

### `WinTheGameEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"You win the game." — an absolute game-ending effect where the controller immediately wins (CR 104.3a: "A player can win the game by having the highest life total when the game ends, by having their opponent lose the game, or by a card effect that says 'you win the game'.").

MAST models this descriptively — it records that the oracle text says "you win the game", without encoding any turn-state or priority machinery. Distinct from opponent-loss effects (which say "an opponent loses the game").

- **Effect discriminator:** `winTheGame`

[Source](AST/Effects/Core/WinTheGameEffect.cs)

## `/AST/Effects/Counter/`

### `BlightEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Blight keyword action (CR 701.68). "To blight N means to put N -1/-1 counters on a creature you control."

CR 701.68a (verbatim): "To 'blight N' means to put N -1/-1 counters on a creature you control." CR 701.68b: "If a player is given the choice to blight but is unable to put N -1/-1 counters on a creature they control (usually because they control no creatures), they can't choose to blight."

MAST records who blights and how many, matching the oracle phrase "[player(s)] blight(s) N". The choice of which creature receives the counters — and whether the player is able to blight at all (CR 701.68b) — is engine territory.

### `CantHaveCountersEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

"[object] can't have counters put on it/them" — a static counter-prohibition (CR 122: counters). Prevents any counter (or, when scoped, a specific kind of counter) from being placed on the named object(s).

- **Effect discriminator:** `cantHaveCounters`

### `MoveCountersEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

## `/AST/Effects/Damage/`

### `CantPreventDamageEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Damage can't be prevented." (Leyline of Punishment) — a global prevention-lock static that nullifies every damage-prevention effect (CR 615.1: prevention effects), including "prevent [damage]" shields like `PreventDamageEffect`, Circles/Runes of Protection, and Fog effects. Written as a plain static statement (CR 604.1: "Static abilities do something all the time rather than being activated or triggered. They are written as statements, and they're simply true."), it is a rules-of-the-game-modifying continuous effect (CR 611.1) — unlike `CantGainLifeEffect` and `CantLoseGameForZeroLifeEffect`, which scope their lock to a named `Player`, this lock is unconditional and global (no player, source, or recipient is named in the oracle text), so no scope field is carried — mirroring the marker-only shape of `CantBeCounteredEffect`.

- **Effect discriminator:** `cantPreventDamage`

[Source](AST/Effects/Damage/CantPreventDamageEffect.cs)

### `DamageCantBePreventedEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Damage that would be dealt by this creature can't be prevented." (Excruciator) — a source-scoped prevention-lock static that nullifies every damage-prevention effect (CR 615.1: prevention effects) applicable to damage dealt BY the named `Source`, while leaving prevention of damage from other sources unaffected. Written as a plain static statement (CR 604.1: "Static abilities do something all the time rather than being activated or triggered. They are written as statements, and they're simply true."), it is a rules-of-the-game- modifying continuous effect (CR 611.1) — the source-scoped sibling of `CantPreventDamageEffect` (Leyline of Punishment's unconditional, global "Damage can't be prevented."): where that marker carries no fields because no source/recipient is named, this effect names exactly one damage source (`Self` for "this creature") and locks prevention only for damage dealt by it.

- **Effect discriminator:** `damageCantBePrevented`

[Source](AST/Effects/Damage/DamageCantBePreventedEffect.cs)

"prevent [damage]"

### `RedirectDamageEffect` — *sealed record* : ContinuousEffect

Damage-redirection replacement shield: "The next N damage that would be dealt to [`From`] this turn is dealt to [`To`] instead." — the {0} en-Kor family (Warrior en-Kor, Nomads en-Kor, Task Mage en-Kor, …).

A one-shot, turn-scoped replacement effect (CR 614.1) created by the resolution of an activated ability (CR 602.1). It watches for the next damage that would be dealt to `From` this turn and reroutes up to `Amount` of it to `To`. Structurally this is the redirection sibling of the prevention shield `PreventDamageEffect` ("Prevent the next N damage … this turn"): both are amount-bounded, turn-scoped damage shields set up by a resolving ability, so both are modelled as a flat `ContinuousEffect` that bears `Amount` and the inherited `Duration` ("this turn") — NOT the permanent-scoped static `ReplacementEffect` (Sphere of Law), which states no duration because it persists while its source is on the battlefield.

CR 602.1 (verbatim): "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as \"[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]\" …"

CR 614.1 (verbatim): "Some continuous effects are replacement effects … Such effects watch for a particular event that would happen and completely or partially replace it …"

The shield / which-instance bookkeeping and the redirected-damage event are engine territory (descriptive-not-engine doctrine), mirroring how `PreventDamageEffect` and `RegenerateEffect` record a "next … this turn" shield without modelling the replacement machinery.

- **Effect discriminator:** `redirectDamage`

[Source](AST/Effects/Damage/RedirectDamageEffect.cs)

## `/AST/Effects/Dice/`

### `ResultsTableRow` — *sealed record*

One row of a die-roll `RollResultsTableEffect` (CR 706.3): an inclusive numeric range and the effect(s) that apply when the die result falls within it.

A single-value row ("20") is encoded as `MinResult` == `MaxResult` (e.g. both 20), so the range is always closed on both ends; there is no separate single-value shape. Ranges are inclusive at both bounds, matching the oracle "1—14" / "15—20" convention (CR 706.1a: a dN produces outcomes 1..N).

[Source](AST/Effects/Dice/RollResultsTableEffect.cs)

### `RollDieEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"roll a dN" — instructs a player to roll an N-sided die (CR 706.1).

CR 706.1: "An effect that instructs a player to roll a die will specify what kind of die to roll and how many of those dice to roll." CR 706.1a: "Such an effect may refer to … one or more 'dN,' where N is a positive integer. … a d20 is a twenty-sided die with possible outcomes from 1 to 20."

CR 706.4: "Some abilities that instruct a player to roll one or more dice do not include a results table. The text of those abilities will indicate how to use the results of the die rolls, if at all." Ancient Copper Dragon rolls a d20 without a results table: the result is used directly by the following CreateTokenEffect via `DieRollResultQuantity`.

The `Sides` field captures N from "dN" (e.g. 20 for a d20). The number of dice rolled is 1 (the common case); multi-die variants are out of scope for this card and would extend this node.

- **Effect discriminator:** `rollDie`

[Source](AST/Effects/Dice/RollDieEffect.cs)

### `RollResultsTableEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

A die-roll RESULTS TABLE (CR 706.3) — the effect that consumes a preceding `RollDieEffect` result and maps it, by numeric RANGE, to the effect(s) that apply.

CR 706.3: "Some abilities that instruct a player to roll one or more dice include a results table." A results table is a list of rows, each beginning with a number or a range of numbers followed by the effect(s) that happen if the die's result falls in that range. The whole d20 attack/ETB-roller cohort (Delina, Wild Mage; Lightfoot Rogue; Chaos Channeler; Earth-Cult Elemental; Hoarding Ogre) prints exactly this shape: <code> roll a d20. 1—9 | [effect A] 10—19 | [effect B] 20 | [effect C] </code>

This node composes AFTER the `RollDieEffect` in the same ability's effect list — `[rollDie, rollResultsTable{rows}]` — mirroring the table-less shape `[rollDie, createToken{dieRollResult}]` (Ancient Copper Dragon). The antecedent of "the result" each row's range tests against is that preceding roll (CR 706.2: "the final number is the result of the die roll"). Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): MAST records the range→effect mapping structurally; the engine evaluates which row applies at resolution time.

Each row's outcome is expressed with the existing effect vocabulary (sacrifice, createToken, gainLife, …) so a results table is purely a structural dispatch over already-modelled effects — generalising over both the number of rows and the die size.

- **Effect discriminator:** `rollResultsTable`

[Source](AST/Effects/Dice/RollResultsTableEffect.cs)

### `ChooseBasicLandTypeEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Choose Island or Swamp." — the basic-land-type-choice declaration (CR 614.12's as-enters chosen-value binding; CR 305.6 constrains the value to one of Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, or Forest — "If an object uses the words 'basic land type,' it's referring to one of these subtypes"). The oracle line records that the controller selects a basic land type from the printed disjunction; subsequent abilities that reference "the chosen type" (via `BasicLandType`) are downstream consumers of this choice (CR 607 linked abilities). MAST models only the choice declaration itself, not the producer/consumer link.

Timing is a separate axis: when this choice happens as the permanent enters ("As this enchantment enters, choose Island or Swamp." — Roots of Life, the CR 614.12 shape), the enclosing `StaticAbility` carries `AsThisEnters`; the effect itself stays plain. Timing and effect are composable, never baked into the effect discriminator.

Sibling of `ChooseCardTypeEffect`, but NOT structured the same way: `ChooseCardTypeEffect` omits an explicit options list because its printed disjunction is the exhaustive five-of-five card-type set (no information is lost by treating the enumeration as reminder context). Here the printed disjunction is frequently a real SUBSET of the five basic land types (Roots of Life offers only Island or Swamp, not all five) — dropping the specific options would erase a genuine game-affecting restriction, so `Options` records the literal printed basic land type names, mirroring the existing `Subtypes` convention used for basic-land-type disjunctions elsewhere (e.g. search-library filters).

### `ChooseColorEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Choose a color." — the color-choice declaration. The oracle line records that the controller makes a color selection; subsequent abilities that reference "the chosen color" are downstream consumers of this choice. MAST models only the choice declaration itself, not the producer/consumer link.

Timing is a separate axis: when this choice happens as the permanent enters ("As this land enters, choose a color." — CR 614.1c), the enclosing `StaticAbility` carries `AsThisEnters`; the effect itself stays plain. Both are explicit player-decision instructions, but collapsing them into one node would erase the descriptive distinction the oracle text draws (per the MAST descriptive-not-engine doctrine).

### `ChooseNamedOptionEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"choose [Name] or [Name]." — the named-mode-choice declaration of the Believe/Doubt family (Phenomenon Investigators: "As this creature enters, choose Believe or Doubt."). The oracle line records that the controller picks exactly one of a fixed set of NAMED options; the two ability lines that follow (each prefixed with an option name) function only if their option was the one chosen — those downstream abilities carry a `ChosenModeCondition` gate naming the same option. MAST models only the choice declaration itself, not the producer/consumer link (ADR 0004, reference-not-resolution).

Timing is a separate axis: this choice happens as the permanent enters ("As this creature enters, choose …" — CR 614.12), so the enclosing `StaticAbility` carries `AsThisEnters`; the effect itself stays plain. Timing and effect are composable, never baked into the effect discriminator.

The chosen value is the mode name, so the alternatives are carried on `Options` rather than left implicit. CR 700.2 (modal): "A spell or ability is modal if it has two or more options … preceded by 'Choose one —' …"; the Believe/Doubt shape makes the choice as the object enters (CR 614.12) and gates ongoing abilities on the result rather than resolving one option immediately.

CR 701.66a (verbatim): "\"Earthbend N\" means \"Target land you control becomes a 0/0 land creature with haste in addition to its other types. Put N +1/+1 counters on it. When that land dies or is put into exile, return it to the battlefield tapped under your control.\""

MAST records the keyword-action and its integer value N descriptively. The land animation, counter placement, and delayed triggered ability (return on death/exile) are engine territory; the node names the action and its parameter, not the execution.

CR 701.66b: "An ability that triggers whenever a player earthbends triggers when the delayed triggered ability described in rule 701.66a is created."

- **Effect discriminator:** `earthbend`

[Source](AST/Effects/Keyword/EarthbendEffect.cs)

### `EscapeEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Escape (Rule 702.138). A keyword on instants and sorceries: "Escape—[cost], Exile N other cards from your graveyard." lets the player cast the card from their graveyard for an alternative cost. That escape cost has two parts — a mana cost and the additional cost of exiling a fixed number of other cards from the controller's graveyard. MAST records both components of the printed escape cost; the cast-from-graveyard permission itself is conventionally inferred from the rules and captured as the `Reminder` parenthetical.

`CardsToExile` is the count of cards in the graveyard-exile half of the escape cost — the additional cost, not a separate game action. MAST describes the cost; it does not model the exile as an `ExileEffect` subtree.

- **Effect discriminator:** `escape`

[Source](AST/Effects/Keyword/EscapeEffect.cs)

### `GiftEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

The payoff of the Gift keyword (CR 702.174) on an instant or sorcery spell — "Gift a [something]". CR 702.174b: on an instant/sorcery the second ability represented by gift is "If this spell's gift cost was paid, [effect]", and CR 702.174e: "'Gift a card' means the effect is 'The chosen player draws a card.'" This node carries the parameterized gifted effect in `Gifted` — for "Gift a card" a `DrawCardsEffect` whose `Player` is the chosen player (`ChosenPlayer`).

The "if the gift was promised" gate and the "before any other spell abilities of the card" timing (CR 702.174j) are inherent to the gift keyword and so are not re-encoded as fields — the node's very presence, paired with its enclosing keyword ability's `Gift` source and the verbatim reminder text, records them (MAST describes, does not execute — ADR 0004). The distinct "choose an opponent" additional cost (CR 702.174a: "As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may choose an opponent.") is modelled separately as an `OptionalEffect` wrapping a `ChoosePlayerEffect` on the same keyword ability.

- **Effect discriminator:** `gift`

### `KeywordAbilityEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

A parameterless keyword ability (CR 702) carried by its identity alone — deathtouch, trample, vigilance, cascade, persist, … The single node every such marker collapses into (ADR 0006): the `KeywordAbility` enum value is the whole content, so the 67 former one-per-keyword empty records become one.

The same enum identifies a keyword wherever it appears — this effect, a granted ability (`GainAbilityEffect.GainedAbility`), a characteristic filter (`KeywordCharacteristic`), an ability-class filter — one source of truth. Carries no trait fields: a temporary grant ("gains trample until end of turn") is a `GainAbilityEffect` whose `Duration` holds the span, not this node.

- **Effect discriminator:** `keywordAbility`

[Source](AST/Effects/Keyword/KeywordAbilityEffect.cs)

### `PayLifeEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Pay N life." — an optional-life-payment declaration. The oracle line describes a single payment the controller MAY make; the `IfYouDoNot` branch carries the fallback effect when payment is declined.

Timing is a separate axis: in the Shockland pattern ("As this land enters, you may pay N life. If you don't, it enters tapped." — CR 614.1c) the enclosing `StaticAbility` carries `AsThisEnters` and the declined branch holds a plain `TapEffect` targeting self; the payment effect itself stays plain. Modelling the verb directly keeps the AST descriptively faithful (MAST records what oracle text says, not what the rules engine derives at run-time).

Distinct from the enters-tapped + condition shape used for checklands/fastlands: those gate entry on a board-state predicate ("unless you control two or fewer lands") via `Condition`; painlands/shocklands carry a life-payment cost instead. CR 614.1c covers both, but the descriptive shapes differ.

- **Effect discriminator:** `payLife`

[Source](AST/Effects/Keyword/PayLifeEffect.cs)

### `TributeEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Tribute N (Rule 702.102). "As this creature enters, an opponent of your choice may put N +1/+1 counters on it." An enters-the-battlefield keyword from Born of the Gods. If the opponent does not pay tribute, an ETB triggered ability typically fires.

MAST records the keyword's presence and its integer value N; the opponent-choice, counter-placement, and conditional ETB semantics are engine territory (per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine).

Integer-parameterized keyword; mirrors the `BushidoEffect` shape.

- **Effect discriminator:** `tribute`

[Source](AST/Effects/Keyword/TributeEffect.cs)

### `TypecyclingEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Typecycling (Rule 702.32; variant subrule 702.32f): a parameterized keyword printed as "[Type]cycling [cost]" — e.g., Plainscycling {2}, Forestcycling {1}, Swampcycling {2}. An activated ability functioning only in hand: "[Cost], Discard this card: Search your library for a [Type] card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle."

Distinct from the plain `CyclingEffect` (Rule 702.32 base): plain Cycling's inner effect is "Draw a card", whereas Typecycling's inner effect is "Search your library for a [Type] card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle." The Comprehensive Rules treat these as variants of the same keyword, but the inner effects differ enough that MAST models them as separate effect types (per the existing pattern of one effect type per distinct oracle-template shape).

MAST records the keyword's presence, the land type, and the typecycling cost; the inner search/reveal/shuffle structure is conventionally inferred from the rules and not re-modeled per fixture.

- **Effect discriminator:** `typecycling`

[Source](AST/Effects/Keyword/TypecyclingEffect.cs)

### `UnearthEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Unearth (Rule 702.84). "[Cost]: Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield. It gains haste. Exile it at the beginning of the next end step or if it would leave the battlefield. Unearth only as a sorcery." MAST records the keyword's presence and the unearth cost; the return-to- battlefield, haste-grant, and exile-at-end-step semantics are conventionally inferred from the rules (per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine), mirroring the KickerEffect, BestowEffect, and EchoEffect patterns.

`Cost` is the polymorphic base type for parity with the other cost-bearing keyword effects (Equip, Cycling, Bestow, Echo, Kicker) — all known Unearth printings use a `ManaCost`, but the base accommodates future variants.

- **Effect discriminator:** `unearth`

[Source](AST/Effects/Keyword/UnearthEffect.cs)

### `VanishingEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Vanishing N (Rule 702.63). A keyword ability that limits how long a permanent remains on the battlefield. Oracle form: "Vanishing N (This creature enters with N time counters on it. At the beginning of your upkeep, remove a time counter from it. When the last is removed, sacrifice it.)".

MAST records the keyword's presence and its integer value (the number of time counters the permanent enters with); the counter-removal upkeep trigger and sacrifice-when-empty mechanics are engine territory.

Integer-parameterized keyword; mirrors `BushidoEffect` and `FadingEffect`. Vanishing differs from Fading in using time counters and in triggering sacrifice when the last counter is removed (rather than when you can't remove one). MAST records the value only; the counter-type distinction is rules-territory.

- **Effect discriminator:** `vanishing`

[Source](AST/Effects/Keyword/VanishingEffect.cs)

### `VentureIntoTheDungeonEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

"Venture into the dungeon" keyword action (CR 701.49 "Venture into the Dungeon").

CR 701.49a–c: when a player is instructed to venture into the dungeon, they either bring a dungeon card into the command zone and place their venture marker on the topmost room (if they own none), or advance their venture marker to the next room (following the arrows), or — from a bottommost room — complete and remove that dungeon and begin a new one. The printed reminder text summarises this as "Enter the first room or advance to the next room."

MAST records the keyword-action invocation descriptively; the dungeon-card selection, venture-marker movement, and room-ability triggering are engine territory — the node names the action, not the execution. This mirrors the bare keyword-action shape of `AmassEffect` / `AdaptEffect` (Keyword directory) and `InvestigateEffect`: the acting player is the ability's controller (implied "you"), so no explicit subject is carried.

- **Effect discriminator:** `ventureIntoTheDungeon`

[Source](AST/Effects/Keyword/VentureIntoTheDungeonEffect.cs)

### `WarpEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Warp [cost] (Rule 702.185). "You may cast this card from your hand for its warp cost. It enters the battlefield tapped..." An alternative-cast keyword that lets a controller cast a permanent for an alternative mana cost, with the permanent entering tapped as a consequence. MAST records the keyword and the warp cost; the alternative-cast and enters-tapped mechanics are engine territory per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine.

Mana-cost-parameterized keyword; mirrors the KickerEffect, PlotEffect, and FlashbackEffect shape.

- **Effect discriminator:** `warp`

[Source](AST/Effects/Keyword/WarpEffect.cs)

### `WebSlingingEffect` — *sealed record* : Effect

Web-slinging (Rule 702.188). A static ability that functions while the spell is on the stack: "Web-slinging [cost]" means "You may cast this spell by paying [cost] and returning a tapped creature you control to its owner's hand rather than paying its mana cost." MAST records the keyword's presence and the web-slinging cost; the return-a-tapped-creature component of the alt cost is expressed in reminder text and is engine territory per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine.

`Cost` is the polymorphic base type for parity with other alt-cost keyword effects (Cycling, Evoke, Flashback, Dash). All known printings use a `ManaCost`.

- **Effect discriminator:** `webSlinging`
