CR 709.5e: "A player who controls a permanent that has one or more locked halves may pay the mana cost of a locked half of that permanent to give that permanent the appropriate unlocked designation." CR 709.5f: "Some spells and abilities instruct a player to 'unlock' half of a permanent." Rule 709.5j: "a 'door' of a Room permanent is a half of that permanent."

`Target` carries the Room filter (CardTypes = ["enchantment"], Subtypes = ["Room"], Controller = You). The choice of which locked half to unlock is the controller's at resolution — engine territory (CR 709.5f).

- **Effect discriminator:** `unlockDoor`

[Source](AST/Effects/ZoneChange/UnlockDoorEffect.cs)

### `SearchDestination` — *enum*

Where cards go after searching.

[Source](AST/Effects/ZoneChange/SearchDestination.cs)

## `/AST/Quantities/`

### `Quantity` — *abstract record*

Base type for numeric quantities that may be literal, variable, or derived.

- **Polymorphic base, discriminator property:** `QuantityType`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `AnyAmountQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

The cost choice "Remove <b>any number of</b> [type] counters" — an unbounded player choice (Hollow Trees, the Mana Batteries). Per CR 107.3 — "Many objects use the letter X as a placeholder for a number that needs to be determined … the rest let their controller choose the value of X" — this is a free, upper-unbounded choice, distinct from `UpToQuantity` (a bounded "up to N") and `VariableQuantity` (a named X with a defined value). Field-less; reusable for any "any number of" text.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `anyAmount`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `AtLeastQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity representing "one or more" — a variable target count whose minimum is `Minimum` (1 for "one or more") and whose maximum is <b>unbounded</b>. Used for spells that target a variable number of objects, e.g. Dwarven Song — "One or more target creatures become red until end of turn."

CR 601.2c (verbatim): "The player announces their choice of an appropriate object or player for each target the spell requires. ... If the spell has a variable number of targets, the player announces how many targets they will choose before they announce those targets. In some cases, the number of targets will be defined by the spell's text. Once the number of targets the spell has is determined, that number doesn't change, even if the information used to determine the number of targets does." "One or more target creatures" is exactly 601.2c's variable number of targets: the controller chooses how many, with a floor of one and no ceiling.

Distinct from its siblings:

`AnyAmountQuantity` — "any number of" is minimum 0 (may choose none); encoding "one or more" as `anyAmount` would be rules-inaccurate. `UpToQuantity` — "up to N" is bounded above by `Maximum`; "one or more" has no upper bound, so this node drops the maximum field.

Serializes as `{"QuantityType":"atLeast","Minimum":1}`. Auto-discovered by reflection (`PolymorphicReflectionConverter&lt;Quantity&gt;`); no registration.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `atLeast`

[Source](AST/Quantities/AtLeastQuantity.cs)

### `CalculatedQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity derived from a calculation or expression. e.g., "half X rounded down", "twice that many", "+2 for each Aura attached".

A calculated quantity carries EITHER a structured `Operand` (a simple "multiply the base count by N") OR a free-text `Expression` for shapes not yet structured. Exactly one is expected; both are optional so each authoring site can use whichever fits.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `calculated`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `CardsRevealedThisWayQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity equal to the number of cards <b>revealed this way</b> by a `RevealCardsEffect` earlier in the same spell or ability — "where X is the number of cards revealed this way" (Scent of Nightshade: "Reveal any number of black cards in your hand. Target creature gets -X/-X until end of turn, where X is the number of cards revealed this way.").

The "this way" sibling of `CounterCountQuantity` (counters on an object) and `CountersRemovedThisWayQuantity` (counters consumed by a cost): a count of cards produced by the same ability's own reveal action. Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): "this way" names the `RevealCardsEffect` in the same effect list — it is a textual link, NOT a variable threaded from the reveal — so MAST records the reference and the engine evaluates the actual count at resolution. Field-less, mirroring `DieRollResultQuantity` / `DomainQuantity` / `AnyAmountQuantity`. Serializes as `{"QuantityType":"cardsRevealedThisWay"}`.

CR 701.20a: "To reveal a card, show that card to all players for a brief time."

- **Quantity discriminator:** `cardsRevealedThisWay`

[Source](AST/Quantities/CardsRevealedThisWayQuantity.cs)

### `CountQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity that counts objects matching a filter. e.g., "the number of creatures you control".

`CountOf` is a structured `ObjectFilter` rather than a verbatim phrase: counting "lands you control" or "Aura and Equipment attached to it" is the same object-selection semantics the rest of the AST expresses through `ObjectFilter` (card types, subtypes, supertypes, controller, the `AttachedTo` relational axis). Counting <i>counters</i> — a number that is not a count of objects — is a distinct shape carried by `CounterCountQuantity`.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `count`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `CounterCountQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity that counts <b>counters</b> of a named kind on an object — "for each oil counter on it" (Serum-Core Chimera). Distinct from `CountQuantity`: a counter is not an object, so an `ObjectFilter` cannot express "how many oil counters are on this permanent". The kind of counter (`CounterType`) and the object bearing them (`On`) are the two axes.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `counterCount`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `CountersRemovedThisWayQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity equal to the number of counters <b>removed this way</b> by the activation cost of the same ability — "Add {G} for each storage counter removed this way" (Hollow Trees), "add an additional {B} for each charge counter removed this way" (Black Mana Battery). The cost-linked sibling of `CounterCountQuantity` (counters currently <i>on</i> an object) and `KeywordCostPaidCountQuantity` (a keyword cost paid): a count of counters consumed by this ability's own `RemoveCountersCost`.

Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): "this way" names the `RemoveCountersCost` on the <i>same</i> ability, it is NOT a variable threaded from the cost — MAST records the textual link, not the runtime value (counter mechanics are engine territory; CR 122.1 — "A counter is a marker placed on an object or player … Counters are not objects and have no characteristics"). The kind of counter removed is the one axis.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `countersRemovedThisWay`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `DerivedQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity derived from a characteristic of an object. e.g., "equal to its power", "equal to the number of cards in your hand"

- **Quantity discriminator:** `derived`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `DevotionQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity equal to the player's devotion to a specific color — the number of mana symbols of that color among mana costs of permanents that player controls.

CR 700.5a: "A player's 'devotion to [color]' is the number of mana symbols of that color among the mana costs of permanents that player controls." MAST records the color identifier (e.g. "U" for blue) without pre-resolving the count; the engine evaluates it against game state (ADR 0004: reference-not-resolution).

- **Quantity discriminator:** `devotion`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `DieRollResultQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity equal to the numeric result of the most recently rolled die within the same ability — "a number … equal to the result" (Ancient Copper Dragon).

CR 706.2: "After the roll, the number indicated on the top face of the die before any modifiers is the natural result … After considering all applicable modifiers, the final number is the result of the die roll." The antecedent of "the result" is the `RollDieEffect` that immediately precedes this quantity's owner in the ability's effect list. Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): MAST records the reference to the roll result; the engine evaluates the actual numeric value at resolution time.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `dieRollResult`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `DomainQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity equal to the card's <b>domain</b> — the number of basic land types among lands the relevant player controls ("for each basic land type among lands you control"). A specific game-value quantity in the same family as `DevotionQuantity` (CR 700.5 devotion), carried as its own record rather than a `DerivedKind` so no shared enum edit is needed.

CR 305.6: "The basic land types are Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, and Forest. If an object uses the words 'basic land type,' it's referring to one of these subtypes. An object with the land card type and a basic land type has the intrinsic ability '{T}: Add [mana symbol],' even if the text box doesn't actually contain that text or the object has no text box." Domain counts how many of these five distinct basic land types appear among the controlled lands.

Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): MAST records the domain reference; the engine counts the distinct basic land types among the controlled lands at evaluation time. It does NOT pre-resolve to a literal 5 (the maximum) or any fixed value. Field-less — mirrors `DieRollResultQuantity` / `AnyAmountQuantity`. Serializes as `{"QuantityType":"domain"}`.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `domain`

[Source](AST/Quantities/DomainQuantity.cs)

### `KeywordCostPaidCountQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity equal to the number of times a keyword's repeatable additional cost was paid as the spell was cast — "for each time it was kicked" (Wolfbriar Elemental, keyed on Kicker: CR 702.33d defines the kicked state and 702.33c folds a multikicker cost into a kicker cost). The count sibling of `KeywordCostPaidCondition` (the boolean was-it-paid): this carries the times-paid for a repeatable keyword (Kicker/Multikicker, and prospectively Squad/Replicate).

Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): keyed on the producing keyword's typed `KeywordAbility` identity (a linked ability, e.g. CR 702.33e), NOT a variable threaded from the `AdditionalCastCostEffect` producer. Distinct from `CounterCountQuantity` (counters on an object) and `CountQuantity` (objects matching a filter): a times-paid count is neither a counter nor an object count.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `keywordCostPaidCount`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `LiteralQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A literal numeric value like 1, 2, 3.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `literal`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `ManaSpentToCastQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity equal to the total amount of mana spent to cast the spell that became this permanent — "equal to the amount of mana spent to cast it" (Gyrus, Waker of Corpses: "Gyrus enters with a number of +1/+1 counters on it equal to the amount of mana spent to cast it.").

CR 601.2f (verbatim): "The player determines the total cost of the spell. Usually this is just the mana cost. ... The total cost is the mana cost or alternative cost (as determined in rule 601.2b), plus all additional costs and cost increases, and minus all cost reductions." CR 601.2h (verbatim): "The player pays the total cost. First, they pay all costs that don't involve random elements or moving objects from the library to a public zone, in any order. Then they pay all remaining costs in any order. Partial payments are not allowed. Unpayable costs can't be paid." — the amount of mana actually spent (e.g. generic mana paid for an `{X}` cost) is a fact fixed once the spell finishes being cast, exactly like the color-keyed `ManaSpentToCastCondition` but reading the total NUMBER of mana spent rather than a boolean color check.

Distinct from `ManaValue` (a `DerivedQuantity` reading the spell's PRINTED mana value, a static characteristic): the amount of mana spent is the dynamic total actually paid at cast time, which may exceed the printed mana value when a variable cost (`{X}`) is involved — Gyrus's own `{X}{B}{R}{G}` cost is the canonical case. Also distinct from Sunburst (CR 702.44, GLOSSARY), which counts the number of DISTINCT COLORS of mana spent (a per-color tally, left as engine territory / keyword presence per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine) rather than the total numeric amount.

Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): the engine reads the actual total mana spent to cast the spell that became this permanent; MAST does not pre-evaluate it. Field-less, mirroring `DomainQuantity` / `DieRollResultQuantity`. Serializes as `{"QuantityType":"manaSpentToCast"}`.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `manaSpentToCast`

[Source](AST/Quantities/ManaSpentToCastQuantity.cs)

### `RemainderQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

"the rest" / "the remaining [cards]" — whatever is left over after the other named shares of a distribution have been accounted for (CR 701.23e-style multi-destination search text: "Put one of them onto the battlefield ... Put two of them onto the battlefield ... and the rest into your hand"). Distinct from `AnyAmountQuantity` (a free, unbounded player CHOICE, e.g. "remove any number of counters"): a remainder is not chosen — it is exactly the found/available total minus every other share already assigned in the same distribution (e.g. `Placements`). Field-less; the sibling placements in the same list supply the amounts being subtracted, so there is nothing to parameterise here beyond "what's left".

- **Quantity discriminator:** `remainder`

[Source](AST/Quantities/RemainderQuantity.cs)

### `UpToQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A quantity representing "up to N" choices. e.g., "discard up to two cards"

- **Quantity discriminator:** `upTo`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `VariableQuantity` — *sealed record* : Quantity

A variable quantity like X, Y, Z.

- **Quantity discriminator:** `variable`

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

### `DerivedKind` — *enum*

What a derived quantity is based on.

[Source](AST/Quantities/Quantity.cs)

## `/AST/References/`

### `AbilityReference` — *abstract record*

A filter over a class of abilities or spells, keyed on the surviving keyword identity — the <b>reference half</b> of the production/reference duality (ADR 0003). When a keyword decomposes into shared primitives, its identity survives as a typed `KeywordAbility` label; an `AbilityReference` is what another card's effect matches that label on.

Strong Back's "Equip abilities you activate that target enchanted creature" and "Aura spells you cast that target enchanted creature" are both `AbilityReference`s with a controller and an optional target predicate. Per ADR 0003, the identity that survives decomposition must be the same identity a filter matches on — which is why this is keyed on the typed `KeywordAbility` enum rather than a bare string.

- **Polymorphic base, discriminator property:** `Kind`

[Source](AST/References/AbilityReference.cs)

### `Characteristic` — *abstract record*

A single characteristic constraint on an `ObjectFilter` beyond the structured axes (card type, subtype, color, zone, comparisons). Where a constraint has a first-class home on `ObjectFilter`, use that; this union is for constraints that do not yet — modelled honestly as typed variants rather than the bare strings this field used to carry.

Today it distinguishes a keyword-ability constraint (`KeywordCharacteristic`) from the typed residual (`OtherCharacteristic`) that holds anything not yet structured. The residual is a deferral, not a destination: state predicates (tapped, attacking), negated types/colors, and relational predicates are carved out into their own variants — or routed to existing `ObjectFilter` fields — in follow-up work.

- **Polymorphic base, discriminator property:** `CharacteristicType`

[Source](AST/References/Characteristic.cs)

### `HistoryPredicate` — *abstract record*

Base type for backward-looking lifecycle predicates that restrict an `ObjectFilter`. Where the rest of `ObjectFilter` describes the object's *current* characteristics, a history predicate describes *something that happened* to or with the object during a window of past time — e.g. "a creature dealt damage by X this turn", "a spell you cast this turn", "a permanent that entered the battlefield this turn".

These predicates are descriptive only — MAST records what the oracle text says happened, not how a runtime engine would track it.

- **Polymorphic base, discriminator property:** `PredicateType`

[Source](AST/References/HistoryPredicate.cs)

### `ActivatedAbilityReference` — *sealed record* : AbilityReference

Matches a class of <b>activated</b> abilities by their surviving keyword identity — Strong Back / LeoninShikari "Equip abilities" (CR 702.6a, the Equip activated ability being filtered).

[Source](AST/References/AbilityReference.cs)

### `CastThisTurnPredicate` — *sealed record* : HistoryPredicate

"cast by [caster] this turn" — a spell was placed on the stack by the named controller during the current turn. Used to count spells in a `CountQuantity` for effects like Aetherflux Reservoir's "you gain 1 life for each spell you've cast this turn" (CR 601 — casting a spell places it on the stack; "this turn" bounds the window to the current turn's actions). The Caster axis identifies who cast them; usually `You` but may be Any for storm-like shapes.

[Source](AST/References/HistoryPredicate.cs)

### `CombatStateCharacteristic` — *sealed record* : Characteristic

A combat-state constraint — the filtered object is attacking and/or blocking. "Attacking creatures get +1/+1", "deals damage to target blocking creature", "exile target attacking creature". The combat-state predicate the `Characteristic` doc calls out as a first-class carve-out from the `OtherCharacteristic` residual. Describes what the oracle text says (the object is in this combat role); the turn/combat machinery is engine territory (CR 508/509).

[Source](AST/References/Characteristic.cs)

### `Comparison` — *sealed record*

A numeric comparison. The right-hand side is either a printed literal (`Value`) or a relative reference to another object's characteristic (`RelativeTo` + `RelativeCharacteristic`) — e.g. "power less than this creature's power" (Mentor, CR 702.134) compares against the source object's power, not a static int. Exactly one side is populated: literal consumers set `Value` and leave the relative axes null (serialized byte-identically — the relative fields are omitted via WhenWritingNull); relative consumers set `RelativeTo`/`RelativeCharacteristic` and leave `Value` null.

[Source](AST/References/ObjectFilter.cs)

### `CounterCharacteristic` — *sealed record* : Characteristic

A counter constraint — the filtered object must have a counter of a given kind, e.g. "creature with a +1/+1 counter on it" (Crowned Ceratok, Sapphire Drake; CR 122). The counter-presence predicate carved out of the `OtherCharacteristic` residual. With no `Count` the constraint is mere presence ("a counter"); a `Count` comparison constrains how many ("two or more +1/+1 counters").

[Source](AST/References/Characteristic.cs)

### `CrewedPredicate` — *sealed record* : HistoryPredicate

"[creature] that crewed [vehicle] [timeframe]". e.g. "target nonlegendary creature that crewed it this turn".

[Source](AST/References/HistoryPredicate.cs)

### `DealtDamageByPredicate` — *sealed record* : HistoryPredicate

"[object] dealt damage by [source] [timeframe]". e.g. "a creature dealt damage by Zurgo this turn".

[Source](AST/References/HistoryPredicate.cs)

### `EquippedStateCharacteristic` — *sealed record* : Characteristic

An equipped/unequipped state constraint — "Equipped creatures you control have flying and haste" (Dalakos, Crafter of Wonders). The attachment-state predicate the `Characteristic` doc calls out as a first-class carve-out from the `OtherCharacteristic` residual, sibling to `TappedStateCharacteristic` (same mechanism: a bool state axis on the filter, not a back-reference to a specific attaching object).

CR 702.6 (Equip, verbatim per `ObjectIsEquippedCondition`'s own citation): "an Equipment can become attached to a creature; a creature with an Equipment attached to it is 'equipped'." Distinct from `IsEquipped` (the Equipment-source's OWN back-reference to the specific permanent IT is attached to, e.g. "whenever equipped creature attacks" printed on an Equipment card): this characteristic instead scopes an unrelated permanent's "Each"-quantified anthem to whichever creatures currently carry ANY Equipment, with no back-reference to a particular attaching object — Dalakos is a creature, not an Equipment, so it has no "own" equipped creature to back-reference. Describes what the oracle text says (the object is equipped, or not); the actual attachment state is engine territory (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004).

[Source](AST/References/Characteristic.cs)

### `ExtremeStatCharacteristic` — *sealed record* : Characteristic

A superlative constraint — the filtered object must hold the greatest (or least) value of a numeric characteristic among a population of objects. "a creature or planeswalker they control with the greatest mana value among creatures and planeswalkers they control" (Blot Out, End of the Hunt); the comparative predicate carved out of the `OtherCharacteristic` residual that the free-text whitelist named as missing ("no MaxStatFilter node exists yet", the Professor Onyx greatest-power carve-out).

A game-state predicate, not machinery: it records what the oracle text says (this object is the maximum/minimum of `Stat` over the population), never how the extremum is computed. CR 202.3 defines mana value; CR 208 power/toughness. Ties are resolved by the choosing player at resolution (CR 701 edict choice) — the predicate merely names which end of the range qualifies.

The population the extremum ranges over is, by default, the enclosing `ObjectFilter`'s own set — the "among …" clause restates the object's own filter ("greatest mana value among creatures and planeswalkers they control" on a filter that already is "creature or planeswalker they control"). When the ranged population differs from the object's own filter, `Scope` names it explicitly; null (the common case) means "among the objects matching this same filter".

[Source](AST/References/ExtremeStatCharacteristic.cs)

### `GameTime` — *sealed record*

A point on the game's turn timeline (CR 500-series turn structure) — the shared primitive composed by the three rules objects that reference the clock: time-triggers ("At the beginning of your upkeep"), delayed triggers ("…at the beginning of the next end step"), and duration endpoints ("until end of turn"). A value type, not an effect or ability. See ADR 0002.

[Source](AST/References/GameTime.cs)

### `KeywordCharacteristic` — *sealed record* : Characteristic

The filtered object must have a keyword ability — e.g. "creature with flying", or (inside an evasion `CanBeBlockedBy` filter) "can be blocked only by creatures with flying".

[Source](AST/References/Characteristic.cs)

### `Kleene` — *static class*

Kleene (strong) three-valued connectives over `Trilean`.

[Source](AST/References/Trilean.cs)

### `ObjectActivatedAbilityReference` — *sealed record* : AbilityReference

Matches <b>activated abilities</b> that belong to a class of permanents identified by `PermanentFilter` — Forensic Gadgeteer's "Activated abilities of artifacts you control" (CR 602.1c). Unlike `ActivatedAbilityReference` (which keys on a keyword identity), this variant keys on the <i>permanent's</i> card-type characteristics, so it clusters cards that reduce activation costs for a whole category of permanents (Vedalken Orrery-style effects, rock-reduction effects).

The `Controller` base field carries "you control" when present.

[Source](AST/References/AbilityReference.cs)

### `ObjectFilter` — *sealed record*

Describes a filter for selecting objects. e.g., "nontoken creature with flying you control"

[Source](AST/References/ObjectFilter.cs)

### `ObjectFilterRelations` — *static class*

Pure relational operators over `ObjectFilter` (magic-ast ADR-0008): can two filters denote a common game object (`Intersects`)? No board state, no object materialization. Type-axis decisions read a vendored `TypeOntology`; the operator hard-codes no type names. Axes land one at a time — any axis a filter constrains but the operator does not yet decide floors the verdict to `Unknown`, so the operator is sound (never a false `Overlaps`/`Disjoint`) at every increment.

[Source](AST/References/ObjectFilterRelations.cs)

### `ObjectReference` — *sealed record*

A reference to an object in the game. e.g., "target creature", "this creature", "it", "you"

[Source](AST/References/ObjectReference.cs)

### `OtherCharacteristic` — *sealed record* : Characteristic, IResidual

Typed residual for a characteristic constraint that does not yet have a structured variant — carries the literal oracle phrase. Use sparingly; prefer a structured variant (or an existing `ObjectFilter` field) when the shape recurs.

[Source](AST/References/Characteristic.cs)

### `OtherHistoryPredicate` — *sealed record* : HistoryPredicate, IResidual

Escape hatch for backward-looking predicates that don't yet have a structured shape — carries only the literal oracle phrase. Use sparingly; prefer a structured concrete predicate when the shape recurs.

[Source](AST/References/HistoryPredicate.cs)

### `PutIntoGraveyardThisTurnPredicate` — *sealed record* : HistoryPredicate

"cards put into [player's] graveyard from [zone] this turn" — a backward- looking count predicate for the Fraying Sanity family (CR 701.17 mill; "At the beginning of each end step, enchanted player mills X cards, where X is the number of cards put into their graveyard from anywhere this turn"). Counts objects that were moved into the named player's graveyard during the current turn window.

CR 406.6 (graveyard zone); CR 400.1 (zones); "from anywhere" in oracle text encodes `Zone.Anywhere` on `FromZone` (null means unqualified, which is any zone by default but distinct from the explicit "from anywhere" qualifier).

[Source](AST/References/HistoryPredicate.cs)

### `SpellReference` — *sealed record* : AbilityReference

Matches a class of <b>spells</b> by a characteristic filter — Strong Back's "Aura spells you cast". The spell's qualifying characteristics live in `Filter` (subtype Aura, controller You).

[Source](AST/References/AbilityReference.cs)

### `SubtypePool` — *sealed record*

One 205.3 subtype pool: its name, owning card type(s), source rule, and members.

[Source](AST/References/TypeOntology.cs)

### `TappedStateCharacteristic` — *sealed record* : Characteristic

A tapped/untapped state constraint — "tapped creature" (Vengeance, CR 110.5a) or "untapped creature" (Saryth). The state predicate the `Characteristic` doc calls out as a first-class carve-out from the `OtherCharacteristic` residual. Describes what the oracle text says (the object is tapped, or untapped); the actual tap status is engine territory (CR 701.21 / 110.5).

[Source](AST/References/Characteristic.cs)

### `TypeOntology` — *sealed record*

magic-ast-local consumer model for the MTG type ontology published by the `mtg-rules` project as `type-ontology.json`. Per ADR-0008 the serialized artifact is the cross-language contract — this is a thin model bound to it, NOT a project reference to mtg-rules. Carries the derived type facts the relation operators read: card types (300.1), the permanent partition (110.4), colors (105.1), supertypes (205.4a), and the 205.3 subtype pools with their owning card type(s) — creature → `{creature, kindred}`, spell → `{instant, sorcery}`.

[Source](AST/References/TypeOntology.cs)

### `ChosenCharacteristicKind` — *enum*

Which "chosen" characteristic an `ChosenCharacteristic` reference points at — the value selected by a "choose a [creature type|color]" effect as this permanent entered (CR 607 linked abilities). Kind-based and implicit: a permanent has at most one chosen creature type and one chosen color.

[Source](AST/References/ObjectFilter.cs)

### `CombatState` — *enum*

The combat role a `CombatStateCharacteristic` constrains.

[Source](AST/References/Characteristic.cs)

### `ComparisonOperator` — *enum*

Comparison operators.

[Source](AST/References/ObjectFilter.cs)

### `ControllerFilter` — *enum*

Filter for who controls an object.

[Source](AST/References/ObjectFilter.cs)

### `FilterRelation` — *enum*

Three-valued result of `Intersects`: can two `ObjectFilter`s denote a common game object? `Unknown` is the soundness floor — an axis the operator does not yet decide yields it rather than a false yes/no (magic-ast ADR-0008 / the operator spec). Composes upward into mast-int as a candidate-pending edge, the same tri-state discipline as the parser's `IUnparsed`.

[Source](AST/References/FilterRelation.cs)

### `KeywordAbility` — *enum*

Canonical identity of a Magic keyword ability (CR 702). A structured alternative to the bare keyword strings the AST has historically carried — casing-proof and exhaustively matchable.

This is the typed target of `Ability.KeywordSource` (ADR 0001): every keyword-as-string a producer emits maps to a member here. Members whose default serialization (the member name verbatim) differs from the exact printed string carry `JsonStringEnumMemberNameAttribute` so the serialized JSON round-trips unchanged (e.g. `BattleCry` ⇄ `"Battle cry"`).

Parameterized keywords carry their parameter separately (in the expanded effect / reminder), so only their bare identity appears here: `Affinity` (the "for &lt;type&gt;" lives in the effect), `Champion` (the championed type lives in `ChampionEffect`), `Landcycling` (the land type lives in `TypecyclingEffect.Type`).

[Source](AST/References/KeywordAbility.cs)

### `ObjectReferenceKind` — *enum*

The kind of object reference.

[Source](AST/References/ObjectReference.cs)

### `RelativeCharacteristic` — *enum*

Which characteristic of a referenced object a relative `Comparison` reads — the "[object]'s power" / "[object]'s toughness" axis a relative threshold compares against (CR 702.134 Mentor compares the target's power to the source's power).

[Source](AST/References/ObjectFilter.cs)

### `StatExtreme` — *enum*

Which end of the numeric range an `ExtremeStatCharacteristic` selects.

[Source](AST/References/ExtremeStatCharacteristic.cs)

### `TimeBoundary` — *enum*

The beginning or end edge of a `TurnPart`.

[Source](AST/References/GameTime.cs)

### `TimeRelation` — *enum*

"this" or "next" occurrence of the referenced point.

[Source](AST/References/GameTime.cs)

### `Trilean` — *enum*

The canonical three-valued (Kleene) logic value for MAST — MAST being the most-upstream library (magic-ast ADR-0008), this is the primitive downstream three-valued models map onto rather than each re-inventing one. `Subsumes` returns it directly; `FilterRelation` is a sibling domain-named enum over the same lattice (`Overlaps≈Yes`, `Disjoint≈No`), kept distinct so call sites read in their own vocabulary.

[Source](AST/References/Trilean.cs)

### `TurnPart` — *enum*

A phase or step of the turn, plus the coarse whole-turn and whole-combat spans.

[Source](AST/References/GameTime.cs)

### `Zone` — *enum*

Game zones where cards can exist.

[Source](AST/References/ObjectFilter.cs)

## `/AST/Triggers/`

### `TriggerOccurrence` — *abstract record*

What fires a trigger: either a game <b>event</b> (a permanent dies, a spell is cast) or a <b>time</b> (a clock point — "at the beginning of your upkeep"). ADR 0002 pulled the clock points out of the flat `TriggerEvent` enum into `GameTime`; this union is the one slot a printed *or* delayed trigger uses, matching CR 603's when/whenever/at.

Serialised heterogeneously to keep the migration small: an event is a bare enum string (every existing event fixture is unchanged), a time is a bare `GameTime` object. The implicit conversions let producer sites keep writing `Event = TriggerEvent.Attacks` (or a `GameTime`) without wrapping.

[Source](AST/Triggers/TriggerOccurrence.cs)

### `EventOccurrence` — *sealed record* : TriggerOccurrence

A trigger fired by a game event (CR 603 — zone change, combat, cast, …).

[Source](AST/Triggers/TriggerOccurrence.cs)

### `TimeOccurrence` — *sealed record* : TriggerOccurrence

A trigger fired at a clock point (CR 603 "at" — the beginning/end of a phase or step).

[Source](AST/Triggers/TriggerOccurrence.cs)

### `TriggerCondition` — *sealed record*

Represents the trigger condition for a triggered ability. Rule 603

[Source](AST/Triggers/TriggerCondition.cs)

### `TriggerOccurrenceConverter` — *sealed class* : JsonConverter<TriggerOccurrence>

Reads/writes `TriggerOccurrence` heterogeneously: a JSON string is an `EventOccurrence` (the `TriggerEvent` enum), a JSON object is a `TimeOccurrence` (a `GameTime`).

[Source](AST/Triggers/TriggerOccurrence.cs)

### `TriggerEvent` — *enum*

Categories of trigger events.

[Source](AST/Triggers/TriggerCondition.cs)

### `TriggerTiming` — *enum*

The timing word that starts a triggered ability.

[Source](AST/Triggers/TriggerCondition.cs)

## `/Diagnostics/`

### `Diagnostic` — *sealed record*

Represents a diagnostic message from parsing.

[Source](Diagnostics/Diagnostic.cs)

### `DiagnosticSeverity` — *enum*

Severity level for diagnostics.

[Source](Diagnostics/Diagnostic.cs)

## `/Keywords/`

### `IKeyword` — *interface*

One self-contained keyword. Each implementation bundles the two facts that used to be split across `KeywordDefinitions.cs` (the expansion definition) and `OracleParsers.cs` (the oracle-text combinator) into a single file under `Keywords/Definitions/`, decorated with `KeywordAttribute` for reflection discovery by `KeywordRegistry`.

Splitting keyword knowledge one-file-per-keyword removes the two-hot-file merge-conflict bottleneck: a new keyword (or a batch of them) is a set of new files with no edits to any shared list or Or-chain.

[Source](Keywords/IKeyword.cs)

### `IKeywordExpander` — *interface*

Service for expanding keywords into their full ability subtrees.

[Source](Keywords/KeywordExpander.cs)

### `KeywordAttribute` — *sealed class* : Attribute, IPrioritizedRuleAttribute

Marks an `IKeyword` implementation for reflection-based discovery by `KeywordRegistry`. Each decorated file contributes one keyword's definition (to the expander) and combinator (to the keyword Or-chain).

<b>Priority convention (range 0–100, default 50, higher = tried first within its `KeywordTier`):</b> the registry folds discovered combinators into the Simple and Parameterized Or-chains ordered by descending priority then ordinal name. Superpower's `.Or` is first-success-wins, so a keyword whose oracle text is a <i>prefix</i> of another must be tried <i>after</i> the longer one — bump the longer/more-specific keyword's priority so it sorts earlier.

<b>60–100</b> — keywords that must precede a sibling whose token prefix they share. Examples: `Partner with [Name]` (must beat bare `Partner`); multi-word `First strike` / `Double strike` before any single-word keyword that could partially consume their first token. Without the bump first-success-wins would let the shorter sibling shadow them. <b>50</b> — default. Non-overlapping keywords whose leading token is unique (the vast majority — Flying, Toxic, Flashback, …). <b>0–40</b> — deliberately-last catch-alls (e.g. a generic `[Type]cycling` matcher that should yield to specific cycling variants first).

The numeric scheme replaces the old source-order convention: ordering used to be implicit in where a combinator appeared in the `SimpleKeyword` / `ParameterizedKeyword` Or-chains. One-file-per-keyword loses that signal, so each keyword now states its priority explicitly when ordering matters.

[Source](Keywords/KeywordAttribute.cs)

### `KeywordDefinition` — *sealed record*

Defines a keyword ability and how it expands to a full ability subtree. Keywords are shorthand as defined in Rules 701 (actions) and 702 (abilities).

[Source](Keywords/KeywordDefinition.cs)

### `KeywordExpander` — *sealed class* : IKeywordExpander

Default implementation of keyword expansion using a registry of definitions.

[Source](Keywords/KeywordExpander.cs)

### `KeywordRegistry` — *static class*

Reflection-discovered registry of one-file-per-keyword `IKeyword` implementations under `Keywords/Definitions/`. Rebuilds the two artifacts a keyword used to contribute across two hot files:

`RegisteredDefinitions` — the expander's definition list (was `KeywordDefinitions.All`). `RegisteredKeywordList` — the keyword Or-chain combinator (was `OracleParsers.KeywordList`).

As of Phase-2 Stage C this registry is the sole source of keyword knowledge: the legacy `KeywordDefinitions` static-property list and the per-keyword `OracleParsers` combinators have been deleted. `CreateDefault` and `OracleParsers.KeywordList` both delegate here directly — no legacy fallback remains.

[Source](Keywords/KeywordRegistry.cs)

### `KeywordCategory` — *enum*

The category of ability that a keyword expands to.

[Source](Keywords/KeywordDefinition.cs)

### `KeywordParameterType` — *enum*

The type of parameter a keyword can have.

[Source](Keywords/KeywordDefinition.cs)

### `KeywordTier` — *enum*

The Or-chain a keyword's combinator folds into, mirroring the legacy `SimpleKeyword` / `ParameterizedKeyword` split. `AnyKeyword` tries `Simple` first, then `Parameterized`.

[Source](Keywords/IKeyword.cs)

## `/Keywords/Definitions/`

### `AffinityKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Affinity for [text]: This spell costs {1} less to cast for each [text] you control. Rule 702.41. The parameter is a free-text type/subtype label (e.g., "artifacts", "Cats", "Plains", "historic permanents"). MAST captures it as a structured `ObjectFilter` on the cost-reduction's per-object axis.

The `Definition` is the verbatim former `KeywordDefinitions.Affinity` (including its inlined `BuildAffinityFilter` helper); the `Combinator` is the verbatim former `OracleParsers.Affinity`, with the expansion inlined to avoid reaching back into `KeywordDefinitions`.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/AffinityKeyword.cs)

### `AfflictKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Afflict N: Whenever this creature becomes blocked, defending player loses N life. CR 702.130 (verbatim): "Afflict is a triggered ability. 'Afflict N' means 'Whenever this creature becomes blocked, defending player loses N life.'" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"Afflict", Trigger:{ Timing:"Whenever", Event:"BecomesBlocked", Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"]} }, Effects:[ LoseLifeEffect{ Player:{Kind:DefendingPlayer}, Amount:LiteralQuantity(N) } ] }.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/AfflictKeyword.cs)

### `AfterlifeKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Afterlife N — a triggered keyword ability. CR 702.135 (verbatim): "Afterlife is a triggered ability. 'Afterlife N' means 'When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, create N 1/1 white and black Spirit creature tokens with flying.'" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"Afterlife", Trigger:{ Timing:When, Event:Dies, Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"]} }, Effects:[ CreateTokenEffect{ Count:N, Token:{ 1/1, W+B, creature, Spirit, [Flying] } } ] }

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/AfterlifeKeyword.cs)

### `AftermathKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Aftermath: Cast this spell only from your graveyard. Then exile it. Rule 702.128. Found on the bottom half of split cards. MAST records the keyword's presence; the graveyard-only cast restriction and exile-on-resolution mechanics are engine territory.

The `Definition` is the verbatim former `KeywordDefinitions.Aftermath`; the `Combinator` is the verbatim former `OracleParsers.Aftermath`.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/AftermathKeyword.cs)

### `AmplifyKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Amplify N: As this creature enters, put a +1/+1 counter on it for each [creature type] card you reveal in your hand. Rule 702.37. MAST records the keyword and its integer value; the creature-type-reveal and counter-placement semantics are engine territory. Integer-parameterized keyword; mirrors the Bushido/Modular/Backup family.

The `Definition` is the verbatim former `KeywordDefinitions.Amplify` (including its inlined `ParseIntValue` guard); the `Combinator` is the verbatim former `OracleParsers.Amplify`.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/AmplifyKeyword.cs)

### `AscendKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Ascend: If you control ten or more permanents, you get the city's blessing for the rest of the game. Rule 702.131. Applies to both permanents (Rule 702.131b) and spells (Rule 702.131a). MAST records the keyword's presence; the city's-blessing designation and downstream effects are engine territory.

The `Definition` is the verbatim former `KeywordDefinitions.Ascend`; the `Combinator` is the verbatim former `OracleParsers.Ascend`.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/AscendKeyword.cs)

### `AssistKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Assist (CR 702.132a): "Assist is a static ability that modifies the rules of paying for the spell with assist (see rules 601.2g-h). If the total cost to cast a spell with assist includes a generic mana component, before you activate mana abilities while casting it, you may choose another player. That player has a chance to activate mana abilities... the player you chose may pay for any amount of the generic mana in the spell's total cost."

Decomposed to `AlternativePaymentEffect` with `DelegatePayment` (another player pays) and `Generic` (generic mana only). Source is null because payment is delegated to a player, not drawn from objects.

Combinator-only keyword — no `KeywordDefinitions.Assist` legacy entry exists; `Definition` returns `null`. `Tier` is `Simple` because no argument follows the keyword token.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/AssistKeyword.cs)

### `AwakenKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Awaken N—[cost]. Rule 702.113. An alternative cost printed on instants and sorceries: "Awaken N—[cost]". If the spell is cast for its awaken cost, it additionally puts N +1/+1 counters on a target land you control and animates that land. MAST records the keyword, the awaken number N, and the alternative cost; the counters-on-land / land-becomes-creature semantics are engine territory (and echoed in reminder text). Combinator-only: no matching `KeywordDefinitions` entry exists in the legacy registry.

Mirrors the Suspend "N—[cost]" shape (`N` + `Cost`). The number/em-dash glue is parsed by private combinators in this file; the trailing cost reuses the shared `ManaCostSymbols` primitive.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/AwakenKeyword.cs)

### `BackupKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Backup N: When this creature enters, put N +1/+1 counters on target creature. If that is another creature, it also gains the non-backup abilities printed below this one until end of turn. Rule 702.165. MAST records the keyword and its integer value; the counter placement, ability-grant, and "printed below this one" scoping are engine territory.

The `Definition` is the verbatim former `KeywordDefinitions.Backup` (including its inlined `ParseIntValue` guard); the `Combinator` is the verbatim former `OracleParsers.Backup`.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/BackupKeyword.cs)

### `BandingKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Banding: Legacy combat ability (Rule 702.22). Any creatures with banding can attack in a band; the attacking player controls how the defending player assigns damage to the band. MAST records keyword presence; combat-band semantics are engine territory. Reminder text varies but keyword token is uniform.

Combinator-only keyword — no `KeywordDefinitions.Banding` static property exists; `Definition` is `null`. The combinator is the verbatim former `OracleParsers.Banding`.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/BandingKeyword.cs)

### `BargainKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Bargain: You may sacrifice an artifact, enchantment, or token as you cast this spell. Rule 702.166. MAST records the keyword's presence; the optional-sacrifice additional-cost and "bargained" designation gating conditional effects are engine territory.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/BargainKeyword.cs)

### `BattleCryKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Battle cry: Whenever this creature attacks, each other attacking creature gets +1/+0 until end of turn. CR 702.91a (verbatim): "Battle cry is a triggered ability. 'Battle cry' means 'Whenever this creature attacks, each other attacking creature gets +1/+0 until end of turn.'" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"BattleCry", Trigger:{ Timing:Whenever, Event:Attacks, Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"]} }, Effects:[ ModifyPTEffect{ Target:{Kind:Each, Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"], ExcludeSelf:true, Characteristics:[CombatStateCharacteristic{Attacking}]}}, PowerModifier:+1, ToughnessModifier:+0, Duration:untilEndOfTurn } ] }. "Other" is encoded as ExcludeSelf=true on the ObjectFilter (CR 109.5, same as Champion/Soulbond). "Attacking" is the combat-state predicate CombatStateCharacteristic{Attacking} (CR 508).

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/BattleCryKeyword.cs)

### `BestowKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Bestow (Rule 702.103a): "Bestow represents a static ability that functions in any zone from which you could play the card it's on. \"Bestow [cost]\" means \"As you cast this spell, you may choose to cast it bestowed. If you do, you pay [cost] rather than its mana cost.\" Casting a spell using its bestow ability follows the rules for paying alternative costs." Rule 702.103b: a spell cast bestowed "becomes an Aura enchantment and gains enchant creature."

Bestow decomposes across two surfaces. The bestow <em>cost</em> is an alternative casting cost — it lives on the card's `AlternativeCostsAttribute` (emitted by `AttributeExtractor`), not in an effect. This static ability carries only the becomes-Aura / gains-enchant-creature <em>mode</em> (702.103b), expressed with the shared `EnchantRestrictionEffect` enchant-creature primitive. The alternative-cast resolution, Aura-mode toggle, and unattach rules are engine territory (descriptive-not-executive doctrine).

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/BestowKeyword.cs)

### `BlitzKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Blitz [cost]: three abilities per CR 702.152a (the sacrifice-variant sibling of `DashKeyword`).

CR 702.152a (verbatim): "Blitz represents three abilities: two static abilities that function while the card with blitz is on the stack, one of which may create a delayed triggered ability, and a static ability that functions while the object with blitz is on the battlefield. 'Blitz [cost]' means 'You may cast this card by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost,' 'If this spell's blitz cost was paid, sacrifice the permanent this spell becomes at the beginning of the next end step,' and 'As long as this permanent's blitz cost was paid, it has haste and \"When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, draw a card.\"' Casting a spell for its blitz cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h."

Oracle-text parsing is handled by `BlitzStaticRule` (priority 1001), which returns all three abilities as a list. This keyword file keeps the combinator live as a fallback but no longer uses the deleted `BlitzEffect` opaque marker: it emits only the PRIMARY alternative-cast static ability ("You may cast this card by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost," from hand). The `Definition` is null because `Expand` can only return a single `Ability` and Blitz decomposes into three.

Combinator-only keyword — no `KeywordDefinition` entry exists in the legacy `KeywordDefinitions.All` list for this keyword.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/BlitzKeyword.cs)

### `BloodthirstKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Bloodthirst N: static ability on the permanent that causes it to enter with N +1/+1 counters when the condition is met. CR 702.54a (verbatim): "Bloodthirst is a static ability. 'Bloodthirst N' means 'If an opponent was dealt damage this turn, this permanent enters with N +1/+1 counters on it.'" MAST shape (ADR-0003 decomposition): StaticAbility{ KeywordSource: Bloodthirst, When: AsThisEnters, Condition: OtherCondition{ Text: "an opponent was dealt damage this turn" }, Effects: [ PutCountersEffect{ Target: Self, CounterType: "+1/+1", Count: LiteralQuantity(N) } ] } The condition "an opponent was dealt damage this turn" has no structured node in the current corpus; ConditionParser.Parse falls through to the typed OtherCondition residual (acceptable per ADR 0001 — residual-debt, not unparsed). Template: KickerConditionalEntersWithCountersRule (StaticAbility{When:AsThisEnters, Condition, PutCountersEffect}).

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/BloodthirstKeyword.cs)

### `BushidoKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Bushido N: Whenever this creature blocks or becomes blocked, it gets +N/+N until end of turn. CR 702.45 (verbatim): "Bushido is a triggered ability. 'Bushido N' means 'Whenever this creature blocks or becomes blocked, it gets +N/+N until end of turn.'" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"Bushido", Trigger:{ Timing:"Whenever", Event:"BlocksOrBecomesBlocked", Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"]} }, Effects:[ ModifyPTEffect{ Target:{Kind:"It"}, PowerModifier:N, ToughnessModifier:N, Duration:untilEndOfTurn } ] }.

Combinator-only: no `KeywordDefinition` exists in the legacy `KeywordDefinitions.cs`. `Definition` returns `null`.

Buyback [cost]: two static abilities per CR 702.27a.

CR 702.27a (verbatim): "Buyback appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents two static abilities that function while the spell is on the stack. 'Buyback [cost]' means 'You may pay an additional [cost] as you cast this spell' and 'If the buyback cost was paid, put this spell into its owner's hand instead of into that player's graveyard as it resolves.'"

Oracle-text parsing is handled by `BuybackStaticRule` (priority 1001), which returns both abilities as a list. This keyword file keeps the combinator live as a fallback but no longer uses the deleted `BuybackEffect` opaque marker: it emits only the PRIMARY additional-cast-cost static ability ("You may pay an additional [cost] as you cast this spell"). The `Definition` is null because `Expand` can only return a single `Ability` and Buyback decomposes into two.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/BuybackKeyword.cs)

### `CascadeKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Cascade: When you cast this spell, exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card whose mana value is less than this spell's mana value. You may cast that card without paying its mana cost. Put the exiled cards not cast on the bottom of your library in a random order. Rule 702.85. Combinator-only: no `KeywordDefinition` exists in the legacy `KeywordDefinitions.cs`. `Definition` returns `null`.

### `CasualtyKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Casualty N: two abilities per CR 702.153a.

CR 702.153a (verbatim): "Casualty is a keyword that represents two abilities. The first is a static ability that functions while the spell with casualty is on the stack. The second is a triggered ability that functions while the spell with casualty is on the stack. Casualty N means 'As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may sacrifice a creature with power N or greater,' and 'When you cast this spell, if a casualty cost was paid for it, copy it. If the spell has any targets, you may choose new targets for the copy.' Paying a spell's casualty cost follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h."

Oracle-text parsing is handled by `CasualtyStaticRule` (priority 1001), which returns both abilities as a list. This keyword file keeps the combinator live as a fallback, emitting only the PRIMARY additional-cost static ability (the cost half). The `Definition` is null because `Expand` can only return a single `Ability` and Casualty decomposes into two.

Combinator-only keyword — no `KeywordDefinition` entry exists in the legacy `KeywordDefinitions.All` list for this keyword.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/CasualtyKeyword.cs)

Champion a [type]: When this enters the battlefield, sacrifice it unless you exile another creature of the named type you control. When this leaves the battlefield, that card returns. Rule 702.71. Changeling: This card is every creature type. Rule 702.73. MAST records keyword presence; the all-creature-type characteristic-defining ability is engine territory.

Choose a Background — Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate partner variant (Rule 702.124g). Emits a static ability whose effect carries `ChooseABackground`. Combinator-only: no matching `KeywordDefinitions` entry exists in the legacy registry.

Cipher: Then you may exile this spell card encoded on a creature you control. Whenever that creature deals combat damage to a player, its controller may cast a copy of the encoded card without paying its mana cost. Rule 702.99. MAST records the keyword's presence; the encoding, copy-creation, and free-cast mechanics are engine territory.

### `CleaveKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Cleave [cost] (CR 702.148a): "Cleave is a keyword that represents two static abilities that function while a spell with cleave is on the stack. 'Cleave [cost]' means 'You may cast this spell by paying [cost] rather than paying its mana cost' and 'If this spell's cleave cost was paid, change its text by removing all text found within square brackets in the spell's rules text.' Casting a spell for its cleave cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h."

It is a static ability, so the combinator emits a `StaticAbility` carrying the shared `AlternativeCastEffect` primitive that Flashback/Surge/Escape etc. also use (`FromZone = Hand` — cleave does not change the legal casting zone, only the cost — `Cost = ` the cleave cost). Mirrors `FlashbackKeyword` exactly, differing only in `FromZone`.

The second static ability (the square-bracket text-removal rewrite) is engine territory, not a descriptive axis of the card — MAST records only the keyword's presence and the alternative cost, mirroring how `OverloadKeyword` treats its own text-rewrite half ("target" → "each") as unmodeled. The printed square-bracket markup itself remains part of the card's other oracle lines and is parsed as printed.

Combinator-only keyword — no `KeywordDefinition` exists in the legacy `KeywordDefinitions` registry.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/CleaveKeyword.cs)

### `CompleatKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Compleated (CR 702.150): a static ability on Phyrexian planeswalkers.

CR 702.150a (verbatim): "Compleated is a static ability found on some planeswalker cards. Compleated means 'If this permanent would enter with one or more loyalty counters on it and the player who cast it chose to pay life for any part of its cost represented by Phyrexian mana symbols, it instead enters the battlefield with that many loyalty counters minus two for each of those mana symbols.'"

MAST records the keyword's presence as a parameterless `KeywordAbilityEffect`; the loyalty-counter reduction logic is engine territory (the descriptive-not-engine doctrine). The parenthetical reminder text explains the Phyrexian mana payment and loyalty reduction; it is stripped by the classifier before the combinator fires, but re-attached to the ability's `Reminder` field.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/CompleatKeyword.cs)

### `ConspireKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Conspire: two abilities per CR 702.78a.

CR 702.78a (verbatim): "Conspire is a keyword that represents two abilities... 'Conspire' means 'As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may tap two untapped creatures you control that each share a color with it' and 'When you cast this spell, if its conspire cost was paid, copy it. If the spell has any targets, you may choose new targets for the copy.'"

Oracle-text parsing is handled by `ConspireStaticRule` (priority 1001), which returns both abilities as a list. This keyword file keeps the combinator live as a fallback: it emits only the PRIMARY additional-cost static ability ("As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may tap two untapped creatures you control that each share a color with it"). The "each share a color with it" relational predicate is modeled via `SharesColorWith` keyed on `{Kind: Self}` (the spell). The `Definition` is null because `Expand` can only return a single `Ability` and Conspire decomposes into two.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/ConspireKeyword.cs)

Converge — ability word. Effects scale with the number of colors of mana spent to cast the spell. Rule 207.2c. MAST records the ability-word marker; the color-counting and scaled-effect semantics are engine territory. Mirrors Sunburst (Rule 702.44).

### `ConvokeKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Convoke (CR 702.51a/b): "Convoke is a static ability that functions while the spell with convoke is on the stack. 'Convoke' means 'For each colored mana in this spell's total cost, you may tap an untapped creature of that color you control rather than pay that mana. For each generic mana in this spell's total cost, you may tap an untapped creature you control rather than pay that mana.'" CR 702.51b: "The convoke ability isn't an additional or alternative cost and applies only after the total cost of the spell with convoke is determined." Accordingly, this is modeled as an `AlternativePaymentEffect` on a static ability — NEVER in a cost slot. `Generic` is the shared baseline (one tapped creature pays {1}); `ColorMustMatchMana` = `true` is Convoke's discriminator (a creature may instead pay one mana of its own color — CR 702.51a).

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/ConvokeKeyword.cs)

### `CraftKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Craft with [materials] [cost]: an activated ability on double-faced cards.

CR 702.167a (verbatim): "Craft represents an activated ability. It is written as \"Craft with [materials] [cost],\" where [materials] is a description of one or more objects. It means \"[Cost], Exile this permanent, Exile [materials] from among permanents you control and/or cards in your graveyard: Return this card to the battlefield transformed under its owner's control. Activate only as a sorcery.\""

MAST models Craft as a single `ActivatedAbility` decomposed into its three cost components and one effect (the Buyback / Embalm multi-part keyword decomposition is the structural precedent):

<b>Costs</b> = the printed mana `ManaCost`, then an `ExileCost` for "Exile this permanent" (`IsSelf`, from the battlefield), then an `ExileCost` for the [materials] (here "another artifact you control or an artifact card from your graveyard"). <b>Effect</b> = a `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect` of `Self` with `Transformed = true` and `UnderControl = Owner` — "Return this card to the battlefield transformed under its owner's control." <b>Restriction</b> = `OnlyAsSorcery` ("Activate only as a sorcery").

The [materials] pool spans two zones — CR 702.167a "from among permanents you control and/or cards in your graveyard". `ObjectFilter` carries a single `Zone` and `FromZone` a single value with no cross-zone disjunction axis, so the keyword-inherent dual pool is represented by `Owner = You` ("yours") + `FromZone = Anywhere` (any Craft-permitted zone). `ExcludeSelf = true` encodes "another"; `CardTypes` is the [materials] type. The verbatim reminder is preserved in `Reminder`.

The combinator recognises the single-card-type-word material shape ("Craft with artifact/creature/enchantment/land/planeswalker/battle [cost]"). Materials it cannot faithfully structure (tokens, "historic", counted "three creatures", etc.) fall through unparsed rather than mis-parsing into a wrong filter (per the lossy-parse avoidance doctrine). The leading `Craft` + `with` anchor is unique to the Craft keyword, so no sibling keyword shares its prefix.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/CraftKeyword.cs)

Kept as a separate file from `EquipKeyword` (mana-cost form): the two forms have disjoint grammars (bare mana symbols vs. a discard clause terminated by a period) and a shared discriminator (`Equip`) is reused rather than the grammars being folded into one combinator. ### `FirstStrikeKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

First strike: This creature deals combat damage before creatures without first strike. Rule 702.7.

Exemplar of the <b>multi-word simple</b> keyword shape (Stage A template). The combinator matches two sequential word tokens ("First" then "Strike"/"strike") via chained `Keyword(string)` calls. The `Definition` is the verbatim former `KeywordDefinitions.FirstStrike`; the `Combinator` is the verbatim former `OracleParsers.FirstStrike`.

<b>Ordering note:</b> multi-word keywords whose first token is a prefix shared with a shorter keyword must sort earlier in the Or-chain (raise `Priority`). "First" has no single-word collision today, so default priority 50 preserves the legacy ordering. The legacy chain placed First strike / Double strike late; because their leading tokens ("First"/"Double") are unique, order among unrelated keywords is immaterial to first-success-wins.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/FirstStrikeKeyword.cs)

### `FlankingKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Flanking: Whenever this creature becomes blocked by a creature without flanking, the blocking creature gets -1/-1 until end of turn. CR 702.25 (verbatim): "Flanking is a triggered ability that triggers during the declare blockers step. 'Flanking' means 'Whenever this creature becomes blocked by a creature without flanking, the blocking creature gets -1/-1 until end of turn.'" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"Flanking", Trigger:{ Timing:"Whenever", Event:"BecomesBlocked", Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"], Characteristics:[OtherCharacteristic{Description:"withoutFlanking"}]} }, Effects:[ ModifyPTEffect{ Target:{Kind:ThatCreature}, PowerModifier:-1, ToughnessModifier:-1, Duration:untilEndOfTurn } ] }.

The trigger's Filter encodes the blocker qualification ("by a creature without flanking") — TriggerCondition has a single Filter field and no dedicated By/blocker axis; the blocking-creature qualifier is placed there and noted. The effect target is ObjectReferenceKind.ThatCreature (the creature named by the trigger condition — the blocking creature), not Self/It (those refer to the Flanking creature itself).

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/FlankingKeyword.cs)

Casting a spell for its freerunning cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h."

### `GiftKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Gift a card (CR 702.174): "Gift a [something]" is a keyword representing two abilities. CR 702.174a — the first is always the static additional cost "As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may choose an opponent." CR 702.174b — on an instant or sorcery spell the second is "If this spell's gift cost was paid, [effect]", and CR 702.174e — "'Gift a card' means the effect is 'The chosen player draws a card.'"

The keyword ability is emitted as a `StaticAbility` (CR 702.174a: the first ability is a static ability) with `KeywordSource` = `Gift` and two composed effects:

an `OptionalEffect` ("you may") wrapping a `ChoosePlayerEffect` — the promise of a gift to an opponent (CR 702.174a); the opponent restriction is inherent to the gift keyword, so the reused `ChoosePlayerEffect` ("choose a player") carries the declaration only (batch-5 descriptive-not-engine convention); a `GiftEffect` whose `Gifted` is a one-card `DrawCardsEffect` by the chosen player (`ChosenPlayer`) — the "Gift a card" payoff (CR 702.174b/e).

The verbatim reminder text is preserved on `Reminder` (CR 207.2).

Parameterized tier: "Gift" is followed by "a card". `Definition` is null (combinator-only, like Flashback / Unleash) — the DTO keyword list is not expanded, and the parameterized payoff is recognized by the combinator, not the expander.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/GiftKeyword.cs)

### `ImpendingKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Impending N—[cost] (CR 702.176). An alternative-cast keyword that also seeds a battlefield time-counter mechanic — it represents four abilities.

CR 702.176a (verbatim): "Impending is a keyword that represents four abilities. The first is a static ability that functions while the spell with impending is on the stack. The second is static ability that creates a replacement effect that may apply to the permanent with impending as it enters the battlefield from the stack. The third is a static ability that functions on the battlefield. The fourth is a triggered ability that functions on the battlefield. \"Impending N-[cost]\" means \"You may choose to pay [cost] rather than pay this spell's mana cost,\" \"If you chose to pay this permanent's impending cost, it enters with N time counters on it,\" \"As long as this permanent's impending cost was paid and it has a time counter on it, it's not a creature,\" and \"At the beginning of your end step, if this permanent's impending cost was paid and it has a time counter on it, remove a time counter from it.\" Casting a spell for its impending cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h."

Oracle-text parsing is handled by `ImpendingStaticRule` (priority 1001), which returns all four abilities as a list (mirroring the `BuybackKeyword` / `BuybackStaticRule` precedent). This keyword file keeps the combinator live as a fallback that emits only the PRIMARY alternative-cast static ability (the first CR clause) — the `Expand` contract returns a single `Ability`, but Impending decomposes into four, so `Definition` is null.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/ImpendingKeyword.cs)

CR 702.126b: "The improvise ability isn't an additional or alternative cost and applies only after the total cost of the spell with improvise is determined."

MAST models the payment substitution as an `AlternativePaymentEffect` on the static ability (per ADR 0003 keyword-decomposition shape): tap artifacts you control to pay generic mana. "Untapped" is a game-state precondition (engine territory), not a filter axis.

### `IngestKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Ingest: Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, that player exiles the top card of their library. CR 702.115a (verbatim): "Ingest is a triggered ability. 'Ingest' means 'Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, that player exiles the top card of their library.'" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"Ingest", Trigger:{ Timing:Whenever, Event:DealsCombatDamageToPlayer, Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"]} }, Effects:[ ExileEffect{ Target:{Kind:Designated, Filter:{CardTypes:["card"], Zone:Library, Characteristics:[Other("top"), Other("that player's")]}} } ] }. "Top" (positional) and "that player's" (ownership back-reference to the damaged player established by the trigger) are predicates that do not yet have first-class ObjectFilter fields; they are carried as OtherCharacteristic residuals per the ADR 0001 free-text doctrine and the Mentor/Flanking convention. The card is Designated (deterministic by position, no choice) rather than Target (no targeting rule keyword in CR 702.115a).

### `KeywordCombinators` — *static class*

Shared combinator primitives for one-file-per-keyword `IKeyword` implementations under `Keywords/Definitions/`. These are lifted from the private helpers in `OracleParsers` so each keyword file can build its combinator without depending on `OracleParsers` internals.

Behaviour-identical to the legacy private helpers: a keyword migrated to a file produces the exact same `StaticAbility` as the combinator it shadows.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/KeywordCombinators.cs)

### `KickerKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Kicker {cost} (CR 702.33): "Kicker is a static ability that functions while the spell with kicker is on the stack. 'Kicker [cost]' means 'You may pay an additional [cost] as you cast this spell.'" It is a static ability, so the combinator emits a `StaticAbility` carrying the shared `AdditionalCastCostEffect` primitive (`IsOptional = true` — "you may pay"; `Repeatable = false` — at most once, distinguishing it from Multikicker's `Repeatable = true`). The linked "if this spell was kicked, ..." resolution (CR 702.33e / 607) is a separate ability on the card and is not modeled here (ADR 0003/0004 describe-not-execute).

Combinator-only keyword — no `KeywordDefinition` exists in the legacy `KeywordDefinitions` registry. The `Keyword("Kicker")` word-matcher matches the whole word "Kicker", so the longer word "Multikicker" (CR 702.33c, handled by `MultikickerKeyword`) does not match this combinator.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/KickerKeyword.cs)

### `MadnessKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Madness {cost} (CR 702.35a/702.35b): "Madness [cost]" represents two abilities. The first is a static ability: "If a player would discard this card, that player discards it, but exiles it instead of putting it into their graveyard." The second is a triggered ability: "When this card is exiled this way, its owner may cast it by paying [cost] rather than paying its mana cost." (CR 702.35a verbatim.) Casting uses rules for alternative costs (CR 702.35b → 601.2b, 601.2f-h).

MAST describes, does not execute. The describe axis MAST keeps is the permission to cast from exile at an alternative cost, modeled by the shared `AlternativeCastEffect` primitive (`FromZone = Exile`). The discard-into-exile replacement event and the "when exiled this way" triggered wrapper are engine territory (ADR-0003 describe-not-execute). No `Condition` — Madness is unconditional once the discard occurs.

Combinator-only keyword: Madness has no entry in `KeywordDefinitions.All` (it is not registered as a `KeywordDefinition`), so `Definition` is <see langword="null"/>.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/MadnessKeyword.cs)

'Melee' means 'Whenever this creature attacks, it gets +1/+1 until end of turn for each opponent you attacked with a creature this combat.'" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"Melee", Trigger:{ Timing:"Whenever", Event:"Attacks", Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"]} }, Effects:[ ModifyPTEffect{ Target:{Kind:"It"}, PowerModifier:CalculatedQuantity{Expression:"for each opponent you attacked with a creature this combat"}, ToughnessModifier:CalculatedQuantity{Expression:"for each opponent you attacked with a creature this combat"}, Duration:untilEndOfTurn } ] }. The per-opponent amount is not a simple integer or a CountQuantity (the "opponents attacked" set is a game-state query outside MAST's ObjectFilter scope); it is carried as a CalculatedQuantity{Expression} per the ADR free-text residual doctrine for quantities not yet expressible structurally.

### `MentorKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

'Mentor' means 'Whenever this creature attacks, put a +1/+1 counter on target attacking creature with power less than this creature's power.'" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"Mentor", Trigger:{ Timing:Whenever, Event:Attacks, Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"]} }, Effects:[ PutCountersEffect{ Target:{Kind:Target, Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"], Characteristics:[CombatStateCharacteristic{Attacking}], PowerComparison:{LessThan, RelativeTo:Self, RelativeCharacteristic:Power}}}, CounterType:"+1/+1", Count:1 } ] }. "Attacking" is the combat-state predicate (CombatStateCharacteristic, CR 508). "With power less than this creature's power" is a relative power comparison against the source object (PowerComparison with RelativeTo=Self), matching the CantBeBlockedRule relative-power convention.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/MentorKeyword.cs)

### `RampageKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Rampage N: Whenever this creature becomes blocked, it gets +N/+N until end of turn for each creature blocking it beyond the first. CR 702.23a (verbatim): "Rampage is a triggered ability. \"Rampage N\" means \"Whenever this creature becomes blocked, it gets +N/+N until end of turn for each creature blocking it beyond the first.\" (See rule 509, \"Declare Blockers Step.\")" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"Rampage", Trigger:{ Timing:"Whenever", Event:"BecomesBlocked", Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"]} }, Effects:[ ModifyPTEffect{ Target:{Kind:"It"}, PowerModifier:CalculatedQuantity{Operand:N, Operation:"multiply", Expression:"for each creature blocking it beyond the first"}, ToughnessModifier:CalculatedQuantity{Operand:N, Operation:"multiply", Expression:"for each creature blocking it beyond the first"}, Duration:untilEndOfTurn } ] }. The parameter N is captured structurally via `Operand` (per the type's own worked example: "+2 for each … → Operation=\"multiply\", Operand=2"), while "creatures blocking it beyond the first" is a combat-state query outside MAST's `ObjectFilter` scope and is carried as the free-text `Expression` residual — identical doctrine to Melee's per-opponent Expression.

Combinator-only: no `KeywordDefinition` exists in the legacy `KeywordDefinitions.cs`. `Definition` returns `null`.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/RampageKeyword.cs)

### `ReinforceKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

The hand-only functional restriction is engine territory — MAST does not add a zone-restriction field (mirrors `CyclingKeyword`).

MAST models this as a fully decomposed `ActivatedAbility`:

### `TypecyclingKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

[Type]cycling [cost]: Discard this card: Search your library for a [Type] card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle. Rule 702.28 (and the 702.29 landcycling variant). Catch-all parser for the type-cycling family. Recognizes three printed shapes:

single-word land-type variants — Forestcycling, Swampcycling, Plainscycling, etc. (the land type is the prefix before "cycling"); two-word "Basic landcycling {cost}" — searches for a basic land card (Type = "Basic land"); bare "Landcycling {cost}" — searches for any land card (Type = "Land").

MAST records the keyword, the land type, and the cost; the inner search/reveal/shuffle structure is inferred from the rules. Lower priority (40) so specific cycling variants can outrank this catch-all in the registry Or-chain.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/TypecyclingKeyword.cs)

### `UmbraArmorKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Umbra armor (oracle text: "Umbra armor"): If enchanted creature would be destroyed, instead remove all damage from it and destroy this Aura. Rule 702.89. "Umbra armor" is the current Oracle name; "totem armor" is the obsolete prior name (CR 702.89: the older text was renamed). MAST records keyword presence using the discriminator that matches the card's current Oracle wording — `UmbraArmor` — distinct from the obsolete `TotemArmor` the literal "totem armor" combinator emits. The replacement-effect semantics are engine territory. Multi-word keyword; mirrors LivingWeapon.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/UmbraArmorKeyword.cs)

### `UndyingKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Undying (CR 702.93, verbatim): "Undying is a triggered ability. 'Undying' means 'When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, if it had no +1/+1 counters on it, return it to the battlefield under its owner's control with a +1/+1 counter on it.'" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"Undying", Trigger:{ Timing:"When", Event:"Dies", Filter:{CardTypes:["creature"]} }, InterveningIf:{ ConditionType:"other", Text:"it had no +1/+1 counters on it" }, Effects:[ ReturnToBattlefieldEffect{ Target:{Kind:"It"}, UnderControl:{Kind:"Owner"}, WithCounters:{ CounterType:"+1/+1", Count:{QuantityType:"literal", Value:1} } }] }. Mirror of Persist (CR 702.78) with opposite counter polarity: Persist checks for no -1/-1 counters; Undying checks for no +1/+1 counters. The intervening-if "if it had no +1/+1 counters on it" is a CR 603.4 condition on the triggered ability, not an effect guard.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/UndyingKeyword.cs)

### `UnearthKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Unearth [cost]: Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield. It gains haste. Exile it at the beginning of the next end step or if it would leave the battlefield. Unearth only as a sorcery. Rule 702.84. Scope: mana-cost parameter (all known printings). MAST records the keyword and its activation cost; the return, haste-grant, and exile-at-end-step semantics are engine territory.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/UnearthKeyword.cs)

### `UnleashKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Unleash: two static abilities per CR 702.98a.

CR 702.98a (verbatim): "Unleash is a keyword that represents two static abilities. 'Unleash' means 'You may have this permanent enter with an additional +1/+1 counter on it' and 'This permanent can't block as long as it has a +1/+1 counter on it.'"

Oracle-text parsing is handled by `UnleashStaticRule` (priority 1001), which returns both abilities as a list. This keyword file keeps the combinator live as a fallback but no longer emits the opaque `KeywordAbilityEffect{Unleash}` marker: it emits only the PRIMARY enters-with-counter static replacement ability ("You may have this permanent enter with an additional +1/+1 counter on it"). The `Definition` is null because `Expand` can only return a single `Ability` and Unleash decomposes into two.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/UnleashKeyword.cs)

### `VanishingKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Vanishing N: This permanent enters with N time counters on it. At the beginning of your upkeep, remove a time counter from it. When the last is removed, sacrifice it. Rule 702.63. MAST records the keyword and its integer value; the counter-removal upkeep trigger and last-counter sacrifice mechanics are engine territory. Mirrors Fading (702.32) but uses time counters and triggers on the last counter rather than inability to remove.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/VanishingKeyword.cs)

### `VigilanceKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Vigilance: Attacking doesn't cause this creature to tap. Rule 702.20.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/VigilanceKeyword.cs)

### `WardKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Ward {cost}: A triggered ability that counters spells or abilities targeting this permanent unless the opponent pays the stated cost. CR 702.21a (verbatim): "Ward is a triggered ability. Ward [cost] means 'Whenever this permanent becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, counter that spell or ability unless that player pays [cost].'" MAST shape (ADR 0003 decomposition): TriggeredAbility{ KeywordSource:"Ward", Trigger:{ Timing:"Whenever", Event:"BecomesTarget", Filter:{Controller:"Opponent"} }, Effects:[ PreventableEffect{ Inner:CounterSpellEffect{ Target:{Kind:"It"} }, Unless:{ Player:{Kind:"ThatPlayer"}, Cost:ManaCost } } ] }.

This combinator handles only the mana-cost form of Ward (e.g. "Ward {2}", "Ward {1}{G}").
