The life-cost and sacrifice-cost forms are handled by the existing `WardKeywordRule` static rule (Priority 989), which is reached for standalone clauses when the KeywordListRule does not consume the full clause. Both produce the same TriggeredAbility shape.

MAST Priority: `Parameterized` — must be tried after all Simple keywords in the Or-chain so a bare keyword word "ward" doesn't mask the parameterized "ward {cost}" form (KeywordRegistry builds Simple.Try().Or(Parameterized)).

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/WardKeyword.cs)

### `WarpKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Warp [cost]: You may cast this card from your hand for its warp cost. It enters the battlefield tapped. Rule 702.185. An alternative-cast keyword. MAST records the keyword and the warp cost; the alternative-cast and enters-tapped mechanics are engine territory — same approach as Plot (702.170) and Dash (702.109).

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/WarpKeyword.cs)

### `WebSlingingKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Web-slinging [cost]: You may cast this spell by paying [cost] and returning a tapped creature you control to its owner's hand rather than paying its mana cost. Rule 702.188. Scope: mana-cost parameter. The return-a-tapped-creature component of the alt cost is engine territory — MAST records the keyword's presence and cost only, mirroring the Cycling/Evoke pattern. Combinator-only: no matching `KeywordDefinitions` entry exists in the legacy registry.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/WebSlingingKeyword.cs)

### `WitherKeyword` — *sealed class* : IKeyword

Wither: This creature deals damage to creatures in the form of -1/-1 counters. Rule 702.80. MAST records keyword presence; the damage-redirection semantics are engine territory.

[Source](Keywords/Definitions/WitherKeyword.cs)

## `/Parsing/`

### `IAbilityParser` — *interface*

Contract for an ability-kind-specific parser. Each implementation handles one `AbilityKind` and is discovered at startup by `AbilityParserRegistry` via an `OracleAbilityParserAttribute` decoration. Implementations own their own fallback behavior — `Parse` must always return at least one ability node (typically an `UnparsedAbility` on failure) so the orchestrator never needs to special-case missing output.

[Source](Parsing/IAbilityParser.cs)

### `AbilityClassifier` — *sealed class*

Classifies oracle text clauses into ability types based on structural patterns. This pre-classification enables routing to specialized parsers.

[Source](Parsing/AbilityClassifier.cs)

### `AbilityParserRegistry` — *sealed class*

Discovers `IAbilityParser` implementations decorated with `OracleAbilityParserAttribute` and maps each `AbilityKind` to its parser. Discovery runs once on first access and is cached for the process lifetime. Adding a new ability-kind parser means creating a new file with the attribute and the interface implementation; no edits to this registry, to `OracleParser`, or to any other existing file are required. Kinds with no registered parser (today: `Modal`, `Spell`, and the fallback path) resolve to a built-in fallback that produces a generic `UnparsedAbility`.

[Source](Parsing/AbilityParserRegistry.cs)

### `AttributeExtractor` — *sealed partial class*

Extracts card attributes from a CardInputDTO. Handles mana costs, colors, color identity, creature stats, and loyalty.

[Source](Parsing/AttributeExtractor.cs)

### `CardParseMetrics` — *sealed record*

Metrics for card parsing.

[Source](Parsing/CardParser.cs)

### `CardParseResult` — *sealed record*

Result of parsing a complete card.

[Source](Parsing/CardParser.cs)

### `CardParser` — *sealed class*

Main entry point for parsing Magic: The Gathering cards. Orchestrates type line parsing, oracle text parsing, and attribute extraction.

[Source](Parsing/CardParser.cs)

### `ClassLevelClause` — *sealed record*

One pre-grouped class level bar from a Class cluster (CR 716.2). Carries the level number, the raw activation-cost text from the bar (e.g. `"{1}{R}"`), and the ability sub-clauses printed in that bar's text-box section. The parser converts these into a `ClassLevel` AST node.

[Source](Parsing/ClauseSplitter.cs)

### `ClauseClassification` — *sealed record*

Classification result for an oracle clause.

[Source](Parsing/AbilityClassifier.cs)

### `ClauseSplitter` — *sealed class*

Splits oracle text into individual ability clauses. Handles paragraph breaks, modal structures, level/chapter markers, and loyalty abilities.

[Source](Parsing/ClauseSplitter.cs)

### `LevelStanzaClause` — *sealed record*

One pre-grouped LEVEL N-M stanza from a level-up cluster. Carries the raw P/T strings and the inner-ability sub-clauses; the parser converts these into `LevelStanza` AST nodes.

[Source](Parsing/ClauseSplitter.cs)

### `ManaCostParser` — *sealed partial class*

Parses mana cost strings into a list of ManaSymbol objects. Handles all standard MTG mana symbol formats: - Basic: {W}, {U}, {B}, {R}, {G} - Colorless: {C} - Generic: {0}, {1}, {2}, ..., {16}, etc. - Variable: {X}, {Y}, {Z} - Hybrid: {W/U}, {B/G}, etc. - Hybrid generic: {2/W}, {2/U}, etc. - Phyrexian: {W/P}, {U/P}, {B/P}, {R/P}, {G/P} - Phyrexian hybrid: {W/U/P}, {G/W/P}, etc. - Snow: {S}

[Source](Parsing/ManaCostParser.cs)

### `OracleAbilityParserAttribute` — *sealed class* : Attribute

Marks a class as the parser for a specific `AbilityKind`. Discovered at startup by `AbilityParserRegistry`. The tagged class must implement `IAbilityParser` and have a public parameterless constructor.

[Source](Parsing/OracleAbilityParserAttribute.cs)

### `OracleClause` — *sealed record*

Represents a clause (ability segment) extracted from oracle text. Each clause typically represents a single ability.

[Source](Parsing/ClauseSplitter.cs)

### `OracleParser` — *sealed class*

Main orchestrator for parsing Magic: The Gathering oracle text. Coordinates the tokenizer, clause splitter, classifier, and the reflection-discovered registry of `IAbilityParser` implementations.

[Source](Parsing/OracleParser.cs)

### `ResultsTableRowClause` — *sealed record*

One pre-grouped row of a die-roll results table (CR 706.3): the inclusive numeric range and the raw effect body text. The triggered-ability parser dispatches `BodyText` through its effect rules and pairs the resulting effects with the range to build a `ResultsTableRow` AST node.

[Source](Parsing/ClauseSplitter.cs)

### `TypeLineParser` — *sealed class*

Parses a card's type line into its structural components. Type lines follow the format: "[Supertypes] [Types] — [Subtypes]" Examples: - "Creature — Elf Druid" → types: [Creature], subtypes: [Elf, Druid] - "Legendary Creature — Squirrel Warrior" → supertypes: [Legendary], types: [Creature], subtypes: [Squirrel, Warrior] - "Artifact" → types: [Artifact] - "Basic Land — Forest" → supertypes: [Basic], types: [Land], subtypes: [Forest] - "Legendary Planeswalker — Daretti" → supertypes: [Legendary], types: [Planeswalker], subtypes: [Daretti]

[Source](Parsing/TypeLineParser.cs)

## `/Parsing/Combinators/`

### `OracleParsers` — *static class*

Keyword-ability parser combinators for Magic: The Gathering oracle text.

As of Phase-2 Stage C this type is a thin facade over `KeywordRegistry`: the per-keyword combinators and the `SimpleKeyword` / `ParameterizedKeyword` Or-chains that used to live here have moved to one-file-per-keyword `IKeyword` implementations under `Keywords/Definitions/`, discovered by the registry. The two members below preserve the public call shape (`OracleParsers.KeywordList(tokens)` from `StaticAbilityParser`) while delegating the actual recognition to the registry.

[Source](Parsing/Combinators/OracleParsers.cs)

## `/Parsing/Parsers/`

### `IPrioritizedRuleAttribute` — *interface*

Contract for an attribute that marks a reflection-discovered rule and carries its intra-tier dispatch priority. Shared by every registry-style parser family (spell rules, triggered rules, keywords, …) so a single generic discovery helper (`RuleRegistry`) can rank decorated types without knowing the concrete attribute.

<b>Priority convention (range 0–100, default 50, higher = tried first):</b> higher-priority rules are dispatched before lower-priority siblings. Each rule family documents its own band convention on its concrete attribute; the shared invariant is only that a larger number wins ties by sorting earlier.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/IPrioritizedRuleAttribute.cs)

### `ActivatedAbilityParser` — *sealed partial class* : IAbilityParser

Parses activated abilities of the form "[Cost]: [Effect.]" Handles: - Mana abilities: {T}: Add {G}. - Complex activated abilities: {3}{B}{B}: Creatures you control gain lifelink until end of turn. - Loyalty abilities: +2: Discard up to two cards, then draw that many cards.

- **Ability-parser registration, kind:** `AbilityKind.Activated`

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/ActivatedAbilityParser.cs)

### `ClassAbilityParser` — *sealed class* : IAbilityParser

Parses Class clusters (CR 716, "Class Cards"; AFR). Consumes a Class cluster head clause (one that `ClauseSplitter` has pre-grouped with its base abilities on `ClassBaseAbilities` and its level bars on `ClassLevels`), then dispatches each base/granted ability body through the registry and converts each level bar's raw cost text into a `Cost`.

- **Ability-parser registration, kind:** `AbilityKind.Class`

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/ClassAbilityParser.cs)

### `FallbackParser` — *sealed class* : IAbilityParser

Fallback parser that always succeeds by producing an UnparsedAbility. This ensures the parsing pipeline never fails completely. Registered for `Unparsed` in the `AbilityParserRegistry`. Also invoked internally by the other concrete parsers when their `TryParse` step fails.

- **Ability-parser registration, kind:** `AbilityKind.Unparsed`

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/FallbackParser.cs)

### `LevelUpAbilityParser` — *sealed class* : IAbilityParser

Parses Level Up clusters (Rule 711). Consumes a level-up cost clause (one that `ClauseSplitter` has pre-grouped with its LEVEL stanzas on `LevelUpStanzas`), then constructs the cost activated ability + the stanza records.

- **Ability-parser registration, kind:** `AbilityKind.LevelUp`

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/LevelUpAbilityParser.cs)

### `ModalAbilityParser` — *sealed class* : IAbilityParser

Parser for modal abilities ("Choose one —", "Choose two —", "Choose one or both —"). The clause splitter attaches each option as a child `OracleClause` on `ModalOptions`; this parser interprets the header text to derive a `ModeSelection` and dispatches each option clause back through the classifier+registry to parse the option body.

Also handles the commander-conditional mode-expansion pattern: "Choose one. If you control a commander as you cast this spell, you may choose both instead." — a `ModeSelection` with base `ChooseOne` and a `ModeSelectionOverride` whose condition is a `CountCondition` filtering Commander-supertype creatures you control. CR 903 (Commander format), MAST describes the condition as written.

- **Ability-parser registration, kind:** `AbilityKind.Modal`

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/ModalAbilityParser.cs)

### `RuleRegistry` — *static class*

Generic reflection-based rule discovery, shared by every ability parser that dispatches over a priority-ordered set of one-file-per-rule implementations. Each parser is a thin dispatcher over `Discover{TRule, TAttr}`; adding a new shape is dropping a new `[TAttr]`-decorated `TRule` file with no edits to any shared file — which is what keeps the rule directories free of merge conflicts under parallel batch dispatch.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/RuleRegistry.cs)

### `SagaAbilityParser` — *sealed class* : IAbilityParser

Parses Saga chapter structures (Rule 715). Consumes a saga-preamble clause (one that `ClauseSplitter` has pre-grouped with its chapter bodies on `SagaChapters`), then dispatches each chapter body through the registry so individual chapters land as whatever ability shape best matches their text.

- **Ability-parser registration, kind:** `AbilityKind.Saga`

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/SagaAbilityParser.cs)

### `SpellAbilityParser` — *sealed class* : IAbilityParser

Dispatches spell-ability oracle-text clauses to the priority-ordered set of `ISpellRule` implementations discovered by reflection at construction time. Each rule lives in its own file under `Parsers/Spell/Rules/` and is decorated with `SpellRuleAttribute` (see attribute docs for priority convention). Adding a new shape means dropping a new file in `Rules/` with no edits to any shared file.

- **Ability-parser registration, kind:** `AbilityKind.Spell`

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/SpellAbilityParser.cs)

### `StaticAbilityParser` — *sealed class* : IAbilityParser

Dispatches static-ability oracle-text clauses to the priority-ordered set of `IStaticRule` implementations discovered by reflection at construction time. Each rule lives in its own file under `Parsers/Static/Rules/` and is decorated with `StaticRuleAttribute` (see attribute docs for the order-preserving priority convention). Adding a new shape means dropping a new file in `Rules/` with no edits to any shared file.

- **Ability-parser registration, kind:** `AbilityKind.Static`

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/StaticAbilityParser.cs)

### `TriggeredAbilityParser` — *sealed class* : IAbilityParser

Parser for triggered abilities: "When/Whenever/At [trigger], [effect]" Supports multiple trigger events and effect types using compositional parsing.

- **Ability-parser registration, kind:** `AbilityKind.Triggered`

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/TriggeredAbilityParser.cs)

## `/Parsing/Parsers/Activated/`

### `IActivatedCostRule` — *interface*

One activated-ability cost-component recognizer. Dispatched by `ActivatedAbilityParser` in descending `Priority` order over each comma-separated cost component; the first non-null result wins. Each rule self-guards and returns `null` when it doesn't recognise the component.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/IActivatedCostRule.cs)

### `IActivatedEffectRule` — *interface*

One activated-ability effect recognizer. Dispatched by `ActivatedAbilityParser` in descending `Priority` order, then ordinal name for tie-breaking; the first non-null result wins. `effectText` is the post-colon effect fragment (a single sentence when reached via the multi-sentence pre-pass). Each rule self-guards and returns `null` when it doesn't recognise the text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/IActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` — *interface*

Extension of `IActivatedEffectRule` for activated-ability effect shapes that expand to a flat list of sibling effects on `Effects` rather than a single `Effect`. Implement this alongside `IActivatedEffectRule` (returning `null` from `TryMatch` so the single-effect path never fires) when a single oracle sentence joins two effects with ", then" and should be represented as a flat array — e.g. Sensei's Divining Top's "Draw a card, then put this artifact on top of its owner's library."

This mirrors `IMultiSpellRule`: not every ", then" is a join (some are a single effect's disposition, such as "look at the top three cards, then put them back in any order"), so the decision belongs to the rule that recognizes the whole sentence, not a generic dispatcher split.

Discovery: `ActivatedAbilityParser` picks this up automatically for any `ActivatedEffectRuleAttribute`-decorated class that also implements this interface, trying the multi-effect path before the single-effect path.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/IMultiActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `ActivatedCostRuleAttribute` — *sealed class* : Attribute, MagicAST.Parsing.Parsers.IPrioritizedRuleAttribute

Marks an `IActivatedCostRule` implementation for reflection-based discovery by `ActivatedAbilityParser`. Priorities are migrated order-preserving from the legacy `ParseCosts` chain as `Priority = 1000 - (chain index)`. See `IPrioritizedRuleAttribute` for the shared priority contract (higher = more specific = tried first).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/ActivatedCostRuleAttribute.cs)

### `ActivatedEffectRuleAttribute` — *sealed class* : Attribute, MagicAST.Parsing.Parsers.IPrioritizedRuleAttribute

Marks an `IActivatedEffectRule` implementation for reflection-based discovery by `ActivatedAbilityParser`. Priorities are migrated order-preserving from the legacy `ParseEffects` chain as `Priority = 1000 - (chain index)`, so an extracted rule keeps the exact relative dispatch order it had as an inline branch. See `IPrioritizedRuleAttribute` for the shared priority contract (higher = more specific = tried first).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/ActivatedEffectRuleAttribute.cs)

### `ActivatedRuleHelpers` — *static class*

Shared utilities used across `IActivatedEffectRule` and `IActivatedCostRule` implementations.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/ActivatedRuleHelpers.cs)

## `/Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/`

### `ActivateLoyaltyAbilityAsThoughEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"For each planeswalker you control, you may activate one of its loyalty abilities once this turn as though none of its loyalty abilities have been activated this turn."

CR 606.3: the once-per-turn restriction on loyalty-ability activation. This activated-effect rule recognises the Chain Veil family: a per-planeswalker permission to activate a loyalty ability once this turn, ignoring the once-per-turn restriction (the "as though none … have been activated" clause).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the surface phrase "loyalty abilities" could appear inside other ability text; anchoring prevents this rule from matching a substring of a broader effect. Priority 985 — specific enough to precede generic effects.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ActivateLoyaltyAbilityAsThoughEffectRule.cs)

### `AdaptEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Adapt N" — e.g. "Adapt 2" (CR 701.46a: "\"Adapt N\" means \"If this permanent has no +1/+1 counters on it, put N +1/+1 counters on it.\"") The trailing parenthetical reminder is stripped by the caller before this rule is invoked.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AdaptEffectRule.cs)

### `AddFixedManaWithSpendRestrictionEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Add [fixed mana symbols]. Spend this mana only to [restriction]." — Dalakos, Crafter of Wonders: "{T}: Add {C}{C}. Spend this mana only to cast artifact spells or activate abilities of artifacts."

CR 605.1a: "An activated ability is a mana ability if it meets all of the following criteria: it doesn't require a target (see rule 115.6), it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves, and it's not a loyalty ability." The enclosing "{T}: Add …" ability is a mana ability. CR 106.4: "When an effect instructs a player to add mana, that mana goes into a player's mana pool." — a spend restriction on that mana (Rule 106.5 governs restricted mana) does not change that.

Sibling to `AddManaEffectRule`'s "Add one mana of any color[. Spend this mana only to &lt;X&gt;]" arm (Unclaimed Territory): that arm requires the free-choice-of-color shape ("one mana of any color"), never fixed mana symbols. `AddManaEffectRule` explicitly BAILS (returns null) on any mana text containing "spend this mana only" that it does not itself recognise (its `UnmodeledManaClause` guard), so this rule — matching the FIXED- mana-symbols shape that guard declines — cannot shadow or be shadowed by it; dispatch order between the two is immaterial (a new, disjoint file rather than an edit to that shared rule body).

The restriction clause is captured verbatim into `SpendRestriction` (its own doc: "MAST describes; it does not execute — this holds the restriction text verbatim"), mirroring Unclaimed Territory's shape exactly, just with a fixed `Mana` symbol string instead of `AnyColor`.

Anchored (^…$) pattern requiring the literal "Add " lead-in, one-or-more curly- brace mana symbols, then the literal "Spend this mana only to " tail — so it cannot match any other effect shape as a substring.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AddFixedManaWithSpendRestrictionEffectRule.cs)

### `AddManaAnyColorAmongEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Add one mana of any color among [filter] you control." — the Mox Amber shape.

This rule handles the "one mana of any color among [filter]" family where the controller may add one mana of freely-chosen color, but that color must be present among a specific set of permanents they control. The canonical example is Mox Amber: "Add one mana of any color among legendary creatures and planeswalkers you control."

Distinct from `AddManaForEachColorAmongControlledPermanentsEffectRule` (Bloom Tender — adds one mana per EACH distinct color present) and from `AddManaEffectRule`'s "one mana of any color" branch (unconstrained — any of the five colors). Here the color is freely chosen but constrained to those present among the filter'd permanents.

CR 605.1a: "An activated ability is a mana ability if it meets all of the following criteria: it doesn't require a target (see rule 115.6), it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves, and it's not a loyalty ability." The "legendary creatures and planeswalkers you control" filter is not a target (CR 115.6); the ability satisfies all three criteria.

Runs at Priority = 1040 — above `AddManaForEachColorAmongControlledPermanentsEffectRule` (1030) and `AddManaEffectRule` (1000) so the "any color among" shape wins before the per-color loop or the unconstrained "any color" match. The regex is anchored at both ends (^…$) so it cannot match as a substring of a more-specific sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AddManaAnyColorAmongEffectRule.cs)

### `AddManaAnyColorProducibleByEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Add one mana of any color that a land an opponent controls could produce." — the Exotic Orchard / Fellwar Stone shape. The produced mana is ONE unit of a freely-chosen color, but the chosen color is constrained to the colors of mana that lands the opponent controls <i>could produce</i> (their mana- production capability), not the colors of those lands as objects.

CR 106.7 (verbatim, which names this exact card): "Some abilities produce mana based on the type of mana another permanent or permanents 'could produce.' The type of mana a permanent could produce at any time includes any type of mana that an ability of that permanent would produce if the ability were to resolve at that time… Example: Exotic Orchard has the ability '{T}: Add one mana of any color that a land an opponent controls could produce.'"

Modelled with `AnyColorProducibleBy` carrying the `ObjectFilter` for the constraining permanents (`CardTypes=["land"], Controller=Opponent, Zone=Battlefield`), with `Mana` left `""` because the color is chosen at resolution. This is DISTINCT from `AddManaAnyColorAmongEffectRule` (Mox Amber: color present among the permanents' own colors) — a Plains produces {W} but is colorless as a permanent, so "could produce" ≠ "color among".

CR 605.1a: "An activated ability is a mana ability if it meets all of the following criteria: it doesn't require a target (see rule 115.6), it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves, and it's not a loyalty ability." The "a land an opponent controls" phrase is not a target (CR 115.6); the enclosing "{T}: Add …" ability satisfies all three criteria, so it carries `IsManaAbility = true`.

Runs at Priority = 1045 — above `AddManaEffectRule` (1000). The regex is anchored at both ends (^…$) so it can only match the whole effect string, never a substring of a more-specific sibling. The controller phrase is captured so the naturally-related "a land you control could produce" variant of this same mechanic maps to `You` without a second rule; the "type" (colorless-inclusive) variant is intentionally out of scope.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AddManaAnyColorProducibleByEffectRule.cs)

### `AddManaEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Add {mana}" — e.g. "Add {G}", "Add {C}{C}{C}", "Add {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}". Also handles "Add one mana of any color" (Crystal Grotto / Chromatic Lantern shape) where the produced mana is a single choice across all five colors, and "Add one mana of the chosen color" (Coldsteel Heart / Shimmerdrift Vale / Thriving lands) where the produced mana's color is the color chosen as this permanent entered — the consumer side of a CR 607 linked "choose a color".

Per CR 605.1a — "An activated ability is a mana ability if it meets all of the following criteria: it doesn't require a target (see rule 115.6), it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves, and it's not a loyalty ability." — the enclosing "{T}: Add ..." ability is a mana ability; the chosen-color back- reference does not introduce a target.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AddManaEffectRule.cs)

### `AddManaForEachColorAmongControlledPermanentsEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

S10 — "For each color among permanents you control, add one mana of that color." (Bloom Tender / Vivid ability-word shape, Eventide).

The effect produces one mana of each distinct color present among the controller's permanents on the battlefield — a per-color loop rather than a fixed symbol or a "choose one" free pick. This is modelled with `ForEachColorAmong` carrying an `ObjectFilter` for controller-scoped permanents, and `Mana` left as `""` because the colors are determined at resolution. The outer ability carries `IsManaAbility = true` (CR 605.1a: no target, could add mana, not loyalty).

CR 207.2c: "Vivid" is an ability word — it appears in italics before the em-dash and has no special rules meaning. The classifier strips the "Vivid — " prefix so this rule receives only the post-colon effect text.

CR 605.1a: "An activated ability is a mana ability if it meets all of the following criteria: it doesn't require a target (see rule 115.6), it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves, and it's not a loyalty ability." The "permanents you control" filter is not a target (CR 115.6); the ability satisfies all three criteria.

Runs at Priority = 1030 — above `AddManaForEachControlledCreatureEffectRule` (1020) and `AddManaForEachControlledSubtypeEffectRule` (1010) so the color-loop shape wins before any "Add {mana} for each …" shape in `AddManaEffectRule`. The regex is anchored at both ends (^…$) so it cannot match as a substring of a more-specific sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AddManaForEachColorAmongControlledPermanentsEffectRule.cs)

### `AddManaForEachControlledCreatureEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

S8 — "Add {mana} for each creature you control." (Circle of Dreams Druid and similar). Counts every creature the ability's controller controls on the battlefield — no subtype restriction, card-type filter only.

CR 605.1a: "An activated ability is a mana ability if it meets all of the following criteria: it doesn't require a target (see rule 115.6), it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves, and it's not a loyalty ability." — the enclosing "{T}: Add … you control" ability is a mana ability; the controller filter does not introduce a target.

CR 122/quantity 'for each': the count is a `CountQuantity` over an `ObjectFilter` with `CardTypes=["creature"]`, `Controller=`You``, `Zone=`Battlefield``.

Runs at Priority = 1020 (higher than `AddManaForEachControlledSubtypeEffectRule`'s 1010) so the card-type "creature" shape is tried before the subtype match — the regex is anchored at both ends so there is no substring-overlap risk with the subtype rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AddManaForEachControlledCreatureEffectRule.cs)

### `AddManaForEachControlledSubtypeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

S7 — "{mana} for each [Subtype] you control" (Elvish Archdruid and similar). Counts only permanents of the named creature subtype controlled by the ability's controller — a controller-scoped variant of S6 (Priest of Titania's "on the battlefield", which counts ALL permanents of the subtype regardless of controller).

CR 605.1a: "An activated ability is a mana ability if it meets all of the following criteria: it doesn't require a target (see rule 115.6), it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves, and it's not a loyalty ability." — the enclosing "{T}: Add … you control" ability is a mana ability; the controller filter does not introduce a target.

Runs at Priority = 1010 (higher than `AddManaEffectRule`'s 1000) so the more-specific "you control" shape wins before the general bail on "for each" in `AddManaEffectRule` is reached.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AddManaForEachControlledSubtypeEffectRule.cs)

### `AddManaXCountDefenderCreaturesEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Add X mana in any combination of colors, where X is the number of creatures you control with defender." — Axebane Guardian's mana ability.

The X is NOT a cost variable (CR 107.3): it is defined inline by the "where X is …" clause as the count of defender creatures the controller controls. MAST records this as a `CountQuantity` over an `ObjectFilter` with `CardTypes=["creature"]`, `Controller=`You``, `Zone=`Battlefield``, and `Characteristics=[KeywordCharacteristic{Defender}]`. Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): MAST names the quantity; the engine evaluates it at resolution time.

The mana produced is X units, freely distributed across any combination of the five colors (`AnyCombinationOf` = `["W","U","B","R","G"]`). Per CR 106.4: "When an effect instructs a player to add mana, that mana goes into a player's mana pool."

Defender is a static ability (CR 702.3a: "Defender is a static ability."; CR 702.3b: "A creature with defender can't attack."). A creature with defender in the filter is expressed as `Characteristics=[KeywordCharacteristic{Defender}]` — the structured `KeywordCharacteristic` rather than an `OtherCharacteristic` residual, because Defender is a first-class `KeywordAbility` enum value.

Per CR 605.1a — "An activated ability is a mana ability if it meets all of the following criteria: it doesn't require a target (see rule 115.6), it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves, and it's not a loyalty ability." — the enclosing `{T}:` ability IS a mana ability; the controller filter does not introduce a target.

Runs at Priority = 1003 (above `AddManaXGreatestPowerEffectRule`'s 1002 and `AddManaEffectRule`'s 1000) so the Axebane Guardian "where X is the number of creatures … with defender" shape is claimed before any more-general rule in the family.

The rule is anchored (`^…$`) to prevent a substring match against a more-specific sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AddManaXCountDefenderCreaturesEffectRule.cs)

### `AddManaXGreatestPowerEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Add X mana in any combination of colors, where X is the greatest power among creatures you control." — Selvala, Heart of the Wilds mana ability.

The X here is NOT a cost variable (CR 107.3): it is defined inline by the "where X is …" clause as the current greatest power among creatures the controller controls. MAST records this as a `CalculatedQuantity` with `Expression` = `"greatest power among creatures you control"` — a game-state query (the maximum over a set of power values) with no structured analog in the existing quantity hierarchy. Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): MAST names the quantity; the engine evaluates it.

The mana produced is X units, freely distributed across any combination of the five colors (`AnyCombinationOf` = `["W","U","B","R","G"]`). Per CR 106.4: "When an effect instructs a player to add mana, that mana goes into a player's mana pool."

Per CR 605.1a — "An activated ability is a mana ability if it meets all of the following criteria: it doesn't require a target, it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves, and it's not a loyalty ability." — the enclosing `{G}, {T}:` ability IS a mana ability; the enclosing parser derives `IsManaAbility = true`.

Runs at Priority = 1002 (above `AddManaXOnePlusManaValueEffectRule`'s 1001 and `AddManaEffectRule`'s 1000) so the Selvala "where X is …" shape is claimed before the base rule's `UnmodeledManaClause` bail (or the S3 `AnyCombination` regex's partial match of the "X mana in any combination of colors" prefix).

The rule is anchored (`^…$`) to prevent a substring match against a more-specific sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AddManaXGreatestPowerEffectRule.cs)

### `AddManaXOnePlusManaValueEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Add X mana of any one color, where X is 1 plus the exiled creature's mana value. Spend this mana only to cast creature spells." — Food Chain's exile-creature mana production with a spend restriction.

The X quantity is a derived calculation: 1 plus the exiled creature's mana value. MAST models this as a `CalculatedQuantity` whose `BaseQuantity` is a `DerivedQuantity` keyed on `ManaValue` with `Source = "exiled creature"` (reference-not-resolution per ADR 0004 — MAST names the source object, it does not thread the runtime value). `Operation = "add"`, `Operand = 1`.

The spend restriction ("Spend this mana only to cast creature spells") is captured verbatim in `SpendRestriction` per the existing MAST doctrine: MAST describes, does not execute; the restriction text is the engine's domain, not the AST's.

Per CR 605.1a — "An activated ability is a mana ability if it meets all of the following criteria: it doesn't require a target, it could add mana to a player's mana pool when it resolves, and it's not a loyalty ability." — this ability is a mana ability despite its spend restriction (a spend restriction does not make an ability non-mana; cf. Unclaimed Territory, Secluded Courtyard).

This rule fires at Priority 1001 (above the existing `AddManaEffectRule`'s 1000) so it claims the Food Chain combined string before the base rule's `UnmodeledManaClause` bail would swallow it.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AddManaXOnePlusManaValueEffectRule.cs)

### `AdditionalCombatAndMainPhaseEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"After this main phase, there is an additional combat phase followed by an additional main phase." — inserts a combat phase and main phase into the current turn's timeline.

CR 500.7 (verbatim): "Some spells and abilities can add phases to a player's turn. They do this by adding the phases directly after the specified phase. If two effects add phases to a player's turn, the most recently created one is added first."

Emits an `AdditionalCombatAndMainPhaseEffect` (a parameterless marker — the insertion point "after this main phase" and the specific phases inserted are fixed by the oracle text and need no parameters, just as SkipUntapEffect is parameterless).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AdditionalCombatAndMainPhaseEffectRule.cs)

### `AdditionalCombatPhaseEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"After this phase, there is an additional combat phase." — inserts a single additional combat phase into the current turn without an accompanying main phase.

Distinct from `AdditionalCombatAndMainPhaseEffectRule`, which handles "After this main phase, there is an additional combat phase followed by an additional main phase." (Aggravated Assault). Godo, Bandit Warlord's trigger says only "After this phase, there is an additional combat phase." — no additional main phase, and "this phase" rather than "this main phase".

CR 506: The combat phase. CR 500.1: turn structure. The insertion point ("after this phase") and the single inserted phase (combat) are the full printed content; engine phase-order bookkeeping (CR 505.1a) is not encoded here.

Priority 990 — above `AdditionalCombatAndMainPhaseEffectRule` (Priority 991) so the more-specific single-phase form is tried first. Both are anchored (^...$), so they cannot cross-match.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AdditionalCombatPhaseEffectRule.cs)

### `AnimateEnchantedBasicLandWithGrantedActivatedAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Until end of turn, enchanted [BasicLandType] becomes a [P/T] [colors] [subtype] creature with "[quoted activated ability]." It's still a land." — the Kamigawa "Genju" cycle's animate line. A variant of the Keyrune/manland "becomes a creature" template (`BecomesCreatureEffectRule`) that differs in two ways the shared rule doesn't cover:

The subject is "enchanted [BasicLandType]" (the Aura's attached permanent, CR 303.4c / 702.5) rather than "This [type]" (the source itself). The granted ability is a full quoted ACTIVATED ability ("{B}: This creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn.") rather than a single keyword word (flying, trample, reach) — CR 113.6 / 607.

The quoted ability is parsed into a real `ActivatedAbility` node, mirroring how a top-level "{cost}: [effect]" ability parses (e.g. Gateway Shade's "{B}: This creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn." → Costs=[mana B], Effects=[modifyPT Self +1/+1 untilEndOfTurn]) — the same structured shape, just nested under `GainedAbilities` instead of at the ability list's top level. This keeps the granted ability fully structured (no free text) rather than a residual string.

Canonical card: Genju of the Fens (DIS) — "{2}: Until end of turn, enchanted Swamp becomes a 2/2 black Spirit creature with "{B}: This creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn." It's still a land." Quote characters are accepted as either straight (") or curly (“ ”) — oracle text sources vary — and the apostrophe in "It's" as either straight (') or curly (’).

Priority 990 — above `BecomesCreatureEffectRule` (985), so this more specific "enchanted [BasicLandType] ... with "[quoted ability]"" shape is tried first; the shared rule's "This [type] becomes..." patterns don't match this subject/granted-ability shape anyway (no collision).

Rule 205.1b (retained card type on a "still a [type]" animate); Rule 305.7 (an animated land keeps its land types); Rule 208 (power/toughness); Rule 113.6 / 607 (granting an ability); Rule 611 (continuous effects).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AnimateEnchantedBasicLandWithGrantedActivatedAbilityRule.cs)

### `AnimateTargetNoncreatureArtifactByManaValueRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Until your next turn, up to one target noncreature artifact becomes an artifact creature with power and toughness each equal to its mana value." — Karn, the Great Creator's +1 loyalty ability. A duration-bounded continuous effect (CR 611.1) that makes the chosen artifact into an artifact creature whose P/T box equals its own mana value (CR 202.3 / CR 208).

Modelled as a `BecomesCreatureEffect` with:

`Subject` — `Target` reference to "up to one … noncreature artifact" (quantity `UpTo 1`, CardTypes ["artifact"], ExcludedCardTypes ["creature"]). `Power` / `Toughness` — `DerivedQuantity` (`ManaValue`) for "each equal to its mana value". `Colors` — empty (no color change stated). `CardTypes` — `["artifact","creature"]` (additive, per CR 205.1b). `AddedSubtypes` — empty (no creature subtype stated). `GainedAbilities` — empty (no keyword granted). `Duration` — `YourNextTurn`.

"Up to one" is modelled as `Quantity = UpToQuantity { Maximum = 1 }` on the `ObjectReference`, not an `OptionalEffect` wrapper (CR 117.3a: "up to X" targets means 0–X are chosen at targeting time, which is a cardinality constraint, not an optionality on the one-shot action).

The pattern is anchored (^…$) to prevent substring collision with other "becomes … creature" animate rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AnimateTargetNoncreatureArtifactByManaValueRule.cs)

### `AnyNumberOfTargetPlayersMillEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability mill keyword action targeting any number of players. CR 701.17a: "For a player to mill a number of cards, that player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard." Handles two oracle forms: "Any number of target players each mill N cards." → Count: LiteralQuantity(N), Player: Target+player+AnyAmount "Any number of target players each mill cards equal to the number of cards in their graveyard." → Count: CountQuantity(cards in target player's graveyard), Player: Target+player+AnyAmount ANCHOR: Both patterns are anchored (^...$) to prevent matching substrings of more-specific sibling effects. For the singular "Target player mills N cards" form see `MillTargetPlayerEffectRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AnyNumberOfTargetPlayersMillEffectRule.cs)

### `AttachThisToTargetEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Attach this [Equipment|Aura|Fortification] to target [type] [you control|an opponent controls]." — an explicit activated-ability re-attach instruction, distinct from the Equip/Fortify/Reconfigure keyword abilities (Rule 701.3: "To take an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification from where it currently is and put it onto a specified object or player.").

Paradigm card: Bloodthirsty Blade — "{1}: Attach this Equipment to target creature an opponent controls. Activate only as a sorcery." The "Activate only as a sorcery" restriction sentence is stripped by `ActivatedAbilityParser`'s shared restriction pre-pass before this rule ever sees the text.

Anchored (^…$) so it only recognises the bare "Attach this [type] to target [filter]." sentence, not compound effect text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/AttachThisToTargetEffectRule.cs)

### `BecomeMonarchEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target player becomes the monarch." — Rule 716 monarch designation granted to a chosen player.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/BecomeMonarchEffectRule.cs)

### `BecomesChosenCreatureTypeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This [permanent] becomes the creature type of your choice [until end of turn]." — the Mistform "shapeshift" template. Emits a single `ChangeSubtypeEffect` whose new subtype is player-chosen (`CreatureType`) rather than literal.

This is one layer-4 type-changing continuous effect (CR 613.1d: "Layer 4: Type-changing effects are applied. These include effects that change an object's card type, subtype, and/or supertype."). It <em>sets</em> the creature's creature type, replacing its existing creature types (CR 205.1a: "when an effect sets one or more of an object's subtypes, the new subtype(s) replaces any existing subtypes from the appropriate set (creature types, land types, …)"). The chosen value must be a single creature type per CR 205.3 ("'Merfolk' or 'Wizard' is acceptable, but 'Merfolk Wizard' is not. Words like 'artifact,' 'opponent,' 'Swamp,' or 'truck' can't be chosen because they aren't creature types.").

The permanent stays a creature and only its creature type changes, so this is a subtype-set effect and not a `BecomesCreatureEffect` (which adds the creature card type). The "of your choice" is a fresh on-resolution choice, so it is modeled on the effect itself, not via the back-referencing `ChosenCharacteristic` filter.

Examples:

Mistform Stalker — "{1}: This creature becomes the creature type of your choice until end of turn." Mistform Dreamer — same activated line.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/BecomesChosenCreatureTypeEffectRule.cs)

### `BecomesCopyEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This [permanent] becomes a copy of target [filter] until end of turn." — the Shifting Woodland delirium template. Emits a single `BecomesCopyEffect` describing the source permanent becoming a copy of the targeted object.

This is a layer-1 copy effect (CR 707.6: "Some effects cause a permanent that's copying a permanent to copy a different object while remaining on the battlefield") — the source stays on the battlefield and takes on the copiable values of the target. Distinct from `CreateCopyTokenWithModificationsEffectRule`, which <em>creates a new token</em> that is a copy.

CR 207.2c (verbatim): "Delirium" is listed as an ability word — the em-dash prefix is mechanically inert and is stripped by `ActivatedAbilityParser` before this rule fires. The `AbilityWord` field on the emitted `ActivatedAbility` is populated by the classifier, not here.

Anchored (^…$) to prevent matching inside a more-specific sibling such as `BecomesCreatureEffectRule` — the surface phrase "becomes a copy of" cannot appear inside a "becomes a [P/T] … creature" animate spec. The guard is belt-and-suspenders: the two patterns are structurally disjoint ("copy of target" vs. a P/T box), but explicit anchoring is the project standard.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/BecomesCopyEffectRule.cs)

### `BecomesCreatureEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This [permanent] becomes a [P/T] [colors] [subtype] [card types] creature with [keyword] until end of turn." — the Keyrune/Monument "animate" template. Emits a single `BecomesCreatureEffect` describing the full set of characteristics the source permanent takes on for the duration.

There is no keyword <em>action</em> for "becomes a creature"; this is one continuous effect (CR 611.1 — "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects ... for a fixed or indefinite period.") that sets card types/subtypes (CR 205), power/toughness (CR 208), colors (CR 105), and grants a keyword ability (CR 113.6). Layer/timestamp ordering (CR 613) is engine territory and is not modeled.

<b>Word order.</b> The Keyrune/Monument form puts the duration LAST ("...with flying until end of turn"). The "manland" animate (Stirring Wildwood, Restless Vents) puts it FIRST ("Until end of turn, this land becomes a 3/4 ... creature with reach"). Both are the same continuous effect; the rule accepts either word order and normalizes to `Duration: untilEndOfTurn`.

<b>"It's still a [type]" retention.</b> Per CR 205.1b — "Some effects change an object's card type, supertype, or subtype but specify that the object retains a prior card type ... This rule applies to effects that ... state that something is 'still a [type...]'" — the animate is ADDITIVE: the source keeps its prior card type and gains `creature`. CR 305.7 says setting/animating a land "doesn't add or remove any card types ... it keeps its land types". So for the manlands the retained `land` card type sits ahead of the added `creature` in `CardTypes`. The retained type is derived from the subject noun ("this <b>land</b> becomes..."); the trailing reminder sentence "It's still a land." is consumed as confirmation, NOT emitted as a separate effect.

Examples:

Azorius Keyrune — "This artifact becomes a 2/2 white and blue Bird artifact creature with flying until end of turn." Gruul Keyrune — "This artifact becomes a 3/2 red and green Beast artifact creature with trample until end of turn." Stirring Wildwood — "Until end of turn, this land becomes a 3/4 green and white Elemental creature with reach. It's still a land." → CardTypes ["land","creature"]. Restless Vents — "Until end of turn, this land becomes a 2/3 black and red Insect creature with menace. It's still a land."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/BecomesCreatureEffectRule.cs)

### `BecomesTreasureArtifactEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

"Target creature becomes a Treasure artifact with &quot;{T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Add one mana of any color&quot; and loses all other card types and abilities." — Vraska, Betrayal's Sting's −2 loyalty ability.

A single continuous-effect sentence that applies four simultaneous layer-4 changes (CR 613.1d) and a layer-6 ability grant (CR 613.1f) to the target creature:

`SetCardTypesEffect` — sets the target's card types to `["artifact"]`, implementing "becomes … artifact … and loses all other card types". `ChangeSubtypeEffect` — sets the target's artifact subtypes to `["Treasure"]`, implementing "becomes a Treasure …". `GainAbilityEffect` — grants the Treasure mana ability `{T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Add one mana of any color` as a nested `ActivatedAbility`. `LoseAbilityEffect` — the "loses all other … abilities" clause, carrying the AbilityText residual `"all other abilities"`.

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the phrase "becomes a Treasure artifact" does not recur as a substring of any other sibling rule, but anchoring prevents future broad patterns from consuming it silently.

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the four effects sit as flat siblings on `Effects`. `TryMatch` always returns null.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/BecomesTreasureArtifactEffectRule.cs)

### `CantAttackThisTurnEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability effect shape "target [filter] can't attack this turn." — e.g. Netter en-Dal: "{W}, {T}, Discard a card: Target creature can't attack this turn." CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as \"[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]\"" The cost container ({W}, {T}, Discard a card) is parsed independently; this rule only recognizes the post-colon effect body. CR 508.1c (declare-attackers step; attacking restrictions constrain the set of legal attacker declarations the active player can make). A "can't attack" effect is an attacker-side restriction under this rule. Maps to `CantAttackEffect` with a `Target` reference parsed via `ParseTargetFilter` (giving the same subtype/type generality as the blocker-side sibling `CantBlockThisTurnEffectRule`) and `Duration` = end of turn, matching the oracle phrase "this turn".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CantAttackThisTurnEffectRule.cs)

### `CantBeBlockedThisTurnEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This creature can't be blocked this turn." / "Target creature can't be blocked this turn." — activated ability effect that grants full unblockability until end of turn. CR 509.1b: "The defending player checks each creature they control to see whether it's affected by any restrictions (effects that say a creature can't block, or that it can't block unless some condition is met)." A "can't be blocked" effect is a blocking restriction on the attacker. Maps to `CantBeBlockedEffect` with:

`Target` = `Self` for the "This creature" form — the creature that pays the cost is the one that becomes unblockable; or a `Target` creature reference for the "Target creature" form (Whirler Rogue, CR 115.1). `Duration` = `untilEndOfTurn` — oracle phrase "this turn" maps to end-of-turn expiry. No `BlockedByFilter` — the restriction is unconditional.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CantBeBlockedThisTurnEffectRule.cs)

### `CantBeRegeneratedThisTurnEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This creature can't be regenerated this turn." — activated ability effect that shuts off regeneration shields for the object bearing the ability through the rest of the current turn (Clergy of the Holy Nimbus: "{1}: This creature can't be regenerated this turn. Only your opponents may activate this ability."). CR 701.19 (regenerate): the effect denies the "next time this creature would be destroyed this turn" shield outright, rather than modifying a specific resolving destroy effect (contrast the `CantBeRegenerated` rider carried on `DestroyEffect` for "Destroy target creature. It can't be regenerated."). Maps to `CantBeRegeneratedEffect` with `Target` left null (means the ability's controlling object — same nullable-Target-means-Self convention as `Target`) and `Duration` = end of turn, matching the oracle phrase "this turn" (same pattern as the sibling turn-scoped restrictions `CantAttackThisTurnEffectRule`/ `CantBlockThisTurnEffectRule`/`CantBeBlockedThisTurnEffectRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CantBeRegeneratedThisTurnEffectRule.cs)

### `CantBlockThisTurnEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability effect shape "target [filter] can't block this turn." — e.g. Sower of Chaos: "{2}{R}: Target creature can't block this turn." CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as \"[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]\"" The cost container ({2}{R}) is parsed independently; this rule only recognizes the post-colon effect body. CR 509.1b: "The defending player checks each creature they control to see whether it's affected by any restrictions (effects that say a creature can't block, or that it can't block unless some condition is met). If any restrictions are being disobeyed, the declaration of blockers is illegal." A "can't block" effect is a blocker-side restriction under this rule. Maps to `CantBlockEffect` with a `Target` reference parsed via `ParseTargetFilter` (giving the same subtype/type generality as the triggered-ability sibling `CantBlockThisTurnTriggeredRule`) and `Duration` = end of turn, matching the oracle phrase "this turn".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CantBlockThisTurnEffectRule.cs)

### `ChangeColorEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target creature/permanent becomes [color] until end of turn." — layer-5 color-changing continuous effect (CR 105.3). Recognizes the standard activated-ability pattern on a target creature or permanent.

CR 105.3 (verbatim): "Effects may change an object's color or give a color to a colorless object. If an effect gives an object a new color, the new color replaces all previous colors the object had (unless the effect said the object became that color 'in addition' to its other colors)."

Supported colors: white, blue, black, red, green, colorless (CR 105.1). Color codes follow the WUBRG convention used throughout the MAST schema.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ChangeColorEffectRule.cs)

### `ChooseCreatureTypeActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Choose a creature type[ other than X]." — the creature-type-choice declaration as a stand-alone sentence inside an activated ability's effect half (Imagecrafter: "{T}: Choose a creature type other than Wall. Target creature becomes that type until end of turn."). Emits a plain `ChooseCreatureTypeEffect` carrying the optional exclusion in `Restriction`.

This is the activated-ability sibling of the static `ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule` ("As this land enters, choose a creature type …", CR 614.1c). The two live in different parsers (static vs activated) and their anchored regexes are disjoint, so they never compete. When this sentence is followed by a "becomes that type" sentence, the activated parser's multi-sentence splitter parses each independently and concatenates them; this effect is the producer of the choice, and the later `ChangeSubtypeEffect` back-references it (CR 607.1 linked abilities). MAST models only the choice declaration itself, not the producer/consumer link.

The restriction is captured verbatim (e.g. "other than Wall"), matching the format stored by `ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule`. CR 205.3 constrains a creature-type choice to a single creature type ("'Goblin' … is a creature type"); the exclusion merely removes one candidate.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ChooseCreatureTypeActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `ConditionalCreateTokenIfCardTypeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"If it was a [card type] card, create [count] [P/T] [color] [subtype(s)] creature token(s)." — the conditional payoff that trails a graveyard-exile sentence, e.g. General's Enforcer: "{2}{W}{B}: Exile target card from a graveyard. If it was a creature card, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token."

The preceding "Exile target card from a graveyard." sentence is handled by `ExileFromGraveyardEffectRule`; the activated-ability parser splits the effect half on sentence boundaries (period-space), so this rule structures the SECOND sentence alone into a `ConditionalEffect` gating a `CreateTokenEffect` (mirrors `ConditionalUntapThatLandEffectRule`'s trailing-conditional shape at the sentence level).

"it" is the card the preceding sentence exiled — a back-reference to the object mentioned earlier in the same ability, modelled as `It` (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004). The card-type check is structured as `ObjectHasCardTypeCondition` (CardType lowercase per the `CardTypes` vocabulary, Subject="It") rather than left as free text — CR 109.2/608.2h: after a card leaves the zone it was checked in, its last known information (the type it had while in the graveyard) is what's checked.

CR 111.1 (verbatim): "A token is a marker used to represent any permanent that isn't represented by a card." CR 205.3m: creature subtypes such as "Human" and "Soldier" may be printed in any combination on a single token.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ConditionalCreateTokenIfCardTypeEffectRule.cs)

### `ConditionalUntapThatLandEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"[Then ]if [condition], untap that land." — the conditional reflexive untap that trails the search-to-battlefield fetch on Fabled Passage: "Search your library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle. Then if you control four or more lands, untap that land."

The search-and-shuffle sentence is handled by `SearchLibraryToBattlefieldEffectRule`; the activated-ability parser splits the effect half on sentence boundaries, so this rule structures the second sentence into a `ConditionalEffect` gating an `UntapEffect`.

"that land" is the land the preceding search put onto the battlefield tapped — a back-reference to the object mentioned earlier in the same ability, modelled as `It` (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004). The condition ("you control four or more lands") is delegated verbatim to `ConditionParser`, which recognises the dominant count shape as a `CountCondition`.

CR 701.26b: "To untap a permanent, rotate it back to the upright position from a sideways position. Only tapped permanents can be untapped." CR 305.6 (basic land types) and CR 701.23a (search) govern the paired search sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ConditionalUntapThatLandEffectRule.cs)

### `ConduitOfWorldsActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class*

"Choose target nonland permanent card in your graveyard. If you haven't cast a spell this turn, you may cast that card. If you do, you can't cast additional spells this turn." — Conduit of Worlds' activated-ability effect.

This is a three-sentence activated-ability body that forms one semantically coupled unit — the "Choose target" targeting declaration, a history-predicate gate, and a conditional cast permission with an IfYouDo restriction — and must be recognized as a whole rather than dispatched sentence-by-sentence.

AST shape:

`ConditionalEffect` whose `Condition` is a `CountCondition` checking that you have cast zero spells this turn (`CastThisTurnPredicate` with Caster=You, Count=Equal:0). The `Then` branch is an `OptionalEffect` ("you may") wrapping a `MayCastTargetFromGraveyardEffect` targeting the chosen nonland permanent card in the controller's graveyard. The `IfYouDo` consequence is a `CantCastAdditionalSpellsThisTurnEffect` — the controller may cast no further spells this turn.

CR 602.5d (verbatim): "Activated abilities that read 'Activate only as a sorcery' mean the player must follow the timing rules for casting a sorcery spell, though the ability isn't actually a sorcery." (The `OnlyAsSorcery` restriction is stripped by `ActivatedAbilityParser` before this rule is invoked.)

ANCHORED (^…$) on the full three-sentence pattern so it cannot fire as a substring of a more-specific sibling or be claimed by a looser dispatcher.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ConduitOfWorldsActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `CopyExiledCardAndCastWithoutPayingEffectRule` — *sealed class*

"You may copy the exiled card. If you do, you may cast the copy without paying its mana cost." — Isochron Scepter's activated-ability effect (MRD:200).

CR 707.10: "To copy a spell, activated ability, or triggered ability means to put a copy of it onto the stack … a copy of a spell isn't cast." Here the copy is made from a card in exile (the imprinted card), not from the stack; it is a copy of the card, and then the controller MAY cast that copy — two separate optional actions. The first "you may" (copy) gates the second "you may" (cast without paying) via an `IfYouDo` consequence (ADR 0005 / CR 117.7).

"The exiled card" refers to the card exiled by this permanent's Imprint trigger (CR 406.6 linked ability). It is modelled as an `Any` reference with Zone.Exile + ExiledWith: Self — a linked-ability reference (ADR 0004 "reference not resolution") that names the linking object, not a threaded binding. The copy target is then referenced as `It`.

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` because the two-sentence body forms ONE `OptionalEffect` (not two sibling effects): the "If you do" clause is the consequence of choosing to copy, not an independent effect. Returning null from `TryMatch` ensures the single-effect path never claims the text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CopyExiledCardAndCastWithoutPayingEffectRule.cs)

### `CopyTargetSpellYouControlEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Copy target instant or sorcery spell you control. You may choose new targets for the copy." — Twinning Staff's activated-ability copy-a-spell-you-control effect (Commander 2021, C21:219).

CR 707.10: "To copy a spell, activated ability, or triggered ability means to put a copy of it onto the stack; a copy of a spell isn't cast…" The copy source is a targeted instant or sorcery spell on the stack controlled by you — modelled as an `Target` reference with `Stack`, the instant/sorcery card types, and `You` on the filter.

"You may choose new targets for the copy" is the structured retarget permission carried on `MayChooseNewTargets`.

Distinguished from `CopyTargetSpellTriggeredRule` (triggered ability) and `CopyTargetSpellRule` (spell ability) by the "you control" controller restriction, which appears uniquely in activated-ability spell-copy contexts and must not be silently dropped. The higher priority (74, below the triggered rule's 75) ensures this rule fires first when the text includes "you control", preventing the more-general triggered variant from claiming it.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CopyTargetSpellYouControlEffectRule.cs)

### `CounterSpellActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Counter target [color/type] spell [unless its controller pays {cost}]" reached as the effect interior of an activated ability — e.g. Douse's "{1}{U}: Counter target red spell." (Scourge). CR 701.6a: "To counter a spell or ability means to cancel it, removing it from the stack."

The counter-spell shape and all of its filter dimensions (color words, non&lt;color&gt; predicates, bare card-type qualifier, "with mana value N", and the optional "unless its controller pays {cost}" tail) are identical whether the effect is the resolution of a spell (instant/sorcery) or of an activated ability. Rather than duplicate that recognizer, this activated-effect rule delegates to the single consolidated `CounterSpellRule` surface — the same anchored (`^Counter\s+target … spell …$`) matcher used by the spell parser — so both paths stay in lock-step and there is no second regex to drift.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CounterSpellActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `CounterTargetSpellWithChosenNameActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Counter target spell with the chosen name." — the activation-cost consumer half of Declaration of Naught's CR 614.12 named-card binder ("As this enchantment enters, choose a card name." pairs with this activated ability's "{U}: Counter target spell with the chosen name."). CR 701.6a: "To counter a spell or ability means to cancel it, removing it from the stack." The chosen-name restriction is modeled as `ChosenCharacteristic` = `CardName` on the countered spell's filter (the structured consumer side of the CR 607 linked ability whose producer is `ChooseCardNameEffect`), rather than a literal `Name` string — the name itself is a fresh per-game choice, not a value printed on the card.

Anchored end-to-end (`^Counter\s+target\s+spell\s+with\s+the\s+chosen\s+name\.?$`) so it is disjoint from `CounterSpellRule`'s "with mana value N" tail and does not shadow that consolidated surface.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CounterTargetSpellWithChosenNameActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `CreateColoredCreatureTokenWithKeywordEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Create a N/N [color] [Subtype] creature token with [keyword]." — creates a colored (not colorless) plain creature token with fixed power/toughness, a single subtype, and one granted keyword ability (CR 111.3).

White, blue, black, red, and green are colors (CR 105.1: "There are five colors in the Magic game: white, blue, black, red, and green."), so the token's `Colors` list carries the mapped color code (e.g. `["W"]`) — unlike the colorless-token rules which use `["C"]`.

Distinct from `CreateTokenEffectRule` (priority 986), which anchors on "…creature tokens?$" and cannot match a trailing "with &lt;keyword&gt;" clause. This rule REQUIRES the with-clause, keeping it strictly disjoint from that sibling: no oracle text can match both. Also distinct from `CreateColorlessArtifactCreatureTokenEffectRule` (colorless, artifact creature) and `CreateColorlessCreatureTokenEffectRule` (colorless, plain creature) — this rule is the colored, plain-creature (no "artifact" type) analogue of those.

Fully anchored (^…$). Priority 987 — alongside `CreateTokenWithChangelingEffectRule` (987), another "with …"-tailed specific-create-token variant; both sit above the generic `CreateTokenEffectRule` (986) so the more specific with-clause forms are tried first.

CR 111.1 (tokens); CR 701.7a (Create); CR 105.1 (colors); CR 702.9a/b (Flying is an evasion ability).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CreateColoredCreatureTokenWithKeywordEffectRule.cs)

### `CreateColorlessArtifactCreatureTokenEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Create a N/N colorless [Subtype] artifact creature token [with keyword]." — creates a colorless artifact creature token with fixed power/toughness, a subtype, and an optional single keyword ability (Rule 111.3).

"Colorless" is not a color (CR 105.1: "Colorless is not a color"); the token's `Colors` list is `["C"]`, matching the colorless encoding convention for artifact creature tokens throughout MAST (e.g. the 1/1 colorless Thopter artifact creature token from Whirler Rogue, Whirler Virtuoso, Thopter Foundry, etc.).

Distinct from `CreateColorlessCreatureTokenEffectRule` which handles pure creature tokens only (and explicitly rejects the word "artifact" in the subtype slot via negative lookahead). This rule matches the more specific "artifact creature" multi-type form.

Fully anchored (^…$). Priority 984 — one below `CreateColorlessCreatureTokenEffectRule` (985) so the plain-creature rule is tried first; only artifact-creature forms fall through to this rule.

CR 111.3 (token creation); CR 105.1 (colorless); CR 701.7 (Create).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CreateColorlessArtifactCreatureTokenEffectRule.cs)

### `CreateColorlessCreatureTokenEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Create a N/N colorless [Subtype] creature token." — creates a colorless (no color) creature token with fixed power/toughness, a creature subtype, and no abilities (Rule 111.3).

"Colorless" is not a color (CR 105.1: "Colorless is not a color"); the token's `Colors` list is empty (`[]`), matching the colorless encoding convention throughout MAST. Distinct from `CreateTokenEffectRule`, which handles colored tokens only (the pattern requires one of white/blue/black/red/green).

Fully anchored (^…$). Priority 985 — one below `CreateTokenEffectRule` (986) so the colored-token rule is tried first; only colorless-specific text falls through to this rule.

CR 111.3 (token creation); CR 105.1 (colorless is not a color).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CreateColorlessCreatureTokenEffectRule.cs)

### `CreateCopyTokenWithModificationsEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Create a token that's a copy of target nonlegendary creature you control, except it has haste." — the copy-token line of an activated ability (Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker). Produces a single `CopyEffect` whose `Target` is the targeted creature and whose `Modifications` carry the "except" clause(s).

CR 111.1: "A token is a marker used to represent any permanent that isn't represented by a card." CR 707.2: "When copying an object, the copy acquires the copiable values of the original object's characteristics…" — the "except" clause overrides one of those copiable values; here "it has haste" is an `AbilityAdder` modification. "nonlegendary creature you control" is encoded as a targeted reference with the Legendary supertype negated via `ExcludedSupertypes`.

Reached through `ActivatedAbilityParser`'s multi-sentence pre-pass, which splits Kiki's two-sentence effect body ("Create … except it has haste. Sacrifice it …") and dispatches each sentence independently. The companion delayed-sacrifice sentence is handled by `SacrificeAtEndStepEffectRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CreateCopyTokenWithModificationsEffectRule.cs)

### `CreateEmblemLoyaltyTimingGrantActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"You get an emblem with [LDQUO]You may activate loyalty abilities of planeswalkers you control on any player's turn any time you could cast an instant.[RDQUO]" -- Teferi, Temporal Archmage -10 loyalty ability.

Rule 114.2: "An effect that creates an emblem is written '[Player] gets an emblem with [ability].' This means that [player] puts an emblem with [ability] into the command zone."

The emblem grants a `TimingModificationEffect` that relaxes the loyalty-ability activation restriction (CR 606.3: normally a player may activate a loyalty ability only during a main phase on their own turn while the stack is empty). With this emblem the controller may activate loyalty abilities of planeswalkers they control on any player's turn any time they could cast an instant.

The timing grant applies to activated abilities of planeswalkers the controller controls -- modelled as `ObjectActivatedAbilityReference` with `CardTypes` = ["planeswalker"] and `You`. "On any player's turn" is recorded on `WhoseTurn` = "AnyTurn" -- CR 606.3 establishes the default turn restriction; this field documents its removal.

ANCHORED: the opening "You get an emblem with" is shared with other emblem-grant shapes. The inner ability text is quoted verbatim from Teferi, Temporal Archmage (C14/C16/CMR) and anchoring is the defensive convention.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CreateEmblemLoyaltyTimingGrantActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `CreateTokenEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Create a [P]/[T] [color] [subtype] creature token." and the predefined artifact-token form "Create [count] [Treasure|Food|Clue|Blood] token(s)." Token creation as an activated-ability effect (Rule 111).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CreateTokenEffectRule.cs)

### `CreateTokenWhereXCountEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Create X P/T color subtype creature tokens, where X is the number of [subtype] you control." Handles the Krenko, Mob Boss pattern (CR 111.2: token creation) where X is defined inline as a count of permanents the controller has. Distinct from the plain X-count variant in `CreateTokenEffectRule`: here X is not a free variable — it is immediately resolved to a `CountQuantity` over an `ObjectFilter`. Rule priority is higher than `CreateTokenEffectRule` (986) so this more-specific pattern is tried first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CreateTokenWhereXCountEffectRule.cs)

### `CreateTokenWithChangelingEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Create a [P/T] [color] [Subtype] creature token with changeling." — activated creature-token creation where the token bears the Changeling keyword.

Maskwood Nexus pattern (CR 111 — tokens; CR 702.73 — changeling): "{3}, {T}: Create a 2/2 blue Shapeshifter creature token with changeling." The token's Changeling ability is modelled as a `StaticAbility` with `KeywordAbilityEffect`{Changeling}, mirroring the `ChangelingKeyword` combinator shape.

ANCHORED (^…$): the "with changeling" tail is distinctive but substring-safe only when anchored. The generic `CreateTokenEffectRule` (priority 986) does not match "with changeling" because its regex is anchored and ends at "creature token[s]$"; this rule fires first (priority 987) for the changeling variant, ensuring the generic rule never sees it.

Priority 987 — one above the generic `CreateTokenEffectRule` (986) so this more-specific shape is tried first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CreateTokenWithChangelingEffectRule.cs)

### `CreaturesYouControlGainKeywordsUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class*

"Creatures you control gain [keyword] [and [keyword] ...] until end of turn" (The Wind Crystal: "Creatures you control gain flying and lifelink until end of turn."). One or more keyword names joined by " and ", all with until-end-of-turn duration, granted to every creature you control.

Mirrors `ModifyPTAndGainKeywordSpellRule`'s keyword-splitting shape at the activated-ability layer: emits one `GainAbilityEffect` per keyword via `TryMatchMulti` rather than collapsing the "and"-joined list into a single grant (which would silently drop every keyword but the first — the single-effect `GainAbilityEffectRule`'s "Creatures you control gain (\w+)" branch only captures one word). Reuses `BuildGrantedKeywordAbility` for the per-keyword `StaticAbility` (CR 113.6/113.10 — a granted ability is a full-fledged ability of the gainer), so a single-keyword card (e.g. Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose's "Creatures you control gain lifelink until end of turn") produces the identical shape it already did via the single-effect path.

The single-effect `TryMatch` always returns null so the flat-list path via `TryMatchMulti` is the only active route. Anchored (^…$).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/CreaturesYouControlGainKeywordsUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `DealsDamageEqualToPowerReciprocalEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

The reciprocal power-fight activated sentences (Karplusan Yeti: "{T}: This creature deals damage equal to its power to target creature. That creature deals damage equal to its power to this creature."). The activated parser's multi-sentence pre-pass splits the effect half on the ". " boundary and dispatches each sentence here individually, so this rule recognises the two surfaces separately:

"This creature deals damage equal to its power to target creature." — source is `Self` (the permanent with the ability); the amount is a `DerivedQuantity` of the source's own power ("its power"); the recipient is a fresh target creature. "That creature deals damage equal to its power to this creature." — source is the previously-targeted creature, referenced back as `ThatCreature` (a linked reference, ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution, not a threaded binding); the amount is that creature's own power; the recipient is `Self`.

Both emit a `DealDamageEffect` — non-combat damage (CR 120.1: "An object that deals damage is the source of that damage."), left as the default (`IsCombat` null) because the ability marks no combat context. This is the long-hand of a two-way fight but is NOT the fight keyword action (CR 701.14): only one creature is a target (the other is the source's `Self`), and the exchange is written as two ordered damage events rather than a single symmetric `FightEffect`. Both patterns are anchored `^…$` on their full surface so neither can claim a substring of any broader sibling sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/DealsDamageEqualToPowerReciprocalEffectRule.cs)

### `DestroyColoredPermanentEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Destroy target permanent that's one or more colors." — destroys a colored (non-colorless) permanent of any type.

"One or more colors" means the permanent has at least one of the five Magic colors (CR 105.1: "There are five colors in the Magic game: white, blue, black, red, and green. Colorless is not a color."). This is the negation of colorless — any permanent that has a color satisfies this filter. The characteristic "one or more colors" is encoded as an `OtherCharacteristic` residual since `ObjectFilter` does not yet have a structured `IsColored` axis (the complement of `IsColorless`). It is a meaningful, rules-distinct filter — not arbitrary free text — and is a candidate for a future first-class boolean axis on `ObjectFilter`.

Fully anchored (^…$). GUARD: handles only "Destroy target permanent that's one or more colors." Does NOT handle "Destroy target [type]" (sibling `DestroyTargetEffectRule`), "Destroy target multicolored permanent" (spell-parser family), or "Destroy target nonland permanent" (different filter axis). Priority 599 — one below `DestroyTargetEffectRule` (600) so the bare-type destroy rule is tried first.

CR 701.8a (destroy); CR 105.1 (colors).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/DestroyColoredPermanentEffectRule.cs)

### `DestroySelfEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Destroy this &lt;type&gt;." — a self-destroy activated-ability effect (Detention Vortex's "{3}: Destroy this Aura."). CR 109.2/CR 701.8a: "this &lt;type&gt;" refers to the permanent with the ability (`Self`), and destroying it moves it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard. Distinct from `DestroyTargetEffectRule` ("Destroy target &lt;type&gt;"): the subject here is the source permanent itself, not a chosen target, so no `Target` ability is granted and no legal-target filter is needed — the type word ("Aura", "creature", "artifact", …) is redundant with Self and is dropped, mirroring the sibling self-reference rules in this directory (e.g. `ReturnSelfFromGraveyardToBattlefieldEffectRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/DestroySelfEffectRule.cs)

### `DestroyTargetEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Destroy target &lt;type&gt;." — single-target destroy as an activated-ability effect. Handles bare card-type targets: creature, artifact, enchantment, land, planeswalker, permanent; and two-type disjunctions: "artifact or enchantment", "creature or planeswalker", etc. CR 701.8a: "To destroy a permanent, move it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard." GUARD: handles only "Destroy target &lt;type&gt;" shapes. Does NOT handle Exile (sibling family F14 owns "Exile target creature").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/DestroyTargetEffectRule.cs)

### `DestroyTargetNonbasicLandEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Destroy target nonbasic land." — single-target destroy of a nonbasic land as an activated-ability effect (Dwarven Miner, Dwarven Blastminer, Rishadan Cutpurse-style land denial). The "nonbasic" qualifier is modeled on the structured supertype-negation axis rather than as free text: a nonbasic land is a land WITHOUT the "basic" supertype (CR 205.4c: "Any land with the supertype 'basic' is a basic land. Any land that doesn't have this supertype is a nonbasic land, even if it has a basic land type."). Hence `CardTypes=["land"]` + `ExcludedSupertypes=["Basic"]`, parallel to how "nonlegendary creature" is encoded (see `ExcludedSupertypes`). CR 701.8a: "To destroy a permanent, move it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard." GUARD: anchored to exactly "Destroy target nonbasic land".
