The bare-type sibling `DestroyTargetEffectRule` (Priority 600) matches "Destroy target land" but NOT "nonbasic land" (its type group has no "nonbasic land" alternative), so the two rules are disjoint; this rule sits at a higher priority only to make precedence explicit.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/DestroyTargetNonbasicLandEffectRule.cs)

### `DestroyTargetNonblackCreatureEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Destroy target nonblack creature." — single-target destroy of a nonblack creature as an activated-ability effect (Attrition: "{B}, Sacrifice a creature: Destroy target nonblack creature."). The "nonblack" qualifier is modeled on the structured colour-negation axis rather than as free text: a nonblack creature is a creature without the color black (CR 105.1: "There are five colors in the Magic game: white, blue, black, red, and green."). Hence `CardTypes=["creature"]` + `ExcludedColors=["B"]`, parallel to how the identical phrase is encoded on the spell side (Doom Blade — see `ExcludedColors`) and to how "nonbasic land" is encoded on this same activated-effect track (see `DestroyTargetNonbasicLandEffectRule`). CR 701.8a: "To destroy a permanent, move it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard." GUARD: anchored to exactly "Destroy target nonblack creature". The bare-type sibling `DestroyTargetEffectRule` (Priority 600) matches "Destroy target creature" but NOT "nonblack creature" (its type group has no "nonblack creature" alternative), so the two rules are disjoint; this rule sits at a higher priority only to make precedence explicit, mirroring `DestroyTargetNonbasicLandEffectRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/DestroyTargetNonblackCreatureEffectRule.cs)

### `DestroyTargetStateQualifiedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Destroy target [state] creature." as an activated-ability effect — handles game-state qualifiers that describe a creature's current combat/tap status rather than its card-type or color.

"Destroy target attacking creature." — e.g., Mine Bearer "Destroy target tapped creature." "Destroy target blocking creature." "Destroy target attacking or blocking creature."

State words go into `Characteristics`, mirroring the spell-side `DestroyTargetStateQualifiedRule` convention (e.g., Immolating Glare's "Destroy target attacking creature."). CR 701.8a: "To destroy a permanent, move it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard."

Discard cost: "Discard a card", "Discard a legendary card", "Discard your hand", etc. Reuses the shared `ParseDiscardPattern` for the card-count shapes. "Discard your hand" (or "discard their hand") is the whole-hand shape: the count is a `DerivedQuantity` with `CardsInHand` — descriptively, "hand" means "all cards in your hand at the time the cost is paid" (CR 701.9a).

### `DrawThenDiscardEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

"Draw a card, then discard a card." — Teferi, Master of Time +1 loyalty ability. A single ", then"-joined sentence that is two sibling effects: draw one card followed by discard one card.

CR 121.1: "A player draws a card by putting the top card of their library into their hand." CR 701.9a: "To discard a card, move it from its owner's hand to that player's graveyard."

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair on `Effects` (the "draw then" multi-sentence convention), not nested under a CompositeEffect. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path (which would greedily claim the "draw" and silently drop the discard) never fires.

ANCHORED (^...$): matches exactly "Draw a card, then discard a card" to prevent substring matches against longer draw-then chains (e.g. "Draw a card, then put this artifact on top of its owner's library."). Priority 952 — above generic DrawCardsEffectRule (998) which would claim the sentence, below DrawThenSelf (950) which is more-specific (so the more-specific sibling fires first when the text is "Draw a card, then put this artifact...").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/DrawThenDiscardEffectRule.cs)

### `DrawThenSelfToTopOfLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

"Draw a card, then put this [artifact/permanent] on top of its owner's library." — Sensei's Divining Top. A single ", then"-joined sentence that is two sibling effects: a `DrawCardsEffect` (you draw 1) followed by a `PutOnTopOfLibraryEffect` moving this permanent (`Self`) to the top of its owner's library.

CR 121.1: "A player draws a card by putting the top card of their library into their hand. … It may also be done as part of a cost or effect of a spell or ability." The draw is the structured action; "on top of its owner's library" is the structured destination carried by `PutOnTopOfLibraryEffect`'s discriminator, not free text.

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair on `Effects` (the SurveilThenDraw / multi-sentence convention), not nested under a CompositeEffect. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path never claims the sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/DrawThenSelfToTopOfLibraryRule.cs)

### `EachOpponentLoseLifeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Each opponent loses N life." — broadcast life-loss as an activated-ability effect (Rule 119), covering drain abilities like Bolas's Citadel's sacrifice-ten activation.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/EachOpponentLoseLifeEffectRule.cs)

### `EachOpponentLosesLifeYouGainLifeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

"Each opponent loses N life and you gain N life." — the vampire-drain activated-ability shape (Vampire Opportunist).

A single "… and …"-joined sentence that expands to two sibling effects: `LoseLifeEffect` (each opponent loses N) and `GainLifeEffect` (you gain N). Differs from the similar `EachOpponentLoseLifeEffectRule` (bare single-clause "Each opponent loses N life" only) and `GainLifeEffectRule` (bare single-clause "You gain N life" only) — neither of those anchored single-effect rules matches this compound sentence.

CR 119.3 (life gain/loss): "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." Both clauses are governed by this rule; the lose-life clause targets each opponent (`EachOpponent`) and the gain-life clause targets the controller (`You`).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): "Each opponent loses N life and you gain N life" appears as a SUBSTRING of no sibling rule, but the anchor prevents a future broader pattern from consuming this sentence and silently dropping either conjunct.

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair on `Effects` — not wrapped in a `CompositeEffect`. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path never claims the sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/EachOpponentLosesLifeYouGainLifeEffectRule.cs)

### `EachOpponentMayDiscardOtherwiseLoseLifeRepeatEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Each opponent may discard a card. If they don't, they lose N life. Repeat this process M more times." — the Professor Onyx −8 loyalty ability shape.

Three-sentence structure:

The base action: each opponent may discard a card ("each opponent may" means each opponent individually decides whether to discard). The consequence: any opponent who chose not to discard loses N life. A repeat instruction: the entire base action + consequence sequence is performed M additional times (total = M + 1).

Modelled as a `RepeatEffect` wrapping an `OptionalEffect`:

`Inner` — the `OptionalEffect` for one iteration (discard or lose life). `AdditionalTimes` — how many times to repeat after the initial pass (the oracle phrase "six more times" → 6). `Inner` — `DiscardCardsEffect` targeting each opponent. `IfYouDoNot` — `LoseLifeEffect` targeting each opponent who declined to discard.

CR 701.9a (discard); CR 119.3 (lose life); CR 608.2 (effects resolve, then the repeat instruction directs additional resolutions).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): this multi-sentence pattern is highly specific; anchoring is the defensive convention. Priority 999 — above `DiscardCardsEffectRule` (Priority 997) because that rule greedily matches any text containing "discard" with no anchoring, so this more-specific three-sentence shape must be tried first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/EachOpponentMayDiscardOtherwiseLoseLifeRepeatEffectRule.cs)

### `EachOpponentSacrificesGreatestPowerCreatureEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Each opponent sacrifices a creature with the greatest power among creatures that player controls." — the Professor Onyx −3 loyalty ability shape.

The "with the greatest power among creatures that player controls" qualifier is a comparative game-state predicate (no dedicated CR — comparative relative power among a player's creatures) with no first-class ObjectFilter axis. It is carried as an `OtherCharacteristic` residual on the sacrificed-creature filter per the ADR 0001 free-text doctrine: the type-honest home for "not yet structured".

The sacrifice target is each opponent (`EachOpponent`); each opponent independently chooses which of their greatest-power creatures to sacrifice (in the case of a tie, they choose among the tied creatures). CR 701.21a (Sacrifice); CR 102.2 (opponents).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): prevents false positives against other "each opponent sacrifices" patterns. Priority 998 — just below `EachOpponentMayDiscardOtherwiseLoseLifeRepeatEffectRule` (999) and above the generic effect rules that could partially match.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/EachOpponentSacrificesGreatestPowerCreatureEffectRule.cs)

### `EachPlayerMillsNCardsEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Each player mills N cards." — broadcast mill keyword action applied to every player simultaneously (CR 701.17a: "For a player to mill a number of cards, that player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard.").

Used by Syr Konrad, the Grim's activated ability: "{1}{B}: Each player mills a card." The symmetrical form applies the same mill count to the controller AND each opponent, modelled as a single `MillEffect` with `EachPlayer` as the recipient — matching the "each player" subject in oracle text.

Anchored (^ … $) to prevent substring collision with the more-targeted `MillTargetPlayerEffectRule` ("target player mills N cards") and the self-mill form handled elsewhere. Distinct from "target player mills" (targeted activation) and "each opponent mills" (opponent-only spread).

CR 701.17a (verbatim): "For a player to mill a number of cards, that player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard." CR 603.2: triggered abilities fire on each matching mill event.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/EachPlayerMillsNCardsEffectRule.cs)

### `EnchantedEquippedModifyPTEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Enchanted creature gets &lt;±P/±T&gt; until end of turn" and "Equipped creature gets &lt;±P/±T&gt; until end of turn" — an activated pump whose subject is the permanent this card is attached to.

<b>CR 611.1:</b> "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects, modifies control of objects, or affects players or the rules of the game, for a fixed or indefinite period."

<b>CR 613.4c:</b> "Layer 7c: Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied."

<b>CR 208.1:</b> "...Power and toughness can be modified or set to particular values by effects."

Subject is modelled as `EnchantedOrEquipped` — the permanent this Aura or Equipment is currently attached to — rather than free text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/EnchantedEquippedModifyPTEffectRule.cs)

### `ExchangeLifeTotalsEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Exchange life totals with target opponent." — Magus of the Mirror.

CR 701.12a: "A spell or ability may instruct players to exchange something (for example, life totals or control of two permanents) as part of its resolution." CR 701.12c: "When life totals are exchanged, each player gains or loses the amount of life necessary to equal the other player's previous life total."

Reuses the shared `ExchangeCharacteristicEffect` with its pre-existing `LifeTotals` facet — no new discriminator. The exchange is between the controller (the implicit first party, "you") and the named target opponent, so `First = You` and `Second = Opponent`. The "target" keyword on the opponent is carried by the `Opponent` reference itself, matching how "target opponent" is modeled elsewhere (e.g. Blood Tribute).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExchangeLifeTotalsEffectRule.cs)

### `ExileAnotherCreatureThenReturnRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

Activated flicker (blink) effect: "Exile another target creature you control, then return it to the battlefield under its owner's control." — moves a targeted other creature the controller controls to exile and then immediately returns it, preserving owner control on re-entry (e.g. Emiel the Blessed's {3} ability).

"another target creature" is modelled with `ExcludeSelf = true` (CR 109.5 — "another" means other than the source object). "then return it" is the linked exiled reference (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution): a `Designated` card in `Exile` whose `ExiledWith` points to `Self` (the same ability instance that exiled it — the Petravark shape). "under its owner's control" rides on `UnderControl` as an `Owner` reference (CR 400.6).

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair on `Effects`, consistent with `ExileSelfThenReturnToBattlefieldRule`. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path never claims this sentence.

CR 701.13a (verbatim): "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is." CR 400.6: "If an effect gives a player control of an object … that player controls that object until the effect ends." CR 109.5: "The words 'you' and 'your' on an object refer to the object's controller, its would-be controller (if a player is casting it), or its owner (if it has no controller)."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileAnotherCreatureThenReturnRule.cs)

### `ExileCardsFromGraveyardCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

"Exile N [type] cards from your graveyard" — exile-from-graveyard as an activation cost. Used by Drivnod, Carnage Dominus: "Exile three creature cards from your graveyard". CR 118.8a classifies exile as a cost action when it precedes the colon separator of an activated ability.

The encoded cost uses `ExileCost` with: `Filter.CardTypes` — the specified card type (e.g. "creature"). `Filter.Controller = You` — "your graveyard" restricts to the activating player's own graveyard (CR 109.4). `FromZone = Graveyard` — the cards are in the graveyard when the ability is activated (CR 406). `Quantity` — the stated count (e.g. three → 3).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileCardsFromGraveyardCostRule.cs)

### `ExileCardsFromGraveyardUntypedCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

"Exile N cards from your graveyard" — exile-from-graveyard as an activation cost, with no card-type qualifier (any card, not "creature card"/"artifact card"/etc.). Used by Psychatog: "Exile two cards from your graveyard: This creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn." CR 118.8a classifies exile as a cost action when it precedes the colon separator of an activated ability.

Sibling of `ExileCardsFromGraveyardCostRule`, which requires a card-type word between the count and "cards" (e.g. "three creature cards"). This rule is anchored (^…$) to only the untyped "N cards" phrasing, so the two never collide: this rule's pattern has no type-word capture group and therefore cannot match "Exile three creature cards from your graveyard", and the typed rule's pattern requires a type word so it cannot match "Exile two cards from your graveyard".

The encoded cost uses `ExileCost` with: `Filter.CardTypes = ["card"]` — no type restriction beyond "card" (mirrors the untyped `DiscardCost` convention for "Discard a card"). `Filter.Controller = You` — "your graveyard" restricts to the activating player's own graveyard (CR 109.4). `FromZone = Graveyard` — the cards are in the graveyard when the ability is activated (CR 406). `Quantity` — the stated count (e.g. two → 2).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileCardsFromGraveyardUntypedCostRule.cs)

### `ExileCreatureCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

"Exile a creature you control" — exile-a-permanent-you-control as an activation cost. Used by Food Chain (Exodus, `EXO:193`): CR 118.8a classifies exile as a cost action when it precedes the colon separator of an activated ability.

The encoded cost uses `ExileCost` with: `Filter.CardTypes = ["creature"]` `Filter.Controller = You` — "you control" restricts to the activating player's own permanents (CR 109.4). `FromZone = Battlefield` — the creature is on the battlefield when the ability is activated (CR 701.13a). `Quantity = 1` — "a creature" is a single object.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileCreatureCostRule.cs)

### `ExileFromGraveyardEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Exile target card from a graveyard." — single-card graveyard-exile as an activated-ability effect (Rule 701.13 — Exile), the common graveyard-hoser pattern.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileFromGraveyardEffectRule.cs)

### `ExilePlayerGraveyardZoneActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Exile target player's graveyard" / "Exile target opponent's graveyard" / "Exile each opponent's graveyard" / "Exile each player's graveyard" — the graveyard-hate family that exiles the entire contents of a player's graveyard zone, in the effect position of an activated ability (Tormod's Crypt: "{T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Exile target player's graveyard.").

CR 701.13a: "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is." The action exiles every card in the named graveyard, so the effect's target is the whole zone's contents rather than a single chosen card — modeled as an `Each` reference (all cards) whose filter pins the graveyard zone and the owning player. The player scope rides the filter's `Owner` axis (CR 108.3 — cards in a graveyard are owned by that player): "target player's" → `Owner=Target`; "target opponent's" / "each opponent's" → `Owner=Opponent`.

Mirrors the triggered-ability sibling `ExilePlayerGraveyardZoneRule` (same effect shape, different ability kind), which cannot be reused directly because the activated and triggered effect-rule pipelines are separate reflection-discovered chains (`IActivatedEffectRule` vs. `ITriggeredRule`).

Anchored (^…$) so it only fires on the bare whole-graveyard-exile body and never inside a longer composite clause a more-specific rule should handle.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExilePlayerGraveyardZoneActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `ExileSelfAndTargetCreatureRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

"Exile this creature and target creature without [keyword] that's attacking you." — a single activated-ability sentence whose one verb ("Exile") governs TWO objects: the source object itself ("this creature") and a targeted attacker. Giant Trap Door Spider: "{1}{R}{G}, {T}: Exile this creature and target creature without flying that's attacking you." The cost half ("{1}{R}{G}, {T}") is parsed by the activated cost rules; this rule recognises only the post-colon effect fragment.

Because the two objects are exiled by one action, the sentence expands to a flat pair of sibling `ExileEffect` nodes on `Effects` — modelled via `TryMatchMulti`, the same "flat sibling list" convention as `ExileAnotherCreatureThenReturnRule` and `ExileSelfThenReturnToBattlefieldRule`. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path never claims this sentence and silently drops one exile.

The first exile targets `Self` ("this creature", CR 109). The second exiles a `Target` creature carrying two characteristic predicates that have no first-class `ObjectFilter` home yet, so they ride as typed `OtherCharacteristic` residuals (IResidual, a deliberate scope deferral per ADR 0001 — NOT IUnparsed): the keyword-absence "without flying" ("withoutFlying", the M10/Falter · ODY/Ashen Firebeast convention) and the combat-defender predicate "that's attacking you" ("attackingYou" — the object is attacking the ability's controller; there is no `CombatStateCharacteristic` defender axis, so the compound is deferred whole rather than split into a structured "attacking" plus a dangling "you").

CR 701.13a (verbatim): "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is." CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect." CR 508.1b: the active player "announces which player, planeswalker, or battle each of the chosen creatures is attacking" — "attacking you" is the subset of attackers whose declared defender is this controller.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileSelfAndTargetCreatureRule.cs)

### `ExileSelfByNameCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

"Exile [CardName]" — exile the source permanent by its own card name as an activation cost. Rule 201.5: if an object's oracle text refers to the object it is applying to by name, that name refers to that object.

Encodes the cost as `ExileCost` with: `Filter.IsSelf = true` — the oracle name refers to the source permanent itself (CR 201.5 self-reference by card name). `Filter.CardTypes = ["permanent"]` — we don't have the type line here; "permanent" is the conservative common type, which the SelfReferenceTypeCorrector in CardParser will narrow at the card level. `FromZone = Battlefield` — the permanent is on the battlefield when the ability is activated (CR 701.13a moves it from there to exile). `Quantity = 1` — a single object.

Distinct from `ExileSelfCostRule` which matches the "Exile this [type]" form. This rule matches the self-by-name form used when a card names itself explicitly (Gonti's Aether Heart: "Exile Gonti's Aether Heart").

ANCHOR: pattern is anchored (^...$) to prevent matching substrings inside a longer exile-as-effect clause (e.g. "Exile target creature." in an effect body). Only fires when the entire cost component is "Exile [Name]".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileSelfByNameCostRule.cs)

### `ExileSelfCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Exile-self cost: "Exile this artifact", "Exile this creature", etc. The activated permanent is moved to the exile zone as part of paying the activation cost. CR 701.13a: "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is." The encoded cost uses `ExileCost` with: - `Filter.CardTypes` = the permanent type named in oracle text - `Filter.Characteristics` = `[OtherCharacteristic("this permanent")]` to record the self-referential "this" phrasing (parallel to the `SacrificeCostRule` convention for "Sacrifice this artifact" costs) - `FromZone` = `Battlefield` (the permanent is on the battlefield when the ability is activated; CR 701.13a moves it from there to exile) - `Quantity` = 1 (oracle text always names a single permanent)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileSelfCostRule.cs)

### `ExileSelfThenReturnToBattlefieldRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

"Exile this creature, then return it to the battlefield under your control." — the Soulbond blink pattern (Deadeye Navigator, CR 702.95). A single ", then"-joined sentence that is two sibling effects: an `ExileEffect` moving self to exile, followed by a `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect` returning the designated just-exiled card to the battlefield under the ability's controller.

CR 701.13a: "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is." CR 400.7: the exiled object is the same object returned. The return target is modelled as `Designated` with `ExiledWith` pointing to `Self`, mirroring the Felidar Guardian blink fixture's consumer side (ADR 0004: reference-not-resolution).

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair on `Effects`. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path never claims this sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileSelfThenReturnToBattlefieldRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetCreatureEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Exile target creature." — moves a targeted creature from whatever zone it occupies to the exile zone. Also handles the Aura/Equipment form: "Exile enchanted creature." — exiles the permanent this card is attached to (CR 303.4m). Not a targeted ability; no "target" keyword in oracle text. CR 701.13a: "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is." CR 303.4m: "An ability of a permanent that refers to the 'enchanted [object or player]' refers to whatever object or player that permanent is attached to…"

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileTargetCreatureEffectRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetLandYouControlThenReturnRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

Activated land blink (self-flicker of a controlled land): "Exile target land you control, then return it to the battlefield under your control." — moves a targeted land the controller controls to exile and then immediately returns it under the ability's controller (Ruin Ghost's {W}, {T} ability). This is the land analogue of `ExileAnotherCreatureThenReturnRule`; the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair on `Effects`.

"target land you control" is an `Target` land with a `You` filter (CR 109.5 — "you"/"your" refer to the object's controller). "then return it" is the linked exiled reference (ADR 0004, reference-not-resolution): an `Designated` card in `Exile` whose `ExiledWith` points to `Self` (the same ability instance that exiled it). "under your control" rides on `UnderControl` as an `You` reference, matching `ExileSelfThenReturnToBattlefieldRule`.

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair, consistent with the creature-blink rules. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path never claims this sentence.

CR 406.2 (verbatim): "To exile an object is to put it into the exile zone from whatever zone it's currently in. An exiled card is a card that's been put into the exile zone." CR 400.7: "An object that moves from one zone to another becomes a new object with no memory of, or relation to, its previous existence." CR 109.5: "The words 'you' and 'your' on an object refer to the object's controller, its would-be controller (if a player is attempting to play, cast, or activate it), or its owner (if it has no controller)."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileTargetLandYouControlThenReturnRule.cs)

### `ExileTopCardFaceDownAndLookRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

"Exile the top card of your library face down and look at it." — moves the top card of the controller's library to the exile zone face down, then allows the controller to look at it (CR 406.3: a player instructed to exile a card face down may look at it).

This is a combined effect: the exile is face-down (`IsFaceDown` = true) and is followed by a `LookAtCardsEffect` targeting the just-exiled card in exile. CR 406.3 (verbatim): "Cards 'exiled face down' can't be examined by any player except when instructions allow it. However, if a player is instructed to look at a card and then exile it face down, or once a player is allowed to look at a card exiled face down, that player may continue to look at that card until it leaves the exile zone."

Fully anchored (^…$): the surface phrase "face down and look at it" must not match as a substring of a more-specific sibling (no other activated-effect sentence contains this exact phrasing). Priority 981 — one below `ExileTopCardOfLibraryEffectRule` (982) so the simpler plain-exile rule is tried first and falls through naturally.

CR 406.3: exiled-face-down visibility rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileTopCardFaceDownAndLookRule.cs)

### `ExileTopCardOfLibraryEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Exile the top card of your library." — moves the top card of the controller's library to the exile zone, as an activated-ability effect (Mystic Forge: "{T}, Pay 1 life: Exile the top card of your library.").

The "top card" is a positionally-designated card — it is deterministic (no player choice) and identified by position in the library, not by targeting (no "target" keyword in oracle text). Therefore the reference is `Designated` rather than `Target`. The positional qualifier "top" is carried as an `OtherCharacteristic` residual (the same convention used by the Ingest keyword expansion: GLOSSARY §Ingest). Zone=Library and Controller=You establish which library the top card comes from.

CR 701.13a: "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileTopCardOfLibraryEffectRule.cs)

### `ExileTopCardPlayUntilNextTurnActivatedRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Exile the top card of your library. Until the end of your next turn, you may play that card." — the single-card, next-turn-bounded impulse in an activated-ability context (Chase Stein, Runaway; Cori Mountain Monastery).

The two oracle sentences are one semantic unit — "that card" back-references the single card exiled by the first sentence — so they collapse to a single `ImpulseEffect` with `RemainExiled` (the one exiled card stays in exile, none kept in hand) and an inherited `Duration` bounding the play window. This is the count-1 / next-turn analogue of the plural, this-turn sibling `ExileTopCardsPlayThisTurnActivatedRule` and the spell-context duration sibling `ExileTopCardsPlayUntilTimeRule`. ADR 0004 (reference, not resolution): MAST records the exile and the play window; the engine tracks which specific card was exiled and enforces the deadline.

CR 406 (exile zone); CR 701.13 (exile); CR 601 / CR 305 ("play" a card). "Until the end of your next turn" → a `GameTime` at the End edge of the controller's Next Turn.

ANCHORED (^…$): the exact singular "the top card … you may play that card" shape. The trailing "$" keeps it from claiming more-specific siblings that append a rider (e.g. "… you may play that card and you may spend mana as though it were mana of any color"), whose extra permission must not be silently dropped. Priority 975 mirrors the plural sibling — above mid-range, so the two-sentence split path (TryParseMultiEffectSentences) cannot claim either sentence independently (the "Until … you may play that card" half parses no standalone rule).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileTopCardPlayUntilNextTurnActivatedRule.cs)

### `ExileTopCardsPlayThisTurnActivatedRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Exile the top N cards of your library. You may play those cards this turn." — the current-turn-bounded impulse in an activated-ability context (Harnfel, Horn of Bounty).

The two oracle sentences are one semantic unit — "those cards" back-references the exiled pile from the first sentence — so they collapse to a single `ImpulseEffect` with `RemainExiled` and `EndOfTurn`, matching the spell-context sibling `ExileTopCardsPlayThisTurnRule`. ADR 0004 (reference, not resolution): MAST records the exile and the play window; the engine tracks which specific cards were exiled and enforces the deadline.

CR 406 (exile zone); CR 701.13 (exile); CR 701.18 ("play").

ANCHORED (^…$): "Exile the top … cards of your library. You may play those cards this turn." is the exact Harnfel shape. Non-anchored matching risks absorbing "Exile the top N … put them into …" shapes that should be plain exile effects. Priority 975 — above mid-range, below ultra-specific multi-sentence composite rules, so the two-sentence split path (TryParseMultiEffectSentences) can't claim either sentence independently.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ExileTopCardsPlayThisTurnActivatedRule.cs)

### `ForageCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Forage keyword-action cost (CR 701.61a): "Exile three cards from your graveyard or sacrifice a Food." Printed as the bare word "Forage" on the cost side of an activated ability, e.g. "{2}, Forage: [effect]".

CR 701.61a (verbatim): "To forage means 'Exile three cards from your graveyard or sacrifice a Food.'" The keyword action appears as a single cost component: comma-separated from any mana cost in the standard "[cost]: [effect]" pattern (CR 602.1). MAST records the invocation as a `ForageCost` descriptor; the two alternative payment modes are engine territory per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine (the node names the action, not the execution). Rule reference: 701.61.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ForageCostRule.cs)

### `GainAbilityEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"gains [keyword]" grants on a target. Supported shapes: - "This [type] gains [keyword] [until end of turn]" (Self) - "Target creature gains [keyword] until end of turn" - "Target [Subtype] gains [keyword] until end of turn" (subtype-filtered target, e.g. Olivia's Bloodsworn "Target Vampire gains haste until end of turn") - "Creatures you control gain [keyword]" (Each, creatures you control) The grant is a continuous effect that modifies the target's characteristics for the stated duration (CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period."). The granted keyword is itself a static ability (e.g. CR 702.10a: "Haste is a static ability.").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/GainAbilityEffectRule.cs)

### `GainLifeAndDrawCardsEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

"You gain N life and draw M cards." — Candy Trail's "{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this artifact: You gain 3 life and draw a card." A single "... and ..."-joined sentence that is two sibling effects: a `GainLifeEffect` (you gain N) followed by a `DrawCardsEffect` (you draw M).

CR 119.3 (gain life), CR 121.1 (draw). The two clauses are independent actions resolved in order; representing them as a flat sibling pair (not one residual) preserves both — the naive re-point otherwise drops the gain-life conjunct.

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair on `Effects` (the DrawThenSelfToTopOfLibrary / SurveilThenDraw convention), not nested under a CompositeEffect. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path never claims the sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/GainLifeAndDrawCardsEffectRule.cs)

### `GainLifeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"You gain N life" — N is a literal number, number word, or variable (X/Y/Z). "You gain X life.", "You gain 2 life.", "You gain three life."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/GainLifeEffectRule.cs)

### `GainLifeEqualToLifeLostEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"You gain life equal to the life lost this way." — controller life-gain whose amount is derived from the life lost by a preceding `LoseLifeEffect` in the same ability (the drain shape). Representative card: Scholar of Athreos ("{2}{B}: Each opponent loses 1 life. You gain life equal to the life lost this way."), whose activated ability's second sentence is dispatched here after the multi-sentence pre-pass splits the effect body on the sentence boundary.

The amount is a `DerivedQuantity` keyed on `LifeLost` — reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): MAST records the textual link to "the life lost this way", not the runtime value (CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."). This is the activated-ability counterpart of `GainLifeSpellRule`'s "You gain life equal to the life lost this way." branch (Blood Tithe, the sorcery twin of this drain sentence).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the exact drain sentence. Distinct from the sibling `GainLifeEffectRule` ("You gain N life", which requires a numeric token after "gain" and so cannot match this life-equal-to phrase) — the anchor prevents a future broader "You gain …" pattern from consuming this sentence and silently losing the derived-quantity link.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/GainLifeEqualToLifeLostEffectRule.cs)

### `GainLifeEqualToSacrificedCreaturesToughnessEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"You gain life equal to the sacrificed creature's toughness." — the derived life-gain resolution of an activated ability whose cost sacrifices a creature (Diamond Valley: "{T}, Sacrifice a creature: You gain life equal to the sacrificed creature's toughness."). The gained amount is a `DerivedQuantity` keyed on `Toughness` whose `Source` is the anaphoric "the sacrificed creature": the object moved to the graveyard by this same ability's `SacrificeCost` (CR 701.21a). That back-reference is a CR 607.1 linked ability — the effect "directly refers to … objects … that were affected by" the cost — so MAST records the textual link, not the runtime toughness value (ADR 0004: reference-not-resolution).

The activated-ability sibling of `YouGainLifeEqualToThatCreaturesToughnessTriggeredRule` (Engulfing Slagwurm's "You gain life equal to that creature's toughness."), which sources the toughness from a trigger's "that creature" instead of a sacrificed-cost creature. CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."

Anchored (`^…$`) to the exact sacrificed-toughness surface so it cannot claim the numeric ("You gain N life", `GainLifeEffectRule`) or life-lost ("You gain life equal to the life lost this way", `GainLifeEqualToLifeLostEffectRule`) siblings, and so a future broader "You gain life equal to …" pattern cannot silently swallow this derived-quantity link.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/GainLifeEqualToSacrificedCreaturesToughnessEffectRule.cs)

### `GetsPTAndGainsKeywordEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This creature gets &lt;±P/±T&gt; and gains &lt;kw&gt; until end of turn" — a single-sentence TWO-clause activated effect that neither `ModifyPTEffectRule` nor `GainAbilityEffectRule` handles alone.

<b>CR 613.4c</b> (P/T modifier clause): "Layer 7c: Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied." The granted keyword is a continuous ability grant that applies in layer 6 (ability-adding effects). Both clauses are present in oracle text; this parser describes them without encoding layer machinery.

Returns a `CompositeEffect` whose child list carries, in order:

A `ModifyPTEffect` targeting Self with EOT duration. A `GainAbilityEffect` targeting Self, the keyword ability, and EOT duration.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/GetsPTAndGainsKeywordEffectRule.cs)

### `InvestigateEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Investigate." — CR 701.16a: "Investigate" means "Create a Clue token." See rule 111.10f. Maps the bare keyword action to `InvestigateEffect` with no count (defaults to one Clue token). Reminder text has already been stripped by the activated-ability parser before this rule runs (Rule 207.2).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/InvestigateEffectRule.cs)

### `KarnWishEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

"You may reveal an artifact card you own from outside the game or choose a face-up artifact card you own in exile. Put that card into your hand." — Karn, the Great Creator's −2 loyalty ability. The controller optionally retrieves an artifact card they own from outside the game (sideboard, CR 400.11) or from face-up exile (CR 406) and puts it into their hand.

Modelled as an `OptionalEffect` whose `Inner` is a `WishEffect` (ADR 0005: "You may" is the wrapper's presence, not a bool). The `WishEffect` records the two retrieval sources (`OutsideGame` and `Exile`), the `ObjectFilter` scoping the card to "artifact" owned by you, and `FaceUpOnly=true` for the exile branch (only face-up exiled cards qualify). Putting the card into hand is the inherent outcome of the Wish action and is recorded in the `WishEffect` node itself — the separate "Put that card into your hand." sentence is consumed as part of the same semantic unit (CR 400.11).

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` because the two oracle sentences ("You may … or choose …" and "Put that card into your hand.") form a single semantic action. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-sentence path never fires. `TryMatchMulti` matches the full two-sentence form anchored at both ends.

CR 400.11: cards brought into the game from outside the game remain until the game ends, the owner leaves, or a rule removes them.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/KarnWishEffectRule.cs)

### `KinnanTopLookEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Recognises the Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy activated ability effect: "Look at the top five cards of your library. You may put a non-Human creature card from among them onto the battlefield. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order."

The three-sentence fragment is one atomic action — the "from among them" and "the rest" back-reference the same looked-at pile — and is emitted as a single `TopLookPutOntoBattlefieldEffect`. Splitting sentences would break the pile-binding. CR 701.12 (look); CR 400.7 (onto the battlefield); CR 400.4 (random order).

The non-Human creature filter is encoded as `CardTypes=["creature"], ExcludedSubtypes=["Human"]` per `ExcludedSubtypes` semantics (parallel to the Mutate "target non-Human creature" shape). CR 205.3m (creature subtypes).

Priority 95: must beat generic look-at-top sentence dispatch.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/KinnanTopLookEffectRule.cs)

### `LookAtTopCardsPutBackEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Look at the top N cards of your library, then put them back in any order." — Sensei's Divining Top's "{1}:" ability. The activated-ability sibling of `LookAtTopCardsTriggeredRule`.

This is a SINGLE `LookAtCardsEffect`: the ", then put them back in any order" clause is the look's disposition (carried by `PutBackInAnyOrder`), not a second sibling effect. CR 701.12 (look) does not define a default disposition, so the reorder is explicit.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/LookAtTopCardsPutBackEffectRule.cs)

### `LookAtTopNPutOneInHandRestBottomActivatedRule` — *sealed class*

"Look at the top N cards of your library. Put one of them into your hand and the other on the bottom of your library." — or "the rest on the bottom of your library [in any order]." The activated-ability Impulse family for both two-card and multi-card variants.

Two surface variants share the same `ImpulseEffect` representation:

"the other on the bottom of your library" — singular "other" (Teferi, Temporal Archmage +1; only 2 cards so there is exactly one unchosen card). "the rest on the bottom of your library in any order" — plural "rest" (Anticipate, Impulse). Semantically identical for the AST.

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` — the two-sentence oracle text cannot be split independently ("them" in the second sentence back-references the look set of the first). `TryMatch` always returns null; only the multi-rule path is served.

CR 701.12 (look at cards); CR 400.4 (order at bottom). Rule 606.3 (loyalty ability activation timing) — this rule is used in both loyalty and non-loyalty activated-ability contexts.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/LookAtTopNPutOneInHandRestBottomActivatedRule.cs)

### `LoseLifeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target player loses N life." — targeted life-loss as an activated-ability effect (Rule 119), covering drain artifacts like Onyx Goblet.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/LoseLifeEffectRule.cs)

### `ManaCostComponentRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Mana / tap / untap cost component: "{1}", "{2}{G}", "{T}", "{Q}". Returns a `TapCost` for {T}, an `UntapCost` for {Q}, otherwise a `ManaCost`. Only fires for components containing a mana brace.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ManaCostComponentRule.cs)

### `MassModifyPTActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"All creatures get -N/-M until end of turn" (and siblings: "Creatures you control get ...", "Creatures your opponents control get ...", "Attacking/ Blocking creatures get ...") appearing as the RESOLUTION EFFECT of an activated ability — e.g. Bone Flute's "{2}, {T}: All creatures get -1/-0 until end of turn."

CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as '[Cost]: [Effect.] [Instructions (if any).]'" — the cost ("{2}, {T}") and the effect ("All creatures get -1/-0 until end of turn") are separate composable nodes; `ActivatedAbilityParser` already splits the cost half off, so this rule only recognises the effect half.

CR 613.4c: "Layer 7c: Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied." — "get -1/-0 until end of turn" is a layer-7c P/T modification, hence a `ModifyPTEffect` built from literal modifiers over an `Each`-kind subject, not a set-P/T effect.

This is a NEW, collision-free file rather than an edit to `ModifyPTEffectRule` (whose Shape D only matches the singular "Creatures you control get ..." subject, not "All creatures ...") or to `MassAnthemSpellRule`: `IActivatedEffectRule`'s `Effect? TryMatch(string effectText)` is a thin wrap of `ISpellRule`'s `bool TryMatch(string text, out Effect? effect)`, so this rule simply delegates to a stateless `MassAnthemSpellRule` instance, reusing the exact node the spell parser already produces for the identical surface (verified against CowerInFear.json / Charge.json gold). This mirrors the in-repo precedent in `MassModifyPTTriggeredRule`, which delegates the same way for the triggered-ability surface.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/MassModifyPTActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `MillTargetPlayerEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability mill keyword action. CR 701.17a: "For a player to mill a number of cards, that player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard." Handles the targeted-player form used by activated abilities: "Target player mills N cards." "Target opponent mills N cards." For the spell-resolution side see `MillSpellRule`. For the triggered-ability side see `MillTriggeredRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/MillTargetPlayerEffectRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target creature gets [+-](N|X)/[+-](M|X) (until end of turn | for as long as [condition])." and the self-referential "This creature gets …" variant. Handles literal and variable modifiers; variable negation is a CalculatedQuantity with Operation = "negate" (see `ParseSignedModifier`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ModifyPTEffectRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTTargetAttackingCreatureEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target attacking creature gets [+-](N|X)/[+-](M|X) until end of turn." — the from-hand bloodrush pump (e.g. Rubblebelt Maaka, "Bloodrush — {R}, Discard this card: Target attacking creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn.").

Distinct from `ModifyPTEffectRule`'s "Target creature gets …" shape: the target is narrowed to an <em>attacking</em> creature, carried as the state-predicate residual `Characteristic.InCombat(CombatState.Attacking)` per ADR 0001 (no first-class ObjectFilter field for combat state) — mirroring how "Attacking creatures get …" (Goblin Oriflamme) and "Destroy target attacking creature" (Immolating Glare) already encode the attacking filter.

"Bloodrush" itself is an ability word with no rules meaning (CR 207.2c — bloodrush is explicitly listed among the ability words); the classifier captures it onto the activated ability's `AbilityWord` label. The P/T modifier is a layer-7c effect (CR 613.4c) — it adds to power/toughness without setting them.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ModifyPTTargetAttackingCreatureEffectRule.cs)

### `MonstrosityEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Monstrosity N" — maps the keyword-action to a `MonstrosityEffect`.

CR 701.37a: "Monstrosity N means 'If this permanent isn't monstrous, put N +1/+1 counters on it and it becomes monstrous.'" CR 701.37b: "Monstrous is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that the monstrosity action and other spells and abilities can identify."

The parenthetical reminder text "(If this creature isn't monstrous, put N +1/+1 counters on it and it becomes monstrous.)" is stripped upstream by `ActivatedAbilityParser.StripTrailingReminder` before this rule fires.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/MonstrosityEffectRule.cs)

### `NextInstantSorceryCastFromHandReturnInsteadEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"The next time you cast an instant or sorcery spell from your hand this turn, put that card into your hand instead of into your graveyard as it resolves." — Soulfire Grand Master's activated-ability effect.

This is the once-form "next … this turn" delayed shield (CR 603.7: "An effect may create a delayed triggered ability that can do something at a later time. A delayed triggered ability will contain 'when,' 'whenever,' or 'at,' although that word won't usually begin the ability.") over the buyback-style zone-change replacement of CR 702.27a ("...put this spell into its owner's hand instead of into that player's graveyard as it resolves."). Mirrors `NextCastCopySpellDelayedRule` (Doublecast's "When you next cast an instant or sorcery spell this turn, copy that spell.") exactly for the trigger half — same `SpellCast` event, same `CardTypes = ["spell", "instant", "sorcery"]` type-disjunction filter, same `When` ("next" is the once-form of an event trigger, composed with the this-turn `Window` rather than a separate field), same `EndOfTurn` window — but reached via the ACTIVATED-ability registry (this ability has a mana cost, not a spell body) and carrying an added "from your hand" qualifier on the filter (`Zone = Zone.Hand` — per `ExcludedZone`'s documented convention, a stated zone other than `Stack` on a `CardTypes=["spell", ...]` filter is shorthand for the pre-cast origin zone, so a POSITIVE `Zone = Zone.Hand` names "cast from your hand").

The resolution effect is the SAME shape `BuybackStaticRule`'s Ability 2 already emits for CR 702.27a's identical "put this spell into its owner's hand instead of into that player's graveyard as it resolves" clause — a `ReplacementEffect` over a `ZoneChangeEvent` (origin stack, destination graveyard) with `OriginalEventOccurs = false` ("instead") and a `ReturnToHandEffect` as the replacement action — except the affected object here is not "this spell" (`Self`) but the delayed trigger's anaphoric "that card", i.e. the spell that just matched the trigger filter, so the `Target` is `It` (CR 109.2) rather than `Self`. Timing ("as it resolves") is the natural clock of the zone-change event, not baked into the effect discriminator.

Anchored (^…$) to the exact surface, so it cannot collide with any sibling activated-effect rule. Priority 80: above the general-purpose activated rule band (50) — no other activated rule shares this "the next time you cast … put that card" opening.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/NextInstantSorceryCastFromHandReturnInsteadEffectRule.cs)

### `PayEnergyCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

"Pay N {E}" — energy-counter payment as an activation cost. Rule 107.14: The energy symbol is {E}; each represents one energy counter removed from the player.

Oracle text may use three forms:

Word-number form: "Pay eight {E}" — word encodes count, symbol names currency. Pay-symbols form: "Pay {E}{E}{E}" — "Pay" prefix + pure symbol repetition; count derived from symbol occurrences (e.g., Whirler Virtuoso, Aetherworks Marvel). Symbol-only form: "{E}{E}{E}" — no "Pay" prefix; count from symbol occurrences.

MAST always emits the declared amount as a LiteralQuantity.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PayEnergyCostRule.cs)

### `PayLifeCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Pay-life cost: "Pay 1 life", "Pay 3 life" (Rule 118). The life payment is a cost that reduces the player's life total.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PayLifeCostRule.cs)

### `PhaseOutTargetEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target creature you don't control phases out." — Teferi, Master of Time −3 loyalty ability. Causes the targeted creature to phase out (CR 702.26) until its controller's next untap step.

CR 702.26a (verbatim): "Phasing is a static ability that modifies the rules of the untap step. During each player's untap step, before the active player untaps permanents, all phased-in permanents with phasing that player controls 'phase out.' Simultaneously, all phased-out permanents that had phased out under that player's control 'phase in.'"

CR 702.26b: "If a permanent phases out, its status changes to 'phased out.' Except for rules and effects that specifically mention phased-out permanents, a phased-out permanent is treated as though it does not exist."

"You don't control" maps to `Opponent` (CR 109.5: an object "you don't control" is controlled by another player — effectively an opponent in the context of targeted effects).

The parenthetical reminder "(Treat it and anything attached to it as though they don't exist until its controller's next turn.)" is stripped by `ActivatedAbilityParser`'s `StripTrailingReminder` before this rule sees the text.

ANCHORED (^...$): prevents partial matches inside broader phase-out effect text. Priority 982 — specific shape, below generic exile (983) but above fallback.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PhaseOutTargetEffectRule.cs)

### `PoisonCounterDifferenceEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"If target player has fewer than nine poison counters, they get a number of poison counters equal to the difference." — Vraska, Betrayal's Sting's −9 loyalty ability.

A `ConditionalEffect` whose condition is an `OtherCondition` ("target player has fewer than nine poison counters") and whose `Then` branch is a `PutCountersEffect` giving that player a `CalculatedQuantity` equal to `"the difference"` (i.e. 9 minus the current poison counter count — engine territory per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine; MAST records the reference, not the resolved value).

CR 122 (counters); CR 704.5c: "If a player has ten or more poison counters, that player loses the game." The ability targets the player (CR 115.6); the target reference is `Target` with a `CardTypes = ["player"]` filter.

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the phrase "fewer than nine poison counters" does not appear in any other sibling rule, but anchoring prevents accidental substring matches.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PoisonCounterDifferenceEffectRule.cs)

### `PreventAllCombatDamageByTargetCreatureThisTurnEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability effect shape "Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt by target creature this turn." — the source-scoped Fog-effect prevention shield activated from a permanent (e.g. Safeguard: "{2}{W}: Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt by target creature this turn."). The mana cost half is parsed independently; this rule only recognizes the post-colon effect body. The "by target creature" qualifier scopes the shield to a single damage SOURCE (the targeted creature) rather than being blanket. It therefore maps to the `Source` reference — a `Target` filtered to `CardTypes=["creature"]` — and NOT to `Target` (which is the damage recipient). This is the source-scoped sibling of the blanket `PreventAllCombatDamageThisTurnActivatedEffectRule`, producing the same combat-only, until-end-of-turn, all-instances (`All`) prevention shield. CR 615.1 (cited verbatim from rules-structure.json): "Some continuous effects are prevention effects. Like replacement effects (see rule 614), prevention effects apply continuously as events happen-they aren't locked in ahead of time. Such effects watch for a damage event that would happen and completely or partially prevent the damage that would be dealt. They act like \"shields\" around whatever they're affecting." ANCHORED (^...$): the surface phrase is matched whole so it cannot be consumed as a substring of a longer clause, and cannot claim a substring of a more specific sibling. The "by target creature" segment sits between "dealt" and "this turn", so the blanket sibling's regex (which requires "dealt this turn" contiguously) never matches this text and vice versa — the two are disjoint.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PreventAllCombatDamageByTargetCreatureThisTurnEffectRule.cs)

### `PreventAllCombatDamageThisTurnActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability effect shape "Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt this turn." — the Fog-effect prevention shield activated from a permanent (e.g. Kami of False Hope: "Sacrifice this creature: Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt this turn."). The cost half (the sacrifice) is parsed independently; this rule only recognizes the post-colon effect body. This is the activated-ability sibling of the spell rule `PreventAllCombatDamageThisTurnRule` (Fog), producing an identical `PreventDamageEffect`: a blanket (no target), combat-only, until-end-of-turn prevention shield. CR 615.1 (cited verbatim from rules-structure.json): "Some continuous effects are prevention effects. Like replacement effects (see rule 614), prevention effects apply continuously as events happen-they aren't locked in ahead of time. Such effects watch for a damage event that would happen and completely or partially prevent the damage that would be dealt. They act like \"shields\" around whatever they're affecting." ANCHORED (^...$): the surface phrase is matched whole so it cannot be consumed as a substring of a longer clause, and cannot claim a substring of a more specific sibling ("Prevent the next N damage …", "The next time a [color] source …"). Those siblings are structurally disjoint from this blanket phrase, but explicit anchoring is the project standard.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PreventAllCombatDamageThisTurnActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `PreventNextDamageFromChosenSourceEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"The next time a source of your choice would deal damage to you this turn, prevent that damage." — the uncoloured one-shot prevention shield with no source restriction (e.g. Pentagram of the Ages, Haazda Shield Mate, Invulnerability, Righteous Aura). This is the sibling of `PreventNextDamageFromColorSourceEffectRule` (the "a [color] source of your choice" Circle/Rune-of-Protection variant): same CR-615.8 next-instance shield, but the designated source carries no colour/type filter — the controller may name any source ("a source of your choice"). Maps to `PreventDamageEffect` with `NextInstance` set (the "next instance, regardless of amount" semantics — distinct from a bounded `Amount` or the all-instances `All`), the damage `Source` as an unfiltered `Designated` reference (any source, controller-chosen — not a target, no targeting keyword in the oracle), the `Target` (recipient) as `You`, and an `untilTime`/end-of-turn `Duration` for "this turn". "of your choice" is recorded as the player-designated reference itself, not its resolution (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution). This is CR-615 prevention, NOT a replacement effect — no replacement ordering/layering is modelled. The pattern is anchored `^…prevent that damage$` so it matches ONLY the standalone uncoloured "to you" line: it cannot fire on the coloured/typed siblings ("a red source", "an artifact source"), a different recipient ("to target creature", "to any target"), or the qualified variants ("… with art by …", "… of the chosen color …") — each carries extra tokens between the fixed anchors and so fails the match. CR 615.8 (cited verbatim): "Some prevention effects generated by the resolution of a spell or ability refer to the next time a specific source would deal damage. These effects prevent the next instance of damage from that source, regardless of how much damage that is. Once an instance of damage from that source has been prevented, any subsequent instances of damage that would be dealt by that source are dealt normally." CR 615.2 (cited verbatim): "Many prevention effects apply to damage from a source. See rule 609.7."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PreventNextDamageFromChosenSourceEffectRule.cs)

### `PreventNextDamageFromChosenSourceToAnyTargetEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"The next time a source of your choice would deal damage to any target this turn, prevent that damage." — the one-shot prevention shield with no source restriction whose recipient is "any target" rather than "you" (e.g. Martyr's Cause, Circle of Despair, Sanctum Guardian). This is the "to any target" sibling of `PreventNextDamageFromChosenSourceEffectRule` (the "to you" variant): same CR-615.8 next-instance shield, same controller-chosen unfiltered designated source, but the protected recipient is `AnyTarget` (matching how `PreventNextNDamageToAnyTargetEffectRule` records "any target"). Maps to `PreventDamageEffect` with `NextInstance` set (the "next instance, regardless of amount" semantics — distinct from a bounded `Amount` or the all-instances `All`), the damage `Source` as an unfiltered `Designated` reference (any source, controller-chosen — not a target, no targeting keyword in the oracle), the `Target` (recipient) as `AnyTarget`, and an `untilTime`/end-of-turn `Duration` for "this turn". "of your choice" is recorded as the player-designated reference itself, not its resolution (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution). This is CR-615 prevention, NOT a replacement effect — no replacement ordering/layering is modelled. The pattern is anchored `^…prevent that damage$` so it matches ONLY the standalone uncoloured "to any target" line: it cannot fire on the "to you" sibling, the coloured/typed variants ("a red source"), or the qualified follow-ups (e.g. Honorable Passage's "… If damage from a red source is prevented this way …"), each of which carries extra tokens outside the fixed anchors. CR 615.8 (cited verbatim): "Some prevention effects generated by the resolution of a spell or ability refer to the next time a specific source would deal damage. These effects prevent the next instance of damage from that source, regardless of how much damage that is. Once an instance of damage from that source has been prevented, any subsequent instances of damage that would be dealt by that source are dealt normally." CR 615.2 (cited verbatim): "Many prevention effects apply to damage from a source. See rule 609.7."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PreventNextDamageFromChosenSourceToAnyTargetEffectRule.cs)

### `PreventNextDamageFromColorSourceEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"The next time a [color] source of your choice would deal damage to you this turn, prevent that damage." — the Circle/Rune of Protection one-shot prevention shield (e.g. Circle of Protection: Red, Rune of Protection: Red). Maps to `PreventDamageEffect` with `NextInstance` set (the "next instance, regardless of amount" semantics — distinct from a bounded `Amount` or the all-instances `All`), the damage `Source` as a `Designated` reference filtered by the named color ("a red source of your choice" — the controller designates which qualifying source at resolution; not a target, no targeting keyword in the oracle, and not controller-bound), the `Target` (recipient) as `You`, and an `untilTime`/end-of-turn `Duration` for "this turn". "of your choice" is recorded as the player-designated reference itself, not its resolution (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution). This is CR-615 prevention, NOT a replacement effect — no replacement ordering/layering is modelled. CR 615.8 (cited verbatim): "Some prevention effects generated by the resolution of a spell or ability refer to the next time a specific source would deal damage. These effects prevent the next instance of damage from that source, regardless of how much damage that is. Once an instance of damage from that source has been prevented, any subsequent instances of damage that would be dealt by that source are dealt normally." CR 615.2 (cited verbatim): "Many prevention effects apply to damage from a source. See rule 609.7."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PreventNextDamageFromColorSourceEffectRule.cs)

### `PreventNextNDamageToAnyTargetEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Prevent the next N damage that would be dealt to any target this turn." Maps to `PreventDamageEffect` with a literal `Amount`, `AnyTarget` as the `Target`, and an `untilEndOfTurn` `Duration`. CR 615.8 (cited verbatim): "Some prevention effects generated by the resolution of a spell or ability refer to the next time a specific source would deal damage. These effects prevent the next instance of damage from that source, regardless of how much damage that is."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PreventNextNDamageToAnyTargetEffectRule.cs)

### `PreventNextNDamageToTargetCreatureEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Prevent the next N damage that would be dealt to target creature this turn." (Kei Takahashi's activated ability.) Maps to `PreventDamageEffect` with a literal `Amount`, a `Target` reference filtered to `CardTypes=["creature"]` as the `Target`, and an `untilEndOfTurn` `Duration`. The creature-targeted sibling of `PreventNextNDamageToAnyTargetEffectRule`. This is a bounded-amount prevention shield, distinct from the "next instance" (Circle/Rune of Protection) shield. CR 615.7 (cited verbatim): "Some prevention effects generated by the resolution of a spell or ability refer to a specific amount of damage-for example, "Prevent the next 3 damage that would be dealt to any target this turn." These work like shields. Each 1 damage that would be dealt to the "shielded" permanent or player is prevented. Preventing 1 damage reduces the remaining shield by 1. ... Once the shield has been reduced to 0, any remaining damage is dealt normally. Such effects count only the amount of damage; the number of events or sources dealing it doesn't matter."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PreventNextNDamageToTargetCreatureEffectRule.cs)

### `ProliferateActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Proliferate." as a standalone activated-ability effect sentence (CR 701.27, CR 701.34).

This mirrors `ProliferateSpellRule` for the spell-parser registry but lives in the activated-effect registry so that `TryParseMultiEffectSentences` can resolve the "Proliferate." fragment that appears as the second sentence of Vraska, Betrayal's Sting's 0-ability ("You draw a card and lose 1 life. Proliferate.").

Priority is set high (999) so this fires before any broader pattern can claim a sentence that starts with "Proliferate".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ProliferateActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `PutCountersCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

"Put a -1/-1 counter on this creature" / "Put a +1/+1 counter on this permanent" — a cost that places one or more counters on this permanent as part of activating an ability (Devoted Druid: "Put a -1/-1 counter on this creature: Untap this creature.").

CR 122.1: "A counter is a marker placed on an object or player that modifies its characteristics and/or interacts with a rule, ability, or effect." CR 602.1a: "The activation cost is everything before the colon (:)." Placing a counter is a valid activation cost; this rule is anchored (^…$) to prevent matching an effect sentence that also contains "put" and "counter".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PutCountersCostRule.cs)

### `PutCountersEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Put N +1/+1 (or -1/-1) counters on [target]" — "Put a +1/+1 counter on this creature", "Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control", "Put a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control" (Leyline of Abundance).

Also handles named counters in the activated path — "Put a storage counter on this land", "Put a charge counter on this artifact" (the storage- land / charge-artifact "load" abilities). CR 122.1: a counter is a marker placed on an object; storage/charge are named counters, the same placement action as +1/+1. Mirrors the named-counter branch already in the triggered PutCounters rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PutCountersEffectRule.cs)

### `PutFromHandOntoBattlefieldEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"[You may ]put a[n] &lt;filter&gt; card from your hand onto the battlefield[ tapped[ and attacking that opponent]]."

Handles the Sakura-Tribe Scout / Kodama of the East Tree pattern reached via an activated (rather than triggered) ability: an optional zone-change that moves a card directly from the controller's hand to the battlefield. Per CR 305.4, "putting" a land onto the battlefield this way is explicitly NOT "playing a land" and does not count against the turn's land-play limit (CR 116.2a describes the distinct "play a land" special action this effect is NOT).

Rule citations:

CR 305.4 — "Effects may also allow players to 'put' lands onto the battlefield. This isn't the same as 'playing a land' and doesn't count as a land played during the current turn." CR 116.2a — "Playing a land is a special action. To play a land, a player puts that land onto the battlefield from the zone it was in (usually that player's hand). By default, a player can take this action only once during each of their turns. A player can take this action any time they have priority and the stack is empty during a main phase of their turn. See rule 305, 'Lands.'" CR 602.1a — the activation cost / effect split at the colon.

Priority 64 — below `SearchLibraryToBattlefieldEffectRule` (65) and above the generic fallback rules. The pattern is fully anchored (^...$) so it cannot match as a substring of a more-complex sibling effect. Duplicated (rather than shared) from the triggered-ability sibling `PutFromHandOntoBattlefieldTriggeredRule` because that rule implements a different interface (`ITriggeredRule`) and sharing would require touching a hot shared file.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PutFromHandOntoBattlefieldEffectRule.cs)

### `PutNamedCounterThenDrawPerCounterRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Put a [counter] counter on [self], then draw a card for each [counter] counter on [self]" — The One Ring's {T} ability ("Put a burden counter on The One Ring, then draw a card for each burden counter on The One Ring").

A two-step `CompositeEffect`: (1) `PutCountersEffect` adds one named counter to the source (`Self`); (2) `DrawCardsEffect` draws a card for each such counter — `Count` is a `CounterCountQuantity` over the same named counter on the source, read AFTER the put (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004; the engine evaluates the live count). CR 122 (counters); CR 121 (draw). The same counter name must appear in both clauses.

The self target is "it" or the card naming itself (capitalized → self-reference, CR 201.5). ANCHORED on the full clause.

Priority 999: must run BEFORE the generic `DrawCardsEffectRule` (Priority 998), which otherwise greedily claims the sentence's "draw a card" clause as a flat `drawCards` and drops the put-counter clause + the per-counter scaling. This rule is strictly more specific (it owns the full anchored put-then-draw-per-counter shape).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PutNamedCounterThenDrawPerCounterRule.cs)

### `PutSelfFromCommandZoneOntoBattlefieldEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Put [SelfName] onto the battlefield from the command zone." — the Commander-zone recast activated ability (Derevi, Empyrial Tactician, C13).

This ability functions from the command zone: the card puts itself onto the battlefield without being cast, bypassing the normal casting rules. The effect is modelled as `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect` with `Self` source zone `CommandZone`. The use of `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect` (rather than a dedicated node) is intentional — both graveryard-reanimate and command-zone activate share the "move from [zone] to battlefield" action (CR 400.7); the `Filter.Zone` discriminates the source zone for clustering (command-zone put vs. graveyard reanimate vs. hand put).

CR 903.9a (Commander zone ability): "Each time a commander would be put into its owner's library, hand, graveyard or exile from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead." Derevi's ability is an activated out-of-band re-entry that avoids the normal casting-tax accumulation by bypassing the cast.

The self-name is one or more title-case name words (capitalised content words and optional lowercase function words) followed by "onto the battlefield from the command zone". The pattern is anchored (^…$) to prevent substring-matching a broader effect sentence. Rule 201.5: "A card's text may refer to itself by its own name as a shorthand for 'this object'" — the name is a self-reference (IsSelf=true on the filter), not a generic card selector.

Rule 701.26 (Tap and Untap) is not involved here; CR 400.7 governs zone changes.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PutSelfFromCommandZoneOntoBattlefieldEffectRule.cs)

### `PutTargetCardFromAGraveyardOnBottomOfOwnersLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability graveyard-to-library-bottom zone change. CR 602.1: activated abilities are written as "[Cost]: [Effect.]" — this rule recognizes the post-colon effect fragment. Handles the "any graveyard" targeted form (the source's own player is not constrained), where the destination is explicitly the moved card's OWNER's library rather than the activating player's: "Put target card from a graveyard on the bottom of its owner's library." Distinct from `PutTargetGraveyardCardOnBottomRule`, which handles the "your graveyard" / "its owner's graveyard" possessive forms — those two regexes are mutually exclusive (one requires a possessive before "graveyard", this one requires the bare article "a"), so neither can shadow the other. Not a defined keyword action (Rule 701.x has no "put on the bottom" entry); this is a plain-language zone-change verb governed by CR 400.7 (a moved object becomes a new object) and CR 401 (library-ordering rules). The paradigmatic instance is Chrome Companion's "{2}, {T}: Put target card from a graveyard on the bottom of its owner's library."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PutTargetCardFromAGraveyardOnBottomOfOwnersLibraryRule.cs)

### `PutTargetGraveyardCardOnBottomRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability graveyard-to-library-bottom zone change. CR 602.1: activated abilities are written as "[Cost]: [Effect.]" — this rule recognizes the post-colon effect fragment. Handles the targeted single-card form: "Put target card from your graveyard on the bottom of your library." Not a defined keyword action (Rule 701.x has no "put on the bottom" entry); this is a plain-language zone-change verb governed by CR 400.7 (a moved object becomes a new object) and CR 401 (library-ordering rules). The paradigmatic instance is Barkform Harvester's "{2}: Put target card from your graveyard on the bottom of your library."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/PutTargetGraveyardCardOnBottomRule.cs)

### `RedirectNextNDamageToTargetCreatureYouControlRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"The next N damage that would be dealt to this creature this turn is dealt to target creature you control instead." — the {0} en-Kor damage-redirection family (Warrior en-Kor, Nomads en-Kor, …).

Maps to `RedirectDamageEffect` with a literal `Amount`, `Self()` as `From` ("this creature"), a "target creature you control" `Target` reference as `To`, and an end-of-turn `Duration` ("this turn").

CR 602.1 (verbatim): "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as \"[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]\" …" — this is the post-colon effect fragment of the {0} activated ability.

CR 614.1 (verbatim): "Some continuous effects are replacement effects … Such effects watch for a particular event that would happen and completely or partially replace it …" — the redirection is a one-shot, turn-scoped replacement shield.

The regex is fully anchored (`^…$`) so it cannot match a substring of another card's effect text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/RedirectNextNDamageToTargetCreatureYouControlRule.cs)

### `RegenerateEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Regenerate this creature." / "Regenerate target [type]." (Rule 701.19). MAST records the effect and target only; shield / destruction-replacement semantics are engine territory.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/RegenerateEffectRule.cs)

### `RegenerateSelfByNameEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Regenerate [SelfName]." — the keyword action of CR 701.19a, where the regenerated permanent is referred to by its own printed name rather than "this creature"/"this permanent" (Silvos, Rogue Elemental: "{G}: Regenerate Silvos.").

CR 701.19a: "If the effect of a resolving spell or ability regenerates a permanent, it creates a replacement effect that protects the permanent the next time it would be destroyed this turn. In this case, "Regenerate [permanent]" means "The next time [permanent] would be destroyed this turn, instead remove all damage marked on it and its controller taps it. If it's an attacking or blocking creature, remove it from combat."" MAST records the effect's presence and target only; the shield / destruction-replacement semantics are engine territory (see `RegenerateEffect`).

CR 201.5: "Text that refers to the object it's on by name means just that particular object and not any other objects with that name, regardless of any name changes caused by game effects." Its own on-point example: "{BB}: Regenerate Skithiryx" resolves to the object the ability is printed on. `TryMatch` has no card-name parameter, so — per the established self-by-name doctrine also used by `PutSelfFromCommandZoneOntoBattlefieldEffectRule` and the "deals damage" self rule — a capitalised proper-noun in the regenerated- object slot is treated as a self-reference (`Self`).

The pattern requires the first word after "Regenerate" to be capitalised, which keeps it disjoint from every branch of the generic `RegenerateEffectRule` (all of which begin with a lowercase token: "this", "enchanted", "equipped", "target"), so the two rules never collide regardless of relative priority.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/RegenerateSelfByNameEffectRule.cs)

### `RemoveCountersCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Remove-counters cost: "Remove three spore counters from this creature" / "Remove two charge counters from this permanent" (Rule 122). The counter type is a named counter; the source is `Self()` since oracle text always reads "from this creature / permanent".
