Beyond the literal counts, scaling-mana costs (ADR 0009) also match "Remove X [type] counters from this [noun]" → `VariableQuantity.X` (CR 107.3) and "Remove any number of [type] counters from this [noun]" → `AnyAmountQuantity`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/RemoveCountersCostRule.cs)

### `ReturnAllFromGraveyardToBattlefieldRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return all [type] cards from your graveyard to the battlefield [tapped]." Mass-recursion pattern — e.g. Aftermath Analyst's activated ability. CR 701 (zone change); CR 400.1 (zones); the optional "tapped" entering status is CR 110.5b. Anchored on "Return all" prefix so it cannot match sibling single-target rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnAllFromGraveyardToBattlefieldRule.cs)

### `ReturnCountTargetPermanentsToOwnersHandsEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return X target creatures to their owners' hands." — the multi-target bounce whose target set has a variable (or literal) cardinality, e.g. Alexi, Zephyr Mage: "{X}{U}, {T}, Discard two cards: Return X target creatures to their owners' hands." Handles a variable count (X/Y/Z) or a literal count ("two", "3") over a PLURAL permanent type ("creatures", "artifacts", …) returned to their owners' hands (plural possessive, because there are multiple returned permanents with potentially different owners).

The cardinality rides on `Quantity` — the documented home for "N target" / "up to N target" phrasings — rather than a bespoke Count field on `ReturnToHandEffect`. This mirrors the sibling `ReturnUpToOneTargetTypeDisjunctionToHandEffectRule` (which uses `UpToQuantity` on the reference) and Frost Breath's "up to two target creatures" tap. A variable X becomes `VariableQuantity`; the ability's {X} in its activation cost defines that value (CR 107.3 — "Many objects use the letter X as a placeholder for a number that needs to be determined").

CR 400.3: "If an object would go to any library, graveyard, or hand other than its owner's, it goes to its owner's corresponding zone." CR 402.1: the hand is a zone; returning an object to hand is a zone change stated directly (no keyword action). CR 108.3: "The owner of a card in the game is the player who started the game with it in their deck." CR 115.1: "target" declares the affected objects.

ANCHOR: the pattern is anchored (^…$) on the full clause and is disjoint from the single-target sibling `ReturnTargetToHandEffectRule` (which matches "Return target <type> … its owner's hand", singular) and from `ReturnUpToOneTargetTypeDisjunctionToHandEffectRule` ("up to one target … its owner's hand", singular hand). This rule requires an explicit count token, a PLURAL type, and the PLURAL "their owners' hands", so no sibling's phrase is a substring of, or subsumes, this one.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnCountTargetPermanentsToOwnersHandsEffectRule.cs)

### `ReturnFromGraveyardToHandEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return this card from your graveyard to your hand." — the self-retrieval pattern on activated abilities (e.g. Abzan Devotee). Models a graveyard-to-hand zone change where the source zone is the controller's graveyard (CR 404) and the destination is the controller's hand (CR 402). The permanent is in the graveyard at the time the cost is paid and ability resolves; Target = Self with a Graveyard zone qualifier captures both the identity of the object and its source zone. Anchored on "from your graveyard" to avoid matching battlefield-self bounce (F6 sibling: "to its owner's hand"), which has no graveyard source qualifier.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnFromGraveyardToHandEffectRule.cs)

### `ReturnLandSubtypeToHandCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Return-a-land-you-control-to-hand cost: "Return a Forest you control to its owner's hand" — Quirion Ranger (CR 602); "Return a land you control to its owner's hand" — Trench Behemoth. Distinct from `ReturnSelfToHandCostRule` (self-bounce) and the effect-position `ReturnSelfToHandEffectRule`: this is a return of a controller-chosen permanent as the activation cost. The returned permanent is a land — identified EITHER by a land subtype (Forest/Island/Swamp/Mountain/Plains and the nonbasic land types, CR 205.3i) OR by the bare card type "land" (CR 300.1 / 205.2a). CR 118.3: any game action may be a cost; CR 602: activated abilities have a cost before the colon. The cost here moves the chosen land to its owner's hand as part of paying. ObjectReferenceKind.Any (not Target): the controller selects any qualifying permanent at activation time — not a legal target (Rule 115.1 — "target" requires the word "target").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnLandSubtypeToHandCostRule.cs)

### `ReturnNamedToHandEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return [CardName] to its owner's hand." — a named-card self-bounce effect where the card refers to itself by its printed name (CR 201.4). Paradigm card: KHM Toralf's Hammer: "… Return Toralf's Hammer to its owner's hand." MAST resolves the self-reference to `Self`.

Distinct from `ReturnSelfToHandEffectRule`, which handles the self-referential pronoun form "Return this [noun] to its owner's hand." This rule handles the card-name form, where the card refers to itself by name rather than by a generic self-referential noun. Both map to the same `Self` reference.

Anchored (^…$) to prevent matching a substring of a longer clause. The card name is captured but not stored — all that matters for structuring is that this is a self-bounce effect; the name is engine-resolved at CR 201.4 and not threaded into the AST as a binding variable (ADR 0004: reference-not-resolution).

Priority 988 — just below `ReturnSelfToHandEffectRule` (989) so the self-referential noun form is tried first; this rule catches the card-name form that falls through.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnNamedToHandEffectRule.cs)

### `ReturnSelfFromGraveyardToBattlefieldEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped." — a graveyard-self reanimation activated ability (Drownyard Temple). The ability functions while the card is in its owner's graveyard; activating it returns the card itself (Self) from the graveyard to the battlefield, and the card enters tapped. Distinct from `ReturnToBattlefieldEffectRule` ("Return TARGET X from [zone] to the battlefield"): the subject here is the source card itself (CR 109.2 — "this card" refers to the object with the ability), expressed as a `Self` reference. The source zone "your graveyard" is the structured `Zone` Graveyard + `You`, not free text. CR 611.1 (verbatim): "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects, modifies control of objects, or affects players or the rules of the game, for a fixed or indefinite period." — the resolving ability changes the card's zone and returns it under its owner's control; the "tapped" entering state is a structured `Tapped` flag, not free text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnSelfFromGraveyardToBattlefieldEffectRule.cs)

### `ReturnSelfToHandCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Return-self-to-hand cost: "Return this creature to its owner's hand" (Grinning Ignus), "Return this enchantment to its owner's hand" (Recurring Nightmare), etc. — the activated permanent is moved to the Hand zone as part of paying the cost (CR 701.x), so it must be recast to use the ability again. Previously this clause, when in the <em>cost</em> position (before the colon), matched no cost rule and was silently dropped — leaving the ability's `Costs` incomplete (or empty). The companion `ReturnSelfToHandEffectRule` handles the same phrase in the <em>effect</em> position; the two run in different parsing phases, so they don't conflict. Mirrors `ExileSelfCostRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnSelfToHandCostRule.cs)

### `ReturnSelfToHandEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return this {creature|permanent|Aura} to its owner's hand." — battlefield-self bounce (CR 402, hand zone). Matches the self-referential phrasing found on creatures like Darting Merfolk and Auras like Mourning/Conviction. Distinct from `ReturnToBattlefieldEffectRule` (which handles graveyard-source reanimation) and the sibling F5 rule (which handles "from your graveyard" sourced returns). CR 402: Return to hand is a plain zone change to the Hand zone; no dedicated keyword action exists for it. CR 303.4(m): "An ability of a permanent that refers to the 'enchanted [object or player]' refers to whatever object or player that permanent is attached to, even if the permanent with the ability isn't an Aura." — the self-subject here is the Aura itself ("this Aura"), not the enchanted object, so Self is correct. Anchor: "return this &lt;noun&gt; to its owner's hand" where &lt;noun&gt; is a self-referential permanent-type word (creature, permanent, Aura, enchantment, artifact, land).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnSelfToHandEffectRule.cs)

### `ReturnTargetFromGraveyardToHandEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return target [type] card from your graveyard to your hand." — the targeted graveyard-to-hand retrieval as an activated-ability effect (Adun Oakenshield: "{B}{R}{G}, {T}: Return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand."). Also handles the untyped "Return target card from your graveyard to your hand."

The activated-ability analogue of the spell-side `ReturnFromGraveyardToHandRule`, producing the identical `ReturnToHandEffect` shape so both parsing paths model the same retrieval uniformly. Source zone is the controller's own graveyard (CR 404.1: a player's graveyard holds objects owned by that player), destination is the controller's hand (CR 402.1). No dedicated keyword action; the text is stated directly. "your graveyard" maps to `You` plus `Graveyard`, mirroring the spell rule's convention.

ANCHOR: the pattern is fully anchored (^…$) on the whole clause, so it cannot match as a substring of any more-specific sibling. It is distinct from the self-retrieval `ReturnFromGraveyardToHandEffectRule` ("Return this card from your graveyard…") and from the battlefield-bounce `ReturnTargetToHandEffectRule` ("…to its owner's hand"), which require different surface text and so never collide.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnTargetFromGraveyardToHandEffectRule.cs)

### `ReturnTargetInstantOrSorceryFromGraveyardToHandEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return target instant or sorcery card from your graveyard to your hand." — the graveyard-recursion effect on an activated ability (e.g. Scribe of the Mindful: "{1}, {T}, Sacrifice this creature: Return target instant or sorcery card from your graveyard to your hand.").

This is a zone change moving a targeted card from the controller's graveyard (source: CR 404.1) to the controller's hand (destination: CR 402.1). The activated path previously left this interior as an `UnstructuredEffect`; the identical shape is already structured on the triggered path (`ReturnInstantOrSorceryFromGraveyardRule`, Izzet Chronarch / Archaeomancer). Both emit the same `ReturnToHandEffect` so the effect is represented consistently regardless of the ability kind that carries it.

The filter encodes the stated restrictions directly: <c>CardTypes = ["instant", "sorcery"]</c> is the type disjunction, `Zone = Graveyard` the source zone, and `Controller = You` the "your graveyard" qualifier.

ANCHOR: the regex is fully anchored (`^…$`) on the complete effect clause, so it neither collides with the battlefield-bounce shape (`ReturnTargetToHandEffectRule`, "to its owner's hand") nor with the self-retrieval shapes. It runs at a high priority because it is a precise, fully specified clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnTargetInstantOrSorceryFromGraveyardToHandEffectRule.cs)

### `ReturnTargetToHandEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return target [type] [you control|an opponent controls] to its owner's hand." — the single-target battlefield-bounce as an activated-ability effect. Handles the most common permanent types (creature, artifact, enchantment, land, permanent, planeswalker) with an optional controller qualifier.

CR 402: returning an object to its owner's hand is a zone change from any zone to the Hand zone. No dedicated keyword action; the text is stated directly.

ANCHOR: pattern is anchored (^…$) on the full clause so it does not collide with the self-bounce rules (`ReturnSelfToHandEffectRule` at 989, `ReturnNamedToHandEffectRule` at 988) or the "up to one target" disjunction rule (`ReturnUpToOneTargetTypeDisjunctionToHandEffectRule` at 985). This rule runs at Priority 984 — below all of those — so they get first refusal on their tighter shapes.

Controller qualifier "you control" maps to `You`; "an opponent controls" maps to `Opponent`; absence of any qualifier leaves `Controller` null.

Rule 107.14 is not directly relevant here; this rule fires on the effect side of activated abilities. The zone-change semantics are CR 402 (hand zone). The owner's hand destination is the canonical phrasing for bounce (CR 109.5: a permanent's "owner" is the player who started with it in their library or starting hand).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnTargetToHandEffectRule.cs)

### `ReturnToBattlefieldEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return target [X] from [zone] to the battlefield." — e.g. "Return target creature or Vehicle card from your graveyard to the battlefield." The full type-phrase is captured as a Characteristics entry and the source zone on Zone.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnToBattlefieldEffectRule.cs)

### `ReturnUpToOneTargetTypeDisjunctionToHandEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Return up to one target [type1], [type2], or [type3] to its owner's hand." — the "up to one target" bounce with a card-type disjunction (e.g. "artifact, creature, or enchantment"). Models the multi-type target as a single `ReturnToHandEffect` whose `Target.Filter.CardTypes` is the disjunction of all named types — the filter is satisfied when the object has ANY of the listed types (OR semantics, CR 115.3).

CR 402: returning an object to its owner's hand is a zone change from any zone to the hand. No dedicated keyword action; the text is stated directly.

"Up to one" is modelled as `Quantity = UpToQuantity { Maximum = 1 }` on the `ObjectReference` — parallel to "up to two target creatures" (Soul Salvage) — rather than an `OptionalEffect` wrapper, because the constraint is on the NUMBER of targets chosen (0–1), not on whether a one-shot action is performed at all (CR 117.3a: "up to X" targets means 0 to X are chosen at time of targeting).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ReturnUpToOneTargetTypeDisjunctionToHandEffectRule.cs)

### `RevealTopCardMatchToBattlefieldElseGraveyardEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Recognises the Call of the Wild reveal-top-card-and-partition effect: "Reveal the top card of your library. If it's a creature card, put it onto the battlefield. Otherwise, put it into your graveyard."

The three-sentence fragment is one atomic action — the "it" in the second and third sentences back-references the single card revealed in the first — and is emitted as a single `RevealTopCardMatchToBattlefieldElseGraveyardEffect`. Splitting the sentences would dangle the "it" reference, so this rule matches the whole clause (the activated-effect single-rule path receives the full effect half because the second/third sentences do not independently parse, so the multi-sentence pre-pass falls through). CR 701.20 (Reveal); CR 400.7 (onto the battlefield — the card becomes a new object on zone change); CR 404.1 (a graveyard is the discard pile).

The regex is fully anchored (`^…$`) and demands the exact "Reveal the top card of your library. If it's a … card, put it onto the battlefield. Otherwise, put it into your graveyard" phrasing, so it does NOT match the fixed-count "top N cards" reveal-and-partition siblings, the "look at the top" siblings, or any variant with a different disposition. The `[filter]` is a bare card type ("creature").

Priority 96: must beat generic reveal/look sentence dispatch.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/RevealTopCardMatchToBattlefieldElseGraveyardEffectRule.cs)

### `RingTemptsActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"The Ring tempts you." — the Rule 701.54 keyword action as an effect within an activated ability. Emits the existing `RingTemptsEffect` node. CR 701.54a (verbatim): "Certain spells and abilities have the text 'the Ring tempts you.' Each time the Ring tempts you, choose a creature you control. That creature becomes your Ring-bearer until another creature becomes your Ring-bearer or another player gains control of it." Distinct from `RingTemptsTriggeredRule` which is used when the Ring tempts you is the entire body of a triggered ability and wraps the effect in an `Optional`. Here, as an activated-ability effect, "The Ring tempts you" is a mandatory instruction (not optional) — the activation always tempts you when paid. Anchored (^…$): collision-free with any sibling that checks for "ring" substring. Priority 80: above general-purpose rules (50) so this exact surface is claimed before broader matchers can fire.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/RingTemptsActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `RollDieActivatedRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Roll [count] [dN | N-sided die/dice]" — the die-roll instruction (CR 706.1) as the effect of an ACTIVATED ability ("{2}{G}: Roll a six-sided die." — Willing Test Subject, Atomwheel Acrobats). These are repeatable roll OUTLETS: an activated ability whose cost the controller pays to produce a die-roll event, which a "whenever you roll" trigger (`DiceRolledConditionRule`) can then consume.

The triggered path (`RollDieTriggeredRule`) and the spell path (`RollDiceSpellRule`) each have their own roll rule because their rule registries are distinct (ITriggeredRule / ISpellRule / IActivatedEffectRule). This is the activated registry's roll rule. All three emit the same `RollDieEffect` node (Count nullable, null ≡ the single-die form), which the interaction projection turns into `emit:rolldice`.

The cost ("{2}{G}", "{4}, Sacrifice this artifact") is parsed separately by the activated cost rules; this rule only recognises the post-colon effect fragment. Handles both the abbreviated "dN" form ("Roll a d20") and the spelled-out "N-sided die/dice" form ("Roll a six-sided die"), with an optional die count (CR 706.1: "how many of those dice to roll"), generalising over die size.

ANCHORED (`^…$`): a bare roll instruction with no trailing result-handling. A roll bundled with inline result-handling ("Roll a d6. Until end of turn, …" — Ebony Fly) is a different shape that the anchor deliberately does not match, leaving it for a future result-table-aware rule rather than silently dropping the result clause. Priority 60 mirrors the triggered/spell roll rules — above the generic fallback (default 50).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/RollDieActivatedRule.cs)

### `SacrificeAtEndStepEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step." — the delayed-sacrifice sentence that trails a token-creation effect in an activated ability (Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker). The pronoun "it" back-references the token created by the preceding sentence (CR 109.2 game objects).

CR 603.7: a triggered ability created by a resolving effect is a delayed triggered ability. MAST records this as a `CreateDelayedTriggerEffect` whose `DelayedTriggeredAbility` fires "at the beginning of the next end step" (a `GameTime` clock point) and whose resolution sacrifices the referenced object. Mirrors the triggered-ability sibling `SacrificeAtEndStepTriggeredRule` so an activated ability with the same trailing sentence (reached via the multi-sentence pre-pass) lands the same shape. CR 701.21 (Sacrifice); CR 513 (End Step).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SacrificeAtEndStepEffectRule.cs)

### `SacrificeCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Sacrifice cost: "Sacrifice another creature", "Sacrifice X Squirrels", etc. Reuses the shared `ParseSacrificePattern` for most patterns; handles "nonland permanent(s)" directly before delegating.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SacrificeCostRule.cs)

### `SacrificeThisAuraCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Sacrifice-self cost naming the Aura subtype specifically: "Sacrifice this Aura" (Floating Shield). Aura is an enchantment SUBTYPE (CR 205.3h), not a base card type, so the shared `ParseSacrificePattern` — whose "this &lt;type&gt;" branches only recognise the base card-type nouns (creature/permanent/artifact/enchantment/land) — falls through to its generic word-capture fallback, which captures only the bare word "this" as a garbage `Subtypes` entry and silently drops "Aura". Intercepting here with a NEW, narrowly-anchored rule (priority above `SacrificeCostRule`'s 999) closes that gap without touching the shared helper (which many other cards' "Sacrifice [creature/permanent/artifact/enchantment/land]" costs route through). CR 701.21a: sacrificing is a cost paid by moving the permanent from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard. Encoded as `CardTypes=["enchantment"]` + `Subtypes=["Aura"]` + `IsSelf=true` — the structured self-reference (parallel to the "this enchantment"/"this creature" branches of `ParseSacrificePattern`), narrowed with the Aura subtype since the oracle text names the subtype specifically rather than the bare card type.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SacrificeThisAuraCostRule.cs)

### `ScryEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Scry N" — e.g. "Scry 2", "Scry 1" (Rule 701.18).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ScryEffectRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryAnyNumberToBattlefieldEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Search your library for any number of [filter] cards, put them onto the battlefield[tapped], then shuffle."

The "any number" variant of the search-to-battlefield tutor pattern, distinct from `SearchLibraryToBattlefieldEffectRule` which handles the singular "search for a[n] … card, put it onto the battlefield" shape. Here the oracle text uses "any number" (an open-ended count) and "them" (plural pronoun) rather than "a" (singular) and "it".

The World Tree's fourth ability is the canonical example: "Search your library for any number of God cards, put them onto the battlefield, then shuffle."

Maps to a `CompositeEffect` containing:

`SearchLibraryEffect` with `Count = AnyAmountQuantity` and `Destination = Battlefield` (or `BattlefieldTapped` when the oracle says "tapped"). `ShuffleEffect` targeting the controller (You).

CR 701.23a: "To search for a card in a zone, look at all cards in that zone (even if it's a hidden zone) and find a card that matches the given description." CR 701.23b: "If a player is searching a hidden zone for cards with a stated quality … that player isn't required to find some or all of those cards even if they're present in that zone." — "any number" is the oracle encoding of this optionality.

Priority 66 — one above `SearchLibraryToBattlefieldEffectRule` (priority 65) so this rule's "any number of … cards, put them" pattern is tried before that rule's "a[n] … card, put it" pattern. Both patterns are anchored (^…$) so there is no substring-overlap risk.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SearchLibraryAnyNumberToBattlefieldEffectRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryToBattlefieldEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Search your library for a &lt;filter&gt; permanent card with mana value N or less, put it onto the battlefield[tapped], then shuffle." Covers the activated tutor-to-battlefield pattern (e.g. Amrou Scout, Lin Sivvi, Deceptive Landscape, Contaminated Landscape). CR 701.23a: "To search for a card in a zone, look at all cards in that zone (even if it's a hidden zone) and find a card that matches the given description." Maps to a CompositeEffect containing: 1. SearchLibraryEffect (Destination = Battlefield or BattlefieldTapped) — the search and placement. 2. ShuffleEffect (Player = You) — the mandatory library shuffle. The ObjectFilter carries: - Subtypes: [subtype] when the qualifier is a creature-type (e.g. "Rebel") - Subtypes: [LandType1, LandType2, ...] when a basic-land subtype disjunction is present (e.g. "basic Plains, Swamp, or Forest" — CR 305.6: "The basic land types are Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, and Forest.") - CardTypes: ["permanent"] when a card-type constraint is present - ManaValueComparison: LessThanOrEqual N when "with mana value N or less"

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SearchLibraryToBattlefieldEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetAndDamageToYouEffectRule` — *sealed class*

"[Self] deals N damage to any target and M damage to you." — the Fireslinger self-ping-with-recoil pattern (a {T} ability that pings any target while also dealing damage back to its own controller).

A single "… and …"-joined sentence that expands to two sibling `DealDamageEffect`s, both sourced from the ability's own object (`Self`): the first to "any target" (`AnyTarget` — a creature, player, or planeswalker), the second to "you" (`You`, the controller). Emitted as a flat list via `TryMatchMulti` so the two pings sit as sibling effects rather than nested in a composite — mirroring the spell-side `DealDamageToAnyTargetAndGainLifeRule`.

CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. This is generally detrimental to the object or player that receives that damage. An object that deals damage is the source of that damage." Both pings are non-combat damage (CR 120), so `IsCombat` is left null.

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the trailing "and M damage to you" clause is part of the match, so this cannot be confused with the bare `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetEffectRule` (which anchors on "… to any target$" and thus never sees the recoil clause). The anchor also prevents a future broader pattern from claiming this sentence and silently dropping the recoil conjunct.

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair on `Effects`. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path never claims the sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetAndDamageToYouEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Two shapes — both map to self-as-source dealDamage:

"[Self] deals N damage to any target." → AnyTarget (CR 119.2: damage is dealt by the source; "any target" selects a creature, player, or planeswalker). "[Self] deals N damage to target creature." → Target with creature filter (CR 119.2: narrower form restricted to creatures only).

GUARD: does NOT match "each opponent" (family F17) — that shape has no "target" keyword.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToAttackingOrBlockingCreatureEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"[This creature|CardName] deals N damage to target attacking or blocking creature." — archer / ballista tap-to-deal-damage pattern. Both subject forms encode the source as `Self()`; the target is a creature with Characteristics = [Characteristic.InCombat(CombatState.AttackingOrBlocking)].

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToAttackingOrBlockingCreatureEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToCreatureWithCharacteristicEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"[This creature|CardName] deals N damage to target/each creature with [characteristic]." — the flying-hoser archer pattern (Centaur Archer: "{T}: This creature deals 1 damage to target creature with flying."). Sibling of `SelfDealsDamageToAttackingOrBlockingCreatureEffectRule` and the spell-side `SelfDealsDamageToFilteredCreatureRule`: both map to self-as-source dealDamage, differing only in the qualifier used to filter the creature target. Anchored on a trailing "with [characteristic]" clause so it cannot claim the bare "target creature" shape (that's `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetEffectRule`'s TargetTypePattern, which is itself anchored to end right after the type word).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToCreatureWithCharacteristicEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureAndPlayerEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This creature deals N damage to each creature and each player." — a Pestilence-style symmetric ping (CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect."; the cost — e.g. "{B}" — is parsed separately by the activated cost rules, this rule recognises only the post-colon effect fragment). The source deals non-combat damage (CR 120.1) simultaneously to every creature (including itself — the ability is symmetric, unlike a one-sided sweeper) and every player, the latter causing life loss (CR 119.2).

Emits the same `CompositeEffect` shape as the spell-side `DealDamageToEachRule` "each creature and each player" branch, but reachable from an activated ability: `ActivatedAbilityParser` dispatches the post-colon effect ONLY through the `IActivatedEffectRule` registry, which is distinct from the spell/triggered registries (see the note in `RollDieActivatedRule`), so the spell rule can never fire here.

Guard: anchors on "each creature and each player" specifically; does NOT match "each opponent" (handled by `SelfDealsDamageToEachOpponentEffectRule`) or "each player equal to half life total" style clauses (`SelfDealsHalfLifeTotalDamageToEachPlayerEffectRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureAndPlayerEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureWithFlyingAndPlayerEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This creature deals N damage to each creature with [keyword] and each player." — the filtered sibling of `SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureAndPlayerEffectRule` where the creature half of the symmetric ping is restricted to creatures that <em>have</em> a keyword ability (Rockcaster Platoon: "{4}{G}: This creature deals 2 damage to each creature with flying and each player."). CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect."; the cost — e.g. "{4}{G}" — is parsed separately by the activated cost rules, this rule recognises only the post-colon effect fragment. CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. … An object that deals damage is the source of that damage." The source deals non-combat damage (CR 120.1) simultaneously to every creature carrying the named keyword and to every player, the latter causing life loss (CR 119.2).

Emits a `CompositeEffect` of two `DealDamageEffect` nodes — one to the filtered creatures, one to `EachPlayer` — mirroring the shape of `SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureAndPlayerEffectRule`. The "with [keyword]" predicate is structured through `FromLabel`, which yields a first-class `KeywordCharacteristic` for keyword abilities this AST models (flying, reach, …) and falls back to the typed `OtherCharacteristic` residual otherwise.

Guard: ANCHORED (`^…$`) and REQUIRES "each creature with &lt;keyword&gt; and each player". It cannot claim the unqualified "each creature and each player" shape (`SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureAndPlayerEffectRule` — no "with" clause), the "each creature without &lt;keyword&gt;" sweeper (`SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureWithoutKeywordEffectRule`), or the "each opponent" form (`SelfDealsDamageToEachOpponentEffectRule`). Conversely those anchored siblings never see this sentence because their patterns lack the "with &lt;keyword&gt; and each player" tail.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureWithFlyingAndPlayerEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureWithoutKeywordEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This creature deals N damage to each creature without [keyword]." — a one-sided activated-ability sweeper that spares creatures carrying a specific evasion/defensive keyword (Ashen Firebeast: "{1}{R}: This creature deals 1 damage to each creature without flying."). CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect."; the cost — e.g. "{1}{R}" — is parsed separately by the activated cost rules, this rule recognises only the post-colon effect fragment. CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. … An object that deals damage is the source of that damage." The source deals non-combat damage simultaneously to every creature (including itself, unless it happens to carry the named keyword) that lacks the named keyword ability.

The keyword-absence predicate is encoded as a typed `OtherCharacteristic` residual ("withoutFlying", etc.) per the convention established by `CreaturesCantBlockThisTurnRule` (Falter, Cosmotronic Wave) and `CreatureWithoutKeywordDiesConditionRule` (Luminous Broodmoth family): `OtherCharacteristic` is `IResidual`, not `IUnparsed` — a deliberate scope deferral (ADR 0001), not a parse failure, since there is currently no `NegatedKeywordCharacteristic` node.

Guard: anchors on "each creature without &lt;keyword&gt;" specifically; does NOT match the unqualified "each creature and each player" shape (`SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureAndPlayerEffectRule`) or "each opponent" (`SelfDealsDamageToEachOpponentEffectRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureWithoutKeywordEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToEachOpponentEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This creature deals N damage to each opponent." — self-as-source dealDamage spreading N damage to every opponent simultaneously (CR 119.2: "Damage dealt to a player normally causes that player to lose that much life."). Guard: anchors on "each opponent"; does NOT match "any target" (handled by `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetEffectRule`) or "target attacking or blocking creature" (`SelfDealsDamageToAttackingOrBlockingCreatureEffectRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToEachOpponentEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToOpponentOrPlaneswalkerEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"[This creature|CardName] deals N damage to target opponent or planeswalker." — the activated-ability sibling of `SelfDealsDamageToPlayerOrPlaneswalkerEffectRule` for the `opponent` variant (Zealot of the God-Pharaoh's "{4}{R}: This creature deals 2 damage to target opponent or planeswalker."). The source is the ability's own object, modeled as `Self()` (CR 602.1 — an activated ability is written "[Cost]: [Effect]"; here the effect's source is "this creature"). The disjunctive target "opponent or planeswalker" is a single `Target` whose `CardTypes` carries the two-entry union `["opponent", "planeswalker"]` — the same shape the triggered sibling `ItDealsDamageToTargetTypeDisjunctionRule` produces for the ETB variants (Cinder Hellion). Both "opponent" (a player, CR 102.2: "a player's opponent is the other player") and "planeswalker" are legal recipients of damage (CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players."). CR 115.1: "target" creates a target. Anchored (`^…$`) and REQUIRES "opponent or planeswalker" exactly, so it stays disjoint from the "player or planeswalker" sibling and the "each opponent" / "any target" / single-type rules — no double-match.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToOpponentOrPlaneswalkerEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToPlayerOrPlaneswalkerEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"[This creature|CardName] deals N damage to target player or planeswalker." — the Heartwood Giant / firebreathing-adjacent ping pattern. Both subject forms encode the source as `Self()`; the target is a single `ObjectReference` whose `ObjectFilter` carries a two-entry `CardTypes` union — the same "X or Y" disjunction shape used by the triggered-ability sibling `ItDealsDamageToTargetTypeDisjunctionRule` (CR 115.4 reasoning generalized to an explicit two-type union; "player" and "planeswalker" are both legal recipients of damage per CR 120.1).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToPlayerOrPlaneswalkerEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsHalfLifeTotalDamageToEachPlayerEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"[Self] deals damage to each player equal to half that player's life total, rounded down." — the Heartless Hidetsugu activated-ability shape.

CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as '[Cost]: [Effect.]'" — this rule fires after the cost ({T}) is stripped, receiving only the effect clause.

The amount is a `CalculatedQuantity` wrapping a `DerivedQuantity` (`DerivedFrom=LifeTotal`) with `Operation="half"` and `Rounding="down"` (CR 107.1a: "If a spell or ability could generate a fractional number, the spell or ability will tell you whether to round up or down.").

CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. This is generally detrimental to the object or player that receives that damage. An object that deals damage is the source of that damage."

GUARD: fully anchored (^ … $). Matches only the named-subject form ending in "each player equal to half that player's life total, rounded down" — does NOT match "each opponent" (handled by `SelfDealsDamageToEachOpponentEffectRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfDealsHalfLifeTotalDamageToEachPlayerEffectRule.cs)

### `SelfGainsProtectionColorActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Self-referential analogue of `TargetGainsProtectionColorActivatedEffectRule`: recognises the "this creature gains protection from the color of your choice UEOT" interior of an activated ability — "This creature gains protection from the color of your choice until end of turn." This is the effect half of Cartel Aristocrat ("Sacrifice another creature: This creature gains protection from the color of your choice until end of turn."). Unlike Mother of Runes ("Target creature you control gains protection ..."), the grant is on the source permanent itself, so the recipient is `Self` with no filter — not a chosen/targeted creature. The chosen color is modeled as `ChosenColor` — a declarative marker that the protection quality is controller-chosen at resolution time (MAST records the instruction to choose, not the chosen value; the descriptive- not-engine doctrine). The grant is a continuous ability-granting effect: a `GainAbilityEffect` whose granted ability is the Protection static ability carrying a `ProtectionEffect`. Rule citations: 702.16 (Protection), 702.16e (protection from a player's choice of color), 613.1c (Layer 6 — ability-granting continuous effects), 611 (continuous effects with a duration).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SelfGainsProtectionColorActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `SurveilEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Surveil N" as an activated-ability effect — e.g. "{4}, {T}: Surveil 1." CR 701.25a: "To 'surveil N' means to look at the top N cards of your library, then put any number of them into your graveyard and the rest on top of your library in any order."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SurveilEffectRule.cs)

### `SwitchTargetCreaturePTActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Switch target creature's power and toughness until end of turn." — the P/T-switch shape as an activated-ability effect (Dwarven Thaumaturgist's `{T}` ability). CR 613.4 (Layer 7d): "Effects that switch a creature's power and toughness are applied. Such effects take the value of power and apply it to the creature's toughness, and take the value of toughness and apply it to the creature's power." The activated-ability counterpart of the instant-speed `SwitchTargetCreaturePTSpellRule` (Twisted Image). Both emit the shared `SwitchPTEffect` node. GUARD: fully anchored (`^…$`) to exactly the switch-P/T sentence with an optional trailing period; no sibling activated effect shares this surface phrase, so the anchored matcher is disjoint from every other rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SwitchTargetCreaturePTActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `SwitchThisCreaturePTEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability effect shape "Switch this creature's power and toughness until end of turn." — e.g. Myr Quadropod: "{3}: Switch this creature's power and toughness until end of turn." CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as \"[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]\"" The cost container ({3}) is parsed independently by `ActivatedAbilityParser`; this rule only recognizes the post-colon effect body. CR 613.4d (Layer 7d): "Effects that switch a creature's power and toughness are applied. Such effects take the value of power and apply it to the creature's toughness, and take the value of toughness and apply it to the creature's power." Self ("this creature") counterpart of the spell-side `SwitchTargetCreaturePTSpellRule` ("Switch target creature's power and toughness ..."). Emits the same `SwitchPTEffect`, but with the source creature (`Self`) as its target. Fully anchored so it cannot capture a sibling effect fragment.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/SwitchThisCreaturePTEffectRule.cs)

### `TakeExtraTurnEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Take an extra turn after this one." — schedules an additional full turn for the ability's controller to be taken immediately after the current turn.

CR 500.7 (verbatim): "Some effects can give a player extra turns. They do this by adding the turns directly after the specified turn." MAST records the verb and player reference; the turn-ordering bookkeeping is engine territory.

ANCHOR: pattern is anchored (^...$) to prevent partial matches inside longer effect text. This is the most-specific extra-turn form (controller takes a turn); target-player forms are handled by extending this rule or adding a sibling rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TakeExtraTurnEffectRule.cs)

### `TakeNExtraTurnsEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Take two extra turns after this one." — Teferi, Master of Time −10 loyalty ability. Grants the controller two additional full turns immediately following the current turn.

CR 500.7 (verbatim): "Some effects can give a player extra turns. They do this by adding the turns directly after the specified turn. If a player is given multiple extra turns, the extra turns are added one at a time. … The most recently created turn will be taken first."

The `Count` field records the two-turn quantity; the engine applies CR 500.7's sequencing rule. This rule handles the "N extra turns" (N ≥ 2) form; the canonical "an extra turn" (N = 1) form is handled by the existing `TakeExtraTurnEffectRule` (no Count field emitted for the singular case).

ANCHORED (^...$): prevents partial matches inside broader text. Priority 984 — more-specific than the generic single-turn rule (985), fires first so the two-turn form is not silently truncated to one turn.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TakeNExtraTurnsEffectRule.cs)

### `TapEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Tap [count] [another] target [type]" — "Tap target creature", "Tap another target creature" (Thassa, Deep-Dwelling), "Tap X target lands", "Tap two target creatures" (CR 701.26a). "another" excludes the source permanent (CR 109.5). For variable-X abilities the X in cost and effect refer to the same chosen value (Rule 107.3b/c).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TapEffectRule.cs)

### `TapOrUntapTargetActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"(You may) tap or untap target [type]." in an activated ability effect position — the controller chooses whether to tap or untap the named target. Runs at higher priority than `TapEffectRule` and `UntapTargetCardTypeActivatedEffectRule` (Priority 995 &gt; 994) so the "tap or untap" phrase is claimed here before the plain tap/untap rules see it.

CR 701.26a: "To tap a permanent, turn it sideways from an upright position. Only untapped permanents can be tapped."

CR 701.26b: "To untap a permanent, rotate it back to the upright position from a sideways position. Only tapped permanents can be untapped."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TapOrUntapTargetActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `TapPermanentsCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Tap-permanents cost: "Tap two untapped artifacts you control", "Tap an untapped creature you control", etc. — the spelled-out "Tap …" verb (not the {T} symbol) used as an activation cost (CR 118.3 / 602.5; CR 701.20 tap/untap). e.g. Whirler Rogue: "Tap two untapped artifacts you control: Target creature can't be blocked this turn." Emits a `TapPermanentsCost` whose `Filter` carries the tapped permanents' card type and controller. The "untapped" qualifier is implicit in the cost (a permanent must be untapped to be tapped to pay the cost — CR 701.20a), so it is not encoded as a separate axis; this matches the existing Conspire `TapPermanentsCost` idiom ("tap two untapped creatures you control").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TapPermanentsCostRule.cs)

### `TapSelfThenGainsKeywordEffectRule` — *sealed class*

"Tap this creature. It gains [keyword] until end of turn." — the classic self-tapping "sentinel" defensive ability (Drudge Sentinel: "{3}: Tap this creature. It gains indestructible until end of turn."). The pronoun "It" in the second sentence unambiguously refers back to "this creature" (the source permanent tapped by the first sentence), so both effects target `Self`.

Two sibling effects on a single activated ability:

a `TapEffect` tapping the source permanent (CR 701.26a: "To tap a permanent, turn it sideways from an upright position."); a `GainAbilityEffect` granting the keyword for the turn — a continuous effect (CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period.") whose granted keyword is itself a static ability (e.g. CR 702.12a: "Indestructible is a static ability.").

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair on `Effects`. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path never claims this two-sentence shape. Mirrors `ExileSelfThenReturnToBattlefieldRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TapSelfThenGainsKeywordEffectRule.cs)

### `TapSingularSubtypeCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Tap-a-singular-subtype cost: "Tap an untapped Gate you control", "Tap a untapped Elf you control" — the spelled-out "Tap …" verb used as an activation cost (CR 118.3 / 602.5; CR 701.26 tap/untap) where the count is the indefinite article ("a"/"an") rather than a number word, and the tapped permanent is identified by subtype rather than (or in addition to) card type. e.g. Gateway Shade: "Tap an untapped Gate you control: This creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn."

Distinct from `TapSubtypesCostRule` (requires an explicit number word "one"/"two"/… before "untapped") — this rule handles the singular article form, which never spells out "one". Distinct from `TapPermanentsCostRule` (requires a literal card-type word — "creature"/"artifact"/"land"/"permanent" — in the cost text); a bare subtype like "Gate" carries no such word.

The tapped permanent's card type is inferred from the subtype: land subtypes (CR 205.3i — the basics plus common single-word nonbasic land types, mirroring the set used by `ReturnLandSubtypeToHandCostRule`) resolve to `CardTypes: ["land"]`; any other (capitalised) subtype word is assumed to be a creature subtype (CR 205.3m), matching `TapSubtypesCostRule`'s idiom. This generalizes the emitted `Filter` beyond the creature-only assumption so land-typed permanents like Gates are modeled correctly rather than mislabeled as creatures.

The "untapped" qualifier is implicit in any tap cost (CR 701.26a: a permanent must be untapped to be tapped to pay the cost), so it is not encoded as a separate axis on the emitted `TapPermanentsCost` — matching the Conspire / `TapPermanentsCostRule` / `TapSubtypesCostRule` idiom.

Anchored (^…$) to avoid matching as a substring of a longer/different cost string. Priority 998 — same tier as `TapSubtypesCostRule`, and mutually exclusive with it (that rule requires a number word; this one requires the indefinite article), so ordering between the two does not matter.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TapSingularSubtypeCostRule.cs)

### `TapSubtypesCostRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedCostRule

Tap-N-subtype cost: "Tap three untapped Elves you control", "Tap two untapped Merfolk you control", etc. — the spelled-out "Tap …" verb used as an activation cost where the permanents are identified by creature subtype rather than card type (CR 118.3 / 602.5; CR 701.20 tap/untap).

This rule handles the pattern where only a creature subtype (e.g. "Elf", "Elves", "Merfolk", "Goblin") appears in the tap cost — no explicit card-type word ("creature", "artifact") is printed. Oracle text capitalises creature subtypes (Rule 205.3m), so the regex requires an uppercase first letter, preventing "Tap three untapped lands you control" from matching here (handled by `TapPermanentsCostRule` which requires a card-type word).

The "untapped" qualifier is implicit in any tap cost (CR 701.20a: a permanent must be untapped to be tapped), so it is not encoded as a separate axis on the emitted `TapPermanentsCost`, matching the Conspire idiom.

Emits a `TapPermanentsCost` with:

`Filter` — CardTypes = ["creature"], Subtypes = [singularized subtype], Controller = You. `Quantity` — parsed from the number word (one/two/three/…) or digit in the cost text.

Priority 996 — above TapPermanentsCostRule (Priority 997 handles generic card-type tap costs; numbered lower = higher priority in the registry). Wait — Priority here is DESCENDING (higher number = higher priority per the convention in ActivatedCostRuleAttribute). Set to 998 so this fires before TapPermanentsCostRule (997), which would otherwise return null on subtype-only costs anyway (it requires a card-type keyword), making the order moot — but explicit priority ensures no future generic rule intercepts first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TapSubtypesCostRule.cs)

### `TargetAttackingCreatureGetsPTAndGainsKeywordEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target attacking creature gets &lt;±P/±T&gt; and gains &lt;kw&gt; until end of turn" — the from-hand bloodrush pump+grant (e.g. Wasteland Viper, "Bloodrush — {G}, Discard this card: Target attacking creature gets +1/+2 and gains deathtouch until end of turn.").

Splices `ModifyPTTargetAttackingCreatureEffectRule`'s target/filter half (attacking-creature target form) with `GetsPTAndGainsKeywordEffectRule`'s pump+grant composite shape (which is anchored to the "This creature" self form). Neither existing rule alone handles the TARGET-form pump+grant sentence.

<b>CR 613.4c</b> (P/T modifier clause): "Layer 7c: Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied." The granted keyword is a continuous ability grant that applies in layer 6 (ability-adding effects). Both clauses are present in oracle text; this parser describes them without encoding layer machinery.

"Bloodrush" itself is an ability word with no rules meaning (<b>CR 207.2c</b>: "An ability word appears in italics at the beginning of some abilities. Ability words are similar to keywords in that they tie together cards that have similar functionality, but they have no special rules meaning and no individual entries in the Comprehensive Rules. The ability words are adamant, addendum, alliance, battalion, bloodrush, ..."); the classifier captures it onto the activated ability's `AbilityWord` label.

<b>CR 702.2a</b> ("Deathtouch"): "Deathtouch is a static ability."

Returns a `CompositeEffect` whose child list carries, in order:

A `ModifyPTEffect` targeting an attacking creature with EOT duration. A `GainAbilityEffect` targeting `It` (anaphora back to the targeted attacking creature — NOT `Self`, since the pumped creature is the one that gains the keyword, not the source permanent), the keyword ability, and EOT duration.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetAttackingCreatureGetsPTAndGainsKeywordEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetBecomesChosenSubtypeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target creature becomes that type[ until end of turn]." — the consumer half of the Imagecrafter template ("{T}: Choose a creature type other than Wall. Target creature becomes that type until end of turn."). Sets the target creature's creature type to the creature type chosen by the preceding `ChooseCreatureTypeEffect` sentence.

Emits a `ChangeSubtypeEffect` — a layer-4 subtype-changing continuous effect (CR 613.1: continuous effects apply in layers). The permanent stays a creature and only its creature type is replaced (CR 205.3: creature types are subtypes), so this is a subtype set, not a `BecomesCreatureEffect` (which adds the creature card type). The new value is the demonstrative "that type", a back-reference to the earlier choice, so it lands in `ChosenSubtypeReference` (`CreatureType`) — NOT the fresh-choice `ChosenSubtype`, which is reserved for "the creature type of your choice" (Mistform). The producer/consumer pairing is a CR 607.1 linked-ability relationship; MAST records both effects but not the link edge.

Anchored on "Target creature becomes that type"; the optional "until end of turn" tail maps to the inherited `Duration`. Disjoint from `ChangeColorEffectRule` ("becomes [color]") and `BecomesChosenCreatureTypeEffectRule` ("This creature becomes the creature type of your choice"), so dispatch priority relative to them is immaterial.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetBecomesChosenSubtypeEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetCantBeBlockedWithPowerFilterThisTurnEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target creature with power N or less/greater can't be blocked this turn." — activated ability effect that grants full unblockability until end of turn to a target creature constrained by a power comparison filter. CR 509.1b: "The defending player checks each creature they control to see whether it's affected by any restrictions (effects that say a creature can't block, or that it can't block unless some condition is met)." A "can't be blocked" effect is a blocking restriction on the attacker — an evasion ability under CR 509.1 (a static ability an attacking creature has that restricts what can block it). CR 602.5: "A player can't begin to activate an ability that's prohibited from being activated." Governs the {T} activation cost (Goblin Tunneler). Maps to `CantBeBlockedEffect` with:

`Target` = a `Target` creature reference filtered by `PowerComparison` (Goblin Tunneler, "power 2 or less"). `Duration` = `untilEndOfTurn` — oracle phrase "this turn" maps to end-of-turn expiry. No `BlockedByFilter` — the restriction is unconditional (full unblockability), mirroring `CantBeBlockedThisTurnEffectRule`.

Power-filter parsing mirrors `PowerPattern`: "power N or greater" maps to `GreaterThanOrEqual`, "power N or less" maps to `LessThanOrEqual`. Sits above (higher priority than) the generic, unfiltered `CantBeBlockedThisTurnEffectRule` (Priority 80) — collision-free, since that rule's exact-string match cannot claim this power-filtered phrase.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetCantBeBlockedWithPowerFilterThisTurnEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureBlocksThisCreatureThisTurnEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability "lure" effect shape "target [filter] blocks this creature this turn if able." — e.g. Tangle Angler: "{G}: Target creature blocks this creature this turn if able." CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as \"[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]\" Example: The activation cost of an ability that reads \"{2}, {T}: You gain 1 life\" is two mana of any type plus tapping the permanent that has the ability." The cost container ({G}) is parsed independently; this rule only recognizes the post-colon effect body. CR 509.1c: "The defending player checks each creature they control to see whether it's affected by any requirements (effects that say a creature must block, or that it must block if some condition is met). ... If a requirement that says a creature blocks if able during a certain turn refers to a turn with multiple combat phases, the creature blocks if able during each declare blockers step in that turn." This is a blocker-side requirement placed on the targeted creature (the forced blocker), naming the activating creature (`Self`) as the attacker it must block — the dual of an attacker-side "must be blocked" lure. Maps to `MustBlockEffect` with `Target` = the targeted forced blocker (parsed via `ParseTargetFilter`), `Blocks` = `Self` (this creature), and `Duration` = end of turn, matching the oracle phrase "this turn".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetCreatureBlocksThisCreatureThisTurnEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureCantBlockThisCreatureThisTurnEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability "anti-lure" effect shape "target [filter] can't block this creature this turn." — e.g. Spin Engine: "{R}: Target creature can't block this creature this turn." CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as \"[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]\" Example: The activation cost of an ability that reads \"{2}, {T}: You gain 1 life\" is two mana of any type plus tapping the permanent that has the ability." The cost container ({R}) is parsed independently; this rule only recognizes the post-colon effect body. CR 509.1: "First, the defending player declares blockers. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack. To declare blockers, the defending player follows the steps below, in order. If at any point during the declaration of blockers, the defending player is unable to comply with any of the steps listed below, the declaration is illegal; the game returns to the moment before the declaration (see rule 733, \"Handling Illegal Actions\"). A restriction may be created by an evasion ability (a static ability an attacking creature has that restricts what can block it). If an attacking creature gains or loses an evasion ability after a legal block has been declared, it doesn't affect that block. Different evasion abilities are cumulative..." This is a blocker-side restriction placed on the targeted creature, naming the activating creature (`Self`) as the specific attacker it can't block — the negative dual of the "lure" requirement shape. Maps to `CantBlockEffect` with `Target` = the targeted restricted creature (parsed via `ParseTargetFilter`), `Blocks` = `Self` (this creature), and `Duration` = end of turn, matching the oracle phrase "this turn".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetCreatureCantBlockThisCreatureThisTurnEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureGainsLandwalkEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target creature gains [basic landwalk] until end of turn." — a targeted activated grant of a basic-land landwalk keyword for the rest of the turn (Ivy Dancer "{T}: Target creature gains forestwalk until end of turn."). The basic landwalk keywords (forestwalk / islandwalk / swampwalk / mountainwalk / plainswalk) are absent from `BuildGrantedKeywordAbility`, so the generic "Target creature gains …" branch of `GainAbilityEffectRule` (Priority 995) returns null for them and the effect lands unstructured (L1). This dedicated, fully-anchored rule structures the interior into the same `GainAbilityEffect` shape those siblings emit — the target being an `Target` creature — granting the landwalk keyword's canonical structured expansion: an `EvasionEffect` whose `UnblockableCondition` is `DefendingPlayerControls` over the matching basic land subtype. This is the target-scoped dual of `ThisCreatureGainsLandwalkEffectRule` (the self-grant shape). CR 702.14 (Landwalk): "Landwalk is an evasion ability." and "A creature with landwalk can't be blocked as long as the defending player controls at least one land with the specified land type (as in 'islandwalk')…". CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period." (the grant expires "until end of turn"). CR 602.1: activated abilities are written "[Cost]: [Effect.]" — this rule handles the post-colon effect fragment. Anchored end-to-end (^…$) and restricted to the five basic-land landwalk words, so it claims only this exact target-grant phrase and never shadows another activated effect. Sits above the generic `GainAbilityEffectRule` (Priority 995); that rule cannot claim these keywords anyway (helper miss), so this is collision-free.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetCreatureGainsLandwalkEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureGetsPTAndGainsKeywordEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target creature gets &lt;±P/±T&gt; and gains &lt;kw&gt; until end of turn" — a single-sentence TWO-clause activated effect that neither `ModifyPTEffectRule` nor `GainAbilityEffectRule` handles alone. This is the targeted sibling of `GetsPTAndGainsKeywordEffectRule` ("This creature gets …"); here the buff lands on a chosen target creature (e.g. Ixalli's Keeper: "{7}{G}, {T}, Sacrifice this creature: Target creature gets +5/+5 and gains trample until end of turn.").

<b>CR 613.4c</b> (P/T modifier clause): "Layer 7c: Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied." The granted keyword is a continuous ability grant that applies in layer 6 ("Ability-adding effects, keyword counters, ability-removing effects, and effects that say an object can't have an ability are applied."). Both clauses are present in oracle text; this parser describes them without encoding the layer machinery.

Returns a `CompositeEffect` whose child list carries, in order:

A `ModifyPTEffect` targeting the chosen creature with EOT duration. A `GainAbilityEffect` targeting "it" (the same creature), the keyword ability, and EOT duration.

This mirrors the spell-side shape emitted by `ModifyPTAndGainKeywordSpellRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetCreatureGetsPTAndGainsKeywordEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureMustBeBlockedThisTurnEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability attacker-side block requirement "Target [filter] must be blocked this turn if able." — e.g. Satyr Piper: "{3}{G}: Target creature must be blocked this turn if able." CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as \"[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]\" Example: The activation cost of an ability that reads \"{2}, {T}: You gain 1 life\" is two mana of any type plus tapping the permanent that has the ability." The cost container ({3}{G}) is parsed independently; this rule only recognizes the post-colon effect body. CR 509.1c: "The defending player checks each creature they control to see whether it's affected by any requirements (effects that say a creature must block, or that it must block if some condition is met). ... If a requirement that says a creature blocks if able during a certain turn refers to a turn with multiple combat phases, the creature blocks if able during each declare blockers step in that turn." This compels the defending player's OTHER creatures to block the named (targeted) creature — the dual of `TargetCreatureBlocksThisCreatureThisTurnEffectRule`, which compels the named creature itself to block a specific attacker. Maps to `MustBeBlockedEffect` with `Target` = the targeted creature that must be blocked (parsed via `ParseTargetFilter`) and `Duration` = end of turn, matching the oracle phrase "this turn". Same effect shape as the spell-resolution `MustBeBlockedTargetRule` (Irresistible Prey), wired into the activated-ability effect path instead.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetCreatureMustBeBlockedThisTurnEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureWithPowerFilterGainsKeywordEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target creature with power N or less/greater gains [keyword] until end of turn." — activated ability effect that grants a keyword ability (CR 702) to a target creature constrained by a power comparison filter, for the stated duration (Mosstodon: "Target creature with power 5 or greater gains trample until end of turn"). CR 602.1: "Activated abilities have a cost and an effect. They are written as \"[Cost]: [Effect.] [Activation instructions (if any).]\"…" — governs the "{1}: [Effect]" shape this rule's effect text is drawn from. CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period." The grant is such a continuous effect, expiring "until end of turn". CR 702.19a: "Trample is a static ability that modifies the rules for assigning an attacking creature's combat damage. The ability has no effect when a creature with trample is blocking or is dealing noncombat damage." Trample (and any other keyword `BuildGrantedKeywordAbility` already resolves) is granted as a `static` ability whose source is the keyword itself (CR 702: keyword abilities are shorthand for static, triggered, or activated abilities spelled out in full elsewhere in the rules). Power-filter parsing mirrors `TargetCantBeBlockedWithPowerFilterThisTurnEffectRule`: "power N or greater" maps to `GreaterThanOrEqual`, "power N or less" maps to `LessThanOrEqual`. Sits above (higher priority than) the generic, unfiltered `GainAbilityEffectRule` (Priority 995) — collision-free, since that rule's "Target creature [you control] gains …" branch requires "gains"/"gain" to immediately follow "creature" (optionally "you control") and cannot claim this "with power N or greater" phrase.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetCreatureWithPowerFilterGainsKeywordEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetGainsProtectionColorActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

Activated-ability analogue of `TargetGainsProtectionColorRule`: recognises the "gains protection from the color of your choice UEOT" interior of an activated ability — "Target creature you control gains protection from the color of your choice until end of turn." This is the effect half of Mother of Runes ("{T}: Target creature you control gains protection from the color of your choice until end of turn."). The spell rule only fires on the spell-parsing path, so the same shape reached via an activated ability's post-colon effect fragment needs its own recognizer here. The chosen color is modeled as `ChosenColor` — a declarative marker that the protection quality is controller-chosen at resolution time (MAST records the instruction to choose, not the chosen value; the descriptive- not-engine doctrine). The grant is a continuous ability-granting effect: a `GainAbilityEffect` whose granted ability is the Protection static ability carrying a `ProtectionEffect`. Rule citations: 702.16 (Protection), 702.16e (protection from a player's choice of color), 613.1c (Layer 6 — ability-granting continuous effects), 611 (continuous effects with a duration).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetGainsProtectionColorActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetGainsProtectionFromChosenColorActivatedEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target creature gains protection from the chosen color until end of turn." (Floating Shield's "Sacrifice this Aura:" activated ability.)

Distinct from `TargetGainsProtectionColorActivatedEffectRule`'s "the color of your choice" (`ChosenColor` — a fresh choice made anew at THIS ability's own resolution, with no persistent binding): "the chosen color" is a DEFINITE back-reference to the single color already bound by the paired "As this Aura enters, choose a color." replacement ability (CR 607 linked ability; CR 614.12; see `ChooseColorOnEntryRule`) — every mention of "the chosen color" printed on this card names the identical value. Modeled as `ChosenCharacteristic` + `ChosenCharacteristic` = `Color`, mirroring the object-reference analogue used by `PreventAllDamageToEnchantedCreatureByChosenColorSourceStaticRule` ("sources of the chosen color").

Also unlike Mother of Runes' "Target creature you control gains …", this text carries no "you control" restriction — plain "Target creature" — so the grant's filter has no `ControllerFilter`.

Rule citations: 702.16 (Protection), 702.16b (protection from a quality), 607.1 (linked abilities), 613.1c (Layer 6 — ability-granting continuous effects), 611 (continuous effects with a duration).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetGainsProtectionFromChosenColorActivatedEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetLandBecomesChosenBasicLandTypeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target land becomes the basic land type of your choice [until end of turn]." — the Reef Shaman template ("{T}: Target land becomes the basic land type of your choice until end of turn."). Emits a single `ChangeSubtypeEffect` whose new subtype is player-chosen (`BasicLandType`) rather than literal.

This is one layer-4 type-changing continuous effect (CR 613.1d: "Layer 4: Type-changing effects are applied. These include effects that change an object's card type, subtype, and/or supertype."). It <em>sets</em> the land's land type, replacing its existing land types (CR 205.1a: "when an effect sets one or more of an object's subtypes, the new subtype(s) replaces any existing subtypes from the appropriate set (creature types, land types, …)"). The chosen value is a single basic land type per CR 305.6 ("The basic land types are Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, and Forest. If an object uses the words 'basic land type,' it's referring to one of these subtypes."). Per CR 305.7 the land loses its old land types and rules text and gains the appropriate mana ability for the new basic land type; MAST records the subtype set and leaves that consequence to the engine.

This is the fresh-choice, land-type analogue of `BecomesChosenCreatureTypeEffectRule` ("This creature becomes the creature type of your choice"): the "of your choice" is a fresh on-resolution pick, so it lands in `ChosenSubtype` (NOT the back-referencing `ChosenSubtypeReference`, which is reserved for the demonstrative "that type" — Imagecrafter). The permanent stays a land and only its land type changes, so this is a subtype-set effect, not a card-type change.

Anchored on the full "Target land becomes the basic land type of your choice" phrase; the optional "until end of turn" tail maps to the inherited `Duration`. Disjoint from `ChangeColorEffectRule` ("becomes [color]"), `BecomesChosenCreatureTypeEffectRule` ("This [permanent] becomes the creature type of your choice"), and `TargetBecomesChosenSubtypeEffectRule` ("Target creature becomes that type"), so dispatch priority relative to them is immaterial.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetLandBecomesChosenBasicLandTypeEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetPlayerGainsLifeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Target player gains N life." — the activated-ability counterpart of `GainLifeSpellRule`'s targeted-player clause. N is a literal number, number word, or variable (X/Y/Z). Representative card: Mournful Zombie ("{W}, {T}: Target player gains 1 life.").

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." Unlike `GainLifeEffectRule` (subject is the controller, "You gain …"), this rule's subject is a targeted player (`Target` over an `Player()` filter) — any player, not just an opponent, may be chosen.

ANCHORED (`^…$`): "Target player gains N life" is not a substring of any sibling activated rule (in particular it is disjoint from "You gain N life" and from "Target player loses N life and you gain N life"), and the anchor prevents a future broader pattern from consuming this sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetPlayerGainsLifeEffectRule.cs)

### `TargetPlayerLosesLifeYouGainLifeEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule, IMultiActivatedEffectRule

"Target player loses N life and you gain N life." — the targeted-drain activated-ability shape (Bloodrite Invoker: "{8}: Target player loses 3 life and you gain 3 life.").

A single "… and …"-joined sentence that expands to two sibling effects: `LoseLifeEffect` (a targeted player loses N) and `GainLifeEffect` (you gain N). This is the activated-ability counterpart of `TargetPlayerLosesLifeYouGainRule` (the instant/sorcery version, e.g. Absorb Vis) and a sibling of `EachOpponentLosesLifeYouGainLifeEffectRule` (the "each opponent" variant, e.g. Vampire Opportunist). The lose-life clause targets a chosen player (`Target` over an `Player()` filter); the gain-life clause credits the controller (`You`).

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." Both clauses are governed by this rule. The two amounts are parsed independently and need not be equal; the conjunction "and you gain N life" is what identifies the shape.

ANCHORED (`^…$`): "Target player loses N life and you gain N life" is not a substring of any sibling activated rule, and the anchor prevents a future broader pattern from consuming this sentence and silently dropping either conjunct.

Implemented as `IMultiActivatedEffectRule` so the two effects sit as a flat sibling pair on `Effects` — not wrapped in a `CompositeEffect`. `TryMatch` always returns null so the single-effect path never claims the sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/TargetPlayerLosesLifeYouGainLifeEffectRule.cs)

### `ThisCreatureGainsFearEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This [type] gains fear until end of turn." — a self-targeting activated grant of the fear keyword for the rest of the turn (Hooded Kavu "{B}: This creature gains fear until end of turn."). Fear is missing from `BuildGrantedKeywordAbility`, so the generic self-grant branch of `GainAbilityEffectRule` (Priority 995) returns null for it and the effect lands unstructured. This dedicated, fully-anchored rule structures the interior into the same `GainAbilityEffect` shape those siblings emit, granting fear's canonical structured expansion (mirrors `FearKeyword` and the printed gold for Razortooth Rats). Fear's structured form is an `EvasionEffect` whose `CanBeBlockedBy` is restricted to artifact creatures and/or black creatures — the evasion semantics of the keyword (the artifact type on CardTypes, the black color on Colors, as one disjunctive filter). CR 702.36a: "Fear is an evasion ability." CR 702.36b: "A creature with fear can't be blocked except by artifact creatures and/or black creatures." CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period." (the grant expires "until end of turn"). CR 602.1: activated abilities are written "[Cost]: [Effect.]" — this rule handles the post-colon effect fragment. Anchored end-to-end (^…$) so it claims only this exact self-grant phrase and never shadows another activated effect. Sits above the generic `GainAbilityEffectRule` (Priority 995); that rule cannot claim fear anyway (helper miss), so this is collision-free.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ThisCreatureGainsFearEffectRule.cs)

### `ThisCreatureGainsLandwalkEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This [type] gains [basic landwalk] until end of turn." — a self-targeting activated grant of a basic-land landwalk keyword for the rest of the turn (Enslaved Scout "{2}: This creature gains mountainwalk until end of turn."). The basic landwalk keywords (forestwalk / islandwalk / swampwalk / mountainwalk / plainswalk) are absent from `BuildGrantedKeywordAbility`, so the generic self-grant branch of `GainAbilityEffectRule` (Priority 995) returns null for them and the effect lands unstructured (L1). This dedicated, fully-anchored rule structures the interior into the same `GainAbilityEffect` shape those siblings emit, granting the landwalk keyword's canonical structured expansion — identical to the printed `MountainwalkKeyword` / `ForestwalkKeyword` combinator output (an `EvasionEffect` whose `UnblockableCondition` is `DefendingPlayerControls` over the matching basic land subtype). CR 702.14 (Landwalk): "Landwalk is an evasion ability." and "A creature with landwalk can't be blocked as long as the defending player controls at least one land with the specified land type (as in 'islandwalk')…". CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period." (the grant expires "until end of turn"). CR 602.1: activated abilities are written "[Cost]: [Effect.]" — this rule handles the post-colon effect fragment. Anchored end-to-end (^…$) and restricted to the five basic-land landwalk words, so it claims only this exact self-grant phrase and never shadows another activated effect. Sits above the generic `GainAbilityEffectRule` (Priority 995); that rule cannot claim these keywords anyway (helper miss), so this is collision-free.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ThisCreatureGainsLandwalkEffectRule.cs)

### `ThisCreatureGainsShadowEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"This [type] gains shadow until end of turn." — a self-targeting activated grant of the shadow keyword for the rest of the turn (Soltari Emissary "{W}: This creature gains shadow until end of turn."; also Thalakos Drifters and Trespasser il-Vec, whose cost is "Discard a card"). Shadow is missing from `BuildGrantedKeywordAbility`, so the generic self-grant branch of `GainAbilityEffectRule` (Priority 995) returns null for it and the effect lands unstructured. This dedicated, fully-anchored rule structures the interior into the same `GainAbilityEffect` shape those siblings emit, granting shadow's canonical structured expansion (mirrors `ShadowKeyword` and the printed gold for Soltari Foot Soldier). Shadow's structured form is an `EvasionEffect` whose `CanBeBlockedBy` is restricted to creatures that also have shadow — the mutual-evasion semantics of the keyword. CR 702.28a: "Shadow is an evasion ability." CR 702.28b: "A creature with shadow can't be blocked by creatures without shadow, and a creature without shadow can't be blocked by creatures with shadow." CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period." (the grant expires "until end of turn"). CR 602.1: activated abilities are written "[Cost]: [Effect.]" — this rule handles the post-colon effect fragment. Anchored end-to-end (^…$) so it claims only this exact self-grant phrase and never shadows another activated effect. Sits above the generic `GainAbilityEffectRule` (Priority 995); that rule cannot claim shadow anyway (helper miss), so this is collision-free.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Activated/Rules/ThisCreatureGainsShadowEffectRule.cs)

### `TransformSelfEffectRule` — *sealed class* : IActivatedEffectRule

"Transform this creature" / "Transform this permanent" — the activated transform-self ability on the front face of a double-faced card (e.g. "{6}: Transform this creature.").
