"Each player shuffles their graveyard into their library." — symmetric whole-zone recycle (Mnemonic Nexus).

CR 400.12: "Some effects instruct a player to do something to a zone (such as 'Shuffle your hand into your library'). That action is performed on all cards in that zone. The zone itself is not affected." CR 701.24a: "To shuffle a library or a face-down pile of cards, randomize the cards within it so that no player knows their order."

Anchored (^ … $) single-sentence match. Emits a `ShuffleGraveyardIntoLibraryEffect` whose `Player` carries `EachPlayer` — matching the "each player" subject in oracle text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/EachPlayerShufflesGraveyardIntoLibraryRule.cs)

### `EachSacrificesRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Each [player|opponent] sacrifices [a|an|N] [type]." — distributed sacrifice addressed to all players or all opponents (Rule 701.21a — Sacrifice).

"Each player sacrifices a creature." (Innocent Blood) "Each player sacrifices two creatures." (Barter in Blood) "Each opponent sacrifices a creature." (edict variant) "Each opponent sacrifices an artifact." (Visions of Ruin variant) "Each opponent sacrifices a permanent." (generic)

Emits a `SacrificeEffect` whose `Target` carries `EachPlayer` or `EachOpponent` and an `ObjectFilter` restricting the sacrificed object type.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/EachSacrificesRule.cs)

### `ExileAllRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Mass-exile spell rules. Two oracle shapes are handled:

"Exile all creatures." — removes every creature on the battlefield (the default game zone). `Zone` is left null (battlefield-scope is the implicit default for permanent references). Rule 701.13a (exile action) + Rule 400.1 (zones). "Exile all [type] cards from all graveyards." — graveyard-scope mass exile. Sets `Zone` to `Graveyard`. Covers Scavenging Ooze cousins and clean-the-graveyard spells. Rule 701.13a + Rule 400.2g (graveyard zone).

Both shapes emit an `ExileEffect` whose `Target` carries `Each` and the appropriate `ObjectFilter` slot populated.

Priority 60 — same band as `DestroyAllRule`. The leading "Exile all" anchor is mutually exclusive with all "Exile target" rules (priority 50–70), so no shadowing risk.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileAllRule.cs)

### `ExileAtYourNextEndStepSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile it at the beginning of your next end step." — the delayed-exile sentence that trails a token-creation (or other object-obtaining) effect in a multi-sentence spell ability (Stone Idol Trap). The pronoun "it" back-references the object created or obtained by the preceding clause (CR 109.2 — game objects).

CR 603.7: a triggered ability created by a resolving effect is a delayed triggered ability. MAST records this as a `CreateDelayedTriggerEffect` whose `Trigger` fires "at the beginning of your next end step" (a `GameTime` clock point with `Whose` = `You` for the "your" qualifier) and whose resolution exiles `It` — the delayed-exile sibling of `SacrificeAtEndStepSpellRule` (which handles the unqualified "the next end step" sacrifice sentence). Distinct GameTime.Whose is the only structural difference; the exiled-vs-sacrificed action is `ExileEffect` rather than `SacrificeEffect`.

Priority 71 — mirrors `SacrificeAtEndStepSpellRule`'s rationale (must supersede generic exile rules that match "exile [it]" without the duration clause). Fully anchored (^…$).

Rule citations: 701.13a (Exile); 513 (End Step); 603.7 (delayed triggers).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileAtYourNextEndStepSpellRule.cs)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileMonocoloredPermanentRule.cs)

### `ExileSelfByNameSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile [this card's name]." as a standalone spell sentence — the self-exile clause many instants/ sorceries use to remove themselves instead of going to the graveyard (older self-referential templating, e.g. Pair o' Dice Lost: "Exile Pair o' Dice Lost."). The exiled object is the spell itself, so this emits `ExileEffect` targeting `Self`.

Matches "Exile [Proper-Noun phrase]$" — a CAPITALISED name with no filter words ("target", "all", "each", "a/an/the" are lower-case and excluded by the capital-letter anchor), so it cannot swallow a real targeted/mass exile. Anchored; spell context only (an ISpellRule).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileSelfByNameSpellRule.cs)

### `ExileSelfThenReturnTransformedRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

"Exile this [permanent], then return it to the battlefield transformed under your control." — the final chapter of a transforming Saga (The Legend of Roku, chapter III). Returns the flat two-effect list [exile{Self}, returnToBattlefield].

The "it" in the second clause back-references the exiled permanent, which re-enters transformed (back face up, CR 712) under the controller's control. CR 701.13 (exile); CR 712 (transform); CR 715 (Saga). The exile-then-return is the standard flicker-to-transform idiom; the permanent's identity across the zone change is engine bookkeeping.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileSelfThenReturnTransformedRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetCardFromGraveyardRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile target card from a graveyard." / "Exile up to one target card from a graveyard." — single-card graveyard-exile spell effect (Rule 701.7). Handles both the bare "target card" form (Purify the Grave) and the "up to one target card" form (Heritage Reclamation). Priority 80: must override `ExileGraveyardsRule` which targets graveyards themselves (the prior agent's noted ordering pair).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileTargetCardFromGraveyardRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetControlledCreatureThenReturnOwnerRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile target creature you control, then return it to the battlefield under its owner's control." — the Ephemerate / blink-to-owner spell pattern.

This is the spell-wrapper of the classic blink (flicker) action where the returned permanent comes back under its <em>owner's</em> control rather than the controller's (contrast with `FlickerTargetPermanentsSpellRule`, which returns under "your control"). The oracle text uses a curly apostrophe (U+2019) in "owner’s", matched verbatim.

The composite shape mirrors the `FlickerTargetPermanentsSpellRule`: an `ExileEffect` on the chosen creature, followed by a `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect` whose target is the linked exiled card (CR 607.2 / ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution), addressed via `ExiledWith` = `{Kind: Self}`. "under its owner's control" maps to `Owner` on `UnderControl` (CR 400.6).

The pattern is anchored (^…$) to prevent substring matches inside more-specific sibling rules (e.g. the "non-Angel" or "another target" families). CR 701.13 (exile). CR 400.6 (owner/controller distinction).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileTargetControlledCreatureThenReturnOwnerRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetCreatureYouControlThenReturnYourControlSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under your control." — the Cloudshift blink-to-controller spell pattern.

Cloudshift is the mandatory (non-optional) single-target blink that returns the exiled creature under the <em>caster's</em> control. It differs from the sibling `ExileTargetControlledCreatureThenReturnOwnerRule`, which uses "return it … under its owner's control" (returning under <em>owner's</em> control), and from `FlickerTargetPermanentsSpellRule`, which targets two permanents of mixed types. This rule handles the "that card" anaphoric pronoun (back-reference to the just-exiled creature) returning under "your control" (the spell controller, CR 400.6).

The composite shape: an `ExileEffect` on the chosen creature, followed by a `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect` whose target is the linked exiled reference (CR 607.2 / ADR 0004 "reference, not resolution"), addressed via `ExiledWith` = `{Kind: Self}`. "under your control" maps to `You` on `UnderControl` (CR 400.6).

The pattern is anchored (^…$) to prevent substring matches inside more-specific sibling rules. Priority 80 ensures this fires before generic exile rules. CR 406.2 (exile — to put into the exile zone from whatever zone it's currently in). CR 400.6 (zone-change control assignment). CR 406.1 (exile may be temporary).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileTargetCreatureYouControlThenReturnYourControlSpellRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetLandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile target land." — Caustic Rain and similar sorceries that exile a single land permanent with no color, subtype, or disjunction qualifier. The bare "target land" shape is not covered by `ExileTypeDisjunctionRule` (which requires two or more types joined by "or") or the color/monocolored variants, so this rule handles the simplest case. Rule 701.13 (exile action) + Rule 205.3j (land as card type).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileTargetLandRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetPermanentByManaValueRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile target [type] with mana value N or less/greater/more/fewer." — a mana-value-gated single-target exile spell (Despark: "Exile target permanent with mana value 4 or greater."). The threshold lands on `ManaValueComparison` (Rule 202.3 defines mana value); the exile action itself is Rule 701.13a. Fully anchored (^…$) so the mandatory mana-value qualifier cannot let this pattern substring-match a more specific sibling; the type group is restricted to the small closed set of bare card types also handled by `ExileTargetSimpleRule`, so a card printing a richer filter phrase (subtype, color+type, …) alongside a mana-value qualifier still falls through to a different/new rule rather than being silently mis-captured here. Priority 70 — same tier as `ExileTargetQualifiedRule` (its sibling "with power N or less/greater" shape); both run ahead of `ExileTargetSimpleRule` (50), which would otherwise try to claim the raw text via its permissive filter-phrase fallback.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileTargetPermanentByManaValueRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetQualifiedRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile target [state] creature" and "Exile target creature with power N or less/greater." Covers:

State qualifiers: "Exile target tapped creature", "Exile target attacking creature" Power filter (less-or-equal): "Exile target creature with power 3 or less" Power filter (greater-or-equal): "Exile target creature with power 4 or greater"

Priority 70 — runs before `ExileTargetSimpleRule` (50), which would otherwise claim the raw text via its FilterPattern fallback and then fail to produce a filter for the "with power N" or state-adjective shapes. Rule 701.13 (exile action). Power comparisons: Rule 208.1 (power is a characteristic of creature cards).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileTargetQualifiedRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetSimpleRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile target [filter]." — single-target exile spell. Covers bare card-type targets (creature, artifact, enchantment, permanent, …) and richer filter phrases via `ParseTargetFilter`:

Subtype-only: "Spirit", "Human" Color + card type: "black creature", "white artifact" non- prefix + card type: "nonbasic land"

Coexistence with `ExileTargetLandRule`: both rules dispatch at priority 50; alphabetical ordering puts ExileTargetLandRule ahead of ExileTargetSimpleRule, so the bare "land" shape is still claimed by the specialised rule. This rule handles all other card-type filters. Rule 701.13 (exile action) + Rule 205.3 (card types).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileTargetSimpleRule.cs)

### `ExileTopCardsPlayThisTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile the top N cards of your library. You may play them this turn." — a current-turn-bounded impulse where all N exiled cards stay playable from exile until end of turn (Jeska's Will).

Modeled as a single `ImpulseEffect` with `RemainExiled` (none kept in hand; all N remain exiled) and an inherited `Duration` of `EndOfTurn`. The two oracle sentences are one game concept — "them" back-references the exiled pile — so they collapse into one node rather than a separate exile + permission. CR 406 (exile zone); CR 701.13 (exile). Sibling of `ExileTopCardsPlayUntilTimeRule` which uses "until the end of your next turn".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileTopCardsPlayThisTurnRule.cs)

### `ExileTopCardsPlayUntilTimeRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile the top N cards of your library. Until [time], you may play those cards." — a duration-bounded impulse where all N exiled cards stay playable from exile for a stated window (The Legend of Roku, chapter I).

Modeled as a single `ImpulseEffect` with `RemainExiled` (none kept in hand; all N remain exiled) and an inherited `Duration` bounding the play window. The two oracle sentences are one game concept — "those cards" back-references the exiled pile — so they collapse into one node rather than a separate exile + permission (ADR 0004: impulse is a cohesive one-shot; the "cards playable from exile" cluster is recovered by consumer projection over {ImpulseEffect, MayPlayFromExile}). CR 406 (exile zone); CR 701.13 (exile).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileTopCardsPlayUntilTimeRule.cs)

### `ExileTypeDisjunctionRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile target [type1] or [type2]." — Gravkill etc. Multi-element CardTypes is the disjunction.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ExileTypeDisjunctionRule.cs)

### `FightRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises fight-spell oracle text in the form:

"Target creature you control fights target creature you don't control." "Target creature you control fights target creature an opponent controls."

CR 701.14 (Fight keyword action). Reminder text "(Each deals damage equal to its power to the other.)" is stripped by the parenthetical-removal pass before spell rules run, so it does not appear in the input text here.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/FightRule.cs)

### `FlickerTargetPermanentsSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Exile [N] target [type list] you control, then return those cards to the battlefield under your control." — the spell-side flicker (blink) of Ghostly Flicker.

The line is a single composite (CR 603.2 governs the triggered sibling, Displacer Kitten; this is the spell wrapper of the same flicker effect): an `ExileEffect` on the chosen permanents, then a `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect` of the just-exiled cards. "those cards" is NOT free text — it is the linked exiled reference (CR 607.2 / ADR 0004 "reference, not resolution"): a `Designated` card in `Exile` exiled with this object (`ExiledWith = {Kind: Self}`), exactly the Petravark return shape. The two effects sit in one `CompositeEffect` because the oracle states them as a single "exile …, then return …" action.

"two" is a structured cardinality on the target reference's `Quantity` (a `LiteralQuantity`), not a literal repeated node. "artifacts, creatures, and/or lands you control" is a structured multi-type disjunction filter (<c>CardTypes = ["artifact", "creature", "land"]</c> + `Controller = You`) — any chosen permanent may be any of the three types. "under your control" rides on `UnderControl` as a `You` reference (CR 400.6).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/FlickerTargetPermanentsSpellRule.cs)

### `GainActivatedAbilitySpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the "Until end of turn, target creature gains &lt;quoted activated ability&gt;." shape — i.e. an instant/sorcery that grants a target creature a full activated ability (cost + effect, quoted in oracle text) for the rest of the turn. Example: Retraction Helix (BNG) — "Until end of turn, target creature gains &quot;{T}: Return target nonland permanent to its owner's hand.&quot;" The granted ability is modelled as a nested `ActivatedAbility` inside a `GainAbilityEffect`; the duration is `untilEndOfTurn`. CR 613.1c (Layer 6 — ability-granting effects); CR 611 (continuous effects with duration); CR 113.6 — abilities granted by effects are still full-fledged abilities of the gaining permanent. Priority 85: must fire before the bare keyword-grant rules (TargetCreatureGainsKeywordRule, priority 50) since this rule is more specific (the quoted text inside the gains clause is a full activated ability, not a keyword).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/GainActivatedAbilitySpellRule.cs)

### `GainLifeForEachCardInHandSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"You gain N life for each card in your hand." — spell-resolution life-gain scaled by a count of cards in the caster's own hand (Gerrard's Wisdom: "You gain 2 life for each card in your hand.").

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." The "for each card in your hand" count is recorded descriptively (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004) as a `CountQuantity` over an `ObjectFilter` (`CardTypes: ["card"], Zone: Hand, Controller: You`) — MAST does not resolve the number, mirroring the hand-count shape on `AddManaForEachCardInHandRule` (which counts a targeted opponent's hand rather than the caster's own). Sibling of `GainLifeForEachPermanentSpellRule` (which counts permanents on the battlefield rather than cards in hand); this rule owns the "in your hand" zone specifically.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/GainLifeForEachCardInHandSpellRule.cs)

### `GainLifeForEachPermanentSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"You gain N life for each [permanent type] you control." — spell-resolution life-gain scaled by a count of permanents the caster controls (e.g. Bountiful Harvest: "You gain 1 life for each land you control.").

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." The "for each &lt;type&gt; you control" count is recorded descriptively (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004) as a `CountQuantity` over an `ObjectFilter` — MAST does not resolve the number, mirroring the amount shape on `AddManaForEachTappedLandOpponentsControlRule`. Since the rate is exactly 1 life per counted object, the amount is the bare count (1 x count = count); a rate other than 1 (e.g. "gain 2 life for each …") is out of scope for this rule's target but the leading count is still captured for family robustness.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/GainLifeForEachPermanentSpellRule.cs)

### `GainLifeSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"You gain N life." — spell-resolution life-gain. Recuperate's first modal option. Also handles "You gain life equal to the life lost this way." — derived-quantity gain linked to a preceding LoseLifeEffect (Rule 119.3). Blood Tithe's second clause. Also handles "Target player gains N life." — life-gain whose subject is a targeted player rather than the controller (CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."). Also handles "If this spell was kicked, you gain life equal to the life lost this way." — a conditioned life-gain gated on the kicker cost having been paid (CR 702.33d–e, Blood Tribute). Uses the `Condition` field (mirrors `Condition`). Representative card: Soothing Balm ({1}{W}, Instant).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/GainLifeSpellRule.cs)

### `InvestigateSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Investigate." — Rule 701.28 keyword action. Creates a Clue token. Oracle lines containing only the keyword action (possibly with a reminder-text parenthetical, which is stripped by SpellAbilityParser before dispatch) produce a bare `InvestigateEffect`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/InvestigateSpellRule.cs)

### `ItDealsDamageEqualToPowerToTargetOpponentSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the pronoun-sourced "bite" continuation sentence: "It deals damage equal to its power to target creature an opponent controls." This is the back-reference companion of `BiteRule` (which handles the self-contained "Target creature you control deals damage equal to its power …" single-sentence form). Here the damage source is a previously-mentioned creature — the "It"/"its" both refer to the creature the preceding sentence pumped (Ambuscade's "Target creature you control gets +1/+0 …. It deals damage …") — so the source is an `It` reference rather than a fresh target. Emits a `DealDamageEffect` (non-combat damage, CR 120.1 — the source is the object dealing the damage) whose amount is a `DerivedQuantity` of the source's power ("equal to its power") and whose target is an opponent-controlled creature ("an opponent controls" → `Opponent`). Anchored `^…$` on the "It deals damage equal to its power to target creature an opponent controls" surface so it cannot swallow any broader sibling. Example:

"It deals damage equal to its power to target creature an opponent controls." (Ambuscade — second sentence)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ItDealsDamageEqualToPowerToTargetOpponentSpellRule.cs)

### `ItFightsColorControlledSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the pronoun-back-referenced fight shape with a colour-qualified opponent's creature: "It fights target green creature an opponent controls." "It fights target green creature you don't control." CR 701.14 (Fight keyword action). Distinct from `FightRule`'s "Target creature you control fights …" form: here the caster's participant is a pronoun back-reference ("It", CR 109.5 / rules of antecedent) to an object named by an earlier sentence in the same spell (e.g. Hunt the Hunter's pumped creature), modelled as `It`. The opponent's creature carries a colour restriction on `Colors` (CR 105.1). As in `FightRule`, both "an opponent controls" and "you don't control" produce identical AST — the Comprehensive Rules treat them as equivalent for targeting, so `Opposed` is always `Controller: Opponent`. Reminder text "(Each deals damage equal to its power to the other.)" is stripped before spell rules run. Examples:

"It fights target green creature an opponent controls." (Hunt the Hunter — second sentence)

Anchored with `^…$`; the mandatory "It fights" prefix keeps it from matching the "Target creature you control fights …" surface handled by `FightRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ItFightsColorControlledSpellRule.cs)

### `ItGainsKeywordSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"It gains [keyword] until end of turn." — a standalone sentence within a multi-sentence spell ability where "it" is a back-reference to an object named in the preceding sentence (e.g. the token created by a copy effect).

Emits a `GainAbilityEffect` targeting `It` with an `untilEndOfTurn` duration. The `It` reference is the standard MAST pronoun-back-reference (Rule 109.2 — game objects referenced by "it") and connects to the immediately preceding object in the same ability's effect list.

This rule handles the trailing "It gains haste until end of turn." sentence that appears in copy-token patterns (Molten Duplication) and similar spells. It is intentionally limited to a single keyword per sentence so the match is unambiguous and does not collide with the multi-effect `ThreatenRule` (which handles the full three-sentence Threaten / Act of Treason pattern as a unit).

Priority 55: above the generic `TargetCreatureGainsKeywordRule` (no priority = default 50) so this "it gains" shape is claimed before the "target … gains" shape could incorrectly fire.

Rule citations: CR 109.2 (pronoun reference), CR 611 (continuous effects with duration), CR 702.10 (haste).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ItGainsKeywordSpellRule.cs)

### `ItsControllerLosesLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Its controller loses N life." — life-loss whose subject back-references the controller of a permanent named in a prior sentence (Rule 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."). This rule handles the trailing sentence in patterns like: "Destroy target land. Its controller loses 2 life." (Spreading Rot) "Its controller" is modelled as `Controller`, which is an anaphoric reference to the controller of the previously mentioned object (the destroyed land). No runtime tracking is introduced — MAST describes the card, it does not execute it. CR 119.3 (verbatim): "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." CR 701.8a (verbatim): "To destroy a permanent, move it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ItsControllerLosesLifeRule.cs)

### `ItsControllerLosesLifeYouGainRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

"Its controller loses N life and you gain M life." — the anaphoric drain pattern where the controller of a permanent/spell named in a prior sentence loses a fixed amount of life and the controller of this spell gains the same (or another) amount.

Recognised shapes:

"Its controller loses 3 life and you gain 3 life." — Punish Ignorance (the trailing sentence of "Counter target spell. Its controller loses 3 life and you gain 3 life.")

"Its controller" is modelled as `Controller`, an anaphoric reference to the controller of the previously mentioned object (here the countered spell). "you" is the controller of this spell, modelled as `You`. No runtime tracking is introduced — MAST describes the card, it does not execute it.

Emits a flat [`LoseLifeEffect`, `GainLifeEffect`] pair via `TryMatchMulti`. The single-effect `TryMatch` always returns false — this shape never reduces to a single Effect. The two amounts are parsed independently and need not be equal; the conjunction "and you gain M life" is what distinguishes this from the plain `ItsControllerLosesLifeRule` ("Its controller loses N life." — Spreading Rot), whose pattern anchors immediately after "life" and so never overlaps.

CR 119.3 (verbatim): "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ItsControllerLosesLifeYouGainRule.cs)

### `ItsControllerMillsRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Its controller mills N cards." — the mill keyword action (CR 701.17a) whose subject back-references the controller of a permanent or spell named in a prior sentence, mirroring the anaphoric-controller pattern already used by `ItsControllerLosesLifeRule`. This rule handles the trailing sentence in patterns like: "Counter target spell. Its controller mills three cards." (Didn't Say Please) "Its controller" is modelled as `Controller`, an anaphoric reference to the controller of the previously mentioned object (the countered spell). No runtime tracking is introduced — MAST describes the card, it does not execute it. CR 701.17a (verbatim): "For a player to mill a number of cards, that player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ItsControllerMillsRule.cs)

### `LookAtHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Look at target player's hand." — the Peek pattern (Rule 701.12). The controller looks at all cards in the named player's hand. "Their hand" means every card present, modelled as `CardsInHand` to mirror the `DiscardHandSpellRule` convention for "their hand" phrasing.

"Look at target player's hand." — Peek (INV) "Look at target opponent's hand." — Ostracize variant

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/LookAtHandRule.cs)

### `LookAtTopPutInHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the Impulse/Strategic Planning pattern: "Look at the top N cards of your library. Put one of them into your hand and the rest into your graveyard." or the bottom-of-library variant: "Look at the top N cards of your library. Put one of them into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in any order." Both sentences are part of a single `ImpulseEffect`. The rule matches the full two-sentence text before the sentence-bundle path splits it, via the single-effect `TryMatch` path which receives the whole clause text. Examples:

"Look at the top three cards of your library. Put one of them into your hand and the rest into your graveyard." — Strategic Planning "Look at the top four cards of your library. Put one of them into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in any order." — Impulse

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/LookAtTopPutInHandRule.cs)

### `LookAtTopTwoPutOneInHandOtherBottomRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the Sleight of Hand "the other" variant of the Impulse/Anticipate look-and-keep-one family: "Look at the top N cards of your library. Put one of them into your hand and the other on the bottom of your library."

This is the singular-remainder spelling of the same single atomic action modelled by `ImpulseEffect` with `BottomOfLibrary`: the controller looks at the top N cards, keeps one in hand, and the remaining card(s) go to the bottom of the library. It differs from the sibling `LookAtTopPutInHandRule` only in surface form — "the other" (rather than "the rest … in any order"), the wording a card uses when exactly one card remains after keeping one of two, so no ordering clause is printed. The semantics are identical, so it reuses the same `ImpulseEffect` node; no new discriminator is introduced.

The two-sentence oracle text is a single game action — "the other" in the second sentence back-references the cards looked at by the first. Matching the whole clause here (an anchored `TryMatch`) keeps it as one coupled `ImpulseEffect` rather than a decomposed [lookAtCards, …] list.

Example:

"Look at the top two cards of your library. Put one of them into your hand and the other on the bottom of your library." — Sleight of Hand

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/LookAtTopTwoPutOneInHandOtherBottomRule.cs)

### `LoseLifeEachSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Each player loses N life." and "Each opponent loses N life." — spell-resolution life-loss addressed to all players or all opponents (Rule 119.3, Rule 113.3a). Examples: Crushing Disappointment, Risky Shortcut (EachPlayer); Blood Tithe (EachOpponent).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/LoseLifeEachSpellRule.cs)

### `MaddeningCacophonyRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Kicker-gated mill-opponent-or-mill-half-library spell pattern. Handles the two-sentence oracle text: <code> Each opponent mills [N] cards. If this spell was kicked, instead each opponent mills half their library, rounded up. </code> Produces two sibling `MillEffect` nodes on `Effects`:

Base mill — count N, player EachOpponent, no condition. Kicked replacement mill — count = half opponent's library rounded up, player EachOpponent, condition = `KeywordCostPaidCondition` Kicker (CR 702.33d–e). The "instead" is expressed by the condition: when the condition holds the kicked effect supersedes the base.

The kicked count is a `CalculatedQuantity` (operation "half", rounding "up") over a `CountQuantity` of cards in the opponent's library.

CR 702.33 (Kicker): "Kicker is a static ability … 'Kicker [cost]' means 'You may pay an additional [cost] as you cast this spell.'" CR 702.33d: "a spell has been kicked" when its kicker cost was paid. CR 702.33e: effects gated on the kicked state are "if this spell was kicked" clauses.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/MaddeningCacophonyRule.cs)

### `MassAnthemAndGainKeywordSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the mass P/T-modification-plus-keyword-grant shape for creatures the caster controls: "Creatures you control get +N/+M and gain &lt;keyword(s)&gt; until end of turn." Sibling of `MassAnthemSpellRule` (which covers the P/T-only shape) — this rule requires the "and gain &lt;keyword&gt;" clause and is fully anchored so it cannot substring-capture the P/T-only sentence that rule owns. Emits a single `CompositeEffect` wrapping the `ModifyPTEffect` and one `GainAbilityEffect` per keyword (all sharing the same duration and the same "creatures you control" target), mirroring the conjunctive-modifier gold convention used on the triggered side (Rule 611 — continuous effects applied simultaneously; see `EtbTeamPumpTriggeredRule` for the trigger-context sibling). Example: "Creatures you control get +1/+1 and gain haste until end of turn." (Goblin War Party's second modal option.)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/MassAnthemAndGainKeywordSpellRule.cs)

### `MassAnthemSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the mass P/T-modification shape for creature subsets: "Creatures you control get +N/+M until end of turn." "Creatures you control get -N/-M until end of turn." "Creatures your opponents control get -N/-M until end of turn." "All creatures get +N/+M until end of turn." "All creatures get -N/-M until end of turn." "Attacking creatures get +N/+M until end of turn." "Blocking creatures get +N/+M until end of turn." This is the mass anthem/debuff version. The single-target "Target creature gets +N/+M ..." shape is handled separately by `ModifyPTSpellRule`. Examples:

"Creatures you control get +1/+1 until end of turn." (Charge) "Creatures you control get +0/+4 until end of turn." (Bar the Door) "All creatures get -1/-1 until end of turn." (Shrivel) "All creatures get -2/-2 until end of turn." (Infest) "All creatures get -4/-4 until end of turn." (Languish) "Attacking creatures get +2/+0 until end of turn." (Army of Allah) "Blocking creatures get +0/+3 until end of turn." (Piety) "Creatures your opponents control get -1/-1 until end of turn." (Cower in Fear) "Creatures your opponents control get -1/-1 until end of turn." (Make Obsolete)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/MassAnthemSpellRule.cs)

### `MassModifyPTVariableSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the mass P/T-modification shape for creature subsets where the power and/or toughness modifiers are the spell's announced X (rather than a literal number): "All creatures get +X/-X until end of turn." (Flowstone Slide) Sibling group to `MassAnthemSpellRule` (which requires a LITERAL digit in both slots — its `\d+` pattern never matches an X/Y/Z letter, so the two rules are disjoint by construction, no dispatch priority needed) and to `ModifyPTBothVariableSpellRule` (which covers the same X-scaled shape but for a SINGLE "Target creature" subject rather than a mass creature-subset subject).

CR 107.3a: "Some spells and abilities have an 'X' in their costs. ... The player announces the value of X when casting the spell." CR 107.3i: "Normally, all instances of X on an object have the same value at any given time." — the same announced X is referenced by both P/T slots here, so both share one `VariableQuantity` letter; a negative slot ("-X") negates that same value via a `CalculatedQuantity` multiply-by -1 wrapper (mirroring how `ScentOfNightshade.json`'s gold AST negates a non-X quantity for its own "-X/-X" shape).

CR 611.2: a continuous effect may be generated by the resolution of a spell — "All creatures get +X/-X until end of turn" is such a one-shot continuous effect, in scope only until end of turn. CR 613.4c (Layer 7c): "Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied" — a P/T modification, hence `ModifyPTEffect`, not a set-P/T effect.

Examples:

"All creatures get +X/-X until end of turn." (Flowstone Slide)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/MassModifyPTVariableSpellRule.cs)

### `MayPutCardFromHandOntoBattlefieldRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"You may put a[n] [filter] card from your hand onto the battlefield [tapped]."

Spell-resolution sentence for the optional hand-to-battlefield land drop that closes cards like Embrace the Paradox ("Draw three cards. You may put a land card from your hand onto the battlefield tapped."). The draw sentence is handled by `DrawCardsSimpleRule`; this rule matches the second sentence of the bundle. The "you may" wrapper is expressed as an `OptionalEffect` around a `PutFromHandOntoBattlefieldEffect` (ADR 0005 clause-modifier composition), mirroring the triggered `DrawThenMayPutLandFromHandRule` (Spelunking) so both surfaces emit the same node shape.

Rule citations:

CR 400.7: "An object that moves from one zone to another becomes a new object..." — the hand-to-battlefield move. CR 110.5: a permanent's status includes tapped/untapped — the optional "tapped" qualifier sets `Tapped`.

ANCHORED (^…$): the whole sentence is matched exactly so this rule cannot fire as a substring of any more-specific sibling. Default priority (50) — the anchor makes it mutually exclusive with other spell rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/MayPutCardFromHandOntoBattlefieldRule.cs)

### `MillSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Spell-resolution mill keyword action. Rule 701.17. Handles five oracle clause forms:

"Mill N cards." — controller (Player = You). "Target player mills N cards." — targeted player (Player = Target + player filter). "Target opponent mills N cards." — targeted opponent (Player = Opponent). "Target player mills half their library, rounded down." — half-library mill, rounded down (Traumatize). CR 701.17a: to mill a number of cards is to put that many cards from the top of the library into the graveyard. "Target player mills half their library, rounded up." — half-library mill, rounded up.

For the triggered-ability side, see `MillTriggeredRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/MillSpellRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTAndGainKeywordControlledSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Recognises the controller-qualified composite buff shape: "Target creature you control gets +N/+M and gains &lt;keyword(s)&gt; until end of turn." This covers protective instants like Dive Down (XLN) where the caster targets only one of their own creatures to apply both a P/T modification and a keyword grant. The "you control" qualifier restricts the target to permanents the active player controls (CR 109.5 — controller filter on target). Emits a flat list via `TryMatchMulti`: `[ModifyPTEffect (Target=you-control creature), GainAbilityEffect (Target=It), …]`, one `GainAbilityEffect` per keyword, all sharing a single `UntilEndOfTurnDuration` instance.

The single-effect `TryMatch` always returns false so the flat-list path is the only active route.

CR citations: 702.11b — "Hexproof" on a permanent means "This permanent can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control." CR 613.1 — "The values of an object's characteristics are determined by starting with the actual object… Then all applicable continuous effects are applied in a series of layers in the following order:" (P/T and ability-granting are continuous effects).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ModifyPTAndGainKeywordControlledSpellRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTAndGainKeywordSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Recognises the composite buff shape: "Target creature gets +N/+M and gains &lt;keyword(s)&gt; until end of turn." This covers any single-target creature buff that combines a P/T modifier with one or more keyword grants, all with until-end-of-turn duration. The keywords group is one or more keyword names joined by " and ". Examples:

"Target creature gets +2/+2 and gains trample until end of turn." "Target creature gets +3/+0 and gains first strike and reach until end of turn." "Target creature gets +1/+1 and gains flying and first strike until end of turn."

Emits a flat list via `TryMatchMulti`: `[ModifyPTEffect, GainAbilityEffect, …]`, one `GainAbilityEffect` per keyword, all sharing a single `UntilEndOfTurnDuration` instance.

The single-effect `TryMatch` always returns false so the flat-list path is the only active route.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ModifyPTAndGainKeywordSpellRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTAndMustBeBlockedSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Recognises the composite "pump + lure" shape: "Target creature gets +N/+M until end of turn and must be blocked this turn if able." (Compelled Duel) Two continuous effects apply to the same single target creature, joined by a bare "and" inside one sentence (no sentence boundary, so the sentence-bundle path never sees it): a P/T modifier (CR 611.2c — a continuous effect from resolution that modifies characteristics) and a block requirement (CR 509.1c — a "must be blocked if able" requirement the defending player must satisfy when declaring blockers). Both last until end of turn ("this turn" for the block requirement is the same clock-bounded expiry). Emits a flat list via `TryMatchMulti`: `[ModifyPTEffect, MustBeBlockedEffect]`, reusing the exact nodes the single-effect siblings emit (`ModifyPTSpellRule` and `MustBeBlockedTargetRule`) so a single-target pump and a single-target lure compose without a new discriminator.

The single-effect `TryMatch` always returns false so the flat-list path is the only active route (mirrors `ModifyPTAndGainKeywordSpellRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ModifyPTAndMustBeBlockedSpellRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTAsLongAsSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the P/T-modification shape with an "as long as [condition]" duration: "Target creature gets +N/+M for as long as [condition]." "Target creature gets -N/-M for as long as [condition]." The condition text (e.g. "this artifact remains tapped") is stored verbatim on `Condition` — not parsed further. This mirrors how `TryParseAsLongAsStaticGrant` handles the same duration suffix on static ability grants. Examples:

"Target creature gets +1/+1 for as long as this artifact remains tapped." (Tawnos's Weaponry) "Target creature gets +0/+2 for as long as this artifact remains tapped." (Spirit Shield) "Target creature gets +0/+3 for as long as this artifact remains tapped." (Endoskeleton)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ModifyPTAsLongAsSpellRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTBothVariableSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the X-scaled P/T-modification shape where BOTH power and toughness are the same announced variable: "Target creature gets +X/+X until end of turn." Per CR 107.3a, the controller announces the value of X when casting the spell. Per CR 107.3i, "Normally, all instances of X on an object have the same value at any given time" — so the power and toughness modifiers here share the same `VariableQuantity` name. Per CR 613.4c (Layer 7c), this is a P/T -modifying effect (not a set-P/T effect), so it is modeled as `ModifyPTEffect`. This pattern requires a variable (X/Y/Z) in BOTH the power and toughness slots and is mutually exclusive with `ModifyPTSpellRule`'s patterns, which all require a literal digit in at least the toughness slot. Examples:

"Target creature gets +X/+X until end of turn." (Untamed Might)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ModifyPTBothVariableSpellRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTConjunctionRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Rookie-Mistake shape (single-effect dispatch path): "Until end of turn, target creature gets +0/+2 and another target creature gets -2/-0." Wrapped in a `CompositeEffect`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ModifyPTConjunctionRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the bare P/T-modification shape (no keyword conjunction): "Target creature gets +N/+M until end of turn." "Target creature gets -N/-M until end of turn." "Target creature gets +X/+0 until end of turn." — variable X form "It gets +N/+M until end of turn." — pronoun back-reference form This is the simple single-effect version. The composite "gets +N/+M and gains &lt;keyword&gt; until end of turn" case is handled separately by `ModifyPTAndGainKeywordSpellRule` and is tried first at higher priority. Examples:

"Target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn." (Giant Growth) "Target creature gets +4/+4 until end of turn." (Titanic Growth) "Target creature gets -2/-2 until end of turn." (Disfigure) "Target creature gets -3/-3 until end of turn." (Last Gasp) "Target creature gets +X/+0 until end of turn." (Howl from Beyond) "It gets +2/+4 until end of turn." (Inspirit — second sentence)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ModifyPTSpellRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTThenConditionalDrawRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Two-sentence compound spell of the "pump-then-conditional-draw" shape: "Target creature gets -N/-M until end of turn. If &lt;condition&gt;, draw &lt;count&gt; card(s)."

Representative card: Chilling Trap — "Target creature gets -4/-0 until end of turn. If you control a Wizard, draw a card."

Sentence 1 is a `ModifyPTEffect` targeting a creature with an end-of-turn `Duration`. Sentence 2 is a `DrawCardsEffect` guarded by its own `Condition` (the standard structured slot for the "If &lt;condition&gt;, draw a card" idiom — see `ReturnKickedDrawRule`). The two effects sit as siblings on `Effects`; the condition is descriptive, not a runtime branch (ADR 0004: MAST describes, does not execute). The condition phrase is structured by `ConditionParser` — "you control a Wizard" becomes a subtype `CountCondition`.

This is a `IMultiSpellRule`: the shape always yields two sibling effects and is anchored to the FULL two-sentence text (sentence 1 MUST be the ModifyPT form), so it cannot collide with the generic sentence-bundle path or with any sibling that shares only the conditional-draw tail.

CR 121.1: "A player draws a card by putting the top card of their library into their hand." CR 611.2: a continuous effect may be generated by the resolution of a spell (the P/T buff).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ModifyPTThenConditionalDrawRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTXCountSubtypeSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the P/T-modification shape whose X is DEFINED by the spell as an object count, rather than announced by the caster: "Target creature gets +X/+X until end of turn, where X is the number of Elves on the battlefield." (Wirewood Pride)

CR 107.3: "Many objects use the letter X as a placeholder for a number that needs to be determined. Some objects have abilities that define the value of X …" Here the ability defines X ("where X is the number of Elves on the battlefield"), so both P/T modifiers resolve to the SAME game-state count rather than a caster -announced `VariableQuantity`. Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): the count is modelled structurally as a `CountQuantity` over an `ObjectFilter` (the creature subtype in the battlefield zone); the engine evaluates the actual number at resolution time.

CR 613.4 (Layer 7 sublayers): a "+X/+X" modifier that adds to power/toughness (rather than setting them) is a P/T-modifying effect, hence `ModifyPTEffect` (not a set-P/T effect). "on the battlefield" carries no controller restriction, so the filter has `Battlefield` with no `Controller` — every Elf, regardless of controller.

Anchored (`^…$`) and distinct from `ModifyPTBothVariableSpellRule`, whose pattern ends at "until end of turn" with no ", where X is …" tail.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ModifyPTXCountSubtypeSpellRule.cs)

### `MustAttackTargetRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target creature attacks this turn if able." — Boiling Blood. Rule 508.1d.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/MustAttackTargetRule.cs)

"Target creature must be blocked this turn if able." — Irresistible Prey. Rule 509.1c.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/MustBeBlockedTargetRule.cs)

### `MustBlockTargetRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target creature blocks this turn if able." — Culling Mark. Rule 509.1c.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/MustBlockTargetRule.cs)

### `NextCastCopySpellDelayedRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"When you next cast an instant or sorcery spell this turn, copy that spell. You may choose new targets for the copy." — a spell whose resolution creates a delayed triggered ability (CR 603.7) bounded to this turn: the trigger is the next instant or sorcery spell cast by you, and the effect copies that spell with optional retargeting (Doublecast).

CR 603.7: "An effect may create a delayed triggered ability that can do something at a later time. A delayed triggered ability will contain 'when,' 'whenever,' or 'at,' although that word won't usually begin the ability." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." "Next" is the once-form of an event trigger — captured by `When` ("triggers once") composed with the this-turn `Duration` window, not a separate field; the codebase's `GameTime{When:"Next"}` marker is reachable only on clock triggers (Timing "At", Event = a GameTime), not an event trigger like `SpellCast`.

CR 707.10: "To copy a spell, activated ability, or triggered ability means to put a copy of it onto the stack ... A copy of a spell or ability copies both the characteristics of the spell or ability and all decisions made for it, including modes, targets ... It does not necessarily have the same target, but only because [an effect] allows choosing of new targets." — the CR basis for `MayChooseNewTargets`: a copy inherits the original's targets unless the effect grants reselection, which this card does.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/NextCastCopySpellDelayedRule.cs)

### `PeerIntoTheAbyssRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

"Target player draws cards equal to half the number of cards in their library and loses half their life. Round up each time." — the Peer into the Abyss draw-half-library-then-lose-half-life pattern.

Both quantities are `CalculatedQuantity` with `Operation="half"` and `Rounding="up"`. The draw count is based on a `CountQuantity` of cards in the target player's library (Zone=Library, Controller=Target). The life-loss amount is based on a `DerivedQuantity` with `DerivedFrom=LifeTotal` (the target player's life total is implicit from the `Player` reference).

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."

The trailing "Round up each time." sentence is a printed instruction clarifying rounding direction for both effects; it is encoded structurally as `Rounding="up"` on each `CalculatedQuantity` rather than as a separate effect.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PeerIntoTheAbyssRule.cs)

### `PermanentsYouControlGainKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Permanents you control gain [keyword] until end of turn." — spell-resolution mass keyword grant to every permanent the caster controls (e.g. Simic Charm's modal option "Permanents you control gain hexproof until end of turn."). This is a modal spell (CR 700.2) option: choosing it triggers a one-shot imperative grant (Rule 113.3a), distinct from the declarative static form "Permanents you control have [keyword]." The target uses the CR 110.4a pseudo card-type "permanent" (broader than "creature") with `You`, mirroring the narrower creature-scoped sibling `CreaturesYouControlGainKeywordRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PermanentsYouControlGainKeywordRule.cs)

### `PreventAllCombatDamageThisTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt this turn." Fog-effect instants (Rule 615.1). Combat damage only; no target (blanket).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PreventAllCombatDamageThisTurnRule.cs)

### `PreventAllCombatDamageToPlayersThisTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt to players this turn." (Commencement of Festivities, Defend the Hearth). A Fog-effect instant (CR 615.1) narrowed to only the damage that would be dealt to players — combat damage aimed at creatures/planeswalkers still applies. Distinct from the unrestricted `PreventAllCombatDamageThisTurnRule` ("this turn", no recipient qualifier) and from single-recipient shields ("to target creature"/"to you"): the "players" plural with no "target" keyword is an untargeted blanket over every player, modeled as `EachPlayer`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PreventAllCombatDamageToPlayersThisTurnRule.cs)

### `PreventDamageThisTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Prevent the next N damage that would be dealt to target [type] this turn." (Rule 615.1) "Prevent the next N damage that would be dealt to any target this turn." (Rule 615.1)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PreventDamageThisTurnRule.cs)

### `ProliferateSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Proliferate (Rule 701.27) in a spell or activated-ability context.

Handled patterns (via `TryMatch`):

"Proliferate." — standalone spell or activated effect.

Handled patterns (via `TryMatchMulti`):

"Destroy target [filter], then proliferate." — emits a flat [`DestroyEffect`, `ProliferateEffect`] list. The "then proliferate" suffix is a sequencing marker; both effects are siblings on the ability's Effects list. (Spread the Sickness pattern.)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ProliferateSpellRule.cs)

### `PutAnyNumberFromGYOnTopRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Put any number of target creature cards from your graveyard on top of your library." Covers the unbounded multi-target graveyard-to-library-top zone change. Examples: Forever Young (ELD), Gravepurge (DTK), Footbottom Feast (CMD). Count is modelled as `UpToQuantity` with `MaxValue` maximum — the same convention used for "choose any number" modal abilities (Rule 700.2). Source zone on `Zone`; count on `Quantity`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PutAnyNumberFromGYOnTopRule.cs)

### `PutCounterOnEachRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Put a [counter-type] counter on each [type] you control." — Titania's Boon. Count=1. Matches the mass-counter shape where the controller distributes one counter to every qualifying permanent they control, e.g.: "Put a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PutCounterOnEachRule.cs)

### `PutCounterOnEachTargetPlayerControlsRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Put a [counter-type] counter on each [type] target player controls." — the mass-counter shape distributed over every qualifying permanent a TARGETED player controls, e.g.: "Put a +1/+1 counter on each creature target player controls." (Requisition Raid's third Spree mode). Count=1. Sibling of `PutCounterOnEachRule` (the "each … you control" form); the controller axis is `Target` rather than `You`. Fully anchored (`^…$`) and required to end in "target player controls", so it is mutually exclusive with the "you control" sibling and cannot substring-capture it.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PutCounterOnEachTargetPlayerControlsRule.cs)

### `PutCounterOnSelfRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Put a [counter-type] counter on this [creature|permanent|...]." — the self-referential counter placement. Count=1.

This surfaces the put-counters-on-self shape on the SPELL rule chain so it is reachable when a modal option body is dispatched as a `SpellAbility`. The "When this creature enters, choose one — • Put a +1/+1 counter on this creature. • ..." family (Saurian Symbiote) routes each bullet body back through the classifier+registry, which classifies a bare "Put a … counter on this creature." imperative as a spell. The triggered `PutCountersTriggeredRule` already handles the same text on the triggered chain; this is its spell-chain sibling so the mode parses to its established `PutCountersEffect` shape rather than falling through to an unparsed ability.

CR 122.1: "A counter is a marker placed on an object or player that modifies its characteristics and/or interacts with a rule or effect." Handles both P/T notation counters ("+1/+1", "-1/-1") and named word counters. Distinct from `PutCounterOnTargetRule` only in subject: "this [permanent]" → a `Self` reference rather than a targeted one.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PutCounterOnSelfRule.cs)

### `PutCounterOnTargetRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Put a [counter-type] counter on target [type]." — Boon of Safety, Battlegrowth. Count=1. Handles both word counters ("shield") and P/T notation counters ("+1/+1", "-1/-1").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PutCounterOnTargetRule.cs)

### `PutCountersTargetSubtypeDisjunctionRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Put N [counter type] counters on target [Subtype1] or [Subtype2] you control." Subtype-disjunction target (Rule 205.3) with an explicit Controller=You.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PutCountersTargetSubtypeDisjunctionRule.cs)

### `PutOnTopOfLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Put target [type] on top of its owner's library." Covers single-target library-top zone change — the Time Ebb / Temporal Spring pattern.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/PutOnTopOfLibraryRule.cs)

### `RegenerateTargetSimpleRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Regenerate target [filter]." — single-target regenerate spell (CR 701.19, "regenerate [permanent]" keyword action). Mirrors `DestroyTargetSimpleRule`: covers bare card-type targets (creature, artifact, land, …) and richer filter phrases via `ParseTargetFilter`:

Subtype-only: "Spirit", "Human" Color + card type: "black creature", "white creature" non- prefix + card type: "nonbasic land"

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/RegenerateTargetSimpleRule.cs)

### `RemoveUpToNCountersFromTargetCreatureRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Remove up to three counters from target creature." — an unqualified counter-removal spell effect with a bounded "up to N" count (Heartless Act, mode 2).

The counters removed are unqualified: the player chooses which counters (of any kind) to remove, up to the stated maximum (CR 122.1 — counters; CR 122.3 governs removal). MAST records this with `RemoveCountersEffect` using the sentinel `CounterType = "any"` ("counters of any kind, chosen by the removing player" — distinct from the printed-type values like "+1/+1" and from the "all" sentinel meaning "every counter type currently present on a source"). The bounded "up to N" cardinality rides on `UpToQuantity` (minimum 0), the documented home for "up to N" quantities, rather than a fixed `LiteralQuantity`.

Anchored to the full "counters from target creature" surface (bare "counters", no type qualifier; "target creature", not "target permanent"/"noncreature artifact"/a type disjunction) so it matches only this shape and does not shadow the siblings that remove typed counters ("charge counters", Gremlin Mine) or target other object sets (Glissa Sunslayer / Render Inert "target permanent", Price of Betrayal's "target artifact, creature, planeswalker, or opponent").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/RemoveUpToNCountersFromTargetCreatureRule.cs)

### `ReturnAnyNumberGraveyardDieBudgetRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Return any number of cards with total mana value X or less from your graveyard to your hand, where X is the total of those results." — Pair o' Dice Lost. A graveyard recursion whose budget is a SET cap on the total mana value of the chosen cards (CR 107.3), and the budget X is the die-roll total (CR 706). Emits a `ReturnToHandEffect` targeting the controller's graveyard cards (Kind = Designated — the player chooses which) with `TotalManaValueBudget` = the die-roll result.

Anchored (^…$) to this exact shape so it cannot match a plain graveyard return. The link from X to the preceding "Roll [N] dice" is the die-roll-result quantity; the engine reads the budget, not the arithmetic.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnAnyNumberGraveyardDieBudgetRule.cs)

### `ReturnArtifactOrEnchantmentFromGraveyardSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Return target artifact or enchantment card from your graveyard to your hand." The Argivian Find family — a Regrowth-style graveyard recursion instant, but with an artifact-or-enchantment type-disjunction (parallel to `ReturnInstantOrSorceryFromGraveyardSpellRule` for instant/sorcery). Resolved as a plain one-shot zone-change instruction (CR 608.2). Source zone is the graveyard (CR 404.1); destination is the hand (CR 402.1); "target" is CR 115.1. Zone = Graveyard encodes the source zone stated in oracle text; Controller = You encodes "your graveyard". CardTypes = ["artifact", "enchantment"] encodes the type-disjunction — the filter is satisfied when the object has ANY of the listed types (OR semantics, CR 115.3). Priority above the generic ReturnFromGraveyardToHandRule because this rule is more specific (type-disjunction shape); the two are mutually exclusive in practice since the generic rule's single-filter alternation never matches "artifact or enchantment".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnArtifactOrEnchantmentFromGraveyardSpellRule.cs)

### `ReturnCommanderToHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Put your commander into your hand from the command zone." — Road of Return.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnCommanderToHandRule.cs)

### `ReturnControlledDrawRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Two-sentence compound spell: "Return target nonland permanent to its owner's hand. If you controlled that permanent, draw a card." (Boomerang Basics).

Sentence 1 is a `ReturnToHandEffect` targeting "nonland permanent". Sentence 2 is a `DrawCardsEffect` guarded by a `ControlledObjectCondition` — "you controlled that permanent", where "that permanent" is the object sentence 1 returned (`It`) and the controller is "you" (`You`). Both effects sit as siblings on the single `Effects` list; the condition is descriptive, not a runtime branch — consistent with the MAST "describes cards, does not execute them" doctrine.

CR 121.1 (draw): "A player draws a card by putting the top card of their library into their hand." CR 109.4 (controller): "Only objects on the stack or on the battlefield have a controller. Objects that are neither on the stack nor on the battlefield aren't controlled by any player." — hence the past-tense gate on the already-returned permanent (see `ControlledObjectCondition`). Priority 80 so this supersedes the general sentence-bundle path, which would dispatch each sentence independently and fail on the conditional-draw fragment. Anchored on the "If you controlled that permanent," lead so it never collides with the kicker sibling (`ReturnKickedDrawRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnControlledDrawRule.cs)

### `ReturnCountTargetPermanentsToOwnersHandsSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Return X target nonland permanents to their owners' hands." — the spell-side multi-target bounce whose target set has a variable (or literal) cardinality over a PLURAL permanent type, e.g. Distorting Wake: "Return X target nonland permanents to their owners' hands." Handles a variable count (X/Y/Z), a literal count ("two", "3"), or the unbounded "any number of" choice (Kiora's Dismissal: "Return any number of target enchantments to their owners' hands.", CR 107.3) over a PLURAL card type ("permanents", "creatures", …), with an optional "non&lt;x&gt;" or colour modifier before the type ("nonland", "green"), returned to their owners' hands (plural possessive, because there are multiple returned permanents with potentially different owners).

Spell-side sibling of the activated-ability `ReturnCountTargetPermanentsToOwnersHandsEffectRule` (Alexi, Zephyr Mage): identical shape, different dispatch surface (a sorcery/instant spell effect rather than an activated-ability effect fragment). The cardinality rides on `Quantity` — the documented home for "N target" / "up to N target" phrasings — rather than a bespoke Count field on `ReturnToHandEffect`. A variable X becomes `VariableQuantity`; the spell's own {X} in its mana cost defines that value (CR 107.3 — "Many objects use the letter X as a placeholder for a number that needs to be determined").

The optional modifier is folded onto the filter via `QualifierAxisMapper`: a "non&lt;x&gt;" token routes to `ExcludedCardTypes` / `ExcludedColors` (e.g. "nonland" → `ExcludedCardTypes:["land"]`); a bare colour word routes to `Colors`. Mirrors the modifier handling in the sibling `ReturnTargetToHandRule` (the "Return all [mod] &lt;type&gt;" branch).

CR 400.3: "If an object would go to any library, graveyard, or hand other than its owner's, it goes to its owner's corresponding zone." CR 402.1: the hand is a zone; returning an object to hand is a zone change stated directly (no keyword action). CR 115.1: targets are declared as the spell is put on the stack.

ANCHOR: the pattern is anchored (^…$) on the full clause and requires an explicit count token (bounded or "any number of"), a PLURAL type, and the PLURAL "their owners' hands", so it is disjoint from the singular-target sibling `ReturnTargetToHandRule` (which matches "Return target &lt;type&gt; … its owner's hand", with no count token before "target", and whose patterns do not accept an "any number of" prefix) and cannot match as a substring of, or subsume, any other Return* sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnCountTargetPermanentsToOwnersHandsSpellRule.cs)

### `ReturnFromGraveyardToHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Return target [filter] card from your graveyard to your hand." Also handles the untyped form: "Return target card from your graveyard to your hand." Source zone on `Zone`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnFromGraveyardToHandRule.cs)

### `ReturnGraveyardToBattlefieldRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Return target [filter] card [with mana value N or less/greater/more/fewer] from your graveyard to the battlefield." Reanimation (CR 701.17-adjacent zone change / CR 608): the target card moves from its owner's graveyard onto the battlefield. Source zone on `Zone`; the optional mana-value qualifier (e.g. Yathan Roadwatcher's "with mana value 3 or less") lands on `ManaValueComparison`. Fully anchored (^…$) so the optional qualifier cannot let the pattern substring-match a more specific sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnGraveyardToBattlefieldRule.cs)

### `ReturnInstantOrSorceryFromGraveyardSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Return target instant or sorcery card from your graveyard to your hand." Models the Regrowth-style regrowth-of-spells family (e.g. Relearn) as a stand-alone sorcery — the same effect body as the triggered Archaeomancer / Izzet Chronarch family, resolved as a plain one-shot zone-change instruction (CR 608.2). Source zone is the graveyard (CR 404.1); destination is the hand (CR 402.1); "target" is CR 115.1. Zone = Graveyard encodes the source zone stated in oracle text; Controller = You encodes "your graveyard". CardTypes = ["instant", "sorcery"] encodes the type-disjunction. Priority above the generic ReturnFromGraveyardToHandRule (default 50) because this rule is more specific (type-disjunction shape); the two are mutually exclusive in practice since the generic rule's filter alternation never matches "instant or sorcery".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnInstantOrSorceryFromGraveyardSpellRule.cs)

### `ReturnKickedDrawRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Two-sentence compound spell: "Return target nonland permanent to its owner's hand. If this spell was kicked, draw a card."

Sentence 1 is a `ReturnToHandEffect` targeting "nonland permanent". Sentence 2 is a `DrawCardsEffect` guarded by `Condition.Text = "this spell was kicked"`. Both effects sit as siblings on `Effects`; the condition is descriptive, not a runtime branch — consistent with the MAST "describes cards, does not execute them" doctrine.

Rule 702.33 (kicker), Rule 120.1 (draw). Priority 80 so this supersedes the general sentence-bundle path, which would try to dispatch each sentence independently and fail on the conditional-draw fragment.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnKickedDrawRule.cs)

### `ReturnMultipleFromGraveyardRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Return up to (one|two|three|…) target [filter] cards from your graveyard to your hand." Covers the bounded multi-target graveyard-retrieval pattern where the count is an "up to N" ceiling, e.g. Soul Salvage / March of the Returned. Source zone on `Zone`; count on `Quantity`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnMultipleFromGraveyardRule.cs)

### `ReturnSorceryFromGraveyardSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Return target sorcery card from your graveyard to your hand." — Déjà Vu. A single-type graveyard-recursion sorcery, sibling to the type-disjunction families `ReturnInstantOrSorceryFromGraveyardSpellRule` ("instant or sorcery") and `ReturnArtifactOrEnchantmentFromGraveyardSpellRule` ("artifact or enchantment"), but for the bare "sorcery" type alone. Resolved as a plain one-shot zone-change instruction (CR 608.2). Source zone is the graveyard (CR 404.1); destination is the hand (CR 402.1); "target" is CR 115.1. Zone = Graveyard encodes the source zone stated in oracle text; Controller = You encodes "your graveyard". CardTypes = ["sorcery"] encodes the single type filter. Priority above the generic ReturnFromGraveyardToHandRule (default 50) — that rule's filter alternation (permanent|creature|artifact|enchantment|land|nonland permanent) never includes "sorcery", so the two are mutually exclusive in practice, but the elevated priority keeps this rule's more specific intent unambiguous and consistent with its type-disjunction siblings.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnSorceryFromGraveyardSpellRule.cs)

### `ReturnTargetSpellToHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Return target spell [you don't control|an opponent controls|you control] to its owner's hand." Handles the special case of returning a spell on the stack (Zone: Stack, CardTypes: ["spell"]) to its owner's hand. This differs from `ReturnTargetToHandRule` which handles permanent types (creature, artifact, land, etc.) but not spells. Rule 400.1 — zones; Rule 608.2b — spell on the stack is a game object with a controller. "A spell you don't control" means the spell is controlled by an opponent (CR 108.4).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnTargetSpellToHandRule.cs)

### `ReturnTargetToHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Return [target|all] [modifier] [type] to [its owner's|their owners'|your] hand[s]." Covers single-target bounce, mass bounce ("Return all X"), "you own" ownership qualifier, "non*" prefix modifiers (e.g. "nonland permanent"), color predicates ("green permanents", "nonblue creatures"), and state adjectives ("tapped creature").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ReturnTargetToHandRule.cs)

### `RevealAnyNumberBlackCardsFromHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Reveal any number of black cards in your hand." — the disclosure sentence of the Scent of Nightshade family. The revealed count feeds a later "for each card revealed this way" / "where X is the number of cards revealed this way" clause parsed by its sibling rule; the two sentences are decomposed into sibling effects by the sentence-bundle dispatch, linked textually via `CardsRevealedThisWayQuantity` (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution).

Emits a `RevealCardsEffect`: the revealer is "you" (`You`), the count is unbounded (`AnyAmountQuantity`), the zone is `Hand`, and the filter is "black cards" (`CardTypes=["card"]` + `Colors=["B"]`).

CR 701.20a (verbatim): "To reveal a card, show that card to all players for a brief time. If an effect causes a card to be revealed, it remains revealed for as long as necessary to complete the parts of the effect that card is relevant to."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/RevealAnyNumberBlackCardsFromHandRule.cs)

### `RevealAnyNumberBlueCardsFromHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Reveal any number of blue cards in your hand." — the disclosure sentence of the Scent of Brine family (the blue sibling of the Scent of Nightshade reveal, see `RevealAnyNumberBlackCardsFromHandRule`). The revealed count feeds a later "for each card revealed this way" clause parsed by its sibling rule; the two sentences are decomposed into sibling effects by the sentence-bundle dispatch, linked textually via `CardsRevealedThisWayQuantity` (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution).

Emits a `RevealCardsEffect`: the revealer is "you" (`You`), the count is unbounded (`AnyAmountQuantity`), the zone is `Hand`, and the filter is "blue cards" (`CardTypes=["card"]` + `Colors=["U"]`).

CR 701.20a (verbatim): "To reveal a card, show that card to all players for a brief time. If an effect causes a card to be revealed, it remains revealed for as long as necessary to complete the parts of the effect that card is relevant to."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/RevealAnyNumberBlueCardsFromHandRule.cs)

### `RevealAnyNumberGreenCardsFromHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Reveal any number of green cards in your hand." — the disclosure sentence of the Scent of Ivy family (the green sibling of Scent of Nightshade's black reveal, parsed by `RevealAnyNumberBlackCardsFromHandRule`). The revealed count feeds a later "where X is the number of cards revealed this way" clause parsed by its sibling rule; the two sentences are decomposed into sibling effects by the sentence-bundle dispatch, linked textually via `CardsRevealedThisWayQuantity` (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution).

Emits a `RevealCardsEffect`: the revealer is "you" (`You`), the count is unbounded (`AnyAmountQuantity`), the zone is `Hand`, and the filter is "green cards" (`CardTypes=["card"]` + `Colors=["G"]`).

CR 701.20a (verbatim): "To reveal a card, show that card to all players for a brief time. If an effect causes a card to be revealed, it remains revealed for as long as necessary to complete the parts of the effect that card is relevant to."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/RevealAnyNumberGreenCardsFromHandRule.cs)

### `RevealChooseDiscardRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Targeted reveal-choose-discard — the Thoughtseize / Coercion / Thought Erasure family: "Target opponent reveals their hand. You choose a nonland card from it. That player discards that card."

These three sentences are ONE coupled game action, not three independent effects: the card "you choose" from the revealed hand is the very card "that player discards". So this is a single `DiscardCardsEffect` capturing all three structured axes rather than a decomposed sentence-bundle —

`Player` (the discarder): `Target` opponent — mirrors `DiscardTargetPlayerRule`'s "target opponent discards" encoding; `Chooser`: "you" (`ObjectReferenceKind.You`) — distinct from the discarder; `Filter`: "a nonland card" → `CardTypes=["card"]` + `ExcludedCardTypes=["land"]`; `RevealHand=true`: the opponent reveals their hand first.

CR 701.9a (verbatim): "To discard a card, move it from its owner's hand to that player's graveyard."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/RevealChooseDiscardRule.cs)

### `RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Reveal the top N cards of your library. You may put a [filter] card from among them into your hand. Put the rest into your graveyard." — the Grisly Salvage / Scout the Borders / Commune with the Gods reveal-then-dredge spell family.

All three sentences are one coupled game action ("from among them" and "the rest" are back-references to the reveal), so this rule matches the whole clause and emits a single `RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardEffect`. The single-effect `TryMatch` path receives the full clause because the neighbouring sentences do not independently parse, so the generic sentence-bundle splitter falls through to here (mirroring `LookAtTopPutInHandRule`). CR 701.20 (Reveal); CR 404.1/404.3 (the remainder goes to the graveyard, owner-arranged).

The `[filter]` is a bare card type ("creature") or a two-or-more-way disjunction ("creature or land", "creature or enchantment"). The regex is fully anchored (`^…$`) and demands the exact "You may put a … card from among them into your hand" phrasing, so it does NOT match the "creature card and/or a land card" (up-to-one-of-each), "any number of …" (unbounded), or "…onto the battlefield" (different destination) siblings, nor the multi-clause cards whose text continues past "graveyard" (Gather the Pack, Malevolent Rumble).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/RevealTopMayPutMatchingRestToGraveyardRule.cs)

### `RollDiceSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Roll [count] [dN | N-sided die/dice]" — the die-roll instruction (CR 706.1) in SPELL context (instants/sorceries: "Roll two six-sided dice." — Pair o' Dice Lost). The triggered-ability path has its own `RollDieTriggeredRule`; the spell-effect registry (ISpellRule) is separate, so the roll needs a spell rule too. Emits the same `RollDieEffect` (Count nullable, null ≡ 1), which projects `emit:rolldice` for the dice flow arm.

Anchored (^…$). Priority 60 — above the generic fallback, mirrors the triggered roll rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/RollDiceSpellRule.cs)

### `SacrificeAtEndStepSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the delayed-sacrifice sentence:

"Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step." "Sacrifice it at end of turn."

This sentence appears as a trailing clause in multi-sentence spell abilities where a creature or token was obtained or created earlier in the same ability text — for example: "Gain control of target creature until end of turn. Untap that creature. It gains haste until end of turn. Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step." (Act of Treason family). The pronoun "it" refers to the object described in the preceding clause (Rule 109.2 — game objects). MAST records this as a `SacrificeEffect` whose `Target` is `It` and whose `Duration` is `AtBeginningOfNextEndStepDuration`. This is descriptive (Rule 701.21 — Sacrifice), not an engine action; the timing semantics are carried by the duration node per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine. Priority 70: must supersede generic sacrifice rules that match "sacrifice [it]" without the duration clause. Rule citations: 701.21 (Sacrifice), 513 (End Step), 603.7 (delayed triggers).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SacrificeAtEndStepSpellRule.cs)

### `SawInHalfRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

"Destroy target creature. If that creature dies this way, its controller creates two tokens that are copies of that creature, except their power is half that creature's power and their toughness is half that creature's toughness. Round up each time." — the Saw in Half destroy-and-create-halved-copy-tokens pattern (CLB).

Produces a flat two-element effect list:

A `DestroyEffect` targeting the creature. A `ConditionalEffect` whose condition is the `OtherCondition` "that creature dies this way" and whose `Then` branch is a `CopyEffect` — Count=2, Target=`{Kind:"It"}`, Player=`{Kind:"Controller"}`, and a single `PowerToughnessOverride` modification encoding "half [stat] rounded up" via `CalculatedQuantity`.

CR 701.7a ("To destroy a permanent, move it to its owner's graveyard") + CR 603.6 (the "if [preceding effect] [happened] this way" conditional — an effect-level gate checked after the destroy resolves). The "Round up each time" sentence is consumed structurally as `Rounding="up"` on each `CalculatedQuantity`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SawInHalfRule.cs)

### `ScrySpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Scry N." — spell-side scry. Rule 701.18. No Player field (implicit you).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ScrySpellRule.cs)

### `SearchBasicLandsSplitOpponentAndYouWithAltCostGateRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Search your library for up to four basic land cards and reveal them. Put one of them onto the battlefield tapped under an opponent's control if the {3}{G} cost was paid. Put two of them onto the battlefield tapped under your control and the rest into your hand. Then shuffle." — the Verdant Mastery shape.
