A three-way `Placements` distribution (CR 701.23), extending the Cultivate / Kodama's Reach two-way split (see `SearchLibraryDistributeBasicLandsToBattlefieldAndHandRule`) with (a) a THIRD share, and (b) one share gated on whether the card's own alternative cost (CR 118.9, printed as a separate ability — see `GrantAlternativeCostForThisSpellRule`) was paid — `AlternativeCostPaidCondition` — and controlled by an opponent rather than the caster — `Controller`. The final share ("the rest") is a `RemainderQuantity`: not a chosen amount, but whatever is left of the found total after the other two shares.

Fully anchored (`^…$`) over the ENTIRE multi-sentence clause (this rule implements `ISpellRule`, tried by `SpellAbilityParser` against the whole clause text once per-sentence bundling and multi-rule dispatch have both declined) so it cannot collide with any other search rule or any standalone "Put N of them..." fragment rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SearchBasicLandsSplitOpponentAndYouWithAltCostGateRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryDistributeBasicLandsToBattlefieldAndHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Search your library for up to two basic land cards, reveal those cards, put one onto the battlefield tapped and the other into your hand, then shuffle." The Cultivate / Kodama's Reach ramp family: a single search that finds up to two basic lands, reveals them, and <b>distributes</b> the found cards across two zones — one onto the battlefield tapped, the other into hand — before shuffling. Distinct from `SearchLibraryToBattlefieldRule` (all found cards to one zone): the split destination is the defining shape, carried by `Placements` with `Distributed` as the effect-level sentinel. The reveal ("reveal those cards" → `Revealed = true`) and the trailing "then shuffle" are folded into the single effect, matching the convention of the sibling search rules. CR 701.23 (Search); CR 701.20 (Reveal). Fully anchored (`^…$`) so there is no substring collision with the other search rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SearchLibraryDistributeBasicLandsToBattlefieldAndHandRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryLandTypeToBattlefieldRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Search your library for (a|up to N) [basic land type] card(s), put (it|them|that card) onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle." The land-fetch ramp sorcery keyed to a specific basic land TYPE (Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, or Forest) rather than to "basic land" generically — e.g. Ranger's Path ("up to two Forest cards"). A "Forest card" is any card with the Forest land subtype (CR 205.3i: Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, and Forest are the basic land types), so the resulting filter carries `CardTypes=["land"]` plus the named `Subtype` — mirroring the encoding existing basic-land-type fetch golds use (Deceptive Landscape, Contaminated Landscape). No "basic" supertype is asserted: the card names only the subtype, so non-basic Forest cards (dual lands, snow lands) qualify too. Sibling of `SearchLibraryToBattlefieldRule` ("basic land card"): the two patterns are mutually exclusive — this one anchors on a specific basic-land- type word where that one anchors on the literal phrase "basic land". Always non-optional (no "you may" prefix); destination is always BattlefieldTapped.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SearchLibraryLandTypeToBattlefieldRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryLandTypeToBattlefieldUntappedRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Search your library for (a|up to N) [basic land type] card(s), put (it|them|that card) onto the battlefield, then shuffle." The land-fetch ramp sorcery keyed to a specific basic land TYPE (Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, or Forest) that puts the found land onto the battlefield UNTAPPED — e.g. Nature's Lore, Three Visits ("a Forest card"), Skyshroud Claim ("up to two Forest cards"). A "Forest card" is any card with the Forest land subtype (CR 305.6: "The basic land types are Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, and Forest."), so the resulting filter carries `CardTypes=["land"]` plus the named `Subtype`. No "basic" supertype is asserted — the card names only the subtype, so non-basic Forest cards (dual lands, snow lands) qualify too (mirrors the tapped sibling's encoding). The search action is CR 701.23. Untapped twin of `SearchLibraryLandTypeToBattlefieldRule`: that one anchors on "...battlefield tapped, then shuffle"; this one anchors on the bare "...battlefield, then shuffle" (no "tapped" token), so the two regexes are mutually exclusive and destination is always `Battlefield`. Always non-optional (no "you may" prefix).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SearchLibraryLandTypeToBattlefieldUntappedRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryToBattlefieldRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Search your library for (a basic land card|up to N basic land cards), put (it|them|that card) onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle." Covers the sorcery ramp pattern (e.g. Rampant Growth, Beneath the Sands). The referent of the "put" clause is written either as a pronoun ("it"/"them") or as an explicit noun phrase ("that card"); the modern Rampant Growth wording uses "that card". Always non-optional (no "you may" prefix). Destination is always BattlefieldTapped.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SearchLibraryToBattlefieldRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryToHandRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Spell-resolution rule for the tutor pattern: "Search your library for a[n] [type] card, [reveal it,] put (that card|it) into your hand, then shuffle." Handles:

"a card" — any card (Filter.CardTypes = ["card"]) "a [type] card" / "an [type] card" — typed filter, e.g. "a creature card", "a basic land card" (type word(s) parsed into CardTypes / Supertypes); the article is "a" or "an" per English grammar depending on the following word (e.g. Wild Idea's "an instant or sorcery card"). "an [type1] or [type2] card" — two-type disjunction (Filter.CardTypes = [type1, type2]), the Wild Idea shape, mirroring `SearchLibraryToTopRevealRule`'s Mystical Tutor disjunction arm. an optional reveal clause ("reveal it," or "reveal that card,") before the put-to-hand clause (e.g. Lay of the Land, Eladamri's Call) — sets `Revealed = true` when present.

All variants map to a single `SearchLibraryEffect` with `Destination = Hand`. The optional reveal, put-to-hand, and shuffle clauses are folded into the effect per the existing convention established by `SearchBasicLandTriggeredRule` and the Solemn Simulacrum fixture. Rule 701.23 (Search).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SearchLibraryToHandRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryToTopRevealRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Spell-resolution rule for the Mystical Tutor pattern: "Search your library for an instant or sorcery card, reveal it, then shuffle and put that card on top." Handles:

"an instant or sorcery card" — two-type disjunction (Filter.CardTypes = ["instant", "sorcery"]) "a[n] [type] card" — single typed filter, e.g. "an artifact card", "a creature card" (type word parsed into CardTypes or Supertypes)

All variants map to a single `SearchLibraryEffect` with `Destination = TopOfLibrary` and `Revealed = true`. The reveal, shuffle, and put-on-top clauses are folded into the effect per the convention established by `SearchLibraryToTopRule` and `SearchLibraryToTopTriggeredRule`. Rule 701.23 (Search). Rule 701.20 (Reveal). Priority 60 — fires before `SearchLibraryToTopRule` (priority 50) because this pattern includes "reveal it," which is absent from the plain Vampiric Tutor form; both rules are fully anchored (^…$) so there is no substring collision between them.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SearchLibraryToTopRevealRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryToTopRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Spell-resolution rule for the Vampiric Tutor pattern: "Search your library for a [type] card, then shuffle and put that card on top." Handles:

"a card" — any card (Filter.CardTypes = ["card"]) "a [type] card" — typed filter, e.g. "a creature card", "a basic land card" (type word(s) parsed into CardTypes / Supertypes)

All variants map to a single `SearchLibraryEffect` with `Destination = TopOfLibrary`. The shuffle and put-on-top clauses are folded into the effect per the convention established by `SearchLibraryToHandRule` and `SearchLibraryToBattlefieldRule`. Rule 701.23 (Search).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SearchLibraryToTopRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageDividedAmongTargetCreaturesRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"[Self] deals N damage divided as you choose among any number of target creatures." — the Fire Covenant divided-damage burn shape. The spell names itself as the source (Rule 113.3a) and deals a single total amount that the controller splits across an unbounded, freely-chosen set of target creatures at announcement, rather than dealing the full amount to each member of the set independently.

CR 601.2d (verbatim): "If the spell requires the player to divide or distribute an effect (such as damage or counters) among one or more targets, the player announces the division. Each of these targets must receive at least one of whatever is being divided." The division fact rides on `Divided`; the target-set cardinality ("any number of") rides on `Quantity` as an `AnyAmountQuantity` (CR 107.3 — an upper-unbounded player choice), mirroring `ReturnCountTargetPermanentsToOwnersHandsSpellRule`'s "any number of target [type]" convention.

The amount is most commonly the additional-cost-defined variable X (CR 601.2b: the controller announces the value of a variable cost as the spell is cast) but a literal/word amount is also recognised for family robustness. Distinct from the sibling `SelfDealsDamageToTypeDisjunctionRule` (which requires "damage to target …" immediately, with no division) — anchored (^…$) on the "damage divided as you choose among any number of target creatures" surface so it cannot collide with that or any other dealDamage sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SelfDealsDamageDividedAmongTargetCreaturesRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageEqualToSacrificedCreaturesPowerToAnyTargetRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"[Self] deals damage equal to the sacrificed creature's power to any target." — the resolution half of the Thud shape, whose additional cost (CR 601.2f: "As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice a creature.") is parsed independently by `AttributeExtractor` into a card-level `AdditionalCostsAttribute` (the prose-cost line is stripped from `Oracle.Abilities` by `ClauseSplitter` before this rule ever sees it — this rule only recognises the trailing spell-effect sentence).

The dealt amount is a `DerivedQuantity` keyed on `Power` whose `Source` is the anaphoric "the sacrificed creature": the object moved to the graveyard by this same spell's `SacrificeCost` (CR 701.21a). That back-reference is a CR 607.1 linked ability — the effect "directly refers to … objects … that were affected by" the cost — so MAST records the textual link, not a runtime power value (ADR 0004: reference-not-resolution). Mirrors the activated-ability sibling `GainLifeEqualToSacrificedCreaturesToughnessEffectRule` (Diamond Valley), which sources the SAME anaphoric "the sacrificed creature" phrase for a toughness-keyed `GainLifeEffect` instead of a power-keyed `DealDamageEffect`.

The spell names itself as the damage source (CR 601.2c self-reference by printed name), modeled as `Self` — the same self-as-source convention as the bare-amount sibling `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetRule`. "any target" is a creature, player, planeswalker, or battle (CR 120.1), modeled as `AnyTarget`.

Anchored (`^…$`) to the exact "deals damage equal to the sacrificed creature's power to any target" surface so it cannot claim a substring of the bare-amount sibling (`SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetRule`, which requires a numeric/word amount, not a derived one) or a future broader "deals damage equal to …'s power" pattern sourced from a different anaphor (e.g. "its power", "that creature's power").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SelfDealsDamageEqualToSacrificedCreaturesPowerToAnyTargetRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"[Self] deals N damage to any target." — bare self-by-name dealDamage with AnyTarget. Covers clean burn spells like Open Fire, Shock, Lightning Strike where the spell names itself as the source and targets "any target" (player, creature, or planeswalker) without any type filter. Distinct from `SelfDealsDamageToTypeDisjunctionRule` (which requires a specific type or type disjunction) and `SelfDealsDamageToFilteredCreatureRule` (which requires a trailing "with [characteristic]" qualifier).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToAttackingOrBlockingCreatureRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"[CardName] deals N damage to target attacking or blocking creature." — spell analogue of the activated `SelfDealsDamageToAttackingOrBlockingCreatureEffectRule`. The source is the spell itself (named; encoded as `Self()`); the target is a creature filtered by Characteristics = [Characteristic.InCombat(CombatState.AttackingOrBlocking)]. Covers clean single-line instants/sorceries such as Divine Arrow and Cosmium Blast.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToAttackingOrBlockingCreatureRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToFilteredCreatureRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"[Self] deals N damage to target/each [type] with [characteristic]." — Take Down's modal options. Distinct from the bare type-disjunction shape: this requires a trailing "with [characteristic]" qualifier. (Source-order pair noted at SpellAbilityParser.cs:592 — both rules currently disjoint via the "with" anchor.)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToFilteredCreatureRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToTypeDisjunctionRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"[Self] deals N damage to target [type] (or [type])?." — Ready to Rumble, Lava Axe ("target player or planeswalker"). Bare-target shape with no "with [characteristic]" suffix. "player" is listed alongside card types here because `CardTypes` encodes both card types and game entities (per CR 120.1: objects deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToTypeDisjunctionRule.cs)

### `ShuffleAnyNumberTargetCardsFromYourGraveyardRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Shuffle any number of target [filter] cards from your graveyard into your library." (Piper's Melody). The controller-performed, unbounded-subset graveyard-to-library recycle keyword action (CR 701.24) — the imperative "you shuffle your own graveyard" sibling of the targeted-player template spelled out in CR 701.24's own worked example (Loaming Shaman: "When this creature enters, target player shuffles any number of target cards from their graveyard into their library"). Here there is no targeted player: the controller (`You`) performs the shuffle of their own library (`Player`), while the cards are a separately-targeted, unbounded selection from that controller's own graveyard (`Cards`, `You` recording "your graveyard", and `AnyAmountQuantity` recording the unbounded "any number of" choice per CR 601.2c — the word "target" appears once, so the card subset is the sole target).

Anchored (`^Shuffle …$`) to avoid shadowing the bounded "up to N" `ShuffleTargetCardsFromGraveyardRule` sibling and the whole-zone `ShuffleGraveyardIntoLibraryEffect`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ShuffleAnyNumberTargetCardsFromYourGraveyardRule.cs)

### `ShuffleIntoLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

"Choose target [type-disjunction]. Its owner shuffles it into their library." Covers the Unravel the Aether pattern — a two-sentence oracle form where the first sentence targets an artifact or enchantment and the second sentence describes the zone-change with shuffle.

Handled patterns (via `TryMatchMulti`):

"Choose target artifact or enchantment. Its owner shuffles it into their library." (Unravel the Aether, BNG) "Choose target artifact or enchantment. Its owner shuffles it into their library." (any reprint of this pattern)

The two-sentence form is not split by the sentence-bundle path because neither sentence individually matches any rule. This rule implements `TryMatchMulti` to match the full two-sentence text (with the period separator present) and emits a single `ShuffleIntoLibraryEffect`. The "Choose target" sentence is a targeting sentence that is inseparable from the zone-change, so both sentences resolve into one effect (Rule 701.19, 701.20).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ShuffleIntoLibraryRule.cs)

### `ShuffleSelfIntoLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Shuffle [CardName] into its owner's library." — the self-referential library shuffle used on cards like Beacon of Immortality. The card refers to itself by name, instructing that it be shuffled into its owner's library on resolution.

Rule 701.24c: "If an effect would cause a player to shuffle one or more specific objects into a library, that library is shuffled even if none of those objects are in the zone they're expected to be in." Rule 701.24 governs shuffle.

MAST maps the card-name self-reference to `Self` (the card itself; CR 201.5). The owner-shuffles mechanic is an inherent part of the zone-change (CR 701.24). Emits a single `ShuffleIntoLibraryEffect` with `Target = Self`.

GUARD: fully anchored (^ … $). Matches ONLY "Shuffle [CapitalizedName] into its owner's library" — the name must begin with a capital letter and end before "into its owner's library". Does NOT match "Its owner shuffles it into their library" (handled by `ShuffleIntoLibraryRule`) or any substring of a broader clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ShuffleSelfIntoLibraryRule.cs)

### `ShuffleTargetCardsFromGraveyardRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target player shuffles up to (one|two|three|…) target [filter] cards from their graveyard into their library." The bounded, targeted-subset shuffle keyword action (CR 701.24) — Krosan Reclamation is the "up to two" variant of the template spelled out in CR 701.24's own worked example (Loaming Shaman: "target player shuffles any number of target cards from their graveyard into their library"). Two independent targets are recorded per CR 601.2c (the word "target" appears twice): the player who shuffles (`Player`) and the bounded card selection from that player's own graveyard (`Cards`, with `Target` recording the "their graveyard" back-reference to the targeted player).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ShuffleTargetCardsFromGraveyardRule.cs)

### `SpellTapTargetRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Tap target [type]." with optional count and type-disjunction target.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SpellTapTargetRule.cs)

### `SurveilSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Surveil N." — standalone spell-side surveil. Rule 701.42. Matches the bare keyword invocation after reminder text has been stripped by the dispatcher. Covers cards like Deadly Visit, Consider, Sinister Sabotage, etc.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SurveilSpellRule.cs)

### `SurveilThenDrawRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

"Surveil N, then draw M cards." — Diresight, Cruel Truths, Risky Research pattern. Expands to a flat [`SurveilEffect`, `DrawCardsEffect`] pair so both effects sit as siblings on `Effects`.

The optional "You lose N life" suffix (sentence 2 in the spell's oracle text) is handled by the sentence-bundle dispatcher, which routes it through `YouLoseLifeSpellRule`. This rule only matches sentence 1.

Rule 701.42 (surveil), Rule 120.1 (draw). Surveil count and draw count are independent small integers and are allowed to differ (e.g. "Surveil 3, then draw three cards").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SurveilThenDrawRule.cs)

### `SwitchTargetCreaturePTSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the P/T-switch shape (CR 613.4d — layer 7d): "take the value of power and apply it to the creature's toughness, and take the value of toughness and apply it to the creature's power." "Switch target creature's power and toughness until end of turn." Examples:

"Switch target creature's power and toughness until end of turn." (Twisted Image)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/SwitchTargetCreaturePTSpellRule.cs)

### `TakeExtraTurnSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Take an extra turn after this one." — a spell-resolution effect (CR 113.3a) that schedules an additional full turn for the spell's controller to be taken immediately after the current turn.

CR 500.7 (verbatim): "Some effects can give a player extra turns. They do this by adding the turns directly after the specified turn. If a player is given multiple extra turns, the extra turns are added one at a time. If multiple players are given extra turns, the extra turns are added one at a time, in APNAP order (see rule 101.4). The most recently created turn will be taken first." MAST records the verb and player reference; the turn-ordering bookkeeping is engine territory (ADR 0001).

ANCHOR: pattern is anchored (^...$) to prevent partial matches inside longer effect text. This is the canonical singular "an extra turn" form (controller takes a turn); the sibling activated-ability form lives at `TakeExtraTurnEffectRule` and the N-turn form at `TakeNExtraTurnsEffectRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TakeExtraTurnSpellRule.cs)

### `TapAndFreezeRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Two-sentence "tap then freeze" spell pattern. Handles both single-target and bounded-multi-target variants:

"Tap target creature. It doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step." (Ojutai's Breath, DTK) — single creature; back-reference via "It". "Tap up to two target creatures. Those creatures don't untap during their controller's next untap step." (Frost Breath, M13) — up-to-N creatures; back-reference via "Those creatures".

Implements both `ISpellRule` (for the freeze sentence when the sentence-bundle dispatcher has already consumed the tap sentence) and `IMultiSpellRule` (for the full two-sentence text as a dedicated pattern). The `TryMatch` path returns `false`; all matching goes through `TryMatch` for the freeze fragment or `TryMatchMulti` for the combined text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TapAndFreezeRule.cs)

### `TapOrUntapSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"You may tap or untap target [type]." and "tap or untap target [type]." The controller chooses whether to tap or untap the named target. Covers single-type and disjunction-type targets (e.g. "artifact, creature, or land"). Rule 701.26 (Tap and Untap).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TapOrUntapSpellRule.cs)

### `TapUpToNTargetsRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Tap up to N target creatures." — bounded-count tap-targets spell effect. Examples: "Tap up to two target creatures." / "Tap up to three target creatures." The quantity lives on `Quantity` (cardinality of the target set), not on `Count`, because the oracle phrase is "up to N target", not "tap N targets". Rule 115.1 / Rule 701.26.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TapUpToNTargetsRule.cs)

### `TapXTargetsRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Tap X target creatures." — variable-count tap-targets spell effect, where the count is the spell's mana-cost X (CR 107.3 / 107.3a: the controller chooses X as the spell is cast; here X also determines how many creatures are tapped). The variable lives on `Count` as a `VariableQuantity` (NOT on `Quantity`, which is reserved for the "up to N target" phrasing handled by `TapUpToNTargetsRule`). CR 701.26 / 701.26a ("Tap and Untap"). Priority 60: above the generic `SpellTapTargetRule` (default 50), whose count path only understands literal/word counts via `TryParseSmallWord` and returns false on "X".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TapXTargetsRule.cs)

### `TargetBlockingCreatureModifyPTSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target blocking creature gets +N/+M until end of turn." (and the "-N/-M" sign form) — a combat-trick pump narrowed to a creature that is currently blocking.

Distinct from `ModifyPTSpellRule`'s bare "Target creature gets …" shape: the target is narrowed to a <em>blocking</em> creature, carried as the `InCombat(CombatState)` state-predicate residual per the established open-ended-qualifier convention (CR 109.3 — characteristics include any quality that can be true or false of a permanent at any moment) — mirroring how "Destroy target blocking creature" (`DestroyTargetStateQualifiedRule`) and "Target attacking creature gets …" (`ModifyPTTargetAttackingCreatureEffectRule`, bloodrush) already encode the combat-state filter.

The P/T modifier is a layer-7c effect (CR 613.4c — "Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied.").

"Target blocking creature gets +3/+1 until end of turn." (Aliban's Tower)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetBlockingCreatureModifyPTSpellRule.cs)

### `TargetCantBeBlockedThisTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Handles "Target creature can't be blocked this turn." — emits a `CantBeBlockedEffect` targeting a single creature with an `untilEndOfTurn` duration. Rule 509.1b (evasion ability; the defending player may not declare any creature as a blocker for the named creature during the declare-blockers step of the current turn). Representative cards: Artful Dodge, Slip Through Space.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetCantBeBlockedThisTurnRule.cs)

### `TargetControlledColorModifyPTSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the colour-and-controller qualified P/T-modification shape: "Target green creature you control gets +N/+M until end of turn." This is distinct from `ModifyPTSpellRule`'s bare "Target creature gets +N/+M" form — the colour word (CR 105.2) and the "you control" controller restriction (CR 109.5 / 601.2c) both narrow the target's `ObjectFilter`. The mono-colour restriction is carried on `Colors` (an object passes if it has at least one of the listed colours, CR 105.1) and the controller restriction on `Controller`. Examples:

"Target green creature you control gets +2/+2 until end of turn." (Hunt the Hunter — first sentence)

Anchored with `^…$`; the mandatory "&lt;colour&gt; creature you control" segment keeps it from matching the bare "Target creature gets …" surface handled by `ModifyPTSpellRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetControlledColorModifyPTSpellRule.cs)

### `TargetControlledVariablePTAndGainKeywordsSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Recognises the controller-qualified X-scaled composite buff shape: "Target creature you control gets +X/+M and gains &lt;keyword(s)&gt; until end of turn." This is the variable-power sibling of `ModifyPTAndGainKeywordControlledSpellRule` (which only matches literal-digit power/toughness). It covers X-cost combat tricks such as Frantic Confrontation ({X}{R}: "Target creature you control gets +X/+0 and gains first strike and trample until end of turn.") where the power modifier is the announced spell variable X (CR 107.3a — the controller chooses X on cast) and the toughness modifier is a literal. Emits a flat list via `TryMatchMulti`: `[ModifyPTEffect (Target=you-control creature), GainAbilityEffect (Target=It), …]`, one `GainAbilityEffect` per keyword, all sharing a single `UntilTimeDuration` instance. The single-effect `TryMatch` always returns false so the flat-list path is the only active route.

CR citations: CR 107.3a — "If a spell or activated ability has a mana cost … with an {X} … in it, and the value of X isn't defined by the text of that spell or ability, the controller of the spell or ability chooses the value of X." CR 613.4c — "Layer 7c: Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied." (the +X/+0 buff). CR 702.7a — "First strike is a static ability that modifies the rules for the combat damage step." CR 702.19a — "Trample is a static ability that modifies the rules for assigning an attacking creature's combat damage."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetControlledVariablePTAndGainKeywordsSpellRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureGainsKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the pure keyword-grant shape (no P/T modification): "Target creature gains &lt;keyword&gt; until end of turn." "Target permanent gains &lt;keyword&gt; until end of turn." This covers single-keyword combat tricks and protection spells whose entire oracle effect is a UEOT ability grant on a single target. Examples:

"Target creature gains flying until end of turn." (Jump) "Target creature gains haste until end of turn." (Unnatural Speed) "Target creature gains deathtouch until end of turn." (Lace with Moonglove) "Target creature gains shroud until end of turn." (Mage's Guile) "Target creature gains shadow until end of turn." (Shadow Rift) "Target creature gains undying until end of turn." (Undying Evil)

Multi-keyword forms ("gains flying and lifelink") and composite forms ("gets +N/+M and gains …") are handled by `ModifyPTAndGainKeywordSpellRule`; this rule is intentionally restricted to exactly one keyword so the regex is unambiguous. Rule citations: 613.1c (Layer 6 — ability-granting effects), 611 (continuous effects with duration).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetCreatureGainsKeywordRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureGainsMultipleKeywordsSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Recognises the multi-keyword UEOT grant shape with NO P/T modifier: "Target creature gains &lt;keyword&gt; and &lt;keyword&gt; [and …] until end of turn." This closes the gap between:

`TargetCreatureGainsKeywordRule` — exactly ONE keyword, e.g. "Target creature gains deathtouch until end of turn." `ModifyPTAndGainKeywordSpellRule` — a P/T modifier PLUS one or more keywords, e.g. "Target creature gets +2/+2 and gains trample …"

Neither matched the pure two-or-more-keyword grant with no buff, e.g.:

"Target creature gains deathtouch and indestructible until end of turn." (Battle-Rage Blessing)

Emits a flat list via `TryMatchMulti`: one `GainAbilityEffect` per keyword, all sharing a single until-end-of-turn duration. The FIRST grant carries the actual `Target creature` object reference; subsequent grants reference the same object anaphorically via `It` (mirroring the existing composite-buff rules). Requiring at least two " and "-joined keyword segments keeps this rule strictly disjoint from the single-keyword rule, so neither shadows the other. Rule citations: 613.1c (Layer 6 — ability-adding effects), 611.2 (continuous effects generated by a resolving spell, with a specified duration), 702.2 (Deathtouch), 702.12 (Indestructible).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetCreatureGainsMultipleKeywordsSpellRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureGetsMinusXRevealedThisWayRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target creature gets -X/-X until end of turn, where X is the number of cards revealed this way." — the payoff sentence of the Scent of Nightshade family, paired with `RevealAnyNumberBlackCardsFromHandRule` (the reveal that supplies X).

X = the number of cards revealed this way (`CardsRevealedThisWayQuantity`). The "-X" modifier is that count negated, modeled with the established negation convention (Dread Slag's "-N/-N for each …"): a `CalculatedQuantity` whose `BaseQuantity` is the revealed count, multiplied by -1. This is a distinct sentence from the reveal, so it does not reference the reveal at runtime — the link is textual (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution).

This rule sits above the generic `ModifyPTSpellRule` (whose anchored patterns require literal-digit modifiers and forbid a trailing "where …" clause, so they never match this shape); the priority bump is defensive precedence only.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetCreatureGetsMinusXRevealedThisWayRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureGetsPlusXRevealedThisWayRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target creature gets +X/+X until end of turn, where X is the number of cards revealed this way." — the payoff sentence of the Scent of Ivy family, paired with `RevealAnyNumberGreenCardsFromHandRule` (the reveal that supplies X). The positive-modifier mirror of Scent of Nightshade's "-X/-X" clause parsed by `TargetCreatureGetsMinusXRevealedThisWayRule`.

X = the number of cards revealed this way (`CardsRevealedThisWayQuantity`), used directly as the "+X" modifier (no negation, unlike the "-X" sibling). This is a distinct sentence from the reveal, so it does not reference the reveal at runtime — the link is textual (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution).

This rule sits above the generic `ModifyPTSpellRule` (whose anchored patterns require literal-digit modifiers and forbid a trailing "where …" clause, so they never match this shape); the priority bump is defensive precedence only.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetCreatureGetsPlusXRevealedThisWayRule.cs)

### `TargetDealsDamageToSelfRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target creature deals damage to itself equal to its power."

The target creature is both the damage source and the damage recipient. The amount is a `DerivedQuantity` with `Power`, sourced from the same object ("it"). Covers Repentance (WL Sorcery) and Justice Strike (GRN Instant).

Distinguished from `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetRule` (spell is the source, not the creature) and from combat-damage rules (this is a non-combat damage event resolving at sorcery/instant speed).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetDealsDamageToSelfRule.cs)

### `TargetGainsProtectionColorRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the "gains protection from the color of your choice UEOT" shape: "Target creature you control gains protection from the color of your choice until end of turn." This covers protection-grant instants such as Gods Willing (THS) and Shelter (INV) where the protected color is chosen by the controller at resolution, not fixed in the oracle text. The chosen color is modeled as `ChosenColor` — a declarative marker that the protection quality is controller-chosen at resolution time. MAST records the instruction to choose, not the chosen value (per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine; see ChooseColorEffect for the analogous standalone color-choice shape, which here has no entry timing — the choice is a spell effect, so no StaticTimingKind.AsThisEnters applies). Rule citations: 702.16 (Protection), 702.16e (protection from a player's choice), 613.1c (Layer 6 — ability-granting continuous effects), 611 (continuous effects with duration).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetGainsProtectionColorRule.cs)

### `TargetOpponentExilesGreatestManaValuePermanentRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target opponent exiles a creature or planeswalker they control with the greatest mana value among creatures and planeswalkers they control." — the edict-style forced exile shape (Blot Out, End of the Hunt).

This is an <em>edict</em>, not targeted removal: the only target is the OPPONENT (CR 115.1); the exiled permanent is not itself targeted. The targeted opponent then chooses one of their own creatures/planeswalkers tied for the greatest mana value (CR 202.3) and moves it to exile (CR 701.13a — "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is"). Modeled as an `ExileEffect` with two distinct axes:

`Player` — the acting player, "target opponent" (`Target` + `CardTypes = ["opponent"]`), mirroring the edict-actor convention of `Player`; `Target` — the exiled object, an indefinite controller-choice reference (`Any`: the opponent picks, no "target" keyword on it) scoped to "a creature or planeswalker they control" (`Controller = Target`, i.e. the same targeted opponent).

The "greatest mana value among creatures and planeswalkers they control" superlative is structured as an `ExtremeStatCharacteristic` (`Stat = ManaValue`, `Extreme = Greatest`) — the "MaxStatFilter" the free-text whitelist named as missing for the sibling greatest-power sacrifice edict (`EachOpponentSacrificesGreatestPowerCreatureEffectRule`). The "among creatures and planeswalkers they control" population equals this object's own filter, so the characteristic's `Scope` is left null (it defaults to the enclosing filter).

Fully anchored (`^…$`): matches only this exact whole-clause sentence, so it cannot substring-capture the shorter siblings that a more-specific rule should own — "Target opponent exiles a creature they control and their graveyard." (Strategic Betrayal), the modal "• Target opponent exiles a creature they control." (Doomfall, Debt to the Kami), and the "Each opponent exiles a creature with the greatest power …" broadcast (Olórin's Searing Light) all fail the anchor.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetOpponentExilesGreatestManaValuePermanentRule.cs)

### `TargetOpponentLosesHalfLifeRoundedUpRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target opponent loses half their life, rounded up." — the targeted half-life-loss spell pattern (Blood Tribute). The opponent is targeted; the amount is half their life total, rounded up.

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." The amount is a `CalculatedQuantity` with `Operation="half"`, `Rounding="up"`, and a `DerivedQuantity` base keyed on `LifeTotal` (the target's own life total is implicit from the `Player` reference).

The player reference is `Opponent` (the oracle text says "Target opponent"). "Target opponent" is a targeted reference to an opponent — represented as `Kind = Opponent` in MAST (see Bargain, HighwayRobber precedents).

Anchored (^…$) to prevent substring matches inside multi-sentence spell clauses (e.g. the full Blood Tribute clause bundles this sentence with the kicked gain-life).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetOpponentLosesHalfLifeRoundedUpRule.cs)

### `TargetPlayerDrawsLosesLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

"Target player draws N cards and loses N life." / "Target opponent draws N cards and loses N life." This is the targeted draw-and-drain pattern. The draw count and life-loss amount use the same quantity token (they may differ in wording but represent the same value in all current oracle text instances). Both effects share the same target reference. Recognised shapes:

"Target player draws X cards and loses X life." — Damnable Pact "Target player draws two cards and loses 2 life." — hypothetical literal variant "Target opponent draws a card and loses 1 life." — opponent-targeted variant

Emits a flat `[DrawCardsEffect, LoseLifeEffect]` list via `TryMatchMulti`. The single-effect `TryMatch` always returns false.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetPlayerDrawsLosesLifeRule.cs)

### `TargetPlayerLosesLifeYouGainRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

"Target player loses N life and you gain N life." — the targeted drain pattern where the opponent-chosen player loses a fixed amount and the controller gains the same amount (CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly.").

Recognised shapes:

"Target player loses 4 life and you gain 4 life." — Absorb Vis

Emits a flat [`LoseLifeEffect`, `GainLifeEffect`] pair via `TryMatchMulti`. The two amounts are allowed to differ in oracle text; each is parsed independently. The drain amounts need not be equal for the rule to fire — the conjunction "and you gain N life" is what identifies the shape.

The single-effect `TryMatch` always returns false — this shape never reduces to a single Effect.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetPlayerLosesLifeYouGainRule.cs)

### `TargetPlayerShufflesGraveyardIntoLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target player shuffles their graveyard into their library." — targeted whole-zone recycle (Reminisce).

CR 400.12: "Some effects instruct a player to do something to a zone (such as 'Shuffle your hand into your library'). That action is performed on all cards in that zone. The zone itself is not affected." CR 701.24a: "To shuffle a library or a face-down pile of cards, randomize the cards within it so that no player knows their order."

Anchored (^ … $) single-sentence match. Emits a `ShuffleGraveyardIntoLibraryEffect` whose `Player` carries `Target` with a player filter — matching the "target player" subject in oracle text. Sibling of `EachPlayerShufflesGraveyardIntoLibraryRule` (which handles the "each player" subject instead).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetPlayerShufflesGraveyardIntoLibraryRule.cs)

### `TargetSacrificesRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Target [player|opponent] sacrifices a [type][.]" — targeted sacrifice. The named player chooses which qualifying permanent to sacrifice (Rule 701.21a).

"Target opponent sacrifices a creature." (Diabolic Edict, Cruel Edict) "Target player sacrifices a creature." (generic) "Target player sacrifices a creature of their choice." (older errata phrasing)

Emits a `SacrificeEffect` where:

`Target` carries `Target` with `Filter.CardTypes = ["opponent"]` or `["player"]` identifying the actor. `Filter` restricts the sacrificed permanent type.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetSacrificesRule.cs)

### `TargetYouControlModifyPTSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the controller-qualified (but uncolored) P/T-modification shape: "Target creature you control gets +N/+M until end of turn." This is the "you control" analogue of `ModifyPTSpellRule`'s bare "Target creature gets +N/+M" form: the "you control" restriction (CR 109.5) narrows the target's `Controller` to `You`. It emits a `ModifyPTEffect`, a continuous effect (CR 611.1) that adjusts the creature's power/toughness characteristic (CR 613) for the stated duration. Distinct from `TargetControlledColorModifyPTSpellRule` (which also requires a colour word before "creature") and from `ModifyPTAndGainKeywordControlledSpellRule` (the "…and gains [keyword]" composite). Anchored `^…$` so the bare "Target creature gets …" surface and the "…and gains …" composite both stay with their own rules. Example:

"Target creature you control gets +1/+0 until end of turn." (Ambuscade — first sentence)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetYouControlModifyPTSpellRule.cs)

### `TargetsBecomeColorRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Recognises the spell shape "One or more target creatures become [color] until end of turn." (Dwarven Song). A one-or-more-targeting spell that applies a layer-5 color-changing continuous effect: each target becomes the named color for the turn.

CR 105.3 (verbatim): "Effects may change an object's color or give a color to a colorless object. If an effect gives an object a new color, the new color replaces all previous colors the object had (unless the effect said the object became that color 'in addition' to its other colors). Effects may also make a colored object become colorless."

CR 613.1e (verbatim): "Layer 5: Color-changing effects are applied."

CR 115.1: "Some spells and abilities require their controller to choose one or more targets for them. ..." — "one or more target creatures" is exactly 115.1's one-or-more targeting, modeled as `AtLeastQuantity` with `Minimum = 1` (a variable number of targets, floor one, no ceiling; CR 601.2c).

The becomes-color effect reuses the existing `ChangeColorEffect` (`[OracleEffect("changeColor")]`) — the same node the activated `ChangeColorEffectRule` emits — with the color-name→WUBRG map and `EndOfTurn` duration mirrored from that rule. The verb here is the plural "become" (targets, not a singular target). Default priority (50) is fine: the anchor is specific and non-overlapping.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/TargetsBecomeColorRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerMayCopyThisSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"That player may copy this spell and may choose a new target for that copy."

Chain of Smog's chain mechanic: the targeted player (that player) gets the option to copy the spell itself (Self), with permission to redirect the copy to a new target. CR 707.10: "To copy a spell … means to put a copy of it onto the stack; a copy of a spell isn't cast and a copy of an activated ability isn't activated. … If the spell has any targets, you may choose new targets for the copy." The "may copy" wraps the whole thing in an `OptionalEffect` (ADR 0005 — "you may" is composition, not a flag).

The `Player` field on `CopyEffect` records who creates the copy — "that player" (`ThatPlayer`), the targeted player from the preceding `DiscardCardsEffect`. The copy target is the spell itself (`Self`). `MayChooseNewTargets` captures "may choose a new target for that copy" (CR 707.10). CR 701.9a governs the preceding discard; this clause governs the optional propagation of the chain.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ThatPlayerMayCopyThisSpellRule.cs)

### `ThreatenRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Recognises the Threaten / Act of Treason pattern: "Gain control of target creature until end of turn. Untap that creature. It gains haste until end of turn." Three sequential effects share one target (the chosen creature), represented in the AST as:

`GainControlEffect` — target creature, until end of turn. `UntapEffect` — It (back-reference to the same creature). `GainAbilityEffect` — It gains haste until end of turn.

"That creature" in the second sentence is a back-reference to the target chosen for the first sentence; it maps to `It` (same pronoun semantics as "it" — Rule 109.2). Rule citations: CR 613.1a (Layer 2 — control-changing effects), CR 613.1c (Layer 6 — ability-granting effects), CR 702.10 (haste).

The single-effect `TryMatch` always returns false so the flat-list path is the only active route.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/ThreatenRule.cs)

### `UntapAllControlledRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Untap all [filter] you control." — mass-untap spell targeting every qualifying permanent under the controller's control (CR 701.19a).

Handled patterns (via `TryMatch`):

"Untap all nonland permanents you control." — Dramatic Reversal "Untap all permanents you control." "Untap all creatures you control." "Untap all artifacts you control."

Emits an `UntapEffect` whose `Target` has `Each` and the appropriate `ObjectFilter` with `Controller` = `You`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/UntapAllControlledRule.cs)

### `UntapTargetRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

Untap spell rules — two shapes:

"Untap target [filter]." — single-target untap spell. "Untap it." — pronoun reference to an already-named target, used as the trailing clause of multi-sentence spells such as "Target creature gets +N/+M and gains &lt;keyword&gt; until end of turn. Untap it."

Covers the bare card-type target shapes most common in the corpus: creature and permanent.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/UntapTargetRule.cs)

### `UntapThatCreatureRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Untap that creature." — the definite-article back-reference form of a trailing untap clause, used as the closing sentence of a multi-sentence spell that already named "target creature" (or a filtered variant of it) earlier in the same effect text: "Target creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn. Untap that creature." (Savage Surge, Veteran's Reflexes), "Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control. Untap that creature." (Stony Strength). "That creature" here is anaphoric within a single spell's resolution — it refers back to the object chosen for the "target creature" earlier in the SAME sentence chain, not to an object named by a trigger condition (contrast `ThatCreature`, which is reserved for the triggered-ability back-reference to the trigger's own Filter — CR 603.2). Per Rule 109.2, an anaphoric reference to a previously-established object uses the same "it" semantics regardless of whether the card's own text spells it "it" or "that creature" — this mirrors the established convention already used by `ThreatenRule` for the identical "Untap that creature." clause ("'That creature' ... maps to ObjectReferenceKind.It (same pronoun semantics as 'it' — Rule 109.2)"). Anchored on the bare fragment (^…$) so only the standalone trailing sentence matches; any trailing qualifier ("Untap that creature and roll a six-sided die.") falls through untouched to its own handling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/UntapThatCreatureRule.cs)

### `UntapUpToNTargetsAndPumpRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

Two-sentence "untap then pump" spell pattern: "Untap up to two target creatures. They each get +2/+2 until end of turn." (Join Forces) — up-to-N target creatures are untapped, and the same creatures ("They each") receive a P/T bonus until end of turn via a plural back-reference.

Structural twin of `TapAndFreezeRule` (tap + freeze), swapping the tap for an `UntapEffect` and the freeze for a `ModifyPTEffect`. The "up to N target creatures" cardinality lives on `Quantity` (an `UpToQuantity`), the target set of the untap; the pump sentence's "They each" back-reference is modeled with `It`, matching the established plural-back-reference convention used by Frost Breath's "Those creatures" (see `TapAndFreezeRule`).

CR 701.26b (untap): "To untap a permanent, rotate it back to the upright position from a sideways position." CR 115.1 ("target") + CR 107.3 ("up to N") make the untap a 0–2 targeted choice. CR 611 (continuous effects) governs the P/T bonus ending at end of turn (CR 514.2 cleanup discards "until end of turn" effects).

Implements `ISpellRule` (matching the pump sentence when the sentence-bundle dispatcher has already consumed the untap sentence — the untap fragment is matched by `UntapUpToNTargetsRule`) and `IMultiSpellRule` (matching the full two-sentence text as one shape). Every pattern is anchored (`^…$`) so it cannot match inside a longer clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/UntapUpToNTargetsAndPumpRule.cs)

### `UntapUpToNTargetsRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Untap up to N target creatures." — bounded-count untap-targets spell effect, the untap twin of `TapUpToNTargetsRule`. Examples: "Untap up to two target creatures." (Join Forces, first sentence). The quantity lives on `Quantity` (an `UpToQuantity` — cardinality of the target set), not on `Count`, because the oracle phrase is "up to N target", not "untap N targets" (mirrors the tap sibling).

CR 701.26b: "To untap a permanent, rotate it back to the upright position from a sideways position." CR 115.1 ("target") + CR 107.3 ("up to N") make this a 0–N targeted choice. Anchored (`^…$`): distinct from the "permanents" activated shape handled by `UntapUpToNTargetPermanentsRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/UntapUpToNTargetsRule.cs)

### `UpToNTargetCreaturesCantBlockThisTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"Up to N target creatures can't block this turn." — a bounded-count-target blocking restriction (Abandon the Post). The count lives on `Quantity` as an `UpToQuantity` (Rule 115.1 targeting; "up to N target" is a bounded target count, not an effect-level count) and the restriction is scoped to the targeted creatures via `Target`, mirroring `TapUpToNTargetsRule`'s up-to-N target-count plumbing. The restriction lasts "this turn" — an `untilEndOfTurn` duration (Rule 509.1: blocking restrictions resolve at the declare-blockers step of the current turn), mirroring `CreaturesCantBlockThisTurnRule`'s effect shape. Scoped to creatures only, since only creatures block.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/UpToNTargetCreaturesCantBlockThisTurnRule.cs)

### `YouDrawCardsAndYouLoseLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule, IMultiSpellRule

"You draw N cards and you lose N life." — the controller draw-and-drain spell shape (Ambition's Cost, Ancient Craving, Succumb to Temptation, Rowan's Grim Search, Feed the Infection, Mordor Muster).

A single "… and you …"-joined sentence that expands to two sibling effects: `DrawCardsEffect` (you draw N) and `LoseLifeEffect` (you lose N). Both clauses reference the controller ("you"), so both effects carry `You`.

CR 121.1 (draw): "A player draws a card by putting the top card of their library into their hand." CR 119.3 (lose life): "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."

Distinct from the targeted `TargetPlayerDrawsLosesLifeRule` ("Target player draws … and loses …") and from the activated-path `YouDrawCardAndLoseLifeEffectRule` ("You draw … and lose …", without the second "you"). The mandatory second "you" ("and <b>you</b> lose") disambiguates this spell shape.

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the full sentence is matched end-to-end so no broader sibling can consume it and silently drop the lose-life conjunct. Emits a flat `[DrawCardsEffect, LoseLifeEffect]` list via `TryMatchMulti`; the single-effect `TryMatch` always returns false.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/YouDrawCardsAndYouLoseLifeRule.cs)

### `YouLoseLifeSpellRule` — *sealed class* : ISpellRule

"You lose N life." — spell-resolution controller life-loss (Rule 119.3). Covers the trailing sentence in oracle texts like Diresight, Cruel Truths, and Risky Research ("Surveil N, then draw M cards. You lose N life.").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Spell/Rules/YouLoseLifeSpellRule.cs)

## `/Parsing/Parsers/Static/`

### `IStaticRule` — *interface*

One static-ability recognition rule. Each implementation maps a single oracle-text shape to the `Ability` list it produces (almost always a single `StaticAbility`, occasionally a keyword-list expansion). Rules are discovered by reflection at `StaticAbilityParser` construction via the `StaticRuleAttribute` decoration and dispatched in descending `Priority` order, with ordinal-name order breaking ties within a band — first non-null (non-empty) result wins.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/IStaticRule.cs)

### `StaticRuleAttribute` — *sealed class* : Attribute, MagicAST.Parsing.Parsers.IPrioritizedRuleAttribute

Marks an `IStaticRule` implementation for reflection-based discovery by `StaticAbilityParser`. Each decorated rule contributes one oracle-text recognizer to the parser's static-ability cascade.

<b>Priority convention (range 0–100, default 50, higher = more specific = tried first):</b>

<b>80–100</b> — rules that supersede a more-general sibling (color-disjunction before type-disjunction, IfYouDo variants before plain variants, "this creature" before "a [type]"). Without the bump these would never fire because the more-general rule would shadow them. <b>50</b> — default. Non-overlapping rules whose regex anchors are mutually exclusive. <b>20–40</b> — catch-all / generic rules that should be tried last so a more-specific sibling gets a chance first.

The numeric scheme replaces the old source-order convention: each rule used to declare its priority implicitly by where it appeared in `TryParse`'s cascade. Splitting rules into one-file-per-rule loses that ordering signal, so each rule now states its priority explicitly.

<b>Phase 3 migration note:</b> priorities are migrated ORDER-PRESERVING as `Priority = 1000 - (index in the legacy dispatch chain)`, so the original first-non-null-wins order of `StaticAbilityParser`'s legacy chain is reproduced exactly by construction. (The 0–100 band convention above describes the intended steady-state once the migration settles; until then the literal 1000-minus-index values keep behavior identical.)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/StaticRuleAttribute.cs)

### `StaticRuleHelpers` — *static class*

Shared utilities used across multiple `IStaticRule` implementations. Lives outside the dispatcher so rules can be added without taking a dependency on `StaticAbilityParser` internals.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/StaticRuleHelpers.cs)

## `/Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/`

### `AbilityWordConditionalEntersWithCountersRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AbilityWordConditionalEntersWithCountersRule.cs)

### `AbundanceDrawReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the Abundance optional draw-replacement shape: "If you would draw a card, you may instead choose land or nonland and reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a card of the chosen kind. Put that card into your hand and put all other cards revealed this way on the bottom of your library in any order."

This is a draw-replacement effect (CR 614.11) whose replacement action is optional ("you may instead") — the controller may let the draw proceed normally. The replacement action itself is the Abundance-specific "choose land or nonland + reveal until found + put rest on bottom in any order" atomic action, modelled as `AbundanceRevealEffect`.

Priority 981: one above `DrawReplacementRule` (980), so this more specific "may instead" variant is checked first and the general "draw N instead" rule is not reached for Abundance's oracle text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AbundanceDrawReplacementRule.cs)

### `ActivateAbilitiesAsThoughHasteRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may activate abilities of creatures you control as though those creatures had haste." — Thousand-Year Elixir.

CR 302.6: a creature's activated ability with {T}/{Q} can't be activated unless it's been under control continuously since your most recent turn began. CR 702.10a: "Haste is a static ability." This static permission removes the CR 302.6 activation restriction for the named creatures' activated abilities without granting them haste outright (see `ActivateAbilitiesAsThoughHasteEffect`).

Anchored start-to-end (^…$) so this only claims the exact singular permission sentence and cannot swallow a longer sibling clause that appends a rider.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ActivateAbilitiesAsThoughHasteRule.cs)

### `AdditionalCostPayLifeReducesColoredCostRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As an additional cost to cast [color] [type] spells, you may pay N life. Those spells cost {[colored]} less to cast if you paid life this way. This effect reduces only the amount of [color] mana you pay." — the Defiler cycle from March of the Machine (Defiler of Instinct and siblings). A single continuous static ability (CR 604.1) that both grants an OPTIONAL additional cost for a filtered class of the controller's future spells and conditionally reduces those same spells' cost when the additional cost was paid.

CR 601.2f (verbatim): "The player determines the total cost of the spell. Usually this is just the mana cost. Some spells have additional or alternative costs. ... The total cost is the mana cost or alternative cost (as determined in rule 601.2b), plus all additional costs and cost increases, and minus all cost reductions."

The three sentences are ONE oracle-text paragraph (`ClauseSplitter` keeps a paragraph as a single clause), so this rule matches the whole span with a single anchored (^…$) pattern rather than three separate rules. The two structured halves: `GrantAdditionalCostEffect` (the "you may pay N life" grant, carrying its own `AffectedSpells` filter per `GrantAlternativeCostEffect` convention) and `CostReductionEffect` (the "{colored} less … if you paid life this way" reduction, gated by `AdditionalCostPaidCondition` and carrying the colored-only reduction in `ManaSymbols` with a zero generic `Amount` — the third sentence, "This effect reduces only the amount of [color] mana you pay," is exactly what putting the reduction on `ManaSymbols` rather than a generic amount already encodes, so it needs no separate node).

Anchored (^…$) to prevent false-positive substring matches inside longer oracle lines — the #1 FAIL class per the vertical-slice contract. Color and spell-class type are both captured so the rule generalises across the cycle (Defiler of Instinct is red/permanent; siblings vary both axes).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AdditionalCostPayLifeReducesColoredCostRule.cs)

### `AllLandsAreCreaturesStillLandsRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"All lands are [P/T] creatures that are still lands." — the Nature's Revolt "animate lands" template: a single always-on static continuous effect (CR 611) that turns EVERY land into a creature with the stated power/toughness box, retaining the land card type.

This is the static (unconditional, no cost, no duration) sibling of the Keyrune/manland "becomes a creature" animate family (`BecomesCreatureEffectRule`): same `BecomesCreatureEffect` node, but here the subject is EVERY land in the game (`Each`, CardTypes=["land"]) rather than the source permanent (`Self`), and the effect has no stated `Duration` — it is an always-on characteristic-setting static ability (CR 604.1) that lasts as long as the source enchantment remains on the battlefield, not a fixed-length continuous effect.

<b>"still lands" retention (CR 205.1b).</b> "Some effects change an object's card type, supertype, or subtype but specify that the object retains a prior card type ... This rule applies to effects that ... state that something is 'still a [type...]'." CR 305.7 confirms an animated land "doesn't add or remove any card types ... it keeps its land types". So the retained `land` card type sits ahead of the added `creature` in `CardTypes` — mirroring the manland "It's still a land." reminder consumption, except here the retention is stated inline ("that are still lands") rather than as a trailing sentence.

Canonical card: Nature's Revolt — "All lands are 2/2 creatures that are still lands."

Anchored (^…$) to the exact "All lands are P/T creatures that are still lands" shape so it cannot collide with siblings that use different verbs/qualifiers (e.g. "become" instead of "are", a "you control" controller qualifier, or an "Until end of turn" prefix) — those are different static/activated shapes, not this one.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AllLandsAreCreaturesStillLandsRule.cs)

### `AllMustBlockRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AllMustBlockRule.cs)

### `AllObjectsAddTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the Mycosynth Lattice "all permanents are [type] in addition to their other types" oracle template: a static continuous effect that additively grants one or more card types to all permanents (or a broadly-scoped subject without controller qualification).

Handled patterns:

"All permanents are artifacts in addition to their other types." → `AddTypeEffect` with Target={Each, permanents}, AddedCardTypes=["artifact"].

CR 205.1b (verbatim): "Some effects change an object's card type, supertype, or subtype but specify that the object retains a prior card type, supertype, or subtype. In such cases, all the object's prior card types, supertypes, and subtypes are retained. This rule applies to effects that use phrases such as 'in addition to its other types' or that state that something is 'still a [type, supertype, or subtype].'"

Priority 969 — one below `NonlandCreatureTypeGrantRule` (970) which handles the more-specific controller-scoped shape, so this broader rule fires only when that rule declines (i.e., the subject is not "Nontoken creatures you control").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AllObjectsAddTypeRule.cs)

### `AllObjectsAreColorRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the "All &lt;subject&gt; are &lt;color(s)&gt;." oracle template (Darkest Hour: "All creatures are black.") — a static layer-5 continuous effect that sets the color of every object matching a broad, unqualified subject filter.

CR 105.1 (verbatim): "There are five colors in the Magic game: white, blue, black, red, and green."

<b>CR 611.1:</b> "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects, modifies control of objects, or affects players or the rules of the game, for a fixed or indefinite period."

Reuses `ChangeColorEffect` (the same node `ChangeColorEffectRule` emits for the singular-target "Target creature becomes [color]" activated-ability shape), scoped here to a broad `Each` `ObjectReference` instead of a singular `Target`. No `Duration` is set: the color-setting is an ongoing static ability that lasts as long as this permanent remains on the battlefield, mirroring `AllObjectsAreColorlessRule`'s undurationed sibling effects.

The subject noun is resolved through a small whitelist of broad, unqualified card-type groups (creatures, permanents, lands, artifacts, enchantments, planeswalkers) — an unrecognized subject or a controller-qualified/multi-noun subject (e.g. "creatures you control", "creatures and planeswalkers") declines the match rather than guessing, falling through to a more specific sibling rule or the fallback parser. The color alternation is restricted to the five named colors (CR 105.1); "colorless" is owned by the sibling `AllObjectsAreColorlessRule` and is not matched here.

Priority 967 — grouped with the sibling "All &lt;subject&gt; are/have &lt;X&gt;" static rules (`AllObjectsAddTypeRule` at 969, `AllObjectsAreColorlessRule` at 968); this rule's color-name alternation is disjoint from both the type-token alternation and "colorless", so relative dispatch ordering among the three is immaterial.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AllObjectsAreColorRule.cs)

### `AllObjectsAreColorlessRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the Mycosynth Lattice "all cards…, spells, and permanents are colorless" oracle template: a continuous layer-5 effect that makes all game objects colorless.

The oracle line enumerates three disjoint groups that together cover every game object: cards not on the battlefield (hand, library, graveyard, exile, command zone), spells (on the stack), and permanents (on the battlefield). Each group is modelled as a separate `ChangeColorEffect` with `Colors: []` (colorless) under a single `StaticAbility`, honouring the oracle sentence as written rather than collapsing it to a single "everything" filter.

CR 105.3 (verbatim): "Effects may change an object's color or give a color to a colorless object. If an effect gives an object a new color, the new color replaces all previous colors the object had (unless the effect said the object became that color 'in addition' to its other colors)." A layer-5 effect setting Colors = [] makes the object colorless (CR 105.2c: "A colorless object has no color.").

Priority 968 — below `AllObjectsAddTypeRule` (969) and `NonlandCreatureTypeGrantRule` (970).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AllObjectsAreColorlessRule.cs)

### `AnthemModifyPTRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AnthemModifyPTRule.cs)

### `AnyNumberInDeckRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"A deck can have any number of cards named [this]." — the self-referential exception to the four-of deck-construction rule (Relentless Rats, Rat Colony, Shadowborn Apostle, Persistent Petitioners, Dragon's Approach).

CR 100.2a: "In constructed play …, each deck has a minimum deck size of 60 cards. A constructed deck may contain any number of basic land cards and no more than four of any card with a particular English name other than basic land cards." This static line lifts that limit for cards sharing this card's name. It is a characteristic-defining-style declarative property of the card, so it lands as a `StaticAbility` — not an activated or triggered ability.

The "[this]" in "named [this]" always names the card the line appears on, so the emitted `AnyNumberInDeckEffect` carries no field: the self- reference is implicit. The regex tolerates any card name in that slot rather than threading the card's own name through (it is structurally always self).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AnyNumberInDeckRule.cs)

### `AppliesToCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Cost reductions that apply to a <i>class of other abilities/spells</i> the enchanted permanent is the target of — Strong Back's "Equip abilities you activate that target enchanted creature cost {3} less to activate." and "Aura spells you cast that target enchanted creature cost {3} less to cast." (ADR 0003 follow-up 1: the surviving keyword identity is what a reference filter matches on).

Distinct from `TypeSpellCostReductionRule` (self/spell-on-stack reductions carried via `AffectedObjects`): here the reduction targets a referenced <i>ability or spell</i> via `AppliesTo`, a typed `AbilityReference`. The "that target enchanted creature" clause becomes `TargetsObject` = `EnchantedOrEquipped`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AppliesToCostReductionRule.cs)

### `ArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Activated abilities of artifacts can't be activated." — Collector Ouphe's static ability. A continuous restriction (CR 604.2 / CR 611.1) that prevents any activated ability on any artifact — regardless of controller — from being put on the stack (CR 602.5: "A player can't begin to activate an ability that's prohibited from being activated.").

Modelled as a `StaticAbility` whose `AffectedObjects` is an `ObjectFilter` scoping the restriction to artifacts (`CardTypes=["artifact"]`, no `Controller` — the lock is symmetric, unlike Karn, the Great Creator's opponent-scoped form), and whose `Effects` list contains a single `CantActivateAbilitiesEffect` with no `Target` (the affected-objects filter on the ability already names the locked objects). This mirrors `OpponentArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` minus the controller qualifier.

The pattern is anchored (^…$) so it cannot fire as a substring of a longer clause, and it does not match the "your opponents control" variant (that phrase makes the text longer than this pattern permits, so `OpponentArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` stays the sole match for that card).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule.cs)

### `AsLongAsAttachedMayPlayFromTopOfLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises "As long as [X] is attached to a creature, you may play lands and cast spells from the top of your library." — a conditional static permission that allows the controller to play lands and cast spells from the top of their library while the source Equipment is attached to a creature. Paradigm card: The Reality Chip (NEO).

CR 702.151b: "Attaching an Equipment with reconfigure to another creature causes the Equipment to stop being a creature until it becomes unattached from that creature." CR 401.5: "Some effects … say that a player may look at the top card of their library." CR 604.2: "Static abilities create continuous effects … active as long as the permanent with the ability remains on the battlefield and has the ability."

The ability is conditional ("as long as [X] is attached to a creature") — the condition body is captured verbatim into an `OtherCondition` residual because no structured `IsAttachedToCreature` arm exists in the `Condition` union yet (debt — PB-7 structured-condition buckets). The effect itself is fully structured as a `MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryEffect` granting both `PlayLands` and `CastSpells`.

Priority 939 — fires before `MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryRule` (940) so the conditioned form is claimed before the unconditional Bolas's Citadel form. The pattern is anchored (^…$) to prevent substring collision with any sibling rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AsLongAsAttachedMayPlayFromTopOfLibraryRule.cs)

### `AsLongAsControlColorCreatureSelfKeywordGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"This creature has [keyword] as long as you control a [color] creature." — the conditional self-keyword-grant gated on a color-qualified control count (Wingrattle Scarecrow: "This creature has flying as long as you control a blue creature."; "This creature has persist as long as you control a black creature. (When this creature dies, if it had no -1/-1 counters on it, return it to the battlefield under its owner's control with a -1/-1 counter on it.)"). CR 702.79a (Persist, verbatim): "Persist is a triggered ability. 'Persist' means 'When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, if it had no -1/-1 counters on it, return it to the battlefield under its owner's control with a -1/-1 counter on it.'"

CR 611.3a (continuous effect from a static ability, not "locked in" — it "applies at any given moment to whatever its text indicates"): the granted keyword applies only while the stated condition is true. The condition is a `CountCondition` over an `ObjectFilter` keyed on `CardTypes:["creature"]`, `Colors:[&lt;color&gt;]`, and `Controller: You` — "you control a [color] creature" is an existence check (at least one), so the threshold is GreaterThanOrEqual 1 — wrapped in an `AsLongAsDuration`. The keyword itself resolves through `MapKeywordToStaticAbility`, the same shared keyword-to-static-ability table every other conditional grant rule uses, so this rule generalizes over any keyword that table supports (not just flying/persist).

Sibling of `AsLongAsStaticGrantRule`'s generic suffix-form "[subject] has [keyword] as long as [condition]" shape, but that generic rule's suffix pattern has no reminder-stripping step before matching the condition clause, so a keyword whose reminder text rides after the "as long as" clause (e.g. Persist) would have the reminder text swallowed whole into the condition. This dedicated rule captures the trailing parenthetical separately and attaches it to the outer `StaticAbility` (CR 207.2), mirroring `NontokenCreaturesHaveKeywordRule`'s reminder handling. Sits above `AsLongAsStaticGrantRule` (968) so this more specific shape is tried first. Fully anchored (^…$) on the specific "This creature has [keyword] as long as you control a [color] creature" surface, so it cannot collide with any other "as long as" shape.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AsLongAsControlColorCreatureSelfKeywordGrantRule.cs)

### `AsLongAsControlledObjectsHaveAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the leading "As long as [condition], [card-types] you control have &quot;[quoted activated ability]&quot;." form — a conditional continuous grant of an activated ability to a set of controlled permanents.

The World Tree's third ability is the canonical example: "As long as you control six or more lands, lands you control have '{T}: Add one mana of any color.'"

Shape: the leading "As long as [condition]" block gates the grant duration (`AsLongAsDuration`). The main clause "[types] you control have [quoted ability]" becomes a `GainAbilityEffect` targeting each permanent of the listed card type(s) controlled by you. The quoted body is dispatched to `ActivatedAbilityParser` to produce a nested `ActivatedAbility`.

CR 604.1: "Static abilities do something all the time rather than being activated or triggered." CR 604.2: "Static abilities create continuous effects, some of which are … ability-granting effects." CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period." CR 602.1: Activated abilities have cost and effect ("[Cost]: [Effect]").

Priority 969 — above `AsLongAsStaticGrantRule` (968) so this rule claims the "lands you control have [quoted]" clause before the generic rule attempts its suffix-pattern and fails. The regex anchors are ^…$ so there is no substring-overlap risk with sibling rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AsLongAsControlledObjectsHaveAbilityRule.cs)

### `AsLongAsEnchantedColorConditionalRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As long as enchanted creature is [color], it gets +N/+N and has [keyword]." "As long as enchanted creature is [color], it gets +N/+N and all creatures able to block it do so."

Produces a `StaticAbility` with the color condition on `Condition` (not encoded in a per-effect Duration) and `EnchantedOrEquipped` as the target of each effect. Both effects originate from one oracle clause gated by one condition (CR 611 — a static ability creates one continuous effect layer). The condition is stored at ability scope to avoid duplicating it across effects and to separate "what applies" (the effects) from "when it applies" (the condition).

Two oracle-text shapes map here:

PT-and-keyword grant: "it gets +1/+1 and has deathtouch" → `ModifyPTEffect` + `GainAbilityEffect` (both targeting `EnchantedOrEquipped`). PT-and-lure: "it gets +1/+1 and all creatures able to block it do so" → `ModifyPTEffect` + `AllMustBlockEffect` (Rule 509.1c; every creature that can legally block the enchanted creature must do so).

Sits at Priority 975 — above `AsLongAsPTAndKeywordGrantRule` (970) so the enchanted-creature shapes (which differ in target and condition placement) are claimed before that rule's `ObjectReference.Self()` path.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AsLongAsEnchantedColorConditionalRule.cs)

### `AsLongAsEnchantedTypeKeywordGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As long as enchanted permanent is a creature, it has flying." "As long as enchanted permanent is an Equipment, it has "Equipped creature has flying.""

A conditional continuous grant gated on the enchanted permanent's OWN card type/subtype (CR 611.3a — a static-ability continuous effect isn't "locked in"; the condition is checked continuously). Paradigm card: Rune of Flight, whose two grants share the same "enchanted permanent is a/an [type]" gate but differ in what "it has" carries — a bare keyword (arm 1) or a quoted static ability (arm 2).

The gate word disambiguates card type vs. subtype (CR 205.2a vs. CR 205.3m): a lowercase noun ("creature", "artifact") is a main card type → `ObjectHasCardTypeCondition`; a capitalised noun ("Equipment", "Vehicle") is a subtype → `ObjectHasSubtypeCondition`, reusing the existing "if it's a [Subtype]" node rather than inventing a duplicate. Both conditions are wrapped in one `AsLongAsDuration` shared by the produced `GainAbilityEffect` (mirrors the Wingcrafter "As long as [X], [target] has flying" shape).

Arm 2's quoted body ("Equipped creature has flying") is itself the ordinary static Equipment-grant shape (CR 301.5d — "Equipped creature has [ability]"), so it is parsed inline into a nested `StaticAbility` whose own effect targets `EnchantedOrEquipped` — the same reference the outer grant uses, since "equipped creature" from the newly-granted ability's perspective is still the creature attached to the Equipment.

Both arms target `EnchantedOrEquipped` (the enchanted permanent itself), NOT `Self` — this rule sits above `AsLongAsStaticGrantRule` (Priority 968), whose generic "it has [keyword]" sub-parser would otherwise mis-map the "it" back-reference to the Aura itself rather than the enchanted permanent the pronoun actually names. The regex is fully anchored (^…$) so it cannot fire as a substring of a broader sibling clause.

CR 611.3a (verbatim): "A continuous effect generated by a static ability isn't 'locked in'; it applies at any given moment to whatever its text indicates." CR 301.5d: an Equipment's ability "may be an ability that's expressed as 'Equipped creature gains [ability]' or 'Equipped creature has [ability]'."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AsLongAsEnchantedTypeKeywordGrantRule.cs)

### `AsLongAsInGraveyardKeywordGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the Incarnation cycle's graveyard-functional conditional keyword grant: "As long as this card is in your graveyard and you control a &lt;basic land subtype&gt;, &lt;card type&gt;s you control have &lt;keyword&gt;." — Brawn's third line: "As long as this card is in your graveyard and you control a Forest, creatures you control have trample."
