CR 113.6a/113.6b: an ability's text can establish that it functions from a zone other than the battlefield (113.6b lists the zones in which an ability can function, including the graveyard when the ability says so); MAST does not model zone-functioning machinery itself (ADR 0003/0004 describe-not-execute) — it simply records that the condition's first conjunct is a state check on the source card's OWN current zone (`ObjectFilter.IsSelf` + `Zone.Graveyard`), composed with the ordinary "you control a [land]" board-state conjunct via `AllCondition` (ADR 0007, composing primitives over new leaves — mirrors `ImpendingStaticRule`'s manually-built compound gate). CR 702.19a: "Trample is a static ability." — the granted keyword is generalised through `MapKeywordToStaticAbility` rather than hard-coded to Trample, so any bare keyword in this template resolves.

The "as long as" gate is a continuous `Duration` on the `GainAbilityEffect` (CR 611.2 — a continuous effect generated by a static ability lasts as long as the source remains in the zone it functions from and the condition holds), not an ability-scope `Condition`: the latter is reserved for "if …" resolution-time gates (e.g. Deepwood Legate's `AllCondition`-gated `castWithoutPaying`), whereas "as long as" is a duration on the grant itself, matching `AsLongAsControlledObjectsHaveAbilityRule` and `TheWorldTree`'s "As long as you control six or more lands, lands you control have […]" sibling shape.

Priority 970 — above the generic `AsLongAsStaticGrantRule` (968) and `AsLongAsControlledObjectsHaveAbilityRule` (969, which requires a QUOTED activated-ability body and would not match this bare-keyword shape anyway). The pattern is anchored (^…$) and requires the literal "this card is in your graveyard and you control a" prefix, so it cannot steal a shorter/longer sibling clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AsLongAsInGraveyardKeywordGrantRule.cs)

### `AsLongAsLifeThresholdSelfKeywordGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As long as your life total is less than or equal to half your starting life total, [CardName] has [keyword]." — the God-template life-threshold conditional keyword grant (Bane, Lord of Darkness: "As long as your life total is less than or equal to half your starting life total, Bane has indestructible.").

CR 611.2 (conditional continuous effect): "Some continuous effects are conditional... Such effects... apply only while the condition is true." CR 702.12a: "Indestructible is a static ability." The leading condition clause is parsed by `ConditionParser` into a `QuantityComparisonCondition` (a `DerivedQuantity` keyed on `LifeTotal` compared against half a `StartingLifeTotal`) and wrapped in an `AsLongAsDuration`.

The subject "Bane" is the card referring to itself by its own name (CR 201.5: "A card's name in its own text refers to that object"), so it resolves to `Self` — the literal name never rides into the AST. Distinct from the sibling `AsLongAsStaticGrantRule`, whose leading-form sub-parsers require the subject to be the pronoun "it" or "this creature"/"this permanent"; a card-name subject does not match those patterns, so this dedicated rule is needed rather than extending that one.

Fully anchored (^…$) on the specific "life total is less than or equal to half [...] starting life total" condition surface, so it cannot collide with any other "As long as [condition], [Name] has [keyword]" shape using a different condition.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AsLongAsLifeThresholdSelfKeywordGrantRule.cs)

### `AsLongAsOtherCreaturesPTBuffRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Leading-form conditional continuous P/T anthem: "As long as &lt;cond&gt;, other creatures you control get +N/+M." (optionally prefixed by an ability word, Rule 207.2c — Gavony Ironwright: "Fateful hour — As long as you have 5 or less life, other creatures you control get +1/+4.").

CR 611.3: "Some continuous effects are... conditional continuous effects. Conditional continuous effects... apply only while their condition is true." The condition clause is parsed by `ConditionParser` (here, a life-total threshold — "you have 5 or less life" — resolving to a `QuantityComparisonCondition` over `LifeTotal`) and wrapped in an `AsLongAsDuration`. The effect is a single `ModifyPTEffect` targeting `Each` creature the controller controls, excluding the source itself (CR 109.5 "another" — the oracle "Other" qualifier maps to `ExcludeSelf`).

A sibling of `AsLongAsPTAndKeywordGrantRule` (self-subject compound P/T + keyword grant): this rule instead targets a FILTERED set of other creatures with a plain P/T modifier only (no keyword grant), so the two do not collide. Also distinct from `LordPTBuffRule`, which explicitly declines any clause containing "as long as" and leaves that leading-condition form to this rule.

The ability-word prefix ("Fateful hour — ", Rule 207.2c, no rules meaning) is captured by the classifier into `AbilityWord`; we record it as the descriptive label on the produced `StaticAbility` and peel the em-dash prefix before matching the leading "As long as" pattern. Anchored (^…$) so it cannot steal a longer or differently-shaped clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AsLongAsOtherCreaturesPTBuffRule.cs)

### `AsLongAsPTAndKeywordGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Leading-form conditional continuous effect bundling a P/T modifier AND a keyword grant under one shared `AsLongAsDuration`: "As long as &lt;cond&gt;, it/this creature gets +N/+M and has &lt;keyword&gt;."

Both effects live on a single `StaticAbility` because they originate from one oracle clause governed by one "as long as" condition (Rule 611 — the continuous effect is created by the static ability and applies for as long as the condition holds). Modelling them as one ability with two effects keeps the condition single-sourced rather than duplicating the static ability per effect.

Sits at a higher priority than `AsLongAsStaticGrantRule` (Priority 968) so the compound "gets +N/+M and has &lt;keyword&gt;" clause is recognised before that rule's single-effect sub-parsers, whose end-anchored regexes decline the compound text and would otherwise let the clause fall through to the fallback.

An ability-word prefix ("Threshold — …", Rule 207.2c) carries no rules meaning; the classifier captures it into `AbilityWord` and we record it as the descriptive label on the produced `StaticAbility`, peeling the em-dash prefix before matching the leading pattern.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AsLongAsPTAndKeywordGrantRule.cs)

### `AsLongAsStaticGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AsLongAsStaticGrantRule.cs)

### `AssignDamageAsToughnessRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Each creature you control assigns combat damage equal to its toughness rather than its power." — High Alert, Doran-the-Siege-Tower family. Rule 510.1a (verbatim): "Each attacking creature and each blocking creature assigns combat damage equal to its power." This static ability establishes a global replacement that substitutes toughness for power in the combat-damage assignment step, governed by CR 614 (replacement effects) and CR 613 (layer ordering).

The pattern is fully anchored (^ … $) to prevent substring-matching another oracle line that contains this phrase embedded inside a larger clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AssignDamageAsToughnessRule.cs)

### `AssignDamageAsUnblockedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may have this creature assign its combat damage as though it weren't blocked." (Pride of Lions). Rule 510.1c: a blocked creature normally assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it; this static grants the optional substitution to assign all combat damage as though unblocked. Distinct from Trample (excess only) — see `AssignDamageAsUnblockedEffect`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AssignDamageAsUnblockedRule.cs)

### `AttachedModifyPTAndAssignDamageAsToughnessRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined attached-P/T anthem + combat-damage-assignment substitution: "[Enchanted|Equipped] creature gets +N/+M and assigns combat damage equal to its toughness rather than its power." e.g. Gauntlets of Light — "Enchanted creature gets +0/+2 and assigns combat damage equal to its toughness rather than its power."

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying TWO effects in its list (the MAST multi-effect-per-clause encoding): a `ModifyPTEffect` (+N/+M) and an `AssignDamageAsToughnessEffect` (CR 510.1a — "Each attacking creature and each blocking creature assigns combat damage equal to its power." — the Doran, the Siege Tower / High Alert combat-damage substitution), BOTH targeting the same attached subject "Enchanted/Equipped creature". One oracle clause generates one continuous effect from one static ability, so the two effects share a single ability rather than being split into two abilities (CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object.").

Sibling of `AttachedModifyPTAndDoesntUntapRule` and `AttachedModifyPTAndGoadedRule` — same compound shape, different rider effect. Reuses the existing `AssignDamageAsToughnessEffect` node (the Doran/High Alert family) rather than inventing a new discriminator; its `AppliesTo` is set to the attached subject since the printed object here (an Aura) is not itself the affected creature.

ANCHORED (^…$): the full oracle sentence is matched exactly so this rule cannot fire on a substring of a more specific sibling clause, and cannot itself swallow a broader sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AttachedModifyPTAndAssignDamageAsToughnessRule.cs)

### `AttachedModifyPTAndCardTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined attached-P/T anthem + card-type grant: "[Enchanted|Equipped] creature gets +N/+M and is a[n] &lt;card type&gt; in addition to its other types." e.g. Silverskin Armor — "Equipped creature gets +1/+1 and is an artifact in addition to its other types."

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying TWO effects in its list (the MAST multi-effect-per-clause encoding): a `ModifyPTEffect` (+N/+M, CR 613.4c — a layer-7c power/toughness-modifying continuous effect) and an `AddTypeEffect` additively granting the card type (CR 613.1d — layer 4, type-changing effects; CR 205.1b — "in addition to its other types" retains all prior card types, supertypes, and subtypes), BOTH targeting the same attached subject "Enchanted/Equipped creature". One oracle clause generates one continuous effect from one static ability, so the two effects share a single ability rather than being split into two abilities (CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object.").

Direct sibling of `AttachedModifyPTAndEveryCreatureTypeRule` (Runed Stalactite: "...and is every creature type.", modeled via a Changeling `GainAbilityEffect` grant instead of an `AddTypeEffect`) — both share the same "attached P/T anthem + type rider" shape, differing only in how the type grant is expressed. Also related to `EquippedPTKeywordAddTypeRule` (Raven Wings: "...has flying, and is a Bird in addition to its other types."), which adds a creature SUBTYPE via a three-part clause including a keyword grant; here the grant is a CARD TYPE (not a subtype) and there is no keyword rider, so the clause is only two parts.

CR 205.1b (verbatim): "Some effects change an object's card type, supertype, or subtype but specify that the object retains a prior card type, supertype, or subtype. In such cases, all the object's prior card types, supertypes, and subtypes are retained. This rule applies to effects that use phrases such as 'in addition to its other types' or that state that something is 'still a [type, supertype, or subtype].'"

CR 613.1d (verbatim): "Layer 4: Type-changing effects are applied. These include effects that change an object's card type, subtype, and/or supertype."

CR 613.4c (verbatim): "Layer 7c: Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AttachedModifyPTAndCardTypeRule.cs)

### `AttachedModifyPTAndDoesntUntapRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined attached-P/T anthem + doesn't-untap rider: "[Enchanted|Equipped] creature gets +N/+M and doesn't untap during its controller's untap step." e.g. T-45 Power Armor — "Equipped creature gets +3/+3 and doesn't untap during its controller's untap step."

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying TWO effects in its list (the MAST multi-effect-per-clause encoding): a `ModifyPTEffect` (+N/+M) and a `DoesntUntapEffect` (CR 502.3 — a continuous effect can keep a permanent from untapping during the untap step), BOTH targeting the same attached subject "Enchanted/Equipped creature". One oracle clause generates one continuous effect from one static ability, so the two effects share a single ability rather than being split into two abilities (CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object.").

Sibling of `AttachedModifyPTAndGoadedRule` (the analogous "gets +N/+M and is goaded" compound) — same shape, different rider effect. Distinct from `AnthemModifyPTRule` (the bare "Enchanted/ Equipped creature gets +N/+M." shape, no rider) and from `DoesntUntapRule`'s bare enchanted/equipped "doesn't untap" shape (no P/T grant).

CR 702.6 (Equip); CR 502.3 (verbatim): "Third, the active player determines which permanents they control will untap. Then they untap them all simultaneously. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack. Normally, all of a player's permanents untap, but effects can keep one or more of a player's permanents from untapping."

ANCHORED (^…$): the full oracle sentence is matched exactly so this rule cannot fire on a substring of a more specific sibling clause. The apostrophe class tolerates both the straight (U+0027) and curly (U+2019) forms used across printings (matching the convention in `SubjectDoesntUntapDuringControllersUntapStepsRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AttachedModifyPTAndDoesntUntapRule.cs)

### `AttachedModifyPTAndEveryCreatureTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined attached-P/T anthem + Changeling grant: "[Enchanted|Equipped] creature gets +N/+M and is every creature type." e.g. Runed Stalactite — "Equipped creature gets +1/+1 and is every creature type."

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying TWO effects in its list (the MAST multi-effect-per-clause encoding): a `ModifyPTEffect` (+N/+M, CR 613.4c — a layer-7c power/toughness-modifying continuous effect) and a `GainAbilityEffect` granting the Changeling characteristic-defining ability (CR 205.3m — creature types are a subset of subtypes; CR 702.73a — Changeling as an ability grant), BOTH targeting the same attached subject "Enchanted/Equipped creature". One oracle clause generates one continuous effect from one static ability, so the two effects share a single ability rather than being split into two abilities (CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object.").

Mirrors the sibling compound-rider shapes `AttachedModifyPTAndGoadedRule` (is goaded), `AttachedModifyPTAndDoesntUntapRule` (doesn't untap), and `AttachedModifyPTAndLosesKeywordRule` (loses [keyword]) — all target the same "Enchanted/Equipped creature" subject with a P/T anthem plus one rider clause. Here the rider is a characteristic-defining-ability grant, so it is recorded via `GainAbilityEffect` wrapping a Changeling `StaticAbility` (KeywordSource = Changeling), exactly the shape `CreaturesAreEveryCreatureTypeRule` (Maskwood Nexus) uses per-scope, but here scoped directly to the single attached subject rather than a filtered "each creature" collection.

CR 702.73a (verbatim): "Changeling is a characteristic-defining ability. 'Changeling' means 'This object is every creature type.' This ability works everywhere, even outside the game. See rule 604.3."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AttachedModifyPTAndEveryCreatureTypeRule.cs)

### `AttachedModifyPTAndGoadedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined attached-P/T anthem + goaded designation: "[Enchanted|Equipped] creature gets +N/+M and is goaded." e.g. Bloodthirsty Blade — "Equipped creature gets +2/+0 and is goaded."

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying TWO effects in its list (the MAST multi-effect-per-clause encoding): a `ModifyPTEffect` (+N/+M) and a `GoadedEffect` (CR 701.15b — the goaded designation), BOTH targeting the same attached subject "Enchanted/Equipped creature". One oracle clause generates one continuous effect from one static ability, so the two effects share a single ability rather than being split into two abilities (CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object.").

Distinct from `AnthemModifyPTRule` (the bare "Enchanted/ Equipped creature gets +N/+M." shape, no goaded rider). Mirrors the compound shape used by `SupertypeAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` for the analogous "and have [keyword]" conjunction, but the rider here is a designation (CR 701.15b — "Goaded is a designation a permanent can have."), not a keyword ability, so it is recorded via `GoadedEffect` rather than `GainAbilityEffect`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AttachedModifyPTAndGoadedRule.cs)

### `AttachedModifyPTAndLosesKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined attached-P/T anthem + keyword-removal rider: "[Enchanted|Equipped] creature gets +N/+M and loses [keyword]." e.g. Magebane Armor — "Equipped creature gets +2/+4 and loses flying."

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying TWO effects in its list (the MAST multi-effect-per-clause encoding): a `ModifyPTEffect` (+N/+M) and a `LoseAbilityEffect` (the removed keyword), BOTH targeting the same attached subject "Enchanted/Equipped creature". One oracle clause generates one continuous effect from one static ability, so the two effects share a single ability rather than being split into two abilities (CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object.").

CR 702.6 (Equip); CR 611.2 — a continuous effect generated by a static ability can, among other things, remove an ability from an object; the removed keyword is recorded on `AbilityText` (a designed free-text field, mirroring the "all other abilities" and "enchant creature card in a graveyard" usages elsewhere) rather than a structured keyword node, since the lost side carries no recursive ability definition to model (unlike a grant, which must recreate the full ability).

Sibling of `AttachedModifyPTAndDoesntUntapRule` and `AttachedModifyPTAndGoadedRule` (same compound shape, different rider effect). Distinct from `AnthemModifyPTRule` (the bare "Enchanted/Equipped creature gets +N/+M." shape, no rider).

ANCHORED (^…$): the full oracle sentence is matched exactly so this rule cannot fire on a substring of a more specific sibling clause. The keyword is generalized (captured as free text, not hardcoded to "flying") so any "loses [keyword]" rider is covered by this one rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AttachedModifyPTAndLosesKeywordRule.cs)

### `AttackingObjectsHaveKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Attacking &lt;creatures|tokens&gt; you control have [keyword]." — a static continuous effect (CR 604.1: "Static abilities do something all the time rather than being activated or triggered. They are written as statements, and they're simply true.") granting a keyword ability to the attacking subset of the controller's creatures/tokens. This is Starry-Eyed Skyrider's third line: "Attacking tokens you control have flying."

CRITICAL: "Attacking" here is a COMBAT STATE (CR 508; glossary "attacking creature": "A creature that has either been declared as part of a legal attack during the combat phase … It remains an attacking creature until it's removed from combat or the combat phase ends"), NOT a creature subtype (CR 205.3m). It is therefore encoded as a `CombatStateCharacteristic` with `Attacking` on the filter — mirroring Goblin Oriflamme ("Attacking creatures you control get +1/+0") — and never as `Subtypes = ["Attacking"]`.

The "tokens" qualifier maps to `IsToken = true` (CR 111.1: "A token is a marker used to represent any permanent that isn't represented by a card."); the bare "creatures" form leaves `IsToken` unset. Following the bare-token convention of `SubtypeTokensHaveKeywordRule`, no `CardTypes` is emitted for "tokens" (the text says "tokens", not "creature tokens"). "you control" is `Controller = You` (CR 109.5). The keyword resolves through `MapKeywordToStaticAbility` (CR 702.9a/702.9b for flying); an unrecognised keyword declines so no free text is emitted.

Priority 972 — ABOVE `SubtypeTokensHaveKeywordRule` (970) so this more-specific combat-state shape intercepts the mis-parse in which the generic "&lt;Subtype&gt; tokens you control have …" rule would capture "Attacking" as a subtype word. Static dispatch is descending-Priority, first-non-null-wins, so intercepting by priority is sufficient — `SubtypeTokensHaveKeywordRule` is left untouched. The case-sensitive literal "Attacking" and the anchored pattern keep this collision-free.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AttackingObjectsHaveKeywordRule.cs)

### `AttackingSubtypeAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined ATTACKING-scoped subtype anthem + keyword grant, with the "creatures" noun OMITTED because the bare plural subtype noun itself stands in for it: "Attacking [Subtype-plural] you control get +N/+N and have [keyword]." e.g. Blight Mound — "Attacking Pests you control get +1/+0 and have menace."

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying TWO effects in its list (the MAST multi-effect-per-clause encoding): a `ModifyPTEffect` (+N/+N) and a `GainAbilityEffect` (the keyword), BOTH targeting the same subtype-and-combat-state-filtered subject "[Subtype] you control [that are] attacking". One oracle clause generates one continuous effect from one static ability, so the two effects share a single ability rather than being split into two abilities (CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object. Example: A permanent with the static ability 'All white creatures get +1/+1' generates an effect that continuously gives +1/+1 to each white creature on the battlefield.").

The leading "Attacking" qualifier (CR 508 — a creature that's attacking) is recorded on `Characteristics` as a `CombatStateCharacteristic` with `Attacking`, mirroring the same combat-state axis `FromLabel` produces for "attacking creature" filters elsewhere (e.g. Goblin Wardriver's Battle cry). The matched noun ALWAYS routes to `Subtypes` (a creature subtype, e.g. "Pests"), matching the sibling `TribalAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule`'s no-"creatures" subject shape. "You control" resolves to the source's controller (CR 109.5).

The granted keyword is itself a static ability, modelled as a recursive `GainedAbility` via the shared `MapKeywordToStaticAbility` mapping. No duration is carried — a static ability's continuous effect lasts for as long as the source remains on the battlefield, not until a stated time.

Distinct from `TribalAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` (the plain "Other [Subtype] you control get +N/+N and have [keyword]" shape, no combat-state qualifier) and `SupertypeAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` (requires the "creatures" word). The mandatory "Attacking" prefix here means this pattern never starts with an optional "Other " group, so the two never collide on the same clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/AttackingSubtypeAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule.cs)

### `BareKeywordGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/BareKeywordGrantRule.cs)

### `BareKeywordListGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the static three-keyword Oxford-comma grant on an attached permanent: "(Enchanted|Equipped) creature has [kw1], [kw2], and [kw3]."

This is a <b>static</b> continuous effect (CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period."; CR 611.3: "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object."). The grant persists for as long as the Aura or Equipment remains attached — there is no Duration node (distinct from the activated "gains [kw] until end of turn" shape).

CR 301.5d: an Equipment's ability "may be an ability that's expressed as 'Equipped creature gains [ability]' or 'Equipped creature has [ability]'." The enchanted/equipped subject maps to `EnchantedOrEquipped`.

Per the MAST multi-effect-per-clause doctrine, "has [kw1], [kw2], and [kw3]" on one oracle line is bundled into a single `StaticAbility` whose `Effects` list carries three independent `GainAbilityEffect` nodes — one per keyword. No `CompositeEffect` wrapper is used: the flat Effects list is the idiomatic multi-effect encoding for a static ability.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/BareKeywordListGrantRule.cs)

### `BareKeywordPairGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the static keyword-pair grant on an attached permanent: "(Enchanted|Equipped) creature has [kw1] and [kw2]."

This is a <b>static</b> continuous effect (CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period."; CR 611.3: "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object."). The grant persists for as long as the Aura or Equipment remains attached — there is no Duration node (distinct from the activated "gains [kw] until end of turn" shape).

CR 702.5a: "Enchant is a static ability … The enchant ability restricts what an Aura spell can target and what an Aura can enchant." The enchanted/equipped subject maps to `EnchantedOrEquipped`.

Per the MAST multi-effect-per-clause doctrine, "has [kw1] and [kw2]" on one oracle line is bundled into a single `StaticAbility` whose `Effects` list carries two independent `GainAbilityEffect` nodes — one per keyword. No `CompositeEffect` wrapper is used: the flat Effects list is the idiomatic multi-effect encoding for a static ability.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/BareKeywordPairGrantRule.cs)

### `BlitzStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes a "Blitz [cost]" oracle line into the three abilities defined by CR 702.152a (the sacrifice-variant sibling of `DashStaticRule`; mirroring the `ReconfigureStaticRule` multi-ability precedent).

CR 702.152a (verbatim): "Blitz represents three abilities: two static abilities that function while the card with blitz is on the stack, one of which may create a delayed triggered ability, and a static ability that functions while the object with blitz is on the battlefield. 'Blitz [cost]' means 'You may cast this card by paying [cost] rather than its mana cost,' 'If this spell's blitz cost was paid, sacrifice the permanent this spell becomes at the beginning of the next end step,' and 'As long as this permanent's blitz cost was paid, it has haste and \"When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, draw a card.\"' Casting a spell for its blitz cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h."

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000) so the three-ability decomposition takes precedence over the single-ability keyword combinator path. The combinator in `BlitzKeyword` remains live as a fallback, emitting only the primary alternative-cast static ability (the keyword expander returns a single `Ability`; Blitz decomposes into three).

Differs from Dash only in the second and third abilities: Blitz's end-step delayed trigger <em>sacrifices</em> the permanent (rather than returning it to hand), and its conditional battlefield static grants TWO abilities — haste plus a "put into a graveyard from the battlefield, draw a card" triggered ability ("put into a graveyard from the battlefield" is the `Dies` event, CR 700.4).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/BlitzStaticRule.cs)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/BlockAdditionalRule.cs)

### `BoastTwicePerTurnRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Creatures you control can boast [N] times during each of your turns rather than once."

CR 702.142a: "A boast ability is a special kind of activated ability. 'Boast - [Cost]: [Effect]' means '[Cost]: [Effect]. Activate only if this creature attacked this turn and only once each turn.'" This static ability modifies that default once-per-turn limit for controller-owned creatures.

ANCHORED (^…$): the surface phrase "can boast … times during each of your turns rather than once" is distinctive and will not match as a substring of any other static rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/BoastTwicePerTurnRule.cs)

### `BuybackStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes a "Buyback [cost]" oracle line into the two static abilities defined by CR 702.27a (mirroring the `DashStaticRule` / `ReconfigureStaticRule` multi-ability precedent).

CR 702.27a (verbatim): "Buyback appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents two static abilities that function while the spell is on the stack. 'Buyback [cost]' means 'You may pay an additional [cost] as you cast this spell' and 'If the buyback cost was paid, put this spell into its owner's hand instead of into that player's graveyard as it resolves.'"

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000) so the two-ability decomposition takes precedence over the single-ability keyword combinator path. The combinator in `BuybackKeyword` remains live as a fallback, emitting only the primary additional-cast-cost static ability (the keyword expander returns a single `Ability`; Buyback decomposes into two).

The buyback cost is usually mana ("Buyback {3}") but CR 702.27a's "[cost]" also covers non-mana costs, printed with an em dash rather than trailing the keyword directly — "Buyback—Sacrifice a land." (Pegasus Stampede). Both forms share the same two-ability decomposition; only the `Cost` payload of ability 1 differs. The non-mana cost text is delegated to the shared `ParseSacrificePattern` helper (same primitive an activation cost "Sacrifice a land" would use) rather than re-deriving sacrifice-cost parsing here.

Ability 2 is a zone-change replacement effect (CR 614 / 702.27a): the spell would go from the stack to the graveyard as it resolves, but instead goes to its owner's hand. Modeled with the existing replacement primitives — `ReplacementEffect` over a `ZoneChangeEvent` (origin stack, destination graveyard) with `OriginalEventOccurs = false` ("instead") and the `ReturnToHandEffect` as the replacement action — gated on `KeywordCostPaidCondition` for Buyback.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/BuybackStaticRule.cs)

### `CanAttackIgnoringDefenderRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Creatures you control can attack as though they didn't have defender." — High Alert, Assault Formation family. Rule 702.3b (verbatim): "A creature with defender can't attack." This static ability overrides that restriction, allowing creatures with Defender to be declared as attackers.

The pattern is fully anchored (^ … $) to prevent substring-matching another oracle line that embeds this phrase inside a larger clause. The "they" pronoun in High Alert's text ("as though they didn't have defender") is a plural referring to the earlier "Creatures you control" subject; both forms are matched.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CanAttackIgnoringDefenderRule.cs)

### `CanBeYourCommanderStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Card name] can be your commander." — printed on non-default-legal commander cards (Teferi, Temporal Archmage; The Prismatic Bridge; etc.) to declare that the card is usable as a commander even though it lacks the Legendary supertype on its own type line or is otherwise excluded from the default commander pool.

Teferi, Temporal Archmage (C14) is Legendary and a Planeswalker, but carries this clause because the Commander format at that time required separate printed permission for planeswalkers to be commanders. Current Oracle errata still preserves the text.

CR 903.3: "Each player chooses a legendary creature card or Legendary Planeswalker card as their commander." The printed permission here expands (or confirms) that the named card qualifies. MAST records this as a `CommanderDesignationEffect` on a `StaticAbility` — the designation is a static fact about the card, not a one-shot action (no zone-change, no event required).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the phrase "can be your commander" does not appear as a substring of any other standard oracle-text clause. Anchoring is the defensive convention.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CanBeYourCommanderStaticRule.cs)

### `CantAttackAloneRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Static restriction: "This creature can't attack alone." The "alone" qualifier conditions the attack restriction on this object being the sole declared attacker — the restriction is lifted whenever at least one other creature is also declared as an attacker.

Static restriction: "This creature can't attack a player it has already attacked this turn." Narrows the attack restriction to a specific player — the named object may still attack any player (or planeswalker/battle) it has NOT already attacked earlier in the current turn.

### `CantAttackOrBlockAloneRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Static restriction: "This creature can't attack or block alone." The "alone" qualifier conditions both the attack and the block restriction on this object being the sole attacker / sole blocker — the restriction is lifted whenever at least one other creature is also declared.

### `CantCastMoreThanNSpellsRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the spell-cast-cap static "Each player can't cast more than one spell each turn." (Eidolon of Rhetoric, Arcane Laboratory) and its single-player-scoped variant "You can't cast more than one spell each turn." (Moderation). CR 601.3a: a player who wants to cast a spell follows the steps of casting it, and a continuous effect such as this one restricts whether that's legal (CR 611.1: a continuous effect "affects players or the rules of the game, for a fixed or indefinite period") — NOT a per-spell "can't be cast" restriction. Emits a single `StaticAbility` carrying one `CantCastMoreThanNSpellsEffect`; the cap, scope, and counting window are structured fields, never free text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CantCastMoreThanNSpellsRule.cs)

### `CantDrawCardsRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the global draw-lock static "Players can't draw cards." (Maralen of the Mornsong). A rules-of-the-game continuous effect (CR 611.1) written as a plain static statement (CR 604.1) that stops a player or players from drawing cards — see CR 121 (drawing a card) for the drawing rule this restriction overrides. Emits a single `StaticAbility` carrying one `CantDrawCardsEffect`, scoped to `EachPlayer` for the symmetric "Players" case — mirroring the `CantGainLifeRule` convention (the `Player` field is left generalised so an asymmetric variant such as "Your opponents can't draw cards" can reuse this node with a different `ObjectReference` scope, should such a pattern be added later).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CantDrawCardsRule.cs)

### `CantGainLifeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the global life-gain lock static "Players can't gain life." (Giant Cindermaw) and the asymmetric "Your opponents can't gain life." (Knight of Dusk's Shadow). A rules-of-the-game continuous effect (CR 611.1) written as a plain static statement (CR 604.1) that stops a player or players from gaining life — see CR 119.7 for the authoritative can't-gain-life rule. Emits a single `StaticAbility` carrying one `CantGainLifeEffect`, scoped to `EachPlayer` for the symmetric "Players" case or `EachOpponent` for the "Your opponents" case.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CantGainLifeRule.cs)

### `CantHaveCountersRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"This creature can't have counters put on it." — a static counter-prohibition (CR 122: counters) scoped to the ability's own controlling object (Self), e.g. Melira's Keepers.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CantHaveCountersRule.cs)

### `CantLoseGameForZeroLifeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises "You don't lose the game for having 0 or less life." (Lich's Tomb) — a static replacement that overrides the zero-or-less-life state-based loss condition (CR 704.5a: a player with 0 or less life loses the game) for the controller. Emits a single `StaticAbility` carrying one `CantLoseGameForZeroLifeEffect` scoped to `You`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CantLoseGameForZeroLifeRule.cs)

### `CantLoseGameOpponentsCantWinGameRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises "You can't lose the game and your opponents can't win the game." (Herald of Eternal Dawn) — a compound static lock pairing a blanket loss exemption for the controller (CR 104.3: "There are several ways to lose the game.") with a blanket win prohibition for the controller's opponents (CR 104.2a: "A player still in the game wins the game if that player's opponents have all left the game. This happens immediately and overrides all effects that would preclude that player from winning the game."). Written as a plain static statement (CR 604.1: "Static abilities do something all the time rather than being activated or triggered. They are written as statements, and they're simply true."). Emits a single `StaticAbility` carrying two effects: a `CantLoseGameEffect` scoped to `You` and a `CantWinGameEffect` scoped to `EachOpponent` — mirroring how the timing and effect of a single sentence can still decompose into two composable nodes.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CantLoseGameOpponentsCantWinGameRule.cs)

### `CantPlayLandsRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the land-play lock static "You can't play lands." (Aggressive Mining) and its symmetric/asymmetric siblings "Players can't play lands." / "Your opponents can't play lands." CR 305.1: "A player who has priority may play a land card from their hand during a main phase of their turn when the stack is empty. Playing a land is a special action; it doesn't use the stack." CR 116.2a describes the default once-per-turn special action this restriction overrides entirely for the scoped player(s). Emits a single `StaticAbility` carrying one `CantPlayLandsEffect`, scoped via `You` / `EachPlayer` / `EachOpponent` — mirroring the `CantDrawCardsRule` / `CantGainLifeRule` convention.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CantPlayLandsRule.cs)

### `CantPreventDamageRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the global damage-prevention lock static "Damage can't be prevented." (Leyline of Punishment) — a rules-of-the-game continuous effect (CR 611.1) written as a plain static statement (CR 604.1), that nullifies every prevention effect (CR 615.1). Emits a single `StaticAbility` carrying one `CantPreventDamageEffect`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CantPreventDamageRule.cs)

### `CastAsFlashWithConsequenceRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CastAsFlashWithConsequenceRule.cs)

### `CastFromExileRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may cast this card from exile." — an unconditional static permission to cast this card from the exile zone (Eternal Scourge, EMN).

CR 601.3e (verbatim, excerpt): "Some rules and effects state that an alternative set of characteristics or a subset of characteristics are considered to determine if a card or copy of a card is legal to cast…" Here the alternative set of characteristics is the <i>zone</i> the card may be cast from — exile rather than only its hand. The permission does not replace the mana cost, so the produced `AlternativeCastEffect` has `FromZone = Exile` and a null `Cost` (cast for its own mana cost) and a null `Condition` (unconditional).

This is not a keyword ability, so the ability carries no `KeywordSource`. Priority 983 places it just below `CastFromGraveyardConditionalRule` (985) and `CastFromMultipleZonesRule` (984), which handle overlapping oracle phrasings — multi-zone permission and conditional graveyard permission respectively. A narrower anchor (^…$) ensures this rule does not match either sibling as a substring.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CastFromExileRule.cs)

### `CastFromGraveyardConditionalRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may cast this card from your graveyard as long as [condition]." — the written-out conditional graveyard-recursion permission (Gravecrawler: "You may cast this card from your graveyard as long as you control a Zombie.").

CR 601.3e (verbatim, excerpt): "Some rules and effects state that an alternative set of characteristics or a subset of characteristics are considered to determine if a card or copy of a card is legal to cast…" Here the alternative set of characteristics is the <i>zone</i> the card may be cast from — its graveyard rather than only its hand. The permission does not replace the mana cost (contrast the alternative-cost keywords Flashback/Escape/Madness), so the produced `AlternativeCastEffect` has `FromZone = Graveyard` and a null `Cost` (cast for its own mana cost).

The "as long as [condition]" gate is structured through `ConditionParser` (ADR 0007) — "you control a Zombie" becomes a `CountCondition` over Zombies you control (≥1), not a free-text residual — and rides on `Condition`, the effect-level precondition home shared with the conditional alternative-cast keywords (Surge/Spectacle/Mayhem). This is not a keyword, so the ability carries no `KeywordSource`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CastFromGraveyardConditionalRule.cs)

### `CastFromMultipleZonesRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may cast this card from your graveyard or from exile." — an unconditional permission to cast this card from two zones (Squee, the Immortal).

CR 601.3e (verbatim, excerpt): "Some rules and effects state that an alternative set of characteristics or a subset of characteristics are considered to determine if a card or copy of a card is legal to cast…" Here the permission grants two separate zone exceptions — graveyard and exile — without an alternative cost and without any condition. Each zone becomes its own `AlternativeCastEffect` inside a single `StaticAbility` (the conjunction of the two permissions is expressed by the single oracle sentence).

The produced `AlternativeCastEffect` nodes each have a null `Cost` (cast for the card's own mana cost) and a null `Condition` (unconditional).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CastFromMultipleZonesRule.cs)

### `CastNoncreatureSpellsAsFlashRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may cast noncreature spells as though they had flash." — Valley Floodcaller and similar cards that grant flash specifically to noncreature spells. This is a continuous static permission (CR 604.2) that allows the controlling player to cast noncreature spells at instant speed, modelled as a `TimingModificationEffect` whose `AppliesTo` targets noncreature spells the controller casts.

CR 702.8a: "Flash is a static ability that functions in any zone from which you could play the card it's on. 'Flash' means 'You may play this card any time you could cast an instant.'" The global grant here extends that permission to every noncreature spell the controller casts. The filter encodes the noncreature restriction via `ExcludedCardTypes = ["creature"]` on the `SpellReference` (parallel to the `SpellCastConditionRule` "noncreature spell" encoding).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CastNoncreatureSpellsAsFlashRule.cs)

### `CastSpellsAsFlashRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may cast spells as though they had flash." — Vedalken Orrery and similar global flash-grant static abilities. This is a continuous static permission (CR 604.2) that allows the controlling player to cast any spell at instant speed, modelled as a `TimingModificationEffect` whose `AppliesTo` targets all spells you cast.

CR 702.8a: "Flash is a static ability that functions in any zone from which you could play the card it's on. 'Flash' means 'You may play this card any time you could cast an instant.'" The global grant here extends that permission to every spell the controller casts rather than to a single card.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CastSpellsAsFlashRule.cs)

### `CasualtyStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes a "Casualty N" oracle line into the two abilities defined by CR 702.153a (mirroring the `ReplicateStaticRule` / `SquadStaticRule` multi-ability precedent).

CR 702.153a (verbatim): "Casualty is a keyword that represents two abilities. The first is a static ability that functions while the spell with casualty is on the stack. The second is a triggered ability that functions while the spell with casualty is on the stack. Casualty N means 'As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may sacrifice a creature with power N or greater,' and 'When you cast this spell, if a casualty cost was paid for it, copy it. If the spell has any targets, you may choose new targets for the copy.' Paying a spell's casualty cost follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h."

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000) so the two-ability decomposition takes precedence over the single-ability keyword combinator path. The combinator in `CasualtyKeyword` remains live as a fallback, emitting only the primary additional-cost static ability (the keyword expander returns a single `Ability`; Casualty decomposes into two).

"you may choose new targets for the copy" is recorded on the `CopyEffect` via `MayChooseNewTargets` = `true` per the CR. The decision to retarget is engine territory, but the PERMISSION is oracle-stated and descriptively meaningful — not omitted (contrast Replicate where the same clause is engine-territory only per its rule text).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CasualtyStaticRule.cs)

### `ChooseBasicLandTypeOnEntryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As this [permanent] enters, choose [BasicLandType1] or [BasicLandType2]." — CR 614.12's as-enters replacement binding a chosen BASIC LAND TYPE value (Roots of Life: "As this enchantment enters, choose Island or Swamp."). Sibling of `ChooseColorOnEntryRule` / `ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule` / `ChooseCardTypeOnEntryRule` but for a basic land type value (CR 305.6: Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, Forest). Unlike the card-type sibling, the printed disjunction here is frequently a real subset of the five basic land types (not the full set), so this rule captures the literal options onto `Options`.

Anchored end-to-end and requires at least one recognized basic land type word immediately after "choose", so this pattern is disjoint from "choose a color" / "choose a creature type" / the card-type enumeration and does not shadow those siblings.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChooseBasicLandTypeOnEntryRule.cs)

### `ChooseCardNameOnEntryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As this [permanent] enters, choose a card name." (Declaration of Naught) — recognizes the as-enters card-name-choice declaration and emits a composite `StaticAbility` carrying `AsThisEnters` (CR 614.12) plus a plain `ChooseCardNameEffect`. Sibling of `ChoosePlayerOnEntryRule` / `ChooseColorOnEntryRule` / `ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule`: the regexes for "choose a card name"/"choose a player"/"choose a color"/"choose a creature type" are disjoint, so dispatch priority relative to those rules is immaterial.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChooseCardNameOnEntryRule.cs)

### `ChooseCardTypeOnEntryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As this [permanent] enters, choose artifact, creature, enchantment, instant, or sorcery." — recognizes the as-enters card-type-choice declaration (Cloud Key shape) and emits a composite `StaticAbility` carrying `AsThisEnters` plus a plain `ChooseCardTypeEffect`.

The oracle text lists the options as a disjunction ("artifact, creature, enchantment, instant, or sorcery") — the specific enumeration is reminder context, not structured data, so no `Options` field is needed: the rule captures any mention of those permanent types in a disjunctive list. A loose anchored pattern is used (does not require the exact five-type enumeration) so that future printings with different subsets still parse correctly.

Sibling of `ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule` and `ChooseColorOnEntryRule`; priority 940 is below both siblings so they claim their distinct noun phrases first and this rule does not shadow them.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChooseCardTypeOnEntryRule.cs)

### `ChooseColorOnEntryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As this [permanent] enters, choose a color." — CR 614.12's Voice of All example ("As this creature enters, choose a color."). The affected-object noun varies with the printed permanent type/subtype (e.g. "As this Aura enters, choose a color." — Prismatic Ward, an Enchantment — Aura), so the noun alternation lists every noun observed on this template rather than a single fixed word.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChooseColorOnEntryRule.cs)

### `ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As this [permanent] enters, choose a creature type." — recognizes the as-enters creature-type-choice declaration (Unclaimed Territory shape) and emits a composite `StaticAbility` carrying `AsThisEnters` plus a plain `ChooseCreatureTypeEffect`. Sibling of `ChooseColorOnEntryRule`; the two regexes are disjoint ("choose a color" vs "choose a creature type"), so dispatch priority relative to the color rule is immaterial.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule.cs)

### `ChooseNamedOptionOnEntryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As this [permanent] enters, choose [Name] or [Name]." (Phenomenon Investigators — "As this creature enters, choose Believe or Doubt.") — the as-enters named-mode binder of the Believe/Doubt family. Emits a composite `StaticAbility` carrying `AsThisEnters` (CR 614.12) plus a plain `ChooseNamedOptionEffect` listing the printed option names in order.

Sibling of `ChoosePlayerOnEntryRule` / `ChooseColorOnEntryRule` / `ChooseBasicLandTypeOnEntryRule`: those bind a choice from a characteristic domain ("choose a player/color", "choose Island or Swamp"), this binds a choice among a closed set of card-specific NAMED modes ("choose Believe or Doubt"). The lowercase "a player"/"a color" forms never match this rule's two-Capitalised-word regex; the basic-land-type form ("choose Island or Swamp") and the five colour words WOULD match on surface, so they are explicitly excluded here (`_reservedWords`) and deferred to their dedicated sibling rules — mode names are, by construction, none of the printed characteristic vocabularies. The two ability lines that follow (each labelled with an option name) are handled by `NamedModeGatedAbilityRule` and carry a `ChosenModeCondition` gate.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChooseNamedOptionOnEntryRule.cs)

### `ChooseNonlandCardNameOnEntryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As this creature enters, choose a nonland card name." (Silverquill Silencer) — the NONLAND-restricted sibling of `ChooseCardNameOnEntryRule`'s unrestricted "choose a card name" (Declaration of Naught). Recognizes the as-enters card-name-choice declaration and emits a composite `StaticAbility` carrying `AsThisEnters` (CR 614.12) plus a `ChooseCardNameEffect` whose `Filter` narrows the choosable name to nonland cards (`ObjectFilter{CardTypes:["card"], ExcludedCardTypes:["land"]}` — the same "nonland" encoding used elsewhere, e.g. the Thoughtseize family's "you choose a nonland card").

Anchored end-to-end and requires the literal "nonland" token between "choose a" and "card name", so this rule is naturally disjoint from `ChooseCardNameOnEntryRule`'s pattern (which has no "nonland" token and therefore never matches this card's text) — dispatch priority relative to that rule is immaterial.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChooseNonlandCardNameOnEntryRule.cs)

### `ChooseOpponentOnEntryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As this [permanent] enters, choose an opponent." (The Rack) — recognizes the as-enters player-choice declaration RESTRICTED to opponents and emits a composite `StaticAbility` carrying `AsThisEnters` (CR 614.1c) plus a `ChoosePlayerEffect` with `Scope` set to `Opponent` (CR 614.12 — the as-enters chosen-value binding, here bound over the restricted "an opponent" pool rather than "a player"). Downstream abilities reference the binding via `ChosenPlayer`.

Sibling of `ChoosePlayerOnEntryRule`: the regexes for "choose a player" and "choose an opponent" are disjoint (the latter requires the "an opponent" noun phrase, never present when the former matches), so dispatch priority relative to that rule is immaterial. Kept as a SEPARATE effect instance (not a shared TryParse helper) because the two surface phrases bind different `Scope` values — collapsing them into one regex/branch would risk silently dropping the opponent restriction for one of the two surface forms.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChooseOpponentOnEntryRule.cs)

### `ChoosePlayerOnEntryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As this [permanent] enters, choose a player." (Sawhorn Nemesis) — recognizes the as-enters player-choice declaration and emits a composite `StaticAbility` carrying `AsThisEnters` (CR 614.1c) plus a plain `ChoosePlayerEffect`. Sibling of `ChooseColorOnEntryRule` / `ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule`: the regexes for "choose a color"/"choose a creature type"/"choose a player" are disjoint, so dispatch priority relative to those rules is immaterial.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChoosePlayerOnEntryRule.cs)

### `ChosenColorAnthemModifyPTRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Creatures you control of the chosen color get +X/+Y." (Heraldic Banner) — a continuous P/T anthem (CR 611.3: "Some continuous effects are generated by spells or abilities that give another object an ability that generates a continuous effect. ... in this case the source of the effect is the object that has the ability") whose affected set is filtered by the color chosen as this permanent entered.

The "of the chosen color" clause is the structured consumer half of a CR 607 linked ability — the producer is the "As this [permanent] enters, choose a color" effect under `StaticAbility.When = AsThisEnters` (`ChooseColorEffect`). It is encoded with the structured `ChosenCharacteristic` = `Color` reference, never free-text.

Sibling of `ChosenTypeAnthemModifyPTRule` (the analogous "of the chosen type" shape): the surface noun chosen ("a color" vs. "a creature type") differs, and downstream references to "the chosen color" name a distinct axis than "the chosen type" (`ChosenCharacteristicKind` is kind-based), so this is a separate rule rather than a shared regex.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChosenColorAnthemModifyPTRule.cs)

### `ChosenNameSourcesActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Activated abilities of sources with the chosen name can't be activated unless they're mana abilities." — Pithing Needle's static ability. A continuous restriction (CR 604.2 / CR 611.1) that prevents any activated ability (CR 602.5: "A player can't begin to activate an ability that's prohibited from being activated.") of a source (CR 609.7: "The source of an ability is the object that generated it.") whose name matches the chosen card name from being put on the stack — with a carve-out for mana abilities (CR 605.1a: "A mana ability is an activated ability that meets [certain] criteria…").

Modelled as a `StaticAbility` whose `AffectedObjects` is an `ObjectFilter` scoped by `ChosenCharacteristic` = `CardName` — "sources with the chosen name" — the structured consumer side of the CR 607 linked ability whose producer is the paired "As this artifact enters, choose a card name." replacement (CR 614.12; see `ChooseCardNameOnEntryRule`). No `CardTypes`/`Zone` restriction: a "source" is any object in any zone, so the chosen-name predicate alone names the affected objects. The `Effects` list holds a single `CantActivateAbilitiesEffect` with `ExceptManaAbilities = true` (the "unless they're mana abilities" carve-out, modeled structurally rather than as free text) and no `Target` (the affected-objects filter already names the locked objects). Mirrors `ArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` with a chosen-name scope and a mana-ability exception.

Anchored end-to-end (^…$) so it cannot fire as a substring of a longer clause and is disjoint from the artifact-scoped `ArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` / `OpponentArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` templates.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChosenNameSourcesActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule.cs)

### `ChosenTypeAnthemModifyPTRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Creatures you control of the chosen type get +X/+Y." — a continuous P/T anthem (CR 613.1: an object's characteristics are recomputed in layers, the anthem being a P/T-modifying continuous effect) whose affected set is filtered by the creature type chosen as this permanent entered.

The "of the chosen type" clause is the structured consumer half of a CR 607 linked ability — CR 607.1: "An object may have two abilities printed on it such that one of them causes actions to be taken or objects or players to be affected and the other one directly refers to those actions, objects, or players. If so, these two abilities are linked: the second refers only to actions that were taken or objects or players that were affected by the first, and not by any other ability." The producer is the "choose a creature type" effect under `StaticAbility.When = AsThisEnters`. It is encoded with the structured `ChosenCharacteristic` = `CreatureType` reference, never free-text.

Distinct from `TribalAnthemModifyPTRule`, whose affected set is a fixed named subtype ("Other Goblin creatures you control get …"). Here the subtype is runtime-chosen rather than printed, so the subtype axis is the chosen-characteristic reference, not `Subtypes`. No "Other " prefix — the source enchantment is not a creature, so it never appears in the affected set.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChosenTypeAnthemModifyPTRule.cs)

### `ChosenTypeSpellCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Spells you cast of the chosen type cost {N} less to cast." — a cost-reduction static ability whose affected set is filtered by the card type chosen as this permanent entered (Cloud Key shape).

This is the consumer half of a CR 607 linked ability pair: the producer is the `ChooseCardTypeEffect` under `StaticAbility.When = AsThisEnters` (Cloud Key, line 1). The "of the chosen type" clause is encoded as `ChosenCharacteristic` = `CardType`, never free-text.

Distinct from `TypeSpellCostReductionRule` (a fixed printed card type like "Creature spells you cast cost {1} less") and from `ChosenTypeAnthemModifyPTRule` (which reads a chosen creature type for a P/T buff, not a chosen card type for a cost reduction). The pattern anchors on "of the chosen type" to distinguish it from the fixed-type family.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ChosenTypeSpellCostReductionRule.cs)

### `ColorSourceDamagePreventionStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Color-source damage-prevention static ability (the "Sphere of X" family): "If a red source would deal damage to you, prevent 2 of that damage." CR 615.10 (cited verbatim — its example is this exact template with N=1): "Some prevention effects generated by static abilities refer to a specific amount of damage — for example, \"If a source would deal damage to you, prevent 1 of that damage.\" Such an effect prevents only the indicated amount of damage in any applicable damage event at any given time. It will apply separately to damage from other applicable events that would happen at the same time, or at a different time." CR 615.1: "Some continuous effects are prevention effects. Like replacement effects (see rule 614), prevention effects apply continuously as events happen … Such effects watch for a damage event that would happen and completely or partially prevent the damage that would be dealt." CR 615.1a: "Effects that use the word \"prevent\" are prevention effects." CR 615.2: "Many prevention effects apply to damage from a source." Structure: a `StaticAbility` with a `ReplacementEffect` that:

Watches for a `DamageEvent` whose `Source` has the named color (`Source.Colors = [color]`) and whose recipient is you (`AffectedObjects.Controller = You`). Replaces the damage with a `PreventDamageEffect` that prevents a fixed `Amount` of it (`LiteralQuantity.Of(N)`) from the affected player (`Target = You`). Only `Amount` is prevented — the color filter lives on the watched event's source, not on the prevention action.

ANCHORED (^...$): the full-line template "If a [color] source would deal damage to you, prevent [N] of that damage." is matched in its entirety, so it cannot fire as a substring of a broader clause. It is distinct from the Circle/Rune of Protection activated shape ("The next time a red source of your choice would deal damage to you this turn, prevent that damage."), which has no leading "If", no numeric amount, and is an activated ability.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ColorSourceDamagePreventionStaticRule.cs)

### `ColoredCreatureSpellCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Color] creature spells you cast cost {N} less to cast." — the Amonkhet Monument cycle (Oketra's Monument, Bontu's Monument, Kefnet's Monument, Rhonas's Monument, Hazoret's Monument). Each reduces the cost of spells that are both a specific colour AND a creature spell.

CR 118.7: "What a player actually needs to do to pay a cost may be changed or reduced by effects." CR 118.7a: "Effects that reduce a cost by an amount of generic mana affect only the generic mana component of that cost."

Sits above `TypeSpellCostReductionRule` (priority 984) and `ConjunctiveTypeSpellCostReductionRule` (priority 983) because the two-word colour+type qualifier would otherwise never reach those rules. Anchored (^…$) to prevent false-positive substring matches inside longer oracle lines.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ColoredCreatureSpellCostReductionRule.cs)

### `ColoredSpellCostIncreaseRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Color] spells you cast cost {[colored]} more to cast." — the Nemesis "Leech" cycle (Ruby Leech, Sapphire Leech, Jade Leech, Alabaster Leech, Andradite Leech) and Derelor. Each self-taxes a colour-filtered class of spells the CONTROLLER casts, where the increase is a specific COLORED mana symbol {W}/{U}/{B}/{R}/{G} — never generic.

A spell's total cost is "locked in" before payments are made (CR 601.2) and the caster pays the mana component of that total (CR 118.7). Because colored ≠ generic (CR 601.2's Altar's Reap example distinguishes {B} from {1}), the colored increase is carried in `ManaSymbols` with a zero generic Amount, rather than being flattened to {1}.

Anchored (^…$) to prevent false-positive substring matches inside longer oracle lines. The colour WORD and the {mana} LETTER are captured independently (they coincide on all six corpus cards but the shape does not require it).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ColoredSpellCostIncreaseRule.cs)

### `ColorlessCreatureAnthemRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Colorless creatures you control get +N/+M." — continuous P/T anthem (CR 613.1, layer 7c) scoped to colorless creatures the controller owns. Colorless is not a color (Rule 105.1: "Colorless is not a color. Effects that specifically affect colorless permanents or spells use the term 'colorless'.") so the filter encodes colorlessness via `IsColorless` rather than the Colors axis. This rule runs at priority 970 (above `LordPTBuffRule` at 969) to intercept the "Colorless creatures" filter noun before LordPTBuffRule can misclassify "Colorless" as a creature subtype. LordPTBuffRule's [Subtype] creatures branch would treat "Colorless" as a subtype name (producing Subtypes: ["Colorless"]) rather than the correct IsColorless: true filter.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ColorlessCreatureAnthemRule.cs)

### `ConditionalFreeCastRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "If an opponent controls a Forest and you control a Swamp, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost." — Deepwood Legate's conditional free-cast permission. Per CR 118.9, "you may cast [this object] without paying its mana cost" IS an alternative cost (the no-cost alternative to the spell's mana cost); the leading "If X and Y" is the board-state gate on when that alternative is available.

CR 118.9 (verbatim): "Some spells have alternative costs. An alternative cost is a cost listed in a spell's text, or applied to it from another effect, that its controller may pay rather than paying the spell's mana cost. Alternative costs are usually phrased, 'You may [action] rather than pay [this object's] mana cost,' or 'You may cast [this object] without paying its mana cost.' Note that some alternative costs are listed in keywords; see rule 702."

CR 118.9b (verbatim): "Alternative costs are generally optional. An effect that allows you to cast a spell may require a certain alternative cost to be paid." — grounds the optional "you MAY cast". CR 118.9c (verbatim): "An alternative cost doesn't change a spell's mana cost, only what its controller has to pay to cast it. Spells and abilities that ask for that spell's mana cost still see the original value." CR 601.3 (verbatim): "A player can begin to cast a spell only if a rule or effect allows that player to cast it and no rule or effect prohibits that player from casting it." — the permission-to-cast rule this free-cast permission grants against.

The two board predicates are joined by "and", so they must both hold: the gate is modelled as an `AllCondition` (the honest AND) carried on `Condition` — a continuous casting-permission gate — rather than a `ConditionalEffect` wrapper. The permission itself reuses `CastWithoutPayingEffect` verbatim (its doc string IS this oracle phrase), targeting the source spell (`Self`).

Forest/Swamp are LAND SUBTYPES (CR 205.3i), so they go on `Subtypes` — mirroring `ConditionParser.NounToFilter`, which routes non-card-type nouns to Subtypes; no `CardTypes:["land"]` is added. The "a"/"an" quantifier is a "one or more" existence check (mirroring `ConditionParser.Quant`): GreaterThanOrEqual 1. The CountConditions are built inline here rather than via ConditionParser, which handles neither "opponent controls" nor "and"-joined compounds.

The surface phrase is fully anchored (^…$): Deepwood Legate's free-cast line is a single standalone ability line, and no sibling trigger or effect shares this exact opening, so the anchoring rules out substring collisions. Priority 90 (high- specificity band): the anchoring makes the exact value non-load-bearing.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ConditionalFreeCastRule.cs)

### `ConspireStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes a "Conspire" oracle line into the two abilities defined by CR 702.78a (mirroring the `DashStaticRule` / `ReconfigureStaticRule` multi-ability precedent).

CR 702.78a (verbatim): "Conspire is a keyword that represents two abilities... 'Conspire' means 'As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may tap two untapped creatures you control that each share a color with it' and 'When you cast this spell, if its conspire cost was paid, copy it. If the spell has any targets, you may choose new targets for the copy.'"

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000) so the two-ability decomposition takes precedence over the single-ability keyword combinator path. The combinator in `ConspireKeyword` remains live as a fallback, emitting only the primary additional-cost static ability (the keyword expander returns a single `Ability`; Conspire decomposes into two).

The "each share a color with it" predicate on the tapped creatures is a relational color filter (the creature shares a color with the spell being cast), modeled via `SharesColorWith` keyed on `{Kind: Self}` (the conspire spell). "Untapped" is creature-state derived from the rules and stays engine. The trigger's "you may choose new targets for the copy" clause is engine territory and is omitted (copy once, no `Count`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ConspireStaticRule.cs)

### `ControlledCreaturesWithCounterHaveKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Creatures you control with a/+1/+1 counter(s) on them/it have &lt;keyword&gt;." — a lord-grants-keyword static continuous effect (CR 604.2) whose subject filter is narrowed to creatures the controller controls that additionally carry a counter of the named kind (CR 122). Badgermole: "Creatures you control with +1/+1 counters on them have trample."

CR 702.19a (verbatim): "Trample is a static ability." The grant is continuous for as long as the source remains on the battlefield with the ability (CR 604.2), reaching every creature the controller controls that has a counter of the stated type at any given time — not just those that had one when the source entered.

Sibling to `BareKeywordGrantRule`'s Arm 5 ("Each creature you control with a +1/+1 counter on it has &lt;keyword&gt;.") — that arm is the singular "Each creature ... has" phrasing; this rule is the plural "Creatures ... have" phrasing ("them"/"it" both accepted for the counter back-reference, "counter"/"counters" both accepted for the count). Kept as a separate file (rather than folding into `BareKeywordGrantRule` or `ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule`) so the new anchored pattern cannot collide with either sibling's arms.

The counter-presence predicate is structured as a `CounterCharacteristic` (CR 122) via `FromLabel`, mirroring how `BareKeywordGrantRule`'s Arm 5 and `ObjectFilter`'s other characteristic predicates (tapped/untapped/combat-state) are structured.

Anchored (^…$) to prevent matching as a substring of a more specific sibling clause. Reminder text is stripped before matching so a trailing parenthetical explanation still lets the rule fire.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ControlledCreaturesWithCounterHaveKeywordRule.cs)

### `ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Other permanents you control have [keyword]." and "&lt;Subtype&gt; tokens you control have [keyword1] and [keyword2]." — static continuous effects (CR 604.2: "Static abilities create continuous effects … These effects are active as long as the permanent with the ability remains on the battlefield.") granting one or two keyword abilities to a filtered subset of the permanents the controller controls.

CR 702.11a (verbatim): "Hexproof is a static ability." Menace is likewise a static evasion ability, granted continuously by the source's static ability for as long as it remains on the battlefield.

Two sibling subject shapes recognised by one pattern:

"Other permanents you control have …" (Sigarda, Font of Blessings) — the "Other" qualifier maps to `ExcludeSelf = true` (CR 109.5 — "another"), the noun "permanents" maps to `CardTypes = ["permanent"]`.

"&lt;Subtype&gt; tokens you control have …" (Gleaming Overseer) — the capitalised subtype word populates `Subtypes`, the noun "tokens" maps to `IsToken = true` (CR 111.1: "A token is a marker used to represent any permanent that isn't represented by a card.").

Only these two combinations are built — any other combination captured by the pattern (e.g. a subtype paired with "permanents", or "Other" paired with "tokens") falls through to null so it doesn't shadow a sibling rule that might legitimately own a different shape.

Keyword list: one or two keywords, optionally joined by "and" ("hexproof and menace" — Gleaming Overseer). Per the MAST multi-effect-per-clause doctrine, a two-keyword grant is bundled into a single `StaticAbility` whose `Effects` list carries two independent `GainAbilityEffect` nodes — mirroring `BareKeywordPairGrantRule`'s enchant/equip dual-keyword shape, generalised here to a filtered-subject target instead of the enchanted/equipped anchor.

Priority 973 — above `AttackingObjectsHaveKeywordRule` (972), `SubtypeTokensHaveKeywordRule` (970), and `BareKeywordGrantRule` (967). Anchored (^…$) pattern prevents substring matches against sibling clauses; the bounded filter-shape guard above prevents this rule from mis-owning shapes already handled by those sibling rules (which return null on the shapes this rule declines, so dispatch order does not change behaviour either way).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule.cs)
