### `CreatureSpellsCantBeCounteredRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Creature spells you control can't be countered." — a static continuous effect on an enchantment (or other permanent) that grants uncounterability to all creature spells the controller casts. This is the Rhythm of the Wild shape.

CR 113.6g (verbatim): "An object's ability that states it can't be countered or can't be copied functions on the stack."

The affected objects are creature spells on the stack controlled by the source's controller. `CardTypes: ["spell", "creature"]` follows the established MAST convention for stack objects that are both spells and creatures (parallel to Maskwood Nexus "creature spells you control" — CardTypes: ["spell", "creature"], Controller: You). The `CantBeCounteredEffect` records the restriction; its presence on a `StaticAbility` with `AffectedObjects` scoping to creature spells is the structured form of the "creature spells can't be countered" lock.

Priority 972 — above `CantBeCastRestrictionRule` (971) and well above the generic counter/spell rules (50–80 band). Anchored (^...$) to prevent substring matches against other static lines.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CreatureSpellsCantBeCounteredRule.cs)

### `CreatureTokensHaveKeywordListRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Creature tokens you control have [keyword1] and [keyword2]." (Aven Wind Guide) — a static continuous effect (CR 604.2: "Static abilities create continuous effects … These effects are active as long as the permanent with the ability remains on the battlefield.") granting two keyword abilities to every creature token the controller controls (CR 702.9 Flying / CR 702.21 Vigilance are both static abilities).

Sibling to `ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule`, which handles the same "[filter] you control have [kw1][ and kw2]" shape for "Other permanents" and "&lt;Subtype&gt; tokens", but deliberately DECLINES the bare "Creature"/"Creatures" noun so it doesn't shadow `BareKeywordGrantRule`'s Arm 2 (which owns the single-keyword "Creature tokens you control have [kw]." shape via its `BuildBareGrantFilterTarget` bare-card-type branch — Combine Chrysalis). That Arm 2 pattern only captures ONE trailing keyword, so a second " and [kw2]" clause becomes part of the (unrecognised) keyword text and the whole match is declined. This rule closes that specific two-keyword gap for the bare "Creature tokens" noun, without touching either sibling rule's body.

Per the MAST multi-effect-per-clause doctrine, the two-keyword grant is bundled into a single `StaticAbility` whose `Effects` list carries two independent `GainAbilityEffect` nodes — mirroring `BareKeywordPairGrantRule`'s enchant/equip dual-keyword shape and `ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule`'s filtered-subject two-keyword shape, generalised here to the bare "Creature tokens you control" filter (`CardTypes=["creature"], IsToken=true, Controller=You` — the same filter shape `BareKeywordGrantRule`'s Arm 2 produces for the single-keyword case, so a card with only one recognised keyword still resolves to an identical AST regardless of which rule wins dispatch).

The pattern requires the " and " conjunction (kw2 is mandatory, not optional) so this rule strictly targets the two-keyword gap and never competes with `BareKeywordGrantRule`'s Arm 2 over the single-keyword shape it already owns.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CreatureTokensHaveKeywordListRule.cs)

### `CreatureTokensHaveQuotedAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Creature tokens you control have "[quoted ability]"" — grants a quoted ability (typically an activated mana ability) to every creature TOKEN the controller controls. Paradigm card: Springleaf Parade — "Creature tokens you control have '{T}: Add one mana of any color.'"

This is a <b>static</b> continuous effect (CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period."; CR 113.3/611.3: "Some effects and static abilities can grant an object an activated ability."). The grant persists for as long as the source remains on the battlefield with the ability — there is no Duration node.

Sibling to `SubtypeCreaturesHaveQuotedAbilityRule` (the subtype variant, e.g. "Sliver creatures you control have …") and `CreatureTokensHaveKeywordListRule` (the bare-keyword variant of this same "Creature tokens you control" filter). This rule owns the QUOTED variant of the bare card-type + token filter: <c>CardTypes=["creature"], IsToken=true, Controller=You</c> — the same filter shape `BareKeywordGrantRule`'s Arm 2 and `CreatureTokensHaveKeywordListRule` already produce for the single/double bare-keyword cases, so the AST is identical regardless of which rule wins dispatch on the filter axis.

The quoted body is dispatched to `ActivatedAbilityParser` first (the common mana-ability grant shape — a "{T}: Add …" mana ability), falling back to `TriggeredAbilityParser`. Returns null (surfacing the gap honestly) when neither recognises the body, mirroring `SubtypeCreaturesHaveQuotedAbilityRule`.

Priority 975 — one above `SubtypeCreaturesHaveQuotedAbilityRule` (974) and `CreatureTokensHaveKeywordListRule` (974), though in practice dispatch order does not matter: the sibling bare-keyword rules' capture groups are restricted to lowercase-letter/space charsets that cannot match a leading quote character, so they decline on their own regardless of priority. Anchored (^…$) pattern prevents substring matches against sibling clauses.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CreatureTokensHaveQuotedAbilityRule.cs)

### `CreaturesAreChosenTypeGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the Arcane Adaptation oracle template: a static continuous effect that additively grants the CHOSEN creature type (CR 607.1 linked-ability consumer of the paired "As this enchantment enters, choose a creature type." producer — `ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule`) to creatures you control, creature spells you control, and creature cards you own that aren't on the battlefield.

Oracle text (verbatim): "Creatures you control are the chosen type in addition to their other types. The same is true for creature spells you control and creature cards you own that aren't on the battlefield."

Three scopes are modelled as three sibling `AddTypeEffect` nodes in a single `StaticAbility`, each additively granting the chosen creature-type subtype (`ChosenSubtypeReference` = `CreatureType`) — parallels the sibling Maskwood Nexus template (`CreaturesAreEveryCreatureTypeRule`), which shares this exact three-scope tail sentence but grants Changeling (every type) via `GainAbilityEffect` instead of one chosen type via `AddTypeEffect`:

Creatures you control — CardTypes: ["creature"], Controller: You (permanents) Creature spells you control — CardTypes: ["spell", "creature"], Controller: You (on stack) Creature cards you own not on battlefield — CardTypes: ["creature"], Owner: You (non-permanent zones)

CR 205.1b (verbatim): "Some effects change an object's card type, subtype, and/or supertype but specify that the object retains a prior card type, subtype, and/or supertype. In such cases, all the object's prior card types, subtypes, and supertypes are retained, and the effect causes the object to gain or lose other card types, subtypes, and/or supertypes." CR 607.1: "An object may have two abilities printed on it such that one of them causes actions to be taken or objects or players to be affected and the other one directly refers to those actions, objects, or players."

ANCHORED (^…$): the two-sentence oracle paragraph is matched in full so this rule cannot fire on a substring of a more-specific sibling. Distinct wording ("the chosen type" vs "every creature type") keeps this disjoint from `CreaturesAreEveryCreatureTypeRule` regardless of dispatch order; priority 971 matches that sibling's tier.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CreaturesAreChosenTypeGrantRule.cs)

### `CreaturesAreEveryCreatureTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the Maskwood Nexus oracle template: a static continuous effect that grants every creature type (the Changeling characteristic-defining ability) to creatures you control, creature spells you control, and creature cards you own that aren't on the battlefield.

Three scopes are modelled as three sibling `GainAbilityEffect` nodes in a single `StaticAbility`, each granting the Changeling characteristic-defining ability:

Creatures you control — CardTypes: ["creature"], Controller: You (permanents) Creature spells you control — CardTypes: ["spell", "creature"], Controller: You (on stack) Creature cards you own not on battlefield — CardTypes: ["creature"], Owner: You (non-permanent zones)

CR 702.73a (verbatim): "Changeling is a characteristic-defining ability. 'Changeling' means 'This object is every creature type.' This ability works everywhere, even outside the game. See rule 604.3."

ANCHORED (^…$): the two-sentence oracle paragraph is matched in full to prevent this rule from firing on any substring of a more-specific sibling. Priority 971 — above `NonlandCreatureTypeGrantRule` (970) since this shape covers a broader set of zones and is more specific in oracle intent.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CreaturesAreEveryCreatureTypeRule.cs)

### `CreaturesEnteringDontCauseTriggerRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Creatures entering don't cause abilities to trigger." (Torpor Orb)

This is the suppressing mirror of the trigger-multiplication statics handled by `PanharmoniconTriggerDoublingRule` and `TriggerDoublingStaticRule`: both model a static ability that intercepts the event of a triggered ability triggering, via a `ReplacementEffect` wrapping an `AbilityTriggerEvent`. Where Panharmonicon scopes `CausedByEntering` and then AUGMENTS the trigger occurrence (`OriginalEventOccurs = true`, <c>Modifier.Type = "additionalTime"</c>), Torpor Orb scopes the identical `CausedByEntering` filter (creatures) and instead SUPPRESSES the occurrence entirely: <c>OriginalEventOccurs = false</c> with no `Replacement` — the watched triggering-event is replaced with nothing, mirroring the "Skip your draw step" pattern (CR 614.10: "'Skip [something]' is the same as 'Instead of doing [something], do nothing.'").

CR 603.2 (verbatim, cited in the dispatch brief): "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." Torpor Orb is a continuous static ability (CR 611/604 static-ability territory, not itself triggered) that watches for the CR 603.2 trigger-matching event — specifically, any creature entering the battlefield causing some OTHER triggered ability to want to trigger — and replaces that occurrence with nothing, so the would-be triggered ability never goes on the stack. No `AffectedObjects` filter is present because the suppression is unscoped as to WHOSE abilities are affected ("abilities", not "abilities of permanents you control"); `CausedByEntering` = <c>{ CardTypes: ["creature"] }</c> narrows the scope to triggers caused by a CREATURE entering (as opposed to Panharmonicon's "artifact or creature").

MAST describes the scope and suppression of the trigger-matching event; it does not model the trigger/stack engine itself (descriptive-not-engine doctrine).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CreaturesEnteringDontCauseTriggerRule.cs)

Board-wide, permanent (not "this turn") attacker-side restriction filtered by the ABSENCE of a keyword ability: "Creatures without flying can't attack." (Moat). CR 508.1c (declare-attackers step; attacking restrictions constrain the set of legal attacker declarations the active player can make). CR 702.9 (flying, the evasion keyword this restriction is scoped around on Moat; the pattern is general over any single-word keyword name, not flying-specific).

Unlike `CreaturesCantBlockThisTurnRule`'s "without &lt;keyword&gt;" arm (Falter, Cosmotronic Wave), which is a temporary "this turn" restriction and still relies on the typed `OtherCharacteristic` residual for the keyword-absence predicate, this rule is a permanent static ability with no stated duration and uses the first-class `LacksKeywords` axis — the structured "without [keyword]" predicate that residual was a deliberate scope deferral for (ADR 0001).

Maps to a `CantAttackEffect` whose `Target` is `Each` creature filtered by `CardTypes=["creature"]` + `LacksKeywords`. No `Duration` — Moat's restriction is always-on, not scoped to the current turn.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/CreaturesWithoutKeywordCantAttackRule.cs)

### `DamagePreventionAndMillReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Damage-prevention-plus-mill replacement effect (The Mindskinner family): "If a source you control would deal damage to an opponent, prevent that damage and each opponent mills that many cards." CR 615.1: some continuous effects are prevention effects; they watch for a damage event that would happen and completely prevent the damage that would be dealt. CR 615.1: effects that use the word "prevent" are prevention effects. CR 615.5: some prevention effects also include an additional effect, which may refer to the amount of damage that was prevented. CR 701.17: to mill a number of cards is to put that many cards from the top of a player's library into their graveyard. Structure: a `StaticAbility` with a `ReplacementEffect` that:

Watches for a `DamageEvent` where the source is controlled by You (`Source.Controller = You`) and the target is an opponent (`AffectedObjects.Controller = Opponent`). Replaces the damage with a `CompositeEffect` of: (1) a `PreventDamageEffect` targeting the opponent (All = true, recording the prevention), and (2) a `MillEffect` targeting each opponent with a `DerivedQuantity(DamageDealt)` — "that many cards" = the damage amount that would have been dealt (CR 615.5).

ANCHORED (^...$): the surface phrase "a source you control would deal damage to an opponent, prevent that damage and each opponent mills that many cards" is highly specific and does not appear as a substring of any other standard oracle-text clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/DamagePreventionAndMillReplacementRule.cs)

### `DamageThenExileInsteadReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Self] deals N damage to any target. If a creature dealt damage this way would die this turn, exile it instead." — the Anger-of-the-Gods / Incendiary Flow damage-exile family: a burn spell whose second sentence installs a linked one-shot replacement effect.

CR 614.1: replacement effects watch for a particular event that would happen and completely or partially replace it with a different event. CR 614.6: if an event is replaced, it never happens — the modified event occurs instead. CR 700.4: "dies" means put into a graveyard from the battlefield. CR 607.1: "this way" links the replacement's scope back to objects affected by this spell's own damage (a linked ability).

Both sentences live in a single un-split oracle-text clause — no printed line break separates them — and `AbilityClassifier` routes the whole clause to Static because it contains both "would" and "instead" tokens (`ContainsReplacementPattern`) regardless of which sentence they appear in, so the compound two-sentence text arrives here as one `OracleClause`. This rule recognises that compound shape as a unit and emits the two abilities it actually describes: the damage-dealing `SpellAbility` (sentence 1) and the linked replacement `StaticAbility` (sentence 2) — mirroring `DrawReplacementRule`'s replacement-effect shape for the second half.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/DamageThenExileInsteadReplacementRule.cs)

### `DamageToChosenPlayerDoublingReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Chosen-player damage-doubling replacement effect (Sawhorn Nemesis): "If a source would deal damage to the chosen player or a permanent they control, it deals double that damage instead." CR 614.12: some replacement effects, printed on a permanent, apply as long as that permanent remains on the battlefield rather than only as it enters; effects using "instead" are replacement effects (CR 614.1a). This effect watches for a damage event directed at the player chosen by the card's paired "As this creature enters, choose a player." ability (CR 607 linked ability — see `ChoosePlayerOnEntryRule`) or a permanent that player controls, and replaces the damage quantity with double. Structure mirrors `NoncombatDamageDoublingReplacementRule`: the replaced event is a `DamageEvent` with no `Source` restriction ("a source", unrestricted — `Source` null per its "null = any source" doc), directed at the chosen player (`AffectedObjects` with `Controller = ControllerFilter.ChosenPlayer` and no `CardTypes`, so the bare controller filter covers both the player themselves and any permanent they control — exactly how `NoncombatDamageDoublingReplacementRule` uses `ControllerFilter.Opponent` bare for "an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls"), and the doubling is a structured `ReplacementModifier{ Type: "double" }` ("double that damage"), not a free-text description. ANCHORED (^...$): the phrase "a source would deal damage to the chosen player or a permanent they control … double that damage … instead" is highly specific and does not appear as a substring of any other standard oracle-text clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/DamageToChosenPlayerDoublingReplacementRule.cs)

A characteristic-defining ability (CDA) that sets a creature's power and/or toughness to a `DerivedQuantity` — a hand or graveyard size, not a board-object count. Handles the oracle pattern:

"[Name]'s power and toughness are each equal to the number of cards in your hand." → `Both`, `CardsInHand` "[Name]'s power is equal to the number of cards in your hand." → `Power`, `CardsInHand` "[Name]'s toughness is equal to the number of cards in your hand." → `Toughness`, `CardsInHand`

Rule 604.3: "A characteristic-defining ability defines a characteristic value for the object it's on." Rule 107.3: the value of * in a CDA box is determined by an ability (layer 7a, Rule 613.1a). The value here is derived from the controller's hand size — a game-state quantity evaluated continuously.

Priority 976 is higher than `DefinePTRule` (Priority 975) so this derived-value branch fires first; if neither derived pattern matches, control falls through to `DefinePTRule`'s board-count branch.

### `DevotionConditionalLoseCreatureTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As long as your devotion to [color] (and [color]) is less than [N], [card name] isn't a creature." — the Theros God template (CR 205.1a / CR 700.5a). Continuous layer-4 type-loss conditional on the controller's devotion to one OR two colours falling below a threshold. Two-colour gods (e.g. Ephara: "devotion to white and blue") are the guild gods from Born of the Gods / Journey into Nyx.

MAST records the condition as a `quantityComparison` (`DevotionQuantity` &lt; threshold — with `Colors` listing one or both counted colours) and the effect as a `loseType` (`LoseTypeEffect` targeting Self, removing the "creature" card type from the permanent's type line). The StaticAbility carries no Duration: the effect persists for as long as the condition holds (modelled via an `AsLongAsDuration` wrapping the condition on the effect).

The modification — "roll that many dice plus one and ignore the lowest roll" — is the atomic `ReplacementModifier{ Type: "advantage" }`: roll N+1 dice and discard the lowest result (CR 706.6 — an ignored roll is treated as never having happened). `OriginalEventOccurs = false` (the N-dice roll is replaced by the N+1 roll, not performed in addition), mirroring `CounterDoublingReplacementRule`/`MillDoublingReplacementRule`.

Wyll prints the same line with no ability word.

Anchored (^…$). Priority 977 — alongside the other replacement rules; the exact phrase cannot be confused with any other static shape.

### `EachControlledMultiSubtypeAnthemAndKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined multi-subtype anthem + keyword grant in the singular "Each creature … that's" relative-clause form, with a TWO-subtype DISJUNCTION qualifier: "Each creature you control that's a [Subtype1] or a [Subtype2] gets +N/+N and has [keyword]." — Brenard, Ginger Sculptor: "Each creature you control that's a Food or a Golem gets +2/+2 and has trample."

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying TWO effects (the MAST multi-effect-per-clause encoding): a `ModifyPTEffect` (+N/+N) and a `GainAbilityEffect` (the keyword), BOTH targeting the same subtype-disjunction-filtered subject. One oracle clause generates one continuous effect from one static ability, so the two effects share a single ability rather than being split into two abilities (CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object. Example: A permanent with the static ability 'All white creatures get +1/+1' generates an effect that continuously gives +1/+1 to each white creature on the battlefield.").

The "that's a [Subtype1] or a [Subtype2]" relative clause qualifies the "creature" noun with a DISJUNCTION on `Subtypes` (OR semantics — CR 205.3: a permanent has zero or more subtypes, so a creature qualifies by having ANY one of the listed subtypes, not all of them): a Food that is not a Golem still gets +2/+2. This mirrors the established multi-subtype-disjunction convention on `MultiSubtypeAnthemModifyPTRule` (Kirri, Talented Sprout's "Plants and Treefolk"). "You control" resolves to the source's controller (CR 109.5). No "other" qualifier is present, so `ExcludeSelf` is left unset (the source is a Human Artificer and never qualifies on its own subtypes, but the rule text does not exclude it either).

The granted keyword is itself a static ability, modelled as a recursive `GainedAbility` via the shared `MapKeywordToStaticAbility` mapping (Trample → CR 702.19). No duration is carried — a static ability's continuous effect lasts as long as the source remains on the battlefield.

Distinct from `TribalAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` (the bare-plural "[Subtype] you control get(s) +N/+N and have [keyword]" form, one subtype, plural subject, no "creature"/"that's" relative clause) and from `EachSupertypeCreatureAnthemModifyPTRule` ("Each [supertype] creature you control gets +N/+N", supertype qualifier, no keyword grant, no disjunction). ANCHORED (^…$) end to end on the singular "Each creature you control that's a X or a Y gets … and has …" surface so it cannot claim a substring of a longer clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EachControlledMultiSubtypeAnthemAndKeywordRule.cs)

### `EachLandIsBasicLandTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the Blanket-of-Night oracle template: a static continuous effect that additively grants a single basic land type to every land, "in addition to its other land types."

Oracle text (verbatim): "Each land is a Swamp in addition to its other land types."

This is a layer-4 (CR 613.1d) continuous type-changing effect. Per CR 305.7: "If a land gains one or more land types in addition to its own, it keeps its land types and rules text, and it gains the new land types and mana abilities." Because the sentence says "in addition to its other land types" (not a bare "is a Swamp"), CR 205.1a governs: the land's prior types are retained and the stated basic land type is appended — an `AddTypeEffect`, never a replacing `SetCardTypesEffect`/`ChangeSubtypeEffect`.

CR 205.1a (verbatim): "Some effects change an object's card type, subtype, and/or supertype but specify that the object retains a prior card type, subtype, and/or supertype. In such cases, all the object's prior card types, subtypes, and supertypes are retained, and the effect causes the object to gain or lose other card types, subtypes, and/or supertypes."

CR 305.6 (verbatim): "The basic land types are Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, and Forest. If an object uses the words 'basic land type,' it's referring to one of these subtypes."

Distinct from `LandsAreEveryBasicLandTypeRule` (Dryad of the Ilysian Grove: a controller-scoped "Lands you control are every basic land type" grant of all five types) and `NonlandCreatureTypeGrantRule` (Ashaya: creatures gain a land card type + subtype). Here the subject is EVERY land (no controller restriction — "Each land") and the granted subtype is a single named basic land type.

ANCHORED (^…$): the full oracle sentence is matched exactly so this rule cannot fire as a substring match against a more specific sibling. Priority 971 — matching the sibling "are every basic land type" shape's priority; the two patterns are mutually exclusive by construction (singular "Each land is" vs. "Lands you control are every basic land type") so there is no collision.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EachLandIsBasicLandTypeRule.cs)

### `EachNonlandGraveyardHasEscapeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the Underworld Breach (THB) two-sentence static paragraph:

"Each nonland card in your graveyard has escape. The escape cost is equal to the card's mana cost plus exile three other cards from your graveyard. (You may cast cards from your graveyard for their escape cost.)"

This is a continuous static ability (CR 604) that grants escape (CR 702.139) to every nonland card in the controller's graveyard, with the escape cost defined as the card's own mana cost plus exiling three other graveyard cards. The parenthetical is standard Escape reminder text (Rule 207.2) and is captured into `Reminder`.

The granted ability is modelled as a `GainAbilityEffect` whose `Target` is each nonland card in your graveyard and whose `GainedAbility` is a `StaticAbility` with `EscapeEffect`. The escape cost's mana half is a `SelfManaCost` (the card's own mana cost — a self-referential reference, not a fixed mana cost); the exile half is represented by `CardsToExile` = 3.

Rule citations: CR 604 (static abilities), CR 702.139 (Escape), CR 202.1 (mana cost), CR 207.2 (reminder text).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EachNonlandGraveyardHasEscapeRule.cs)

### `EachNontokenCreatureSameNameCountAnthemRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

The same-name-count anthem — "Each nontoken creature you control gets +N/+M for each other creature you control with the same name as that creature." (Mirror Box). A per-object continuous effect: every nontoken creature the controller controls is buffed by +N/+M multiplied by the number of OTHER creatures they control that share its name.

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` with a single `ModifyPTEffect`:

`Target` = <c>Kind=Each, Filter={CardTypes:["creature"], IsToken:false, Controller:You}</c> — "each nontoken creature you control" (the token predicate on the first-class `IsToken` boolean, CR 111). `PowerModifier` / `ToughnessModifier` = a `CountQuantity` over "other creature you control with the same name as that creature" — <c>CountOf={CardTypes:["creature"], Controller:You, ExcludeSelf:true, SharesNameWith:{Kind:It}}</c>. The per-item increment of +1 is carried by the count itself (each counted object contributes one), mirroring `EnchantedPTForEachRule`. "the same name as that creature" is the structured relational `SharesNameWith` axis (CR 201.2 — same-name comparison), whose referent "that creature" is the anthem's per-object subject, an anaphoric back-reference mapped to `{Kind:It}` (Rule 109.2 — a pronoun to a previously-mentioned object). "other" (CR 109.5) is the `ExcludeSelf` self-exclusion.

CR 611.3 (a static ability generates a continuous effect); CR 613.4c (layer 7c, P/T-modifying continuous effects). ANCHORED (^…$) on the exact surface so it claims only this clause. Only the +1-per-item increment is handled (higher per-item multipliers are a distinct shape); the rule declines otherwise so a mismatched buff is never emitted.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EachNontokenCreatureSameNameCountAnthemRule.cs)

### `EachOpponentSorcerySpeedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Each opponent can cast spells only any time they could cast a sorcery." — Teferi, Time Raveler and similar effects that restrict opponents to casting spells only at sorcery speed. This is a continuous static effect (CR 604.2 / CR 611.1) that modifies the rules of the game for all opponents: they may only cast spells during their own main phase when the stack is empty, rather than at instant speed.

CR 116.1b: "A player can cast an instant spell any time they have priority. A player can cast a noninstant spell during their main phase when the stack is empty." This restriction locks opponents to the latter (sorcery-speed) window, preventing instant-speed interaction.

Modelled as a `TimingModificationEffect` with `Modification = Restrict` and `Timing = Sorcery`, where `AppliesTo` is a `SpellReference` constraining opponents' spells (`Controller = Opponent`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EachOpponentSorcerySpeedRule.cs)

### `EachSupertypeCreatureAnthemModifyPTRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

The bare supertype anthem in the "Each [supertype] creature you control gets +N/+M." form (Mirror Box: "Each legendary creature you control gets +1/+1."). Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying a single `ModifyPTEffect` whose `Target` is the supertype-filtered subject "[supertype] creatures you control" (<c>Kind=Each, Filter={CardTypes:["creature"], Supertypes:[…], Controller:You}</c>).

CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object": one oracle clause generates one continuous P/T effect from one static ability. The subject's supertype qualifier (e.g. "legendary", CR 205.4a) is recorded on `Supertypes`, NOT as a subtype or name: it categorises the affected objects by supertype.

Distinct from `SupertypeAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` (the "[Supertype] creatures you control get +N/+N and have &lt;keyword&gt;." compound, plural subject + keyword grant) and from `LordPTBuffRule` (which handles the "Other/All &lt;filter&gt; get(s) +N/+M" shapes but recognises neither the leading "Each" quantifier nor the supertype qualifier). ANCHORED (^…$) on the singular "Each [supertype] creature you control gets" surface so it cannot claim a substring of a longer clause (e.g. the "… gets +1/+1 for each …" same-name anthem falls through to its own rule because the trailing text defeats the $ anchor here).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EachSupertypeCreatureAnthemModifyPTRule.cs)

### `EnchantBasicLandTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Enchant Swamp" / "Enchant Island" / etc. — the Enchant keyword ability (CR 702.5) qualified by a single basic land subtype (CR 305.6) rather than the generic "land"/"creature" noun that `EnchantRule` handles. The legal-target descriptor is a basic land TYPE word, not a card-type noun, so it lands on `Subtypes` (CardTypes still records "land").

Canonical corpus: the Kamigawa "Genju" cycle (Genju of the Fens enchants Swamp, siblings enchant the other four basic land types) — "Enchant Swamp\n{2}: ...".

Priority 993 — above `EnchantRule` (992), which returns null for a bare basic-land-type descriptor (only the generic noun set is in its simpleTypes whitelist), so this more specific shape is tried first.

Rule 702.5a: "Enchant [object or player] is a static ability ... that restricts what an Aura ... can legally enchant." Rule 305.6: "The basic land types are Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, and Forest."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EnchantBasicLandTypeRule.cs)

### `EnchantedHasGrantedTriggeredAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"(Enchanted|Equipped) creature has "[quoted TRIGGERED ability]"" — the bare grant (no P/T buff) of a full triggered ability quoted in the Aura/Equipment's oracle text (Sunbond: <c>Enchanted creature has "Whenever you gain life, put that many +1/+1 counters on this creature."</c>). CR 113.3 (an object can gain an ability from an effect) / CR 603.2 (triggered abilities are written "when," "whenever," or "at").

Sibling of `EnchantedPTAndGrantedAbilityRule` (the PT-plus-grant composite shape) and `GrantedAbilityRule` (the generic grant rule, whose `TryParseGrantedBody` dispatches ONLY to `ActivatedAbilityParser`, so it cannot claim a quoted TRIGGERED body). This rule instead dispatches the quoted body to `TriggeredAbilityParser`; when the body isn't a triggered ability this rule returns null so `GrantedAbilityRule`'s activated-ability path continues to own the bare-grant activated-ability shape unchanged.

Priority 996 — one above `GrantedAbilityRule` (995) so this triggered-ability shape is recognised before the generic grant rule (which would otherwise match the same clause, fail to parse the quoted TRIGGERED body via `ActivatedAbilityParser`, and return null — dropping the whole ability to the fallback). When the quoted body is NOT a triggered ability, this rule returns null and `GrantedAbilityRule` picks up the activated-ability case exactly as before — collision-free.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EnchantedHasGrantedTriggeredAbilityRule.cs)

### `EnchantedHasProtectionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Enchanted creature has protection from [quality]." optionally followed by the self-preservation sentence "This effect doesn't remove this Aura."

The protection grant is a static continuous effect (CR 702.16a — protection from a quality). Unlike `EquippedPTAndProtectionRule`, this clause carries no P/T buff — it is the bare grant, so it emits a single `GainAbilityEffect` rather than a `CompositeEffect`.

CR 702.16n: "Some Auras both give the enchanted creature protection from a quality and say 'this effect doesn't remove' either that specific Aura or all Auras. This means that the specified Auras aren't put into their owners' graveyards as a state-based action. If the creature has other instances of protection from the same quality, those instances affect Auras as normal." When present, this trailing sentence is captured as `DoesNotRemoveThisAura` — the faithful encoding of the clause referenced against CR 702.16c (the state-based action it overrides): "A permanent or player with protection can't be enchanted by Auras that have the stated quality. Such Auras attached to the permanent or player with protection will be put into their owners' graveyards as a state-based action."

Priority 969 — one above `EquippedPTAndProtectionRule` (968) so the bare "Enchanted creature has protection from" grant (with no P/T buff prefix) is claimed before any generic keyword-grant splitter gets a chance at it.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EnchantedHasProtectionRule.cs)

### `EnchantedIsCreatureStillTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Enchanted [type] is a [P/T] [colors] [subtype] creature. It's still a [type]." — the Zendikon cycle's "animate the enchanted land" template: a single always-on static continuous effect (CR 613) that turns the enchanted permanent into a fully-specified creature (power/toughness, colors, a creature subtype), while retaining the permanent's prior card type via the trailing "It's still a [type]" sentence (CR 205.1b).

Sibling of `EnchantedIsCreatureWithBasePTRule` (Ensoul Artifact's "...with base power and toughness P/T in addition to its other types" shape) and `AllLandsAreCreaturesStillLandsRule` (Nature's Revolt's "All lands are P/T creatures that are still lands" shape) — all three emit the same `BecomesCreatureEffect` node. This rule differs from both: it states a full color + creature-subtype spec (not just a bare P/T box) inline in the head clause, and states the retention as a SEPARATE trailing sentence ("It's still a land.") rather than an inline "in addition to"/"that are still" clause — the same trailing-retention shape the manland activated animate (`BecomesCreatureEffectRule`) uses, but here unconditional/static (no cost, no "until end of turn" duration) and scoped to the single enchanted permanent (`EnchantedOrEquipped`) rather than the source itself.

<b>"It's still a [type]" retention (CR 205.1b).</b> "Some effects change an object's card type ... but specify that the object retains a prior card type ... This rule applies to effects that ... state that something is 'still a [type...]'." CR 305.7: an animated land "doesn't add or remove any card types ... it keeps its land types." So the retained type (here "land", matching the Aura's own "Enchant land" restriction) sits ahead of the added "creature" in `CardTypes`. The trailing sentence is consumed as confirmation, not emitted as a separate effect.

Canonical card: Vastwood Zendikon — "Enchanted land is a 6/4 green Elemental creature. It's still a land." → Power/Toughness 6/4, Colors ["G"], AddedSubtypes ["Elemental"], CardTypes ["land","creature"].

Anchored (^…$) to the exact "Enchanted [type] is a P/T [spec] creature. It's still a [type]" shape so it cannot collide with `EnchantedIsCreatureWithBasePTRule` (requires the literal "with base power and toughness ... in addition to its other types" wording, absent here) or `EnchantedLandIsSubtypeRule` (a bare "Enchanted land is a(n) [BasicLandType]" subtype declaration, no P/T box).

Rule 613 (Layer System / continuous effects); Rule 205.1b, 205.2 (card types); Rule 208.3 (power/toughness); Rule 105 (color); Rule 305.7 (animated lands retain land types); Rule 303.4c / 702.5 ("enchanted [type]" refers to the attached permanent).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EnchantedIsCreatureStillTypeRule.cs)

### `EnchantedIsCreatureWithBasePTRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Enchanted [type] is a creature with base power and toughness [P]/[T] in addition to its other types." — the Ensoul Artifact "animate the enchanted permanent" template: a single always-on static continuous effect (CR 613) that turns the enchanted permanent into a creature with a fixed base power/toughness box (CR 208.3), while keeping whatever other types it already has.

This is the Aura-scoped sibling of the Nature's Revolt "animate lands" template (`AllLandsAreCreaturesStillLandsRule`): same `BecomesCreatureEffect` node, but here the subject is the single enchanted permanent (`EnchantedOrEquipped`) rather than every land in the game, and the retained type is whatever the Aura's own "Enchant [type]" line restricts it to (here, "artifact") rather than a hardcoded "land". The effect has no stated `Duration` — it is an always-on characteristic-setting static ability (CR 604.1) that lasts as long as the source Aura remains attached (CR 613 layer application while the source persists), not a fixed-length continuous effect.

"in addition to its other types" retention mirrors "that are still lands" in the Nature's Revolt sibling: the enchanted permanent's prior card types (here, "artifact", per the Aura's own "Enchant artifact" restriction) are retained ahead of the added "creature" type in `CardTypes`.

Canonical card: Ensoul Artifact — "Enchanted artifact is a creature with base power and toughness 5/5 in addition to its other types."

Anchored (^…$) to the exact "Enchanted [type] is a creature with base power and toughness P/T in addition to its other types" shape so it cannot collide with the unrelated "[X] in addition to its other types" siblings elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. Raven Wings' "...and is a Bird in addition to its other types", Titan of Littjara's "is the chosen type in addition to its other types") — those grant a single subtype/type addition via `AddTypeEffect`, not a full creature-animate-with-base-P/T composite.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EnchantedIsCreatureWithBasePTRule.cs)

### `EnchantedPTAndGrantedAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"(Enchanted|Equipped) creature gets +N/+M and has "[quoted ability]"" — the P/T buff plus a granted <em>quoted ability</em> (Bear Umbra: <c>gets +2/+2 and has "Whenever this creature attacks, untap all lands you control."</c>). Sibling of `EnchantedPTAndKeywordRule`, which grants a bare <em>keyword</em>; this rule grants the quoted body the Aura confers (CR 303.4 / 702.5 — the enchanted permanent gains the quoted ability).

The quoted body is dispatched to the `TriggeredAbilityParser` first (the recurring Aura shape grants a triggered ability), falling back to the `ActivatedAbilityParser` (mirroring `GrantedAbilityRule`'s hand-off). The self-reference inside the quoted body ("this creature") resolves to the granted ability's own source (CR 109), so it is marked `IsSelf` by `ParseObjectFilter` — NOT to a separate "enchanted creature" filter.

Emits a `CompositeEffect` of [`ModifyPTEffect`, `GainAbilityEffect`] both targeting `EnchantedOrEquipped` — the exact shape of `EnchantedPTAndKeywordRule`, with a parsed ability in place of the keyword's static expansion. Priority 967 (above `EnchantedPTAndDualKeywordRule` at 966 and `EnchantedPTAndKeywordRule` at 965) so the quoted form is recognised before the keyword forms attempt (and fail) to map the quoted body.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EnchantedPTAndGrantedAbilityRule.cs)

The counted set is the relational "attached to it" axis (CR 303/301 Aura/Equipment attachment), and the per-item increment exceeds 1, so the dynamic amount is a `CalculatedQuantity` with a structured `Operand` ("multiply the attached-count by N").

Sibling to `EnchantedPTForEachRule` (which handles the "you control" board count at increment 1) and `SelfPTForEachAuraAttachedRule` (the "This creature" subject). This rule covers the Enchanted/Equipped subject over an attached-to-it relational count at increment &gt; 1.

### `EnchantedPermanentIsVehicleArtifactRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Enchanted permanent is a Vehicle artifact with crew N and it loses all other card types." — the Swift Reconfiguration static ability (Aura from NEO) that transforms any enchanted permanent into a Vehicle artifact and strips its non-artifact card types.

The oracle clause decomposes into three simultaneous continuous effects (all targeting `EnchantedOrEquipped`):

<b>SetCardTypes</b> (layer 4, CR 613.1d) — sets the permanent's card types to `["artifact"]`, which together with "it loses all other card types" establishes the complete type picture. CR 205.2: artifact is a card type. <b>ChangeSubtype</b> (layer 4, CR 613.1d) — sets the permanent's subtype to `["Vehicle"]`. CR 301.7: Vehicle is a subtype of artifact. <b>GainAbility</b> (layer 6, CR 613.1f) — grants `Crew N` (CR 702.122), structured as a `StaticAbility` carrying a `CrewEffect` with the printed power threshold, mirroring the native Crew encoding on Vehicle cards (e.g. Bomat Bazaar Barge, Ripclaw Wrangler).

The parenthetical reminder "(It's not a creature unless it's crewed.)" is stripped by `StripReminderText` before matching. The reminder text is not modelled: the rule engine applies it via CR 702.122a (Crew's becomes-artifact-creature clause). The `Parenthetical` is preserved in the emitted `Reminder` field for round-tripping.

CR 702.122 (Crew): "Crew N" means "Tap any number of other untapped creatures you control with total power N or greater: This permanent becomes an artifact creature until end of turn." CR 301.7 (Vehicles): "Some artifacts have the subtype 'Vehicle.'" CR 205.1a: an effect that sets card types replaces existing types not listed.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EnchantedPermanentIsVehicleArtifactRule.cs)

### `EnterAsCopyRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may have this [permanent] enter as a copy of [filter][, except it's a [Subtype] in addition to its other types]." — the Clone / Glasspool Mimic enter-as-a-copy replacement (CR 707.2). A static/replacement ability that modifies how the permanent enters the battlefield: as it enters, its controller may have it enter as a copy of a qualifying object, optionally with an "except" rider overriding one of the copy's copiable values.

CR 707.2 (verbatim): "When copying an object, the copy acquires the copiable values of the original object's characteristics and, for an object on the stack, choices made when casting or activating it…" — the entering permanent is the copy; no new object is created, so the copy relationship is modelled by `BecomesCopyEffect` (Subject: Self becomes a copy of the chosen object), NOT `CopyEffect` (which creates a NEW token/spell copy).

Decomposition (ADR 0003): timing and effect are separate composable axes. The "as it enters" replacement timing lives on the enclosing `When` = `AsThisEnters` (CR 603.6d/614.1c — a static replacement modifying entry, not a triggered ability); the "may" optionality lives on an `OptionalEffect` wrapper (CR 117.7); the copy relationship lives on the plain `BecomesCopyEffect` inner effect. None of the three axes is baked into another.

The copy target — "any creature on the battlefield" (Clone) or "a creature you control" (Glasspool Mimic) — is an indefinite controller choice (`Any`: not a target, no "target" keyword; CR 115.1), carrying a typed `ObjectFilter` for the object class, zone, and (for the "you control" form) controller. Anchored ^…$ so the surface phrase cannot be matched as a substring inside a more-specific sibling.

Glasspool Mimic's trailing "except it's a Shapeshifter Rogue in addition to its other types" is a `TypeAdder` modification on the `Modifications` list (CR 707.2 copiable values — the except-clause overrides the copy's inherited subtypes without removing them, CR 205.1b). Optional group: Clone's plain form has no except-clause and still matches with a null `Modifications`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EnterAsCopyRule.cs)

### `EntersWithCounterPerFilterRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Name] enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each [filter]." — the per-object-count sibling of `EntersWithCountersRule` (a literal/word/X count) and `EntersWithCountersEqualToManaSpentRule` (a derived mana-spent count). Golgari Grave-Troll: "This creature enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each creature card in your graveyard."

CR 614.12 (verbatim, head): "Some replacement effects modify how a permanent enters the battlefield. (See rules 614.1c-d.) Such effects may come from the permanent itself if they affect only that permanent (as opposed to a general subset of permanents that includes it). They may also come from other sources." The replacement affects only the permanent itself (a self-only "This creature enters with..." reading), so `AsThisEnters` is used, matching `EntersWithCountersRule`'s own citation.

"for each creature card in your graveyard" is modelled as `CountQuantity` — a count of objects matching an `ObjectFilter` — rather than a derived characteristic, since the count is over discrete objects (cards in a zone), not a scalar characteristic of a single object. The filter shape (`CardTypes: ["creature"], Controller: You, Zone: Graveyard`) reuses the same "creature card in your graveyard" convention as `CostReductionForEachRule`'s per-object cost-reduction filter.

The counter placement itself reuses `PutCountersEffect` exactly as `EntersWithCountersRule` does, with `Count` set to the `CountQuantity` instead of a `LiteralQuantity`/`VariableQuantity`.

ANCHORED (^…$) and specific to the "a &lt;counterType&gt; counter on it for each &lt;filter&gt;" surface — the "for each" suffix keeps it disjoint from `EntersWithCountersRule` (anchored to end at "counters? on it") and from `EntersWithCountersEqualToManaSpentRule` (anchored to the "equal to the amount of mana spent to cast it" suffix). Only the single "creature card in your graveyard" filter phrase is recognised today; an unrecognised filter phrase falls through to the unparsed fallback (matching `CostReductionForEachRule`'s own gap-reporting convention) rather than being guessed at. Priority 950 matches the sibling rules' specificity tier.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EntersWithCounterPerFilterRule.cs)

### `EntersWithCountersEqualToManaSpentRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Name] enters with a number of +1/+1 counters on it equal to the amount of mana spent to cast it." — the VARIABLE-count sibling of `EntersWithCountersRule` (Gyrus, Waker of Corpses: "Gyrus enters with a number of +1/+1 counters on it equal to the amount of mana spent to cast it."). `EntersWithCountersRule` only recognises a literal/word count or the bare variable "X"; here the count is instead a DERIVED quantity — "the amount of mana spent to cast it" — so it needs its own matcher rather than an extra alternative on that rule's count group.

CR 614.12 (verbatim, head): "Some replacement effects modify how a permanent enters the battlefield. (See rules 614.1c-d.) Such effects may come from the permanent itself if they affect only that permanent (as opposed to a general subset of permanents that includes it). They may also come from other sources." Gyrus's replacement affects only itself (the self-only `AsThisEnters` family, matching `EntersWithCountersRule`'s own citation), so `AsThisEnters` is used, not the general-subset `AsObjectEnters` shape (`OtherSubtypeEntersWithCounterRule`).

"the amount of mana spent to cast it" is modelled as `ManaSpentToCastQuantity` — the numeric-total sibling of `ManaSpentToCastCondition` (which reads a boolean "was this color spent"). Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): MAST records the reference to the casting event's total mana paid; the engine reads the actual amount at resolution, matching the existing convention for mana-spent facts (CR 601.2f/601.2h — the total cost is determined and paid once, fixing "the amount of mana spent" as a historical fact of the cast).

The counter placement itself reuses `PutCountersEffect` exactly as `EntersWithCountersRule` does, with `Count` set to the derived quantity instead of a `LiteralQuantity`/`VariableQuantity`. The timing wrapper (`AsThisEnters`) and the effect (`putCounters`) stay the same composable nodes as the fixed-count sibling — only the <em>count</em> shape differs.

ANCHORED (^…$) and specific to the "+1/+1 counters ... equal to the amount of mana spent to cast it" surface, so it cannot collide with `EntersWithCountersRule`'s literal/word/X counts or with any other "enters with counters equal to ..." derived-count sibling (e.g. a hypothetical "equal to its power" card, which would need its own `DerivedQuantity` rule). Priority 950 matches `EntersWithCountersRule`'s specificity tier.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EntersWithCountersEqualToManaSpentRule.cs)

### `EntersWithCountersRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EntersWithCountersRule.cs)

### `EquipAbilityYouActivateCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Equip abilities you activate cost {N} less to activate." — a static cost reduction scoped to the CLASS of Equip activated abilities the controller activates (Éowyn, Lady of Rohan; Arms Scavenger; Bureau Headmaster; Fighter Class's level-2 bar). Unlike Strong Back's "Equip abilities you activate <b>that target enchanted creature</b> cost {3} less to activate." (handled by `AppliesToCostReductionRule`), the reference here carries NO target predicate — it applies to every Equip ability the controller activates (the LeoninShikari-style unqualified `ActivatedAbilityReference`).

CR 118.7 (cost reduction): "What a player actually needs to do to pay a cost may be changed or reduced by effects." (CR 118.9 governs ALTERNATIVE costs, not reduction.) CR 702.6 (Equip): the activated ability being reduced is the Equipment's Equip ability. The class of reduced abilities is keyed on the surviving keyword identity (ADR 0003 follow-up 1) via an `ActivatedAbilityReference` with `Equip` and a "you activate" `You` — the exact same reference shape `AppliesToCostReductionRule` builds, minus the `TargetsObject` predicate.

Anchored (^…$) so it matches ONLY the standalone sentence: it cannot fire on Nahiri, Storm of Stone's compound line ("During your turn, creatures you control have first strike and equip abilities you activate cost {1} less to activate.") — that carries a different prefix and is not a bare sentence — and it cannot fire on Strong Back's "…that target enchanted creature…" variant, whose extra clause sits between "you activate" and "cost".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquipAbilityYouActivateCostReductionRule.cs)

### `EquipAbilityYouActivateTargetingSelfCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Equip abilities you activate that target this creature cost {N} less to activate." (Fervent Champion) — a static cost reduction scoped to Equip activated abilities the controller activates that ALSO target the source creature itself. Sibling of `EquipAbilityYouActivateCostReductionRule` (Éowyn, Lady of Rohan's unqualified "Equip abilities you activate cost {N} less to activate.", no target predicate) and `AppliesToCostReductionRule` (Strong Back's "…that target enchanted creature…", a different referent). Here the referent of "this creature" is the source object itself (CR 109.5), so the predicate is a `Self` reference rather than `EnchantedOrEquipped`.

CR 118.7 (cost reduction): "What a player actually needs to do to pay a cost may be changed or reduced by effects." (CR 118.9 governs ALTERNATIVE costs, not reduction.) CR 702.6 (Equip): the activated ability being reduced is the Equipment's Equip ability. Per ADR 0003 follow-up 1, the class of reduced abilities is keyed on the surviving keyword identity via an `ActivatedAbilityReference` with `Equip` and a "you activate" `You`, plus a `TargetsObject` predicate for "that target this creature".

Anchored (^…$) so it matches ONLY the standalone sentence, and requires the literal "that target this creature" clause — it cannot fire on the bare EquipAbilityYouActivateCostReductionRule surface (no target clause) nor on AppliesToCostReductionRule's "…that target enchanted creature…" surface (a distinct referent noun phrase).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquipAbilityYouActivateTargetingSelfCostReductionRule.cs)

### `EquipCostReductionPerOtherEquipmentRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Equip [cost]. This ability costs {N} less to activate for each other Equipment you control." (Plate Armor) — the Equip activated ability (CR 702.6a) plus a self-scoped, scaling cost reduction on that same ability. Both sentences sit in ONE oracle-text paragraph (no line break between them), so `ClauseSplitter` hands the whole thing to this rule as a single clause; the rule returns BOTH abilities the paragraph describes.

CR 118.7 (cost reduction): "What a player actually needs to do to pay a cost may be changed or reduced by effects." Unlike `EquipAbilityYouActivateCostReductionRule` (Éowyn's unqualified "Equip abilities you activate", which reduces EVERY Equip ability the controller activates, including other Equipment's), "This ability" refers only to the Equip ability defined earlier in the SAME sentence — a self-scoped reduction. Per `CostReductionEffect`'s docs, the self-only case leaves `AppliesTo` null (mirrors `PrimevalProtector`'s "This spell costs {1} less to cast for each creature your opponents control.", modeled as its own `StaticAbility` with no `AppliesTo`) rather than referencing `ActivatedAbilityReference` by keyword class.

"For each other Equipment you control" (CR 109.5, "another"/"other" excludes the source) is `ExcludeSelf` combined with the Equipment subtype and `You` — the same shape used for other self-excluding count filters (e.g. "another creature you control").

Both abilities drop their trailing/embedded reminder text (Rule 207.2), matching the sibling convention that bare Equip reminders are not carried into the gold AST (e.g. BrambleArmor's "Equip {4} (reminder)").

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000), which would otherwise match just the "Equip {cost}" prefix (its combinator invocation does not require consuming the clause to end) and silently drop the trailing cost-reduction sentence. Mirrors `ReconfigureStaticRule`'s documented reason for the same priority bump.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquipCostReductionPerOtherEquipmentRule.cs)

### `EquippedCreatureHasQuotedAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Equipped creature has "[quoted ability]"" — grants a quoted activated ability to the equipped creature with no accompanying P/T modifier. Paradigm card: KHM Toralf's Hammer — "Equipped creature has '{1}{R}, {T}, Unattach Toralf's Hammer: It deals 3 damage to any target. Return Toralf's Hammer to its owner's hand.'"

This is a <b>static</b> continuous effect (CR 611.1). The grant persists for as long as the Equipment remains attached — there is no Duration node.

The quoted body is dispatched to `ActivatedAbilityParser` first (the common Equipment grant shape), falling back to `TriggeredAbilityParser`. Returns null (surfacing the gap honestly) when neither recognises the body.

Priority 964 — below `EnchantedPTAndGrantedAbilityRule` (967) and `EquippedPTKeywordAndGrantedAbilityRule` (968) so those compound forms are recognised first. Only the bare "Equipped creature has [quoted]" form falls through to this rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquippedCreatureHasQuotedAbilityRule.cs)

### `EquippedCreaturesHaveKeywordListRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Equipped creatures you control have [keyword1][ and keyword2]." — Dalakos, Crafter of Wonders: "Equipped creatures you control have flying and haste." — a static continuous effect (CR 611.3 (verbatim): "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object. Example: A permanent with the static ability 'All white creatures get +1/+1' generates an effect that continuously gives +1/+1 to each white creature on the battlefield.") granting one or two keyword abilities to every creature the controller controls that currently has an Equipment attached (CR 702.9 Flying / CR 702.10 Haste are both static abilities).

"Equipped" is a permanent STATE (CR 702.6: a creature with an Equipment attached to it is "equipped"), NOT a creature subtype (CR 205.3 lists no such subtype). `SubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordListRule` explicitly declines the capitalised word "Equipped" (alongside "Tapped"/"Enchanted"/"Modified" and others) from its bare subject-capture group precisely so it never shadows this rule — this rule is the sibling that owns that declined shape, mirroring how `TappedStateSubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordRule` owns the "Tapped &lt;Subtype&gt;s …" shape declined by the same guard. The equipped-state predicate is expressed as an `EquippedStateCharacteristic` on the granted-to filter's `Characteristics` — the same mechanism `TappedStateSubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordRule` uses for tapped/untapped, and distinct from `IsEquipped` (which names the specific permanent a SOURCE Equipment is itself attached to, e.g. "whenever equipped creature attacks" printed on an Equipment — Dalakos is a creature, not an Equipment, so it has no such back-reference; it instead quantifies over ANY creature carrying ANY Equipment). MAST describes the printed predicate; the engine evaluates which creatures are actually equipped (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004).

No subtype qualifier — the bare "Equipped creatures you control" shape, unlike a hypothetical "Equipped &lt;Subtype&gt;s you control" sibling. Filter: <c>CardTypes=["creature"], Controller=You, Characteristics=[EquippedStateCharacteristic {Equipped=true}]</c>.

Keyword list: one or two keywords, optionally joined by "and". Per the MAST multi-effect-per-clause doctrine, a two-keyword grant is bundled into a single `StaticAbility` whose `Effects` list carries two independent `GainAbilityEffect` nodes — mirroring `SubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordListRule`'s and `ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule`'s two-keyword grant shape. Each keyword resolves through `MapKeywordToStaticAbility` (read, not modified, by this rule) — "flying" yields the CR 702.9 evasion effect, "haste" the CR 702.10 keyword-ability effect.

Anchored (^…$) pattern with the case-sensitive literal "Equipped" lead-in, so this rule cannot match any other subject shape and cannot be matched as a substring inside a longer clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquippedCreaturesHaveKeywordListRule.cs)

### `EquippedPTAndCantBlockRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses a static Equipment/Aura line of the form "Equipped creature gets +N/+N and can't block."

The P/T modification is a layer-7c continuous effect (CR 613.4c: "Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied."). The blocking restriction is a CR 509.1a constraint (CR 509.1a: "The defending player chooses which creatures they control, if any, will block. The chosen creatures must be untapped and they can't also be battles..."). Both effects are always-on (static, no Duration) and apply to the equipped/enchanted permanent (ObjectReferenceKind.EnchantedOrEquipped).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquippedPTAndCantBlockRule.cs)

### `EquippedPTAndProtectionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Equipped creature gets +N/+M and has protection from [quality] and from [quality]." Also handles the Enchanted form and single-quality protection.

The P/T buff is a layer-7c continuous effect (CR 613.4c). The protection grant is a static continuous effect (CR 702.16 — protection from a quality). Both apply as long as the Aura or Equipment remains attached (static, no Duration).

The protection may be from one or more qualities, each preceded by "from" (or "and from" for additional qualities), e.g. "protection from black and from green" → two Color qualities (B, G).

CR 613.4c: "Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied." CR 702.16a: "Protection is a static ability … this permanent can't be blocked, targeted, dealt damage, enchanted, or equipped by anything [with the quality]."

Priority 968 — above `EnchantedPTAndDualKeywordRule` (966) so the "protection from" phrase is recognised before the dual-keyword rule attempts to split it into two bare keyword names.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquippedPTAndProtectionRule.cs)

### `EquippedPTAndWardRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Equipped creature gets +N/+M and has ward {cost}." — the P/T buff plus a Ward keyword grant (CR 702.21a) on the equipped creature. Sibling of `EnchantedPTAndKeywordRule` (bare bodyless keywords, e.g. trample/flying via `MapKeywordToStaticAbility`): that rule's keyword capture group is letters-only and cannot match a parameterized "ward {N}" phrase, so Ward needs its own rule that builds the full Ward `TriggeredAbility` shape (mirroring `WardKeywordRule`'s mana-cost form) as the granted ability.

CR 702.21a (verbatim): "Ward is a triggered ability. Ward [cost] means 'Whenever this permanent becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, counter that spell or ability unless that player pays [cost].'" CR 613.4c (P/T layer 7c) and CR 613.1f (keyword-ability-grant layer 6) both apply to the equipped creature (CR 702.6, Equipment); MAST records the oracle text descriptively — layer ordering is engine territory.

Priority 969 — just above `EnchantedPTAndKeywordRule` (965) so a future generalisation of that sibling's keyword capture cannot shadow this more specific parameterized-keyword shape. Trailing reminder text (e.g. the Ward reminder parenthetical) is stripped before matching and dropped from the gold AST — Rule 207.2, and matches the convention on sibling bare-grant rules (`StripReminderText`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquippedPTAndWardRule.cs)

### `EquippedPTAsLongAsConditionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Equipped creature gets +N/+M as long as [condition]." — a conditional P/T modifier applied to the equipped creature. Paradigm card: KHM Toralf's Hammer — "Equipped creature gets +3/+0 as long as it's legendary."

This is a <b>static</b> continuous effect with an `AsLongAsDuration`: the P/T modification applies only while the stated condition holds (CR 611.2 — "A continuous effect generated by a static ability has no defined end; it lasts as long as the permanent with that ability remains on the battlefield and the condition holds"). The condition is parsed by `ConditionParser`; conditions not yet structured emit an `OtherCondition` residual.

Emits a single `StaticAbility` with one `ModifyPTEffect` targeting `EnchantedOrEquipped` and an `AsLongAsDuration` carrying the condition. Both the P (power) and T (toughness) modifiers accept a '+'/'-' sign and a digit so "+3/+0" and "+0/+3" round-trip correctly.

Priority 963 — below `EquippedCreatureHasQuotedAbilityRule` (964) and below the existing "Equipped creature gets … and has …" compound rules (965-968) so those more-specific forms are consumed first. Sits above the generic `AsLongAsStaticGrantRule` (968) priority so it is tried before the leading/suffix forms in that rule (which require "it/this creature" as the subject rather than "Equipped creature").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquippedPTAsLongAsConditionRule.cs)

### `EquippedPTKeywordAddTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the compound static Equipment line: "Equipped creature gets +N/+N, has [keyword], and is a [Subtype] in addition to its other types."

Raven Wings is the canonical example: "Equipped creature gets +1/+0, has flying, and is a Bird in addition to its other types." This is a three-part continuous ability:

P/T modification (layer 7c — CR 613.4c) Keyword ability grant (layer 6 — CR 613.1f) Additive subtype gain (layer 4 — CR 613.1d)

All three effects target the equipped creature (`EnchantedOrEquipped`) and persist for as long as the Equipment is attached (no Duration — always-on static).

Unlike `EquippedPTKeywordColorSubtypeRule` (Nim Deathmantle: "...and is a black Zombie."), which REPLACES the color and subtype via `ChangeColorEffect` and `ChangeSubtypeEffect`, this clause has no color and is ADDITIVE ("in addition to its other types"). Per CR 205.1b, "in addition to its other types" means all prior card types, supertypes, and subtypes are retained — so the subtype gain is modeled with `AddTypeEffect`, not a replacing type-change effect.

CR 205.1b (verbatim): "Some effects change an object's card type, supertype, or subtype but specify that the object retains a prior card type, supertype, or subtype. In such cases, all the object's prior card types, supertypes, and subtypes are retained. This rule applies to effects that use phrases such as "in addition to its other types" or that state that something is "still a [type, supertype, or subtype]."

CR 613.1d (verbatim): "Layer 4: Type-changing effects are applied. These include effects that change an object's card type, subtype, and/or supertype."

CR 613.1f (verbatim): "Layer 6: Ability-adding effects, keyword counters, ability-removing effects, and effects that say an object can't have an ability are applied."

CR 613.4c (verbatim): "Layer 7c: Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied."

Rule 702.6 (Equipment): an Equipment's static abilities apply to the equipped creature.

Reminder text is stripped by `StripReminderText` before matching, following the convention of sibling Equipment static rules such as `EquippedPTKeywordColorSubtypeRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquippedPTKeywordAddTypeRule.cs)

### `EquippedPTKeywordAndGrantedAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Equipped creature gets +N/+M and has [keyword] and "[quoted ability]"" — the P/T buff plus a bare keyword grant and a quoted ability grant on the equipped creature.

Canonical example: The Reaver Cleaver — "Equipped creature gets +1/+1 and has trample and 'Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player or planeswalker, create that many Treasure tokens.'" This is a three-part continuous ability:

P/T modification (layer 7c — CR 613.4c) Keyword ability grant (layer 6 — CR 613.1f) — the bare keyword (e.g. trample) Triggered ability grant (layer 6 — CR 613.1f) — the quoted triggered ability

All three effects apply to the equipped creature (`EnchantedOrEquipped`) and are always-on (static, no Duration).

Rule 702.6 (Equipment): an Equipment's static abilities apply to the equipped creature. Rule 613.1 (layer ordering): P/T and keyword/ability grants are applied in strict layer order; MAST records the oracle text descriptively — layer ordering is engine territory.

The quoted body is dispatched to the `TriggeredAbilityParser` first, falling back to `ActivatedAbilityParser`, mirroring the sibling `EnchantedPTAndGrantedAbilityRule`. Priority 968 (above `EnchantedPTAndGrantedAbilityRule` at 967) so the three-part keyword+quoted form is recognised before the two-part quoted form could attempt to match it.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquippedPTKeywordAndGrantedAbilityRule.cs)

### `EquippedPTKeywordColorSubtypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the compound static Equipment line: "Equipped creature gets +N/+N, has [keyword], and is a [color] [Subtype]."

Nim Deathmantle (SOM) is the canonical example: "Equipped creature gets +2/+2, has intimidate, and is a black Zombie." This is a four-part continuous ability:

P/T modification (layer 7c — CR 613.4c) Keyword ability grant (layer 6 — CR 613.1f) Color change to [color] (layer 5 — CR 613.1e) Subtype change to [Subtype] (layer 4 — CR 613.1d)

All four effects target the equipped creature (`EnchantedOrEquipped`) and persist for as long as the Equipment is attached (no Duration — always-on static).

Rule 702.6 (Equipment): an Equipment's static abilities apply to the equipped creature. Rule 613.1 (layer ordering): type, color, and P/T changes are applied in strict layer order; MAST records the oracle text descriptively — layer ordering is engine territory.

Reminder text is stripped by `StripReminderText` before matching, following the convention of sibling Equipment static rules such as `EquippedPTAndCantBlockRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquippedPTKeywordColorSubtypeRule.cs)

### `EquippedSubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Equipped &lt;Subtype&gt;s you control have [keyword]." — Kor Blademaster: "Equipped Warriors you control have double strike." — a static continuous effect (CR 611.3 (verbatim): "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object. Example: A permanent with the static ability 'All white creatures get +1/+1' generates an effect that continuously gives +1/+1 to each white creature on the battlefield.") granting a keyword ability to every creature of the named subtype the controller controls, further restricted to those currently carrying an attached Equipment (CR 702.6).

A "state-qualified subtype anthem": the bare-plural subtype noun ("Warriors") is prefixed by the "Equipped" state adjective rather than immediately following "have". Sibling to `TappedStateSubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordRule` (which owns the same shape for the "Tapped"/"Untapped" state words) and to `SubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordListRule`, which owns "&lt;Subtype&gt; creatures you control have …" (literal "creature(s)" noun after the subtype) and explicitly DECLINES "Equipped" as a captured subtype word (it is a state, not a subtype — CR 205.3 does not list it as a creature type) so it never shadows this rule. This rule requires the state word "Equipped" to come FIRST, followed directly by the bare plural subtype noun (no "creatures" word), so the two rules' anchored patterns are disjoint by construction — neither is a substring match inside the other.

The equipped-state predicate is expressed as an `EquippedStateCharacteristic` on the granted-to filter's `Characteristics` (CR 702.6), the attachment-state analogue of the tap-state `TappedStateCharacteristic` already used by the sibling rule — MAST records only that the granted-to set is scoped to that attachment state; whether any given permanent actually has an Equipment attached is engine territory.

Double strike (CR 702.4) is resolved via the shared keyword map (`StaticRuleHelpers.MapKeywordToStaticAbility`'s "double strike" arm) — read, not modified, by this rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EquippedSubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordRule.cs)

### `EvokeStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes an "Evoke [cost]" oracle line into the two abilities defined by CR 702.74a — a static alternative-cast ability and an ETB-sacrifice triggered ability.

CR 702.74a (verbatim): "Evoke represents two abilities: a static ability that functions in any zone from which the card with evoke can be cast and a triggered ability that functions on the battlefield. 'Evoke [cost]' means 'You may cast this card by paying [cost] rather than paying its mana cost' and 'When this permanent enters, if its evoke cost was paid, its controller sacrifices it.' Casting a spell for its evoke cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h."

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000) so the two-ability decomposition takes precedence over the single-ability keyword combinator path. "if its evoke cost was paid" is the generalized cost-paid reference node `KeywordCostPaidCondition` keyed on Evoke (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004); both abilities carry `Evoke` as their `KeywordSource` (keyword-inherent, mirroring the Reconfigure precedent where both abilities carry their KeywordSource).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/EvokeStaticRule.cs)

### `ExertStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes an Exert paragraph into the two linked abilities defined by CR 701.43d: a static ability (the optional cost to attack) and a triggered ability ("When you do").

CR 701.43d (verbatim): "'You may exert [this creature] as it attacks' is an optional cost to attack (see rule 508.1g). Some objects with this static ability have a triggered ability that triggers 'when you do' printed in the same paragraph. These abilities are linked. (See rule 607.2h.)"

Combat Celebrant's oracle text (with trailing reminder stripped): <c>"If this creature hasn't been exerted this turn, you may exert it as it attacks. When you do, untap all other creatures you control and after this phase, there is an additional combat phase."</c>

Returns two abilities in order:

A `StaticAbility` with `KeywordSource = "Exert"`, a `OtherCondition` capturing the "hasn't been exerted this turn" gate, and an `ExertEffect` recording the optional cost to attack. A `TriggeredAbility` with `KeywordSource = "Exert"`, `Trigger.Event = TriggerEvent.Exerted` ("When you do"), and the combined untap + additional-combat-phase effects.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ExertStaticRule.cs)

### `FaceDownCreatureSpellCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Face-down creature spells you cast cost {N} less to cast." — Obscuring Aether. A cost-reduction static ability (CR 601.2f) scoped to creature spells that are cast face down (CR 708.1: "Some cards allow spells and permanents to be face down.").

CR 118.7: "What a player actually needs to do to pay a cost may be changed or reduced by effects." CR 118.7a: "Effects that reduce a cost by an amount of generic mana affect only the generic mana component of that cost." (Flagging a citation mismatch with the dispatch brief: the brief cited CR 118.9, which per the local comprehensive-rules corpus covers alternative costs, not cost reduction — this rule instead cites CR 118.7, matching the sibling `ColoredCreatureSpellCostReductionRule`'s convention; see worker report.)

Sibling of `ColoredCreatureSpellCostReductionRule` (same `CardTypes=["spell","creature"]` + `Controller=You` shape) but filtered by `IsFaceDown` instead of `Colors`. Anchored (^…$) to prevent false-positive substring matches inside longer oracle lines.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/FaceDownCreatureSpellCostReductionRule.cs)

### `FirstTypeSpellEachTurnCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"The first creature spell you cast each turn costs {2} less to cast." (Shadow in the Warp) — CR 601.2f cost-reduction static ability, scoped to only the FIRST spell of the named type the controller casts in a given turn. Sibling of `TypeSpellCostReductionRule` (same `CostReductionEffect` + `ObjectFilter` shape rooted at `CardTypes: ["spell", &lt;type&gt;]` via `BuildTypeSpellFilter(string)`), but additionally narrowed by an ordinal "first ... each turn" qualifier — the same descriptive occurrence-counting convention `DrawNthCardEachTurnConditionRule` uses on `TriggerCondition.Ordinal`/`PerTurn`, here carried on `Ordinal` (a backward- looking `HistoryPredicate` restricting the filter, CR 601.2f: "the effect that applies while the spell is on the stack"). MAST records which occurrence the oracle text names ("first"); the per-turn tally and resetting are engine territory, not modelled here.

Priority 1002 — above every other cost-reduction rule (max prior priority 1001) so the "The first ..." anchor is tried before any generic type/spell cost-reduction shape could otherwise be reached; the anchored `^…$` pattern with the literal "The first" lead-in and "each turn" tail means it cannot collide with any sibling that lacks both qualifiers.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/FirstTypeSpellEachTurnCostReductionRule.cs)

### `FoodTokenAugmentationReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Token-augmentation replacement effect (Peregrin Took family): "If one or more tokens would be created under your control, those tokens plus an additional Food token are created instead." CR 614.1: A replacement effect watches for a particular event — "If [event] would happen, [modified result] instead" — and modifies that event. The original tokens are still created (`OriginalEventOccurs` is true), and one additional Food token is created alongside them. Distinct from `TokenAugmentationReplacementRule` (Chatterfang family), which adds a creature token matching the count of the original tokens ("that many"), and from `TokenDoublingReplacementRule` (Doubling Season family), which doubles the quantity. This family adds a single named token subtype regardless of the original token count. The trailing parenthetical "(It's an artifact with ...)" is reminder text for the Food token (CR 207.2) and is preserved on `Reminder`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/FoodTokenAugmentationReplacementRule.cs)

### `FoodsHaveActivatedAbilitiesOfExiledCreaturesRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Foods you control have all activated abilities of all creature cards exiled with this creature." — the Hazel's Brewmaster continuous static ability that copies a dynamic set of activated abilities from exiled creature cards onto Foods the controller controls.

<b>CR 613.1f</b> (layer 6 — ability-granting continuous effects): this static ability continuously grants abilities to the target permanents while the source is on the battlefield.

Anchored (^…$) to prevent matching substrings of longer ability lines. Must run before `BareKeywordGrantRule` (which tries to match "Foods you control have …") to claim the more-specific "all activated abilities" surface before the keyword-grant fallback can attempt it. Priority 996 (above BareKeywordGrantRule at 967).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/FoodsHaveActivatedAbilitiesOfExiledCreaturesRule.cs)

### `GainControlOfEnchantedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule
