### `GrantAlternativeCostForAllSpellsRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "You may pay {cost} rather than pay the mana cost for spells you cast." — the Fist of Suns shape: an UNFILTERED grant, applying to every spell the controller casts (as opposed to `GrantAlternativeCostRule`'s Rooftop Storm shape, which restricts the grant to a named type/subtype).

CR 118.9 (verbatim): "Some spells have alternative costs. An alternative cost is a cost listed in a spell's text, or applied to it from another effect, that its controller may pay rather than paying the spell's mana cost. Alternative costs are usually phrased, 'You may [action] rather than pay [this object's] mana cost,' or 'You may cast [this object] without paying its mana cost.'"

The regex is anchored (^…$) — Fist of Suns's full oracle text is a single ability line and no sibling trigger or effect shares this opening. It requires "for spells you cast" to follow "the mana cost" with NO intervening filter noun; that absence is exactly what distinguishes this shape from Rooftop Storm's (whose filter phrase is mandatory in `GrantAlternativeCostRule`'s pattern), so the two rules cannot collide on the same input.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/GrantAlternativeCostForAllSpellsRule.cs)

### `GrantAlternativeCostForThisSpellRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "You may pay {cost} rather than pay this spell's mana cost." — the Verdant Mastery / Bringer cycle shape: a self-referential alternative cost printed on the spell itself, as opposed to `GrantAlternativeCostForAllSpellsRule`'s Fist of Suns shape (a permanent granting the option to every OTHER spell the controller casts) and `GrantAlternativeCostRule`'s Rooftop Storm shape (a permanent granting the option to a filtered class of other spells).

CR 118.9 (verbatim): "Some spells have alternative costs. An alternative cost is a cost listed in a spell's text, or applied to it from another effect, that its controller may pay rather than paying the spell's mana cost. Alternative costs are usually phrased, 'You may [action] rather than pay [this object's] mana cost,' or 'You may cast [this object] without paying its mana cost.'" CR 604.5 confirms these abilities function while the spell itself is on the stack.

Reuses `GrantAlternativeCostEffect` (the Fist of Suns representation) rather than introducing a new discriminator: the only difference is the scope of `AffectedSpells` — here a self-only filter (`IsSelf`, CR 109's "this spell") instead of "spells you cast" or a filtered class thereof. The regex requires "this spell's mana cost" verbatim (not "the mana cost for … spells you cast"), so it cannot collide with either sibling rule's anchored pattern.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/GrantAlternativeCostForThisSpellRule.cs)

### `GrantAlternativeCostRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "You may pay {cost} rather than pay the mana cost for [type] [subtype] creature spells you cast." — the Rooftop Storm shape.

CR 118.9 (verbatim): "Some spells have alternative costs. An alternative cost is a cost listed in a spell's text, or applied to it from another effect, that its controller may pay rather than paying the spell's mana cost. Alternative costs are usually phrased, 'You may [action] rather than pay [this object's] mana cost,' or 'You may cast [this object] without paying its mana cost.'"

The surface phrase "You may pay {0} rather than pay the mana cost for" is fully anchored (^…$) because Rooftop Storm's full oracle text is a single ability line; no sibling trigger or effect shares this opening. The filter noun phrase "<em>subtype</em> creature" (or just "<em>subtype</em>") before "spells you cast" is captured and routed through `BuildTypeSpellFilter(string)` to emit a structured `ObjectFilter`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/GrantAlternativeCostRule.cs)

### `GrantEquipInstantTimingRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may activate equip abilities any time you could cast an instant." — Leonin Shikari. Grants instant-speed timing (CR 601/602 activation timing) to a referenced class of abilities. The affected class is a typed `ActivatedAbilityReference` keyed on the surviving `Equip` identity (ADR 0003): the keyword that survives decomposition is the same identity this timing grant filters on.

Shares the `AbilityReference` value type with `AppliesToCostReductionRule`; here it is carried on `AppliesTo` rather than a cost effect.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/GrantEquipInstantTimingRule.cs)

### `GrantMultipleLoyaltyAbilitiesRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Subject] have [quoted loyalty ability 1] and [quoted loyalty ability 2]." -- grants two loyalty activated abilities to the named permanent type.

Paradigm card: Ichormoon Gauntlet -- "Planeswalkers you control have [0]: Proliferate and [-12]: Take an extra turn after this one."

The quoted bodies use Scryfall bracket-notation loyalty costs: [0], [+N], [-N]. Each body is parsed by stripping the bracket-notation cost, setting `LoyaltyCost` accordingly, and routing the remaining effect text through `ActivatedAbilityParser`.

The output is a single `StaticAbility` whose Effects list contains one `GainAbilityEffect` per granted ability, all sharing the same Target (the filtered subject). This mirrors the multi-effect pattern established by Bloodsworn Steward ("+2/+2 and have haste").

ANCHOR: the full-line regex is anchored (^...$) to prevent matching substrings of longer ability lines. Priority 997 -- fires BEFORE GrantedAbilityRule (Priority 995) so the two-quote form is captured here and not partially matched by the single-quote shape.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/GrantMultipleLoyaltyAbilitiesRule.cs)

### `HistoricSpellCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Historic spells you cast cost {N} less to cast." — the static cost-reduction ability granted by cards like Jhoira's Familiar (DOM). CR 700.6: "The term historic refers to an object that has the legendary supertype, the artifact card type, or the Saga subtype." Historic is a named game quality (not a printed card type or supertype), so the filter uses `IsHistoric` rather than the Supertypes/CardTypes axes. Priority 985 — fires before `TypeSpellCostReductionRule` (priority 984) so the "Historic" token is claimed before the generic single-noun type rule misclassifies it as a creature subtype. The pattern is anchored (^…$) after stripping reminder text; the "Historic" match is case-sensitive (oracle text always uses title case for the quality name) to prevent false positives.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/HistoricSpellCostReductionRule.cs)

### `ImpendingStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes an "Impending N—[cost]" oracle line into the four abilities defined by CR 702.176a (mirroring the `DashStaticRule` / `BuybackStaticRule` multi-ability precedent).

CR 702.176a (verbatim): "Impending is a keyword that represents four abilities. The first is a static ability that functions while the spell with impending is on the stack. The second is static ability that creates a replacement effect that may apply to the permanent with impending as it enters the battlefield from the stack. The third is a static ability that functions on the battlefield. The fourth is a triggered ability that functions on the battlefield. \"Impending N-[cost]\" means \"You may choose to pay [cost] rather than pay this spell's mana cost,\" \"If you chose to pay this permanent's impending cost, it enters with N time counters on it,\" \"As long as this permanent's impending cost was paid and it has a time counter on it, it's not a creature,\" and \"At the beginning of your end step, if this permanent's impending cost was paid and it has a time counter on it, remove a time counter from it.\" Casting a spell for its impending cost follows the rules for paying alternative costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h."

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000) so the four-ability decomposition takes precedence over the single-ability keyword combinator path. The combinator in `ImpendingKeyword` remains live as a fallback, emitting only the primary alternative-cast static ability (the keyword expander returns a single `Ability`; Impending decomposes into four).

The four abilities are modelled by composing existing primitives — no timing is baked into an effect discriminator:

Ability 1: `AlternativeCastEffect` (cast from hand at the impending cost). The interaction-relevant half — a cast permission a flow arm can read. Ability 2: an `AsThisEnters` replacement (CR 614.1c) — a `PutCountersEffect` placing N time counters, gated on the impending cost having been paid (`KeywordCostPaidCondition`). Ability 3: a `LoseTypeEffect` removing the "creature" card type, for as long as (`AsLongAsDuration`) the impending cost was paid AND the permanent has a time counter (`AllCondition` of `KeywordCostPaidCondition` + `ObjectHasCounterCondition`). Ability 4: an end-step `TriggeredAbility` (CR 603.4 intervening-if) removing one time counter (`RemoveCountersEffect`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ImpendingStaticRule.cs)

### `InstantAndSorcerySpellsCantBeCounteredRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Instant and sorcery spells you control can't be countered." — a static continuous effect (CR 611.3: the duration "you control" scopes a continuous effect generated by a static ability) that grants uncounterability to every instant or sorcery spell the controller casts. This is the Sphinx of the Final Word shape, the type-disjunction sibling of `CreatureSpellsCantBeCounteredRule` (creature spells) and Archwing Dragon-style "you control" scoping.

CR 113.6g (verbatim): "An object's ability that states it can't be countered or can't be copied functions on the stack."

The affected objects are instant or sorcery spells on the stack controlled by the source's controller. `CardTypes: ["instant", "sorcery"]` follows the established MAST modeling convention for the "instant and/or sorcery" type disjunction — no separate "spell" entry is needed since instant and sorcery cards only ever exist as spells while eligible to be countered. The `CantBeCounteredEffect` records the restriction; its presence on a `StaticAbility` with `AffectedObjects` scoping to instant/sorcery spells you control is the structured form of this lock.

Priority 972 — same tier as the sibling `CreatureSpellsCantBeCounteredRule`, above `CantBeCastRestrictionRule` (971) and well above the generic counter/spell rules (50–80 band). Anchored (^...$) to prevent substring matches against other static lines.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/InstantAndSorcerySpellsCantBeCounteredRule.cs)

### `IrregularPluralSubtypeAnthemRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Other &lt;IrregularPluralSubtype&gt; you control get +N/+M." — the bare plural-subtype anthem shape (CR 611.3: a static ability generating a continuous +N/+M effect) for creature subtypes whose plural form does NOT end in a literal "s" (Mouse → Mice, Locus → Loci; Djinn is invariant singular/plural — e.g. Mabel, Heir to Cragflame: "Other Mice you control get +1/+1.").

`LordPTBuffRule`'s bare-plural-subtype branch already carries a `_subtypeIrregularPlurals` table with entries for "Mice", "Loci", and "Djinn", but its surrounding regex (`^(?&lt;sub&gt;[A-Z][a-z]+)s$`) requires the whole word to end in a literal "s" before that table is ever consulted. "Elves"/"Dwarves"/"Wolves" satisfy that (they end in "s") and resolve correctly today; "Mice"/"Loci"/"Djinn" do not end in "s" at all, so those three table entries are structurally unreachable in the shared rule. Rather than editing that shared rule body (and risking the sibling shapes it already owns), this is a disjoint, fully-anchored sibling that owns only the irregular no-trailing-s subset; it declines (returns null) for every other bare-plural-subtype shape, which `LordPTBuffRule` continues to own unchanged.

CR 611.3 (static ability generates the continuous effect); CR 109.5 ("another" / "other" — self-exclusion, `ExcludeSelf`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/IrregularPluralSubtypeAnthemRule.cs)

### `IsChosenCreatureTypeInAdditionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"This creature is the chosen type in addition to its other types." — the CONSUMER half of the "As this creature enters, choose a creature type." producer (`ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule`; the Unclaimed-Territory-adjacent "choose a creature type" template, e.g. Titan of Littjara). CR 607.1 linked abilities: "An object may have two abilities printed on it such that one of them causes actions to be taken or objects or players to be affected and the other one directly refers to those actions, objects, or players." — here the producer "chooses" a creature type as the permanent enters and this SEPARATE static ability grants that same creature type to the permanent, additively.

CR 205.1b governs the "in addition to its other types" retention: existing subtypes (and card types) are kept, and the object also gains the new subtype — an additive grant, not a replacement (contrast `ChangeSubtypeEffect`, which SETS/ replaces the subtype for "This creature becomes the creature type of your choice"). The granted value is the chosen characteristic itself (`ChosenSubtypeReference` = `CreatureType`), not a literal subtype string, since the value is only known once the paired as-enters choice resolves.

Sibling of `ChooseCreatureTypeOnEntryRule`: the two regexes are disjoint ("choose a creature type" vs "is the chosen type in addition to its other types"), so dispatch priority relative to that rule is immaterial.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/IsChosenCreatureTypeInAdditionRule.cs)

### `KickedCountEntersWithCountersRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"This [type] enters with a [counterType] counter on it for each time it was kicked." (Skitter of Lizards). The kicked-count-scaled sibling of `EntersWithCountersRule` (a literal/X count): the number of counters is the number of times the spell was kicked, not the article "a".

The count is a `KeywordCostPaidCountQuantity` keyed on `Kicker` — a multikicker cost is a kicker cost, so "for each time it was kicked" references Kicker. Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): the count names the producing keyword's identity, NOT a variable threaded from the Multikicker `AdditionalCastCostEffect` producer on the same card (mirrors CreateTokenRule's Wolfbriar handling of the same "for each time it was kicked" phrase).

Rules: 614.1c (enters-with replacement is a static ability applied as the permanent enters), 702.33d ("If a spell's controller declares the intention to pay any of that spell's kicker costs, that spell has been 'kicked.' If a spell has two kicker costs or has multikicker, it may be kicked multiple times.").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/KickedCountEntersWithCountersRule.cs)

### `KickerConditionalEntersWithCountersAndKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"If this creature was kicked, it enters with N &lt;counterType&gt; counters on it and with &lt;keyword&gt;." — the counters-only sibling (`KickerConditionalEntersWithCountersRule`) extended with a trailing bare-keyword grant, e.g. Pouncing Kavu: "...it enters with two +1/+1 counters on it and with haste."

CR 702.33a/d/e: kicker is a static ability paid as an additional cost while casting; "kicked" is the linked condition an object can later refer to. CR 614.1c: "[This permanent] enters with ..." is a replacement effect (modeled as `AsThisEnters`). CR 122.6: counters granted as an object enters are put on it as part of that replacement. The trailing keyword (e.g. haste, CR 702.10a) is a second, static-ability-scoped effect on the same ability — one oracle sentence, two conjoined effects — not a second ability.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/KickerConditionalEntersWithCountersAndKeywordRule.cs)

### `KickerTapPermanentsStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes a "Kicker—Tap an untapped [Subtype] you control." oracle line (em-dash kicker with a tap-permanents non-mana cost, CR 702.33a) into a single `StaticAbility` carrying an `AdditionalCastCostEffect` with a `TapPermanentsCost`.

CR 702.33a (verbatim): "Kicker is a static ability that functions while the spell with kicker is on the stack. 'Kicker [cost]' means 'You may pay an additional [cost] as you cast this spell.' Paying a spell's kicker cost(s) follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f-h."

The em-dash separator ("Kicker—") is the Wizards printing convention for non-mana kicker costs (e.g. Blood Tribute: "Kicker—Tap an untapped Vampire you control."). The `KickerKeyword` combinator handles the mana-symbol form ("Kicker {cost}") via the tokenised Superpower pipeline; this rule intercepts the em-dash + tap-permanents shape before `KeywordListRule` fires so the full cost is preserved as a typed `TapPermanentsCost`.

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000). The pattern is anchored (^…$) to avoid substring-matching inside a more-specific sibling. Requires the cost phrase to match "Tap an untapped [Subtype] you control" exactly (case-insensitive); the subtype is captured and used as the filter criterion.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/KickerTapPermanentsStaticRule.cs)

### `LandCardsInGraveyardHaveDredgeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the Necrobloom static paragraph: "Land cards in your graveyard have dredge N. ([reminder])"

This is a continuous static ability (CR 604) that grants Dredge N (CR 702.52) to every land card in the controller's graveyard. The parenthetical is standard Dredge reminder text (CR 207.2) and is captured into `Reminder`.

The granted ability is modelled as a `GainAbilityEffect` whose `Target` is each land card in your graveyard (Filter: CardTypes=["land"], Controller=You, Zone=Graveyard) and whose `GainedAbility` is a `StaticAbility` with `DredgeEffect` and `KeywordSource` = "Dredge". Mirrors `EachNonlandGraveyardHasEscapeRule` (Underworld Breach) over the land-type axis and with Dredge in place of Escape.

Rule citations: CR 604 (static abilities), CR 702.52 (Dredge), CR 207.2 (reminder text), CR 404/404.1 (graveyard zone).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/LandCardsInGraveyardHaveDredgeRule.cs)

### `LandTriggerDoublingRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"If a land entering causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time."

This models Ancient Greenwarden's trigger-multiplication static ability — the land-scoped sibling of Panharmonicon (see `PanharmoniconTriggerDoublingRule`, "an artifact or creature entering") and Drivnod (see `DrivnodTriggerDoublingRule`, "a creature dying"). Like both, the effect is a `ReplacementEffect` over an `AbilityTriggerEvent`. The critical difference: Ancient Greenwarden is scoped to triggered abilities whose cause is "a land entering the battlefield" — encoded via `CausedByEntering` with a single-type card-type filter (land).

CR 603.2d (verbatim from rules-structure.json): "An ability may state that a triggered ability triggers additional times. In this case, rather than simply determining that such an ability has triggered, determine how many times it should trigger, then that ability triggers that many times."

`AffectedObjects` (via `AffectedObjects`) = <c>{ CardTypes: ["permanent"], Controller: You }</c> — only triggered abilities of <em>permanents you control</em> are doubled. `CausedByEntering` = <c>{ CardTypes: ["land"] }</c> — only when the entering object was a land.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/LandTriggerDoublingRule.cs)

### `LandsAreEveryBasicLandTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the Dryad-of-the-Ilysian-Grove oracle template: a static continuous effect that additively grants every basic land type to all lands the controller controls, "in addition to their other types."

Oracle text (verbatim): "Lands you control are every basic land type in addition to their other types."

This is a layer-4 (CR 613.1d) continuous type-changing effect. Per CR 305.7: "If a land gains one or more land types in addition to its own, it keeps its land types and rules text, and it gains the new land types and mana abilities." The five basic land types (CR 305.6: Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, Forest) are all granted additively via an `AddTypeEffect` with `AddedSubtypes` containing all five.

CR 305.6 (verbatim): "The basic land types are Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, and Forest. If an object uses the words 'basic land type,' it's referring to one of these subtypes."

CR 305.2 (verbatim): "A player can normally play one land during their turn; however, continuous effects may increase this number." (context for the first ability on the Dryad, handled by `PlayAdditionalLandRule`).

ANCHORED (^…$): the full oracle sentence is matched exactly to prevent this rule from firing on any substring of a more-specific sibling. Priority 971 — above `NonlandCreatureTypeGrantRule` (970) since this shape is dedicated to the "every basic land type" template and the controller-scoped land subject.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/LandsAreEveryBasicLandTypeRule.cs)

### `LandsYouControlEnterUntappedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Lands you control enter untapped." — a static continuous replacement effect (CR 614.1d) that causes all lands the controller controls to enter the battlefield untapped rather than tapped. Canonical card: Spelunking.

CR 614.1d (verbatim): "Continuous effects that read '[This permanent] enters . . .' or '[Objects] enter [the battlefield] . . .' are replacement effects." This oracle sentence matches the second template exactly: "[Lands you control] enter [untapped]." — a replacement that suppresses any tapped-entry for controller-owned lands.

Modelled as a `StaticAbility` with `AsObjectEnters` — the same timing used by the "Creatures your opponents control enter tapped" arm of `EntersTappedRule` — carrying a `UntapEffect` targeting each land the controller controls. The parallel with `EntersTappedRule` is intentional: the structure is "as each [object] enters, [tap/untap] it"; only the direction (untap instead of tap) and the filter (lands you control instead of creatures opponents control) differ.

ANCHORED (^…$): fully anchored to prevent substring-matching any sibling oracle line that mentions lands or untapped. Priority 972 — one above `LandsAreEveryBasicLandTypeRule` (971) so both land-static shapes are tried before the generic fall-through.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/LandsYouControlEnterUntappedRule.cs)

### `LegendRuleSuppressionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"The 'legend rule' doesn't apply." (Mirror Gallery, unscoped) / "The 'legend rule' doesn't apply to creatures you control." (Council of Reeds, scoped to creatures) / "The 'legend rule' doesn't apply to permanents you control." (Mirror Box, scoped to permanents). Rule 704.5j: "If two or more legendary permanents with the same name are controlled by the same player, that player chooses one of them, and the rest are put into their owners' graveyards. This is called the 'legend rule.'" All three surfaces emit a `LegendRuleSuppressionEffect`; the optional trailing "to &lt;noun&gt; you control" clause populates that effect's `Target` with a "&lt;noun&gt; you control" reference (reusing the established <c>Kind=Each, Filter={CardTypes:[…], Controller:You}</c> shape), narrowing the suppression's scope. The noun maps to the corresponding card type — "creatures" → `creature`, "permanents" → `permanent` (the permanent pseudo-type, CR 110.4a). Absence of the clause leaves `Target` null — the original unscoped form. ANCHORED (^…$) so no surface can match as a substring of a broader clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/LegendRuleSuppressionRule.cs)

### `LifeGainAugmentationReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Life-gain augmentation replacement effect (Pest Rescuer): "If you would gain life, you gain that much life plus 1 instead."

CR 614.1 (verbatim): "Some continuous effects are replacement effects. Like prevention effects (see rule 615), replacement effects apply continuously as events happen—they aren't locked in ahead of time. Such effects watch for a particular event that would happen and completely or partially replace it…" This line is therefore a continuous <b>static</b> replacement ability (`Kind: static`), NOT a triggered "whenever you gain life" ability: it watches the life-gain event and increases the amount by a fixed quantity before the gain resolves.

CR 119.3 (verbatim): "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." The replaced event is a `LifeChangeEvent` with `ChangeType = "gain"` for you (`Controller = You`, from "If <b>you</b> would gain life"). The "that much life" clause preserves the original amount, so the original gain still occurs (`OriginalEventOccurs` = true — augmentation, mirroring `SpellCopyAugmentationReplacementRule`'s "that many times plus an additional time"), and "plus 1" is carried as a typed `ReplacementModifier` (`Type = "plus"`, `Amount` a `LiteralQuantity`) rather than baked into the discriminator, so a "plus 2" variant reuses the same shape.

Anchored (^…$); the captured digit is the additive amount. Priority 971 — alongside the other replacement rules; the exact phrase cannot be confused with any other static shape.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/LifeGainAugmentationReplacementRule.cs)

### `LifeGainDoublingReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Life-gain doubling replacement effect (The Wind Crystal): "If you would gain life, you gain twice that much life instead."

CR 614.1 (verbatim): "Some continuous effects are replacement effects. Like prevention effects (see rule 615), replacement effects apply continuously as events happen—they aren't locked in ahead of time. Such effects watch for a particular event that would happen and completely or partially replace it…" This line is therefore a continuous <b>static</b> replacement ability (`Kind: static`), NOT a triggered "whenever you gain life" ability: it watches the life-gain event and replaces it with one for double the amount.

The replaced event is a `LifeChangeEvent` with `ChangeType = "gain"` for you (`Controller = You`, from "If <b>you</b> would gain life"). Unlike the "plus N" augmentation in `LifeGainAugmentationReplacementRule` (where "that much life plus N" preserves the original gain and adds to it, `OriginalEventOccurs = true`), "twice that much life instead" fully replaces the original event with a new one of double the quantity, so `OriginalEventOccurs` = false — mirroring `MillDoublingReplacementRule`/`NoncombatDamageDoublingReplacementRule`'s "twice that many"/"double that damage" shape. The doubling is carried as a typed `ReplacementModifier` (`Type = "double"`), not baked into the discriminator or a free-text description.

Anchored (^…$); a sibling of `LifeGainAugmentationReplacementRule` — the two phrases ("plus N" vs "twice") never overlap as substrings of each other, so this cannot mis-fire on that rule's cards or vice versa. Priority 971 — alongside the other replacement rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/LifeGainDoublingReplacementRule.cs)

### `MarvinHasAllActivatedAbilitiesRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Marvin has all activated abilities of creatures you control that don't have the same name as this creature." — the Marvin, Murderous Mimic continuous static ability that grants all activated abilities from other creatures the controller controls to itself.

<b>CR 613.1f</b> (layer 6 — ability-adding continuous effects): the static ability continuously grants abilities to Marvin while it is on the battlefield.

<b>CR 602.1</b>: "An activated ability is the only kind of ability that can be activated." The class of abilities granted is identified as "activated."

Anchored (^…$) to prevent matching substrings of longer ability lines. The card name prefix ("[Name] has all activated abilities …") is matched by a general pattern so this rule generalises to other mimic-style cards with the same oracle shape. Priority 996 (above generic keyword-grant rules at 967) so this specific shape is claimed before a keyword-grant fallback attempts it.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MarvinHasAllActivatedAbilitiesRule.cs)

### `MaxHandSizeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Your maximum hand size is ten." (The Ten Rings) and its symmetric all-players sibling "Each player's maximum hand size is seven." — Rule 402.2. The numeric-SET sibling of `NoMaxHandSizeRule` ("You have no maximum hand size."): here the size is fixed to a printed number rather than removed. Scopes `Player` to `You` or `EachPlayer` depending on which subject the clause names, mirroring `NoMaxHandSizeRule`'s subject dispatch exactly.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MaxHandSizeRule.cs)

### `MayCastExiledWithSelfRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"During your turn, you may cast cards exiled with [this object] and you may cast them as though they had flash. Mana of any type can be spent to cast those spells." — the persistent play-from-exile permission of a CR 406.6 linked pair (Azula, Cunning Usurper).

This is the second, separate static ability of the linked pair: it refers to "cards exiled with [object]" via the `ExiledWith` reference rather than threading a binding from the exile trigger (ADR 0004 "reference, not resolution"). It is a separate static permission — not a one-shot bundled inside the exile ability — so a window exists (ADR 0004 "topology, not annotation"). A card referring to itself by name resolves to the `Self` source (CR 201.4 self-reference). CR 406.6 (linked exile); CR 702.8 (flash timing).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MayCastExiledWithSelfRule.cs)

### `MayCastFromTopOfLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises "You may cast [X] spells and [Y] spells from the top of your library." and produces a `StaticAbility` with two `MayPlayFromLibraryEffect` instances — one per named eligibility class.

The oracle line is a single sentence but names two disjoint eligibility classes. Each eligibility word maps to an `ObjectFilter` axis: the literal "colorless" → `IsColorless = true` (CR 105.1 — colorless is the absence of any color, so it is a boolean axis rather than a Colors entry); a lowercase card-type word (e.g. "artifact") → `CardTypes = [word]`; a capitalised subtype word (e.g. "Angel", "Human") → `Subtypes = [word]` (CR 205.3m). Mystic Forge ("artifact spells and colorless spells") and Sigarda, Font of Blessings ("Angel spells and Human spells") are both instances of this shape. MAST models these as two sibling `MayPlayFromLibraryEffect` nodes under one `StaticAbility`: the pair expresses "you have permission to cast from the top if the card matches filter A OR filter B". The effects sit on the same ability rather than two separate abilities because the oracle sentence is one continuous permission grant, not two discrete abilities (CR 604.2 — topology not annotation).

CR 604.2: "Static abilities create continuous effects … These effects are active as long as the permanent with the ability remains on the battlefield."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MayCastFromTopOfLibraryRule.cs)

### `MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the Bolas's Citadel two-sentence permission: "You may play lands and cast spells from the top of your library. If you cast a spell this way, pay life equal to its mana value rather than pay its mana cost."

This is a static ability (Rule 604 — continuous effect) that grants two simultaneous permissions: (a) play lands from the top of the library, and (b) cast spells from the top of the library, with (c) an alternative cost rider that replaces the mana cost of any spell cast this way with "pay life equal to its mana value" (CR 118.9b — alternative cost; CR 202.3 — mana value). MAST describes the permission; evaluation of what the top card is at a given moment is engine territory (ADR 0003 describe-not-execute).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryRule.cs)

### `MayPlayLandsAndCastSpellsFromTopOfLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the standalone, unrestricted permission sentence "You may play lands and cast spells from the top of your library." (no card-type/subtype eligibility restriction, and no attached alternative-cost rider) and produces a `StaticAbility` with a `MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryEffect` granting both `PlayLands` and `CastSpells` (Magus of the Future).

This is the same permission grant Bolas's Citadel makes, but printed as a single, standalone sentence with no eligibility restriction and no alternative-cost rider — CR 604.2 (continuous effect from a static ability): "Static abilities create continuous effects … These effects are active as long as the permanent with the ability remains on the battlefield." CR 305.1 and CR 601.2 govern playing lands and casting spells respectively; this ability extends both permissions to cards on top of the library. `SpellAltCost` is left null (no alternative cost applies).

Fully anchored (^…$) so it does not misfire on the Bolas's Citadel two-sentence form ("… from the top of your library. If you cast a spell this way, pay life equal to its mana value rather than pay its mana cost."), which is handled by `MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryRule` and is a single clause containing additional text beyond this shape (oracle clauses are split on newlines, not sentence boundaries, so the Citadel permission + rider sentence remain one clause and this pattern's trailing `$` anchor declines it).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MayPlayLandsAndCastSpellsFromTopOfLibraryRule.cs)

### `MayPlayLandsFromGraveyardRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may play lands from your graveyard." — a static permission granting the controller the ability to play land cards from their graveyard.

CR 305.1: "A player who has priority may play a land card from their hand during a main phase of their turn when the stack is empty. Playing a land is a special action; it doesn't use the stack." This rule extends that permission so eligible land cards may come from the graveyard. The description is static (it persists as long as the source is on the battlefield — CR 604.2); MAST models the permission, not the execution. Crucible of Worlds and Ramunap Excavator share this exact oracle line.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MayPlayLandsFromGraveyardRule.cs)

### `MayPlayLandsFromTopOfLibraryRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "You may play lands from the top of your library." and produces a `StaticAbility` with a `MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryEffect` whose `Actions` list contains only `PlayLands`.

CR 305.2: "A player can normally play one land during their turn; however, continuous effects may increase this number." This rule extends the play-land permission so eligible land cards may come from the top of the library rather than (or in addition to) the hand. The "You may" preamble makes the permission elective — the controller is not required to play lands from the top.

The effect node is `MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryEffect` (not `OptionalEffect` wrapping a separate effect) because "may" is semantically built into the effect type — it is a permission grant, not a wrapped optional action. This follows the same convention as `MayPlayLandsFromGraveyardRule`, which uses `MayPlayFromGraveyardEffect` directly without an `OptionalEffect` wrapper.

The pattern is fully anchored (^…$) so it does not misfire on "You may play lands and cast spells from the top of your library." (Bolas's Citadel), which is handled by `MayPlayFromTopOfLibraryRule` and contains additional text beyond this shape.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MayPlayLandsFromTopOfLibraryRule.cs)

### `MillDoublingReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Mill-doubling replacement effect (Bruvac the Grandiloquent): "If an opponent would mill one or more cards, they mill twice that many cards instead." CR 614.1: replacement effects apply continuously as events happen and watch for a particular event — "If [event] would happen, [modified event] instead" is a replacement, NOT a triggered ability. CR 701.17a: to mill a number of cards is to put that many cards from the top of a library into a graveyard. Structure mirrors `TokenDoublingReplacementRule`/`CounterDoublingReplacementRule`: the replaced event is a `MillEvent` by an opponent ("one or more" → MinimumQuantity 1), and the doubling is a structured `ReplacementModifier{ Type: "double" }` ("twice that many"), not a free-text description. The trailing mill reminder (CR 207.2) carries no rules meaning and is preserved on `Reminder`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MillDoublingReplacementRule.cs)

### `MirranSafehouseGraveyardLandAbilitiesRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"As long as this artifact is on the battlefield, it has all activated abilities of all land cards in all graveyards." — the Mirran Safehouse continuous static ability that grants Self every activated ability belonging to any land card currently sitting in any player's graveyard.

The leading "As long as this artifact is on the battlefield" clause states the default lifespan of any static ability of a permanent (CR 604.2: a permanent's static ability generates a continuous effect that is active only while the source remains on the battlefield with that ability) — it is not modelled as an explicit `Duration`/`Condition`, matching the sibling grant rules (`MarvinHasAllActivatedAbilitiesRule`, `FoodsHaveActivatedAbilitiesOfExiledCreaturesRule`) which carry the same implicit battlefield-scoping without a stated clause at all.

Reuses `HasAllAbilitiesOfControlledCreaturesEffect` — the Marvin, Murderous Mimic node for "[Subject] has all [abilityKind] abilities of [SourceFilter]." That node's `SourceFilter` is a general `ObjectFilter`, not restricted to controlled creatures, so it faithfully carries this card's "all land cards in all graveyards" source set too (`CardTypes=["land"], Zone=Graveyard` — no `Owner`, matching every player's graveyard, per `Terravore`'s identical "land cards in all graveyards" filter shape).

<b>Reference, not resolution (ADR 0004):</b> `SourceFilter` names the class of graveyard cards declaratively; it does not pre-resolve which cards are currently in that set.

<b>CR 113.3</b> (abilities): "Abilities of an object can affect the game in ways other than by generating game actions." Mirran Safehouse's static ability continuously grants Self the class of activated abilities carried by every land card in every graveyard. <br/> <b>CR 602.1c</b>: "An activated ability is the only kind of ability that can be activated."

Anchored (^…$) to prevent matching substrings of longer ability lines. Priority 996, matching the sibling ability-acquisition rules — above the generic keyword-grant fallback (967) so this more specific shape is claimed first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MirranSafehouseGraveyardLandAbilitiesRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTThenExileInsteadReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Target creature gets -N/-M until end of turn. If that creature would die this turn, exile it instead." — the Ob Nixilis's Cruelty family: a P/T-shrinking removal spell whose second sentence installs a linked one-shot death-replacement so the shrunk creature is exiled (not merely killed) if it would die this turn.

CR 614.1: replacement effects watch for a particular event that would happen and completely or partially replace it. CR 614.6: if an event is replaced, it never happens — the modified event (exile) occurs instead. CR 700.4: "dies" means "is put into a graveyard from the battlefield." "That creature" and the trailing "it" are anaphoric back-references to the "target creature" established earlier in the SAME spell's resolution, so both map to `It` — the identical treatment `UntapThatCreatureRule` gives the "that creature" back-reference (same pronoun semantics as "it").

Both sentences live in a single un-split oracle-text clause (no printed line break), and `AbilityClassifier` routes the whole clause to Static because it contains both "would" and "instead" (`ContainsReplacementPattern`) regardless of which sentence they appear in. So the compound two-sentence text arrives here as one `OracleClause`. This rule recognises that compound shape as a unit and emits the two abilities it describes: the P/T-modifying `SpellAbility` (sentence 1) and the linked death-replacement `StaticAbility` (sentence 2) — mirroring `DamageThenExileInsteadReplacementRule` (Incendiary Flow), which differs only in that its first sentence deals damage and its replacement scope is a filter/history predicate rather than an anaphoric reference.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ModifyPTThenExileInsteadReplacementRule.cs)

### `ModularStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes a "Modular N" oracle line into the two abilities defined by CR 702.43a (mirroring the `DashStaticRule` / `ReconfigureStaticRule` multi-ability precedent).

CR 702.43a (verbatim): "Modular represents both a static ability and a triggered ability. 'Modular N' means 'This permanent enters with N +1/+1 counters on it' and 'When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, you may put a +1/+1 counter on target artifact creature for each +1/+1 counter on this permanent.'"

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000) so the two-ability decomposition takes precedence over the single-ability keyword combinator path. The combinator in `ModularKeyword` remains live as a fallback, emitting only the PRIMARY enters-with-counters static ability (the keyword expander returns a single `Ability`; Modular decomposes into two).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/ModularStaticRule.cs)

### `MultiSubtypeAnthemModifyPTRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Multi-subtype tribal anthem, no "creatures" noun (the bare plural subtype nouns themselves stand in for it, same convention as the single-subtype sibling `TribalAnthemModifyPTRule`), with TWO OR MORE subtypes joined by "and": "Other [Subtype1] and [Subtype2] you control get +N/+N." Kirri, Talented Sprout: "Other Plants and Treefolk you control get +2/+0."

CR 611.3 — a continuous effect generated by a static ability. The listed subtypes form a DISJUNCTION on `Subtypes` (OR semantics — CR 205.3: a card/permanent has zero or more subtypes, so a creature qualifies by having ANY one of the listed subtypes, not all of them): a Plant that is not a Treefolk still gets +2/+0. This mirrors the established multi-subtype-disjunction convention elsewhere in the corpus (e.g. `AddManaThenIfSecondTimeRevealUntilRule`'s "an Elf or Elemental card" → `Subtypes: ["Elf","Elemental"]`).

The leading "Other " qualifier (CR 109.5 — "another") sets `ExcludeSelf` = true so the source itself is excluded from its own buff, matching `TribalAnthemModifyPTRule`'s convention. "You control" resolves to the source's controller (CR 109.5).

Each subtype word is depluralised with a conservative trailing-"s" strip (regular plurals like "Plants" → "Plant"); plural-invariant subtypes (e.g. "Treefolk", mirroring "Merfolk"/"Sheep" noted on `TribalAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule`) have no trailing "s" to strip and pass through unchanged.

Distinct from `TribalAnthemModifyPTRule` (exactly ONE subtype, REQUIRES the literal "creatures" word) and from `LordPTBuffRule` (whose bare-plural-subtype branch only recognises a SINGLE trailing subtype word, so it declines — and thus never collides with — this rule's two(+)-word "and"-joined list). ANCHORED (^…$) end to end.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/MultiSubtypeAnthemModifyPTRule.cs)

### `NamedModeGatedAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"• [Name] — [ability]" — one option-labelled ability line of the Believe/Doubt named-mode family (Phenomenon Investigators). The line is an ordinary triggered ability that FUNCTIONS only when the printed option name was the one chosen by the as-enters binder (`ChooseNamedOptionOnEntryRule` / `ChooseNamedOptionEffect`). This rule peels the "• [Name] — " label, recovers the underlying trigger by re-parsing the ability body through `OracleParser` (reusing the existing trigger recognisers — e.g. the "a nontoken creature you control dies" and end-step triggers), builds the mode-specific effects, and couples the whole ability to its option via a `ChosenModeCondition` gate carried in `InterveningIf` (CR 603.4 intervening-if shape; CR 700.2 modal; CR 614.12 choose-on-enter).

Anchored to a leading bullet (U+2022) + a single Capitalised mode word + an em-dash (U+2014): only the unconsumed named-mode option lines reach the static parser in this shape (a "Choose one —" modal card's bullets are consumed into a modal header by the clause splitter and never surface here), so there is no sibling to collide with. The mode-specific effect construction is self-contained (it constructs effects directly rather than delegating to the trigger-effect pipeline, whose sentence-bundle splitter would flatten the "you may … If you do, …" idiom), so this rule affects no other card.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/NamedModeGatedAbilityRule.cs)

"You have no maximum hand size." (Graceful Adept) and its symmetric all-players sibling "Players have no maximum hand size." (Price of Knowledge) — Rule 402.2. Both share the same effect node (`NoMaxHandSizeEffect`); this rule scopes `Player` to `You` or `EachPlayer` depending on which subject the clause names.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/NoMaxHandSizeRule.cs)

### `NonbasicLandsAreBasicLandTypeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the Harbinger-of-the-Seas oracle template: a static continuous effect that SETS every nonbasic land's land type to a single named basic land type.

Oracle text (verbatim): "Nonbasic lands are Islands."

This is a layer-4 (CR 613.1d) continuous type-changing effect. Unlike `EachLandIsBasicLandTypeRule` (Blanket of Night: "Each land is a Swamp <em>in addition to</em> its other land types" — additive, no "in addition" clause here means the land's prior types are replaced, not retained. CR 205.1a: "when an effect sets one or more of an object's subtypes, the new subtype(s) replaces any existing subtypes from the appropriate set (creature types, land types, …)." So this emits a SET `ChangeSubtypeEffect`, never the additive `AddTypeEffect`. Per CR 305.7 the affected lands lose their old land types and rules text and gain the appropriate mana ability for the new basic land type; MAST records the subtype set and leaves that consequence to the engine.

The subject "Nonbasic lands" is scoped on the structured supertype-negation axis (CR 205.4c: "Any land with the supertype 'basic' is a basic land. Any land that doesn't have this supertype is a nonbasic land, even if it has a basic land type."), mirroring `DestroyTargetNonbasicLandEffectRule`'s `CardTypes=["land"]` + `ExcludedSupertypes=["Basic"]` encoding — hence this filter EXCLUDES basic lands from the affected set (unlike the unrestricted "Each land" subject of `EachLandIsBasicLandTypeRule`).

CR 305.6 (verbatim): "The basic land types are Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain, and Forest. If an object uses the words 'basic land type,' it's referring to one of these subtypes."

ANCHORED (^…$): the full oracle sentence is matched exactly so this rule cannot fire as a substring match against a more specific sibling. Priority 971 — matching the sibling "Each land is [type] in addition" shape's priority; the two patterns are mutually exclusive by construction ("Nonbasic lands are" vs. "Each land is … in addition to its other land types") so there is no collision.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/NonbasicLandsAreBasicLandTypeRule.cs)

### `NoncombatDamageDoublingReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Noncombat-damage-doubling replacement effect (Solphim, Mayhem Dominus): "If a source you control would deal noncombat damage to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls, it deals double that damage to that player or permanent instead." CR 614.1a: effects using "instead" are replacement effects. This effect watches for a noncombat-damage event from a source the controller owns and replaces the damage quantity with double. Structure mirrors `MillDoublingReplacementRule`: the replaced event is a `DamageEvent` with Source controlled by You and DamageType "noncombat", directed at an opponent-controlled recipient, and the doubling is a structured `ReplacementModifier{ Type: "double" }` ("double that damage"), not a free-text description. ANCHORED (^...$): the phrase "noncombat damage to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls … double that damage … instead" is highly specific and does not appear as a substring of any other standard oracle-text clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/NoncombatDamageDoublingReplacementRule.cs)

Parses the Ashaya-family oracle template: a static continuous effect that additively grants one or more card types and subtypes to a group of permanents "in addition to their other types."

Handled pattern:

"Nontoken creatures you control are Forest lands in addition to their other types." → `AddTypeEffect` with Target={Each, nontoken creatures you control}, AddedCardTypes=["land"], AddedSubtypes=["Forest"].

CR 205.1a (verbatim): "Some effects change an object's card type, subtype, and/or supertype but specify that the object retains a prior card type, subtype, and/or supertype. In such cases, all the object's prior card types, subtypes, and supertypes are retained, and the effect causes the object to gain or lose other card types, subtypes, and/or supertypes."

### `NontokenCreaturesHaveKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Nontoken creatures you control have [keyword]." — a static continuous effect that grants a keyword ability to every nontoken creature the controller controls. This is the Rhythm of the Wild shape.

CR 702.136a (verbatim): "Riot is a static ability. 'Riot' means 'You may have this permanent enter with an additional +1/+1 counter on it. If you don't, it gains haste.'"

The "nontoken" qualifier maps to `IsToken = false` on the `ObjectFilter` (CR 111.1: a token is not a card). The grant is a continuous effect with no explicit duration — a static ability's continuous effect lasts for as long as the source remains on the battlefield.

Priority 969 — above `BareKeywordGrantRule` (967) so this more-specific nontoken-scoped shape fires before the broader filter arm would mis-match "Nontoken creatures" as a subtype "Nontoken". Anchored pattern prevents substring matches against more-specific siblings.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/NontokenCreaturesHaveKeywordRule.cs)

### `ObjectActivatedAbilityCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Static cost-reduction ability that lowers the activation cost for all activated abilities belonging to a category of permanents the controller controls, with an optional mana floor.

Canonical pattern (Forensic Gadgeteer, CR 602.1): "Activated abilities of `ObjectFilter` you control cost {N} less to activate[. This effect can't reduce the mana in that cost to less than one mana]."

CR 602.1c: "An activated ability is the only kind of ability that can be activated." The reference here is to all activated abilities on permanents matching the type filter, not to a specific keyword's activated ability (contrast `AppliesToCostReductionRule` which keys on a keyword identity). Encoded as `PermanentFilter` on a `CostReductionEffect`.

The optional trailing sentence "This effect can't reduce the mana in that cost to less than one mana." becomes `MinimumManaCost` = 1.

### `OpponentArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Activated abilities of artifacts your opponents control can't be activated." — Karn, the Great Creator's static ability. A continuous restriction (CR 604.2 / CR 611.1) that prevents any activated ability on an artifact controlled by an opponent from being put on the stack (CR 602.5: "A player can't begin to activate an ability that's prohibited from being activated.").

Modelled as a `StaticAbility` whose `AffectedObjects` is an `ObjectFilter` scoping the restriction to artifacts controlled by opponents (`CardTypes=["artifact"], Controller=Opponent`), and whose `Effects` list contains a single `CantActivateAbilitiesEffect` with no `Target` (the affected-objects filter on the ability already names the locked objects). This matches the pattern used for global activation locks (cf. `EnchantedCantAttackOrBlockRule` for the per-Aura form where Target is set to `EnchantedOrEquipped`).

The pattern is anchored (^…$) so it cannot fire as a substring of a longer clause such as a reminder parenthetical.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/OpponentArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule.cs)

### `OpponentCreaturesActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Activated abilities of creatures your opponents control can't be activated." — Linvala, Keeper of Silence's static ability. A continuous restriction (CR 602.5c: activation is prohibited by a static ability) that prevents any activated ability on a creature controlled by an opponent — including mana abilities, since the oracle text carries no "unless they're mana abilities" carve-out — from being put on the stack.

Modelled as a `StaticAbility` whose `AffectedObjects` is an `ObjectFilter` scoping the restriction to creatures controlled by opponents (`CardTypes=["creature"], Controller=Opponent`), and whose `Effects` list contains a single `CantActivateAbilitiesEffect` with no `Target` (the affected-objects filter on the ability already names the locked objects) and no `ExceptManaAbilities` (unset — the lock is total, unlike the Pithing Needle / Sorcerous Spyglass mana-ability carve-out). Mirrors `OpponentArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` with a creature-scoped filter in place of the artifact-scoped one.

The pattern is anchored (^…$) so it cannot fire as a substring of a longer clause such as a reminder parenthetical, and is disjoint from the artifact-scoped and chosen-name-scoped templates.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/OpponentCreaturesActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule.cs)

### `OpponentsCantCastDuringYourTurnRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Your opponents can't cast spells during your turn." (Dragonlord Dromoka) — a continuous static cast prohibition (CR 601.3a: a spell can't be cast if doing so would violate a rule or effect that says a player can't cast a spell) scoped two ways at once: WHO is prohibited (a player class — "your opponents") and WHEN the prohibition is in effect (a timing window — "during your turn").

Reuses `CantBeCastEffect` (the existing cast-prohibition node, already established by `CantBeCastRestrictionRule` for the mana-value and {X}-in-cost shapes on Gaddock Teeg) rather than inventing a new effect: the WHO half is expressed the same way those siblings express "which spells" — via the enclosing `AffectedObjects` filter, here scoped by `Controller` = `Opponent` (a spell's controller is the player casting it, CR 108.4a) rather than by card type/mana-value characteristics.

The WHEN half reuses the established "during your turn" timing qualifier — an `OtherCondition` carrying the verbatim phrase "During your turn" (the same PB-7 structured-condition bucket `SelfKeywordDuringTurnSuffixRule` uses for Razorkin Needlehead's "This creature has first strike during your turn.") on `Condition`, produced via the shared `ConditionParser` entry point rather than hand-built.

Anchored (^…$) so the subject phrase "Your opponents can't cast spells" cannot match as a substring of a more specific sibling static line.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/OpponentsCantCastDuringYourTurnRule.cs)

### `OpponentsCantCastOrActivateDuringYourTurnRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"During your turn, your opponents can't cast spells or activate abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments." (Myrel, Shield of Argive) — a continuous static prohibition scoped two ways at once, mirroring `OpponentsCantCastDuringYourTurnRule`: WHO is prohibited (a player class — "your opponents") and WHEN the prohibition is in effect (a timing window — "during your turn"), except the timing qualifier LEADS the sentence here rather than trailing it, and the sentence bundles TWO prohibitions joined by "or" rather than one.

CR 601.3a: a spell can't be cast if doing so would violate a rule or effect that says a player can't cast a spell. CR 602.5c: a player can't begin to activate an ability that's prohibited from being activated. Both halves are therefore emitted as TWO separate `StaticAbility` nodes sharing the same "During your turn" `Condition` rather than one ability with two effects: each prohibition scopes a DIFFERENT class of affected objects (spells vs. artifacts/creatures/enchantments) via `AffectedObjects`, and that filter lives once per ability — it cannot carry two different `CardTypes` sets at once.

Cast half reuses `CantBeCastEffect` exactly as `OpponentsCantCastDuringYourTurnRule` does: the WHO half rides on `Controller` = `Opponent` (a spell's controller is the player casting it, CR 108.4a), with `CardTypes=["spell"]`.

Activate half reuses `CantActivateAbilitiesEffect` exactly as `OpponentArtifactsActivatedAbilitiesLockedRule` does for Karn, the Great Creator's single-type form: `CardTypes=["artifact","creature","enchantment"]` (OR semantics per CR 115.3, mirroring `ReturnUpToOneTargetTypeDisjunctionToHandEffectRule`'s established type-disjunction convention) with `Controller=Opponent` — the default activator of a permanent's activated ability is its controller (CR 602.5c), so scoping the affected permanents to those opponents control is the structural equivalent of restricting the opponents themselves as actors, exactly as the cast half does for spells.

Both abilities carry the same "During your turn" `OtherCondition` (the same PB-7 structured-condition bucket `SelfKeywordDuringTurnSuffixRule` and `OpponentsCantCastDuringYourTurnRule` use), produced via the shared `ConditionParser` entry point.

Anchored (^…$) so the subject phrase cannot match as a substring of a more specific sibling static line.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/OpponentsCantCastOrActivateDuringYourTurnRule.cs)

### `OpponentsCreaturesCantHaveOrGainKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Creatures your opponents control lose &lt;keyword&gt; and can't have or gain &lt;keyword&gt;." — the Archetype-cycle opponent ability-lock (e.g. Archetype of Imagination's "lose flying and can't have or gain flying").

Per CR 113.11 the "can't have" construct DEFINES the loss as well: "These effects say that the object 'can't have' that ability. If the object has that ability, it loses it. It's also impossible for an effect or keyword counter to add that ability to the object." So "lose flying and can't have or gain flying" is ONE continuous effect (a can't-have lock), captured by a single `CantHaveOrGainKeywordEffect` — the removal is subsumed, not double modelled. CR 611.3 is the static-ability continuous-effect authority.

The keyword is recognised by REUSING `MapKeywordToStaticAbility` and lifting its `KeywordSource` so unrecognised keywords return null (dispatch keeps cascading — no false parse). Priority 985 is very specific; the anchored pattern guards against sibling shadowing.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/OpponentsCreaturesCantHaveOrGainKeywordRule.cs)

### `OtherChosenTypeAnthemModifyPTRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Other creatures you control of the chosen type get +X/+Y." — the creature-source sibling of `ChosenTypeAnthemModifyPTRule` (Adaptive Automaton shape, e.g. paired with "As this creature enters, choose a creature type." and "This creature is the chosen type in addition to its other types."). CR 613.1: an object's characteristics are recomputed in layers, the anthem being a P/T-modifying continuous effect scoped by the creature type chosen as this permanent entered.

The "of the chosen type" clause is the structured consumer half of a CR 607 linked ability — CR 607.1: "An object may have two abilities printed on it such that one of them causes actions to be taken or objects or players to be affected and the other one directly refers to those actions, objects, or players." The producer is the "choose a creature type" effect under `StaticAbility.When = AsThisEnters`. It is encoded with the structured `ChosenCharacteristic` = `CreatureType` reference, never free-text.

Distinct from `ChosenTypeAnthemModifyPTRule`: that rule's source is a noncreature permanent (e.g. an enchantment), so it never appears in its own affected set and no "Other " prefix is printed. Here the source IS a creature (and per `IsChosenCreatureTypeInAdditionRule` is itself the chosen type), so the printed "Other " prefix excludes it from its own anthem (CR 611.3; `ExcludeSelf` = true) — mirrors `TribalAnthemModifyPTRule`'s "Other [Subtype] creatures" shape but with a runtime-chosen subtype instead of a printed one.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/OtherChosenTypeAnthemModifyPTRule.cs)

### `OtherCreaturesAreSubtypeAndHaveAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the Ygra-family static ability template: "Other creatures are [Subtype] [card-types] in addition to their other types and have &quot;[quoted activated ability]&quot;."

This oracle template combines a layer-4 additive type grant (CR 205.1a) with a layer-6 ability grant (CR 613.1f) in a single printed sentence. MAST represents this as ONE `StaticAbility` carrying two effects in order:

`AddTypeEffect` — grants the named card types and subtypes. `GainAbilityEffect` — grants the quoted activated ability.

Both effects share the same target filter ("Other creatures" = all creatures excluding the source, `ExcludeSelf` = true, no controller restriction — this affects ALL creatures on the battlefield except the source).

Example oracle text: "Other creatures are Food artifacts in addition to their other types and have &quot;{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this permanent: You gain 3 life.&quot;" (Ygra, Eater of All, BLB).

CR 205.1a (verbatim): "Some effects change an object's card type, subtype, and/or supertype but specify that the object retains a prior card type, subtype, and/or supertype." CR 613.1d (layer 4 — type-changing effects), CR 613.1f (layer 6 — ability-granting). CR 111.10b: "A Food token is a colorless Food artifact token with '{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: You gain 3 life.'" (The CR definition of the Food subtype.)

Priority 968 — below the controller-scoped type-grant rules (969–970) and above the fallback anthem rules so this dedicated shape fires before the generic type-grant rules decline it (they require "you control"). Anchored (^…$) to prevent substring overlap.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/OtherCreaturesAreSubtypeAndHaveAbilityRule.cs)

### `OtherSubtypeEntersWithCounterRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Each other [Subtype] creature you control enters with an additional [counter] counter on it." — a static continuous replacement effect (CR 614.1d) applying to a class of OTHER permanents (a filtered subtype) as each one enters, rather than to the source permanent itself. Canonical card: Oona's Blackguard.

CR 614.12 (verbatim, head): "Some replacement effects modify how a permanent enters the battlefield. (See rules 614.1c-d.) Such effects may come from the permanent itself if they affect only that permanent (as opposed to a general subset of permanents that includes it). They may also come from other sources." Here the source (this permanent, Oona's Blackguard) grants the replacement to a GENERAL SUBSET of permanents (other Rogues the controller controls) — not to itself — so this is `AsObjectEnters` (CR 614.1d's "[Objects] enter . . ." template), distinct from the self-only `AsThisEnters` family handled by `EntersWithCountersRule`. The timing qualifier and the counter-put effect remain separate composable nodes: the "when" (as each matching object enters) lives on `When`, never baked into the effect.

The subject noun phrase "each other [Subtype] creature you control" decomposes onto the effect's `Target` filter exactly like the analogous triggered-side tribal shapes (mirrors `OtherSubtypePumpTriggeredRule`): `Subtypes` for the capitalised creature subtype (CR 205.3m), `Controller` = You, and `ExcludeSelf` = true for the "other" self-exclusion (CR 109.5) — the source permanent's own entry is not affected by its own replacement. The counter is put via the existing `PutCountersEffect` node (Count = 1, CounterType as printed); "additional" describes that the counter stacks with any other counter-granting replacement rather than requiring a separate AST flag (mirrors `UnleashStaticRule`'s "an additional +1/+1 counter" reading).

New, collision-free file. ANCHORED (^…$) so it cannot steal any sibling oracle line; requires the literal "Each other" self-exclusion prefix and a capitalised subtype token, so it is disjoint from the self-only "[This/Name] enters with . . ." family (`EntersWithCountersRule`) and from the unfiltered "[Objects] enter [tapped/untapped]" mass shapes (`LandsYouControlEnterUntappedRule`, the opponents-creatures arm of `EntersTappedRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/OtherSubtypeEntersWithCounterRule.cs)

### `PanharmoniconTriggerDoublingRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"If an artifact or creature entering causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time."

This models Panharmonicon's trigger-multiplication static ability. Like Echoes of Eternity (see `TriggerDoublingStaticRule`), the effect is a `ReplacementEffect` over an `AbilityTriggerEvent`. The critical difference: Panharmonicon is scoped to triggered abilities whose cause is "an artifact or creature entering the battlefield" — encoded via `CausedByEntering` with a two-type card-type filter.

CR 603.2d (verbatim from rules-structure.json): "An ability may state that a triggered ability triggers additional times. In this case, rather than simply determining that such an ability has triggered, determine how many times it should trigger, then that ability triggers that many times."

`AffectedObjects` = <c>{ CardTypes:["permanent"], Controller: You }</c> — only triggered abilities of <em>permanents you control</em> are doubled. `CausedByEntering` = <c>{ CardTypes: ["artifact", "creature"] }</c> — only when the ETB entering object was an artifact or creature.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/PanharmoniconTriggerDoublingRule.cs)

### `PartyCostReductionForEachRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "This spell costs {N} less to cast for each creature in your party." (Deadly Alliance, ZNC) — the party cost-reduction ability introduced by the party mechanic. CR 700.8: "Some cards refer to a player's party. A player's party consists of up to one Cleric creature that player controls, up to one Rogue creature they control, up to one Warrior creature they control, and up to one Wizard creature they control." The "up to one each of the four classes, capped at four" counting is engine territory (descriptive-not-engine doctrine); the AST records only the filter phrase "creature in your party" via `InParty`. The printed line always carries a trailing reminder-text parenthetical ("(Your party consists of up to one each of Cleric, Rogue, Warrior, and Wizard.)") per Rule 207.2; it is stripped before matching so the anchored end-of-string pattern still matches. Priority 989 — fires before the generic `CostReductionForEachRule` (priority 987), which matches clause.RawText directly (without stripping reminder text) and would otherwise capture the whole reminder parenthetical into its filter-phrase group as an unrecognised phrase.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/PartyCostReductionForEachRule.cs)

### `PayLifeForColoredManaRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses the K'rrik, Son of Yawgmoth static ability: "For each {X} in a cost, you may pay N life rather than pay that mana."

This is a continuous static permission (CR 604) that allows the controller to substitute N life for each instance of the named mana color in any cost. The mechanic is a generalization of the Phyrexian mana rule (CR 107.4f) applied universally to all costs paid by the controller rather than only to Phyrexian mana symbols on the card itself.

Pattern: "For each {COLOR} in a cost, you may pay N life rather than pay that mana." Anchored (^…$) to prevent substring matches in sibling trigger/effect contexts. No other static rule in the registry matches this surface phrase — the anchor is belt-and-suspenders against future rules that happen to contain the words "life" and "cost" (the #1 FAIL class per the vertical-slice contract).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/PayLifeForColoredManaRule.cs)

### `PermanentTriggerDoublingRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"If a permanent entering causes a triggered ability of a permanent you control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time."

This models Yarok, the Desecrated's trigger-multiplication static ability — the any-permanent-scoped sibling of Ancient Greenwarden (see `LandTriggerDoublingRule`, "a land entering"), Panharmonicon (see `PanharmoniconTriggerDoublingRule`, "an artifact or creature entering"), and Drivnod (see `DrivnodTriggerDoublingRule`, "a creature dying"). Like all three, the effect is a `ReplacementEffect` over an `AbilityTriggerEvent`. The distinguishing scope: Yarok doubles triggered abilities caused by ANY permanent entering the battlefield — encoded via `CausedByEntering` with the unrestricted "permanent" card-type filter.

CR 603.2d (verbatim from rules-structure.json): "An ability may state that a triggered ability triggers additional times. In this case, rather than simply determining that such an ability has triggered, determine how many times it should trigger, then that ability triggers that many times."

`AffectedObjects` (via `AffectedObjects`) = <c>{ CardTypes: ["permanent"], Controller: You }</c> — only triggered abilities of <em>permanents you control</em> are doubled. `CausedByEntering` = <c>{ CardTypes: ["permanent"] }</c> — any permanent entering (not scoped to a specific card type).

### `PreventAllDamageToCreaturesYouControlStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Prevent all damage that would be dealt to creatures you control." (Inner Sanctum) — a permanent, always-on damage-prevention shield scoped to every creature the controller controls, from any source (no "by [source]" qualifier). Sibling of `PreventAllDamageToSelfByCreaturesStaticRule` (which shields only "this creature" and only from creature sources); here the protected class is a filtered set ("creatures you control") and the shield is unconditional on source.

CR 615.1 (cited verbatim): "Some continuous effects are prevention effects. Like replacement effects (see rule 614), prevention effects apply continuously as events happen-they aren't locked in ahead of time. Such effects watch for a damage event that would happen and completely or partially prevent the damage that would be dealt. They act like \"shields\" around whatever they're affecting." CR 615.1a: "Effects that use the word \"prevent\" are prevention effects." CR 604.2 (cited verbatim): "Static abilities create continuous effects, some of which are prevention effects or replacement effects. These effects are active as long as the permanent with the ability remains on the battlefield and has the ability, or as long as the object with the ability remains in the appropriate zone, as described in rule 113.6."

Structure: a `StaticAbility` whose sole effect is a direct `PreventDamageEffect` with `All=true` and `Target` = an unbound `Each` reference filtered to `CardTypes=["creature"], Controller=You` ("creatures you control"). No `Source` restriction (unlike the "by creatures" sibling) — the shield blocks damage regardless of origin. No `Duration`: an always-on static ability that persists while the permanent remains on the battlefield (CR 604.2), so it carries no stated duration.

ANCHORED (^…$, well, `^…\b` at the classifier and full-line here): the template is matched in its entirety so it cannot fire as a substring of a broader clause, and cannot claim a substring of the "this creature by [source]" sibling's distinct wording.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/PreventAllDamageToCreaturesYouControlStaticRule.cs)

Such effects watch for a damage event that would happen and completely or partially prevent the damage that would be dealt. They act like \"shields\" around whatever they're affecting."
