### `RevealOrEntersTappedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Reveal-or-enters-tapped land ("Snarl" cycle, Strixhaven): "As this land enters, you may reveal a [TypeA] or [TypeB] card from your hand. If you don't, this land enters tapped."

Modelled descriptively as the checkland/fastland shape — the composite "as this enters, tap it" (`When = StaticTimingKind.AsThisEnters` on the `StaticAbility`, a plain `TapEffect` targeting self) gated by `Condition`. The condition names the predicate under which the land enters UNtapped (the controller revealing a qualifying card): the land enters tapped whenever that does not happen. The "you may reveal" choice is recorded as the condition's text rather than as a game action — MAST describes the card, it does not execute the reveal (descriptive-not-engine doctrine).

The reveal is a pure entry gate carrying no quantified resource, so it collapses cleanly onto the `Condition` axis. This differs from the painland/shockland template (`PainlandRule`) where the optional action is a life payment — a quantified cost that warrants its own `PayLifeEffect`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/RevealOrEntersTappedRule.cs)

### `SelfIsAlsoSubtypesRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[CardName] is also a [Subtype], [Subtype], ... and [Subtype]." — the self-by-name creature-subtype-addition static template (e.g. Tajuru Paragon: "Tajuru Paragon is also a Cleric, Rogue, Warrior, and Wizard.").

CR 205.1b (verbatim): "Some effects change an object's card type, supertype, or subtype but specify that the object retains a prior card type, supertype, or subtype. In such cases, all the object's prior card types, supertypes, and subtypes are retained, and the effect causes the object to gain or lose other card types, subtypes, and/or supertypes." CR 205.3: creature subtypes appear after a long dash on the type line and are drawn from the creature-type list. "Is also a" is the additive phrasing WotC uses for this grant — unlike "becomes a" or "is a" (which would replace the subject's subtypes), "also" signals the listed subtypes are gained IN ADDITION TO the subject's printed subtypes (no subtype is lost).

This is the self-by-name sibling of `NonlandCreatureTypeGrantRule` (which handles the "in addition to their other types" phrasing over a group of permanents): both emit `AddTypeEffect`, but this rule's subject is always the named source card itself (CR 201.5 — a card's own name in its own text means that object), so the target is `Self` rather than an `Each` group reference, and only subtypes (never card types) are granted by this surface phrase.

Anchored (^…$) to the full clause so this cannot match as a substring of a broader sentence, and requires the literal "is also a[n]" connective — no sibling static rule in this parser shares that exact connective, so this pattern is disjoint from every other registered rule. Default priority (50): the anchoring makes the exact value non-load-bearing.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfIsAlsoSubtypesRule.cs)

### `SelfKeywordDuringTurnSuffixRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"This creature has [keyword] during your turn." — the SUFFIX-condition form of a conditional self-keyword ability (CR 702.7 for first strike, etc.). The condition phrase "during your turn" follows the keyword statement rather than preceding it, which differs from the PREFIX form handled by `ConditionalSelfKeywordRule` ("During your turn, this creature has [keyword]").

Razorkin Needlehead is the canonical example: "This creature has first strike during your turn." produces the same AST as Fresh-Faced Recruit's prefix form "During your turn, this creature has first strike." — a `StaticAbility` with `KeywordSource` set and an `OtherCondition` carrying "During your turn" (PB-7 structured-condition bucket; the turn-phase condition is entangled with the reference-not-resolution engine contract).

CR 702.7a: "First strike is a static ability that modifies the rules for the combat damage step." The condition "during your turn" limits when this static ability is in effect.

ANCHOR note: the regex is anchored (^…$) — the subject phrase "this creature" / "this permanent" cannot appear as a substring inside a more-specific sibling trigger or effect clause. The condition phrase "during your turn" is equally anchored to the END of the clause after the keyword, preventing false positives on cost-reduction clauses like "this spell costs {1} less to cast during your turn" (which start with "this spell costs", a distinct prefix).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfKeywordDuringTurnSuffixRule.cs)

### `SelfLoyaltyAbilityInstantTimingStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"You may activate loyalty abilities of [Self-name] on any player's turn any time you could cast an instant." — Teferi, Master of Time. A static ability on a planeswalker that relaxes the loyalty-ability activation timing restriction (CR 606.3) specifically for <em>this</em> planeswalker, granting instant-speed activation on any player's turn.

CR 606.3 (verbatim): "A player may activate a loyalty ability of a permanent they control any time they have priority and the stack is empty during a main phase of their turn, but only if no player has previously activated a loyalty ability of that permanent that turn."

This static ability removes the "during a main phase of their turn" restriction for this planeswalker specifically. The "any player's turn" and "any time you could cast an instant" clauses together grant timing equivalent to instant-speed on any turn, recorded as `WhoseTurn` = "AnyTurn" and `Timing` = `Instant`. The `AppliesTo` is keyed on `ObjectActivatedAbilityReference` with `IsSelf` = true — restricting the grant to this permanent's own loyalty abilities.

ANCHORED (^...$): the phrase "loyalty abilities" could appear in other static ability text. The self-reference pattern ("of [word(s)]") is specific enough that anchoring is the primary guard, but the IsSelf filter in the output also isolates this rule to self-referencing planeswalker forms. Priority 989 — precedes generic timing-grant rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfLoyaltyAbilityInstantTimingStaticRule.cs)

### `SelfNameEntersPreparedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Name] enters prepared." — the bare self-by-name prepared-designation static ability printed on the front face of prepare-layout double-faced cards that name themselves rather than using "This creature" (e.g. "Sanar enters prepared."). Sibling of `SelfNameEntersTappedRule` for the self-by-name convention; the "This creature enters prepared." form is already recognised by `PreparedKeyword`'s token-level combinator (dispatched via `KeywordListRule`), which cannot match a literal card name since the tokenizer has no access to it. This rule closes that gap with the same regex-on-raw-text technique used for the enters-tapped self-by-name sibling.

CR 722.3a: "Some spells and abilities cause a permanent with a prepare spell to become prepared or state that a permanent enters prepared. If that permanent has the alternative characteristics of a prepare spell, this gives the permanent the 'prepared' designation. Prepared is a designation that acts as a marker which rules and effects can identify."

Produces the identical `StaticAbility` shape as `PreparedKeyword`'s expansion (`KeywordSource = Prepared`, a single `KeywordAbilityEffect`) so the two recognition paths ("This creature enters prepared." vs. "[Name] enters prepared.") stay indistinguishable downstream.

Anchored (^…$) immediately after "enters prepared." (with an optional trailing reminder parenthetical) so this cannot steal a substring of a longer clause. A negative lookahead excludes a leading "This" so this rule stays disjoint from `KeywordListRule`'s "This creature enters prepared." shape even if dispatch order ever changes; the required "enters" (with the s) restricts to the singular self form.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfNameEntersPreparedRule.cs)

### `SelfNameEntersTappedDoesntUntapRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Name] enters tapped and doesn't untap during your untap step." — the compound static restriction printed on Grimgrin, Corpse-Born and similar permanents that name themselves rather than using "This [type]".

Produces two `StaticAbility` nodes from one oracle sentence:

`AsThisEnters` + `TapEffect` targeting `Self` — the entry-tapped replacement (CR 603.6d: "Such text is a static ability—not a triggered ability—whose effect occurs as part of the event that puts the permanent onto the battlefield."). `DoesntUntapEffect` with `WhoseUntapStep = "your"` — the continuous skip-untap effect (CR 502.3: "effects can keep one or more of a player's permanents from untapping.").

Priority 963 — just above `EntersTappedRule` (Priority 962) so this compound form is matched first; both rules handle different surface shapes (self-by-name compound vs. "This [type] enters tapped" simple). Pattern is anchored (^…$) so it cannot consume a plain "enters tapped" clause that the `EntersTappedRule` already handles correctly.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfNameEntersTappedDoesntUntapRule.cs)

### `SelfNameEntersTappedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Name] enters tapped." — the bare self-by-name entry-tapped static ability printed on permanents that name themselves rather than using "This [type]" (e.g. "Winter Soldier enters tapped.").

CR 603.6d: "Some permanents have text that reads ... '[This permanent] enters tapped.' Such text is a static ability-not a triggered ability-whose effect occurs as part of the event that puts the permanent onto the battlefield."

CR 614.1d: "Continuous effects that read '[This permanent] enters . . .' or '[Objects] enter [the battlefield] . . .' are replacement effects."

Priority 960 — below the more specific enters-tapped rules (`RevealOrEntersTappedRule` = 961, `EntersTappedRule` = 962, `SelfNameEntersTappedDoesntUntapRule` = 963, `EntersTappedWithCountersRule` = 964) so those specific shapes are matched first; this general self-by-name form only fires as the fallthrough for a bare "enters tapped." with no unless/counters/doesn't-untap/reveal tail. The pattern is anchored (^…$) immediately after "enters tapped." so it cannot steal any of those other shapes, and the required "enters" (with the s) excludes the plural other-permanent "…enter tapped" form.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfNameEntersTappedRule.cs)

### `SelfNamePTForEachCounterYouHaveRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Name] gets +N/+M for each [counterType] counter you have." — a self-anthem scaled by a player-owned (not permanent-owned) counter count (Kalemne, Disciple of Iroas: "Kalemne gets +1/+1 for each experience counter you have."). CR 611.3 (a static ability that sets or modifies power/toughness); CR 122 (counters — CR 122.1 counters may be placed on a player, not only an object; CR 122.1 experience counters specifically).

Self-by-name sibling of `SelfPTForEachRule` (which is anchored to "This creature gets…"): legendary creatures frequently name themselves instead, mirroring the `SelfName*` convention used elsewhere (e.g. `SelfNameEntersTappedDoesntUntapRule`). Distinct from `SelfPTForEachRule`'s "&lt;counterType&gt; counter on it" phrase (a permanent-owned `CounterCountQuantity` with `Self`): "counter … you have" is a player-owned counter count, so `On` is `You` instead.

Priority 973 — just below `SelfPTForEachRule` (974); the two patterns are disjoint (one requires the literal "This creature", the other a capitalised card name) so ordering between them is not load-bearing, but the tier mirrors the sibling rule's specificity. Fully anchored (^…$) so it cannot substring-match a differently-shaped sibling clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfNamePTForEachCounterYouHaveRule.cs)

### `SelfPTAsLongAsConditionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"This creature gets -N/-M as long as [condition]." — a conditional P/T modifier applied to the source permanent itself (self subject). Paradigm card: CLB Halam Djinn — "This creature gets -2/-2 as long as red is the most common color among all permanents or is tied for most common."

This is a <b>static</b> continuous effect with an `AsLongAsDuration`: the P/T modification applies only while the stated condition holds (CR 604.2 — static abilities create continuous effects that are active as long as the permanent with the ability remains on the battlefield and has the ability). The -N/-M is a layer-7c modification (CR 613.4c). The condition is parsed by `ConditionParser`; conditions not yet structured emit an `OtherCondition` residual.

A near-verbatim sibling of `EquippedPTAsLongAsConditionRule`, differing only in the subject ("This creature/permanent" instead of "Equipped creature") and the target (`Self()` instead of `EnchantedOrEquipped`). Emits a single `StaticAbility` with one `ModifyPTEffect`. Both the P and T modifiers accept an explicit '+'/'-' sign, so "-2/-2" round-trips.

Priority 964 — deliberately BELOW the generic `AsLongAsStaticGrantRule` (968), whose self-P/T pattern hard-requires '+' signs and therefore declines the negative form. This rule claims only that negative self form that currently falls through; the generic rule keeps first crack at the positive/ability-word self forms it already handles. The pattern is end-anchored (^…$) so it cannot steal a longer clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfPTAsLongAsConditionRule.cs)

### `SelfPTForEachAuraAttachedRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"This creature gets +N/+N for each Aura attached to it." — the Kor Spiritdancer family. Distinct from `SelfPTForEachRule` in two ways: (1) the counted set is "Aura attached to it" (an attachment relationship, not a "you control" board count), and (2) the per-Aura increment may exceed 1 (Spiritdancer is +2/+2 per Aura), which `SelfPTForEachRule` explicitly defers to a "distinct family shape" by returning null on multiplier &gt; 1.

The dynamic amount is "N × (number of Auras attached)". A per-each increment of 1 reuses a bare `CountQuantity` (matching the single-increment convention); an increment &gt; 1 wraps that count in a `CalculatedQuantity` with `Operation = "multiply"`, mirroring the established CalculatedQuantity-wrapping convention (e.g. the "negate" wrapper in `ActivatedRuleHelpers.ParseSignedModifier`). No new `Quantity` subtype is introduced — both discriminators (`count`, `calculated`) already exist.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfPTForEachAuraAttachedRule.cs)

### `SelfPTForEachRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfPTForEachRule.cs)

### `SelfRegenerateOnDestructionReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"If this creature would be destroyed, regenerate it." — an unconditional, permanent self-regeneration replacement (Clergy of the Holy Nimbus). CR 614.1 (replacement effect): "If [event] would [happen], [alternative] instead." The stated event is the object's own destruction; the stated alternative is the keyword action "regenerate" (CR 701.19), which itself creates the standard regeneration shield (remove damage, tap, and — if attacking/blocking — remove from combat) rather than letting the destruction occur.

Modeled with the existing replacement primitives — `ReplacementEffect` over a `DestructionEvent` (`AffectedObjects.IsSelf = true`) with `OriginalEventOccurs = false` ("regenerate it" supplants the destruction entirely, mirroring how `SelfWouldBePutIntoGraveyardExileInsteadRule` models "exile it instead") and a `RegenerateEffect` (Target = Self) as the replacement action — reusing the same node the activated/spell "Regenerate this creature." rules already emit, per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine (MAST records the effect's presence, not the shield-creation machinery).

Anchored (^…$) to the exact "this creature would be destroyed, regenerate it" clause shape so it cannot collide with other "would be destroyed" replacement phrasings elsewhere in the corpus (e.g. Umbra armor's "If enchanted creature would be destroyed, instead remove all damage from it and destroy this Aura.", which names a different subject and a different replacement action).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfRegenerateOnDestructionReplacementRule.cs)

### `SelfWouldBePutIntoGraveyardExileInsteadRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"If [Name] would be put into a graveyard from anywhere, exile it instead." — the standard self-by-name replacement clause printed on the back face of every Disturb double-faced card (CR 702.146a family; e.g. Luminous Phantom), preventing the transformed permanent from ever returning to the graveyard.

CR 614.1 (replacement effect): "If [event] would [happen], [alternative] instead." Modeled with the existing replacement primitives — `ReplacementEffect` over a `ZoneChangeEvent` (destination graveyard, origin left unset since "from anywhere" names no specific origin zone) with `OriginalEventOccurs = false` ("instead") and an `ExileEffect` as the replacement action. The subject is the card's own printed name, resolved to `IsSelf`/`Self` — the same self-by-name resolution used by `SelfNameEntersTappedRule` for "[Name] enters tapped.".

Anchored (^…$) on the exact clause shape so it cannot collide with the differently- worded exile-instead replacements elsewhere in the corpus ("would die this turn, exile it instead" — `ModifyPTThenExileInsteadReplacementRule` / `DamageThenExileInsteadReplacementRule`; "is countered this way, exile it instead of putting it into its owner's graveyard" — the counter-replacement rules): those require a preceding "this way"/"this turn" antecedent clause this pattern does not have, and this pattern requires the "from anywhere" zone-origin phrase they don't have.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SelfWouldBePutIntoGraveyardExileInsteadRule.cs)

### `SetBasePTRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"(Enchanted|Equipped) creature has base power and toughness N/M." — a layer-7b continuous effect (CR 613.4: "Layer 7b: Effects that set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value are applied.") from an Aura's or Equipment's own static ability that overwrites the attached creature's base P/T box with a fixed value. Anchored tightly (no trailing "until end of turn"/"and gains ..." clause, no "target creature" subject) so it only recognises the plain always-on Aura/ Equipment shape — corpus-swept against every "has base power and toughness" surface (Reduce in Stature, Illusory Wrappings, Belt of Giant Strength, and the Wicked half of Wicked // Cursed all share this exact anchored line; every other "base power and toughness" card in the corpus carries additional clauses/subjects this pattern deliberately does not match).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SetBasePTRule.cs)

### `SiegeReminderStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Standalone Siege type-reminder line, identical on every "Battle — Siege" front face (the March-of-the-Machine Invasions): "(As a Siege enters, choose an opponent to protect it. You and others can attack it. When it's defeated, exile it, then cast it transformed.)".

Emits a `StaticAbility` carrying a field-less `SiegeEffect` marker, with the verbatim parenthetical preserved on `Reminder` via the existing reminder mechanism (CR 207.2 — italic text with no game function). This honors no-silent-drop: the recognized reminder is captured, not discarded, and the marker gives it a structured host that anchors the Siege mechanic on the card's rules text.

MAST describes, it does not execute. The defeat → exile → cast-transformed life cycle (CR 310.7 — a battle with defense 0 leaves the battlefield as a state-based action) and the casting of a battle as a spell (CR 310.1) are engine territory, summarized in the captured reminder rather than modeled. The Siege's defense value is absent from the MAST `Input`, so it is out of scope.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SiegeReminderStaticRule.cs)

### `SkipDrawStepRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Skip your draw step." — a continuous static replacement effect (Symbiotic Deployment). CR 614.10 (verbatim): "An effect that causes a player to skip an event, step, phase, or turn is a replacement effect. \"Skip [something]\" is the same as \"Instead of doing [something], do nothing.\" Once a step, phase, or turn…" — so "Skip your draw step" is modeled as a `ReplacementEffect` over the typed draw step (`TurnPartEvent` with `Draw`), with `OriginalEventOccurs = false` and no `Replacement` ("do nothing"). CR 500.10 (turn-structure context) frames the draw step as the skipped part of the turn. It is a static replacement, not an activated or triggered ability.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SkipDrawStepRule.cs)

### `SkipUntapRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SkipUntapRule.cs)

### `SpellCopyAugmentationReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"If you would copy a spell one or more times, instead copy it that many times plus an additional time. You may choose new targets for the additional copy." — Twinning Staff's spell-copy augmentation static ability.

CR 707.10: "To copy a spell, activated ability, or triggered ability means to put a copy of it onto the stack; a copy of a spell isn't cast…" This replacement effect intercepts any event where the controller would copy a spell one or more times and adds one additional copy to that total. The original copies still occur (`OriginalEventOccurs` = true); the modifier (Type = "plusOne") specifies one extra copy beyond the original count. The retarget permission (`MayChooseNewTargets = true`) applies specifically to the additional copy, not the original copies.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SpellCopyAugmentationReplacementRule.cs)

### `SpellTypeListHaveKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "Instant and sorcery spells you control have [keyword]." — a static continuous effect (CR 611.3: "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object.") granting a keyword ability to a filtered class of the controller's OWN spells while they sit on the stack (Soulfire Grand Master: "Instant and sorcery spells you control have lifelink.").

`CardTypes = ["spell", "instant", "sorcery"]` is the established MAST convention for the "instant and sorcery spell" type-disjunction on a stack object: identical to the filter `CastOrCopyInstantOrSorceryConditionRule` and `NextCastCopySpellDelayedRule` already emit for "an instant or sorcery spell", and parallel to `CreatureSpellsCantBeCounteredRule`'s `["spell", "creature"]` (a single type appended to the "spell" marker). "you control" is <c>Controller = You</c> — CR 109.4 controller of an object on the stack.

Reuses `GainAbilityEffect` targeting an `Each`-kinded reference over the spell filter, mirroring the "&lt;filter&gt; you control have [keyword]" family (`ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule`, `SubtypeTokensHaveKeywordRule`): the grant is CR 611.1's "continuous effect [that] modifies characteristics of objects" for as long as this ability's source remains on the battlefield (CR 604.2). Lifelink itself is CR 702.15a: "Lifelink is a static ability."

Anchored (^…$) to the exact "Instant and sorcery spells you control have [keyword]." surface, so it cannot fire as a substring of a broader clause or collide with a sibling anthem over a different subject noun (permanents, tokens, creatures). Priority 973 — same band as the sibling filter-scoped keyword-grant rules (`ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule`), well above the unfiltered `BareKeywordGrantRule` (967).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SpellTypeListHaveKeywordRule.cs)

### `SpellsCastFromGraveyardCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Spells you cast from your graveyard cost {N} less to cast." — a static cost reduction (CR 601.2f) scoped to the controller's spells whose zone of origin is their own graveyard (Patrician Geist).

The affected-objects filter is <c>CardTypes=["spell"], Controller=You, Zone=Graveyard</c>: a spell's current zone is always the stack (CR 111.6/109.5), so on a `CardTypes=["spell"]` filter `Zone` is unambiguous shorthand for the pre-cast origin zone (see that property's doc-comment, and `ExcludedZone`'s parallel negative case). This is the POSITIVE counterpart of `SpellsCastFromNonHandZoneCostReductionRule` (Savvy Trader's "from anywhere other than your hand", which negates via `ExcludedZone`); here the origin zone is named directly rather than excluded. Sibling of `TypeSpellCostReductionRule` (same `CostReductionEffect` + `AffectedObjects` shape), scoped by cast-zone rather than a type/color adjective.

Anchored (^...$) to the exact "Spells you cast from your graveyard cost {N} less to cast." surface so it cannot fire as a substring of a differently-scoped cost-reduction sibling. CR 601.2f (verbatim, excerpt): "If the object any part of this cost is paid with is defined ... the total cost is used to determine the legality of the spell's being cast and is the amount of resources that will actually be spent when the spell is cast. ... Some effects instruct a player to add or subtract an amount from the total cost of a spell rather than modify the mana cost..."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SpellsCastFromGraveyardCostReductionRule.cs)

### `SpellsCastFromNonHandZoneCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Spells you cast from anywhere other than your hand cost {N} less to cast." — a static cost reduction (CR 601.2f) scoped to the controller's spells whose zone of origin is anything BUT hand (Savvy Trader).

The affected-objects filter is <c>CardTypes=["spell"], Controller=You, ExcludedZone=Hand</c>: a spell's current zone is always the stack (CR 111.6/109.5), so the printed "from anywhere other than your hand" clause names the pre-cast origin zone, not the spell's present location — the negative counterpart of `ExcludedZone`'s spell-filter special case (see its doc-comment). Sibling of `TypeSpellCostReductionRule` (same `CostReductionEffect` + `AffectedObjects` shape), but scoped by cast-zone rather than a type/color adjective.

Anchored (^...$) to the exact "Spells you cast from anywhere other than your hand cost {N} less to cast." surface so it cannot fire as a substring of a differently-scoped cost-reduction sibling. CR 601.2f (verbatim, excerpt): "If the object any part of this cost is paid with is defined ... the total cost is used to determine the legality of the spell's being cast and is the amount of resources that will actually be spent when the spell is cast. ... Some effects instruct a player to add or subtract an amount from the total cost of a spell rather than modify the mana cost..."

### `SpellsTargetingCostMoreRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SpellsTargetingCostMoreRule.cs)

### `SpreeModeRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"+ [cost] — [effect]" — one selectable mode of a <b>Spree</b> spell (CR 702.172a: "Spree is a static ability found on some modal spells (see rule 700.2) … 'Spree' means 'Choose one or more additional costs.'"). Each printed mode line pairs an additional cost ("+ {1}") with an effect ("Destroy target artifact."); the caster chooses one or more modes and pays each chosen mode's cost as an additional cost to cast the spell.

The clause splitter emits the leading "Spree (…)" keyword line as its own `StaticAbility` (recording the "choose one or more" selection) and each "+ [cost] — [effect]" paragraph as a separate clause that classifies as static and reaches this rule. This rule peels the "+ [cost] — " prefix, parses the cost with `ManaCostParser`, and recovers the mode's effect by re-parsing the label-stripped body through the full pipeline (reusing the existing effect recognisers — the destroy and put-counter rules), emitting a `SpreeModeAbility`.

Anchored to a leading "+" plus one-or-more brace-wrapped cost symbols and an em-dash (U+2014): only the Spree mode lines surface in this shape, so there is no sibling to collide with. Declines (returns null) when the body fails to parse to a spell effect, leaving the gap visible rather than emitting a malformed mode.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SpreeModeRule.cs)

### `SquadStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes a "Squad [cost]" oracle line into the two linked abilities defined by CR 702.157a (mirroring the `DashStaticRule` / `ReconfigureStaticRule` multi-ability precedent).

CR 702.157a (verbatim): "Squad is a keyword that represents two linked abilities... 'Squad [cost]' means 'As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may pay [cost] any number of times' and 'When this creature enters, if its squad cost was paid, create a token that's a copy of it for each time its squad cost was paid.'"

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000) so the two-ability decomposition takes precedence over the single-ability keyword combinator path. The combinator in `SquadKeyword` remains live as a fallback, emitting only the primary additional-cost static ability (the keyword expander returns a single `Ability`; Squad decomposes into two).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SquadStaticRule.cs)

### `StrivePerTargetCostIncreaseRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"This spell costs [cost] more to cast for each target beyond the first." — the Strive pattern (Kiora's Dismissal, Kiora's Follower's cycle mates, etc.). Strive is an ability word (CR 207.2c: ability words "have no special rules meaning and no individual entries in the Comprehensive Rules"; the "Strive —" prefix is decorative and carries no semantics of its own), so the operative rules text is the plain static sentence this rule matches — the "Strive —" lead-in is stripped as prose, mirroring how ability-word preambles (Landfall, Raid, …) are dropped elsewhere.

CR 601.2f: "The total cost is the mana cost or alternative cost … plus all additional costs and cost increases, and minus all cost reductions." The tax is self-referential (the spell taxes only itself as it's cast, unlike the permanent-taxes-other-spells shapes on the sibling `CostIncreaseEffect` rules), so no `AffectedObjects`/`TargetedObject`/`CasterFilter` is set — `PerTargetBeyondFirst` carries the "for each target beyond the first" scaling instead.

The extra cost is generalized via `ManaCostParser` (any combination of generic and colored symbols — {U}, {G}, {1}{U}, {2}{B}, …): the generic component sums into `Amount` and any non-generic symbols are carried verbatim in `ManaSymbols`, mirroring the split `ColoredSpellCostIncreaseRule` already uses so colored mana is never flattened to generic (CR 601.2's Altar's Reap example distinguishes {B} from {1}).

Anchored (^…$) to prevent false-positive substring matches inside longer oracle lines. Target selection itself is not modeled (out of scope per the family brief).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/StrivePerTargetCostIncreaseRule.cs)

### `SubjectDoesntUntapDuringControllersUntapStepsRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"[Lands/Creatures/Artifacts/Permanents] don't untap during their controllers' untap steps." — a static continuous effect (CR 502.3) that suppresses the untap-step untapping of an entire class of permanents, regardless of who controls them or the ability's source. Canonical card: Hokori, Dust Drinker.

Distinct from `DoesntUntapRule`'s self-reference and enchanted/equipped forms: those key the affected object off the ability's own source ("This [type]" / "Enchanted [type]"), a single object. This rule keys the affected object off a bare card-type noun with no controller qualifier — the effect applies to every permanent of that type, across every player's battlefield — so the subject is modelled as an `ObjectReference` with `Each` over an unqualified `CardTypes` filter, not a single `Self`/ `EnchantedOrEquipped` target.

Generalizes over the subject noun (Lands / Creatures / Artifacts / Permanents) — the four card types that commonly carry this template — rather than a card-literal or "Lands"-literal regex, so a sibling like "Creatures don't untap during their controllers' untap steps." is covered by the same rule.

Also generalizes over the five basic land SUBTYPES (Islands / Swamps / Plains / Mountains / Forests), which key an unqualified `Subtypes` filter rather than `CardTypes` — mirroring how "Destroy all Islands." models its target as `Subtypes:["Island"]` with no card-type filter. Canonical card: Choke ("Islands don't untap during their controllers' untap steps.").

Also generalizes over an optional leading COLOR qualifier on the four card-type nouns — "Red creatures don't untap during their controllers' untap steps." (Wrath of Marit Lage) — which adds an `Colors` constraint alongside the `CardTypes` filter rather than replacing it, mirroring how "Destroy target green or white creature." keys `Colors` and `CardTypes` together on one filter (CR 105). The color qualifier does not apply to the basic land subtype forms (a bare land subtype like "Islands" carries no color axis of its own).

CR 502.3 (verbatim): "Third, the active player determines which permanents they control will untap. Then they untap them all simultaneously. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack. Normally, all of a player's permanents untap, but effects can keep one or more of a player's permanents from untapping."

ANCHORED (^…$): the full oracle sentence is matched exactly so this rule cannot fire on a substring of a more specific sibling clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SubjectDoesntUntapDuringControllersUntapStepsRule.cs)

### `SubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordListRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "&lt;Subtype&gt; creatures you control have [keyword1][ and keyword2]." (Cloudshredder Sliver: "Sliver creatures you control have flying and haste.") — a static continuous effect (CR 604.2: "Static abilities create continuous effects … These effects are active as long as the permanent with the ability remains on the battlefield.") granting one or two keyword abilities to every creature of the named subtype the controller controls (CR 702.9 Flying / CR 702.10 Haste are both static abilities).

Sibling to `ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule` (which owns "Other permanents you control have …" and "&lt;Subtype&gt; tokens you control have …") and `CreatureTokensHaveKeywordListRule` (which owns the bare, non-subtyped "Creature tokens you control have …" two- keyword shape). Neither sibling's pattern matches the "creatures" noun paired with a capitalised subtype qualifier and no "tokens"/"token" restriction, so this rule is a new, disjoint sibling rather than an edit to either shared rule body — its regex only recognises the literal noun "creature(s)" immediately following the subtype word, which `ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule`'s `noun` group (`permanents?|tokens?`) never matches.

The granted subjects are ordinary (non-token) permanents of the named creature subtype, so the built filter is `CardTypes=["creature"], Subtypes=[&lt;Subtype&gt;], Controller=You` — deliberately omitting `IsToken` (unlike the sibling "tokens" shapes) since the oracle text says "creatures", not "tokens".

Keyword list: one or two keywords, optionally joined by "and". Per the MAST multi-effect-per-clause doctrine, a two-keyword grant is bundled into a single `StaticAbility` whose `Effects` list carries two independent `GainAbilityEffect` nodes — mirroring `ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule`'s and `CreatureTokensHaveKeywordListRule`'s two-keyword grant shape.

Anchored (^…$) pattern; the mandatory literal "creatures" (or "creature") noun and capitalised subtype qualifier keep this rule from matching any sibling clause shape (bare "Creature tokens …", "Other permanents …", "&lt;Subtype&gt; tokens …"). Because the capturing group for the subject qualifier is a bare "any capitalised word" ([A-Z][a-z]+), a corpus sweep of the existing fixtures surfaced three capitalised words that precede "creatures … you control have …" WITHOUT being a creature subtype, each already owned by a more specific sibling rule producing a materially different filter shape — these are explicitly declined below so this rule never shadows them:

"Other creatures you control have …" (Aggressive Mammoth) — the exclusion-of-self qualifier, owned by `BareKeywordGrantRule` Arm 3 (`ExcludeSelf = true`, no Subtypes). "Nontoken creatures you control have …" (Rhythm of the Wild) — the token-exclusion qualifier, owned by `NontokenCreaturesHaveKeywordRule` (`IsToken = false`, no Subtypes). "Attacking creatures you control have …" — the combat-state qualifier, owned by `AttackingObjectsHaveKeywordRule` (a `CombatStateCharacteristic`, no Subtypes).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordListRule.cs)

### `SubtypeCreaturesHaveQuotedAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"&lt;Subtype&gt; creatures you control have "[quoted ability]"" — grants a quoted ability (typically an activated mana ability) to every creature of the named subtype the controller controls. Paradigm card: Manaweft Sliver — "Sliver creatures you control have '{T}: Add one mana of any color.'"

This is a <b>static</b> continuous effect (CR 611.1: "A continuous effect modifies characteristics of objects … for a fixed or indefinite period."; CR 113.3: "Some effects and static abilities can grant an object an activated ability."). The grant persists for as long as the source remains on the battlefield with the ability — there is no Duration node.

The quoted body is dispatched to `ActivatedAbilityParser` first (the common tribal-lord grant shape — a "{T}: Add …" mana ability), falling back to `TriggeredAbilityParser`. Returns null (surfacing the gap honestly) when neither recognises the body, mirroring `EquippedCreatureHasQuotedAbilityRule`.

Priority 974 — above `ControlledFilterHaveKeywordListRule` (973) so this more-specific quoted-ability shape is tried first, though in practice the sibling bare-keyword rules already decline on their own: their keyword capture groups are restricted to lowercase-letter/space charsets that cannot match a leading quote character, so dispatch order does not change behaviour either way. Anchored (^…$) pattern prevents substring matches against sibling clauses.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SubtypeCreaturesHaveQuotedAbilityRule.cs)

### `SubtypeTokensHaveKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "&lt;Subtype&gt; tokens you control have [keyword]." — a static continuous effect (CR 604.1: "Static abilities do something all the time rather than being activated or triggered. They are written as statements, and they're simply true."; CR 604.2: static abilities create continuous effects that remain active as long as the source remains on the battlefield with the ability) that grants a keyword ability to the token-restricted subset of a named creature subtype the controller controls. This is the Eternal Skylord shape ("Zombie tokens you control have flying.").

The "tokens" qualifier maps to `IsToken = true` on the `ObjectFilter` (CR 111.1: "A token is a marker used to represent any permanent that isn't represented by a card."). The capitalised subtype word populates `Subtypes` — no `CardTypes` is emitted, matching the bare plural-subtype filter convention used elsewhere in this family.

GUARD: if the captured word is "Creature"/"Creatures" (case-insensitive), this rule declines — that card-type token grant (e.g. Combine Chrysalis) stays owned by `BareKeywordGrantRule` Arm 2, which already handles it via `BuildBareGrantFilterTarget`'s bare card-type branch.

Priority 970 — above `BareKeywordGrantRule` (967) and `NontokenCreaturesHaveKeywordRule` (969) so this more-specific "&lt;Subtype&gt; tokens you control have &lt;keyword&gt;" shape fires first and documents precedence over the broader filter arm (functionally order-independent here since BareKeywordGrantRule's Arm 2 bare-subtype branch is guarded against token filters and declines on its own). Anchored pattern prevents substring matches against sibling clauses.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SubtypeTokensHaveKeywordRule.cs)

### `SupertypeAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined supertype anthem + keyword grant: "[Supertype] creatures you control get +N/+N and have [keyword]." e.g. Bloodsworn Steward — "Commander creatures you control get +2/+2 and have haste."

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying TWO effects in its list (the MAST multi-effect-per-clause encoding): a `ModifyPTEffect` (+N/+N) and a `GainAbilityEffect` (the keyword), BOTH targeting the same supertype-filtered subject "[Supertype] creatures you control". One oracle clause generates one continuous effect from one static ability, so the two effects share a single ability rather than being split into two abilities (CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object. Example: A permanent with the static ability 'All white creatures get +1/+1' generates an effect that continuously gives +1/+1 to each white creature on the battlefield.").

The subject's supertype qualifier (e.g. "Commander", CR 903 — a commander designation that behaves as a supertype on the affected set) is recorded on `Supertypes`, NOT as a name or subtype: it categorises the affected objects rather than naming a specific card or its creature-type line.

The granted keyword is itself a static ability (e.g. CR 702.10a — "Haste is a static ability."), modelled as a recursive `GainedAbility` via the shared `MapKeywordToStaticAbility` mapping. No duration is carried — a static ability's continuous effect lasts for as long as the source remains on the battlefield, not until a stated time.

Distinct from `AnthemModifyPTRule` (the bare anchor-target "Enchanted/ Equipped creature gets +N/+M." shape, no keyword grant and no supertype subject) and from `TribalAnthemModifyPTRule` (the named-SUBTYPE anthem with no keyword conjunction). This rule is the supertype-subject compound (pump AND keyword grant).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SupertypeAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule.cs)

### `SupertypeSubtypeKeywordGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined SUPERTYPE + SUBTYPE keyword-only grant, with the "creatures" noun OMITTED because the bare plural subtype noun itself stands in for it (same convention as `TribalAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule`): "[Supertype] [Subtype-plural] you control have [keyword]." e.g. General's Enforcer — "Legendary Humans you control have indestructible."

Unlike `SupertypeAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` (which requires the literal "creatures" noun AND a "get +N/+N and" P/T clause before the keyword grant), this shape has NO P/T modification at all — the clause is a bare keyword grant gated on BOTH a supertype and a subtype qualifier simultaneously (CR 611.3: "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object."). A creature must have BOTH the named supertype (CR 205.4a) AND the named creature subtype (CR 205.3m) to qualify — `ObjectFilter`'s `Supertypes` and `Subtypes` axes are independent AND-ed filters on the same object, not a disjunction.

The recognised supertype vocabulary mirrors `SupertypeAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule`'s closed set (Commander, Legendary, Snow, Basic, World, Ongoing) so a capitalised non-supertype word immediately preceding another capitalised word (e.g. an "Untapped Dragons"/ "Equipped Warriors" combat-/attachment-state qualifier, each owned by its own sibling rule) is never misclassified as a supertype — it declines instead, leaving those clauses to their owning rules.

The granted keyword is itself a static ability (CR 702.12b: "Indestructible is a static ability."), modelled as a recursive `GainedAbility` via the shared `MapKeywordToStaticAbility` mapping. No duration is carried — a static ability's continuous effect lasts for as long as the source remains on the battlefield (CR 611.3 example generalised to two filter axes), not until a stated time.

Distinct from `TribalAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` (subtype-only, but REQUIRES a "get +N/+N and" P/T clause before "have") and from `SubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordListRule` (subtype-only, but REQUIRES the literal "creatures" noun). This rule's two-capitalised-word subject with NO "get ... and" P/T clause and NO "creatures" noun is a disjoint third shape. Optional leading "Other " (CR 109.5 — "another") sets `ExcludeSelf`, mirroring the sibling anthem rules. Anchored (^…$) end to end so it can never match a substring of a longer clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/SupertypeSubtypeKeywordGrantRule.cs)

### `TappedStateSubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses "&lt;Tapped|Untapped&gt; &lt;Subtype&gt;s you control have [keyword]." — Dragonologist: "Untapped Dragons you control have hexproof." — a static continuous effect (CR 611.3 (verbatim): "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object. Example: A permanent with the static ability 'All white creatures get +1/+1' generates an effect that continuously gives +1/+1 to each white creature on the battlefield.") granting a keyword ability to every creature of the named subtype the controller controls, further restricted to those currently in the named tap state (CR 701.26 / 110.5, per `TappedStateCharacteristic`'s own established citation, reused below).

A "state-qualified subtype anthem": the bare-plural subtype noun ("Dragons") is prefixed by a tapped/untapped state adjective rather than immediately following "have". Sibling to `SubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordListRule`, which owns "&lt;Subtype&gt; creatures you control have …" (literal "creature(s)" noun after the subtype) and explicitly DECLINES "Tapped"/"Untapped" as a captured subtype word (they are states, not subtypes — CR 205.3 lists neither as a creature type) so it never shadows this rule. This rule instead requires the state word to come FIRST, followed directly by the bare plural subtype noun (no "creatures" word), so the two rules' anchored patterns are disjoint by construction — neither is a substring match inside the other.

Also distinct from `BareKeywordGrantRule`'s "Other tapped/untapped creatures you control have …" arm (`ParseLordPTFilter`'s bare "tapped creature(s)"/"untapped creature(s)" shape, Saryth, the Viper's Fang): that shape has NO subtype qualifier and REQUIRES the "Other " prefix. This rule has NO "Other" prefix and REQUIRES a capitalised subtype noun immediately after the state word, so the two anchored patterns cannot double-match the same clause.

The tapped/untapped predicate is expressed as a `TappedStateCharacteristic` on the granted-to filter's `Characteristics` (CR 701.26 / 110.5, per that node's own doc), the same node `BareKeywordGrantRule`'s Saryth arm and `AddManaForEachTappedLandOpponentsControlRule` already use — MAST records only that the granted-to set is scoped to that tap state; the actual tap status of any given permanent is engine territory.

Hexproof (Rule 702.11, per the existing citation on `StaticRuleHelpers.MapKeywordToStaticAbility`'s "hexproof" arm: "this permanent can't be the target of spells or abilities opponents control") is resolved via that shared keyword map — read, not modified, by this rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/TappedStateSubtypeCreaturesHaveKeywordRule.cs)

### `TargetPlayerTakesExtraTurnStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Target player takes an extra turn after this one." — schedules an additional full turn for a targeted player (rather than the controller) to be taken immediately after the current turn (Walk the Aeons).

CR 500.7 (verbatim): "Some effects can give a player extra turns. They do this by adding the turns directly after the specified turn. If a player is given multiple extra turns, the extra turns are added one at a time. If multiple players are given extra turns, the extra turns are added one at a time, in APNAP order (see rule 101.4). The most recently created turn will be taken first." MAST records the verb and the targeted-player reference; the turn-ordering bookkeeping is engine territory (ADR 0001).

This clause is NOT intercepted by `AbilityClassifier`'s "Take [an/N] extra turn(s) after this one" spell route — that route is anchored on the bare imperative "Take …" opener (controller takes the turn); "Target player takes …" has a distinct subject and third-person verb, so it falls through to the classifier's declarative-statement default (`Static`) and is handled here instead, mirroring the sibling spell-form rule `TakeExtraTurnSpellRule` and the activated-cost form `TakeExtraTurnEffectRule`.

ANCHOR: pattern is anchored (^...$) so it cannot match as a substring of a longer, more complex ability line.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/TargetPlayerTakesExtraTurnStaticRule.cs)

### `TribalAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Combined tribal (subtype) anthem + keyword grant, with the "creatures" noun OMITTED because the subject subtype is plural-invariant in oracle text: "Other [Subtype] you control get +N/+N and have [keyword]." e.g. Mist Dancer — "Other Merfolk you control get +1/+0 and have flying."

Emits ONE `StaticAbility` carrying TWO effects in its list (the MAST multi-effect-per-clause encoding): a `ModifyPTEffect` (+N/+N) and a `GainAbilityEffect` (the keyword), BOTH targeting the same subtype-filtered subject "[Subtype] you control". One oracle clause generates one continuous effect from one static ability, so the two effects share a single ability rather than being split into two abilities (CR 611.3 — "A continuous effect may be generated by the static ability of an object. Example: A permanent with the static ability 'All white creatures get +1/+1' generates an effect that continuously gives +1/+1 to each white creature on the battlefield.").

The matched noun ALWAYS routes to `Subtypes` (a creature subtype, e.g. "Merfolk"), never to Supertypes — this rule requires the ABSENCE of the "creatures" word, which is what a subtype-only oracle subject looks like when the subtype is plural-invariant. It means a Merfolk permanent on the battlefield (CR 109.2 — "If a spell or ability uses a description of an object that includes a card type or subtype, but doesn't refer to a specific zone or include the word 'card,' 'spell,' 'source,' or 'scheme,' it means a permanent of that card type or subtype on the battlefield."). "You control" resolves to the source's controller (CR 109.5 — "The words 'you' and 'your' on an object refer to the object's controller... For a static ability, this is the current controller of the object it's on.").

The granted keyword is itself a static ability (e.g. Flying — "A keyword ability that restricts how a creature may be blocked. See rule 702.9, 'Flying.'"), modelled as a recursive `GainedAbility` via the shared `MapKeywordToStaticAbility` mapping. No duration is carried — a static ability's continuous effect lasts for as long as the source remains on the battlefield, not until a stated time.

Distinct from `SupertypeAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule` (the sibling compound REQUIRING the "creatures" word — "[Supertype/Subtype] creatures you control get +N/+N and have [keyword]"). The two patterns are disjoint: this rule requires "creatures" to be ABSENT (noun directly followed by the controller clause), so despite sharing a priority band, they never both match the same clause. Also distinct from `TribalAnthemModifyPTRule` (the bare tribal anthem with no keyword conjunction).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/TribalAnthemAndKeywordGrantRule.cs)

### `TriggerDoublingStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"If a triggered ability of a colorless spell you control or another colorless permanent you control triggers, that ability triggers an additional time."

This models the trigger-multiplication static ability on Echoes of Eternity. The effect is a `ReplacementEffect` over an `AbilityTriggerEvent`: the replaced event is "a triggered ability of [colorless thing you control] fires", and the replacement is that it fires one additional time (`OriginalEventOccurs` = true, `Modifier` Type = "additionalTime").

The "another colorless permanent" excludes the Echoes card itself from the source set (modeled via `ExcludeSelf` = true on the AffectedObjects filter). "Colorless spell you control" covers spells on the stack; "another colorless permanent you control" covers permanents on the battlefield. The zone distinction and the exact "another" scope are engine territory; MAST records the colorless + controller-you + exclude-self scope.

CR 603 (triggered abilities trigger whenever the event they watch for occurs). Rule 105.1: "Colorless is not a color." The IsColorless filter axis encodes colorlessness rather than the Colors axis.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/TriggerDoublingStaticRule.cs)

### `TypeSpellColoredCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"&lt;Type&gt; spells you cast cost {&lt;colored symbols&gt;} less to cast. This effect reduces only the amount of colored mana you pay." — Edgewalker and its cycle (each two-color Cleric lord from Onslaught reduces the cost of the shared creature type by its own guild's colored pip pair, e.g. Edgewalker's {W}{B}). Unlike `TypeSpellCostReductionRule` (a single GENERIC digit), the reduction here is one or more COLORED mana symbols — CR 118.7: "What a player actually needs to do to pay a cost may be changed or reduced by effects."

Reusing `BuildTypeSpellFilter` for the type/subtype filter half (Rule 205.3 subtypes fall to the catch-all branch, matching Ballyrush Banneret's "Kithkin spells" encoding) and the established `ManaSymbols` convention for the colored-only reduction half (zero generic `Amount` + explicit symbols — the same shape as `AdditionalCostPayLifeReducesColoredCostRule`'s "This effect reduces only the amount of [color] mana you pay" sentence). The closing "This effect reduces only the amount of colored mana you pay." sentence needs no separate node: putting the whole reduction on `ManaSymbols` with a zero generic component already IS "reduces only colored mana" by construction. The trailing parenthetical worked example ("(For example, if you cast a Cleric spell with mana cost {1}{W}, it costs {1} to cast.)") carries no additional rules content beyond what the effect already states, so it is matched but not separately modeled (reminder-adjacent).

Anchored (^…$) to prevent false-positive substring matches inside longer oracle lines — the #1 FAIL class per the vertical-slice contract.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/TypeSpellColoredCostReductionRule.cs)

### `TypeSpellCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/TypeSpellCostReductionRule.cs)

### `UnleashStaticRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Decomposes a bare "Unleash" oracle line into the two static abilities defined by CR 702.98a (mirroring the `DashStaticRule` / `ReconfigureStaticRule` multi-ability precedent).

CR 702.98a (verbatim): "Unleash is a keyword that represents two static abilities. 'Unleash' means 'You may have this permanent enter with an additional +1/+1 counter on it' and 'This permanent can't block as long as it has a +1/+1 counter on it.'"

Priority 1001 — fires before `KeywordListRule` (priority 1000) so the two-ability decomposition takes precedence over the single-ability keyword combinator path. The combinator in `UnleashKeyword` remains live as a fallback, emitting only the primary enters-with-counter static ability (the keyword expander returns a single `Ability`; Unleash decomposes into two).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/UnleashStaticRule.cs)

### `UnrestrictedSpellCostReductionRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

"Spells you cast cost {N} less to cast." (Stone Calendar) — the flat, UNqualified cost-reduction base case: every spell the controller casts, no colour/type/zone/history qualifier.

CR 118.7: "What a player actually needs to do to pay a cost may be changed or reduced by effects." CR 118.7a: "Effects that reduce a cost by an amount of generic mana affect only the generic mana component of that cost."

Sibling of `TypeSpellCostReductionRule` (which requires a leading capitalised type/colour noun before "spells you cast") — this rule is the base case with NO qualifying noun at all, so the affected-objects filter is the bare `CardTypes: ["spell"], Controller: You` shape with no further narrowing axis set. Anchored (^…$) so it only matches the literal, unqualified "Spells you cast cost {N} less to cast." sentence and falls through (returns null) for every qualified variant (those are each their own sibling rule's job) — this keeps the base case from ever shadowing a more specific sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/UnrestrictedSpellCostReductionRule.cs)

### `VorinclexCounterReplacementRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses Vorinclex-style counter-placement replacement effects: 1. "If you would put one or more counters on a permanent or player, put twice that many of each of those kinds of counters on that permanent or player instead." — the controller doubles counter placement on any target (permanent or player). Actor = you (Controller: {Kind:You}); Modifier = double. CR 614 (replacement effects). 2. "If an opponent would put one or more counters on a permanent or player, they put half that many of each of those kinds of counters on that permanent or player instead, rounded down." — opponents halve counter placement on any target, rounded down. Actor = opponent (Controller: {Kind:Opponent}); Modifier = halveRoundDown. CR 614 (replacement effects). AffectedObjects is null on both (permanent or player = all valid counter recipients; no restriction expressed by the oracle text beyond exhaustive enumeration).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/VorinclexCounterReplacementRule.cs)

### `WardKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Parses Ward keyword abilities in five cost forms:

Mana cost: "Ward {N}" — e.g. "Ward {2}" Life cost: "Ward—Pay N life." — e.g. "Ward—Pay 7 life." Sacrifice cost: "Ward—Sacrifice a [filter]." — e.g. "Ward—Sacrifice a Food." Discard cost: "Ward—Discard a card." — e.g. "Ward—Discard a card." (Sunset Saboteur) Compound mana+life cost: "Ward—{N}, Pay N life." — e.g. Ovika, Enigma Goliath's "Ward—{3}, Pay 3 life." A single Ward cost slot (CR 702.21a) that is itself a comma-joined pair of a mana cost and a life payment, mirrored on `CompositeCost` the same way activated-ability cost lists bundle multiple cost kinds (CR 601.2f — "the total cost is the mana cost plus all additional costs").

CR 702.21a: "Ward is a triggered ability. Ward [cost] means 'Whenever this permanent becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, counter that spell or ability unless that player pays [cost].'"

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/WardKeywordRule.cs)

### `WithKeywordAnthemModifyPTRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Recognises the "Other creatures you control with [keyword] get +X/+Y" anthem shape. A continuous P/T modification (CR 613.1, layer 7c) scoped to permanents the controller owns that carry a particular keyword. The keyword predicate is a "has [keyword]" filter encoded on `Characteristics` (e.g. `"flying"`), consistent with how game-state predicates like "tapped" and "with a +1/+1 counter" are encoded by sibling rules. Example oracle text: "Other creatures you control with flying get +1/+0." → ObjectFilter { CardTypes: ["creature"], Controller: You, ExcludeSelf: true, Characteristics: ["flying"] }

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/WithKeywordAnthemModifyPTRule.cs)

### `YouHaveKeywordRule` — *sealed class* : IStaticRule

Handles the "You have [keyword]." static ability shape, where the permanent grants a keyword to its controller (a player, not a permanent). CR 702.11a: "Hexproof is a static ability." Oracle examples: "You have hexproof." (Spirit of the Hearth) "You have shroud." (Teferi's Protection effect) The subject "You" maps to `You` — the controller player, NOT the permanent itself (not Self). The granted ability is embedded as a full `StaticAbility` node via `GainAbilityEffect`. Reminder text (the parenthetical) is stripped before matching; the caller places it on the `Reminder` field.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Static/Rules/YouHaveKeywordRule.cs)

## `/Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/`

### `ITriggerConditionRule` — *interface*

One trigger-condition recognition rule (the event + filter half of a triggered ability). Implementations are discovered by reflection via `TriggerConditionRuleAttribute` and dispatched by `TriggeredAbilityParser` in descending `Priority` order, then ordinal name for tie-breaking; the first non-null result wins.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/ITriggerConditionRule.cs)

### `ITriggeredRule` — *interface*

One triggered-effect recognition rule. Dispatched by `TriggeredAbilityParser` in priority order (descending). The `text` input is the post-trigger effect fragment, already split off by the trigger/effect boundary detection in the dispatcher.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/ITriggeredRule.cs)

### `TriggerConditionRuleAttribute` — *sealed class* : Attribute, MagicAST.Parsing.Parsers.IPrioritizedRuleAttribute

Marks an `ITriggerConditionRule` implementation for reflection-based discovery by `TriggeredAbilityParser`. Mirrors `TriggeredRuleAttribute` for the trigger-condition side.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/TriggerConditionRuleAttribute.cs)

### `TriggeredRuleAttribute` — *sealed class* : Attribute, MagicAST.Parsing.Parsers.IPrioritizedRuleAttribute

Marks an `ITriggeredRule` implementation for reflection-based discovery by `TriggeredAbilityParser`. See `SpellRuleAttribute` for the shared priority convention (0–100, default 50, higher = more specific = tried first).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/TriggeredRuleAttribute.cs)

### `TriggeredRuleHelpers` — *static class*

Shared utilities used across `ITriggeredRule` implementations.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/TriggeredRuleHelpers.cs)

## `/Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/`

### `ActivateAbilityConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you activate an ability" — the bare activated-ability trigger condition (Rings of Brighthearth). Emits `AbilityActivated` with a `Controller = You` filter (the ability you activate).

CR 603.2 / CR 602.1: an activated ability is "[cost]: [effect]" put on the stack by its controller; "whenever you activate an ability" is a triggered ability that fires on that act. The intervening-if "if it isn't a mana ability" (CR 605) is handled separately by `ConditionParser` as a `TriggeringAbilityIsManaCondition`; this rule owns only the trigger event + subject filter.

ANCHORED (`^…$`) deliberately: "you activate an ability" recurs as a SUBSTRING of more-specific siblings ("…activate an ability of a creature", "…activate an ability that targets only…", "…activate a loyalty ability"). An unanchored matcher would mislabel those, dropping their qualifiers — the #1 overfit FAIL class. The bare form (the post-split `triggerPart` is exactly "Whenever you activate an ability") matches; every qualified sibling carries extra words after "ability" and falls through to its own rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ActivateAbilityConditionRule.cs)

### `AddAdditionalManaRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"add an additional [mana]" — triggered mana-doubling effect. The effect clause of a mana-doubling trigger, covering two subject forms and three mana forms:

Bare subject "add an additional {X}" (Forsaken Monument: "Whenever you tap a permanent for {C}, add an additional {C}") — the player is the implicit ability controller, so `Player` is null. Named subject "its controller adds an additional …" — the mana-doubler Aura family (Fertile Ground, Wild Growth, Glittering Frost, Market Festival). "Its controller" is the controller of the enchanted land that was tapped, recorded as `Player` = `Controller`.

The mana form is one of:

a specific symbol — "{G}" (Wild Growth) → `Mana`; "one mana of any color" (Fertile Ground, Glittering Frost) → `AnyColor` with empty `Mana`; "&lt;n&gt; mana in any combination of colors" (Market Festival) → `Amount` + `AnyCombinationOf` over the five colors, with empty `Mana`.

The word "additional" distinguishes this from the baseline `AddManaRule` which handles "add {X}" directly. CR 106.4: "When an effect instructs a player to add mana, that mana goes into a player's mana pool." The "additional" qualifier is descriptive context for the trigger (the named player gets one more mana on top of what the tapping already produced); MAST models what the oracle text says.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AddAdditionalManaRule.cs)

### `AddManaRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"add {...}" / "add one mana of any color" — Rule 106. Note: triggered mana production is NOT a Rule 605 mana ability, so no IsManaAbility flag is set.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AddManaRule.cs)

### `AddManaThenIfSecondTimeRevealUntilRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Recognises the Nissa, Resurgent Animist Landfall effect: "add one mana of any color. Then if this is the second time this ability has resolved this turn, reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal an Elf or Elemental card. Put that card into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order."

The full effect is a single coherent resolution: unconditional mana, then a conditional library-reveal. The "Then if" clause gates the reveal on an ordinal history predicate; "that card" in the Put sentence back-references the card found in the reveal. This rule captures all three sentences as one match and emits them as a `CompositeEffect` containing:

`AddManaEffect` — add one mana of any color (unconditional). `ConditionalEffect` — if this is the second time the ability has resolved this turn (`OtherCondition` residual per ADR 0001, as no structured history-ordinal condition exists yet), perform the `RevealUntilEffect` atomic reveal-until-found action.

The "second time this ability has resolved this turn" predicate does not yet have a structured `Condition` variant; it is recorded as `OtherCondition` — the typed IResidual residual (acceptable per ADR 0001).

Priority 95: must beat generic sentence-bundle dispatch.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AddManaThenIfSecondTimeRevealUntilRule.cs)

### `AdditionalCombatPhaseTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"After this phase, there is an additional combat phase." — triggered-ability mirror of `AdditionalCombatPhaseEffectRule`.

Emits an `AdditionalCombatPhaseEffect`, which inserts exactly one additional combat phase into the current turn without an accompanying main phase (distinct from the Aggravated Assault pattern). This variant is used inside a triggered ability (e.g. Godo, Bandit Warlord's second ability), where the sentence bundle dispatcher routes each sentence through `ITriggeredRule` implementations rather than through activated rules.

Pattern anchored (^...$) so it cannot match as a substring of a longer phrase. CR 506 (combat phase); CR 500.1 (turn structure).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AdditionalCombatPhaseTriggeredRule.cs)

### `AmassTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"amass [Subtype] N" / "amass N" — the Amass keyword action as a triggered effect.

CR 701.47a: "Amass [subtype] N means 'Either put N +1/+1 counters on an Army you control, or create a 0/0 black [Subtype] Army creature token, then put N +1/+1 counters on it.'"

Matches both the modern typed form ("amass Orcs 1", which specifies a subtype) and the legacy untyped form ("amass 1", from War of the Spark before subtype- specific amass was templated). Handles an optional leading "Then " prefix (from multi-sentence oracle text like "...deals 1 damage. Then amass Orcs 1.") so the rule fires correctly when the sentence-bundle splitter produces a "Then amass" fragment.

MAST records the keyword-action and its parameters descriptively. The army- selection logic, token creation, and counter placement are engine territory.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AmassTriggeredRule.cs)

### `AnimateTargetIntoVehicleWithCrewAndCrashLandRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Captain Rex Nebula's combat trigger resolution: "choose target nonland permanent you control. Until end of turn, it becomes a Vehicle artifact with base power and toughness each equal to its mana value, and it gains crew 2 and 'Crash Land — Whenever this Vehicle deals damage, roll a six-sided die. If the result is equal to this Vehicle's mana value, sacrifice this Vehicle, then it deals that much damage to any target.'"

A duration-bounded continuous effect (CR 611) that animates the chosen permanent into a <b>noncreature</b> Vehicle artifact (CR 301.7: a Vehicle isn't a creature unless an effect says it is — this one does not), whose base power/toughness each equal its mana value (CR 202.3, CR 208), and that gains two abilities: the Crew 2 keyword (CR 702.122) and a nested "Crash Land" triggered ability (CR 207.2c — the em-dash ability word names the granted ability).

Modelled as a single `BecomesPermanentEffect` — NOT `BecomesCreatureEffect`, whose discriminator asserts "becomes a creature", which would be a fidelity error for a Vehicle (CR 301.7). The Subject is the inline `Target` reference to "target nonland permanent you control" (ExcludedCardTypes ["land"], Controller You); the cross-sentence "it" in sentence two is bound back to that target. The granted abilities are fully structured:

Crew 2 — a `StaticAbility` with KeywordSource Crew and a `CrewEffect` (Power 2), mirroring the Bomat Bazaar Barge gold. Crash Land — a `TriggeredAbility` with AbilityWord "Crash Land", triggering on this Vehicle dealing damage (`DealsDamage`, Filter IsSelf), whose effects are [rollDie d6, conditional(roll == this Vehicle's mana value → sacrifice this Vehicle, then it deals that much damage to any target)]. The damage carries Source Self (the Vehicle) and Target AnyTarget.

Anchored (^…$) and highly specific so it cannot collide with any other "becomes …" or combat-trigger sibling. The terminal period and the embedded sentence boundary ("die. If …") inside the quoted clause are tolerated explicitly by the regex; this rule is tried in the single-rule dispatch loop AFTER the sentence-bundle splitter has failed to parse the two-sentence body.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnimateTargetIntoVehicleWithCrewAndCrashLandRule.cs)

### `AnotherColorCreatureEntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"another [color] creature you control enters" — color-filtered creature ETB trigger, excluding the source permanent (the "another" qualifier).

CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." The "another" qualifier (CR 109.5) excludes the source permanent from the matching set; the color filter narrows which entering creatures match (e.g. "another green creature you control enters" — only green creatures controlled by the trigger's controller, not the source itself).

Uses `Colors` (not `IsColorless`) per Rule 105.1: "Colorless is not a color" — the five named MTG colors (white, blue, black, red, green) are encoded as single-letter codes (W, U, B, R, G) in the Colors list.

Running at priority 996 — tried after `AnotherColorlessCreatureEntersConditionRule` (997) and before the general `EntersConditionRule` (990).

Example: Ivy Lane Denizen — "Whenever another green creature you control enters, put a +1/+1 counter on target creature."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnotherColorCreatureEntersConditionRule.cs)

### `AnotherColorlessCreatureEntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"another colorless creature you control enters" — trigger condition for watching colorless creature ETB events from the same controller, excluding the source itself.

CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." The "another" qualifier (CR 109) excludes the source permanent from the matching set; the "colorless creature" filter (CR 105.1: "Colorless is not a color") encodes colorlessness via `IsColorless` rather than `Colors` (which encodes the five named colors). Running at priority 997 to be tried after `ColorlessSpellCastConditionRule` (999) but before the general `EntersConditionRule` (990).

Example: Glaring Fleshraker — "Whenever another colorless creature you control enters, this creature deals 1 damage to each opponent."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnotherColorlessCreatureEntersConditionRule.cs)

### `AnotherLegendaryCreatureDiesConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"another legendary creature you control dies" — the Ratadrabik of Urborg trigger. Fires on `Dies` filtering for legendary creatures under the controller's control, excluding the source permanent itself.

CR 702.20a: "Vigilance is a static ability…" — vigilance is the keyword context for this card. CR 603.2: a triggered ability fires whenever its event occurs. The filter narrows the match to legendary creatures you control (not the source).

Rule 205.4: "Legendary is a supertype. It is placed before the card's type." Supertypes on `Supertypes` encode the positive-match requirement (CR 205.4 — legendary must be among the permanent's supertypes).

The "another" qualifier ("another" = any object other than this source; plain-language English, no dedicated CR rule number in the bundled data) maps to `ExcludeSelf` = true, consistent with the DiesConditionRule and AnotherSubtypeEntersConditionRule conventions.

ANCHORED (^…$): the pattern targets a highly specific surface phrase and is fully anchored to prevent matching inside broader sibling trigger texts. Priority 994 (above the generic DiesConditionRule at 991, below IsSelfByNameTrigger-based rules) so this more-specific legendary filter is claimed first.

Rule citations: CR 603.2 (triggered ability), CR 205.4 (Legendary supertype), CR 700.4 ("dies" → moved to graveyard from battlefield). ("another" is plain-language exclusion — no dedicated CR rule — modeled on the ExcludeSelf axis.)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnotherLegendaryCreatureDiesConditionRule.cs)

### `AnotherLegendaryCreatureEntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"another legendary creature you control enters" — the Gimli of the Glittering Caves trigger. Fires on `Enters` filtering for legendary creatures under the controller's control, excluding the source permanent itself.

This is the "enters" analogue of `AnotherLegendaryCreatureDiesConditionRule` (which handles the same subject filter for the Dies event). CR 603.6a: "Enters-the- battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." The filter narrows the match to legendary creatures you control (not the source).

Rule 205.4: "Legendary is a supertype. It is placed before the card's type." Supertypes on `Supertypes` encode the positive-match requirement (CR 205.4 — legendary must be among the permanent's supertypes).

The "another" qualifier ("another" = any object other than this source; plain-language English, no dedicated CR rule number in the bundled data) maps to `ExcludeSelf` = true, consistent with the EntersConditionRule and AnotherLegendaryCreatureDiesConditionRule conventions.

ANCHORED (end): the pattern targets a highly specific surface phrase; "enters" must be the final word so this does not match inside a broader compound trigger clause. Priority 994 (mirrors AnotherLegendaryCreatureDiesConditionRule) — above the generic EntersConditionRule (990), which would otherwise fail on this shape anyway because ParseObjectFilter has no branch for the "legendary creature" supertype-qualified noun phrase (it would return null and EntersConditionRule would decline to match).

Rule citations: CR 603.2 (triggered ability), CR 603.6a (enters-the-battlefield abilities), CR 205.4 (Legendary supertype). ("another" is plain-language exclusion — no dedicated CR rule — modeled on the ExcludeSelf axis.)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnotherLegendaryCreatureEntersConditionRule.cs)

### `AnotherSubtypeDiesConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"this creature or another [Subtype] you control dies" — subtype-filtered dies trigger. The dies analog of `AnotherSubtypeEntersConditionRule`: the trigger fires when a permanent of a specific creature subtype that you control is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.

CR 603.1: triggered abilities use "when," "whenever," or "at" to watch for an event; the subtype filter narrows which dying permanents fire the ability. CR 700.4: "dies" means "is put into a graveyard from the battlefield." CR 205.3: subtypes (e.g. Vampire, Ally, Zombie) are named on the type line; the disjunction "this creature or another Vampire you control" resolves to a single "Vampire you control" filter that includes the source.

Examples: "Whenever this creature or another Vampire you control dies, ..." (Kalastria Highborn, WWK).

Priority 995 (matching the enters analog) so this specific subtype form is tried before the generic `DiesConditionRule` (991), whose `ParseObjectFilter` would resolve "this creature" to a plain `CardTypes=["creature"]` filter and silently drop the subtype.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnotherSubtypeDiesConditionRule.cs)

### `AnotherSubtypeEntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"another [Subtype] you control enters" — subtype-filtered enters trigger. Handles the Ally-rally pattern and analogous mechanics where the trigger fires when another permanent of a specific creature subtype enters the battlefield under your control. Rule 603.1: triggered abilities use "when," "whenever," or "at" to watch for zone changes; the subtype filter narrows which entering permanents cause the ability to trigger. Examples: "Whenever another Ally you control enters, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnotherSubtypeEntersConditionRule.cs)

### `AnotherTargetAttackingCreatureCantBeBlockedThisTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Triggered-ability effect clause "another target attacking creature can't be blocked this turn." — the resolution half of an attack trigger that makes a chosen attacking creature (other than the source) unblockable for the turn. Covers Clammy Prowler: "Whenever this creature attacks, another target attacking creature can't be blocked this turn." The trigger side is owned by `AttacksConditionRule` (CR 508.1 — declare attackers); this rule handles the effect clause only (CR 603.1).

Emits a `CantBeBlockedEffect` — attacker-side evasion (CR 509.1b: "effects that say a creature can't block") — with an `untilEndOfTurn` duration ("this turn"). The target is `Target` whose filter carries two axes beyond the bare "target creature can't be blocked this turn" shape (`TargetCantBeBlockedThisTurnRule`): `ExcludeSelf = true` ("another" — the codebase convention mapping "another" to `ExcludeSelf`, CR 109.5) and the combat-state predicate `CombatState.Attacking` ("attacking creature"), mirroring how `ModifyPTTargetAttackingCreatureEffectRule` encodes the attacking filter.

Fully anchored (^ … $) and prefixed with "another" so it can never substring the sibling `^target … can't be blocked` / `^target … can't block` surfaces, and vice versa.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnotherTargetAttackingCreatureCantBeBlockedThisTurnRule.cs)
