### `AnotherTargetAttackingSubtypeYouControlPumpTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"another target attacking [Subtype] you control gets +N/+M until end of turn." — the effect clause of an attack trigger that pumps a chosen ATTACKING creature of a specific subtype the controller controls, other than the source (Fervent Champion: "Whenever this creature attacks, another target attacking Knight you control gets +1/+0 until end of turn.").

CR 603.1: the trigger condition and the effect are separate composable nodes; this rule handles only the effect clause (the trigger side is owned by `AttacksConditionRule`). CR 611.2a / CR 514.2: an "until end of turn" continuous effect ends during cleanup — modelled as `EndOfTurn`.

The filter carries four axes on top of the bare `ModifyPTTargetAttackingCreatureEffectRule` shape ("target attacking creature gets…"): a single capitalised subtype token (`Subtypes`, CR 205.3m), `Controller = You` ("you control", CR 109.5), `ExcludeSelf = true` ("another" — the codebase convention mapping "another" to `ExcludeSelf`, mirrored from `AnotherTargetAttackingCreatureCantBeBlockedThisTurnRule` and `AnotherTargetControlledCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule`), and the combat-state predicate `InCombat` with `Attacking` ("attacking").

Anchored (^…$) and requires the capitalised subtype token immediately between "attacking" and "you control", so it cannot substring-match the generic-noun sibling <c>^another target attacking creature can't be blocked…</c> surface, nor `OtherSubtypePumpTriggeredRule`'s untargeted, plural "other [Subtype]s you control get…" mass-pump shape.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnotherTargetAttackingSubtypeYouControlPumpTriggeredRule.cs)

### `AnotherTargetControlledCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"another target creature you control gains [keyword] until end of turn." — the effect clause of an attack/enter trigger that grants a keyword ability to a chosen creature the controller controls, other than the source, for the remainder of the turn. Covers Starry-Eyed Skyrider's attack trigger: "Whenever this creature attacks, another target creature you control gains flying until end of turn."

CR 603.1: triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect; this rule handles the effect clause only (the trigger side is owned by `AttacksConditionRule`). CR 611.2a: "A continuous effect generated by the resolution of a spell or ability lasts as long as stated by the spell or ability creating it (such as 'until end of turn')." CR 514.2: all "until end of turn" effects end during the cleanup step — modelled as `EndOfTurn`.

"another target creature you control" is a targeted reference (`Target`) whose filter carries two axes distinct from the bare `TargetCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` ("target creature gains …"): `Controller = You` ("you control", CR 109.5: "The words 'you' and 'your' on an object refer to the object's controller …") and `ExcludeSelf = true` ("another" — codebase convention mapping "another" to `ExcludeSelf`, per GLOSSARY.md and `AnotherTargetModifyPTSpellRule`). The granted keyword resolves through `BuildKeywordStaticAbility` (CR 702.9a/702.9b for flying); an unrecognised keyword bails so no free text is emitted.

Anchored (^ … $) and prefixed with "another" so it can never substring-match the sibling `^target creature gains …` surface, and vice versa.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnotherTargetControlledCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `AnotherTargetCreatureYouControlGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"another target creature you control gains [keyword] until end of turn." — grants a keyword ability to a separately chosen target creature the controller controls, excluding the source itself, for the remainder of the turn. Covers Void Grafter's ETB trigger effect clause: "another target creature you control gains hexproof until end of turn." Rule 603.1: triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect; this rule handles the effect clause. Rule 115.1: "target creature" requires a chosen target, modelled as `Target`. Rule 611.1: the keyword grant is a continuous effect with a duration — "until end of turn" is the fixed duration, ending per rule 514.2 cleanup. Hexproof itself is a static ability (CR 702.11a) meaning "This permanent can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control" (CR 702.11b). Distinct from `TargetCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` (a bare "target creature", no controller/self restriction), `ItGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` (anaphoric "it", the object named by the trigger's own filter), and `EnchantedCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` (the Aura's fixed attachment, not a separately chosen target). Here the subject is "another target creature you control": a chosen target (`Target`), restricted to the controller's own creatures (`Controller = You`, CR 109.4), and excluding the source object itself ("another", `ExcludeSelf = true`, CR 109.5). Builds the gained keyword ability with a small local switch rather than calling `BuildKeywordStaticAbility`, which has no "hexproof" arm.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnotherTargetCreatureYouControlGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `AnyOpponentMayHaveItDealDamageThenSacrificeSelfRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"any opponent may have it deal N damage to them. If a player does, sacrifice this creature." — the opponent-choice downside ping (Longhorn Firebeast's ETB). An opponent (not the controller) decides whether the source deals damage to that opponent; if one does, the controller must sacrifice the source.

CR 118.12: "[A player] may [do something]. If [that player] [does…], [effect]." — the whole clause is one `OptionalEffect` (wrapper presence IS the "may"; no bool, ADR 0005). The decision-maker is NOT the controller, so `Chooser` is set to `Opponent` ("any opponent") rather than left null (≡ "you may"); this is load-bearing because the source ("it") and the "sacrifice" actor (the controller) are distinct from the choosing opponent, so the chooser cannot be inferred from the inner references.

CR 120.1: an object (source) deals damage to a player. The source is the pronoun "it" — the ability's own source permanent (mirrors `ItDealsDamageToTargetTypeDisjunctionRule`), modeled as `It`; absent any "combat damage" marker the damage is non-combat, so `IsCombat` is left null. The recipient "them" is the choosing opponent (`Opponent`).

The "If a player does" branch is the opt-in consequence, carried in `IfYouDo` (the branch that fires when the chooser performs the optional action). CR 701.21a: "To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner's graveyard." — "sacrifice this creature" is a `SacrificeEffect` whose target is the source itself (`Self`). CR 603.2: triggered abilities.

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the full two-sentence effect interior is matched, so no sibling "sacrifice this creature" / "deal N damage" surface in a different pattern is mis-labelled.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AnyOpponentMayHaveItDealDamageThenSacrificeSelfRule.cs)

### `AttachThisEquipmentToItTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"[you may] attach this [Equipment|Aura|Fortification] to it" — the ETB-triggered auto-attach shape where the object named by the trigger condition (Rule 603.6a — a "Whenever a [X] enters" ability) IS the attachment target itself, referenced back as "it" rather than picked via a fresh target. Rule 701.3: "To take an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification from where it currently is and put it onto a specified object or player."

Paradigm card: Cloak and Dagger — "Whenever a Rogue creature enters, you may attach this Equipment to it." The "it" is a back-reference (ADR 0004) to the permanent named by the trigger's own `Filter`, so the attach target is `It` carrying no filter of its own — mirroring the same reference the compound Animate Dead / Nim Deathmantle rules already build for their "…and attach this [Aura|Equipment] to it" tails.

Distinct from `AttachTriggeredRule`, which handles "attach it to target [filter] you control" — there the object being attached TO is a fresh target, not the triggering object.

Tightly anchored (^…$) to the bare "[you may] attach this &lt;type&gt; to it" sentence so this rule only claims the whole effect fragment when there is nothing else in it — the higher-priority compound rules (`AuraLosesGainsEnchantReturnAndAttachRule` at 95, `YouMayPayReturnAndAttachEquipmentRule` at 81) already own the longer "…and attach this [Aura|Equipment] to it" tails that appear inside a multi-effect sentence, and this rule's anchoring means it can never steal a match from within those compounds even if dispatch order changed.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AttachThisEquipmentToItTriggeredRule.cs)

### `AttachTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"attach it to target [filter] you control" — an explicit attach instruction inside a triggered ability. Covers the ETB auto-attach pattern common on Equipment: "When this Equipment enters, attach it to target creature you control."

Rule 701.3: "To take an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification from where it currently is and put it onto a specified object or player." MAST records the oracle-text instruction descriptively; the legality checks, zone-change details, and resulting continuous effects are engine territory.

Distinct from `EquipEffect`, which models the Equip activated-ability keyword (Rule 702.6). This rule handles explicit "attach it to target" instructions in triggered ability effects.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AttachTriggeredRule.cs)

### `AttackWithAndAnotherConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you attack with [Name] and another [qualifier] creature" (Merry shape) — models the companion-attack trigger (Rule 508). Emits `Attacks` with a companion-creature filter carrying the structured ExcludeSelf self-exclusion plus any supertype qualifier.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AttackWithAndAnotherConditionRule.cs)

### `AttackWithNumberOrMoreCreaturesConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you attack with two or more creatures, [effect]" — an attacker-count-gated attack-declaration trigger (Military Intelligence). Emits `Attacks` with `MinimumCount` set to the named threshold and a creature-you-control filter.

CR 508.3c: "An ability that reads "Whenever [a player] attacks with [a creature], . . ." triggers if a creature that player controls is declared as an attacker."

CR 508.3d: "An ability that reads "Whenever [a player] attacks, . . ." triggers if one or more creatures that player controls are declared as attackers." (supports the "two or more" count framing on top of the base attack-declaration event.)

CR 508.1a: "The active player chooses which creatures that they control, if any, will attack. ..." — justifies the Filter's Controller = You.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AttackWithNumberOrMoreCreaturesConditionRule.cs)

### `AttacksAnOpponentConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever [CardName] attacks an opponent" — emits `AttacksAnOpponent` (CR 508 — Declare Attackers Step; CR 102.2 — opponent = player not on the controller's team).

Distinguished from the plain `AttacksConditionRule` (Event: Attacks) by the presence of "an opponent" after "attacks". The "attacks an opponent" phrasing constrains the attack target to a player (not a planeswalker or battle), so the trigger fires only when the creature is declared as attacking a player who is an opponent of its controller.

Priority 990 — above `AttacksConditionRule` (Priority 987) so the opponent-specific form is matched first and never falls through to the generic "attacks" rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AttacksAnOpponentConditionRule.cs)

### `AttacksConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever [CardName] attacks" / "Whenever this creature attacks" / "Whenever a creature you control attacks" — emits `Attacks` (Rule 508 — Declare Attackers). The filter shape is shared with dies/enters via `ParseObjectFilter`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AttacksConditionRule.cs)

### `AttacksFirstTimeEachTurnConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever [subject] attacks for the first time each turn" — a once-per-turn attack trigger that fires only on the subject's first attack in a given turn.

Produces a `TriggerCondition` with `Attacks`, `Ordinal` = 1, and `PerTurn` = true, matching the encoding used for other first-N-per-turn ordinal triggers (e.g. Lat-Nam Adept's second draw each turn). CR 603.2: the trigger fires on the first event that matches the condition within the qualifying window; subsequent attacks that turn do not re-trigger.

Priority 988 — above the generic `AttacksConditionRule` (Priority 987) so this more-specific ordinal form is matched first. Both rules share the same surface verb "attacks"; the ordinal qualifier "for the first time each turn" distinguishes them. The pattern is anchored (^...$) so it cannot silently consume a sibling trigger that merely contains "attacks for the first time" as a substring of a longer phrase.

CR 603.2: triggered abilities trigger every time the event they specify occurs; the Ordinal + PerTurn qualification narrows which occurrence of that event actually fires the ability, recorded descriptively — the per-turn counter is engine territory.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AttacksFirstTimeEachTurnConditionRule.cs)

### `AttacksOrBlocksConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever [subject] attacks or blocks" — combined combat trigger (Rule 508/509), modelled as a single `AttacksOrBlocks` event. Tried before the individual Attacks/Blocks rules (higher priority) so the disjunction isn't partially matched.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AttacksOrBlocksConditionRule.cs)

### `AttacksPlayerAndIsntBlockedConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Compound trigger condition: "this creature attacks a player and isn't blocked" — fires when the creature attacks and the compound condition holds. Produces a plain `Attacks` trigger on self; the compound qualifier "attacks a player and isn't blocked" is communicated as a pending `PendingInterveningIf` for `TriggeredAbilityParser` to pick up.

Rule 508.1: "The active player declares attackers" — attack target is a player (not a planeswalker or battle). Rule 509 (declare-blockers step): "isn't blocked" is the state immediately after blockers are declared. Together they form the compound condition governing when this trigger fires.

Must be tried at higher priority (Priority = 990) than `AttacksConditionRule` (Priority = 987) so this specific compound form is matched before the generic "attacks" rule consumes the text and drops the "a player and isn't blocked" qualifier. The pattern is anchored (^...$) so it cannot silently match as a substring.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AttacksPlayerAndIsntBlockedConditionRule.cs)

### `AttacksWithPowerComparisonConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever [a creature you control] with power N or less/greater attacks" — an attack trigger whose subject filter carries a printed power threshold (Cavalcade of Calamity: "Whenever a creature you control with power 1 or less attacks, …"). Produces the same `Attacks` condition as the generic `AttacksConditionRule` (Rule 508 — Declare Attackers), but augments the subject `ObjectFilter` with a `Comparison` on the `PowerComparison` axis so the "with power N or less" qualifier is not silently dropped.

Priority 991 — above the generic `AttacksConditionRule` (Priority 987), whose `ParseObjectFilter` ignores the power qualifier and would otherwise claim the trigger first with a power-less filter. The pattern is anchored on the right ("… with power N or (less|greater) attacks$") so it cannot consume a sibling trigger that merely contains "attacks" elsewhere; the base filter (card type + controller) is resolved by the shared `ParseObjectFilter` after the power clause is stripped, keeping this rule's own surface additive.

CR 508.1a (declare attackers). The threshold is recorded descriptively on the filter — MAST states the printed constraint; the engine evaluates it against the actual power of the attacking creature.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AttacksWithPowerComparisonConditionRule.cs)

### `AuraDealsDamageToPlayerOrPlaneswalkerRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"this Aura deals N damage to that player or a planeswalker that player controls." — the upkeep-damage trigger of a player-enchanting Curse (Curse of the Pierced Heart). The "or" is a single chooser-selected reference, so the damage Target is a `Choice` over two options: the enchanted player ("that player", on a player Aura = the enchanted player) and a planeswalker that player controls.

Rule 120 (dealing damage); Rule 702.5 (Enchant player — the enchanted player is the Aura's enchanted object). The chooser picks exactly one option at resolution, so a single Choice reference is correct rather than two targets.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AuraDealsDamageToPlayerOrPlaneswalkerRule.cs)

### `AuraLosesGainsEnchantReturnAndAttachRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Recognises the multi-effect sentence produced by Animate Dead's ETB resolution: <c>it loses "enchant creature card in a graveyard" and gains "enchant creature put onto the battlefield with this Aura." Return enchanted creature card to the battlefield under your control and attach this Aura to it.</c>

This sentence is the first sentence in the complex ETB ability's effect body. It produces four effects in sequence:

`LoseAbilityEffect` — "it" (the Aura, `Self`) loses the quoted enchant ability text (captured on the free-text `AbilityText` field, which is a typed residual per ADR 0001). `GainAbilityEffect` — "it" gains a new static `EnchantRestrictionEffect` targeting any creature (the revised enchant restriction once the Aura is on the battlefield). `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect` — returns the enchanted creature card (`EnchantedOrEquipped`) to the battlefield under the controller's control. `AttachEffect` — attaches this Aura to "it" (`It` — the creature just returned).

CR 702.5 (Enchant — Aura ability); CR 303.4 (Aura attachment to a permanent); CR 400.6 (entering under a specific player's control); CR 701.3 (Attach). CR 614.1 (replacement effects for the new enchant restriction on entry).

The overall pattern: <c>^it loses "(?&lt;lost&gt;.+?)" and gains "enchant creature put onto the battlefield with this (?:Aura|enchantment)\.?" Return enchanted creature card to the battlefield under your control and attach this Aura to it\.?$</c> This is narrow enough to be safely anchored — the combination of "loses" + quoted text + "gains" + "enchant creature put onto the battlefield with this Aura" is unique to the Animate Dead / Dance of the Dead family.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/AuraLosesGainsEnchantReturnAndAttachRule.cs)

### `BecomeMonarchTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you become the monarch." — Rule 725. The controller of the source permanent becomes the monarch game-state designation. MAST records the descriptive instruction; the draw-at-end-step and combat-damage-transfer rules (725.2–725.6) are engine territory.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/BecomeMonarchTriggeredRule.cs)

### `BecomesBlockedConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever this creature becomes blocked" — Rule 509 (Declare Blockers Step). Fires on the attacking creature when one or more blockers are assigned to it. The `BecomesBlocked` event is distinct from `Blocks` (the blocking creature's trigger).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/BecomesBlockedConditionRule.cs)

### `BecomesCrewedConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever this Vehicle becomes crewed [for the first time each turn]" — Rule 702.122 trigger.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/BecomesCrewedConditionRule.cs)

### `BecomesTappedConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever this creature becomes tapped" — CR 603.2: "Some trigger events use the word 'becomes' (for example, 'becomes attached' or 'becomes blocked'). These trigger only at the time the named event happens... An ability that triggers when a permanent 'becomes tapped' or 'becomes untapped' doesn't trigger if the permanent enters the battlefield in that state." The `BecomesTapped` event is distinct from `TapsForMana` (which fires specifically on tapping for mana, not any tapping).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/BecomesTappedConditionRule.cs)

### `BecomesTargetConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"When this creature becomes the target of a spell or ability" — triggered-ability machinery: Rule 603.1-603.2; "becomes the target" relationship: Rule 115.1. The subject "this creature" is the source permanent; only the self-reference shape is modelled here.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/BecomesTargetConditionRule.cs)

### `BecomesUnattachedConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever this Equipment becomes unattached from a permanent" — Stitcher's Graft.

CR 701.3d (verbatim): "To 'unattach' an Equipment from a creature means to move it away from that creature so the Equipment is on the battlefield but is not equipping anything. It should no longer be physically touching any creature. If an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification that was attached to an object or player ceases to be attached to it, that counts as 'becoming unattached [from that object or player]'; this includes if that Aura, Equipment, or Fortification leaves the battlefield, the object leaves the zone it was in, or that player leaves the game."

Emits `BecomesUnattached`. The `Filter` carries the "from a permanent" complement — the object the source became unattached from — NOT the source ("this Equipment") itself, mirroring the Flanking convention where the trigger's Filter names the OTHER object needed for a later back-reference ("that permanent" → `ThatPermanent`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/BecomesUnattachedConditionRule.cs)

### `BecomesUntappedConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever this artifact becomes untapped" — CR 603.2: "Some trigger events use the word 'becomes' (for example, 'becomes attached' or 'becomes blocked'). These trigger only at the time the named event happens... An ability that triggers when a permanent 'becomes tapped' or 'becomes untapped' doesn't trigger if the permanent enters the battlefield in that state." Sibling of `BecomesTappedConditionRule`, which handles the "becomes tapped" half of the same rules text; this rule targets the `BecomesUntapped` event.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/BecomesUntappedConditionRule.cs)

### `BlocksConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever this creature blocks" / "Whenever [CardName] blocks" / "Whenever this creature blocks a creature" — Rule 509 (Declare Blockers Step). Excludes "becomes blocked" (BecomesBlocked event), which also contains "blocks".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/BlocksConditionRule.cs)

### `BlocksOrBecomesBlockedConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever this creature blocks or becomes blocked" — combined combat trigger (CR 702.45 Bushido). Fires from the perspective of BOTH the blocking creature (Rule 509 — it declared as a blocker) AND the attacked creature (Rule 509 — a blocker was assigned to it). Modelled as a single `BlocksOrBecomesBlocked` event. Tried before the individual Blocks/BecomesBlocked rules (higher priority) so the disjunction is not partially matched.

CR 702.45 (verbatim): "Bushido is a triggered ability. 'Bushido N' means 'Whenever this creature blocks or becomes blocked, it gets +N/+N until end of turn.'"

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/BlocksOrBecomesBlockedConditionRule.cs)

### `CantBlockThisTurnTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Handles the triggered-ability effect shape "target [filter] can't block this turn." CR 603.6a: Enters-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield. Written "When [this object] enters, ..." or "Whenever a [type] enters, ..." CR 509.1 (declare-blockers step): a "can't block" restriction applies during the declare-blockers turn-based action. The effect is durative — it expires at the end of the current turn (`untilEndOfTurn`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CantBlockThisTurnTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CardPutIntoOpponentGraveyardConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Recognises "a [type] card is put into an opponent's graveyard from anywhere" — the trigger event that fires whenever any card moves to an opponent's graveyard from any zone (Bloodchief Ascension, ZEN).

CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." The matched event is a card entering a graveyard (CR 701.7 — "put into a graveyard"). The destination is specifically an opponent's graveyard rather than the controller's own graveyard (CR 102.2 — "opponent" is any player not on the same team). The "from anywhere" clause omits a source-zone restriction.

The controller axis (`Opponent`) on the filter identifies whose graveyard receives the card, mirroring the `You` convention in the sibling `PutIntoGraveyardConditionRule`.

Representative card: Bloodchief Ascension (ZEN) — "Whenever a card is put into an opponent's graveyard from anywhere, if this enchantment has three or more quest counters on it, …" Rule citations: CR 603.2 (Triggered Abilities), CR 701.7 (Put into a graveyard), CR 102.2 (Opponent).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CardPutIntoOpponentGraveyardConditionRule.cs)

### `CardsLeaveGraveyardAggregateConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever one or more cards leave your graveyard, ..." — the aggregate (untyped) leave-graveyard trigger (Quintorius, Field Historian).

CR 603.2 (verbatim): "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." The "one or more" qualifier is a threshold condition on the trigger event, recorded structurally on `MinimumCount` (=1) — the same convention used by `SacrificeOneOrMoreSubtypeConditionRule` for the analogous "you sacrifice one or more [Subtype]s" shape. The event maps to `LeavesGraveyard`, which already exists for the untyped-card "a card leaves your graveyard" concept (documented on the enum member with Syr Konrad, the Grim as the singular-form precedent). The filter carries the generic `CardTypes = ["card"]` (no type restriction — "cards", not "creature cards" or "land cards") plus `Controller = You` ("your graveyard").

Distinct from `SyrKonradTripleOrConditionRule`'s tertiary clause, which is the SINGULAR "a creature card leaves your graveyard" (no "one or more", type-restricted to creature) embedded inside a three-event compound trigger — that rule's anchored pattern spans the full triple-or phrase and cannot match this simpler, standalone shape (and vice versa).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CardsLeaveGraveyardAggregateConditionRule.cs)

### `CastAuraSpellConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you cast an Aura spell" (Kor Spiritdancer family). Aura is an enchantment <em>subtype</em> (Rule 205.3h), so the cast filter is recorded as `Subtypes = ["Aura"]` rather than a card-type characteristic — the distinction that `SpellCastConditionRule` cannot express (its per-word loop matches card types like "creature"/"noncreature", and it has no subtype channel). Sits above `SpellCastConditionRule` (priority 998) so the Aura subtype qualifier is captured instead of being silently dropped by the generic spell-cast recognizer.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CastAuraSpellConditionRule.cs)

### `CastCreatureSpellWithManaValueConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"you cast a creature spell with mana value N or greater" — a cast trigger narrowed by a mana-value threshold on the cast spell (Kalemne, Disciple of Iroas: "Whenever you cast a creature spell with mana value 5 or greater, you get an experience counter.").

Distinct from the general `SpellCastConditionRule` (priority 998) which recognises card-type/color qualifiers on the cast spell but has no mana-value axis, so it would silently drop the "with mana value N or greater" threshold. Mirrors `CreatureWithManaValueEntersConditionRule` (the enters-trigger sibling) by landing the threshold on the filter's `ManaValueComparison` axis. CR 202.3 (mana value) / CR 601 (casting spells) / CR 603.2 (a game event matching the trigger event triggers the ability).

Runs at priority 999, above `SpellCastConditionRule` (998), so this more-specific mana-value-gated form is matched first. End-anchored (mirrors `ColorlessSpellCastConditionRule`/`CreatureWithManaValueEntersConditionRule`): `triggerText` still carries the leading timing word ("Whenever"), so the pattern is NOT start-anchored, only word-boundary + end-anchored, so it cannot substring-match a longer or differently-qualified sibling clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CastCreatureSpellWithManaValueConditionRule.cs)

### `CastOrCopyInstantOrSorceryConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you cast or copy an instant or sorcery spell" — the Magecraft ability-word trigger condition (CR 207.2c: "magecraft" is listed as an ability word with no rules meaning of its own; the trigger text is the mechanical definition).

CR 707.10: "To copy a spell … means to put a copy of it onto the stack; a copy of a spell isn't cast." The disjunction "cast or copy" therefore covers both the casting event and the copy event, which is why this rule produces `CastOrCopySpell` rather than `SpellCast`.

ANCHORED (`^…$`) on the trigger text after the timing word so that the matcher cannot fire as a substring inside a more-specific sibling (e.g. a bare "cast a spell" trigger). Priority 999 — above `SpellCastConditionRule` (998) so the more-specific "cast or copy" disjunction is recognised before the plain "cast" rule can claim the text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CastOrCopyInstantOrSorceryConditionRule.cs)

### `CastsNthSpellEachTurnConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever an opponent casts their first noncreature spell each turn" (Shadow in the Warp) — the ordinal-qualified spell-cast trigger (CR 601: Casting Spells; CR 603.2: the event-match is the trigger). Sibling of `DrawNthCardEachTurnConditionRule`: the oracle text names a specific occurrence within the turn ("their <i>first</i> ... spell") and a per-turn counting window ("each turn"), recorded descriptively on `Ordinal`/`PerTurn` rather than any turn-state counting machinery — the ordinal merely narrows which cast-event match counts, it does not model the tally itself.

Distinct from the unqualified `SpellCastConditionRule` ("Whenever [x] casts a spell", no ordinal/per-turn qualifier). Priority 999 (just above SpellCastConditionRule's 998) so this more specific ordinal shape is tried first and doesn't get swallowed by the generic one. "Noncreature" maps to the existing `ExcludedCardTypes=["creature"]` negation axis, matching how `SpellCastConditionRule` already encodes it.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CastsNthSpellEachTurnConditionRule.cs)

### `ChooseAndPutAdditionalCounterOfChosenKindRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Choose a counter on target permanent. Put an additional counter of that kind on that permanent." — Ichormoon Gauntlet's triggered ability effect.

ANCHOR: fully anchored (^...$) over the combined two-sentence effect so it cannot match as a substring of other triggered effect text. The two-sentence structure is matched as a unit because splitting them by ". " would lose the "of that kind" anaphor linking the second sentence to the choice made in the first.

CR 122.1: counters are placed on permanents; the chosen kind must already be present. This produces a `PutAdditionalCounterOfChosenKindEffect` whose `Target` is the "target permanent" reference established by "choose a counter on target permanent".

Priority 999: fires before generic put-counter rules to avoid partial matches.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ChooseAndPutAdditionalCounterOfChosenKindRule.cs)

### `ChosenPlayerPhaseTriggerConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"At the beginning of the chosen player's upkeep" (The Rack) — the clock-point possessive bound to the CR 614.12 as-enters player choice (`ChoosePlayerEffect`) rather than to "your"/"each opponent's"/"each player's" (CR 109.5 — "that player" downstream references resolve to whichever player the clock point names). Maps the phase/step word to the same `TurnPart` vocabulary as `PhaseTriggerConditionRule`, binding `Whose` to `ChosenPlayer`.

A SEPARATE rule rather than an added branch on `PhaseTriggerConditionRule` (a shared, high-traffic fallback with no per-branch anchor of its own): this rule requires the ANCHORED "chosen player" cue and is dispatched at a higher priority so it intercepts before the shared rule would otherwise match with an unset (null) `Whose`, silently losing the chosen-player binding. "chosen player" never appears in the "your"/"each opponent"/"each player"/"enchanted player" cues the shared rule already checks, so the two rules are disjoint and this addition cannot regress any sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ChosenPlayerPhaseTriggerConditionRule.cs)

### `ColorlessSpellCastConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"you cast a colorless spell" — trigger condition for watching colorless spell casts. Distinct from the general `SpellCastConditionRule` (priority 998) which handles color-word qualifiers (white, blue, black, red, green) but not "colorless". Colorless is not a color (Rule 105.1: "Colorless is not a color."), so it is encoded via `IsColorless` rather than the `Colors` axis. Running at priority 999 ensures this rule is tried before the general rule. Examples: Forsaken Monument — "Whenever you cast a colorless spell, you gain 2 life."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ColorlessSpellCastConditionRule.cs)

### `CommitsCrimeConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you commit a crime" — the crime-mechanic trigger (CR 700.13).

CR 700.13: "A player commits a crime as that player casts a spell, activates an ability, or puts a triggered ability on the stack and that spell or ability targets at least one opponent; at least one permanent, spell, or ability an opponent controls; and/or at least one card in an opponent's graveyard."

The trigger fires on the controller ("you"), encoded as `You` on the filter. The crime definition is purely a rules term (CR 700.13); its expansion is engine territory. MAST records only the canonical event label `CommitsACrime` and the controller constraint.

The phrase "Whenever you commit a crime" is unique and cannot appear as a substring of a more-specific trigger phrase, so no priority elevation is needed. The anchor on `_pattern` is full-string (^…$) to guard against future sibling triggers that might extend the phrase.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CommitsCrimeConditionRule.cs)

### `ConditionalPaySubtypeCounterTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Handles "you may pay {COST}. If you do, put a +1/+1 counter on it. If it's a [Subtype], put two +1/+1 counters on it instead." — the optional-pay triggered ability with a subtype-conditional counter boost (Emiel the Blessed pattern).

The effect is an `OptionalEffect` wrapping a `ConditionalPayEffect`; the `IfYouDo` consequence is a `ConditionalEffect` whose `Condition` is an `ObjectHasSubtypeCondition` (CR 205.3m — creature subtypes). When the subtype matches, two +1/+1 counters are placed (the "instead" branch — the `Then`); otherwise one counter (the `Else`). "instead" signals a replacement of the base action for the qualified subtype — modelled as an if-then-else rather than a sequential pair so the engine knows that the one-counter placement does NOT happen for Unicorns.

Priority 85: higher than `ConditionalPayTriggeredRule` (Priority 80) so this specific subtype-counter shape is claimed first; the generic conditional-pay handler never sees this text. Anchored sub-patterns guard against substring capture on sibling rules that match on "{counter} counter(s)".

CR 122.1 (verbatim): "A counter is a marker placed on an object or player that modifies its characteristics and/or interacts with a rule, ability, or effect." CR 205.3m (verbatim): "Creature subtypes are always a single word and are listed after a long dash on the card's type line." CR 602.1 / CR 603.2: activated/triggered ability structure.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ConditionalPaySubtypeCounterTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ConditionalPayTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Handles "you may pay {COST}. If you do, [effect]." conditional-pay triggers and the discard-as-cost loot variant "you may discard a card. If you do, draw a card."

Two shapes:

<b>Mana-pay shape</b>: "you may pay {N}. If you do, [EFFECT]." → `ConditionalPayEffect` with the mana cost on `Cost` and the parsed consequent on `IfYouDo`. Example: "Whenever a creature dies, you may pay {1}. If you do, you gain 1 life." (Deathgreeter, ALA). <b>Discard-loot shape</b>: "you may discard [N] card(s). If you do, draw [M] card(s)." → `DiscardCardsEffect` with `IsOptional = true` and `IfYouDo = DrawCardsEffect`. Mirrors the spell-level `DiscardThenDrawSpellRule`.

Priority 80: both shapes contain the trigger text "you may [action]. If you do," as a prefix. Without elevated priority the discard-loot shape would race against the plain `EachOpponentDiscardsRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ConditionalPayTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ConniveTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it connives." — Rule 701.50a keyword action on the triggered side. Matches the canonical ETB-connive pattern where the entering creature (referred to as "it") performs the Connive keyword action.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ConniveTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ControlNoLandTypeConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"When you control no [LandSubtype]" — state-triggered ability (Rule 603). Fires when the controlling player transitions to controlling no lands of the named basic-land subtype (e.g. "When you control no Islands, sacrifice this creature."). Expanded oracle for the obsolete Islandhome family. The land subtype is stored in Filter.Subtypes; CardTypes=["land"], Controller=You.

Supported subtypes: Island, Forest, Swamp, Mountain, Plains.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ControlNoLandTypeConditionRule.cs)

### `ControlNoLandsConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"When you control no lands, [effect]." — a state-triggered ability (CR 603.8 — "Some triggered abilities trigger when a game state (such as a player controlling no permanents of a particular card type) is true", i.e. a state trigger, NOT the CR 603.2e "becomes"-transition trigger). Fires when the controlling player transitions to controlling zero lands of any kind (no basic-land-subtype qualifier), distinct from `ControlNoLandTypeConditionRule`, which matches the Islandhome-style "when you control no [Islands|Forests|Swamps|Mountains|Plains]" subtype-scoped form. Both share `ControlNoLandType` — the underlying state-trigger shape is identical; the only structural difference is whether the Filter carries a `Subtypes` restriction. Here it does not: the filter is simply "a land" (CardTypes=["land"], Controller=You), matching the "a land" / "another land" filter convention used elsewhere for the unqualified land type (`ParseObjectFilter`).

Example: Serendib Djinn (ARN): "When you control no lands, sacrifice this creature."

ANCHORED (`^…$`) on the literal "you control no lands" surface so this cannot claim any subtype-qualified sibling ("you control no Islands", etc.) — those retain the more specific `ControlNoLandTypeConditionRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ControlNoLandsConditionRule.cs)

### `ControllerMayDrawIfGreatestPowerTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"its controller may draw a card if its power is greater than each other creature's power" — Selvala, Heart of the Wilds ETB trigger pattern.

The entering creature's controller gets an optional draw, but only when the entering creature has strictly greater power than every other creature on the battlefield. CR 603.5: an optional triggered effect ("may") goes on the stack regardless of whether the controller intends to exercise it; the choice is made on resolution. CR 121.1: drawing a card is placing the top card of the library into hand.

AST shape: `ConditionalEffect` whose `Condition` is an `OtherCondition` residual (the relative-maximum-power predicate "its power is greater than each other creature's power" has no structured `GreatestPowerCondition` node — PB-7 debt) and whose `Then` is an `OptionalEffect` wrapping a `DrawCardsEffect` targeting the creature's controller (`ThatPlayer`).

"Its controller" is the controller of the entering creature (the trigger's subject), not the ability's controller ("you"). Encoded as `ThatPlayer` following the Smothering Tithe convention (CR 109.5 — the controller of an object is the player who controls it).

The rule is fully anchored (`^…$`) so it cannot match as a substring inside a more-specific sibling's text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ControllerMayDrawIfGreatestPowerTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CopyAllSpellsAndAbilitiesTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Handles the Ulalek, Fused Atrocity triggered-ability effect: "you may pay {COST}. If you do, copy all spells you control, then copy all other activated and triggered abilities you control. You may choose new targets for the copies."

The effect decomposes as:

`OptionalEffect` (the "you may" wrapper) `ConditionalPayEffect` as the `Inner` — the mana cost the controller may optionally pay. `CompositeEffect` as the `IfYouDo` — two `CopyEffect` nodes with `MayChooseNewTargets = true`: "copy all spells you control" → `Each` + filter `CardTypes=["spell"], Controller=You, Zone=Stack` "copy all other activated and triggered abilities you control" → `Each` + filter <c>CardTypes=["activatedAbility","triggeredAbility"], Controller=You, Zone=Stack, ExcludeSelf=true</c> — the word "other" excludes the source ability itself (this triggered ability of Ulalek), CR 109.5. Both copies carry `MayChooseNewTargets = true` because the retarget grant in "You may choose new targets for the copies" applies to all copies produced by this ability. CR 707.10.

Priority 90: must run BEFORE `ConditionalPayTriggeredRule` (priority 80), whose `TryParseIfYouDoEffect` cannot handle a composite copy-all consequent and would reject the full text, leaving the ability unparsed. This rule takes priority because it is more specific.

CR 707.10: "To copy a spell, activated ability, or triggered ability means to put a copy of it onto the stack." The copies are placed onto the stack; the controller then may choose new targets for each copy independently (CR 707.10b / CR 117.7).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CopyAllSpellsAndAbilitiesTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CopyItForEachPrecedingSpellTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"copy it for each other instant and sorcery spell you've cast before it this turn. You may choose new targets for the copies." — Thousand-Year Storm's triggered effect.

The copy count equals the number of other instant and sorcery spells the controller cast earlier this turn (the "storm count" for instants/sorceries). Each copy represents one preceding spell in the cast sequence. The count is expressed as a `CountQuantity` over an `ObjectFilter` with `CastThisTurnPredicate` (Caster=You) and `ExcludeSelf` = true (the "other" qualifier, excluding the triggering spell itself, CR 109.5).

"Before it this turn" — the temporal ordering qualifier restricting the count to spells cast earlier in the turn rather than the full "this turn" set — is engine-execution semantics (CR 603.1: a triggered ability fires once the triggering event occurs; the storm-count state is tracked by the engine, not by the AST descriptor). MAST records the "other [filter] spells cast this turn" reference (ExcludeSelf + CastThisTurnPredicate); the ordering is implied by the trigger event itself and not separately encoded.

CR 707.10: "To copy a spell, activated ability, or triggered ability means to put a copy of it onto the stack; a copy of a spell isn't cast." CR 702.40a: "Storm" is the keyword for the analogous "copy for each spell cast before it this turn" mechanic on a spell itself; Thousand-Year Storm is a standing enchantment that applies a Magecraft-style storm effect to instants and sorceries only. CR 603.1: "Triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect."

"You may choose new targets for the copies" is the structured retarget permission carried on `MayChooseNewTargets` — a rules-meaningful flag, not free text (CR 707.10c).

Priority 76: must run BEFORE `CopyTriggeringSpellTriggeredRule` (priority 74), which handles the shorter "copy it. You may choose new targets for the copy." body and would fail to match this longer clause, but to be safe this more-specific rule runs first. The pattern is ANCHORED (^…$) so it cannot match as a substring of a more-specific sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CopyItForEachPrecedingSpellTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CopyTargetSpellTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"copy target instant or sorcery spell. You may choose new targets for the copy." — the resolution clause of Dualcaster Mage's ETB trigger (and the broader "copy a spell on the stack" family).

CR 707.10: "To copy a spell, activated ability, or triggered ability means to put a copy of it onto the stack; a copy of a spell isn't cast and a copy of an activated ability isn't activated." The copy source is a targeted spell on the stack — modelled as an `Target` reference whose filter pins the instant-or-sorcery card types in `Stack`.

The optional second sentence "You may choose new targets for the copy" is the structured retarget permission carried on `MayChooseNewTargets` — a rules-meaningful flag, not free text. The whole two-sentence body is matched as one effect so the retarget permission rides the copy rather than splitting into a spurious second effect.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CopyTargetSpellTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CopyTriggeringAbilityConditionalPayTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Rings of Brighthearth's conditional-pay copy-the-triggering-ability effect: "you may pay {COST}. If you do, copy that ability. You may choose new targets for the copy."

Decomposes as the canonical "you may pay [cost]. If you do, [Y]" shape (Nim Deathmantle pattern):

`OptionalEffect` — the "you may" wrapper. `ConditionalPayEffect` as `Inner` — the mana cost the controller may optionally pay. `CopyEffect` as `IfYouDo` — the copy of the triggering ability. `Target` is `TriggeringAbility` ("that ability" — the activated/triggered ability on the stack named by the `AbilityActivated` trigger, CR 113), and `MayChooseNewTargets = true` ("You may choose new targets for the copy", CR 707.10b).

Priority 90: must run BEFORE the generic `ConditionalPayTriggeredRule` (priority 80), whose consequent delegation cannot structure "copy that ability" into the `TriggeringAbility` reference and would leave a residual. This rule is more specific (it owns the full anchored clause).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the clause is matched in full so no sibling conditional-pay text is mislabeled.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CopyTriggeringAbilityConditionalPayTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CopyTriggeringSpellConditionalPayTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Mirari's conditional-pay copy-the-triggering-spell effect: "you may pay {COST}. If you do, copy that spell. You may choose new targets for the copy."

Decomposes as the canonical "you may pay [cost]. If you do, [Y]" shape (Nim Deathmantle pattern), the spell-side twin of `CopyTriggeringAbilityConditionalPayTriggeredRule` (Rings of Brighthearth's "copy that ability"):

`OptionalEffect` — the "you may" wrapper. `ConditionalPayEffect` as `Inner` — the mana cost the controller may optionally pay. `CopyEffect` as `IfYouDo` — the copy of the triggering spell. `Target` is `It` — the anaphoric back-reference to the triggering spell named by the enclosing `SpellCast` trigger (the MAST pronoun convention: "that spell" ≡ "it", as in `CopyTriggeringSpellTriggeredRule`'s "copy it" and `CounterThatSpellTriggeredRule`'s "counter that spell"), and `MayChooseNewTargets = true` ("You may choose new targets for the copy", CR 707.10b).

Priority 90: must run BEFORE the generic `ConditionalPayTriggeredRule` (priority 80), whose consequent delegation list does not structure "copy that spell" and would leave a residual. This rule is more specific (it owns the full anchored clause).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the clause is matched in full so no sibling conditional-pay text is mislabeled. The "copy that spell" surface here is distinct from the Rings "copy that ability" surface owned by the twin rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CopyTriggeringSpellConditionalPayTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CopyTriggeringSpellTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"copy it. You may choose new targets for the copy." — the resolution clause of triggers that copy the triggering spell (e.g. Echoes of Eternity: "Whenever you cast a colorless spell, copy it. You may choose new targets for the copy.").

Distinct from `CopyTargetSpellTriggeredRule` (which handles "copy target instant or sorcery spell") — here the copy target is "it": a pronoun referring to the colorless spell named by the trigger condition (i.e. the spell that caused the trigger to fire). The reference is `It` rather than an explicit targeted filter.

CR 707.10: "To copy a spell, activated ability, or triggered ability means to put a copy of it onto the stack." The reminder text "(A copy of a permanent spell becomes a token.)" is engine semantics carried on the enclosing `Reminder`, not modeled in the effect node.

"You may choose new targets for the copy" is the structured retarget permission carried on `MayChooseNewTargets` — a rules-meaningful flag, not free text. The whole two-sentence body is matched as one effect so the retarget permission rides the copy rather than splitting into a spurious second effect.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CopyTriggeringSpellTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CounterPutOnCreaturePassiveConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"a -1/-1 counter is put on a creature" — passive counter-placement trigger (Flourishing Defenses).

CR 122.1: "A counter is a marker placed on an object or player that modifies its characteristics and/or interacts with a rule or effect." This trigger fires whenever any player places a -1/-1 counter on any creature (passive voice: "is put on"). Unlike `PutNegativeCountersOnCreatureConditionRule` which covers "you put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature" (controller-scoped, "one or more" quantity), this rule covers the broader "a [counter] is put on a creature" (any player, single counter, passive). The event is still `CounterPlaced` with `CounterType="-1/-1"` and `MinimumCount=1` (any single counter placement fires this trigger).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CounterPutOnCreaturePassiveConditionRule.cs)

### `CounterThatSpellTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"counter that spell" — a bare counter effect that counters the spell referenced by the trigger's own event (the "that" pronoun anaphoric back-reference to the triggering spell). Encodes as `CounterSpellEffect` with `Target = { Kind: It }` — the `It` reference follows the MAST pronoun convention: the object named by the trigger condition (analogous to the Ward-keyword "counter it" shape; WilsonRefinedGrizzly gold fixture). CR 701.6a: "To counter a spell or ability means to cancel it, removing it from the stack. It doesn't resolve and none of its effects occur. A countered spell is put into its owner's graveyard." This rule is collision-free: anchored (^…$) so it cannot match as a substring of a more-specific sibling (e.g. CounterSpellRule's "counter target spell" or CounterUnlessPaysRule's "counter it unless …"). The surface phrase "counter that spell" occurs only in this bare-counter pattern; the Ward shape uses "counter it" (handled by the Ward combinator, not this rule) and the spell rules use "counter target spell". Priority 80: above the general-purpose rules (50) so the bare anaphoric form is claimed before a broader match could fire.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CounterThatSpellTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CreateColorlessTokenWithSacrificeManaAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create a [P/T] colorless [Subtype(s)] creature token with 'Sacrifice this token: Add {C}.'" — colorless creature token whose only ability is a sacrifice-for-mana activated ability.

This covers Eldrazi Spawn and Eldrazi Scion tokens (CR 701.6: "Create" puts a token on the battlefield; CR 111.1: a token is a marker representing a permanent that isn't a card). The token has a single activated mana ability (CR 605.1a: an activated ability that doesn't require a target and could add mana is a mana ability): "Sacrifice this token: Add {C}." The sacrifice cost targets the token itself (CR 701.21a), encoded via `IsSelf` = `true` on the `Filter`.

Runs at priority 75, above the generic `CreateTokenRule` (default 50), so this specific shape is matched first and the generic rule never overwrites the token's structured ability with an empty ability list.

Example: Glaring Fleshraker — "create a 0/1 colorless Eldrazi Spawn creature token with \"Sacrifice this token: Add {C}.\""

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateColorlessTokenWithSacrificeManaAbilityRule.cs)

### `CreateCopyOfEquippedCreatureTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create a token that's a copy of equipped creature, except the token isn't legendary. That token gains haste." — Helm of the Host's combat trigger resolution. Produces a single `CopyEffect` whose `Target` is the equipped creature and whose `Modifications` carry both "except"-style overrides on the copy: it isn't legendary (`SupertypeRemover`) and it gains haste (`AbilityAdder`).

CR 111.1: "A token is a marker used to represent any permanent that isn't represented by a card." CR 707.2: "When copying an object, the copy acquires the copiable values of the original object's characteristics…" — the two modifications override copiable values the token would otherwise inherit. The trailing "That token gains haste." sentence is folded into the same `CopyEffect` as a haste modification (one oracle line → one copy with its modifications), not split into a separate gain-ability effect. "equipped creature" is the `EnchantedOrEquipped` reference (CR 301.5c).

Priority 70 — more specific than the generic create-token rules so the "copy of equipped creature" phrasing is claimed here first. The rule matches the whole two-sentence body; the dispatcher's sentence-bundle pre-pass bails (the "That token gains haste" sentence has no standalone rule), so the full body reaches this rule intact.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateCopyOfEquippedCreatureTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CreateCopyOfThatCreatureNotLegendaryWithTypeAndColorTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create a token that's a copy of that creature, except it's not legendary and it's a [P]/[T] [color] [Subtype] in addition to its other colors and types." The Ratadrabik of Urborg pattern: a copy of the dying creature with three structured "except"-clauses applied in order:

`SupertypeRemover` strips Legendary (CR 704.5j — legend rule would otherwise cull the token copy if the original creature is still on the battlefield). `PowerToughnessOverride` fixes the token at 2/2 regardless of the original's power/toughness (CR 707.2 copiable values). `ColorAdder` adds black "in addition to its other colors" (CR 105.3 additive colour change — the token keeps the original's colours). `TypeAdder` adds Zombie "in addition to its other types" (CR 205.1b — subtype addition preserves all existing subtypes).

"that creature" back-references the object named by the trigger's filter (the dying legendary creature), encoded as `ThatCreature`.

Rule citations: CR 707.2 (copy semantics), CR 105.3 (additive colour change), CR 205.1b (subtype addition), CR 704.5j (legend rule), CR 111.1 (token creation).

ANCHORED (^…$): the full surface phrase is anchored to prevent substring matches against any sibling triggered rule. Priority 76 — above the general copy-of-this-creature rules (70–75), well above the generic token rule (50).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateCopyOfThatCreatureNotLegendaryWithTypeAndColorTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CreateCopyOnCombatDamageTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create a token that's a copy of this creature" — token-copy effect that fires as the resolution clause of a `DealsCombatDamageToPlayer` trigger.

Rule 707.2: A token that is a copy of an object copies the copiable values of that object. Rule 111.8: Such tokens are created on the battlefield under their creator's control. The copy source is the card itself ("this creature"), modelled as `Self`.

Priority 70 — more specific than the generic `CreateTokenRule` (50) so this rule is tried first and the generic rule never sees the "copy of this creature" phrasing.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateCopyOnCombatDamageTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CreateEmblemTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Matches "you get an emblem with [quoted abilities]" — creates an emblem in the command zone whose abilities are parsed from the quoted oracle-text fragment (CR 114.2).

The quoted string is extracted and re-parsed via `OracleParser` so the emblem abilities receive the same full triggered/static/activated parsing as any other oracle text. The resulting abilities become `Abilities`.

ANCHORED (^...$): matches only the full "you get an emblem with ..." clause. Priority 90: runs before generic keyword or residual rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateEmblemTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CreateNamedEquipmentTokenWithQuotedAnthemAndEquipRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create [Name], a legendary colorless Equipment artifact token with "[quoted static ability]" and equip [cost]" — Mabel, Heir to Cragflame's ETB: "When Mabel enters, create Cragflame, a legendary colorless Equipment artifact token with "Equipped creature gets +1/+1 and has vigilance, trample, and haste" and equip {2}."

The generic `CreateTokenRule` only recognises creature tokens (its subtype/P-T helpers assume a "creature token" noun phrase) and has no path for a non-creature Equipment token carrying both a quoted static ability AND a separate bare "equip [cost]" keyword clause tacked onto the SAME sentence (not its own oracle line). This dedicated rule builds the token's two abilities directly:

The quoted body "Equipped creature gets +N/+M and has kw1, kw2[, ...][, and kwN]." — an attached P/T buff (CR 613.4c layer 7c) plus an N-keyword grant (CR 613.1f layer 6) to the equipped creature (CR 702.6), built the same way as the two-keyword shape `EquippedCreaturesHaveKeywordListRule` and the keyword+quoted-body shape `EquippedPTKeywordAndGrantedAbilityRule` already cover, generalised to an arbitrary-length Oxford-comma keyword list via the same `MapKeywordToStaticAbility` keyword table both siblings read from. "equip [cost]" (CR 702.6a verbatim: "'[Cost]: Attach this permanent to target creature you control. Activate only as a sorcery.'") — built identically to `EquipKeyword`'s combinator output (same `AttachEffect` target shape, same `OnlyAsSorcery` restriction), constructed directly here since that combinator only runs over an independent top-level oracle clause, not an embedded sentence fragment.

Runs at priority 70, above the generic `CreateTokenRule` (default 50), so this specific shape is matched first. Fully anchored (^…$) on the literal "a legendary colorless Equipment artifact token with … and equip {N}" spine, so it cannot match any other create-token shape.

CR 111.3 (token creation); CR 205.4a (Legendary supertype); CR 105.1 (colorless); CR 702.6 (Equipment); CR 613.1f/613.4c (layered continuous effects — descriptive only, MAST records what the text says).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateNamedEquipmentTokenWithQuotedAnthemAndEquipRule.cs)

### `CreateTappedAttackingCopyOfNontokenCreatureRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create a tapped and attacking token that's a copy of up to one other target nontoken creature you control" — Satya, Aetherflux Genius's attack-trigger copy effect (CR 111.1: token creation; CR 508.1k: token enters as an attacking creature declared in the same attack step; CR 707.2: the token copies the copiable values of the target).

"Up to one" is encoded as `UpToQuantity` on the `Quantity` (maximum 1, minimum 0). "Other" excludes the source creature (`ExcludeSelf` = true). "Nontoken" is the `IsToken` = false axis (CR 111: a token is not a card; "nontoken" means the object is not a token).

The "tapped and attacking" qualifier is contextually implicit from the attack trigger and is not serialised as a separate field on `CopyEffect` — matching the convention established by Kari Zev, Skyship Raider's gold fixture, where the same phrasing on a `CreateTokenEffect` is also omitted.

ANCHORED (^…$): prevents spurious matches inside a longer copy-token sentence that happens to contain this phrase as a substring. Priority 75 — above the generic `CreateCopyOnCombatDamageTriggeredRule` (70) and well above the `CreateTokenRule` fallback (50); specific enough to be tried before any broader "create a … copy" path.

Rule citations: CR 111.1 (token creation), CR 508.1k (attacking token), CR 707.2 (copy semantics), CR 107.14 (energy), CR 603.7 (delayed triggered ability).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTappedAttackingCopyOfNontokenCreatureRule.cs)

### `CreateTappedPredefinedTokenRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create a tapped [Subtype] token" — creates a predefined artifact token that enters the battlefield tapped (CR 111.10 — predefined tokens; the creating effect "may also modify or add to the predefined characteristics", which is how the "tapped" entry modifier on the create instruction is reconciled with the predefined token definition). Handles the "create a tapped Treasure token" form produced by cards such as Nuka-Cola Vending Machine (PIP), and the "create a tapped Powerstone token" form on the enters-the-battlefield Powerstone family (Argothian Opportunist, Koilos Roc, Horned Stoneseeker, Junkyard Genius — BRO/DMU). The "tapped" qualifier is recorded on the `EntersTapped` field so consumers know the token enters already tapped rather than untapped. This is a descriptive datum, not an engine tap action (MAST describes what oracle text says, not engine execution). Per the CR glossary, a Powerstone token is a colorless artifact token with "{T}: Add {C}. This mana can't be spent to cast a nonartifact spell." (a predefined token, see CR 111.10). As with every predefined token in this rule, the token's predefined activated-ability body is NOT re-asserted here as free text: it is carried by the parenthetical reminder ("It's an artifact with ...") that the trigger parser strips into the ability's Reminder field and discards from the effect AST (CR 207.2: reminder text has no rules meaning). The token is identified structurally by its artifact type + named subtype. Treasure/Food/Clue/Blood retain their AbilityText body for back-compat with the existing golds; Powerstone, added clean, omits it (no free-text residual). Priority 96: sits above `CreateTokenRule` (default priority 50) so the tapped variant is matched before the plain vanilla path, which would fail anyway because it doesn't recognise "tapped" between the article and the subtype word. CR 111 (Tokens), CR 111.10 (predefined tokens), CR 603.2 (triggered ability event matching).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTappedPredefinedTokenRule.cs)

### `CreateThatManyTokensRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create that many [P/T] [color] [Subtype] creature tokens" — token creation where the quantity is derived from the triggering event's counter count (Nest of Scarabs).

"That many" is an anaphoric reference to the number of counters placed in the triggering event — the antecedent of "that many" is the count from a `CounterPlaced` trigger (CR 122.1: counters are markers placed on objects; the count placed in a single event is the antecedent). Modelled as `DerivedQuantity` keyed on `CountersPlaced`, the counter-placement analog of `DamageDealt` and `LifeLost`.

Rule 111.1: "A token is a marker used to represent any permanent that isn't represented by a card." Rule 603.2: the triggering event fires the ability; the effect clause creates tokens equal to the number of counters placed.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateThatManyTokensRule.cs)

### `CreateThatManyTreasureTokensRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create that many Treasure tokens." — token creation where the quantity is derived from the damage dealt by the triggering combat-damage event (The Reaver Cleaver: "Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player or planeswalker, create that many Treasure tokens.").

"That many" is an anaphoric reference to the amount of combat damage dealt in the triggering event (CR 510.1 — combat damage step). Modelled as `DerivedQuantity` keyed on `DamageDealt`, the same derived quantity used by "you gain that much life" lifelink analogs. The predefined Treasure token is as specified in CR 111.10a: "A Treasure token is a colorless Treasure artifact token with '{T}, Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color.'"

Rule 111.1: "A token is a marker used to represent any permanent that isn't represented by a card." Rule 603.2: the triggering event fires the ability; the effect clause creates tokens equal to the damage dealt.

ANCHORED (^…$): the full effect clause is matched to prevent this rule from misfiring inside a broader effect sentence. Runs as a standard `[TriggeredRule]` — lower priority than the predefined-token patterns in `CreateTokenRule` but named uniquely so it does not collide with the creature-token "that many" shape in `CreateThatManyTokensRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateThatManyTreasureTokensRule.cs)

### `CreateTokenChoiceRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create a [TokenA] token or a [TokenB] token" — a one-of-two CHOICE between creating one predefined artifact token or another (Tireless Provisioner: "create a Food token or a Treasure token").

"X or Y" is a modal choice the controller makes on resolution, not two creations — Rule 700.2 (modal). It is modelled as a `ModalEffect` with `ChooseOne` whose two modes each wrap a single `CreateTokenEffect` in a `SpellAbility`, mirroring the bullet-modal shape produced for "choose one —" triggers (Saurian Symbiote).

Both options name a predefined artifact token whose colorless, P/T-less body is fully specified by its subtype: Treasure (Rule 111.10a) and Food (Rule 111.10b). Their activated abilities are reminder text (stripped to the ability's Reminder field upstream), so each token reuses the predefined `TokenDefinition` factory rather than re-parsing the body.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTokenChoiceRule.cs)

### `CreateTokenCopyOfSelfByNameTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create a token that's a copy of Council of Reeds" — a self-copy effect where the card names ITSELF rather than saying "this creature" (current Oracle templating convention for self-reference on many post-2020 cards). Sibling of `CreateCopyOnCombatDamageTriggeredRule` (which handles the "of this creature" phrasing); here the copy source is the card's own printed name.

CR 201.5: text that refers to the object it's printed on by name means just that particular object — a self-reference exactly like "this creature" (CR 109). CR 707.1: "Some effects create a token that's a copy of another object." CR 707.2: the copy acquires the copiable values of the original object's characteristics. CR 111.2: the player who creates a token is its owner (and, absent a stated alternative, its controller). The copy source is modelled as `Self`, mirroring `CreateCopyOnCombatDamageTriggeredRule` and `IsSelfByNameTrigger`'s established self-by-name convention for trigger conditions, extended here to the effect side.

The parser does not have access to the card's own name at this layer (mirroring `IsSelfByNameTrigger`'s documented limitation), so this is a STRUCTURAL match, not a name-equality check: the captured name must begin with a capitalised word and may continue with capitalised words or the lowercase function words that legally appear inside MTG card names ("of", "the", "a", "an", "from", "for", "to", "in", "at", "with", "by", "and", "or", "as"). This case-sensitivity is exactly what keeps this rule disjoint from the lowercase-pronoun siblings — "of it" (`YouMayCreateTokenCopyOfItTriggeredRule`), "of that creature" (`CreateCopyOfThatCreatureNotLegendaryWithTypeAndColorTriggeredRule`), "of equipped creature" (`CreateCopyOfEquippedCreatureTriggeredRule`), and "of target creature" (`CreateTokenRule`/spell-side copy rules) never begin with an uppercase letter, so none of those surfaces can match here.

ANCHORED (^…$): the whole effect fragment must be exactly "create a token that's a copy of [Name]" so this rule cannot claim a substring of a longer "except …" clause (those stay with the sibling rules that model modifications).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTokenCopyOfSelfByNameTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CreateTokenOrInsteadIfConditionRule` — *static class*

Recognises the two-sentence conditional-token-creation shape: "create a P1/T1 color1 Subtype1 creature token. If [condition], create a P2/T2 color2 Subtype2 creature token instead."

Rule 111 (tokens), CR 603 (triggered abilities). The word "instead" signals that the second creation REPLACES the first (not in addition to it). Modelled as a `ConditionalEffect`:

`Condition` — the mid-resolution board-state predicate; `Then` — the token created when the condition is true (the "instead" token from the second sentence); `Else` — the token created when the condition is false (the default token from the first sentence).

The Necrobloom (BIG) is the canonical example: "create a 0/1 green Plant creature token. If you control seven or more lands with different names, create a 2/2 black Zombie creature token instead." CR 207.2c: "Landfall" is a CR ability word with no special rules meaning. CR 603: triggered abilities fire "Whenever a land you control enters". The condition "you control seven or more lands with different names" is an `OtherCondition` residual (ADR 0001) because `ObjectFilter` does not yet have a "different names" axis.

Called as a composite path from `TriggeredAbilityParser` BEFORE the sentence bundle splitter, so the two-sentence shape is not incorrectly split into two independent token creation effects.

A sibling shape handled by the same composite path: "create a P/T color Subtype creature token [with "&lt;ability&gt;"]. If the creature had power N or greater, create &lt;count&gt; of those tokens instead." — the SAME token definition, with the "instead" branch creating MULTIPLE copies of it rather than a distinct replacement token (Anax, Hardened in the Forge: "create a 1/1 red Satyr creature token with "This token can't block." If the creature had power 4 or greater, create two of those tokens instead."). "The creature" is the creature named by the trigger's dies event — recorded as `Source` = "the creature" (the established short-antecedent convention, e.g. "it"/"the card you exiled"), not a free-text condition. CR 604.3 does not apply here (this is an ordinary triggered effect, not a CDA); CR 111.2 (token creation) and CR 603 (triggered abilities) do.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTokenOrInsteadIfConditionRule.cs)

### `CreateTokenRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create [article] [P/T] [colors] [subtypes] creature token [with ...]" — Rule 111. Also handles predefined artifact tokens (Food, Treasure, Clue, Blood) which have no P/T and whose activated ability is reminder text only (Rule 107.10b). Handles the optional "you may" prefix (Rule 116.1b) by setting IsOptional = true on the resulting CreateTokenEffect.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTokenRule.cs)

### `CreateTokenWhereXCountTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Create X [P]/[T] [color|colorless] [Subtype] [artifact] creature tokens, where X is the number of [Subtype]s you control." — the triggered-ability sibling of the activated Krenko, Mob Boss pattern (`CreateTokenWhereXCountEffectRule`), reached here from an attack trigger (Myrel, Shield of Argive: "Whenever Myrel attacks, create X 1/1 colorless Soldier artifact creature tokens, where X is the number of Soldiers you control.").

CR 111.2 (token creation): X is not a free variable — it is immediately resolved to a `CountQuantity` over an `ObjectFilter` counting the named subtype the controller controls, mirroring the activated sibling exactly.

Adds the "colorless ... artifact creature" shape (`Colors=["C"], Types=["artifact","creature"]`) alongside the colored plain-creature shape the activated sibling already handles, matching the established colorless-token convention (CR 105.1; e.g. `CreateColorlessArtifactCreatureTokenEffectRule`).

Priority above the generic `CreateTokenRule` (default 50) so this more-specific "where X is …" shape is tried first — the generic rule has no "where X is" handling and would otherwise silently emit a fixed literal count of 1 instead of the derived count. Fully anchored (^…$).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTokenWhereXCountTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CreateTokenWhereXManaValueOfThatSpellTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Create X [P]/[T] [color] [Subtype][ Subtype] creature tokens, where X is the mana value of that spell." — the cast-triggered token-count sibling of `CreateTokenWhereXCountTriggeredRule` (which resolves X to a count of controlled permanents), reached from a "Whenever you cast a[n] [X] spell, ..." trigger. Covers Ovika, Enigma Goliath: "Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, create X 1/1 red Phyrexian Goblin creature tokens, where X is the mana value of that spell."

CR 111.2 (token creation); CR 202.3 (mana value). X is not a free variable (CR 107.3) — the "where X is …" clause defines it inline as the mana value of the spell that caused the trigger to fire, i.e. the object anaphorically named "that spell". MAST records this as a `DerivedQuantity` with `DerivedFrom = ManaValue` and `Source = "that spell"`, mirroring the Food Chain "exiled creature's mana value" shape (`DerivedQuantity` with a named `Source` string; ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution — the engine resolves the actual number at trigger time).

Priority above the generic `CreateTokenRule` (default 50) and at the same tier as its "count of controlled permanents" sibling (90) so this more-specific "where X is the mana value of that spell" shape is claimed before any less-specific fallback. Fully anchored (^…$) and its tail phrase ("mana value of that spell") is disjoint from the sibling's tail ("number of [Subtype]s you control"), so the two rules cannot collide.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTokenWhereXManaValueOfThatSpellTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CreateTokenWithDiesGainLifeAbilityRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create a [P/T] [colors] [Subtype] creature token with \"When this token dies, you gain N life.\"" — the Strixhaven Pest token (Pest Rescuer, Sedgemoor Witch, Callous Bloodmage, …), created here inside an upkeep trigger.

The generic `CreateTokenRule` parses the token's power/toughness, colors, subtypes and types but drops the quoted <i>triggered</i> ability (its `TriggeredRuleHelpers.ParseTokenAbilities` only recognises bare keywords). This dedicated rule reuses the same base-token helpers so the token's characteristics are identical, then attaches the quoted ability as a structured `TriggeredAbility`: "When this token dies" is a self-referential `Dies` trigger (`IsSelf` = true), and "you gain N life" is a `GainLifeEffect` for you (CR 119.3 — "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."). The additive life amount N is carried as a typed `LiteralQuantity`.

Runs at priority 60, above the generic `CreateTokenRule` (default 50), so this specific shape is matched first and the generic rule never overwrites the token's structured ability with an empty ability list (mirrors `CreateColorlessTokenWithSacrificeManaAbilityRule`). Anchored on the exact quoted ability and the singular "create a [P/T]" form, so plural / "twice X" token counts (which the base helpers would miscount) fall through to `CreateTokenRule` unchanged.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTokenWithDiesGainLifeAbilityRule.cs)

### `CreateTokensEqualToDieResultTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"You create a number of [PredefinedToken] tokens equal to the result." — creates predefined artifact tokens (Treasure, Food, Clue, Blood) in a count equal to the result of a preceding die roll (CR 706.4).

CR 706.4: "Some abilities that instruct a player to roll one or more dice do not include a results table. The text of those abilities will indicate how to use the results of the die rolls, if at all." This sentence is the "how to use" clause: the count of created tokens equals the die-roll result, modelled as `DieRollResultQuantity` (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004).

CR 111.10a: "A Treasure token is a colorless Treasure artifact token with '{T}, Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color.'"

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the "equal to the result" tail is distinctive enough to not match siblings, but anchoring is applied per the standing contract. Priority 72: above the generic `CreateCopyOnCombatDamageTriggeredRule` (70) and above the generic CreateTokenRule (50) so this more-specific pattern is tried first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTokensEqualToDieResultTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CreateTreasureForEachOpponentDealtDamageRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you create a Treasure token for each opponent dealt damage" — the Malcolm, Keen-Eyed Navigator effect pattern. The controller creates one Treasure token per opponent who was dealt damage by the triggering event.

The quantity "for each opponent dealt damage" is modelled as a `CalculatedQuantity` with `Expression = "for each opponent dealt damage"` — an anaphoric reference to the set of opponents hit in the triggering `DealsDamageToOpponents` event.
