There is no structured `CountQuantity` for "opponents dealt damage" (that set is a dynamic game-state query outside `ObjectFilter` scope); the free-text expression is the type-honest residual per ADR 0001.

The predefined Treasure token is as specified in CR 111.10a: "A Treasure token is a colorless Treasure artifact token with '{T}, Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color.'" Rule 111.1: "A token is a marker used to represent any permanent that isn't represented by a card." Rule 603.2: the triggering event fires the ability; the effect clause creates tokens equal to the number of opponents dealt damage.

ANCHORED (^…$): the full effect clause is matched to prevent this rule from misfiring inside a broader effect sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateTreasureForEachOpponentDealtDamageRule.cs)

### `CreateXTokensWithChangelingTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"create X [P]/[T] colorless [Subtype] creature tokens with changeling." — a variable-count (X) token-creation effect where the created tokens bear the Changeling keyword (CR 702.73a: "'Changeling' means 'This object is every creature type.'"). The Springleaf Parade shape: "create X 1/1 colorless Shapeshifter creature tokens with changeling."

The count is the value chosen for the spell's own {X} in its mana cost (CR 107.3 / CR 601.2b) — recorded as a `VariableQuantity` named "X" rather than resolving the numeric value (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution), mirroring the variable-count convention used elsewhere (e.g. Mind Shatter's "discards X cards").

Distinct from the generic `CreateTokenRule`: that rule's helpers (`TriggeredRuleHelpers.ParseArticle`, `ParseColors`, `ParseTokenAbilities`) don't recognise an "X" count, the "colorless" color word, or a "with changeling" keyword suffix, so it would either silently miscount (falling through to the default count of 1) or drop the Changeling ability outright. This rule owns the full "create X … colorless … creature tokens with changeling" shape end-to-end, mirroring the activated-ability sibling `CreateTokenWithChangelingEffectRule`.

Priority 65 — above the generic `CreateTokenRule` (default 50) so this more-specific shape is tried first, mirroring the priority band used by other specific create-token variants (`CreateTokenWithDiesGainLifeAbilityRule` at 60, `CreateTokensEqualToDieResultTriggeredRule` at 72). Anchored (^…$) pattern prevents substring matches against sibling clauses.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreateXTokensWithChangelingTriggeredRule.cs)

### `CreatureDealtDamageConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever a creature is dealt damage" — emits `CreatureDealtDamage` with a Filter of `{CardTypes: ["creature"]}` (Rule 120 — Damage; Rule 603.2 — triggered abilities). Covers the Repercussion trigger pattern: any creature (not just a specific one) receiving damage fires the ability.

CR 120.1: "Any time an object, player, or battle would be dealt damage, that damage is dealt instead to the appropriate target." CR 120.3: "Damage can be dealt to creatures, planeswalkers, battles, and players." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." The filter carries the creature predicate so the trigger's subject is clearly a creature (not a player or planeswalker).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreatureDealtDamageConditionRule.cs)

### `CreatureDealtDamageThisTurnDiesConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Death-watch with a damage-provenance qualifier: "Whenever a creature dealt damage by [source] this turn dies, …" — Sengir Bats, Sengir Vampire, Predator Ooze, Blood Cultist, Vein Drinker, Zurgo Helmsmasher, Garza Zol, Madame Vastra, Rot Wolf, Abattoir Ghoul, and the rest of the family.

The trigger event is a `Dies` (CR 700.4 / 603.2 — a creature is put into a graveyard from the battlefield). The qualifier "dealt damage by [source] this turn" is a backward-looking provenance condition on the dying creature: it is the existing `DealtDamageByPredicate` history predicate (whose own doc-comment names exactly "a creature dealt damage by Zurgo this turn"). The source that dealt the damage is the ability's own permanent — written "this creature" / "this permanent", as the card's own name (CR 201.5 self-reference), or "equipped creature" for the Equipment in the family (Scythe of the Wretched).

This rule sits ABOVE `DiesConditionRule` (Priority 991) because the shared `ParseObjectFilter` would otherwise read the "this creature" inside the provenance clause as a self-reference on the dying subject (returning `IsSelf = true` and dropping the History) — wrong: the subject is "a creature" (any creature), and "this creature" is the damage source, not the dying object. Recognising the whole shape here keeps the subject and the provenance source correctly separated.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreatureDealtDamageThisTurnDiesConditionRule.cs)

### `CreatureWithKeywordEntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"a creature you control with [keyword] enters" — an enters trigger on a creature-type filter that additionally requires a keyword ability. Handles Dragon Tempest's first ability: "Whenever a creature you control with flying enters, …" Rule 603.6a: enters-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield. The keyword constraint ("with flying") narrows which entering creatures fire the ability. The constraint is structured on the `Characteristics` axis as a `KeywordCharacteristic`, not free text (ADR 0001: no free text for structurable concepts). Sits below `EntersConditionRule` (Priority 990) so the plain "a creature you control enters" shape is handled first; this rule fires only when a "with [keyword]" qualifier is present.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreatureWithKeywordEntersConditionRule.cs)

### `CreatureWithManaValueEntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"a creature with mana value N or greater enters" — a creature ETB trigger narrowed by a mana-value threshold on the entering creature (the Dragon-Aura cycle: Dragon Fangs / Dragon Scales / Dragon Breath / Dragon Wings / Dragon Shadow). The threshold lands on the filter's `ManaValueComparison` axis as a literal `Comparison`.

CR 603.2: a game event matching the trigger event triggers the ability. The "with mana value N or greater" qualifier (CR 202.3 / CR 107.1) restricts the matching set to entering creatures whose mana value is at least N. The subject is a plain "a creature" (not "this creature", not "another creature") so the trigger watches ANY creature entering — including ones an opponent controls — with no self-reference and no controller restriction.

Runs at priority 992 — above the general `EntersConditionRule` (990), which would otherwise swallow "a creature ... enters" via the bare "a creature" branch of `ParseObjectFilter` and silently drop the mana-value threshold. Below the more specific colour/colorless/another rules (995–997) so those still win for their narrower shapes.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreatureWithManaValueEntersConditionRule.cs)

### `CreatureWithoutKeywordDiesConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Dies trigger on a creature a player controls that lacks a specific keyword ability — the Luminous Broodmoth family. Oracle text: "a creature you control without flying dies", "a creature you control without flying or reach dies", etc.

The filter encodes the keyword absence as a typed `OtherCharacteristic` residual ("withoutFlying", "withoutFlanking", etc.) per the convention established by Falter (M10). `OtherCharacteristic` is `IResidual`, not `IUnparsed` — a deliberate scope deferral (ADR 0001), not a parse failure.

"without flying" is not a structured negation of the keyword-presence axis on `Characteristics` because there is currently no `NegatedKeywordCharacteristic` node; the "withoutX" residual is the approved frontier encoding. See: Falter (M10), Cosmotronic Wave (GRN).

CR 700.4 ("dies" = moves from battlefield to graveyard, see also TriggerEvent.Dies). Priority above generic DiesConditionRule (991) so this more specific guard fires first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/CreatureWithoutKeywordDiesConditionRule.cs)

### `DealThatMuchDamageToControllerRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"[source] deals that much damage to that creature's controller" — the Repercussion effect: a named source deals damage equal to the amount just dealt to the triggering creature, targeting that creature's controller.

The antecedent of "that much" is the damage dealt to the creature in the triggering event (`DamageDealt`), matching the `CreatureDealtDamage` trigger (CR 120 — Damage; CR 603.2). The target is the controller of the creature that was dealt damage (`Controller`); the source is the enchantment itself (`Self`).

CR 120.1: "Any time an object … would be dealt damage, that damage is dealt to the appropriate target." CR 120.3: damage can be dealt to players. This triggered effect redirects an equivalent amount to the damaged creature's controller, who is a player (not the creature). The source is "this enchantment" — a self-reference carried on the `Source` field rather than inferred, so the interact-oracle operator can distinguish the damage source.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DealThatMuchDamageToControllerRule.cs)

### `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever [subject] deals combat damage to (a player|an opponent|any player|a player or planeswalker)" — emits `DealsCombatDamageToPlayer` for player-only recipients and `DealsCombatDamageToPlayerOrPlaneswalker` for the broader "player or planeswalker" form (The Reaver Cleaver, Sword of Sinew and Steel). Rule 510 — Combat Damage Step; Rule 603.6 — triggered abilities. The recipient class is encoded in the event enum value; the Filter captures the subject.

"a creature you control with [keyword] deals combat damage to a player" — the "with [keyword]" suffix on the subject noun phrase is a keyword-ability characteristic constraint on the matched object (CR 702 — keyword abilities). Modelled as `Characteristics` carrying a structured `KeywordCharacteristic` so the filter is fully typed with no free-text residual.

CR 510.1 (Combat Damage Step): "First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage … This turn-based action doesn't use the stack." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DealsCombatDamageConditionRule.cs)

### `DealsCombatDamageToCreatureConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever [subject] deals combat damage to a creature" — emits `DealsCombatDamageToCreature`.

CR 510.1 (Combat Damage Step): "First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then the defending player announces how each blocking creature assigns its combat damage. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack." The combat-damage assignment is the game event; CR 603.2 — "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers."

The recipient class (a creature) is implied by the enum value; the Filter captures the subject — the thing dealing the damage ("this creature", self-by-name, etc.). Sits above `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule` (player recipient, Priority 985) and `DealsDamageConditionRule` (any damage, Priority 984) so the creature-recipient variant is recognised before the broader shapes; those sibling rules guard on "to a player" / exclude "deals combat damage" respectively, so there is no overlap.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DealsCombatDamageToCreatureConditionRule.cs)

### `DealsDamageConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever [subject] deals damage" — any damage (Rule 120), not only combat damage. Emits `DealsDamage`. Covers lifelink-analog oracle text printed before the lifelink keyword existed. The combat variant is handled by `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule` (higher priority), so this excludes it.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DealsDamageConditionRule.cs)

### `DealsDamageToAttackedPlayerOrPlaneswalkerRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"[this enchantment|this creature|it|Name] deals N damage to the player or planeswalker [that creature is|it's|it is] attacking." — the attack-trigger burn family. Two surface forms of the same effect:

Cavalcade of Calamity — "Whenever a creature you control with power 1 or less attacks, this enchantment deals 1 damage to the player or planeswalker <b>that creature is</b> attacking." The attacking creature named by the trigger is a different object than the source enchantment, so the back-reference is "that creature". Scorch Spitter — "Whenever this creature attacks, it deals 1 damage to the player or planeswalker <b>it's</b> attacking." Here the trigger's attacking creature IS the source ("this creature" / "it"), so the back-reference is the contracted "it's" (= "it is").

Both forms name the same thing — the single defending object the trigger's attacking creature is attacking — and therefore the same `AttackedPlayerOrPlaneswalker` reference, so they share one rule/one gold shape.

Emits a `DealDamageEffect` (Rule 120 — non-combat damage dealt by a resolving triggered ability) whose `Target` is a `AttackedPlayerOrPlaneswalker` reference: the single defending object (a player OR the attacked planeswalker) that the trigger's attacking creature is attacking (CR 508.1b). The "or" is the two possible kinds of that one determined object, not a chooser's alternatives, so it is a single determined reference rather than a `Choice`. The damage `Source` is `Self` — "this enchantment"/"this creature"/"it" is the ability's own source object (CR 109).

The tail "the player or planeswalker [that creature is|it's|it is] attacking" is anchored on the right (^…$) so this rule cannot claim a differently-shaped damage effect; the subject is captured but always resolves to the source object (Self), because a resolving ability's damage is dealt by the permanent that has the ability. The numeric-amount requirement (`\d+|one…ten`) keeps trample reminder text — "can deal excess combat damage to the player or planeswalker it's attacking" — out (no counted amount, "deal" not "deals N").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DealsDamageToAttackedPlayerOrPlaneswalkerRule.cs)

### `DealsDamageToOpponentConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever [subject] deals damage to an opponent" — any damage (combat or non-combat, Rule 120) specifically to an opponent (not any player, Rule 102.2). Emits `DealsDamageToOpponent`. The Filter captures the subject (the thing dealing the damage).

Distinct from `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule` (combat damage only) and `DealsDamageConditionRule` (any damage, unspecified recipient). The guard excludes "deals combat damage" so combat-damage text routes to `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule` (higher priority), and requires "to an opponent" to distinguish from the generic unrecipient-qualified `DealsDamageConditionRule`.

Rule 120: a source deals damage when it assigns damage to a player or permanent. Rule 102.2: an opponent is any player not on the same team as the controller. Rule 603.2: triggered abilities fire automatically on matching game events.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DealsDamageToOpponentConditionRule.cs)

### `DealsThatMuchDamageToEachOtherOpponentRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals that much damage to each other opponent." — reflexive combat-damage spread (Grenzo's Ruffians pattern). Paired with a DealsCombatDamageToPlayer trigger; the "that much" refers to the amount of combat damage dealt to the trigger's original recipient, and "each other opponent" is every opponent other than that recipient. Rule 120.1: a source deals damage. Rule 510 (Combat Damage Step): the trigger fires when combat damage is dealt to an opponent. "Each other opponent" is the set of opponents excluding the one already hit; this is recorded descriptively as an EachOpponent reference with Characteristics: ["other"] — the "other" predicate's runtime resolution (relative to the trigger's opponent) is engine territory per the descriptive-not-engine doctrine. Rule 702.121 (Melee) lists Grenzo's Ruffians as a canonical example of this pattern. The rule encodes "that much" as a CalculatedQuantity with Expression="that much" and Operation="match", matching the convention established for Chatterfang's "that many" token-augmentation replacement.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DealsThatMuchDamageToEachOtherOpponentRule.cs)

### `DefendingPlayerDiscardsTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"defending player discards [a/N] card[s]" (optionally "at random") as the effect clause of a triggered ability — the combat-nuisance shape on attack/block triggers (Alley Grifters, Slate Street Ruffian: "Whenever this creature becomes blocked, defending player discards a card"; Shrieking Specter / The Haunt of Hightower on attack; Corrupt Official's "…discards a card at random").

The discarder is `DefendingPlayer` — CR 508.5: "If an ability of an attacking creature refers to a defending player … the defending player it's referring to is the player that creature is attacking …" (equivalently, on a becomes-blocked trigger, the player who declared the block). The card count is the literal quantity of cards moved from hand to graveyard — glossary "Discard": "To move a card from its owner's hand to that player's graveyard. See rule 701.9, 'Discard.'" A trailing "at random" sets `Random`.

This is the defending-player counterpart of `TargetOpponentDiscardsTriggeredRule` ("target opponent discards …"); both are dispatched after the trigger/effect split has peeled the "Whenever …," prefix, and both emit `DiscardCardsEffect` differing only in the `Player` reference kind. The surface is anchored (`^…$`) so the "at random" and "…all the cards in their hand, then draws that many cards" (Robber Fly) siblings are NOT mislabeled — the former is captured explicitly by the optional group, the latter falls through unmatched.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DefendingPlayerDiscardsTriggeredRule.cs)

### `DestroyDefendingCreatureThenPutCounterRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"destroy target creature defending player controls, then put a +1/+1 counter on [Name]." — the compound triggered attack-effect on Grimgrin, Corpse-Born and similar attack-triggered destroy-then-counter abilities.

Produces a single `CompositeEffect` containing two sibling effects (consistent with the BloodArtist/multi-effect triggered convention):

`DestroyEffect` targeting a `Target` creature with `DefendingPlayer` — "destroy target creature defending player controls" (CR 701.8: destroy means put the permanent into its owner's graveyard; CR 508.1b: the defending player is whoever is being attacked). `PutCountersEffect` targeting `Self` with one +1/+1 counter — "then put a +1/+1 counter on [Name]" where [Name] is a self-reference by the card's own name (CR 201.5; CR 122.1).

The pattern is anchored (^…$) to prevent substring collision with `DestroyTargetTriggeredRule`, which would otherwise consume the "destroy target creature" prefix and silently drop the ", then put" clause. Priority 60 — above `PutCountersTriggeredRule` (default 50) so this anchored compound form is tried first; it will not match unless both "destroy ... defending player" and "then put a +1/+1 counter" are present.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DestroyDefendingCreatureThenPutCounterRule.cs)

### `DestroyTargetTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"destroy target [filter]." / "you may destroy target [filter]." — single-target destroy on the triggered side. Delegates single-noun filter parsing to `ParseTargetFilter` (same lexical surface as `DestroyTargetSimpleRule`). Handles type-disjunction filters ("artifact or enchantment", "creature, artifact, or enchantment") via `SplitTypeDisjunction`, matching the spell-side `DestroyTargetTypeDisjunctionRule`. Covers: land, artifact, enchantment, creature, permanent, and richer filter phrases (color + type, non- prefix, etc.), as well as any two-or-more-type disjunction. The optional "you may" prefix sets `IsOptional` = <see langword="true"/>.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DestroyTargetTriggeredRule.cs)

### `DestroyThatCreatureCantBeRegeneratedTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"destroy that creature. It can't be regenerated." — the regeneration-denial variant of the combat/damage back-reference destroy family (Toxin Sliver, Phage the Untouchable, Dripping Dead, Grotesque Hybrid, Merieke Ri Berit, …). The target is the creature named by the trigger condition (the damaged/blocked creature), encoded as `ThatCreature`; the trailing "It can't be regenerated." sentence rides as `CantBeRegenerated` = true (a modifier on the destroy, NOT a separate effect).

Sibling of `DestroyThatCreatureTriggeredRule` (same "that creature" anaphora and destroy, but no regeneration clause). That rule anchors on the bare "destroy that creature" fragment (`^…$`) and therefore does NOT match this two-sentence form; this rule anchors the whole "destroy that creature. It can't be regenerated" body so the two are mutually exclusive by surface. Mirrors the spell-side `DestroyTargetCantBeRegeneratedRule` and `DestroyAllRule` handling — the "can't be regenerated" clause is not broken apart into a sibling effect.

CR 701.8 (Destroy): to destroy a permanent, move it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard. CR 701.19 (Regenerate): regeneration is a replacement effect; "can't be regenerated" turns off that shield for this destruction. CR 603.2: the anaphoric "that creature" back-references the object named by this ability's own trigger event.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DestroyThatCreatureCantBeRegeneratedTriggeredRule.cs)

### `DestroyThatCreatureTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"destroy that creature" — the destroy resolution of the combat/damage back-reference family (Engulfing Slagwurm, Sylvan Basilisk, Voracious Cobra, Horobi, …). The target is the creature named by the trigger condition (the blocking/blocked/damaged creature), encoded as `ThatCreature` — the creature analogue of "that player". Sibling of `ThisCreatureDealsDamageToThatCreatureTriggeredRule` (same "that creature" anaphora, destroy instead of damage).

Anchored to the bare "destroy that creature" fragment (`^…$`). More-specific siblings carry trailing qualifiers — "destroy that creature at end of combat", "… and this creature", "… It can't be regenerated" (a separate sentence), "… unless its controller …" — which do NOT match this anchor and fall through to their own handling (CR 701.8 destroy always leaves the "can't be regenerated" clause as a distinct sentence, so it never rides here).

CR 701.8 (Destroy): "To destroy a permanent, move it from the battlefield to its owner's graveyard." CR 603.2: triggered abilities (When/Whenever/At) — the anaphoric "that creature" back-references the object named by this ability's own trigger event.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DestroyThatCreatureTriggeredRule.cs)

### `DiceRolledConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you roll one or more dice" (and the equivalent "roll a die" / "roll dice" forms) — the die-roll trigger, CR 706. This is the dice CONSUMER side: the event a `RollDieEffect` (the emitter) satisfies. Modeling it is what lets the interaction engine close a dice loop — roll → this trigger → effect → … → roll again — so a self-feeding roll engine (e.g. Brazen Dwarf) is reconstructable.

A player-action trigger (no battlefield object), so no `Filter` — the controller restriction ("you") is implicit. The trigger may carry a <i>result qualifier</i> on the rolled value (CR 706.7 references comparing "the results of that roll … to a given number"):

"roll a 4 or higher" → a <i>minimum</i>, captured on `DieResultThreshold` (Mr. House, Chittering Doom — the "on a die" suffix is tolerated). "roll a 1" / "roll a 1 or 2" → an <i>exact value set</i>, captured on `DieResultValues` (Complaints Clerk, Atomwheel Acrobats). no qualifier ("roll one or more dice") → fires on any roll.

The two result qualifiers are mutually exclusive; a roll trigger carries at most one. CR 706.2: "the final number is the result of the die roll."

Priority 985 — a specific player-action phrase; anchored on the "roll" verb so it cannot be confused with the emitter (an effect-side rule).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DiceRolledConditionRule.cs)

### `DiesConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"dies" triggers: "this creature dies", "a creature dies", "another creature dies", etc. "dies" is modern oracle; the longform "is put into a graveyard from the battlefield" (Rule 700.4) describes the same event and normalises to the same TriggerEvent.Dies.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DiesConditionRule.cs)

### `DiscardAndUntapAllLandsRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player discards a card and you untap all lands you control" — the combined triggered effect of a `DealsCombatDamageToPlayer` trigger (Rule 510 — Combat Damage Step) where the recipient discards a card AND the controller untaps all their lands.

Sword of Feast and Famine is the canonical card for this pattern. The two effects are conjunctive in a single clause, wrapped in a `CompositeEffect` mirroring the single-sentence-conjunction convention used elsewhere in triggered resolution text (Rule 701.9 — Discard; Rule 701.26 — Untap).

"That player" refers back to the player named in the trigger condition (Rule 603.2 — "that player" in a triggered ability resolution resolves to the player identified by the trigger event). "All lands you control" references the controller's entire land permanents (CR 301 — Artifacts; CR 701.26a — untapping a permanent).

Priority 62 — sits above the generic single-effect rules (which would fail on the conjoined clause) but below more specific multi-effect rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DiscardAndUntapAllLandsRule.cs)

### `DiscardOnCombatDamageTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player discards a card" — discard effect imposed on the player who received combat damage. Fires as the effect clause of a `DealsCombatDamageToPlayer` trigger (Rule 510 — Combat Damage Step). "That player" refers back to the player mentioned in the trigger condition (Rule 701.9 — Discard).

Covers the canonical single-card form. The N-card variant ("that player discards N cards") is also handled: count is parsed from a word-or-digit group so both shapes land on the same rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DiscardOnCombatDamageTriggeredRule.cs)

### `DrawCardConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you draw a card" — draw-card trigger (Rule 121: Drawing a Card). Fires whenever the controller draws a card by any means. Controller defaults to You.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DrawCardConditionRule.cs)

### `DrawCardPerCounterOnItTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"draw a card for each [counter] counter on it" — Vexing Sphinx's dies-trigger payoff ("When this creature dies, draw a card for each age counter on it").

Modeled as a `DrawCardsEffect` whose `Count` is a `CounterCountQuantity` over the named counter on `Self` (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004 — the engine reads the live counter count at the time the triggered ability resolves). The "it" pronoun back-references the dying permanent named "this creature" in the trigger — mirrors `LoseLifePerNamedCounterTriggeredRule`'s "it"/named-source → Self convention, and the cumulative-upkeep cost siblings' own "for each age counter on it" → Self mapping (e.g. `CumulativeUpkeepDiscardCardStaticRule`).

ANCHORED (^…$) on the full effect clause so it cannot match as a substring of a broader clause and so it doesn't collide with the unanchored generic `DrawCardsTriggeredRule` — a higher priority than that rule's default 50 ensures this more specific shape is tried first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DrawCardPerCounterOnItTriggeredRule.cs)

### `DrawCardsEqualToHandSizeDifferenceRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"draw cards equal to the difference" — the effect half of The Ten Rings' end-step top-up ability: "At the beginning of your end step, if you have fewer than ten cards in hand, draw cards equal to the difference." "The difference" is the gap between the intervening-if's hand-size threshold (ten) and the player's current hand size — CR 402.2 (maximum hand size).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DrawCardsEqualToHandSizeDifferenceRule.cs)

### `DrawCardsTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"draw a card" with optional "unless that player pays {N}" tail.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DrawCardsTriggeredRule.cs)

### `DrawNthCardEachTurnConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you draw your second card each turn" — ordinal-qualified draw trigger (Rule 121: Drawing a Card). Unlike the unqualified `DrawCardConditionRule` ("you draw a card"), this shape names a specific occurrence within the turn ("your <i>second</i> card") and a per-turn counting window ("each turn"). MAST records those two qualifiers descriptively on the `TriggerCondition` (`Ordinal` and `PerTurn`) rather than encoding any turn-state counting machinery — Rule 603.2 makes the event-match the trigger; the ordinal merely narrows which match counts. Controller defaults to You.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DrawNthCardEachTurnConditionRule.cs)

### `DrawPerSharedCreatureTypeThenDiscardRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"You may draw a card for each other creature you control that shares a creature type with it. If you do, discard a card." — Titan of Littjara's enters-or-attacks card-advantage trigger. The count is the number of OTHER creatures the controller controls that overlap the source's (chosen-plus-printed) creature types (`SharesCreatureTypeWith`), and the draw is coupled to a mandatory "if you do, discard a card" follow-up (CR 118.12) via `IfYouDo`.

Priority 90: must outrank the generic `DrawCardsTriggeredRule` (default priority 50), whose unanchored "draw a card" regex would otherwise match the "draw a card" substring anywhere in this text and silently drop both the "for each …" count qualifier and the entire "If you do, discard a card" follow-up — confirmed as the PRE-EXISTING lossy baseline for this exact oracle line before this rule was added.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DrawPerSharedCreatureTypeThenDiscardRule.cs)

### `DrawThatManyCardsLifeLostRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"draw that many cards" (imperative form) — draw effect where the count is derived from life just LOST by the triggering player. Backs the `LosesLife` trigger on Vilis, Broker of Blood: "Whenever you lose life, draw that many cards."

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." The antecedent of "that many" is the amount of life lost in the triggering event, keyed on `LifeLost`.

Distinct from `YouDrawThatManyCardsTriggeredRule` (which handles the "you draw that many cards" surface and keys the count on `DamageDealt`): Vilis's effect text omits the "you" subject (imperative form) and the triggering event is life loss, not damage dealt. This rule is NOT reflection-discovered into the generic effect loop (no `[TriggeredRule]` attribute); the `TriggeredAbilityParser` dispatches to it directly only when the resolved trigger event is `LosesLife`, preventing the "that many" surface from ever being resolved as `DamageDealt` under a life-loss trigger.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DrawThatManyCardsLifeLostRule.cs)

### `DrawThenMayPutLandFromHandRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"draw a card, then you may put a [filter] card from your hand onto the battlefield"

Handles the Spelunking ETB pattern: a two-step action within a single sentence where the controller draws a card and then optionally puts a qualifying card from their hand onto the battlefield. The two sub-effects are emitted as a `CompositeEffect` so the sentence-bundle dispatcher's one-effect-per-sentence invariant is preserved while the full semantics of the sentence are captured.

Rule citations:

CR 121.1: "A player draws a card by putting the top card of that player's library into that player's hand." CR 603.1: "Triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect." CR 400.7: "If an object in the exile zone or a face-up object in the command zone is put into another zone, it ceases to exist in its current zone and enters the new zone." (zone-change for the hand-to-battlefield move)

ANCHORED (^…$): the full sentence is matched exactly to prevent this rule from firing as a substring of any more-specific sibling. Priority 97 — higher than the plain `DrawCardsTriggeredRule` (default 50) and `PutFromHandOntoBattlefieldTriggeredRule` (63) so neither grabs a portion of this composite sentence before the full form is tried.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/DrawThenMayPutLandFromHandRule.cs)

### `EachOpponentBlightsTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"each opponent blights N" — triggered effect where each opponent performs the blight keyword action (CR 701.68). Emits a `BlightEffect` with `Player = EachOpponent`.

CR 701.68a (verbatim): "To 'blight N' means to put N -1/-1 counters on a creature you control." When an opponent blights, they put the counters on a creature THEY control (not the active player's creature). CR 701.68b: A player who controls no creatures cannot blight.

Pattern: "^each opponent blights \d+$" — anchored so "each opponent blights 1" cannot match inside a broader clause such as hypothetical multi-clause text. Reminder text "(They each put a -1/-1 counter on a creature they control.)" is stripped by the triggered-ability parser before this rule is called.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EachOpponentBlightsTriggeredRule.cs)

### `EachOpponentDiscardsRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"each [player|opponent] discards [a|N] card[s]" — the distributed discard effect imposed on every player (or every opponent) simultaneously. Rule 701.9 (Discard). MAST records the discard event, the count, and the player scope (`EachPlayer` or `EachOpponent`); the simultaneous discard order for multiplayer is engine territory, not described by the oracle text.

This is the triggered-side counterpart of the spell-level `DiscardEachPlayerRule` and mirrors the scope/count shape of `EachPlayerSacrificesTriggeredRule`: the player scope rides on the `Player` reference kind, and the count rides on `Count`. The dominant ETB form ("When this creature enters, each player discards a card." — Miasmic Mummy, Rotting Rats, Earsplitting Rats) lands here once the trigger/effect split has peeled the trigger prefix. "a card" yields a literal count of 1.

Despite the legacy name, this rule covers both the `each player` and `each opponent` scopes (the original opponent-only shape it was named for).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EachOpponentDiscardsRule.cs)

### `EachOpponentLosesLifeTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"each opponent loses N life" — symmetric drain trigger (Marauding Blight-Priest pattern). Covers triggered effects where all opponents lose a fixed life amount simultaneously.

Rule 119.3: "If a player would lose life, that player's life total is reduced by that amount." Rule 102.2: "An opponent is each other player." In multiplayer, this effect applies to each opponent simultaneously; the simultaneous-resolution ordering is engine territory, not described by oracle text.

This rule handles the bare N-life form only. The compound drain pattern "each opponent loses N life and you gain N life" is handled by `TryParseEachOpponentLoseAndYouGainLife` in the multi-effect composite path.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EachOpponentLosesLifeTriggeredRule.cs)

### `EachOpponentSacrificesUnlessPayTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"each [player|opponent] sacrifices [a|an|one|N] [type] [of their choice] unless they pay {COST}" — the distributed taxing-edict triggered form (Rishadan Cutpurse: "When this creature enters, each opponent sacrifices a permanent of their choice unless they pay {1}.").

CR 701.21 (Sacrifice) — the affected player always chooses which permanent they sacrifice, so "of their choice" is mechanically inert and is matched-and-discarded (mirroring `EachPlayerSacrificesTriggeredRule`). CR 118.1 — "A cost is an action or payment necessary to take another action or to stop another action from taking place"; the "unless they pay {COST}" clause is the payment each affected player may make to stop their own sacrifice from happening.

Produces a `PreventableEffect` wrapping a `SacrificeEffect`. The sacrificing scope rides on the `Target`'s `ObjectReferenceKind` (`EachPlayer` or `EachOpponent` — the same Target-holds-the-player convention used by `EachPlayerSacrificesTriggeredRule`); the sacrificed-object type rides on that reference's `ObjectFilter`. The `UnlessClause` Player carries the same scope ("they" refers back to each affected player). "a"/"an"/"one" yields no `Count` (singular is the default).

Distinct from `ThatPlayerSacrificesUnlessPayTriggeredRule` ("that player sacrifices … unless they pay …", the single triggering player) by the leading "each player/opponent" distributed scope, and from `EachPlayerSacrificesTriggeredRule` (same scope, no payment option) by the required "unless they pay {COST}" suffix.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EachOpponentSacrificesUnlessPayTriggeredRule.cs)

### `EachPlayerDrawsTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"each player draws a card" / "each opponent draws a card" — draw effect applied to all players simultaneously or to all opponents simultaneously. Rule 121 (Drawing a Card). MAST records the draw event and the player scope (EachPlayer or EachOpponent); the simultaneous draw order for multiplayer is engine territory, not described by the oracle text.

This rule covers the bare single-card form only. The composite "each player draws a card and loses N life" (Stormfist Crusader shape) is handled by the `TryParseEachPlayerDrawAndLoseLife` orchestrator in `TriggeredAbilityParser`, which runs before this rule and takes priority.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EachPlayerDrawsTriggeredRule.cs)

### `EachPlayerLosesLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"each player loses N life" — a symmetric life-loss effect (CR 119.3, VERBATIM: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."). "Each player" scopes the effect to every player in the game (controller and opponents alike) and maps to `EachPlayer`. Commonly paired with an enters-the-battlefield trigger (CR 603.6) such as Howling Banshee's "When this creature enters, each player loses 3 life."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EachPlayerLosesLifeRule.cs)

### `EachPlayerMillsTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"each player mills N cards." / "each opponent mills N cards." — Rule 701.17 keyword action (mill) broadcast across every player or every opponent simultaneously, on the triggered-ability effect side.

CR 701.17a (verbatim): "For a player to mill a number of cards, that player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard."

Mirrors `EachPlayerMillsNCardsEffectRule` (the activated-ability sibling covering "{cost}: Each player mills N cards.") but on the triggered side, e.g. Returned Reveler: "When this creature dies, each player mills three cards." Anchored (^ … $) so it never collides with the self-mill or targeted-mill patterns handled by `MillTriggeredRule`, both of which require the clause to start with "mill"/"target", not "each player"/"each opponent".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EachPlayerMillsTriggeredRule.cs)

### `EachPlayerSacrificesTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"each [player|opponent] sacrifices [a|an|one|N] [type] [of their choice]" — the triggered-ability form of the distributed (edict) sacrifice (CR 701.21 — Sacrifice). Covers the classic ETB edict family:

"each player sacrifices a creature of their choice." (Fleshbag Marauder, Slum Reaper) "each player sacrifices a land of their choice." (Razing Snidd) "each opponent sacrifices a creature." (edict variant) "each player sacrifices two creatures." (count variant)

"of their choice" is mechanically inert (CR 701.21a — the affected player always chooses which permanent they sacrifice), so it carries no extra AST; the optional suffix is matched and discarded. This mirrors the spell-level `EachSacrificesRule` shape: the sacrificed-object type rides on the `Target`'s `ObjectFilter`, and the player scope rides on the target's `ObjectReferenceKind` (`EachPlayer` or `EachOpponent`). "a"/"an"/"one" yields no `Count` (singular is the default).

Distinct from `SacrificeAnyCreatureTriggeredRule` ("sacrifice a creature" — the controller alone sacrifices) by the leading "each player/opponent" scope.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EachPlayerSacrificesTriggeredRule.cs)

### `EarthbendTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"earthbend N" — the Earthbend keyword action as a triggered effect.

CR 701.66a (verbatim): "\"Earthbend N\" means \"Target land you control becomes a 0/0 land creature with haste in addition to its other types. Put N +1/+1 counters on it. When that land dies or is put into exile, return it to the battlefield tapped under your control.\""

MAST records the keyword-action and its N parameter descriptively. The animation, counter placement, and delayed triggered ability are engine territory (CR 701.66b).

Pattern is anchored (^...$) to prevent matching as a substring of a more-specific sibling. Handles an optional leading "then " prefix so the rule fires correctly when the sentence-bundle splitter produces a "then earthbend" fragment.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EarthbendTriggeredRule.cs)

### `EnchantedBasicLandTypePutIntoGraveyardConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"When enchanted Swamp is put into a graveyard" — the Kamigawa "Genju" cycle's self-return trigger condition. The Aura's enchant restriction is a single basic land type (CR 305.6), so the trigger subject is "enchanted [BasicLandType]" rather than the generic "enchanted land"/"enchanted creature" noun handled elsewhere (`ParseObjectFilter`'s "enchanted creature" branch). The attachment is recorded on `IsEnchanted` (CR 303.4c / 702.5); the card type is "land" and the named subtype is the printed basic land type word.

Maps to `PutIntoGraveyard` rather than `Dies` — the oracle text says "is put into a graveyard" verbatim, without the "from the battlefield" longform that `DiesConditionRule` requires (CR 700.4 defines "dies" specifically as that longform; this line does not use it).

Canonical card: Genju of the Fens (DIS) — "When enchanted Swamp is put into a graveyard, you may return this card from your graveyard to your hand." The effect half is handled separately by `ReturnSelfFromGraveyardTriggeredRule` (identical effect text to the Eidolon cycle).

Priority 994 — above `SubtypePutIntoGraveyardConditionRule` (993), `DiesConditionRule` (991) and `PutIntoGraveyardConditionRule` (985), so this more specific "enchanted [BasicLandType]" shape is tried first. Anchored pattern (whole trigger-condition string) prevents substring collisions with longer/differently-scoped siblings.

Rule 603.2 (Triggered Abilities); Rule 404 (Graveyard); Rule 305.6 (basic land types); Rule 303.4c / 702.5 ("enchanted [type]" refers to the Aura's attached permanent).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EnchantedBasicLandTypePutIntoGraveyardConditionRule.cs)

### `EnchantedCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"enchanted creature gains [keyword] until end of turn." — grants a keyword ability to the creature enchanted by this Aura for the remainder of the turn. Covers Fae Flight's ETB trigger effect clause: "enchanted creature gains hexproof until end of turn." Rule 603.1: triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect; this rule handles the effect clause. Rule 611.1: a keyword grant is a continuous effect with a duration — "until end of turn" is the fixed duration, ending per rule 514.2 cleanup. Hexproof itself is a static ability (CR 702.11a) meaning "This permanent can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control" (CR 702.11b). "Enchanted creature" refers to the creature this Aura (CR 303.4) is attached to — modelled as `EnchantedOrEquipped`, the same reference used for static Aura/Equipment grant clauses (e.g. "Enchanted creature gets +1/+1"). Distinct from `ItGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` (anaphoric "it", the object named by the trigger's own filter) and `TargetCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` (a separately chosen target). "Enchanted creature" is neither — it is the Aura's fixed attachment, resolved via `EnchantedOrEquipped`. Builds the gained keyword ability with a small local switch rather than calling `BuildKeywordStaticAbility`, which has no "hexproof" arm.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EnchantedCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `EnchantedPlayerMillsXCardsWhereXIsGraveyardCountRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"enchanted player mills X cards, where X is the number of cards put into their graveyard from anywhere this turn." — the Fraying Sanity pattern (CR 701.17: "To mill N cards, a player puts the top N cards of their library into their graveyard."; CR 702.5: "Enchant player" — the enchanted player is the Aura's enchanted object).

X is a `CountQuantity` over cards owned by the enchanted player with a `PutIntoGraveyardThisTurnPredicate` history predicate, encoding the backward-looking "cards put into their graveyard from anywhere this turn" phrase faithfully per ADR 0004 (reference-not-resolution). The milling subject is the `EnchantedOrEquipped` reference (the enchanted player). The `FromZone` field on the predicate is set to `Anywhere` for the explicit "from anywhere" qualifier.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EnchantedPlayerMillsXCardsWhereXIsGraveyardCountRule.cs)

### `EnchantedTypeDiesConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"When enchanted land dies" — the Zendikon cycle's self-return trigger condition. The generic sibling of `EnchantedBasicLandTypePutIntoGraveyardConditionRule` (which is scoped to a single BASIC land subtype, e.g. "enchanted Swamp") and of the generic "enchanted creature" branch of `ParseObjectFilter` (which `DiesConditionRule` uses) — that helper has no "enchanted land"/ "enchanted [type]" branch, so this dedicated rule is added rather than widening the shared helper.

CR 700.4: "The term dies means 'is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.'" CR 303.4c / 702.5: an Aura's "enchanted [type]" refers to the permanent it's attached to (recorded on `IsEnchanted`, mirroring the IsSelf/IsToken axes). The card type stays whatever noun the oracle text used ("land" here), matching the Aura's own "Enchant land" restriction.

Canonical card: Vastwood Zendikon (and the rest of the Rise of the Eldrazi Zendikon cycle) — "When enchanted land dies, return that card to its owner's hand." The effect half ("return that card to its owner's hand") is handled separately by `ReturnThatCardToHandOnDeathTriggeredRule`.

Priority 992 — above the generic `DiesConditionRule` (991), whose `ParseObjectFilter` only recognises "enchanted creature" (not "enchanted land") and would otherwise return null and leave the trigger unparsed. Anchored pattern (whole trigger-condition string) prevents substring collisions with longer/differently-scoped siblings.

Rule 603.2 (Triggered Abilities); Rule 700.4 ("dies"); Rule 303.4c / 702.5 ("enchanted [type]" refers to the Aura's attached permanent).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EnchantedTypeDiesConditionRule.cs)

### `EnchantmentEntersOrFullyUnlocksRoomConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Compound Eerie trigger: "Whenever an enchantment you control enters and whenever you fully unlock a Room" (CR 207.2c ability word — Eerie). This is a single triggered ability that fires on EITHER of two events: (1) whenever an enchantment you control enters the battlefield, or (2) whenever you fully unlock a Room permanent.

CR 603.2: a triggered ability triggers whenever any of its listed events occurs. The "and whenever" phrase in oracle text combines two disjoint trigger conditions into one ability; the ability fires whenever EITHER condition is met. The primary condition (enchantment enters) is encoded on `TriggerCondition` (Trigger); the secondary condition (fully unlock a Room) is encoded on `AdditionalTrigger`.

CR 709.5i: "Some abilities trigger when a player 'fully unlocks' a permanent with a shared type line. Such an ability triggers when that permanent has one of the two unlocked designations and gets the other, or when it has neither designation and gains both." The Filter on the secondary trigger carries Controller = You (the ability fires only when the controller fully unlocks a Room).

Eerie is an ability word (CR 207.2c) — it has no special rules meaning and is stripped by TriggeredAbilityParser before trigger-condition parsing. This rule must be tried at higher priority than the generic `EntersConditionRule` so the compound phrase is matched before the enchantment-enters sub-phrase.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EnchantmentEntersOrFullyUnlocksRoomConditionRule.cs)

### `EntersAndCreatureControllerDealsCombatDamageToPlayerConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Compound trigger: "When [SelfName] enters and whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to a player" — Derevi, Empyrial Tactician (C13). A single triggered ability that fires on EITHER of two events: (1) when this permanent (self) enters the battlefield, or (2) whenever a creature the controller controls deals combat damage to a player.

CR 603.2: a triggered ability triggers whenever any of its listed events occurs. The "and" in oracle text ("When A and whenever B") combines two disjoint trigger conditions into one ability; the ability fires whenever EITHER condition is met. The primary condition (ETB self-by-name) is returned from `Match`; the secondary (creature you control deals combat damage) is signalled via `PendingAdditionalTrigger` so `TriggeredAbilityParser` can promote it to `TriggeredAbility.AdditionalTrigger`.

Rule 603.6a (ETB triggers): "Enters-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield." The self-by-name ETB primary (CR 201.5) is encoded as `IsSelf=true` on the filter (not `Controller=You`), because it refers to this permanent itself, not any creature the controller controls.

Rule 510 (Combat Damage Step): combat damage is dealt; CR 603.2 triggers fire. The secondary condition is `DealsCombatDamageToPlayer` with `Controller=You` on the filter — "a creature you control" means any creature the ability's controller controls (CR 109.5).

Anchored (`^...$`) to prevent substring-matching a broader trigger phrase. Must be tried at higher priority than the generic `EntersConditionRule` and `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule` so the compound phrase is matched as a unit before either sub-phrase claims it.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EntersAndCreatureControllerDealsCombatDamageToPlayerConditionRule.cs)

### `EntersAndOpponentDrawsNotFirstConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Compound trigger: "When this creature enters and whenever an opponent draws a card except the first one they draw in each of their draw steps" — Orcish Bowmasters (LTR). This is a single triggered ability that fires on EITHER of two events: (1) when this creature enters the battlefield, or (2) whenever an opponent draws any card that is not the first card drawn in their draw step.

CR 603.2: a triggered ability triggers whenever any of its listed events occurs. The "and" in oracle text ("When A and whenever B") combines two disjoint trigger conditions into one ability; the ability fires whenever EITHER condition is met. The primary condition (ETB) is encoded on `TriggerCondition` (Trigger); the secondary condition (opponent-draws-not-first) is encoded on `AdditionalTrigger`. Both share the same effect list.

The "except the first one they draw in each of their draw steps" qualifier is captured on the secondary condition's `ExceptFirstDrawStep` flag (CR 121.1: "a player draws a card"; CR 603.2: the qualifier narrows which draw events match). This is descriptive — the engine determines whether a given draw event is the first draw of the step; MAST records that the exclusion exists.

Must be tried at higher priority than the generic Enters and OpponentDrawsCard rules so the full compound phrase is matched before either sub-phrase.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EntersAndOpponentDrawsNotFirstConditionRule.cs)

### `EntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"enters" triggers: "this creature enters", "a creature enters", etc.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EntersConditionRule.cs)

### `EntersOrAttacksConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"enters or attacks" combined triggers — fires on either zone-change/combat event. Oracle form: "Whenever this creature enters or attacks, [effect]." Rule 603: "enters" (ETB, CR 400.4) and "attacks" (Declare Attackers step, CR 508) are distinct game events; a single triggered ability may name both via the "or" conjunction, triggering on whichever event occurs. Must be tried before the individual Enters/Attacks rules (higher priority = 993) so the disjunction isn't split and misclassified.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EntersOrAttacksConditionRule.cs)

### `EntersOrDiesConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"enters or dies" compound triggers — fires on either zone-change event. Rule 603: "When [subject] enters or dies, [effect]." The oracle phrase "enters or dies" (always in that order) denotes a single triggered ability watching for the permanent either entering the battlefield or dying. Must be tried before the individual Enters/Dies rules (higher priority) so the disjunction isn't split and misclassified.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EntersOrDiesConditionRule.cs)

### `EtbTeamPumpTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Creatures you control get +N/+M [and gain &lt;keyword&gt;] until end of turn." ETB team-pump pattern: the triggering creature buffs the whole team. The keyword grant is optional — both shapes are covered by one rule:

"Creatures you control get +1/+0 until end of turn." "Creatures you control get +1/+1 and gain haste until end of turn."

When only P/T is present the rule emits a bare `ModifyPTEffect`. When a keyword follows "and gain" the rule wraps both effects in a `CompositeEffect`, matching the conjunctive-modifier gold convention used on the static side (Rule 611 — continuous effects applied simultaneously). Recognised keywords (the set that appears in existing oracle corpus): haste, trample, flying, first strike, double strike, reach, lifelink, vigilance, deathtouch, menace, indestructible, hexproof, shroud.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/EtbTeamPumpTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ExcessNoncombatDamageDealtConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever a creature or planeswalker an opponent controls is dealt excess noncombat damage" — the Toralf trigger condition (KHM: Toralf, God of Fury). Fires when a creature or planeswalker controlled by an opponent receives noncombat damage that exceeds lethal damage or the permanent's loyalty (CR 120.10).

The filter carries `CardTypes = ["creature", "planeswalker"]` with `Controller = Opponent`. Both card types share one filter because the oracle text unifies them with "or" — no separate arms for each type.

CR 120.10 (verbatim): "Some triggered abilities check whether a permanent has been dealt excess damage. These abilities check after the permanent has been dealt damage by one or more sources. If those sources together dealt an amount of damage to a creature greater than lethal damage, excess damage equal to the difference was dealt to that creature. If those sources together dealt an amount of damage to a planeswalker greater than that planeswalker's loyalty before the damage was dealt, excess damage equal to the difference was dealt to that planeswalker."

Anchored (^…$) and scoped to the trigger clause to prevent matching inside a broader clause that contains "dealt excess noncombat damage" as a substring. Runs at priority 987 — above `SourceDealsNoncombatDamageConditionRule` (986) so the "excess noncombat" specialisation is claimed before the more-general "deals noncombat damage" rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExcessNoncombatDamageDealtConditionRule.cs)

### `ExileInstantFromHandImprintTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may exile an instant card with mana value 2 or less from your hand" — the Imprint triggered-ability effect (Isochron Scepter, Mirrodin / MRD:200).

CR 702.38 (Imprint): an imprint ability exiles a card from the controller's hand onto this permanent so a second ability may reference it. The exile is a one-shot effect (Rule 701.13) from Zone.Hand: the controller chooses an eligible card from their hand (not a targeted card — the word "target" does not appear) and exiles it. The choice is modelled as `Any` (controller-choice reference, CR 109.5) with Zone.Hand so the interaction layer can distinguish "from hand" from "on the battlefield". The "you may" gate is modelled as an `OptionalEffect` per ADR 0005.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExileInstantFromHandImprintTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ExilePlayerGraveyardZoneRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"exile target player's graveyard" / "exile target opponent's graveyard" / "exile each opponent's graveyard" / "exile each player's graveyard" — the graveyard-hate family that exiles the entire contents of a player's graveyard zone (Angel of Finality, Bojuka Bog, Hedonist's Trove, Dauntless Scrapbot).

CR 701.13a: "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is." The action exiles every card in the named graveyard, so the effect's target is the whole zone's contents rather than a single chosen card — modeled as an `Each` reference (all cards) whose filter pins the graveyard zone and the owning player. This mirrors the established whole-zone exile shape used by "Exile all creature cards from all graveyards" (`Kind=Each` + `Zone=Graveyard`) and the target-player graveyard scoping used by Riverchurn Monument (`Owner=Target` on a graveyard filter). The player scope rides the filter's `Owner` axis (CR 108.3 — cards in a graveyard are owned by that player): "target player's" → `Owner=Target`; "target opponent's" / "each opponent's" → `Owner=Opponent`.

Anchored (^…$) so it only fires on the bare whole-graveyard-exile body and never inside a longer composite clause a more-specific rule should handle.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExilePlayerGraveyardZoneRule.cs)

### `ExileSelfTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"exile it" / "exile this creature" / "exile this permanent" — a self-exile effect where the triggered ability's source exiles itself (or the trigger subject). Maps to an `ExileEffect` with `It` (the trigger subject / source).

Rule 701.13a (verbatim): "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is." MAST records the target as It (the subject of the trigger, i.e., the source permanent); the engine performs the zone change.

Examples: Eternal Scourge (EMN): "exile this creature."

Rule citations: 701.13a (Exile action), 109.2 (object reference), 603.1-603.2 (triggered ability machinery).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExileSelfTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetByManaValueUntilLeavesTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"exile target [filter] [an opponent controls] with mana value N or less/greater until this [type] leaves the battlefield." — the mana-value-gated variant of the Oblivion-Ring / Hieromancer's Cage ETB exile family (Portable Hole: "exile target nonland permanent an opponent controls with mana value 2 or less until this artifact leaves the battlefield").

This is the sibling of `ExileUntilLeavesTriggeredRule`: identical temporary-exile shape (Rule 611.1 — a continuous effect with a duration; Rule 406.1 — the exile zone; the return when this permanent leaves the battlefield is the linked engine behaviour, not a separate emitted effect), but with a mandatory "with mana value N or less/greater" qualifier (Rule 202.3 — mana value) sitting between the exile-target filter and the "until this ... leaves the battlefield" tail. That interior qualifier makes the plain family rule's `ParseTargetFilter` decline (the "or" in "N or less" defeats its card-type split), so this dedicated rule closes the gap. The threshold lands on `ManaValueComparison`.

The whole pattern is anchored (^…$) and the mana-value clause is mandatory, so it cannot substring-match a sibling that lacks the qualifier (which `ExileUntilLeavesTriggeredRule` continues to own). Rule 701.13 (exile); Rule 603.6 (the ETB zone-change trigger that carries this effect).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExileTargetByManaValueUntilLeavesTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetCardFromOpponentGraveyardTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"exile target card from an opponent's graveyard" — single-card graveyard-hate on the triggered side (Leonin of the Lost Pride, Ruin Rat, Disposal Mummy, Scavenging Harpy, Carrion Locust, General Kudro of Drannith): one chosen card in an opponent's graveyard is exiled.

Distinct from `ExilePlayerGraveyardZoneRule` (which exiles the WHOLE contents of a player's graveyard via `Each`). Here a single `Target` card is chosen, so the reference is `Kind=Target` with a `CardTypes=["card"]` + `Zone=Graveyard` filter, and the owning-player scope rides the filter's `Owner` axis: "an opponent's" / "target opponent's" → `Owner=Opponent` (CR 108.3 — a card in a graveyard is owned by that player; CR 404.2 — a graveyard is that player's pile).

The bare "exile target card from a graveyard" form (no owner scope) is handled by the activated/spell graveyard-exile rules and by `ExileTargetCardFromGraveyardRule`; this triggered rule deliberately covers only the opponent-scoped variant so it never overlaps the owner-less form.

Anchored (^…$) so it fires only when the entire effect clause is this single-card opponent-graveyard exile, never as a substring of a longer composite clause a more-specific sibling should own. Rule 701.13 (Exile) + Rule 108.3 (ownership) + Rule 404.2 (graveyard).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExileTargetCardFromOpponentGraveyardTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetPermanentCardFromGraveyardTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"exile target permanent card from your graveyard." — a single-target exile of a card sitting in the controller's graveyard, restricted to permanent card types (CR 110.4a: a "permanent card" is a card that is a permanent card type — artifact, battle, creature, enchantment, land, or planeswalker).

Distinct from `ExileTargetTriggeredRule` (which handles bare "exile target [filter]" with no zone suffix, via `ParseTargetFilter`, which does not parse a trailing "from your graveyard" zone phrase): this rule is anchored to the exact "... permanent card from your graveyard" composite surface (Savvy Trader's ETB), so it does not widen the shared helper's grammar or collide with the bare-filter sibling.

CR 701.13a (exile); CR 110.4a (permanent card); CR 404 (graveyard).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExileTargetPermanentCardFromGraveyardTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ExileTargetTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"exile target [filter]." — single-target permanent exile on the triggered side. Delegates filter parsing to `ParseTargetFilter` (same lexical surface as `ExileTargetSimpleRule`). Covers bare card-type targets (creature, permanent, artifact, enchantment, planeswalker) and richer filter phrases via `ParseTargetFilter`:

Subtype-only: "Spirit", "Human" Color + card type: "black creature", "white artifact" non- prefix + card type: "nonblack creature", "nontoken creature"

This rule handles PERMANENT exile (no "until [this] leaves the battlefield" suffix). The `ExileUntilLeavesTriggeredRule` handles the temporary Oblivion Ring shape.

An optional "another" before "target" is the CR 109.5 self-exclusion marker ("exile another target permanent" — Flickerwisp): it rides on `ExcludeSelf` = true rather than on the card-type axis.

Rule 701.13 (exile action) + Rule 205.3 (card types) + Rule 109.5 ("another").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExileTargetTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ExileThenReturnFlickerTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

ETB "flicker" (blink) effect: "you may exile [target] you control, then return that card to the battlefield under [its owner's / your] control." — the resolution half of an ETB trigger (Felidar Guardian, Restoration Angel).

The "you may" is a structured `OptionalEffect` (CR 117.7), not a flag: the controller may choose to perform the whole exile-then-return action. The action itself is a `CompositeEffect` of two ordered effects — an `ExileEffect` followed by a `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect`. "then return that card" is the LINKED exiled reference (the Petravark / Azula precedent), modelled via `ExiledWith` as a `{Zone: Exile, ExiledWith: {Kind: Self}}` reference (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution) rather than a threaded runtime binding or free text: the just-exiled card and this return are the same one resolving ability.

The exile target keeps its printed filter — "another target permanent you control" (`ExcludeSelf`, CR 109.5) or "target non-Angel creature you control" (`ExcludedSubtypes`). "under its owner's control" rides on `UnderControl` as an `Owner` reference; "under your control" as a `You` reference (CR 400.6).

CR 603.6a (enters-the-battlefield abilities) — this is the resolution half; the trigger condition ("When this creature enters") is recognised separately. CR 603.2 (the event-match is the trigger).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExileThenReturnFlickerTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ExileTopCardPlayThisTurnTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Exile the top card of your library. You may play that card this turn." — the single-card, current-turn-bounded impulse in a TRIGGERED context (Count on Luck: "At the beginning of your upkeep, ...").

The two oracle sentences are one semantic unit — "that card" back-references the single exiled card from the first sentence — so they collapse to a single `ImpulseEffect` with `RemainExiled` (nothing kept in hand; the one exiled card stays playable) and an inherited `Duration` of `EndOfTurn`. This is the singular sibling of the plural spell/activated shapes `ExileTopCardsPlayThisTurnRule` ("... You may play them this turn.") and `ExileTopCardsPlayThisTurnActivatedRule` ("... You may play those cards this turn."), emitting the identical node so the same effect reads consistently across spell, activated, and triggered contexts. CR 406 (exile zone); CR 701.13 (exile); CR 601.3 (play).

ANCHORED (^…$) to the exact two-sentence phrase so it can only ever claim the whole unit — never a lone "Exile the top card of your library" or a lone "You may play that card this turn". This is what keeps the dispatcher's sentence-bundle splitter from fragmenting the pair: neither half parses on its own, so the splitter bails and the full text reaches this rule intact.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExileTopCardPlayThisTurnTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ExileUntilLeavesTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"exile target [filter] [an opponent controls] until this [type] leaves the battlefield." — the Banisher Priest / Oblivion Ring / Hieromancer's Cage ETB exile family. Generalises across:

self subject — creature (Banisher Priest, Bishop of Binding), enchantment (Citizen's Arrest, Hieromancer's Cage), artifact/Vehicle (Detention Chariot), …; carried in the duration's `Object` self-reference phrase; exile target — a single card type ("creature"), a card-type disjunction ("creature or planeswalker", "artifact or creature"), or "nonland permanent"; optional "an opponent controls" controller restriction.

The effect is a temporary exile: the exiled permanent returns when this [type] leaves the battlefield (Rule 611 — continuous effects with duration; Rule 406 — the exile zone). MAST records the exile action descriptively (Rule 701.13 — Exile) with an `UntilLeavesBattlefieldDuration` whose `Object` is the literal self-reference phrase from oracle text ("this enchantment", "this creature", etc.). The combined "exile ... until this leaves the battlefield" clause IS the linkage (Rule 603.6 — zone-change triggers; Rule 603.7 — the delayed/linked return). The implicit LTB return is engine territory; MAST does not emit a separate return effect for the combined-clause form (descriptive-not-engine doctrine). Cards that instead print two explicit triggers (Fiend Hunter, Petravark) are modelled as two abilities elsewhere — not this rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExileUntilLeavesTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ExileUpToOneGraveyardAndCreateFoodRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"exile up to one target card from a graveyard and create a Food token" — the compound triggered-effect pattern from Hazel's Brewmaster. Produces a `CompositeEffect` of an `ExileEffect` (up to one target graveyard card) followed by a `CreateTokenEffect` (Food).

CR 701.13a: "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is." CR 111.10b: "A Food token is a colorless Food artifact token with '{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: You gain 3 life.'" CR 602 / 603: the exile and token-creation are bundled into a single effect body separated by "and"; both effects resolve together at ability resolution.

Anchored (^…$) to prevent matching inside a longer "exile…and…" body that carries additional clauses a more-specific rule should handle.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExileUpToOneGraveyardAndCreateFoodRule.cs)

### `ExploreTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it explores." — Rule 701.44a keyword action on the triggered side. Matches the canonical ETB-explore pattern where the entering creature (referred to as "it") performs the Explore keyword action.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ExploreTriggeredRule.cs)

### `FlickerUpToOnePermanentTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"exile up to one [other] target [type] you control, then return that card to the battlefield under [its owner's | your] control" — the "up to one" flicker (blink): the cast-trigger of Displacer Kitten ("Avoidance — Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, …", nonland permanent / its owner's control) and the end-step trigger of Thassa, Deep-Dwelling ("At the beginning of your end step, exile up to one other target creature you control, … under your control").

This is the triggered-side wrapper of the same flicker effect the spell-side `FlickerTargetPermanentsSpellRule` (Ghostly Flicker) builds: an `ExileEffect` on the chosen permanent, then a `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect` of the just-exiled card. The trigger condition itself ("Whenever you cast a noncreature spell" / "At the beginning of your end step") is recognised separately per CR 603.2 (a game event matching the trigger event triggers the ability); this rule only builds the effect.

"that card" is NOT free text — it is the linked exiled reference (CR 607.2 / ADR 0004 "reference, not resolution"): a `Designated` card in `Exile` exiled with this object (`ExiledWith = {Kind: Self}`), the Petravark return shape. "up to one" is a structured `UpToQuantity` on the target reference's `Quantity`, not a literal. The target keeps its printed filter — "[other] target [type] you control" (`CardTypes` + the `ExcludeSelf` "other" self-exclusion, CR 109.5 + `Controller = You`; the "nonland permanent" shape adds `ExcludedCardTypes = ["land"]`). "under its owner's control" rides on `UnderControl` as a `Owner` reference, "under your control" as a `You` reference (CR 400.6). The two effects sit in one `CompositeEffect` because the oracle states them as a single "exile …, then return …" action.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/FlickerUpToOnePermanentTriggeredRule.cs)

### `GainControlTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"gain control of target [filter] [until end of turn]" — single-target control-change on the triggered side (ETB, dies, upkeep, etc.). Delegates single-noun filter parsing to `ParseTargetFilter`. Also handles the controller qualifier "an opponent controls" after the filter phrase, which is the canonical way oracle text restricts steal effects to opposing permanents (Rule 109.5 — control relationship). Duration is optional:

"until end of turn" → `UntilEndOfTurnDuration` No duration clause → <see langword="null"/> (permanent control change)

The optional "you may" prefix sets `IsOptional` = <see langword="true"/>. Recognized filter nouns (via `ParseTargetFilter`): creature, permanent, artifact, enchantment, planeswalker, land, and richer filter phrases (color + type, non- prefix, etc.). Rule 701.3 (control-changing effects) + Rule 115.1 (target).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/GainControlTriggeredRule.cs)

### `GainEnergyTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you get {E}", "you get {E}{E}", ... — energy-counter gain triggered effect. Rule 107.14: Energy counters are a player resource represented by the {E} symbol. Each "{E}" symbol in the oracle text represents one energy counter; we count the symbols to derive the literal amount.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/GainEnergyTriggeredRule.cs)

### `GainProtectionFromEverythingTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you gain protection from everything until your next turn" — The One Ring's ETB consequent.

A player gains protection from everything (CR 702.16 — protection; CR 702.16e — a player can have protection). Modeled as a `GainAbilityEffect` granting the controller (`You`) a static `Protection` ability whose quality is `Everything`, for `YourNextTurn` (CR 611 — continuous effect with a duration). The "if you cast it" gate is a separate intervening-if (`CastThisObjectCondition`) handled by the triggered-ability parser, not this effect.

ANCHORED (`^…$`) on the full clause so no sibling protection-grant is mislabeled.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/GainProtectionFromEverythingTriggeredRule.cs)

### `GainsLifeConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you gain life" — life-gain trigger. Controller defaults to You, flips to Opponent when the oracle text names an opponent.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/GainsLifeConditionRule.cs)

### `HauntCompoundConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"When this creature enters or the creature it haunts dies" — Haunt compound trigger (Rule 702.55). Fires in two situations: (1) when this creature enters the battlefield, and (2) when the creature this card haunts dies. Both events are modelled as the single `EntersOrHauntedCreatureDies`. Must be tried before the generic enters/dies rules (higher priority) — this trigger contains both words.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/HauntCompoundConditionRule.cs)

### `HaveItFightTargetTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Recognises the ETB-trigger "have it fight" shape: "you may have it fight target creature you don't control." "you may have it fight target creature an opponent controls." "have it fight target creature you don't control." (non-optional variant) The controller's participant is a pronoun back-reference ("it", CR 109.5 / antecedent) to the object that triggered the ability — the creature that just entered (e.g. Somberwald Stag: "When this creature enters, you may have it fight target creature you don't control."). Modelled as `It`, mirroring `ItFightsColorControlledSpellRule`. Distinct from that spell rule in two ways: (1) surface is the causative "have it fight" (an ETB trigger directs the entering creature) rather than the bare "It fights"; (2) the opponent's creature carries no colour restriction. As in `FightRule`, both "you don't control" and "an opponent controls" produce identical AST — the Comprehensive Rules treat them as equivalent for targeting, so `Opposed` is always `Controller: Opponent`. Reminder text "(Each deals damage equal to its power to the other.)" is stripped before rules run. CR 701.14 (Fight keyword action). The "you may" prefix is optional; its presence wraps the `FightEffect` in an `OptionalEffect` via `Optional` (ADR 0005 clause-modifier composition), the same convention the sibling ETB tutor rules use. Anchored with `^…$`; the mandatory "have it fight" core keeps it from matching the "Target creature you control fights …" or "It fights …" surfaces handled by the spell-side fight rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/HaveItFightTargetTriggeredRule.cs)

### `IfPutSubtypeOntoBattlefieldThisWayGainLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"If you put a [Subtype] onto the battlefield this way, you gain [N] life."

Handles the Spelunking pattern: a conditional effect sentence (CR 603.12 — reflexive triggered ability) that fires based on whether the card moved to the battlefield by the preceding optional zone-change in the same ability had a particular subtype. Modelled as a `ConditionalEffect` whose `Condition` is an `OtherCondition` (the causation-gate "this way" plus a subtype filter is a compound shape without a dedicated structured arm yet — ADR 0001 residual) and whose `Then` is a `GainLifeEffect`.

CR 603.12 (verbatim): "A resolving spell or ability may allow or instruct a player to take an action and create a triggered ability that triggers 'when [a player] [does or doesn't]' take that action or 'when [something happens] this way.' These reflexive triggered abilities follow the rules for delayed triggered abilities (see rule 603.7), except that they're checked immediately after being created and trigger based on whether the trigger event or events occurred earlier during the resolution of the spell or ability that created them."

CR 119.3 (verbatim): "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."

ANCHORED (^…$): fully anchored to prevent false-positive substring matches. Priority 97 — same band as `DrawThenMayPutLandFromHandRule` so both Spelunking sentences are processed before less-specific rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/IfPutSubtypeOntoBattlefieldThisWayGainLifeRule.cs)

### `IfSacrificeSubtypeThisWayDealsDamageToYouRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule
