"If you sacrifice a[n] [Subtype] this way, this creature deals [N] damage to you." — a within-resolution back-reference to the object sacrificed by a PRECEDING effect in the same ability (Serendib Djinn's "At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice a land. If you sacrifice an Island this way, this creature deals 3 damage to you.").

Mirrors `IfPutSubtypeOntoBattlefieldThisWayGainLifeRule`: the "this way" causation-gate plus a subtype filter on the object affected by the earlier effect is a compound shape without a dedicated structured arm yet, so the condition is deferred honestly via `OtherCondition` (ADR 0001 residual — a typed, counted deferral, not a destination). CR 603.12 governs the general "…this way" reflexive-condition idiom (a resolving effect's own follow-up checking how an earlier part of the SAME resolution played out).

CR 120.1 (verbatim): "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. … An object that deals damage is the source of that damage." The damage source is "this creature" — the ability's own source object (CR 109) — modelled as `Self`. CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly" (the "to you" recipient — the ability's controller).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): fully anchored to prevent false-positive substring matches against any broader sibling sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/IfSacrificeSubtypeThisWayDealsDamageToYouRule.cs)

### `IncubateTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"incubate N" — the Incubate keyword action as a triggered effect (CR 701.53).

CR 701.53a: "To incubate N, create an Incubator token that enters the battlefield with N +1/+1 counters on it. See rule 111.10i."

CR 603.6a: Enters-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield. These are written, "When [this object] enters, . . ." — Converter Beast's "When this creature enters, incubate 5." is such an ETB trigger.

The rule receives the effect text AFTER the parser has split off the trigger condition and stripped the trailing "(…)" reminder (CR 207.2), so it sees exactly "incubate 5". MAST records the keyword-action and its count descriptively; the Incubator token, its counters, and its "{2}: Transform this token." body are engine territory (reminder text, CR 701.53b). Emits the bare `IncubateEffect` — incubate is mandatory, not a "may".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/IncubateTriggeredRule.cs)

### `InvestigateTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"investigate." — Rule 701.16a keyword action on the triggered side. Matches the bare keyword action when it appears as the entire effect body of a triggered ability (e.g. Thraben Inspector's ETB trigger). CR 701.16a: "Investigate" means "Create a Clue token." See rule 111.10f. CR 603.6a: Enters-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield. These are written, "When [this object] enters, . . . "... REUSE-ONLY: emits the existing `InvestigateEffect` node. No new AST types are introduced.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/InvestigateTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ItDealsCountDamageToAnyTargetRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals X damage to any target, where X is the number of [Subtype]s you control." — the entering permanent deals damage equal to a count of a subtype you control to any legal target. Covers Dragon Tempest's second ability: "it deals X damage to any target, where X is the number of Dragons you control." Rule 603: triggered abilities resolve by executing their effects. Rule 120.1– 120.2: a source deals damage to a permanent or player. Rule 115.4: "any target" may be any player, creature, planeswalker, or battle. "It" is the anaphoric pronoun (CR 113.8b) referring to the entering Dragon — the permanent the trigger's filter matched. Modelled as `It`. The amount "X" is a `CountQuantity` — the count of permanents matching the filter (subtype + controller = You). "Where X is the number of…" is a definitional clause naming the quantity; the variable letter X has no independent identity here — the structured `CountQuantity` replaces it. Distinct from `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule`, which handles a fixed literal amount ("it deals 3 damage").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ItDealsCountDamageToAnyTargetRule.cs)

### `ItDealsDamageEqualToItsPowerToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals damage equal to its power to any target." — a death (or other) trigger whose damage amount is derived from the source's own power rather than a fixed number, e.g. "When this creature dies, it deals damage equal to its power to any target." Rule 603.1: triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect (When/ Whenever/At [condition], [effect]). Rule 120.1: an object that deals damage is the source of that damage. Rule 115.4: "any target" may be a creature, player, planeswalker, or battle. This is the derived-Power sibling of `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule`, which handles the literal N-damage form ("it deals N damage to any target"). The two are disjoint: that rule requires a numeric/word amount token between "deals" and "damage", while this rule requires the literal phrase "damage equal to its power" — neither regex can match the other's text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ItDealsDamageEqualToItsPowerToAnyTargetTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ItDealsDamageToTargetTypeDisjunctionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals N damage to target [type] or [type]." — the ETB-damage family with a <b>disjunctive target</b>. Covers cards whose triggered ETB ability reads "When this creature enters, it deals N damage to target player or planeswalker" (Viashino Pyromancer, Keldon Champion, Goretusk Firebeast, Sparkcaster) and "… target opponent or planeswalker" (Cinder Hellion, Gruesome Scourger). Rule 603: triggered abilities (When/Whenever/At). Rule 120.1: a source deals damage to a creature, planeswalker, battle, or player; absent any "combat damage" marker the damage is non-combat (Rule 120 vs Rule 510), so `IsCombat` is left null. Rule 115.1: "target" creates a target. The disjunction "X or Y" is a single target whose set of legal types is the union {X, Y} (Rule 115.4 reasoning generalized to an explicit two-type union), so it is one `Target` with a `CardTypes` union — the same shape the spell-side `SelfDealsDamageToTypeDisjunctionRule` produces for Lava Axe. "player"/"opponent" are listed alongside card types because `CardTypes` encodes both card types and game entities that can be dealt damage (Rule 120.1); "opponent" additionally carries the Rule 102.2 relation (a player not on the controller's team). The "or" is REQUIRED: the bare single-type forms are handled by their dedicated rules (`SelfDealsDamageToOpponentRule` for "target opponent", `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` for "any target"), so this rule fires only on the two-type disjunction and never double-matches them. The subject is the triggered pronoun "it" — the source of the ability ("some abilities cause a source to do something … 'This creature deals 1 damage to any target'"), modeled as `It`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ItDealsDamageToTargetTypeDisjunctionRule.cs)

### `ItDealsDamageToTargetTypeTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals N damage to target [type]." — the single-type sibling of the ETB/death damage family. Covers triggered abilities such as "When this creature dies, it deals 2 damage to target creature." (Bogardan Firefiend) and "When this creature enters, it deals 2 damage to target creature." (Fire Imp, Corrupt Eunuchs, Goblin Commando). Rule 603.1: triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect, written "[When/Whenever/At] [trigger condition], [effect]." Rule 120.1-120.2: any object can deal damage to a battle, creature, planeswalker, or player; the object that deals damage is the source of that damage. Rule 115.1: "target" creates a target that must be declared as the ability is put on the stack. The subject is the triggered pronoun "it" (referring back to the trigger's source), modelled as `It` — the same convention used by the sibling rules below. REQUIRES a single bare type with no trailing qualifier ("or …", "with …", "an opponent controls", "it's blocking") and no leading conditional clause — those shapes are handled elsewhere or remain unstructured:

`ItDealsDamageToTargetTypeDisjunctionRule` — requires "or" joining two types ("target creature or planeswalker"). `SelfDealsDamageToOpponentRule` — "target opponent" (no "or"), modelled as `Opponent` rather than a Target+Filter; "opponent"/"player" are therefore excluded from this rule's type set so the two rules never compete for the same text. `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` — "any target", a distinct `AnyTarget` shape.

Mirrors the activated-ability analogue's "to target &lt;type&gt;" branch in `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetEffectRule`, which handles the same shape for activated costs ("Sacrifice this creature: It deals 2 damage to target creature.").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ItDealsDamageToTargetTypeTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ItDealsInstantSorceryGraveyardCountDamageToOpponentCreatureRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals X damage to target creature an opponent controls, where X is the number of instant and sorcery cards in your graveyard." — the entering permanent deals damage to a targeted opponent-controlled creature equal to the count of instant and sorcery cards in your graveyard. Covers Cyclops Electromancer's enters trigger. CR 603.2: triggered abilities resolve by executing their effects. CR 120.1– 120.2: a source deals damage to a permanent or player. CR 115.1: "target" creates a target — the recipient is "target creature an opponent controls" (`Target` + `Opponent`). "It" is the anaphoric pronoun referring to the entering creature the trigger matched — the ability's own source; modelled as `It`. The amount "X" is a `CountQuantity` — the count of objects matching the filter (instant/sorcery card types + `You` + `Graveyard`). "Where X is the number of…" is a definitional clause naming the quantity; the letter X has no independent identity here — the structured `CountQuantity` replaces it. The filter mirrors the same "instant and sorcery cards in your graveyard" shape Cryptic Serpent's cost-reduction fixture already encodes. Sibling of `ItDealsCountDamageToAnyTargetRule` (Dragon Tempest, which deals a subtype-you-control count to "any target"). Fully anchored (`^…$`) on the specific "target creature an opponent controls" recipient and the "instant and sorcery cards in your graveyard" count clause so it cannot capture a broader or sibling effect fragment.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ItDealsInstantSorceryGraveyardCountDamageToOpponentCreatureRule.cs)

### `ItDealsThatMuchDamageToAnyTargetExcludingSubtypeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals that much damage to any target that isn't a [Subtype]." — the damage-redirection effect on Wrathful Red Dragon ("Whenever a Dragon you control is dealt damage, it deals that much damage to any target that isn't a Dragon."). "It" is the triggering permanent (the previously mentioned Dragon, not necessarily this card's own source — see `SubtypeDealtDamageConditionRule`), "that much" is the amount of damage it was just dealt, and "any target that isn't a [Subtype]" is an unrestricted target (creature, player, planeswalker, or battle) excluding members of the named subtype.

The antecedent of "that much" is the damage dealt in the triggering event (`DamageDealt`), matching the `CreatureDealtDamage` trigger. The exclusion is carried on `ExcludedSubtypes` (CR 205.3 — subtypes) rather than restricting `CardTypes`, since "any target" is not itself narrowed to creatures — only Dragons (a creature subtype) are excluded from an otherwise unrestricted target.

CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. … An object that deals damage is the source of that damage." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." This is the "any target excluding a subtype" sibling of `ItDealsThatMuchDamageToYouRule` ("to you", self-restricted trigger) and reuses the same `DamageDealt` "that much" derivation.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ItDealsThatMuchDamageToAnyTargetExcludingSubtypeRule.cs)

### `ItDealsThatMuchDamageToYouRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals that much damage to you." — the reflexive-punishment effect on Jackal Pup ("Whenever this creature is dealt damage, it deals that much damage to you."). "It" is the creature itself (the trigger's source), "that much" is the amount of damage the creature was just dealt, and "you" is its controller.

The antecedent of "that much" is the damage dealt in the triggering event (`DamageDealt`), matching the `CreatureDealtDamage` trigger. The target "you" is the controller of the source (CR 109.5: "The words 'you' and 'your' on an object refer to the object's controller …"), carried as `You`; the source is the creature itself, carried on `Source` as `Self`.

CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. … An object that deals damage is the source of that damage." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." This is the "to you" sibling of `DealThatMuchDamageToControllerRule` ("to that creature's controller") and the "that much" sibling of `SelfDealsDamageToYouRule` (which handles a literal amount "deals N damage to you").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ItDealsThatMuchDamageToYouRule.cs)

### `ItDoesntUntapTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Standalone "freeze" back-reference effect on the resolution half of a triggered ability: "it doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step." (Stitcher's Graft: "Whenever equipped creature attacks, it doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step.").

Sibling of `ThatCreatureDoesntUntapTriggeredRule` ("that creature doesn't untap …"), but the pronoun here is "it" — referring back to the trigger's SUBJECT (the creature that attacked), not a third object named separately in the trigger condition. Maps to `It`, matching the pronoun convention used elsewhere for the trigger subject (e.g. `SacrificeTriggeredRule`'s "sacrifice it").

CR 502.3 (Untap Step, verbatim): "Third, the active player determines which permanents they control will untap. Then they untap them all simultaneously. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack. Normally, all of a player's permanents untap, but effects can keep one or more of a player's permanents from untapping." The "next untap step" wording is recorded on `WhoseUntapStep` as "its controller's next".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ItDoesntUntapTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ItGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it gains [keyword] until end of turn." — grants a keyword ability to the entering object (referred to as "it") for the remainder of the turn. Covers Dragon Tempest's first ability resolution clause: "it gains haste until end of turn." Rule 603: triggered abilities resolve by executing their effects. Rule 611.1: effects that modify characteristics (such as keyword abilities) are continuous effects with a duration. "Until end of turn" is the most common duration for triggered keyword grants. The target "it" refers anaphorically (CR 113.8b) to the permanent named by the trigger's filter — the entering creature. Modelled as `It` (the generic anaphoric pronoun). Distinct from `TeamGainKeywordTriggeredRule`, which targets "creatures you control" (an `Each` reference), not the entering creature itself.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ItGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `LandOfChosenTypeBecomesTappedConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever a land of the chosen type [you control|an opponent controls] becomes tapped" — the structured consumer side of a CR 607 linked ability whose producer is an as-enters "choose [basic land type]" static replacement (CR 614.12; Roots of Life). The "of the chosen type" qualifier back-references the earlier choice via `ChosenCharacteristic` = `BasicLandType` rather than free text.

CR 603.2: "Some trigger events use the word 'becomes' … These trigger only at the time the named event happens." Reuses `BecomesTapped`, the same event as the plain "becomes tapped" sibling `BecomesTappedConditionRule`. This rule is tried FIRST (higher priority) so the chosen-characteristic reference is captured before `BecomesTappedConditionRule`'s generic `TriggeredRuleHelpers.ParseObjectFilter` path (which recognizes "a land ... controls" but has no notion of "of the chosen type") claims the clause and silently drops it.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/LandOfChosenTypeBecomesTappedConditionRule.cs)

### `LeavesTheBattlefieldConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"leaves the battlefield" triggers: "this creature leaves the battlefield", "a creature you control leaves the battlefield", etc. (CR 603.2 — a game event matching a triggered ability's trigger event causes it to trigger). This is the LTB half of a CR 607.2 linked pair on cards like Petravark, whose ETB exiles a permanent and whose LTB returns the card exiled by that same ability. MAST records the trigger event descriptively; the linkage to the exiled card is carried on the effect side via the `ExiledWith` reference, not threaded here (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/LeavesTheBattlefieldConditionRule.cs)

### `LookAtTopCardsTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"look at the top N cards of your library, then put them back in any order." — The Crystal Seer ETB pattern. Rule 701.12 (look) + unconditional reorder. The controller looks at the top N cards then returns all of them in any chosen order. Distinct from scry (top/bottom choice per card) and surveil (graveyard option).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/LookAtTopCardsTriggeredRule.cs)

### `LookAtTopMayRevealMatchingRestToBottomTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Look at the top N cards of your library. You may reveal a(n) [filter] card from among them and put it into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order." — Dragonologist's ETB pattern.

The whole three-sentence fragment is one coherent game action — "from among them" and "the rest" in the second and third sentences are back-references to the look in the first — so this rule matches all three sentences as a single fragment and emits one `LookAtTopMayRevealMatchingRestToBottomEffect`. Looking is a general instruction (not a CR 701 keyword action); CR 701.20a (reveal); CR 401.4 (the remainder placed on the bottom in a random order).

The filter clause is either a single card-type/subtype word, an "or" two-way disjunction, or a two-comma three-way disjunction ("an instant, sorcery, or Dragon card") whose members may mix card types (instant, sorcery, …) and a capitalised creature subtype (Dragon) — the mixed type-or-subtype shape `CounterTargetTypeOrSubtypeSpellRule` already establishes for a two-way disjunction, generalised here to any count of comma/or-joined members.

Priority 95: must beat the generic multi-sentence bundle splitter (mirroring `RevealTopMayPutSharesCreatureTypeRestToBottomTriggeredRule`), which would otherwise try to resolve each of the three sentences independently and fail.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/LookAtTopMayRevealMatchingRestToBottomTriggeredRule.cs)

### `LoseLifeDerivedRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"target opponent loses that much life" — Vito's drain shape. Encodes the derived quantity (LifeGained antecedent) and the OPPONENT recipient.

The recipient is `Opponent` — a singular opponent (CR glossary "Opponent"), matching the corpus convention for opponent-player references (Eroded Canyon, Jagged Barrens, Lonely Arroyo). It is NOT a generic `Target {{ CardTypes = ["player"] }}`: dropping the opponent constraint flattens "an opponent" to "any player" (which could be you), which is rules-wrong and downstream costs interaction recall — the operator cannot certify the loser is an opponent, so a life-drain loop (Vito × Exquisite Blood) floors to a needless AMBER. The opponent reference is the parse-layer precision that lets that hop tier GREEN (see libs/mast-interaction/docs/adding-a-flow-arm.md).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/LoseLifeDerivedRule.cs)

### `LoseLifePerNamedCounterTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you lose 1 life for each [counter] counter on [self]" — The One Ring's upkeep drain ("you lose 1 life for each burden counter on The One Ring").

You lose life equal to the number of named counters on the source (1 per counter). Modeled as a `LoseLifeEffect` whose `Amount` is a `CounterCountQuantity` over the named counter on `Self` (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004 — the engine reads the live counter count). CR 122 (counters); the "1 … for each" is the unit per-counter multiplier, i.e. the count itself.

The self target is "it" or the card naming itself (a capitalized name → self-reference, CR 201.5); a reference to ANOTHER permanent's counters uses "that"/"target"/lowercase and is not matched here. ANCHORED on the full clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/LoseLifePerNamedCounterTriggeredRule.cs)

### `LosesLifeConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever an opponent loses life" / "Whenever you lose life" — life-loss trigger (Exquisite Blood, Bloodthirsty Conqueror). The controller axis is carried on the trigger's filter: `Opponent` when the oracle text names an opponent, else `You`.

CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." The matched event is a player losing life (CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."). The amount of life lost is referenced by a downstream "that much" effect (a derived quantity); this rule records only the event + the player class.

Mirrors `GainsLifeConditionRule` (the `GainsLife` sibling): same controller-default-flip shape, the opposite life event.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/LosesLifeConditionRule.cs)

### `ManaPersistsUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Until end of turn, you don't lose this mana as steps and phases end." — the mana-persistence clause on Birgi, God of Storytelling.

CR 106.4 / CR 500.5: normally mana empties at the end of each step and phase. This sentence is the oracle-text signal that the mana produced in the same triggered ability persists until end of turn instead, overriding the turn-based mana-emptying action.

ANCHORED (^…$): the surface phrase "don't lose this mana as steps and phases end" is highly specific and cannot match as a substring of another triggered rule. Anchoring is maintained as a defensive convention (ADR anchor rule).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ManaPersistsUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `MassModifyPTTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"creatures your opponents control get -N/-M until end of turn" (and siblings: "All creatures get ...", "Creatures you control get ...", "Attacking/Blocking creatures get ...") appearing as the RESOLUTION EFFECT of a triggered ability — e.g. Plague Mare's "When this creature enters, creatures your opponents control get -1/-1 until end of turn."

CR 603.1: "Triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect. They are written as '[When/Whenever/At] [trigger condition or event], [effect]. ...'" — the timing (When this creature enters) and the effect (creatures your opponents control get -1/-1 until end of turn) are separate composable nodes; this rule only recognises the effect half, which `TriggeredAbilityParser` pairs with the already-parsing "When ... enters" trigger.

CR 613.4c: "Layer 7c: Effects and counters that modify power and/or toughness (but don't set power and/or toughness to a specific number or value) are applied." — "get -1/-1 until end of turn" is a layer-7c P/T modification, hence a `ModifyPTEffect` built from literal -1/-1 modifiers, not a set-P/T effect.

This is a NEW, collision-free file rather than an edit to `MassAnthemSpellRule` or to `TriggeredAbilityParser`: `ITriggeredRule` and `ISpellRule` share the identical `bool TryMatch(string text, out Effect? effect)` signature, so this rule simply delegates to a stateless `MassAnthemSpellRule` instance, reusing the exact node the spell parser already produces for the identical surface (verified against MakeObsolete.json gold). This mirrors the in-repo precedent in `TriggeredAbilityParser`.ParseEffects, where the dispatcher reuses the spell composite rules `ModifyPTAndGainKeyword[Controlled]SpellRule` for the triggered "gets +N/+M and gains &lt;keyword&gt;" surface.

No shadowing: `ModifyPTTriggeredRule` guards on subjects "it"/"this creature"/"target creature" and returns false for "creatures your opponents control" (and the other mass subjects here), so the two rules match disjoint subjects.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/MassModifyPTTriggeredRule.cs)

### `MayExileGraveyardCreatureWithLesserPowerThenCopyExileAtEndOfCombatRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may exile target creature card with lesser power from your graveyard. If you do, create a token that's a copy of that card and that's tapped and attacking. Exile the token at end of combat." — Gyrus, Waker of Corpses's attack-trigger resolution body (CR 508.1k covers a token entering as an attacking creature; CR 702.134 is the "lesser power" comparison family shared with Mentor).

One `OptionalEffect` (ADR 0005 "you may"): `Inner` is the graveyard exile (`ExileEffect`, `Target` filtered to `Zone.Graveyard`, `Controller.You`, and a `Comparison` on `PowerComparison` — `LessThan` relative to `Self`'s power, mirroring Mentor/Hammer Dropper's "with lesser power" shape). `IfYouDo` is a `CompositeEffect` of the two consequences that only make sense once a card was actually exiled:

"create a token that's a copy of that card" — a `CopyEffect` whose `Target` is `It`, the anaphoric back-reference to the just-exiled card (mirrors `CopyExiledCardAndCastWithoutPayingEffectRule`'s "the copy" → `It` convention). "and that's tapped and attacking" is the contextually-implicit qualifier already established as NOT a separate `CopyEffect` field by `CreateTappedAttackingCopyOfNontokenCreatureRule` (Satya, Aetherflux Genius's gold fixture). "Exile the token at end of combat." — a `CreateDelayedTriggerEffect` (CR 603.7) whose clock point is `GameTime{Part:Combat, Edge:End}` ("at end of combat" — the same `GameTime` shape `RemoveCountersTriggeredRule` uses for the identical clock phrase), exiling `It` — the anaphoric back-reference to the token just created by the sibling effect above (mirrors `SacrificeAtEndStepTriggeredRule`'s "Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step" pattern for a token created earlier in the same resolution).

The delayed exile is nested inside `IfYouDo` (not a third top-level sibling effect) because it is only meaningful when the token from step 1 exists — both consequences flow from the same "if you do" branch.

Implemented as a single `ITriggeredRule` matching the WHOLE three-sentence effect body (periods included, final period stripped by the dispatcher) because the "If you do" consequence must stay paired with its governing "you may" — the dispatcher's generic sentence-bundle splitter (`TriggeredAbilityParser`) tries each "`. `"-delimited sentence independently and would otherwise strand the "If you do, ..." clause from its antecedent "you may exile ..." clause.

ANCHORED (^…$) to the exact card-specific surface, so it cannot collide with any other "you may exile ... from your graveyard" sibling (none of which pair with this "create a copy token, then delayed-exile it at end of combat" follow-up). CR 701.13 (exile); CR 111.1 (token creation); CR 707.2 (copy semantics); CR 603.7 (delayed triggered abilities); CR 117.7/CR 118.12 ("you may").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/MayExileGraveyardCreatureWithLesserPowerThenCopyExileAtEndOfCombatRule.cs)

### `MayHaveThatPlayerLoseLifeYouGainRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may have that player lose N life. If you do, you gain N life." — an optional triggered drain where the controller optionally applies life-loss to the player who triggered the ability (a "that player" back-reference), and if they do, the controller gains life (Bloodchief Ascension, ZEN).

The "you may" makes the life-loss optional (CR 117.7: "if you do" clauses are optional branches). The controller chooses whether to have "that player" (CR 109.5 — the player identified by the trigger condition's filter, e.g. the opponent whose graveyard received a card) lose life. If the controller opts in, they also gain an equal amount of life.

Modelled as an `OptionalEffect` whose `Inner` is `loseLife` (player = `ThatPlayer`) and whose `IfYouDo` is `gainLife` (player = You). The "If you do" follow-up is the canonical structured `IfYouDo` slot of `OptionalEffect` (ADR 0005 — clause modifiers are composition).

Representative card: Bloodchief Ascension (ZEN) — "… you may have that player lose 2 life. If you do, you gain 2 life." Rule citations: CR 117.7 (optional effects / "if you do"), CR 119.3 (life totals), CR 109.5 ("that player").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/MayHaveThatPlayerLoseLifeYouGainRule.cs)

### `MayHaveThisCreatureDealDamageToTargetTypeDisjunctionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may have this creature deal N damage to target [type] or [type]." — the OPTIONAL self-ping family with a <b>disjunctive target</b>. Covers triggered abilities whose resolution reads "… you may have this creature deal 1 damage to target player or planeswalker" (Hissing Iguanar, Cosi's Ravager, Kyren Sniper, Exuberant Firestoker, Noggle Hedge-Mage — the disjunction differs only in the controlling trigger/intervening-if, which the parser peels before this rule sees the effect interior).

CR 118.12: "[A player] may [do something] …" — the "you may" makes the ping an optional action taken when the ability resolves, so the whole effect is wrapped in an `OptionalEffect` (the wrapper presence IS the "you may"; no bool — ADR 0005). Its `Inner` is the `DealDamageEffect`.

CR 120.1: a source deals damage to a creature, planeswalker, battle, or player; absent any "combat damage" marker the damage is non-combat (CR 120 vs CR 510), so `IsCombat` is left null. The source is "this creature" — the permanent itself (CR 109), modeled as `Self` (the same pronoun shape `ThisCreatureDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` produces). CR 115.1: "target" creates a target; the disjunction "X or Y" is one target whose legal-type set is the union {X, Y} (the same shape `ItDealsDamageToTargetTypeDisjunctionRule` produces for the mandatory "it deals … to target player or planeswalker" ETB form), so it is one `Target` with an `CardTypes` union — "player"/"opponent" listed alongside card types because CardTypes encodes both card types and the game entities that can be dealt damage (CR 120.1).

The "or" is REQUIRED (the anchored `… or …` alternation): the bare single-type forms ("… deal N damage to target creature") are a distinct family and are not matched here, so this rule never shadows them. CR 603.2: triggered abilities.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/MayHaveThisCreatureDealDamageToTargetTypeDisjunctionRule.cs)

### `MayPayTargetPlayerDrainRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may pay {COST}. If you do, target player loses N life and you gain N life." — the optional-drain conditional-pay shape (Kalastria Highborn, WWK: "Whenever this creature or another Vampire you control dies, you may pay {B}. If you do, target player loses 2 life and you gain 2 life.").

CR 118.12: a spell or ability that reads "[A player] may [do something]. If [that player] does, [effect]" treats the "do something" (here, paying {COST}) as a cost paid on resolution; the consequent runs only if the payment was made. This is the `ConditionalPayEffect` shape wrapped in an `OptionalEffect`, mirroring `ConditionalPayTriggeredRule` but with the Blood-Artist drain composite ("target player loses N life and you gain N life") as the "if you do" consequent. CR 603.1: the whole ability is a triggered ability whose effect is this composite.

The consequent is delegated to the existing anchored `TargetPlayerLoseAndYouGainLifeRule`, which emits the `CompositeEffect` of `LoseLifeEffect` (target player) + `GainLifeEffect` (you). Priority 90 (above `ConditionalPayTriggeredRule` at 80) so this specific drain shape wins cleanly; the regex is fully anchored so no other conditional-pay text matches.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/MayPayTargetPlayerDrainRule.cs)

### `MayPayUntapAttackingAndAdditionalCombatRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may pay {COST}. If you do, untap all attacking creatures and after this phase, there is an additional combat phase." — the Hellkite Charger combat-reset pattern.

Produces an `OptionalEffect` whose `Inner` is a `ConditionalPayEffect` carrying the mana cost, and whose `IfYouDo` is a `CompositeEffect` containing:

An `UntapEffect` targeting all attacking creatures (CR 701.26: untap; CR 508: attacking creatures). An `AdditionalCombatPhaseEffect` (CR 500.8: adding phases to a turn).

Pattern is anchored (^...$) to prevent matching as a substring of a more-specific sibling. Only the COST is variable; "untap all attacking creatures" and "after this phase, there is an additional combat phase" are fixed. This rule deliberately handles only this exact clause shape rather than extending the general `ConditionalPayTriggeredRule` to avoid broad combinatorial coupling.

CR references: CR 500.8 (adding a phase to a turn); CR 508.3a (attacks trigger); CR 701.26 (tap/untap); CR 117.3 (paying costs optionally).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/MayPayUntapAttackingAndAdditionalCombatRule.cs)

### `MillThenOptionalReturnFromGraveyardToHandRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"mill N cards, then you may return [type-disjunction] card from your graveyard to your hand." — the single-sentence "mill, then optionally reanimate to HAND" composite (Overlord of the Balemurk). Distinct from the reflexive "mill N cards. When you do, return target … to the BATTLEFIELD" shape (`ReflexiveMillThenReturnCreatureFromGraveyardRule`): here the two actions happen in one resolution ("…, then you may…", CR 608.2 sequencing), not as a reflexive delayed trigger (CR 603.12), and the return destination is the hand.

CR 701.17a (Mill): "For a player to mill a number of cards, that player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard." CR 118.12 ("you may …"): the optional return is wrapped in an `OptionalEffect`. The return card is an indefinite reference ("a … card", not "target") → `Any` (CR 115.1 — only "target" creates a target).

The return filter is a card-type disjunction ("a non-Avatar creature card or a planeswalker card", CR 115.3 OR semantics) with an optional "non-[subtype]" exclusion captured on `ExcludedSubtypes` and the source zone/controller on `Zone` / `Controller` ("from your graveyard").

ANCHORED (^…$): the whole "mill … then you may return … from your graveyard to your hand" sentence is anchored, so it cannot substring-match into a more specific sibling. Priority 990 places it above the broad, unanchored `ReturnToHandRule` and `MillTriggeredRule` (default priority) so the whole composite is captured in one place rather than either half being parsed in isolation (which drops the other).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/MillThenOptionalReturnFromGraveyardToHandRule.cs)

### `MillTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"mill N cards." / "mill a card." — Rule 701.17 keyword action on the triggered side. The implicit subject (controller) is encoded as Player = You. Also handles "target player mills N cards." (Constellation pattern such as Sage of Mysteries / Thassa's Devourer) where the target is encoded as Player = Target + player filter (Rule 115.1). Also handles "defending player mills half their library, rounded up/down." (Terisian Mindbreaker) where the defending player (CR 508.1b) mills a calculated half of their own library, rounded in the named direction. The `DefendingPlayer` reference already exists in the reference system; this rule composes it with a `CalculatedQuantity` using `CardsInLibrary` as the base (mirroring the Heartless Hidetsugu pattern where LifeTotal is used without a source — context is provided by the Player field of MillEffect).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/MillTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTByDieResultTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"[subject] gets +X/+0 until end of turn, where X is the result[ minus N]" — a P/T modification whose modifier is driven by the result of the die rolled earlier in the same ability (the attack-triggered die-roll family: Velukan Dragon). The X variable is resolved to the die roll's result (`DieRollResultQuantity`, CR 706.2), with an optional "minus N" arithmetic adjustment.

This is the die-result-driven sibling of `ModifyPTTriggeredRule` (which handles only literal "+N/+N" modifiers). The two are disjoint: that rule requires a numeric modifier on at least one axis, this one requires a variable X on exactly one axis with a "where X is the result" binding. Dispatched as one sentence of the "roll a die. [subject] gets +X/+0 ..." bundle (CR 706.4 — the text indicates how to use the roll result).

CR 706.2: "the final number is the result of the die roll." The "result minus N" form is modeled as a `CalculatedQuantity` over the `DieRollResultQuantity` base with Operation "add" and a negative `Operand` (X + (-N)), reusing the established additive-offset shape rather than introducing a new operation. The subject ("this creature" / "it") is the triggering creature; "that creature" (the equipped/affected creature) is also accepted.

ANCHORED (`^…$`) so it cannot match inside a longer sibling sentence. Priority 70: above the literal-modifier `ModifyPTTriggeredRule` (default 50) so the die-result form is preferred when both could superficially apply.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ModifyPTByDieResultTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ModifyPTTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it gets +N/+N until end of turn" — triggered P/T modification on the creature that fired the trigger (Rule 508 attack trigger pattern). The subject "it" refers to the attacking or otherwise-triggering creature and maps to `It`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ModifyPTTriggeredRule.cs)

### `MutatesConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever this creature mutates" — mutate trigger (Rule 702.140). Fires each time the creature successfully mutates. The Filter captures the subject ("this creature") as a creature-type filter.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/MutatesConditionRule.cs)

### `NamedSourceDealsDamageEqualToExcessToAnyTargetRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"[CardName] deals damage equal to the excess to any target [other than that permanent]." — named-source ping where the damage amount equals the excess from an `ExcessNoncombatDamageDealt` trigger (KHM: Toralf, God of Fury). The subject starts with a capital letter (a card name, CR 201.4: a card's name in its own text refers to itself). MAST resolves the self-reference to `Self`.

The amount "equal to the excess" is modelled as `DerivedQuantity { DerivedFrom = DerivedKind.DamageDealt }`: the triggering event's excess is the distinct quantum of damage dealt beyond lethal (CR 120.10 — "excess damage equal to the difference"). `DamageDealt` is the canonical derived-quantity axis for damage dealt in a triggering event, reused here for excess damage since there is no separate `ExcessDamage` kind.

The trailing "other than that permanent" exclusion is dropped: no `ObjectReferenceKind` carries a "ThatPermanent" exclusion; the engine resolves the targeting constraint via the existing AnyTarget + CR 115.7 legality. This matches the precedent in PawpatchRecruit ("target creature you control other than that creature" → unfiltered creature target).

Anchored (^…$) to prevent matching inside a broader clause. Priority 61 — just above `NamedSourceDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` (Priority 60) so the "equal to the excess" shape is claimed before the literal-amount form attempts to parse the non-numeric "equal to the excess" amount.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/NamedSourceDealsDamageEqualToExcessToAnyTargetRule.cs)

### `NamedSourceDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"[CardName] deals N damage to any target." — named-source self-ping triggered effect. Covers cards whose triggered ability effect reads "[CardName] deals N damage to any target." where the card refers to itself by its own printed name (Rule 201.4 — a card's name refers to itself when used in its own text). MAST resolves the self-reference to `Self`. Rule 120.1-120.2: dealing damage (a source deals damage to a permanent/player). Rule 115.4: "any target" — a target may be any player, creature, planeswalker, or battle unless otherwise restricted. Distinct from `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` (which handles the pronoun "it deals N damage" shape — same event, different oracle phrasing). Both map to Source=Self; the difference is naming convention only.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/NamedSourceDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule.cs)

### `NamedSourceDealsDamageToThatPlayerTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"[CardName] deals N damage to that player." — named-source self-ping effect directed at the trigger's named player. Covers triggered abilities whose effect reads "[CardName] deals N damage to that player." where the card refers to itself by its own printed name (CR 201.5 — a card's name in its own text refers to itself). MAST resolves the self-reference to `Self`. "That player" back-references whichever player caused the trigger to fire (CR 603.2: the event-match player).

CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players." CR 603.1: "Triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect."

Anchored (^…$) to prevent substring matches. Priority 62 — just above `NamedSourceDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` (Priority 60) so the more-specific "that player" target is claimed before the "any target" form. Distinct from `SelfDealsDamageToThatPlayerRule`, which handles the pronoun form "this creature/it deals N damage to that player/them".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/NamedSourceDealsDamageToThatPlayerTriggeredRule.cs)

### `NoCombatDamageThisCombatRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"This creature assigns no combat damage this combat." — the source creature is excluded from assigning combat damage for the remainder of the current combat.

Rule 510.1: "Each attacking creature and each blocking creature assigns combat damage." This effect records the explicit oracle override preventing the named creature from assigning any combat damage in the current combat phase. Descriptive only; the zero-damage assignment is engine territory.

Canonical use: Master of Cruelties — the triggered ability that sets an attacked player's life total to 1 also prevents the creature from dealing combat damage, so the combined effect is: reduce to 1 life without also dealing the 1/4 base damage. Oracle text: "This creature assigns no combat damage this combat."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/NoCombatDamageThisCombatRule.cs)

### `NontokenCreatureToGraveyardFromBattlefieldConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Trigger condition: "a nontoken creature is put into your graveyard from the battlefield."

This is the long-form "dies" trigger (CR 700.4: "a creature, planeswalker, or battle is put into a graveyard from the battlefield") qualified with two restrictions:

<b>nontoken</b> — the creature is not a token (CR 111.1: a token is not a card; the `IsToken = false` axis on `ObjectFilter` encodes this). <b>your graveyard</b> — the creature entered a graveyard you own (`Controller = You` on the filter).

Maps to `Dies` because "put into your graveyard from the battlefield" is definitionally the Dies event (CR 700.4), with the controller constraint naming whose graveyard receives it. The nontoken qualifier is the standard creature-token distinction used throughout the corpus (CR 111.1).

Canonical card: Nim Deathmantle (SOM) — "Whenever a nontoken creature is put into your graveyard from the battlefield, you may pay {4}. If you do, return that card to the battlefield and attach this Equipment to it."

CR 700.4 (verbatim): "The word 'dies' means 'is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.'" CR 111.1 (tokens are not cards).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/NontokenCreatureToGraveyardFromBattlefieldConditionRule.cs)

### `OneOrMoreCreaturesDealCombatDamageToPlayerConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever one or more creatures you control deal combat damage to a player" — the aggregate combat-damage payoff family (Rapacious Guest, Professional Face-Breaker, Excogitator Sphinx, Vincent, Vengeful Atoner, and many other cards sharing this exact subject phrase with varying payoffs). The plural "one or more creatures" subject takes the plural verb "deal" (not "deals"), so `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule`'s "deals combat damage" guard never matches this shape — this is a dedicated sibling rule, not an extension of the shared file, so it cannot collide with that rule's singular-subject forms (CardName/this creature/a creature you control with [keyword]).

Emits `DealsCombatDamageToPlayer` with a generic creature-you-control filter (no subtype restriction, unlike `OneOrMoreSubtypeDealsDamageToOpponentsConditionRule`'s named-subtype shape) and `MinimumCount` = 1, mirroring the "one or more Foods" quantity qualifier already used for `Sacrifices` (Camellia, the Seedmiser).

ANCHORED (^…$) against the full trigger clause (after the timing-word strip) so this rule matches ONLY the exact "…to a player" recipient form — the sibling "…to one or more players" (Forth Eorlingas!, The Destined Thief) and "…to a player this turn" (Jace, Cunning Castaway) surfaces deliberately fall through unmatched rather than being coerced into this shape.

Rule 510.1 (Combat Damage Step); Rule 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/OneOrMoreCreaturesDealCombatDamageToPlayerConditionRule.cs)

### `OneOrMoreSubtypeDealsDamageToOpponentsConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever one or more [Subtype] you control deal damage to your opponents" — the group-damage-to-multiple-opponents trigger condition (Malcolm, Keen-Eyed Navigator pattern).

Emits `DealsDamageToOpponents` (plural). The Filter carries the creature subtype and controller (You). Distinct from `DealsDamageToOpponentConditionRule` (singular "an opponent" / single source) and `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule` (combat damage only).

Rule 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. This is generally detrimental to the object or player that receives that damage." Rule 102.2: an opponent is any player not on the same team as the controller. Rule 603.2: triggered abilities fire automatically on matching game events.

ANCHORED (^…$): matched against the full trigger clause (after timing-word strip) to prevent misfiring on broader trigger phrases that include this as a substring. Priority 987: above `DealsDamageToOpponentConditionRule` (986) so the more specific "your opponents" (plural) shape is tried before the singular form.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/OneOrMoreSubtypeDealsDamageToOpponentsConditionRule.cs)

### `OpenAttractionTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"open an Attraction." — keyword action (Rule 701.51) on the triggered side. Matches the bare keyword action when it is the entire effect body of a triggered ability (e.g. Seasoned Buttoneer's ETB trigger). The trailing parenthetical reminder is stripped by the dispatcher before this rule runs (Rule 207.2). CR 701.51b: "To open an Attraction, move the top card of your Attraction deck off the Attraction deck, turn it face up, and put it onto the battlefield under your control." CR 603.6a: Enters-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield. These are written, "When [this object] enters, . . ." Emits the `OpenAttractionEffect` node.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/OpenAttractionTriggeredRule.cs)

### `OpponentCastsSpellWithChosenNameConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever an opponent casts a spell with the chosen name" (Silverquill Silencer) — the trigger-condition consumer half of a CR 614.12 named-card binder, paired with a "choose a [nonland] card name" declaration elsewhere on the card (`ChooseCardNameEffect`). The chosen-name restriction is modeled as `ChosenCharacteristic` = `CardName` on the trigger's spell filter (the structured consumer side of the CR 607 linked ability), mirroring `CounterTargetSpellWithChosenNameActivatedEffectRule`'s activation-cost analogue for the same binder shape.

Anchored end-to-end so it is disjoint from the generic `SpellCastConditionRule` (which has no "with the chosen name" handling and would otherwise silently drop the chosen-name filter). Priority 999 — one above `SpellCastConditionRule` (998) so this more specific shape is tried first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/OpponentCastsSpellWithChosenNameConditionRule.cs)

### `OpponentDrawsCardConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever an opponent draws a card" — draw-card trigger scoped to an opponent (CR 121.1: "A player draws a card by putting the top card of their library into their hand"; CR 603.2: the event-match fires the ability whenever any opponent performs that action). The Filter Controller = Opponent narrows the trigger to draws performed by an opponent rather than the controller.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/OpponentDrawsCardConditionRule.cs)

### `OptionalMillTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may mill N cards." — the optional variant of the CR 701.17a mill keyword action on the triggered side (Daggerfang Duo's ETB, CR 603.6a).

The "you may" is a structured `OptionalEffect` (the codebase's convention, matching `ExileThenReturnFlickerTriggeredRule`) rather than a boolean flag: wrapper presence alone encodes the optionality. Mill is a one-shot action effect, so it composes directly under the wrapper with no further decomposition.

Anchored (^you may mill … cards$) so it never collides with `MillTriggeredRule`'s `^mill …$` pattern (which has no "you may" prefix) — the two patterns are mutually exclusive by construction, so rule priority is irrelevant.

CR 701.17a (Mill): "For a player to mill a number of cards, that player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/OptionalMillTriggeredRule.cs)

### `OtherSubtypePumpTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"other [Subtype] you control get +N/+M until end of turn." — the single-subtype tribal pump that appears as the RESOLUTION EFFECT of a triggered ability, e.g. Perimeter Sergeant's "Whenever this creature attacks, other Humans you control get +1/+0 until end of turn."

The leading "other" is the self-exclusion qualifier ("another" / CR 109.5): the source creature is omitted from the pumped set, recorded as `ExcludeSelf` = true. The subtype noun ("Humans") names a creature subtype (CR 205.3m); it lands on `Subtypes` in its singular oracle-canonical form ("Human"), alongside `CardTypes = ["creature"]` — the same shape the static "Other [Subtype] creatures you control get +N/+M" lord buff (LordPTBuffRule) produces for the isOther case.

The timing (Whenever this creature attacks) and the effect (other Humans get +1/+0 until end of turn) are separate composable nodes (CR 603.1): this rule recognises only the effect half, which `TriggeredAbilityParser` pairs with the already-parsing trigger. The boost is a layer-7c continuous P/T modification (CR 613.4c), so it is a `ModifyPTEffect` with literal +N/+M modifiers and `Duration` = `untilTime{Turn, End}`.

New, collision-free file. The pattern is anchored (`^…$`) and requires the subtype token to be capitalised, so it never steals the lowercase generic-noun mass shapes ("other creatures you control …", handled elsewhere). It requires a SINGLE subtype word immediately followed by "you control", so it does not overlap the comma/"and"-joined multi-subtype list handled by `SubtypeListPumpTriggeredRule`, nor the bare "creatures you control" shape handled by `EtbTeamPumpTriggeredRule` and `MassModifyPTTriggeredRule`. It also requires "get" (plural), so it is disjoint from the singular-subject "it/this creature/target creature gets" shape handled by `ModifyPTTriggeredRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/OtherSubtypePumpTriggeredRule.cs)

### `PhaseTriggerConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"At the beginning of your upkeep" / "...first main phase" / "...draw step" / "...end step" / "...combat on your turn". Maps the phase/step word to a `TriggerEvent`. The "your" / "each opponent's" possessive lands on the filter as a `Controller`. Only fires for At-timing triggers.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/PhaseTriggerConditionRule.cs)

### `ProliferateTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"proliferate." — Rule 701.27 keyword action on the triggered side. Matches the bare proliferate instruction that appears after the trigger comma (reminder text has already been stripped by the time this rule is called).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ProliferateTriggeredRule.cs)

### `PutCounterOnItAndDrawCardRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"put a +1/+1 counter on it and draw a card" — the ETB trigger effect on The Great Henge family. The entering creature (the subject of the enters trigger) receives one +1/+1 counter, and the ability's controller draws one card. Both effects resolve simultaneously as a `CompositeEffect`.

CR 603.6a: "Enters-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield." The "it" pronoun back-references the permanent that just entered — the trigger's subject — encoded as `It` following the existing PutCountersTriggeredRule convention for pronoun antecedents (Rule 109.2).

CR 121.1: Drawing a card is "putting the top card of that player's library into their hand." The draw targets `You` — the ability's controller — which is the canonical reference for "draw a card" without an explicit subject.

The rule is fully anchored (^…$) so it cannot match as a substring inside a more-specific sibling's text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/PutCounterOnItAndDrawCardRule.cs)

### `PutCountersTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"put a +1/+1 counter on this creature" / "put a -1/-1 counter on target creature" / "that player gets N [type] counters" (poison/energy/etc. given to a player on combat damage — Fynn, the Fangbearer; Blighted Agent; etc.).

CR 122.1: "A counter is a marker placed on an object or player that modifies its characteristics and/or interacts with a rule or effect." Poison counters are placed on players; the "gets" verb in oracle text means the player receives those counters. Distinct from "put a counter on [permanent]" only in subject (player vs. permanent) and verb ("gets" vs. "put … on"). MAST models both as `putCounters` effect — the counter placement is the same action regardless of verb.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/PutCountersTriggeredRule.cs)

### `PutFromHandOntoBattlefieldTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may put a[n] &lt;filter&gt; card from your hand onto the battlefield tapped and attacking that opponent"

Handles the Kaalia of the Vast pattern: an optional zone-change from hand to battlefield where the card enters tapped and attacking the opponent named by the enclosing trigger. The "you may" wrapper is materialised as `OptionalEffect` around the inner `PutFromHandOntoBattlefieldEffect`.

Rule citations:

CR 508.1b — "attacks an opponent" trigger; the card enters attacking that same opponent. CR 400.7 — zone change creates a new object. CR 110.5b — permanent enters tapped. CR 603.1 — triggered ability trigger + effect.

Priority 63 — above the generic battlefield-search rules and sibling hand-to-play rules so the "from your hand onto the battlefield" form is matched before any library-search fallback. The pattern is fully anchored (^...$) so it cannot match as a substring of a more-complex sibling effect.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/PutFromHandOntoBattlefieldTriggeredRule.cs)

### `PutIntoGraveyardConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Recognises the "one or more [type] cards are put into your graveyard from anywhere" trigger condition (Rule 603 — Handling Triggered Abilities; Rule 404 — Graveyard, the destination zone; "put into a graveyard" is a zone change, not a keyword action). Maps to `PutIntoGraveyard` with a filter that captures the card type and the controller whose graveyard is the destination.

The "one or more" qualifier is a threshold condition on the trigger event: the ability fires once per batch-triggering event, regardless of whether one or many qualifying cards entered the graveyard simultaneously. MAST records this descriptively (the filter names the type; the threshold semantics are engine territory).

"from anywhere" omits a source-zone restriction; the filter carries only the destination (owner's graveyard). A future zone-of-origin axis on the filter could refine this when needed, but the current corpus does not require it.

Representative cards: The Gitrog Monster (SOI) — "Whenever one or more land cards are put into your graveyard from anywhere, draw a card." Rule citations: CR 603 (Triggered Abilities), CR 404 (Graveyard — the destination zone).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/PutIntoGraveyardConditionRule.cs)

### `PutNegativeCountersOnCreatureConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"you put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature" — counter-placement trigger (Nest of Scarabs).

CR 122.1: "A counter is a marker placed on an object or player that modifies its characteristics and/or interacts with a rule or effect." This trigger fires whenever the controller places one or more -1/-1 counters on any creature. The filter carries the target card type (creature) and the controller (You) so the interaction layer knows whose action triggered. The counter type is encoded in a companion `CounterType` field on the `TriggerCondition` Filter-as-written (the creature being the object that receives the counters).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/PutNegativeCountersOnCreatureConditionRule.cs)

### `PutPermanentCardByManaValueFromHandRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may put a permanent card with equal or lesser mana value from your hand onto the battlefield"

Handles the Kodama of the East Tree pattern: an optional zone-change from hand to battlefield for a permanent card whose mana value is less than or equal to the mana value of a referenced object (typically the permanent that triggered the enclosing triggered ability — represented as `It`).

The "equal or lesser mana value" phrase is a relative comparison (CR 202.3 — mana value is the sum of the mana symbols in a card's mana cost) against the triggering permanent's mana value, encoded as a `Comparison` with `RelativeTo` set to `It` and `RelativeCharacteristic` set to `ManaValue`.

Rule citations:

CR 202.3 — mana value (formerly converted mana cost) is the sum of mana symbols. CR 400.7 — zone change creates a new object. CR 603.1 — triggered ability trigger + effect.

Priority 64 — above `PutFromHandOntoBattlefieldTriggeredRule` (priority 63) so this more-specific mana-value-comparison form is matched first. Fully anchored (^...$) to prevent substring matches against sibling effects.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/PutPermanentCardByManaValueFromHandRule.cs)

### `PutPlusCountersOnThisCreatureConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"one or more +1/+1 counters are put on this creature" — passive counter-placement trigger on the source creature itself (Scurry Oak, Spike Feeder variants).

CR 122.1: "A counter is a marker placed on an object or player that modifies its characteristics and/or interacts with a rule or effect." This trigger fires whenever one or more +1/+1 counters are placed on the ability's source creature (passive voice: "are put on this creature"). The filter carries `IsSelf = true` to record that the recipient is the source permanent, not an arbitrary creature, so the interaction layer can distinguish "counters placed on this specific permanent" from "counters placed on any creature". The counter type is encoded in `CounterType` and the minimum quantity in `MinimumCount`.

Rule 603.2: each event matching the trigger condition fires the ability; "one or more" constrains the per-event count to at least 1 (MinimumCount = 1). The event fires on any +1/+1 counter placement — by the controller or any other source — as long as the recipient is this creature.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/PutPlusCountersOnThisCreatureConditionRule.cs)

### `PutThatManyPlusOneCountersGainsLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"put that many +1/+1 counters on this creature" — counter-placement effect where the count is derived from life just GAINED by the triggering player. Backs the `GainsLife` trigger on Sunbond: "Enchanted creature has &quot;Whenever you gain life, put that many +1/+1 counters on this creature.&quot;"

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." CR 122.1: "A counter is a marker placed on an object or player that modifies its characteristics and/or interacts with a rule or effect." The antecedent of "that many" is the amount of life just gained in the triggering event, keyed on `LifeGained` — the same derived-quantity axis used by `LoseLifeDerivedRule` for the sibling "loses that much life" surface (Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose).

"This creature" resolves to `Self` — the object bearing the ability (CR 109.5), which becomes the enchanted creature once the ability is granted by the Aura (CR 113.6: an ability granted to an object by an effect is a fully-fledged ability of that object). Mirrors the plain "on this creature" → Self mapping used by `PutCountersTriggeredRule`, but with a DERIVED count instead of a literal one.

This rule is NOT reflection-discovered into the generic effect loop (no `[TriggeredRule]` attribute); `TriggeredAbilityParser` dispatches to it directly only when the resolved trigger event is `GainsLife` — mirroring `DrawThatManyCardsLifeLostRule`'s LosesLife-guarded wiring — so the "put that many … counters" surface is never resolved against this LifeGained antecedent under a DIFFERENT trigger event (e.g. a hypothetical damage- or counter-placement-triggered card sharing the same effect-text idiom with a different antecedent).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/PutThatManyPlusOneCountersGainsLifeRule.cs)

### `ReflexiveMillThenReturnCreatureFromGraveyardRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"When you do, return target [filter] card [with mana value N or less/greater/…] from your graveyard to the battlefield." — the reflexive tail of the "mill N cards. When you do, reanimate …" family (Yathan Roadwatcher).

The preceding sentence ("mill four cards") parses to a `MillEffect` via `MillTriggeredRule`; the sentence-bundle dispatcher in `TriggeredAbilityParser` feeds this rule the following "When you do, …" sentence, which is a <b>reflexive triggered ability</b> (CR 603.12) created when the ETB ability resolves — a separate object, not an inline effect. Modelled as a `CreateDelayedTriggerEffect` wrapping a `DelayedTriggeredAbility` whose trigger is "when you mill" (`Mills`, Controller = You), mirroring the fetchland reflexive shape (`ReflexiveSacrificeSearchBasicLandGainLifeRule`, which bakes `Sacrifices`).

CR 603.12 (verbatim): "A resolving spell or ability may allow or instruct a player to take an action and create a triggered ability that triggers 'when [a player] [does or doesn't]' take that action or 'when [something happens] this way.' These reflexive triggered abilities follow the rules for delayed triggered abilities (see rule 603.7) …"

CR 603.7 (verbatim): "An effect may create a delayed triggered ability that can do something at a later time. A delayed triggered ability will contain 'when,' 'whenever,' or 'at,' although that word won't usually begin the ability." CR 701.17a (Mill): "For a player to mill a number of cards, that player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard."

ANCHORED (^…$): the whole "when you do, return … battlefield" sentence is anchored, so it cannot substring-match into a more specific sibling. The reanimation interior is delegated to `ReturnGraveyardToBattlefieldRule` (the same node the spell parser builds for the identical surface), so the optional mana-value qualifier and filter-type variants are handled in one place.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReflexiveMillThenReturnCreatureFromGraveyardRule.cs)

### `ReflexiveSacrificeSearchBasicLandGainLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"When you do, search your library for a basic &lt;subtypes&gt; card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle[ and you gain &lt;N&gt; life]."

The reflexive tail of a fetchland-style ETB (the Obscura Storefront / SNC "surveil dual" fetch family): "When this land enters, sacrifice it. When you do, search your library for a basic Plains, Island, or Swamp card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle and you gain 1 life." The "sacrifice it" sentence parses via `SacrificeTriggeredRule`; this rule handles the following "When you do, …" sentence, which is a <b>reflexive triggered ability</b> (CR 603.12) created when the ETB ability resolves — a separate object, not an inline effect and not a second printed ability. Modelled as a `CreateDelayedTriggerEffect` wrapping a `DelayedTriggeredAbility` whose trigger is "when you sacrifice this land" (`Sacrifices`, `IsSelf`).

CR 603.12 (verbatim): "A resolving spell or ability may allow or instruct a player to take an action and create a triggered ability that triggers 'when [a player] [does or doesn't]' take that action or 'when [something happens] this way.' These reflexive triggered abilities follow the rules for delayed triggered abilities (see rule 603.7), except that they're checked immediately after being created and trigger based on whether the trigger event or events occurred earlier during the resolution of the spell or ability that created them." Obscura Storefront is structurally identical to the rule's Heart-Piercer Manticore example, save that the sacrifice here is mandatory ("sacrifice it") rather than "you may sacrifice" — so the reflexive trigger always fires, but it is still a separate delayed/reflexive ability object, hence `CreateDelayedTriggerEffect`.

CR 603.7 (verbatim): "An effect may create a delayed triggered ability that can do something at a later time. A delayed triggered ability will contain 'when,' 'whenever,' or 'at,' although that word won't usually begin the ability."

CR 701.23a (Search): "To search for a card in a zone, look at all cards in that zone (even if it's a hidden zone) and find a card that matches the given description." CR 119.3 (gain life): "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."

ANCHORED (^…$): fully anchored on the whole "When you do, search …" sentence, so it cannot substring-match into a more specific sibling. The search is NOT wrapped in optional — it is a mandatory instruction (contrast Solemn Simulacrum's "you may search"). The optional "and you gain N life" tail adds a `GainLifeEffect` only when present, so subtype/life variants across the fetch cycle reuse this one rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReflexiveSacrificeSearchBasicLandGainLifeRule.cs)

### `RemoveCounterTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"remove a +1/+1 counter from it" / "remove a charge counter from it" / "remove a -1/-1 counter from this creature" as a triggered effect. Covers counter-removal as the primary triggered action, e.g.: "At the beginning of your upkeep, remove a -1/-1 counter from Aboroth." "At end of combat, remove a +1/+1 counter from it." "At the beginning of your upkeep, remove a charge counter from this artifact." Counter type resolution mirrors `PutCountersTriggeredRule`: "+1/+1" and "-1/-1" are matched directly; all other types are captured from the "a(n) &lt;type&gt; counter" pattern (Rule 122.1 — named counters). Target resolution order: 1. "from it" → ObjectReference.It() 2. "from this creature/permanent/artifact/enchantment" → ObjectReference.Self() 3. Named self-reference fallback (card name in text) → ObjectReference.Self()

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/RemoveCounterTriggeredRule.cs)

### `RemoveCountersTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"remove a +1/+1 counter from it at end of combat" — Phantom-creature counter-removal pattern (Judgment set). Fires as the resolution effect of an attacks-or-blocks triggered ability; "it" is the pronoun for the creature that declared as an attacker or blocker.

Rule 122.3: removing a counter from a permanent means taking one counter of the specified type off that permanent. Rule 511: the end of combat step is the last step of the combat phase; delayed removal effects scheduled "at end of combat" resolve here.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/RemoveCountersTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnAllFromGraveyardToBattlefieldTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return all [type] cards from your graveyard to the battlefield [tapped]." Mass-recursion pattern as a triggered-ability effect — e.g. the second clause of Lumra, Bellow of the Woods's ETB: "Then return all land cards from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped." Parallel to `ReturnAllFromGraveyardToBattlefieldRule` (the same semantic pattern on the activated-ability side); split into a separate file because `ITriggeredRule` and `IActivatedEffectRule` are distinct interfaces. Handles an optional leading "Then " prefix (produced by the sentence-bundle splitter in `TriggeredAbilityParser` when the return clause follows another sentence, e.g. "mill four cards. Then return all land cards …"). CR 701 (zone change); CR 400.1 (zones); the optional "tapped" entering status is CR 110.5b. Fully anchored (^…$) to prevent substring collision with single-target return rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnAllFromGraveyardToBattlefieldTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnEnchantedOnDeathTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return that card to the battlefield under your control" — the Animate Dead / Unhallowed Pact pattern. This effect appears as the resolution clause of a "When enchanted creature dies" trigger on Auras that reanimate their host. "That card" is a pronoun back-reference (Rule 113.8b) to the enchanted creature that just moved from the battlefield to the graveyard. MAST models it as `It` — the generic anaphoric reference kind ("it", "that card", "the creature" all denote the same game object). The "under your control" clause is captured in `UnderControl = You` on the `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect`. Rule 400.6: an object that returns to the battlefield under a specific player's control enters under that player's control as a replacement on zone-change resolution. Variant: "return it to its owner's hand" is handled by `ReturnSelfToHandOnDeathTriggeredRule` — the effect text is identical regardless of whether the trigger subject is "this Aura" or "enchanted creature", so no separate rule is needed for the hand-return variant. Rule 303.4 (Aura attachment); Rule 700.4 ("dies"); Rule 400.6 (enters under control).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnEnchantedOnDeathTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnEnchantmentFromGraveyardOrUnlockDoorRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return an enchantment card from your graveyard to your hand or unlock a locked door of a Room you control" — a one-of-two modal choice between returning an enchantment from the graveyard and unlocking a door of a Room you control.

This is the ETB modal effect on Ghostly Dancers. "X or Y" is a controller's choice at resolution — Rule 700.2 (modal). Modelled as a `ModalEffect` with `ChooseOne` whose two modes each wrap one effect in a `SpellAbility`: Mode 1: `ReturnToHandEffect` — an enchantment card in the controller's graveyard, non-targeted ("an enchantment card", indefinite article, no "target" keyword — CR 115.1 / 601.2c: the "target" keyword creates a target; without it the controller simply picks an object that matches at resolution); Mode 2: `UnlockDoorEffect` — a locked half of a Room the controller controls (CR 709.5e–f: unlock half of a permanent with a shared type line).

The return is Zone = Graveyard, Controller = You (CR 701.9). The unlock is Subtypes = ["Room"], Controller = You (CR 709.5e, 709.5j).

Must be tried at higher priority than the generic `ReturnToHandRule` to prevent the return-only half from being matched and discarding the modal shape.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnEnchantmentFromGraveyardOrUnlockDoorRule.cs)

### `ReturnExiledCardAtNextEndStepTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control at the beginning of the next end step." — the delayed-return resolution sentence of a blink that returns NEXT end step (Flickerwisp).

Unlike an immediate blink (exile + return now, the `ExileThenReturnFlickerTriggeredRule` shape), this clause sets up a <i>delayed</i> triggered ability (CR 603.7): "at the beginning of the next end step" is the firing point of an ability created when the ETB ability resolves, not a duration on the return effect itself (ADR 0002/0004). The return therefore lives INSIDE a `CreateDelayedTriggerEffect` whose `DelayedTriggeredAbility` fires "At" the `End` step's `Beginning`, when `Next` — the exact GameTime the sibling `SacrificeAtEndStepTriggeredRule` uses.

"that card" is the just-exiled card from the preceding sentence — NOT free text. It is the linked exiled reference (CR 607.2, the Petravark / Felidar precedent), modelled via `ExiledWith` as a `Designated` card in the `Exile` zone exiled with this object (`ExiledWith = {Kind: Self}`) — a reference, not a threaded runtime binding (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution). "under its owner's control" rides on `UnderControl` as an `Owner` reference (CR 400.6).

Rule citations: 603.7 (delayed triggers), 513 (End Step), 607.2 (linked exile), 701.13 (exile) / 400.6 (control on return).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnExiledCardAtNextEndStepTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnExiledCardOnLeaveTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return the exiled card to the battlefield under its owner's control." — the LTB resolution clause of a CR 607.2 linked pair (Petravark): the card a prior linked exile ability put in exile is returned to the battlefield. "the exiled card" is NOT free text — it is a linked reference (CR 607.2). The returned object is identified by the `ExiledWith` reference (the same axis Azula's play-from-exile permission uses): a `Designated` card in the `Exile` zone exiled with this object (`ExiledWith = {Kind: Self}`). This is a reference, not a threaded runtime binding (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution); the ETB exile ability and this LTB return ability are two separate triggered abilities, linked by CR 607.2. "under its owner's control" rides on `UnderControl` as an `Owner` reference (CR 400.6 — an object returning under a specific player's control enters under that control).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnExiledCardOnLeaveTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnInstantOrSorceryFromGraveyardRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return target instant or sorcery card from your graveyard to your hand" Models the Izzet Chronarch / Archaeomancer family (Rule 701.9: Return). The oracle text always targets a card by type-disjunction ("instant or sorcery") in the controller's graveyard and moves it to the controller's hand. Zone = Graveyard encodes the source zone stated in oracle text; Controller = You encodes "your graveyard". CardTypes = ["instant", "sorcery"] encodes the disjunction (Rule 700.4). Priorities above the generic ReturnToHandRule (default 50) because this rule is more specific (graveyard source + type-disjunction shape).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnInstantOrSorceryFromGraveyardRule.cs)

### `ReturnItToBattlefieldWithCounterRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return it to the battlefield under its owner's control with a [type] counter on it" — the Luminous Broodmoth / Persist / Undying-style counter-on-return shape where the return and the counter placement are written as a single clause (CR 400.6 / CR 122.1).

This complements `ReturnSelfToBattlefieldUnderOwnerControlRule` (bare "return it … under its owner's control", no counter suffix). Priority is higher (71) so the more specific counter-bearing form is tried before the bare form.

The counter is encoded on `WithCounters` — the same field used by the Undying/Persist keyword expansions (UndyingKeyword, PersistKeyword) — so the interaction layer treats it identically. Counter type is lowercased to match the `CounterType` convention ("flying", "+1/+1", "-1/-1", "time", etc.).

CR 400.6 (enters under owner's control); CR 113.8b ("it" = the triggering object); CR 122.1 (counters); CR 702.9a (flying counter).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnItToBattlefieldWithCounterRule.cs)

### `ReturnSelfFromGraveyardAttachedToThatCreatureRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"(you may) return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield attached to that creature" — the recursion-clause of the Dragon-Aura cycle (Dragon Fangs / Dragon Scales / Dragon Breath / Dragon Wings / Dragon Shadow). This Aura, sitting in its owner's graveyard, returns itself to the battlefield and re-attaches to the big creature that just entered (the antecedent of "that creature" is the trigger's own entering creature, CR 603.2).

Produces a `CompositeEffect` of two atomic effects sharing one resolution sequence:

`ReturnToBattlefieldEffect` — the Aura returns itself (`Self`) FROM the graveyard (`Zone = Graveyard`, `Controller = You`). This is a reanimation-style return (CR 603.2 / CR 614): a graveyard self-return, NOT an exile-blink, so the filter deliberately carries NO `ExiledWith` marker (that marker is reserved for CR 406.6 linked-exile returns — see Cloudshift). `AttachEffect` — attaches this Aura to "it" (`It`), the creature that just entered and triggered the ability. CR 701.3 (Attach); CR 303.4 (Aura attachment).
