The leading "you may" is optional (CR 117.7): when present, the composite is wrapped in an `OptionalEffect`. The whole text is end-anchored and gated on the distinctive "from your graveyard to the battlefield attached to that creature" phrase, so it is narrow to this Aura-return family.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnSelfFromGraveyardAttachedToThatCreatureRule.cs)

### `ReturnSelfFromGraveyardToBattlefieldRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield" — graveyard self-reanimation as a triggered effect (Forsaken Miner, CR 700.13 / CR 603).

The source zone "your graveyard" is encoded on the Target's ObjectFilter.Zone axis (`Graveyard`) and Controller axis (`You`). The card re-enters the battlefield NOT tapped (no "tapped" qualifier); Tapped = false.

This is the un-tapped counterpart to the activated-ability rule `ReturnSelfFromGraveyardToBattlefieldEffectRule` (which handles the tapped form). The regex is fully anchored (^…$) so it cannot match inside a longer effect clause.

CR 113.6 example (Reassembling Skeleton): an ability on a card in the graveyard that returns the card to the battlefield functions from that zone. This rule models the equivalent triggered-effect form.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnSelfFromGraveyardToBattlefieldRule.cs)

### `ReturnSelfFromGraveyardTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may return this card from your graveyard to your hand" — graveyard-based self-retrieval triggered from the graveyard zone (Rule 603.6a: a triggered ability on a card in a graveyard functions from that zone). The Eidolon family (Dissension) is the canonical corpus for this pattern. The source zone (Graveyard) is encoded on the Target filter's Zone axis rather than on the ability itself — MAST describes what the oracle text says, not where the object resides at runtime (Rule 400 series). Example corpus patterns: "you may return this card from your graveyard to your hand"

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnSelfFromGraveyardTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnSelfToBattlefieldUnderOwnerControlRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return it to the battlefield under its owner's control" — the Enduring Tenacity / Glimmer-creature dies-and-returns pattern. The returning permanent is described by the pronoun "it" (back-reference to the triggering object, CR 113.8b — "it" in an ability always refers to the object the trigger is about), and it re-enters under its owner's control.

"under its owner's control" rides on `UnderControl` as an `Owner` reference (CR 400.6 — an object that returns to the battlefield under a specific player's control enters under that player's control). The target is `It` (the triggering object), matching the Persist / Undying / Animate Dead family of return effects.

Distinct from `ReturnEnchantedOnDeathTriggeredRule` ("return that card to the battlefield under your control" — Aura reanimation where the controller gains control) and `ReturnExiledCardOnLeaveTriggeredRule` ("return the exiled card to the battlefield under its owner's control" — exile–return pairs). This rule handles the bare "return it … under its owner's control" form used for non-keyword self-return triggers.

CR 400.6 (enters under owner's control); CR 113.8b ("it" refers to the trigger subject).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnSelfToBattlefieldUnderOwnerControlRule.cs)

### `ReturnSelfToHandOnDeathTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return it to its owner's hand" — self-referential bounce that appears on Aura (and occasionally other) cards whose death trigger returns themselves to hand. The pronoun "it" back-references the triggering object named in the trigger condition ("this Aura", "this artifact", etc.). There is no formal target (Rule 115.1 — "target" keyword absent); the card simply moves zone-change without targeting. Example corpus patterns: "return it to its owner's hand"

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnSelfToHandOnDeathTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnTargetCardWithManaValueFromGraveyardToBattlefieldTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return target [filter] card with mana value N or less/greater[/exactly N] from your graveyard to the battlefield [tapped]" — a single-target, filtered reanimation triggered effect whose filter carries a printed mana-value bound (Driver of the Dead: "When this creature dies, return target creature card with mana value 2 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield."). The mana-value-bounded sibling of `ReturnTargetFromGraveyardToBattlefieldTriggeredRule`: that rule requires "[filter] card from" with no interposed clause, so it cannot match this "[filter] card WITH mana value …" shape, and this rule requires the "with mana value …" clause, so it cannot match the plain sibling — the two are mutually exclusive and both fully anchored (^…$). The mana-value bound lands on `ManaValueComparison` (the existing structured axis; mirrors Kami of Empty Graves' return-to-hand gold), so no new discriminator is introduced — the effect reuses `ReturnToBattlefieldEffect`. CR 400.7 (an object that moves from one zone to another becomes a new object); CR 404.1 (a player's graveyard is their discard pile); CR 115.1 (target); CR 603.2 (triggered ability fires on its trigger event — "when this creature dies").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnTargetCardWithManaValueFromGraveyardToBattlefieldTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnTargetFromGraveyardToBattlefieldTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return target [filter] card from your graveyard to the battlefield [tapped]" — a single-target, filtered reanimation triggered effect (Undergrowth Recon: "At the beginning of your upkeep, return target land card from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped."). Parallel to the spell-side `ReturnGraveyardToBattlefieldRule` (same filter vocabulary and zone/controller shape), split into a separate file because `ITriggeredRule` and `ISpellRule` are distinct interfaces, and extended with the optional trailing "tapped" entering status (CR 110.5b) that the spell-side sentence never carries. Distinct from `ReturnAllFromGraveyardToBattlefieldTriggeredRule` ("return ALL … cards" — an `Each` reference, no targeting) and from `ReturnSelfFromGraveyardToBattlefieldRule` ("return THIS card" — a `Self` reference): this rule is the single-target ("return TARGET … card") counterpart, fully anchored (^…$) so it cannot match either sibling. CR 400.7 (an object that moves from one zone to another becomes a new object); CR 404.1 (graveyard); CR 115.1 (target); CR 110.5b (entering tapped).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnTargetFromGraveyardToBattlefieldTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnTargetTypeOrSubtypeFromGraveyardToHandTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Return target [X], [Y], or [Z] card from your graveyard to your hand." where the disjunction MIXES a capitalised card subtype (Plant, Treefolk, ...) with a base card type (land, creature, ...) — Kirri, Talented Sprout: "At the beginning of each of your postcombat main phases, return target Plant, Treefolk, or land card from your graveyard to your hand."

Reuses the mixed type-or-subtype classification `CounterTargetTypeOrSubtypeSpellRule` establishes for a two-way disjunction, generalised to any count of comma/or-joined members the same way `LookAtTopMayRevealMatchingRestToBottomTriggeredRule` generalises it: known card-type words route to `CardTypes`; capitalised non-card-type words route to `Subtypes` (OR semantics — CR 205.3, a card has zero or more subtypes). Source zone is the controller's own graveyard (CR 404.1); destination is the controller's hand (CR 402.1). "Return … to hand" is ordinary zone movement (CR 400.7), not a CR 701 keyword action.

DELIBERATELY declines any disjunction whose members are ALL recognised card types (e.g. "artifact or creature") — that pure-card-type shape is already produced (if incompletely — no `Zone`/`Controller`) by the generic `ReturnToHandRule` for existing cards (Interceptor Mechan's "return target artifact or creature card from your graveyard to your hand."). Requiring at least one genuine capitalised subtype member guarantees this rule can never collide with that sibling's gold fixture — it only claims the mixed shape no existing rule covers.

Priority 70, matching the sibling graveyard-return triggered rules (e.g. `ReturnInstantOrSorceryFromGraveyardRule`), beating the generic `ReturnToHandRule` (default priority 50) so the graveyard source zone and the subtype members are not silently dropped. ANCHORED (^…$) end to end so it cannot collide as a substring of any other return-effect sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnTargetTypeOrSubtypeFromGraveyardToHandTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnThatCardToHandOnDeathTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return that card to its owner's hand" — the Demonic Vigor pattern. This effect appears as the resolution clause of a "When enchanted creature dies" trigger on Auras whose enchanted host is returned to hand instead of the battlefield. Glossary "Dies": 'A creature or planeswalker "dies" if it is put into a graveyard from the battlefield. See rule 700.4.' CR 700.4: 'The term dies means "is put into a graveyard from the battlefield."' "That card" is a pronoun back-reference to the enchanted creature that just moved from the battlefield to the graveyard. CR 400.7: 'An object that moves from one zone to another becomes a new object with no memory of, or relation to, its previous existence.' MAST models this anaphoric reference as `It` — the generic back-reference kind ("it", "that card", "the creature" all denote the same game object). Variant: "return that card to the battlefield under your control" is handled by `ReturnEnchantedOnDeathTriggeredRule`; "return it to its owner's hand" (self-referential Auras) is handled by `ReturnSelfToHandOnDeathTriggeredRule`. This rule closes the remaining "that card" x hand quadrant. Example corpus patterns: "return that card to its owner's hand"

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnThatCardToHandOnDeathTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnThisToHandTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return this [type] to its owner's hand" — a self-referential bounce where the card names its own type word ("this enchantment", "this creature", "this artifact"...) to refer to itself. Resolves to `Self` — the card moving its own zone with no target (Rule 115.1 — "target" keyword absent, so no target is chosen). Higher priority than `ReturnToHandRule` so the self-reference "this [type]" is recognised as Self rather than mis-read as an indefinite "a [type] you control" choice (ObjectReferenceKind.Any). The "this [object]" phrasing is the oracle convention for a card referring to itself; modelling it as Self keeps the AST descriptively faithful to what the text says. Example corpus pattern: "return this enchantment to its owner's hand"

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnThisToHandTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ReturnToHandRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"return ... to its owner's hand" — type-disjunction, you-control, optional "you may"/"up to N", and non-prefix qualifiers (e.g. "nonland permanent", "nontoken creature").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnToHandRule.cs)

### `ReturnToHandWithIfYouDoGainLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Niambi shape: "you may return ... to its owner's hand. If you do, you gain life equal to that creature's mana value." Priority 80: must override `ReturnToHandRule` so the IfYouDo continuation isn't dropped.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ReturnToHandWithIfYouDoGainLifeRule.cs)

### `RevealTopMayPutSharesCreatureTypeRestToBottomTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Reveal the top N cards of your library. You may put a card that shares a creature type with it from among them into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order." — the Tajuru Paragon kicked-ETB reveal family.

The whole three-sentence fragment is one coherent game action — "from among them" and "the rest" in the second and third sentences are back-references to the reveal in the first — so this rule matches all three sentences as a single fragment and emits one `RevealTopMayPutSharesCreatureTypeRestToBottomEffect`. CR 701.20 (Reveal); CR 205.3m (creature types); CR 401.4 (the remainder placed on the bottom in a random order).

"It" (the object the revealed card must share a creature type with) is the source creature — `Self` — since this line only ever appears as the resolution of a self-referential "when this creature enters, if it was kicked" trigger (CR 201.5/109.5).

Priority 95: must beat the generic multi-sentence bundle splitter (mirroring `RevealTopPutMatchingToHandTriggeredRule`), which would otherwise try to resolve each of the three sentences independently and fail.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/RevealTopMayPutSharesCreatureTypeRestToBottomTriggeredRule.cs)

### `RevealTopPutMatchingToHandTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Reveal the top N cards of your library. Put all [filter] cards revealed this way into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in any order." — the Sylvan Messenger ETB reveal-and-partition family.

The whole two-sentence fragment is one coherent game action — "revealed this way" and "the rest" in the second sentence are back-references to the reveal in the first — so this rule matches both sentences as a single fragment and emits one `RevealTopPutMatchingToHandEffect`. CR 701.20 (Reveal); CR 401.4 (the remainder placed on the bottom in any order, player-chosen).

Priority 95: must beat the generic multi-sentence bundle splitter, which would otherwise try to resolve each sentence independently and fail (mirroring `ThassasOracleRule`).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/RevealTopPutMatchingToHandTriggeredRule.cs)

### `RingTemptsTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"the Ring tempts you." — the Rule 701.54 keyword action on the triggered side. Matches the bare keyword action when it is the entire effect body of a triggered ability (e.g. Uruk-hai Berserker's ETB trigger). CR 701.54a: "Certain spells and abilities have the text 'the Ring tempts you.' Each time the Ring tempts you, choose a creature you control. That creature becomes your Ring-bearer until another creature becomes your Ring-bearer or another player gains control of it." REUSE-ONLY emits the existing `RingTemptsEffect` node.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/RingTemptsTriggeredRule.cs)

### `RollDieTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"roll [count] [dN | N-sided die/dice]" — emits a `RollDieEffect` for the canonical die-roll instruction (CR 706.1). Handles both the abbreviated "dN" form ("roll a d20") and the spelled-out "N-sided die/dice" form ("roll a six-sided die", "roll two six-sided dice"), with an optional die count (CR 706.1: "how many of those dice to roll").

CR 706.1a: the die has N equally likely outcomes numbered 1 to N. This rule handles rolls without a results table (CR 706.4); the result is consumed by a following effect or by a die-roll trigger.

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the roll phrase could appear as a substring of a longer results-table instruction; anchoring prevents matching inside a more-specific sibling. Priority 60: above the generic fallback (default 50) and below combat-damage specialisations (70+).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/RollDieTriggeredRule.cs)

### `RollResultLifeChangeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

The life-changing CONSUMER of a die roll — the second sentence in the ETB-roll family ("When this creature enters, roll a [die]. [life change]"). The roll itself is the `RollDieEffect` emitted by `RollDieTriggeredRule`; this rule recognises the follow-up sentence that spends the roll's result on a life total. The multi-sentence dispatcher in `TriggeredAbilityParser` composes the two into one effect list — exactly as Ancient Copper Dragon's `[rollDie, createToken{result}]` is composed.

Two surfaces are handled, generalised over life direction (gain/lose):

<b>Bare consumer</b> — "you gain/lose life equal to the result" (Adorable Kitten: "You gain life equal to the result."). The amount is the roll result, modelled as `DieRollResultQuantity` (CR 706.2 — "the result of the die roll"; CR 706.4 — abilities without a results table indicate how to use the result). <b>Result-gated consumer</b> — "if the result is N or less/more, you gain/lose that much life" (Dissatisfied Customer: "If the result is 3 or less, you lose that much life."). The gate is a `QuantityComparisonCondition` comparing the roll result (`DieRollResultQuantity`) against the literal threshold; "that much" is the roll result again (the antecedent of "that much" is the roll, CR 706.2). Mirrors Captain Rex Nebula's <c>conditional{quantityComparison{result}, …{result}}</c> shape.

Scoped to the controller ("you"): both pinning golds spend the result on the ability's controller. The targeted-player forms ("target opponent loses life equal to the result", Big Boa Constrictor) are a sibling slice that needs its own gold to fix the targeting shape — deliberately NOT generalised here so every branch is gold-pinned.

Reference-not-resolution (ADR 0004): MAST records the textual reference to the roll result; the engine reads the actual rolled value at resolution. CR 119.3 — gaining or losing life adjusts the player's life total accordingly.

ANCHORED (`^…$`). Priority 74: in the dice-result-consumer band beside `CreateTokensEqualToDieResultTriggeredRule` (72), above the generic life rules so the "equal to the result" / "that much" forms are claimed by this die-aware rule rather than mis-bound to a fixed-amount sibling.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/RollResultLifeChangeRule.cs)

### `SacrificeALandTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice a land" — triggered player-choice sacrifice of an unqualified land. The controller picks any land they control at resolution; there is no formal targeting declaration (Rule 115.1 — only the "target" keyword creates a target), so the reference kind is `Any`. Mirrors `SacrificeAnyCreatureTriggeredRule` ("sacrifice a creature"), swapping the filtered card type from creature to land.

Example: Serendib Djinn (ARN): "At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice a land."

Distinct from `SacrificeLandAndDiscardHandRule` ("sacrifice a land and discard your hand"), which is a longer compound sentence; this rule is anchored to the bare "sacrifice a land" clause only.

CR 701.21a (verbatim): "To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner's graveyard."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeALandTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SacrificeAnotherCreatureDrawCardRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may sacrifice another creature. If you do, draw a card." — optional sacrifice-a-different-creature then draw (Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER ability 1).

Decomposes as an `OptionalEffect`:

`Inner` — `SacrificeEffect` targeting any creature the controller controls other than the source (ExcludeSelf = true, Kind = `Any`). "Another creature" in oracle text is the standard self-exclusion phrasing (CR 201.5 — the name or "this" refers to the source; "another" excludes it). The sacrifice is a player choice at resolution, not a target (CR 115.1 — "target" keyword only), so Kind = Any not Target. `IfYouDo` — `DrawCardsEffect` for exactly one card (CR 120.1 — "draw a card" = one card from the top of the library). Player = `You`.

Priority 95 — must run BEFORE `DrawCardsTriggeredRule` (priority 50), which matches any text containing "draw a card" and would fire on the full "you may sacrifice … If you do, draw a card" text first (producing an incorrect OptionalEffect wrapping only the draw). This rule is anchored (`^…$`) so it cannot fire on a sibling draw-only clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeAnotherCreatureDrawCardRule.cs)

### `SacrificeAnyCreatureTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice a creature" — triggered player-choice sacrifice. The controller picks any creature they control at resolution; there is no formal targeting declaration (Rule 115.1 — only the "target" keyword creates a target), so the reference kind is `Any`. Covers the classic upkeep-tax pattern used on cards like Necrite (FEM/ME2). Distinct from `SacrificeTriggeredRule`, which handles the pronoun forms "sacrifice it / this creature / this permanent" where the object to sacrifice is already determined by the trigger context.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeAnyCreatureTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SacrificeAnyNumberOtherCreaturesDrawThatManyRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may sacrifice any number of other creatures. If you do, draw that many cards." — optional mass-sacrifice-then-draw-that-many (Sephiroth, One-Winged Angel ability 3).

Decomposes as an `OptionalEffect`:

`Inner` — `SacrificeEffect` targeting any number of other creatures. "Any number of other creatures" → Kind = `Any`, Filter.ExcludeSelf = true (the card's "other" clause, CR 201.5 self-exclusion), Count = `AnyAmountQuantity` (the "any number of" upper-unbounded player choice, CR 107.3). The sacrifice is a player choice, not a target (CR 115.1 — no "target" keyword). `IfYouDo` — `DrawCardsEffect` for "that many" cards. "That many" is an anaphoric reference to the number of creatures sacrificed in the Inner — backed by `Other` (the sacrificed- creature count is not a named `DerivedKind` variant; Other is the structured residual per ADR 0001). Player = `You`.

Priority 95 — must run BEFORE `YouDrawThatManyCardsTriggeredRule` (default priority 50) and `DrawCardsTriggeredRule` (50), which would fire on the "draw that many cards" tail and produce an incorrect shape. ANCHORED (`^…$`) so it cannot fire on a standalone "draw that many cards" clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeAnyNumberOtherCreaturesDrawThatManyRule.cs)

### `SacrificeAtEndStepTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Recognises the delayed-sacrifice sentence within a triggered ability effect body:

"Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step."

This sentence appears as a trailing clause in multi-sentence triggered ability effects — typically after a token-creation effect. For example: "Whenever this creature attacks, create a 1/1 red Goblin creature token. Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step." The pronoun "it" refers to the token or creature created/obtained by the preceding clause (Rule 109.2 — game objects). MAST records this as a `SacrificeEffect` whose `Target` is `It` and whose `Duration` is `AtBeginningOfNextEndStepDuration`. Descriptive, not engine-executable (descriptive-not-engine doctrine). The trigger timing semantics are carried by the duration node. Priority 70: must supersede `SacrificeTriggeredRule` (plain "sacrifice it") so the more-specific duration-bearing form fires first. Rule citations: 701.21 (Sacrifice), 513 (End Step), 603.7 (delayed triggers).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeAtEndStepTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SacrificeAttachThenUntapAllAndAdditionalCombatRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice it and attach this Aura to a creature you control. If you do, untap all creatures you control and after this phase, there is an additional combat phase." — the Breath of Fury extra-combat-engine pattern (the combat-damage Aura that hops to a fresh creature and grants another combat phase).

Produces a `CompositeEffect` of three effects:

A `SacrificeEffect` on "it" — the enchanted creature named by the trigger condition (CR 701.21: sacrifice; the "it" pronoun is the trigger subject, modelled as `It`). An `AttachEffect` moving this Aura onto "a creature you control" — an indefinite, non-targeted controller choice (CR 701.3: attach; `Any` per the "a [filter] you control" convention, not a target since the oracle omits the word "target"). A `ConditionalEffect` gating the payoff on "If you do" — i.e. the attach actually happened (CR 101.3: any part of an instruction that's impossible to perform is ignored; the attach can fail when no legal creature is available, in which case the consequent is skipped). Its `Then` is a nested `CompositeEffect` of an `UntapEffect` on every creature the controller controls (CR 701.26: untap) and an `AdditionalCombatPhaseEffect` inserting one extra combat phase (CR 500.8: adding phases to a turn; CR 506.1: the combat phase).

The "If you do" antecedent is structured as a `PrecedingActionPerformedCondition` — the within-resolution gate on whether the preceding attach happened (CR 101.3: an impossible instruction is ignored). MAST records the printed gate without pre-evaluating it (ADR 0004); this idiom is fixed and parameter-free, so it is de-stringed rather than left as an `OtherCondition` residual.

Pattern is anchored (^...$) to the entire effect text so it cannot match as a substring of a longer phrase. The clause is one semantic unit — the second sentence ("If you do, …") is conditional on the first — so this full-text rule wins over the sentence-bundle splitter: the splitter bails when its fragments ("sacrifice it and attach …" / "If you do, …") fail to parse independently, after which the dispatcher's single-rule loop reaches this rule on the whole text (the same fall-through that lets `MayPayUntapAttackingAndAdditionalCombatRule` handle Hellkite Charger).

CR references: CR 500.8 (adding a phase to a turn); CR 506.1 (the combat phase); CR 701.3 (attach); CR 701.21 (sacrifice); CR 701.26 (tap/untap); CR 101.3 (an impossible instruction is ignored — the "if you do" gate).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeAttachThenUntapAllAndAdditionalCombatRule.cs)

### `SacrificeConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you sacrifice [object]" — player-sacrifice trigger (Rule 701.21 Sacrifice; Rule 603).

Covers two oracle shapes, both keyed on `Sacrifices`:

<b>"you sacrifice another [creature|permanent|…]"</b> — the aristocrat sac-payoff family (Bloodbriar, Gixian Infiltrator, Pirate Peddlers, Body Dropper). "you sacrifice another permanent" → Filter{ CardTypes:["permanent"], Controller:You, ExcludeSelf:true }; the creature variant → CardTypes:["creature"]. The card-type + "another" exclusion are recovered by `ParseObjectFilter` (the same machinery the dies-family uses for "another creature dies"); the controller (You) is overlaid here because the player doing the sacrificing is "you" (CR 701.21a — a player can only sacrifice a permanent they control), regardless of whether the oracle text spells out "you control". <b>"you sacrifice a [Subtype]"</b> — a named permanent subtype such as Food, Treasure, Clue, or Blood. "you sacrifice a Food" → Filter{ Subtypes:["Food"], Controller:You }. ParseObjectFilter does not recognise a bare subtype phrase ("a Food"), so this path is the fallback when the general object form yields no filter.

CR 701.21a: "To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner's graveyard. A player can't sacrifice something that isn't a permanent, or something that's a permanent they don't control." "another" excludes the source object of the ability (plain-language, per the dies-family convention). CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeConditionRule.cs)

### `SacrificeItAtEndStepUnlessPayEnergyEqualToManaValueRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"At the beginning of the next end step, sacrifice that token unless you pay an amount of {E} equal to its mana value." — Satya, Aetherflux Genius's delayed-trigger energy-buyback pattern (CR 603.7: delayed triggered ability; CR 107.14: energy counters; CR 701.21: sacrifice).

Oracle structure: this sentence encodes a `CreateDelayedTriggerEffect` that schedules a one-shot trigger at the beginning of the next end step. When that trigger resolves its controller must either pay energy equal to the token's mana value or sacrifice it. Modelled as `PreventableEffect` wrapping `SacrificeEffect` with an `UnlessClause` whose cost is `PayEnergyCost` with a `DerivedQuantity` referencing `ManaValue` (the mana value of the token = "it").

"That token" / "it" — both pronouns refer to the token created by the preceding copy-effect sentence in the same triggered ability. MAST models this as `It` (the conventional back-reference pronoun, matching `SacrificeAtEndStepTriggeredRule` and `SacrificeUnlessPayTriggeredRule`).

ANCHORED (^…$): the "at the beginning of the next end step" phrase could match inside a broader sentence on a sibling trigger, so the anchor prevents substring collisions. Priority 73 — above `SacrificeAtEndStepTriggeredRule` (70) so the more-specific energy-buyback form is claimed here first.

Rule citations: CR 603.7 (delayed triggered ability), CR 107.14 (energy symbol), CR 513 (end step), CR 701.21 (sacrifice), CR 117.7 (unless clause).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeItAtEndStepUnlessPayEnergyEqualToManaValueRule.cs)

### `SacrificeItUnlessDiscardLandRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice it unless you discard a land card" — the ETB sacrifice-tax whose alternative payment is discarding a land card (Fallow Wurm). Structurally the sibling of `SacrificeItUnlessDiscardRandomRule` ("sacrifice it unless you discard a card at random"): the `UnlessClause` cost is a `DiscardCost`, but here the discarded card is a land card chosen by the player (not a random discard), so `Random` is left false and the filter narrows to land cards.

Oracle text split by `TriggeredAbilityParser`: trigger = "When this creature enters" effect = "sacrifice it unless you discard a land card"

The "unless you [pay a cost]" gate is a cost-or-consequence: the sacrifice (CR 701.21a — "To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner's graveyard.") happens unless its controller chooses to pay the stated cost, and paying a cost is never automatic (CR 118.5 — "The same is true for an ability … it won't [pay] itself automatically"). The stated cost is a discard (CR 701.9a — "To discard a card, move it from its owner's hand to that player's graveyard.") restricted to a land card.

Produces a `PreventableEffect` with Inner = `SacrificeEffect` (Target = It, the pronoun referring back to the trigger subject, matching `SacrificeItUnlessDiscardRandomRule`) and an `UnlessClause` whose Player is You and whose Cost is a one-card land `DiscardCost`.

Representative card: Fallow Wurm. Rule citations: 701.21a (Sacrifice), 118.5 (paying a cost is not automatic), 701.9a (Discard).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeItUnlessDiscardLandRule.cs)

### `SacrificeItUnlessDiscardRandomRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice it unless you discard a card at random" — the ETB sacrifice-tax whose alternative payment is a random discard rather than mana (Balduvian Horde). Structurally identical to the mana-tax `SacrificeUnlessPayTriggeredRule` ("sacrifice it unless you pay {C}") except the `UnlessClause` cost is a `DiscardCost` whose card is chosen at random rather than a `ManaCost`.

Oracle text split by `TriggeredAbilityParser`: trigger = "When this creature enters" effect = "sacrifice it unless you discard a card at random"

The "unless you [pay a cost]" gate is a cost-or-consequence: the sacrifice (CR 701.21a — Sacrifice) happens unless its controller chooses to pay the stated cost, and paying a cost is never automatic (CR 118.5). The stated cost here is a random discard — CR 701.9b: "By default, effects that cause a player to discard a card allow the affected player to choose which card to discard. Some effects, however, require a random discard or allow another player to choose which card is discarded." The randomness is carried structurally by `Random`.

Produces a `PreventableEffect` with Inner = `SacrificeEffect` (Target = It, the pronoun referring back to the trigger subject, matching `SacrificeUnlessPayTriggeredRule`) and an `UnlessClause` whose Player is You and whose Cost is a one-card random `DiscardCost`.

Representative card: Balduvian Horde (ALL). Rule citations: 701.21a (Sacrifice), 118.5 (paying a cost is not automatic), 701.9b (random discard variant).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeItUnlessDiscardRandomRule.cs)

### `SacrificeLandAndDiscardHandRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice a land and discard your hand" — Psychic Vortex's end-step tax: the controller sacrifices a land they choose AND discards their entire hand, two mandatory conjunctive effects in a single clause. CR 701.21a (sacrifice); CR 701.9a (discard). The two effects are wrapped in a `CompositeEffect`, mirroring the single-sentence-conjunction convention used elsewhere for "and"-joined mandatory effect pairs (`DiscardAndUntapAllLandsRule`).

"A land" has no formal target declaration (Rule 115.1 — only the "target" keyword creates a target), so the reference kind is `Any`, mirroring `SacrificeAnyCreatureTriggeredRule`'s "sacrifice a creature" shape but filtered to `CardTypes:["land"]`. "Your hand" is modelled as a `DerivedQuantity` with `CardsInHand`, matching `DiscardHandSpellRule`'s "discard your hand" decomposition — descriptively, "hand" means "all cards in hand at the time the effect resolves."

Priority 62 — matches the sibling `DiscardAndUntapAllLandsRule`: above the generic single-effect rules (which would fail on the conjoined clause). ANCHORED (^…$) so it cannot match as a substring of a broader clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeLandAndDiscardHandRule.cs)

### `SacrificeOneOrMoreSubtypeConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you sacrifice one or more [Subtype]s" — player-sacrifice trigger for a batch of named-subtype permanents (Rule 701.21; Rule 603).

Handles oracle text of the form "Whenever you sacrifice one or more [Subtype]s,", where [Subtype] is a named permanent subtype (e.g. Food, Treasure, Clue). The "one or more" qualifier sets `MinimumCount` = 1, matching the CR convention that the ability fires on any positive-count sacrifice event regardless of exact quantity. The filter carries the sacrificed object's subtype and the controller (You), so "you sacrifice one or more Foods" maps to `Sacrifices` + Filter{ Subtypes:["Food"], Controller:You } with MinimumCount = 1.

Distinct from `SacrificeConditionRule` which handles the singular "you sacrifice a [Subtype]" form (no MinimumCount qualifier). Both rules share the same TriggerEvent; the MinimumCount distinguishes "one or more" (batch) from the singular form (any single instance).

CR 701.21a: "To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner's graveyard." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeOneOrMoreSubtypeConditionRule.cs)

### `SacrificePerLifeLostRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice a [type] for each 1 life you lost" — a sacrifice effect whose count scales with the life just lost by the triggering player (Lich's Tomb: "Whenever you lose life, sacrifice a permanent for each 1 life you lost.").

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." The "for each 1 life you lost" scaling is self-contained (unlike the bare "that many"/"that much" antecedent forms, which need the enclosing trigger's event to disambiguate — see `DrawThatManyCardsLifeLostRule`'s remarks), so this rule is safe to reflection-discover into the generic effect-rule pool: the explicit "life you lost" phrase names its own antecedent regardless of the enclosing trigger.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificePerLifeLostRule.cs)

### `SacrificeSelfTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice this [enchantment|artifact|land|sorcery|instant|planeswalker|…]" — a self-sacrifice effect where the oracle text names the source's own card type (e.g. "sacrifice this enchantment") rather than the generic "sacrifice this permanent" form. Maps to a `SacrificeEffect` with `Self`.

Rule 701.21a: "To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner's graveyard." MAST records the target as Self (the source of the ability); the engine performs the move.

This rule supersedes any broader "sacrifice this permanent" fallback by Priority = 65 (above the default 50 but below the 70 used by the `SacrificeAtEndStepTriggeredRule` which handles the delayed form). Examples: Underworld Breach (THB): "sacrifice this enchantment."

Rule citations: 701.21a (Sacrifice), 201.4 (self-name reference).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeSelfTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SacrificeSelfUnlessPayRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice this [permanent-noun] unless you pay {COST}" — the upkeep-tax pattern. The "unless you pay" gate is a cost-or-consequence: the sacrifice (Rule 701.21 — Sacrifice) happens unless its controller chooses to pay the stated cost, and paying a cost is never automatic (Rule 118.5 — "it's not automatically paid"). This exact templating is the canonical Echo wording (Rule 702.30 — Echo: "At the beginning of your upkeep, ... sacrifice it unless you pay [cost]"), here printed directly on the card rather than abbreviated to the keyword.

Oracle text split by `TriggeredAbilityParser`: trigger = "At the beginning of your upkeep" effect = "sacrifice this creature unless you pay {B}"

The self-noun varies by the card's type — "this creature" (Whipstitched Zombie), "this enchantment" (Breeding Pit, Glaciers), "this artifact" (Forethought Amulet), "this Aura" (Melancholy, Thirst), and the generic "this permanent" all name the same object: the source bearing the ability. The noun is descriptive type-flavour and carries no AST distinction, so the pattern accepts the full set and the produced shape is identical regardless of which noun was printed.

The pronoun form "this [noun]" is a self-reference (Rule 109.2): the permanent bearing the ability is the object that would be sacrificed. MAST models this as `Self`, distinct from the "sacrifice it" ETB-land pattern handled by `SacrificeUnlessPayTriggeredRule` which uses `It`.

Produces a `SacrificeEffect` with Target = Self and an `UnlessClause` whose Player is You and whose Cost is the parsed mana expression.

Representative cards: Whipstitched Zombie (NEM), Wild Leotau (CON), Spindrift Drake (WTH), Molting Harpy (UDS) — creatures; Breeding Pit (5ED), Glaciers (ICE), Drought (MIR), Justice (LEG), Thelon's Chant (TSP) — enchantments; Forethought Amulet (MIR) — artifact; Melancholy, Thirst (WTH) — Auras. Rule citations: 701.21 (Sacrifice), 118.5 (paying a cost is not automatic), 702.30 (Echo — the canonical "sacrifice it unless you pay" templating).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeSelfUnlessPayRule.cs)

### `SacrificeSelfUnlessSacrificePermanentRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice [this creature / this permanent / CardName] unless you sacrifice a [type]" — the upkeep-tax pattern where the cost to prevent self-sacrifice is sacrificing another permanent of a given type (Rule 701.21a — Sacrifice; Rule 117.7 — unless clause).

Oracle text split by `TriggeredAbilityParser`: trigger = "At the beginning of your upkeep" effect = "sacrifice [this creature|The Gitrog Monster] unless you sacrifice a land"

The self-reference ("this creature", "this permanent", or a named card like "The Gitrog Monster") is the source object itself (CR 201.4 / CR 109.2) — MAST models this as `Self`. The preventive cost is a `SacrificeCost` whose Filter restricts to the stated permanent type.

Representative cards: The Gitrog Monster (SOI), Yavimaya Ants (ALL). Rule citations: 701.21 (Sacrifice), 117.7 (unless clause), 201.4 (self-name reference).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeSelfUnlessSacrificePermanentRule.cs)

### `SacrificeThatPermanentTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice that permanent" — the resolution half of the becomes-unattached trigger, paired with `BecomesUnattachedConditionRule` (Stitcher's Graft: "Whenever this Equipment becomes unattached from a permanent, sacrifice that permanent.").

Rule 701.21a: "To sacrifice a permanent, its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner's graveyard." The pronoun "that permanent" back-references the object named by the trigger condition's Filter (the permanent the Equipment detached from — CR 701.3d), maps to `ThatPermanent`, mirroring the "that creature"/"that player" back-reference convention used elsewhere (e.g. Flanking's `ThatCreature`).

Distinct from `SacrificeTriggeredRule` ("sacrifice it"/"sacrifice this permanent" — the trigger SUBJECT) and `SacrificeSelfTriggeredRule` ("sacrifice this [type]" — the ability's own source): here the sacrificed object is neither the subject nor the source, but a third object named earlier in the trigger condition.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeThatPermanentTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SacrificeTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice it" / "sacrifice this creature" / "sacrifice this permanent" — triggered self-sacrifice (Rule 701.21a — Sacrifice). The reference kind depends on the surface form: the pronoun "it" refers back to a previously-mentioned object and maps to `It`, whereas the explicit "this creature"/"this permanent" self-reference (no antecedent) maps to `Self` — matching the canonical `ObjectReference` convention (Self = "this creature", It = a prior object) and every existing "sacrifice this creature" gold (Longhorn Firebeast, Wild Leotau, Whipstitched Zombie).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SacrificeUnlessColorSpentToCastRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice it unless {COLOR} was spent to cast it" — the Plaxmanta-family ETB self-sacrifice gated on which mana color paid the casting cost (CR 601.2f–h; CR 701.21a — Sacrifice).

Distinct from `SacrificeUnlessPayTriggeredRule` ("sacrifice it unless you pay {COST}"): that shape is a payable cost with a live decision at resolution (`UnlessClause`: `Player` + `Cost`). "Unless {COLOR} was spent to cast it" offers no choice at resolution — it's a lookup against a fact already fixed when the spell was cast (CR 601.2h). Modelled instead as a `ConditionalEffect` gated on a `ManaSpentToCastCondition` (`WasSpent = false`) whose `Then` is the sacrifice — this is effect-level (CR 603), NOT an intervening-if (CR 603.4): the ability always triggers on ETB, and the color-spent check happens at resolution.

"It" refers back to the entering creature named as the trigger subject (`It()`), matching the pronoun-reference convention used in `SacrificeUnlessPayTriggeredRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeUnlessColorSpentToCastRule.cs)

### `SacrificeUnlessPayTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice it unless you pay {COST}" — the Karoo/bounce-land ETB sacrifice pattern (Rule 701.21a — Sacrifice; Rule 117.7 — unless clause).

Oracle text split by `TriggeredAbilityParser`: trigger = "When this land enters" effect = "sacrifice it unless you pay {1}"

Produces a `SacrificeEffect` with Target = It and an `UnlessClause` whose Player is You and whose Cost is the parsed mana expression. "It" refers back to the land named as the trigger subject — matching the pronoun-reference convention used in `SacrificeTriggeredRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeUnlessPayTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SacrificeUnlessReturnUntappedLandTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"sacrifice it unless you return an untapped [basic land type] you control to its owner's hand" — the Visions "Karoo" bounce-land ETB pattern (Everglades, Karoo, Coral Atoll, Dormant Volcano, Jungle Basin). Rule 701.21a — Sacrifice; the "unless" clause is a preventive alternative cost (CR 117.7-adjacent — paying a cost to avoid an effect), not a separate effect.

Oracle text split by `TriggeredAbilityParser`: trigger = "When this land enters" effect = "sacrifice it unless you return an untapped Swamp you control to its owner's hand"

"it" refers back to the land named as the trigger subject — the pronoun-reference convention shared with `SacrificeUnlessPayTriggeredRule` (Karoo/ETB self-sacrifice uses `It`, not Self). "untapped" is a tapped/untapped status (CR 110.5) modeled as a <c>TappedStateCharacteristic { Tapped = false }</c>. "Swamp" is a basic land subtype (CR 305.6); "its owner's hand" is by ownership (CR 108.3) — modeled the same way as the cost-position return in `ReturnLandSubtypeToHandCostRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SacrificeUnlessReturnUntappedLandTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ScryOrSurveilConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you scry or surveil" — fires on either keyword action (Rule 701.18 / 701.43).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ScryOrSurveilConditionRule.cs)

### `ScryTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"scry N." — Rule 701.18 keyword action on the triggered side.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ScryTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SearchBasicLandTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may search your library for a basic land card, [reveal it,] put [it|that card] onto the battlefield tapped / into your hand, then shuffle." Covers the ETB-search-land pattern (Rule 701.23: Search). Two destination variants: - put it into your hand (Destination=Hand, Revealed=true) - put that card onto the battlefield tapped (Destination=BattlefieldTapped, Revealed=false)

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SearchBasicLandTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SearchFoodCardOrCreateFoodTokenRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Courier of Comestibles: "you may search your library for a Food card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle. If you don't put a card into your hand this way, create a Food token."

A single-effect "you may [tutor], else [predefined token]" body. Decomposes — mirroring the established Smothering Tithe convention (`ThatPlayerMayPayYouCreateTreasureRule`) — into an `OptionalEffect` whose:

`Inner` is the tutor: a `SearchLibraryEffect` for a Food card (`Subtypes: ["Food"]`, CR 205.3g Food is an artifact subtype), revealed, to hand (CR 701.23a — to search is to look through a zone for a card matching the description). `IfYouDoNot` is the "if you don't put a card into your hand this way" fallback: a `CreateTokenEffect` for one predefined Food token (CR 111.10b: "A Food token is a colorless Food artifact token with '{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: You gain 3 life.'").

ANCHORED (`^…$`) over the FULL two-sentence body so no sibling search or create-token surface is mislabelled. The dispatcher's sentence-bundle splitter first tries the two sentences independently; sentence two ("If you don't …") matches no standalone rule, so the bundle returns null and this whole-body rule is reached in the single-rule loop.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SearchFoodCardOrCreateFoodTokenRule.cs)

### `SearchForNamedCardTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may search your library [and/or graveyard] for a card named [Name], reveal it, [and] put it into your hand. [If you search your library this way, shuffle.]" Covers the ETB named-card tutor pattern (Rule 701.23: Search), e.g. Sorin's Guide. Distinct from `SearchLibraryToHandTriggeredRule` in two ways the older rule cannot express: 1. The search target is pinned by exact name ("a card named X") rather than a card-type/subtype category — recorded on `Name`. 2. The search may span multiple source zones ("library and/or graveyard") — recorded on `Sources`. A library-only search leaves Sources null (the default Rule 701.23 case). The "you may" prefix is optional; its presence sets IsOptional=true. The reveal clause sets Revealed=true. The trailing conditional-shuffle sentence ("If you search your library this way, shuffle.") is rules-inferred bookkeeping and is folded into the effect rather than modelled separately — the same convention SearchLibraryToHandTriggeredRule uses for its "then shuffle" tail. Priority 70 (above SearchLibraryToHandTriggeredRule's 60) so the named/ multi-zone shape is recognised before the generic category-tutor rule.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SearchForNamedCardTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SearchForNamedCardsUpToNTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may search your library for up to N cards named [Name], reveal them, put them into your hand, then shuffle." Covers the ETB named-card tutor pattern bounded by a count (Rule 701.23: Search), e.g. Nesting Wurm ("up to three cards named Nesting Wurm"). This is the plural, count-bounded sibling of `SearchForNamedCardTriggeredRule` (which only matches the singular "a card named X, reveal it, put it into your hand" shape) — the "up to N cards"/"reveal them"/"put them" wording here cannot match that rule's singular anchors, and it cannot match `SearchLibraryToHandTriggeredRule` either, since that rule's filter clause is anchored on "for a[n] " while this text begins "for up to N", so the two are disjoint. The found cards are revealed (Rule 701.20: Reveal — Revealed=true), put into hand, then the library is shuffled (Rule 701.24: Shuffle). Per the convention set by the direct CR 701.23 precedent template (Veteran Explorer: "search their library for up to two basic land cards, put them onto the battlefield, then shuffle"), the trailing "then shuffle" is rules-inferred bookkeeping folded into the effect rather than modelled as a separate node. The "you may" prefix is optional; its presence sets IsOptional=true via `Optional`. Priority 80 — above both `SearchForNamedCardTriggeredRule` (70) and `SearchLibraryToHandTriggeredRule` (60); the three rules are mutually disjoint by anchor shape so ordering among them is not load-bearing, but the higher priority keeps this most-specific rule tried first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SearchForNamedCardsUpToNTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryToBattlefieldTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may search your library for a[n] &lt;filter&gt; card, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle." — optional triggered tutor directly to the battlefield.

Handles the pattern found on Godo, Bandit Warlord and similar ETB tutors that place the found card directly onto the battlefield (not into the hand or top of library). The "you may" prefix is optional; its presence wraps the effect in `OptionalEffect`.

Maps to a `CompositeEffect` containing:

`SearchLibraryEffect` with Destination = `Battlefield` (or `BattlefieldTapped` when "tapped" is present). `ShuffleEffect` for the mandatory library shuffle.

CR 701.23 (Search); CR 701.26 (Tap and Untap for tapped variant).

Priority 62 — above the generic Hand-destination rule (Priority 60) so this battlefield-specific rule is tried before the hand rule, and the two cannot cross-match because their destination clauses are anchored differently.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SearchLibraryToBattlefieldTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryToHandTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may search your library for a [filter] card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle." Handles the non-basic-land ETB tutor pattern (Rule 701.23: Search). Supports three filter shapes: 1. Plain card type — "a creature card", "an artifact card", etc. 2. Subtype (tribal) — "an Elf card", "a Goblin card", etc. 3. Card type + mana value comparison — "a creature card with mana value 6 or greater" The "you may" prefix is optional; its presence sets IsOptional=true. Only the Hand destination is covered here (reveal → hand → shuffle). The SearchBasicLandTriggeredRule handles basic-land searches at higher priority. Priority 60 (above default 50) so this is tried before generic fallback rules but after any higher-priority specialised rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SearchLibraryToHandTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SearchLibraryToTopTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may search your library for a [filter] card, reveal it, then shuffle and put that card on top." The ETB tutor-to-top pattern (the Lorwyn "Harbinger" cycle and kin), e.g. Boggart Harbinger ("a Goblin card") and Dune Mover ("a basic land card"). Distinct from the existing ETB tutor rules (`SearchLibraryToHandTriggeredRule`, `SearchBasicLandTriggeredRule`) only in its destination: the found card goes on top of the library (`TopOfLibrary`) rather than into the hand or onto the battlefield. The spell-resolution analogue is `SearchLibraryToTopRule`. Rule 701.23a (Search). The "you may" prefix is optional; its presence sets IsOptional=true via `Optional`. The reveal clause sets Revealed=true. The "shuffle and put that card on top" tail is folded into the effect (Destination=TopOfLibrary) rather than modelled separately — the same convention every sibling tutor rule uses for its shuffle clause. The filter group is partitioned into Supertypes / CardTypes / Subtypes the same way `SearchLibraryToTopRule` partitions it, so "basic land" → Supertypes=[Basic] CardTypes=[land] and a bare subtype word ("Goblin") → Subtypes=[Goblin].

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SearchLibraryToTopTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SelfCreatureDealtDamageConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever this creature is dealt damage" — emits `CreatureDealtDamage` with a self-restricted Filter (`{CardTypes: ["creature"], IsSelf: true}`). This is the "this creature" self sibling of `CreatureDealtDamageConditionRule` (which handles the generic "a creature is dealt damage" — any creature, e.g. Repercussion).

"This creature" refers to the ability's own source object (CR 109 — the object bearing the ability), so the filter carries `IsSelf` to restrict the trigger to that single permanent rather than any creature — the self/any axis the interaction operator gates on (an arbitrary creature is not provably the source). Jackal Pup: "Whenever this creature is dealt damage, it deals that much damage to you."

CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." Higher priority than the generic rule so "this creature" wins the self-restricted reading; the generic rule's guard still catches "a creature" (which lacks "this").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfCreatureDealtDamageConditionRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals N damage to any target." — ETB self-ping targeting any legal target (creature, player, or planeswalker). Covers cards whose triggered ETB ability reads "When this [creature|artifact] enters, it deals N damage to any target." Rule 603: triggered abilities (When/Whenever/At). Rule 120.1-120.2: dealing damage (a source deals damage to a permanent/player). Rule 115.4: "any target" — a target may be any player, creature, planeswalker, or battle unless otherwise restricted. Distinct from `SelfDealsDamageToYouRule` (targets the controller only) and the spell-side `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetRule` (subject is the spell itself, not a triggered pronoun).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureAndPlaneswalkerRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Triggered board-sweep: "[it] deals N damage to each creature and each planeswalker." — the Siege-ETB sweeper (Invasion of Karsus). The source fires N damage simultaneously into both the creature population and the planeswalker population.

CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. … An object that deals damage is the source of that damage." Each population is a distinct `DealDamageEffect` targeting `Each` filtered to the respective card type; the two are bundled in a `CompositeEffect` mirroring the spell-side "each creature and each player" sweeper (`DealDamageToEachRule`).

Triggered-side companion to that spell-side rule — the ETB self-reference is "it" (the permanent named by the trigger condition) rather than the substituted card name, so `It` is the source.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToEachCreatureAndPlaneswalkerRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToEachOpponentTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Triggered self-as-source spread: "this creature deals N damage to each opponent." — the cast-trigger drain on Refraction Elemental ("Whenever you cast a spell, this creature deals 2 damage to each opponent.").

CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." (Here the trigger is the spell-cast event, parsed by the condition side.) CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to … players. … An object that deals damage is the source of that damage." The source is the permanent itself ("this creature" → `Self`); the target population is every opponent (`EachOpponent`), dealt N simultaneously.

Triggered-side companion of the activated/spell each-opponent damage rules (`SelfDealsDamageToEachOpponentEffectRule`); the effect node is identical, only the dispatch context differs.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToEachOpponentTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToOpponentRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals N damage to target opponent." — ETB self-ping targeting a single opponent. Covers cards whose triggered ETB ability reads "When this [land|creature|artifact] enters, it deals N damage to target opponent." Rule 603: triggered abilities (When/Whenever/At). Rule 120.1-120.2: dealing damage (a source deals damage to a player). Rule 115.1: "target" creates a target. Rule 102.2: an opponent is a player not on the same team as the controller. Distinct from `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` (which targets any legal target — creature, player, or planeswalker — per Rule 115.4) and from `SelfDealsDamageToYouRule` (which targets the controller).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToOpponentRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToThatPlayerRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"this creature deals N damage to them" — the effect clause of an upkeep trigger whose recipient is the player named by the trigger condition (Prickle Faeries: "At the beginning of each opponent's upkeep, …, this creature deals 2 damage to them"). "Them" is the singular pronoun for that opponent — the player whose upkeep fired the trigger — and maps to `ThatPlayer` (the same back-reference `ThatPlayerLosesLifeRule` uses). The source is the card itself, `Self`.

CR 603.2: the event-match (the opponent's upkeep beginning) is the trigger. The damage is dealt by the source to that player (CR 120.1-120.2). Distinct from `SelfDealsDamageToYouRule` (recipient = the controller) and `SelfDealsDamageToOpponentRule` ("it deals … to target opponent", a fresh targeted opponent rather than the trigger's named player).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToThatPlayerRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsDamageToYouRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"it deals N damage to you" / "this creature deals N damage to you" — reflexive damage.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfDealsDamageToYouRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsHandMinusNDamageToThatPlayerRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"this artifact deals X damage to that player, where X is the number of cards in their hand minus N" — the effect clause of an each-opponent's-upkeep trigger whose damage amount is the recipient's hand size reduced by a constant (Iron Maiden: "At the beginning of each opponent's upkeep, this artifact deals X damage to that player, where X is the number of cards in their hand minus 4"). "That player"/"them" and "their hand" both back-reference the opponent whose upkeep fired the trigger (`ThatPlayer` / `ThatPlayer`), and the source is the card itself (`Self`) — the same singular back-references the operand-reversed sibling `SelfDealsThreeMinusHandDamageToThatPlayerRule` (Rackling: "X is 3 minus the number of cards in their hand") uses.

The where-clause resolves X inline to the computed amount. "the number of cards in their hand minus N" is a binary subtraction between two full quantities — a `CountQuantity` over the opponent's hand as the minuend and a `LiteralQuantity` N as the subtrahend — carried by `CalculatedQuantity` with `Operation="subtract"` and the second operand in `OperandQuantity`. This mirrors the sibling exactly but with the operands swapped (count minus constant, not constant minus count). The hand-count filter `{ card, Owner=ThatPlayer, Zone=Hand }` is identical to the sibling's.

CR 603.2: the event-match (the opponent's upkeep beginning) is the trigger. The damage is dealt by the source to that player (CR 120.1-120.2). Amount is engine territory at resolution (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004): MAST records the "hand-size minus N" reference, not a pre-resolved number (and it may be zero or less — the engine floors damage at 0 per CR 120.6).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the variable "X damage … where X is the number of cards in … hand minus N" shape is disjoint from the literal-amount `SelfDealsDamageToThatPlayerRule` (which requires a numeric amount immediately before "damage" and ends right after the recipient) and from the operand-reversed `SelfDealsThreeMinusHandDamageToThatPlayerRule` (whose where-clause opens "X is N minus"), so the three never collide. Priority above default so the more-specific variable form is tried first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfDealsHandMinusNDamageToThatPlayerRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsHandSizeDamageToThatPlayerRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"this enchantment deals damage to that player equal to the number of cards in that player's hand" — the effect clause of an each-opponent's-upkeep trigger whose damage amount is exactly the recipient's hand size, with no further arithmetic (Price of Knowledge). "That player"/"them" and "that player's hand"/"their hand" both back-reference the opponent whose upkeep fired the trigger (`ThatPlayer` / `ThatPlayer`), and the source is the card itself (`Self`) — the same singular back-references `SelfDealsHandMinusNDamageToThatPlayerRule` uses.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfDealsHandSizeDamageToThatPlayerRule.cs)

### `SelfDealsThreeMinusHandDamageToThatPlayerRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"this creature deals X damage to that player, where X is N minus the number of cards in their hand" — the effect clause of an each-opponent's-upkeep trigger whose damage amount is a constant reduced by the recipient's hand size (Rackling: "At the beginning of each opponent's upkeep, this creature deals X damage to that player, where X is 3 minus the number of cards in their hand"). "That player"/"them" and "their hand" both back-reference the opponent whose upkeep fired the trigger (`ThatPlayer` / `ThatPlayer`) — the same singular back-reference the literal-amount sibling `SelfDealsDamageToThatPlayerRule` uses. The source is the card itself (`Self`).

The where-clause resolves X inline to the computed amount (the same "X is …" inlining `ModifyPTByDieResultTriggeredRule` performs). "N minus the number of cards in their hand" is a binary subtraction between two full quantities — a `LiteralQuantity` N as the minuend and a `CountQuantity` over the opponent's hand as the subtrahend — carried by `CalculatedQuantity` with `Operation="subtract"` and the second operand in `OperandQuantity` (the scalar `Operand` cannot hold a game-state count). The hand-count filter `{ card, Owner=ThatPlayer, Zone=Hand }` mirrors the intervening-if filter Prickle Faeries uses for the identical "cards in their hand" concept.

CR 603.2: the event-match (the opponent's upkeep beginning) is the trigger. The damage is dealt by the source to that player (CR 120.1–120.2). Amount is engine territory at resolution (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004): MAST records the "N minus hand-size" reference, not a pre-resolved number (and it may be zero or less — the engine floors damage at 0 per CR 120.6).

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the variable "X damage … where X is N minus the number of cards in … hand" shape is disjoint from the literal-amount `SelfDealsDamageToThatPlayerRule` (which requires a numeric amount immediately before "damage" and ends right after the recipient), so the two never collide. Priority above default so the more-specific variable form is tried first.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfDealsThreeMinusHandDamageToThatPlayerRule.cs)

### `SelfOrAnotherArtifactEntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"[CardName] or another artifact you control enters" — self-by-name disjunction enters trigger on artifacts. The oracle pattern "X or another artifact you control enters" means the trigger fires when ANY artifact the controller controls enters — including the source card itself (named in the "X" half) and any other artifact.

This is the artifact-type analogue of the creature disjunction handled in `ParseObjectFilter` (the Blood Artist shape: "this creature or another creature"). The correct filter is artifact + Controller=You, with NO ExcludeSelf (the disjunction explicitly includes the source). Setting ExcludeSelf = true would be rules-wrong: the card itself does trigger the ability when it enters.

Example: Gonti's Aether Heart — "Whenever Gonti's Aether Heart or another artifact you control enters, you get {E}{E}."

Rule 603.1: triggered abilities use "when", "whenever", or "at" to watch for events. Rule 603.2: the trigger fires each time the condition is met. Rule 107.14: energy counters ({E}) are a player resource.

ANCHOR: the pattern is anchored (^...$) and requires "or another artifact you control" to prevent collision with the generic EntersConditionRule on simpler artifact triggers. Runs at Priority 992 — above EntersConditionRule (990) and AnotherSubtypeEntersConditionRule (995), below the most-specific rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfOrAnotherArtifactEntersConditionRule.cs)

### `SelfOrAnotherNontokenSubtypeEntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"[CardName] or another nontoken [Subtype] you control enters" — a self-by-name disjunction enters trigger on a creature subtype. The oracle pattern "X or another nontoken [Subtype] you control enters" fires when ANY nontoken permanent of the named creature subtype the controller controls enters — INCLUDING the source card itself, which is named in the "X" half of the disjunction. Because the source's own entry triggers the ability, the filter must be SELF-INCLUSIVE: NO `ExcludeSelf` is set.

This is the enters/subtype analogue of the dies-side disjunction guard in `ParseObjectFilter` (Anax, Hardened in the Forge — "Whenever Anax or another nontoken creature you control dies") and of `SelfOrAnotherArtifactEntersConditionRule` (Gonti's Aether Heart — "Whenever Gonti's Aether Heart or another artifact you control enters"). All three share the same rule: a self-name disjunction is self-inclusive, so the bare-"another" ExcludeSelf convention (CR 109.5) does NOT apply here.

Paradigm card: Arahbo, the First Fang — "Whenever Arahbo or another nontoken Cat you control enters, create a 1/1 white Cat creature token." Arahbo's own entry triggers the ability.

The filter is CardTypes=creature + Subtypes=[Subtype] + IsToken=false + Controller=You (CR 111: tokens are not cards, so "nontoken" restricts to IsToken=false; Rule 205.3m: the capitalised word is a creature subtype). CR 603.1: triggered abilities use "when"/"whenever"/"at" to watch for events. CR 603.2: the trigger fires each time the condition is met.

ANCHOR: the pattern is anchored (^...$) and requires the literal "or another nontoken [Capitalised Subtype] you control enters" tail — the leading ".+" absorbs the timing keyword and the self-name half. A plain "X or another nontoken creature you control enters" (lowercase "creature", no proper-noun subtype) is NOT matched here — the subtype capture requires a capital initial — and is instead handled by `EntersConditionRule` via ParseObjectFilter's own nontoken-creature disjunction guard, so this rule does not collide with that shape. Runs at Priority 996 — above the generic `EntersConditionRule` (990) and the subtype-enters rules so the more specific self-inclusive-nontoken shape wins.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfOrAnotherNontokenSubtypeEntersConditionRule.cs)

### `SelfPutIntoGraveyardFromAnywhereConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"[Self-name] is put into a graveyard from anywhere" — the self-referential zone-change trigger of the Future Sight anti-mill family (Dread, Guile, Hostility, Purity, Vigor, Worldspine Wurm, Serra Avatar). The card names itself and triggers when it lands in a graveyard from ANY zone, not just the battlefield (so this is broader than `Dies`).

Maps to `PutIntoGraveyard` with a self filter (`CardTypes = ["creature"]`, `IsSelf = true`). The "creature" type is a DEFAULT for this layer (no type line here); a non-creature self-by-name is retyped downstream by SelfReferenceTypeCorrector in CardParser (CR 201.5) — the same convention `ParseObjectFilter` uses for the "[Self-name] dies/enters" shapes. IsSelf marks the source-self distinction the interaction operator gates (an arbitrary card put into a graveyard is not provably the source).

Distinct from `DiesConditionRule`: "dies" / "is put into a graveyard from the battlefield" (CR 700.4) is the battlefield→graveyard event mapped to `Dies`; "from anywhere" omits the source-zone restriction (hand, library, stack, exile, battlefield) and so is the broader `PutIntoGraveyard` event. Distinct from `PutIntoGraveyardConditionRule`, which recognises the "[type] cards are put into your graveyard from anywhere" batch form (The Gitrog Monster) with a type/controller filter rather than a self-by-name subject.

Rule citations: CR 603.6 (zone-change triggers), CR 700.4 (dies = battlefield→graveyard, the contrast), CR 404.1 (graveyard zone), CR 201.5 (a card naming itself is a self-reference).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SelfPutIntoGraveyardFromAnywhereConditionRule.cs)

### `SetCardTypesTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"It's an enchantment." / "It's a creature." / "It's a land." — a layer-4 (CR 613.1d) card-type declaration sentence that sets the subject's card types. Typically follows a return-to-battlefield sentence to declare the returned permanent's new type (e.g. Enduring Tenacity: "… return it to the battlefield under its owner's control. It's an enchantment.").

"It" is the generic anaphoric pronoun (CR 113.8b) back-referencing the triggering object — the same object named by the preceding effect sentence. MAST models it as `It` on the `Subject` field.

CR 613.1d: "Layer 4: Type-changing effects are applied." An "It's an X" oracle sentence sets the object's card types to the declared set, removing any types not listed (e.g. removing the creature type from a creature/enchantment). The parenthetical "(It's not a creature.)" is a clarifying reminder printed by WotC for card types that lose creature status; it is not a separate effect and is stripped by the reminder-extraction pass before this rule fires. This rule handles the imperative declaration that remains.

CR 205.2 (card types list); CR 613.1d (type-changing layers); CR 113.8b ("it" pronoun reference).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SetCardTypesTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ShuffleSelfIntoLibraryTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"shuffle it into its owner's library" — the resolution effect of the Future Sight anti-mill family (Dread, Guile, Hostility, Purity, Vigor, Worldspine Wurm, Serra Avatar). The trigger fires when the source is put into a graveyard (see `SelfPutIntoGraveyardFromAnywhereConditionRule`); on resolution the source is shuffled back into its owner's library so it can't be milled out.

"it" is the trigger subject — the source permanent/card itself — so this maps to a `ShuffleIntoLibraryEffect` with `Self`, identical in shape to the spell-side self-shuffle (`ShuffleSelfIntoLibraryRule`, e.g. Beacon of Immortality). The owner-shuffles mechanic is an inherent part of the zone change (CR 701.24).

Anchored ^…$ to match only the bare "shuffle it into its owner's library" effect clause and not a substring of a broader sentence. Reuses the existing `ShuffleIntoLibraryEffect` discriminator (no new effect node).

Rule citations: CR 701.24 (Shuffle — its own example is this exact family text: "When Guile is put into a graveyard from anywhere, shuffle it into its owner's library."), CR 603.2 (triggered-ability resolution).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ShuffleSelfIntoLibraryTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SourceDealsDamageToThatCreaturesControllerTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"[this source] deals N damage to that creature's controller" — the literal-amount resolution of a "whenever a creature dies" (or other creature-naming) trigger (Dingus Staff: "Whenever a creature dies, this artifact deals 2 damage to that creature's controller."). The source is the permanent itself (`Self` — "this artifact"/"this creature"/…); the target is the player who controls the creature named by the trigger condition, encoded as `Controller` (the same "that creature's controller" modeling used by `DealThatMuchDamageToControllerRule`).

The dealt damage is NONCOMBAT damage (CR 120): a triggered ability resolving and dealing damage, not combat damage assigned during the combat damage step (CR 510), so `IsCombat` is left null (≡ noncombat) and omitted from the JSON.

Distinct from `DealThatMuchDamageToControllerRule` (amount is the "that much" derived quantity of a Repercussion redirection) — here the amount is a literal number stated in the effect text. Distinct from `ThisCreatureDealsDamageToThatCreatureTriggeredRule` (target is the creature itself, `ThatCreature`) — here the target is that creature's <em>controller</em>, a player.

CR 700.4: "The term dies means 'is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.'" CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. … An object that deals damage is the source of that damage." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." MAST describes; the "that creature's controller" back-reference is a linked reference (ADR 0004), not a threaded binding.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SourceDealsDamageToThatCreaturesControllerTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SourceDealsDamageToThatLandsControllerTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"[this source] deals N damage to that land's controller" — the literal-amount resolution of a "whenever a land enters" (or other land-naming) trigger (Ankh of Mishra: "Whenever a land enters, this artifact deals 2 damage to that land's controller."). The source is the permanent itself (`Self` — "this artifact"/"this creature"/…); the target is the player who controls the land named by the trigger condition, encoded as `Controller` (the same "that … 's controller" modeling used by `SourceDealsDamageToThatCreaturesControllerTriggeredRule` and `DealThatMuchDamageToControllerRule`). The possessive noun ("land") merely restates the object the trigger identified; it is inert to the output, which is why this rule emits the identical shape as the creature sibling.

The dealt damage is NONCOMBAT damage (CR 120): a triggered ability resolving and dealing damage, not combat damage assigned during the combat damage step (CR 510), so `IsCombat` is left null (≡ noncombat) and omitted from the JSON.

Disjoint from `SourceDealsDamageToThatCreaturesControllerTriggeredRule` (matches "that creature's controller") by the possessive noun, so the two rules never both match the same fragment. Both are anchored (^…$) to the full effect tail so neither can swallow a more-specific sibling ("… to that player", "… to that creature", or a trailing "and you gain N life").

CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players. … An object that deals damage is the source of that damage." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." MAST describes; the "that land's controller" back-reference is a linked reference (ADR 0004), not a threaded binding.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SourceDealsDamageToThatLandsControllerTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SourceDealsNoncombatDamageConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever a source you control deals noncombat damage to an opponent" — noncombat-damage trigger gated to sources the controller owns (CR 609.7: a source is any object, spell, or ability that deals damage; CR 510.1: combat damage is dealt only in the Combat Damage Step). Emits `NoncombatDamageDealt`.

The filter records `CardTypes = ["source"]` with `Controller = You`: "source" is the CR 609.7 rules term for any damage-dealing entity that a player controls, modelled as a CardTypes singleton so it is structurally parallel to "a creature you control" and "a permanent you control" filters.

Runs at priority 986 — above `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule` (985) and `DealsDamageConditionRule` (984) — so "deals noncombat damage" is claimed before those rules consume the more-general "deals damage" surface.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SourceDealsNoncombatDamageConditionRule.cs)

### `SpellCastConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you cast a spell" / "Whenever an opponent casts a spell" / "Whenever you cast a spell that's white, blue, black, or red" / etc. Encodes the caster and any inline spell-color/type qualifiers on the filter.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SpellCastConditionRule.cs)

### `SubtypeCreatureEntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"a [Subtype] creature enters" — an unqualified creature-subtype ETB trigger, with no "you control"/"another" qualifier, so it watches ANY entering creature of the named subtype regardless of controller (Rule 603.2: a game event matching the trigger event triggers the ability).

Paradigm card: Cloak and Dagger — "Whenever a Rogue creature enters, you may attach this Equipment to it." The trigger doesn't restrict to creatures "you control", so any Rogue entering (yours or an opponent's) fires it.

Distinct from `SubtypeEntersConditionRule` (requires "you control" and omits the "creature" type word — e.g. "a Cartouche you control enters") and from `AnotherSubtypeEntersConditionRule` (requires "another" + "you control"). Here both the card-type word "creature" and the subtype are present, and there's no controller qualifier at all.

Runs at priority 991 — above the generic `EntersConditionRule` (990), whose `ParseObjectFilter` only recognises the bare "a creature" substring and would otherwise silently drop the subtype (since "a Rogue creature" does not contain the literal substring "a creature").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SubtypeCreatureEntersConditionRule.cs)
