### `SubtypeDealsCombatDamageToCreatureConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever a [Subtype] deals combat damage to a creature" — the subtype-subject variant of the deals-combat-damage-to-a-creature trigger (Toxin Sliver: "Whenever a Sliver deals combat damage to a creature, …"). The subject is any creature of the named subtype, so the Filter carries `Subtypes` = [subtype].

Sits ABOVE `DealsCombatDamageToCreatureConditionRule` (Priority 986), whose `ParseObjectFilter` path would otherwise grab the recipient "a creature" and silently drop the subtype constraint. This rule is anchored to the "a &lt;ProperNounSubtype&gt; deals combat damage to a creature" surface (case-sensitive on the subtype so lowercase type words like "creature" cannot match), mirroring `AnotherSubtypeEntersConditionRule`'s subtype-capture convention (Rule 205.3m — creature subtypes are capitalised in oracle text). Self-by-name subjects ("Whenever Phage deals combat damage …") carry no "a"/"an" article and so fall through to the self-by-name path unchanged.

CR 510.1 (Combat Damage Step): combat damage assignment is the game event. CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." The recipient class (a creature) is implied by `DealsCombatDamageToCreature`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SubtypeDealsCombatDamageToCreatureConditionRule.cs)

### `SubtypeDealtDamageConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"a [Subtype] you control is dealt damage" — a subtype-filtered damage-receipt trigger keyed on the indefinite article "a"/"an" rather than "this". The triggering object is some permanent you control sharing the named subtype (not necessarily the ability's own source), so the filter carries the subtype on the Subtypes axis with a You controller restriction, mirroring how `SubtypeEntersConditionRule` handles "a [Subtype] you control enters" for the Enters event.

Wrathful Red Dragon: "Whenever a Dragon you control is dealt damage, it deals that much damage to any target that isn't a Dragon." The subject need not be Wrathful Red Dragon itself — any Dragon you control qualifies — so the paired effect resolves "it" as `It` (the previously mentioned triggering object), not `Self`.

CR 120.1: "Objects can deal damage to battles, creatures, planeswalkers, and players." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." This is the subtype-indefinite sibling of `CreatureDealtDamageConditionRule` (generic "a creature is dealt damage") and `SelfCreatureDealtDamageConditionRule` ("this creature is dealt damage"); higher priority than both so the named-subtype reading wins whenever the oracle text names a proper-noun subtype instead of the plain word "creature".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SubtypeDealtDamageConditionRule.cs)

### `SubtypeEntersConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"a [Subtype] you control enters" — a subtype-filtered enters trigger keyed on the indefinite article "a"/"an" rather than "another". The triggering object is some OTHER permanent (not this card) that shares the named subtype; the subtype is the most precise type word the oracle text gives, so the filter carries it on the Subtypes axis with no CardTypes constraint. Rule 603.6a: enters-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield, written "When [this object] enters, ..." or "Whenever a [type] enters, ...". Rule 603.2: when a game event matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers. This is distinct from a this-object ETB trigger (handled by `EntersConditionRule` via the "this [type]" self-reference) and from the creature-subtype "another [Subtype] you control enters" shape (`AnotherSubtypeEntersConditionRule`, which keys on "another" and pins CardTypes to creature). Here the subtype may be any permanent subtype — e.g. the Aura subtype Cartouche — so no card-type is asserted. Examples: "When a Cartouche you control enters, ..." Sits just below `EntersConditionRule` (Priority 990) so the generic enters recogniser gets first refusal on plainer shapes ("a creature you control enters", "this enchantment enters"); this rule only fires once that generic recogniser has declined, then narrows on the proper- noun subtype.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SubtypeEntersConditionRule.cs)

### `SubtypeListPumpTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"[SubtypeA], [SubtypeB], [SubtypeC], and [SubtypeD] you control get +N/+N until end of turn." Handles the multi-subtype tribal pump pattern: a comma-and-"and"-joined list of creature subtypes that the controller's creatures of those types get a temporary P/T boost. The "you control" controller filter is required. Covers both two-item ("[A] and [B] you control") and three-or-more-item ("[A], [B], and [C] you control") forms.

The subtypes list uses OR semantics on the `Subtypes` axis (a creature qualifies if it has ANY of the listed subtypes — CR 205.3m). The boost is recorded as a `ModifyPTEffect` with `Duration` = `untilTime{Turn, End}`.

Rule 613.1c (Layer 6, ability-granting effects) and 613.4c (Layer 7c, P/T-modification effects): temporary boosts are layer-7c continuous effects. CR 205.3m: creature subtypes list.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SubtypeListPumpTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SubtypePutIntoGraveyardConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Recognises the "a [Subtype] is put into a graveyard from the battlefield" trigger condition — the longform "dies" trigger (CR 700.4) qualified by an artifact subtype rather than a card type (e.g. "Food", "Treasure", "Blood", "Clue").

CR 700.4 (verbatim): "The word 'dies' means 'is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.'" Subtype-qualified dies triggers fire on the same event as creature dies triggers, but the filter names an artifact subtype (e.g. Food, CR 111.10b) rather than the card type "creature". MAST maps to `Dies` because the zone-change is identical; the filter carries `Subtypes` to record the named subtype faithfully.

Canonical card: Ygra, Eater of All (BLB) — "Whenever a Food is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, put two +1/+1 counters on Ygra." CR 700.4 (Dies = put into graveyard from battlefield). CR 111.10b (Food token is a colorless Food artifact token).

Priority 993 — above `DiesConditionRule` (991) and above `NontokenCreatureToGraveyardFromBattlefieldConditionRule` (992) so this more-specific subtype-qualified shape fires before the generic "dies" fallback. Anchored pattern prevents substring matches against longer, more-specific siblings.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SubtypePutIntoGraveyardConditionRule.cs)

### `SubtypeSpellCastConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you cast an Eldrazi spell" / "Whenever you cast a Zombie spell" — the subtype-qualified spell-cast condition family. The subtype is a creature subtype (Rule 205.3m), NOT a card type, so it lands on `Subtypes` while the card type remains `"spell"`.

Sits above `SpellCastConditionRule` (priority 998) so the subtype qualifier is captured first. `CastAuraSpellConditionRule` (priority 1001) handles the Aura enchantment-subtype specifically; this rule handles all other subtypes and sits between them at priority 1000.

CR 205.3m: subtypes appear after the em-dash on the type line and are distinct from the broad card types. "An Eldrazi spell" is a spell whose subtype includes "Eldrazi".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SubtypeSpellCastConditionRule.cs)

### `SubtypeYouControlDealsCombatDamageToPlayerConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever a [Subtype] you control deals combat damage to a player" — the subtype-subject variant of the deals-combat-damage-to-a-player trigger (Ingenious Infiltrator: "Whenever a Ninja you control deals combat damage to a player, …"). The subject is any creature of the named subtype under the controller's control, so the Filter carries `Subtypes` = [subtype] and `Controller` = You.

Sits ABOVE `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule` (Priority 985) so the subtype constraint is captured before that rule's generic `ParseObjectFilter` path is tried (which has no "a &lt;Subtype&gt; you control" branch and would fall through to null). Mirrors `SubtypeDealsCombatDamageToCreatureConditionRule`'s subtype-capture convention (Rule 205.3m — creature subtypes are capitalised in oracle text) and `OneOrMoreSubtypeDealsDamageToOpponentsConditionRule`'s "you control" possessive handling, but for the singular "a &lt;Subtype&gt;" subject with the "deals" (not "deal") verb form and the "to a player" recipient.

ANCHORED (^…$) against the full trigger clause (after the timing-word strip) so this rule matches ONLY the exact "a &lt;Subtype&gt; you control deals combat damage to a player" surface — case-sensitive on the subtype (leading capital) so "a creature you control deals combat damage to a player" does NOT match here and instead falls through to `DealsCombatDamageConditionRule`.

CR 510 (Combat Damage Step): combat damage assignment is the game event. CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SubtypeYouControlDealsCombatDamageToPlayerConditionRule.cs)

### `SupportTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"support N" — Rule 701.41 keyword action on the triggered side.

Rule 701.41a: "\"Support N\" on a permanent means \"Put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to N other target creatures.\"" This rule covers the permanent form (the "other" variant); a permanent's "support N" never targets itself.

The keyword action is unpacked into its literal meaning per the rule (MAST describes what the keyword says, not how it resolves): a single +1/+1 counter placed on each of an up-to-N choice of OTHER target creatures. The "up to N" is the multiplicity of the target reference (Rule 115.1 — "up to N target"), not the per-target counter count, which is one. Hence `Count` is the literal 1 and the "up to N" lives on the reference's `Quantity`.

The reminder text "(Put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to two other target creatures.)" has already been stripped by the dispatcher before this rule is called, so the matched fragment is the bare "support N".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SupportTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SurveilTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"surveil N." and "you may surveil N." — Rule 701.42 keyword action on the triggered side. The "you may" prefix produces an optional `SurveilEffect` (IsOptional = true).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SurveilTriggeredRule.cs)

### `SyrKonradTripleOrConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Compound triple-OR trigger for Syr Konrad, the Grim (ELD): "Whenever another creature dies, or a creature card is put into a graveyard from anywhere other than the battlefield, or a creature card leaves your graveyard, …"

This is a single triggered ability with THREE disjoint firing events (CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event … matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers"):

Primary: another creature dies (Dies event, ExcludeSelf filter). Secondary: a creature card is put into a graveyard from anywhere other than the battlefield (PutIntoGraveyard event — covers hand/library/exile/stack origins; the "other than battlefield" restriction distinguishes it from the Dies clause which already covers battlefield→graveyard transitions via CR 700.4). Tertiary: a creature card leaves your graveyard (LeavesGraveyard event, Controller=You — covers cards removed from graveyard by any means).

The primary condition is returned normally; the secondary is signalled via `AdditionalTrigger`'s normal single-pending mechanism (piggy-backed on `PendingAdditionalTrigger` — we use our own static field here to avoid coupling). The tertiary is stored in `PendingAdditionalTriggers` so `TriggeredAbilityParser` can populate `AdditionalTriggers` (the list form introduced for 3+ events).

CR 700.4 (verbatim): "The term dies means 'is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.'" CR 603.2 (verbatim): "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." CR 701.17a (verbatim, mill): "For a player to mill a number of cards, that player puts that many cards from the top of their library into their graveyard."

Priority 998 — must fire before the generic `DiesConditionRule` (991) or `PutIntoGraveyardConditionRule` (985) see the first clause in isolation.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/SyrKonradTripleOrConditionRule.cs)

### `TakeExtraTurnTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Take an extra turn after this one." — schedules an additional full turn for the ability's controller when used as a triggered effect.

CR 500.7: "Some effects can give a player extra turns. They do this by adding the turns directly after the specified turn." MAST records the verb and player reference; the turn-ordering bookkeeping is engine territory.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TakeExtraTurnTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TakeInitiativeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you take the initiative." — Rule 726. The player takes the initiative game-state designation. Parameterless; mirrors AscendEffect doctrine.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TakeInitiativeRule.cs)

### `TapAllTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"tap all [color]? [type]s [you control]?" — mass-tap triggered effect. Covers patterns such as:

"tap all red creatures" (Wrath of Marit Lage) "tap all lands you control" "tap all creatures"

Produces a `TapEffect` whose Target is `Each` filtered to the named card type, with an optional `Colors` constraint when a color qualifier precedes the type noun, and with `You` when "you control" is present (or no controller filter otherwise, e.g. "tap all creatures"). Mirrors `UntapAllTriggeredRule` (the untap sibling of this exact template) plus the color axis, parallel to how `SubjectDoesntUntapDuringControllersUntapStepsRule` keys "Red creatures don't untap..." with the same Colors + CardTypes combination (CR 105 "Destroy target green or white creature." precedent). Rule 701.26 (Tap and Untap).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TapAllTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TapAndFreezeBackReferenceTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Single-sentence "tap then freeze" back-reference effect, as it appears on the resolution half of a triggered ability: "tap that creature and it doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step." (Kashi-Tribe Warriors — the combat-damage-to-a-creature trigger family).

Two conjoined instructions on one sentence: a `TapEffect` on the back-referenced creature ("that creature") and a `DoesntUntapEffect` on that same creature ("it"). Both back-references resolve to `It` — the creature the trigger condition just named (the one dealt combat damage). The pair is wrapped in a single `CompositeEffect`, matching the single-sentence-conjunction convention already used on the triggered side (`EtbTeamPumpTriggeredRule` for "get +N/+M and gain &lt;keyword&gt;").

CR 502.3 (Untap Step): "Third, the active player determines which permanents they control will untap. Then they untap them all simultaneously... Normally, all of a player's permanents untap, but effects can keep one or more of a player's permanents from untapping." The "next untap step" wording is recorded on `WhoseUntapStep` as "its controller's next".

Mirrors `TapAndFreezeRule` (the two-sentence spell form, "Tap target creature. It doesn't untap...") but covers the one-sentence "and"-joined back-reference form that surfaces in triggered-ability resolution text, where the creature is not re-targeted.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TapAndFreezeBackReferenceTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TapEnchantedTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"tap enchanted [type]" — Aura enters-the-battlefield tap effect. Fires when an Aura's triggered ability instructs it to tap the enchanted permanent. The target is always the permanent the Aura is attached to, modelled as `EnchantedOrEquipped`. Rule 701.26 (Tap and Untap); Rule 303.4 (Aura attachment).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TapEnchantedTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TapForManaConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

Trigger condition for "tap a [nonland] permanent for [mana/{C}]" shapes. Handles two variants:

Specific-symbol: "you tap a permanent for {C}" (Forsaken Monument) — the produced mana symbol is recorded in `ProducedMana`. Controller: You when "you tap"; Any when "a player taps". Any-mana: "you tap a nonland permanent for mana" (Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy) — the trigger fires on any mana production by tapping a nonland permanent. No specific symbol is recorded (`ProducedMana` is null). The nonland qualifier is expressed as `ExcludedCardTypes: ["land"]` on the filter. Enchanted-subject (passive): "enchanted land is tapped for mana" (Fertile Ground, Wild Growth, Glittering Frost, Market Festival — the mana-doubler Aura family). The triggering object is the enchanted land itself, modeled as `IsEnchanted: true` with the named card type. No specific symbol is recorded (`ProducedMana` is null) — the trigger fires for any mana the enchanted land produces. Land any-mana: "a player taps a land for mana" (Dictate of Karametra) — the trigger fires on any mana production by ANY player tapping a land (`CardTypes: ["land"]`, no nonland exclusion — the mirror-image of the Kinnan nonland-permanent variant above). No specific symbol is recorded (`ProducedMana` is null). Controller: You when "you tap"; Any when "a player taps". Creature any-mana: "you tap a creature for mana" (Leyline of Abundance) — the trigger fires on any mana production by tapping a creature (`CardTypes: ["creature"]`). No specific symbol is recorded (`ProducedMana` is null) — the mirror-image of the Dictate of Karametra land variant above, for creatures rather than lands. Controller: You when "you tap"; Any when "a player taps". Subtype-land any-mana: "you tap a Swamp for mana" (Nirkana Revenant) — narrows the land any-mana variant above to a single named land subtype (`CardTypes: ["land"]` + `Subtypes: [word]`, mirroring the land-subtype filter shape used by `TapSingularSubtypeCostRule`). No specific symbol is recorded (`ProducedMana` is null). Controller: You when "you tap"; Any when "a player taps".

CR 106.12: "To 'tap [a permanent] for mana' is to activate a mana ability of that permanent that includes the {T} symbol in its activation cost." CR 603.2: the event-match (the enchanted land being tapped for mana) is the trigger. This rule encodes the trigger that fires when that mana-tap occurs.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TapForManaConditionRule.cs)

### `TapSelfRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"tap this creature" / "tap this permanent" / "tap it" — the plain self-tap triggered effect (Rule 701.26, Tap and Untap). Fleshmad Steed: "Whenever another creature dies, tap this creature."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TapSelfRule.cs)

### `TapSelfUnlessPayLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"tap this [permanent-noun] unless you pay N life" — the upkeep-tap-tax pattern (Carnophage, Sewer Rats, Wall of Vipers, and other black one-drops). The "unless you pay" gate is a cost-or-consequence: the source is tapped (Rule 701.26a — Tap: "To tap a permanent, turn it sideways from an upright position.") unless its controller chooses to pay the stated life cost, and paying a cost is never automatic (Rule 118.5 — "it's not automatically paid").

Oracle text split by `TriggeredAbilityParser`: trigger = "At the beginning of your upkeep" effect = "tap this creature unless you pay 1 life"

The self-noun varies by the card's type — "this creature", "this permanent", "this artifact", "this enchantment", "this Aura" — all name the same object: the source bearing the ability (Rule 109.2 — self-reference). The noun is descriptive type-flavour and carries no AST distinction, so the pattern accepts the full set and the produced shape is identical regardless of which noun was printed. MAST models the reference as `Self`, matching `SacrificeSelfUnlessPayRule`.

Produces a `TapEffect` with Target = Self wrapped in a `PreventableEffect` whose `UnlessClause` Player is You and Cost is a `PayLifeCost` for the stated amount. Mirrors `SacrificeSelfUnlessPayRule` on the tap side.

Rule citations: 701.26a (Tap), 118.5 (paying a cost is not automatic).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TapSelfUnlessPayLifeRule.cs)

### `TapUntapTargetTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Triggered-ability rule for tap, untap, and tap-or-untap effects on a named target. Covers three surface patterns:

"tap target [filter]" → `TapEffect` "untap target [filter]" → `UntapEffect` "(you may) tap or untap target [filter]" → `TapOrUntapEffect`

The filter phrase may be a single card type ("creature") or a disjunction ("artifact or creature", "creature or land", "artifact, creature, or land"). Rule 701.26 (Tap and Untap).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TapUntapTargetTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TargetControllerCantBlockThisTurnTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Triggered-ability effect shape "target [filter] [controller-clause] can't block this turn." — the controller-scoped sibling of `CantBlockThisTurnTriggeredRule`, which only recognizes an unqualified filter (e.g. "target creature can't block this turn"). Here the target's controller axis is pinned by a trailing possessive clause, e.g. Smelt-Ward Minotaur: "Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell, target creature an opponent controls can't block this turn." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers." The trigger ("Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell") is parsed separately; this rule recognizes only the post-comma effect body. CR 509.1 (declare-blockers step): "First, the defending player declares blockers. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack. … If at any point during the declaration of blockers, the defending player is unable to comply with any of the steps listed below, the declaration is illegal…" A "can't block" effect is a blocker-side restriction applied during this step; the "this turn" qualifier makes it durative (expires at end of turn). Maps to `CantBlockEffect` with a `Target` whose `Controller` records the controller clause, and `Duration` = end of turn. Anchored (^…$) so it never claims the unqualified surface owned by `CantBlockThisTurnTriggeredRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TargetControllerCantBlockThisTurnTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureGainsChoiceOfKeywordsUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"target creature gains your choice of &lt;kw1&gt; or &lt;kw2&gt;[ or …] until end of turn." — a triggered-ability effect clause that grants the target creature one of several keyword abilities, the controller's choice at resolution (Éowyn, Lady of Rohan: "…target creature gains your choice of first strike or vigilance until end of turn.").

The "your choice of X or Y" is modelled as a `ModalEffect` with `ChooseOne` and one `ModalOption` per keyword — the same modal primitive used for "create a Food token or a Treasure token" (Tireless Provisioner). Each option is a `SpellAbility` whose single `GainAbilityEffect` grants the keyword to the chosen target creature (`Target`) with an "until end of turn" duration (CR 611.1). CR 700.2 (modal): the mode is the controller's choice; MAST records the alternatives, the engine resolves the pick (ADR 0004).

Anchored (^…$) and requires the exact "target creature gains your choice of …" subject — the "you control" / named-subtype variants (Steel Seraph, Manifold Mouse, Atraxa's Skitterfang) carry different subject tokens and do not match. Distinct from `TargetCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` (a single fixed keyword, no choice). Any unrecognised keyword option causes a bail (returns false) so the clause falls through rather than being guessed at.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TargetCreatureGainsChoiceOfKeywordsUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"target creature gains [keyword] until end of turn." — grants a keyword ability to a chosen target creature for the remainder of the turn. Covers Soaring Seacliff's ETB trigger effect clause: "target creature gains flying until end of turn." Rule 603.1: triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect; this rule handles the effect clause. Rule 115.1: "target creature" requires a chosen target, modelled as `Target` (CR 115.1 example: "target creature gets -1/-1 until end of turn" is a targeted triggered ability). Rule 611.1: the keyword grant is a continuous effect with a duration — "until end of turn" is the fixed duration. Distinct from `ItGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule`, which grants the keyword to the anaphoric "it" (the object named by the trigger's own filter), not a separately chosen target.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TargetCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `TargetCreatureYouControlGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"target creature you control gains [keyword] until end of turn." — grants a keyword ability to a chosen target creature under the trigger controller's control, for the remainder of the turn. Covers Dinotomaton's ETB trigger effect clause: "target creature you control gains menace until end of turn." CR 115.1: "target creature" requires a chosen target; the "you control" qualifier restricts the legal targets to creatures controlled by the ability's controller, modelled on `Target` via `Controller` = `You`. CR 611.1: the keyword grant is a continuous effect with a duration — "until end of turn" is the fixed duration. Distinct from `TargetCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule`, which matches the bare "target creature gains ..." (no controller qualifier) and would otherwise falsely match this text's "creature" as its whole subject were "you control" not anchored between "creature" and "gains" in this rule's own pattern. CR 702.111 "Menace"; 702.111a "Menace is an evasion ability."; 702.111b "A creature with menace can't be blocked except by two or more creatures. (See rule 509, "Declare Blockers Step.")"; 702.111c "Multiple instances of menace on the same creature are redundant."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TargetCreatureYouControlGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `TargetOpponentDiscardsTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"target opponent discards [a/N] card[s]" as the effect clause of a triggered ability — the Invasion of Eldraine ETB shape ("When this Siege enters, target opponent discards two cards"). The discarder is a targeted opponent (CR 115.1 — "target" in oracle text creates a targeting requirement); the count is the literal quantity of cards moved from hand to graveyard (CR 701.9a: "To discard a card, move it from its owner's hand to that player's graveyard"). CR 603.2: the event-match (the Siege entering) is the trigger.

The spell-speed sibling for this surface is `DiscardTargetPlayerRule` ("Target opponent discards two cards." as a standalone spell effect); this rule is the triggered-side counterpart, dispatched after the trigger/effect split has peeled the "When this Siege enters," prefix. The all-opponents variant is `EachOpponentDiscardsRule`; this rule is the single-targeted-opponent shape, so the Player reference is `Target` filtered to "opponent" rather than `EachOpponent`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TargetOpponentDiscardsTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TargetOpponentExilesCardFromHandTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"target opponent exiles a card from their hand" as the effect clause of a triggered ability — the Skullcap Snail / Unscrupulous Agent ETB shape ("When this creature enters, target opponent exiles a card from their hand") and the cast-trigger sibling (Kyoki, Sanity's Eclipse: "Whenever you cast a Spirit or Arcane spell, target opponent exiles a card from their hand").

The targeted opponent moves one card from their own hand to exile. Because the hand is a hidden zone (CR 108.3 — hand membership is by ownership), the card is not itself a legal target: the "target" keyword (CR 115.1) creates a targeting requirement on the OPPONENT, and that opponent — the card's owner — chooses which card. This is the exile analogue of a self-chosen discard, but the card is moved to exile (CR 701.13a — "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is") rather than the graveyard, so it is an `ExileEffect` and not a `DiscardCardsEffect`.

Following the convention already committed for "target opponent exiles [an indefinite object]" (the Azula, Cunning Usurper composite in `TriggeredAbilityParser.TryParseOpponentExileCreatureThenExileGraveyardCard` and the graveyard-hate `ExileTargetCardFromOpponentGraveyardTriggeredRule`), the exiled card is folded into `Target` with `Target` (carrying the targeting requirement) and its filter scoped by `Owner` = `Opponent` (whose card) + `Hand` (the source zone). No separate actor axis is added — the owner-scope + hidden zone already imply the opponent is the one who chooses and moves the card.

Anchored (^…$) so it fires only when the entire effect clause is this single-card hand exile, never as a substring of a longer composite a more-specific sibling should own: the "each opponent exiles a card from their hand …" broadcast forms (Yarok's Fenlurker, Lightstall Inquisitor — different subject and trailing permission clauses), the "at random" / "face down" variants, and the two-card "Witness the End" form all fail the anchor.

CR 701.13 (Exile) + CR 115.1 (target) + CR 108.3 (ownership).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TargetOpponentExilesCardFromHandTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TargetOpponentLosesLifeEqualToItsPowerRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"target opponent loses life equal to its power" — a leaves-the-battlefield (or other) trigger whose life-loss amount is derived from the triggering permanent's own power rather than a fixed number (Rapacious Guest: "When this creature leaves the battlefield, target opponent loses life equal to its power.").

CR 608.2h: when a triggered ability that triggers on a permanent leaving the battlefield needs information about that permanent, it uses the game state as it existed immediately before the permanent left — so "its power" refers to the leaving creature's last-known power. MAST records the reference descriptively (the pronoun antecedent), not the resolved value (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution), matching the existing "it" convention on `ItDealsDamageEqualToItsPowerToAnyTargetTriggeredRule`.

"Target opponent" is the targeted-opponent player reference — `Opponent` — matching the established convention for this exact phrase (`LoseLifeDerivedRule`, `TargetOpponentLosesHalfLifeRoundedUpRule`).

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." CR 120.1 (power as a characteristic used in a derived quantity).

Anchored (^…$) so this only matches the bare sentence, not a longer effect body this phrase might appear inside.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TargetOpponentLosesLifeEqualToItsPowerRule.cs)

### `TargetOpponentMayDrawElsePutCreatureFromHandRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"target opponent may have you draw a card. If they don't, you may put a creature card with equal or lesser toughness from your hand onto the battlefield." — Bane, Lord of Darkness's dies-trigger consequent, where a targeted opponent (not the controller) decides whether the controller draws a card, with a fallback battlefield-reanimation option scaled to the toughness of the creature that just died.

Decomposes as a nested `OptionalEffect`:

`Chooser` — "target opponent" (CR 115.1: "target" creates a targeting requirement) → `Target` filtered to `opponent`, mirroring `TargetOpponentDiscardsTriggeredRule`'s "target opponent" convention. This is load-bearing per `OptionalEffect`'s doc comment: the decider (the opponent) is distinct from the recipient of `Inner` (the controller, "you draw"). `Inner` — `DrawCardsEffect` for the controller (CR 121.1 — to draw a card is to move the top card of the library to hand); Player = You (the "have you draw" recipient, distinct from the Chooser). `IfYouDoNot` — a second, controller-optional ("you may") `OptionalEffect` wrapping a `PutFromHandOntoBattlefieldEffect`: "a creature card with equal or lesser toughness" restricts the filter with a `Comparison` relative to `ThatCreature` (the creature named by the enclosing dies-trigger's filter, CR 109.5/CR 603.2) — mirroring the relative-comparison convention used by `PowerComparison`/`ToughnessComparison` elsewhere (e.g. Mentor, CR 702.134).

Priority 95 — must run BEFORE `DrawCardsTriggeredRule` (default priority 50), which matches ANY text containing "draw a card" and would otherwise claim this two-sentence text and produce a bare, non-optional `drawCards` effect, silently dropping both the "target opponent" chooser and the entire "If they don't, …" fallback branch — the exact lossy-fallback failure mode `SacrificeAnotherCreatureDrawCardRule` guards against for its own sibling surface. Fully anchored (`^…$`) so it cannot fire on any other "target opponent may …" or "draw a card" clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TargetOpponentMayDrawElsePutCreatureFromHandRule.cs)

### `TargetPlayerLoseAndYouGainLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"target player loses N life and you gain N life" — Blood Artist / drain-on-death shape.

Distinct from `TryParseTargetOpponentLoseAndYouGainLife` (which requires "target opponent") — this rule handles the more general "target player" form, which allows targeting any player (including yourself). Blood Artist uses this phrasing because the drain applies to any chosen player, not constrained to an opponent.

The two effects (lose life, gain life) are wrapped in a `CompositeEffect` because `ITriggeredRule` returns a single `Effect`; the composite preserves both effects as structured children rather than collapsing to free text. CR 700.4: "The term dies means 'is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.'" CR 603.2 (triggered ability event matching).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TargetPlayerLoseAndYouGainLifeRule.cs)

### `TargetPlayerLosesLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"target player loses N life" — a bare targeted life-loss effect on a triggered ability, with no accompanying gain-life clause (Infectious Host: "When this creature dies, target player loses 2 life.").

Sibling of `TargetPlayerLoseAndYouGainLifeRule` (which requires the trailing "and you gain N life" conjunct, the Blood Artist drain shape) and `ThatPlayerLosesLifeRule` (which uses the anaphoric "that player" pronoun instead of an explicit "target player"). The anchored pattern ends immediately after "life", so it never matches the "and you gain" compound sentence handled by `TargetPlayerLoseAndYouGainLifeRule`.

CR 119.3 (verbatim): "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." CR 603.2 (triggered ability event matching).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TargetPlayerLosesLifeRule.cs)

### `TeamGainKeywordTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Creatures you control gain &lt;keyword&gt; until end of turn." — the bare team keyword-grant (no power/toughness modifier), as on the Rally/Ally rallying creatures (Chasm Guide, Ondu Champion).

Distinct from `EtbTeamPumpTriggeredRule`, which requires a leading "get +N/+M" P/T modifier. Here the whole resolution clause is a keyword grant: the entering creature grants the named keyword to the whole team for the turn. CR 611.1 — the grant is a continuous effect with a fixed duration (until end of turn).

The granted keyword is structured, not free text: each keyword resolves to a `GainAbilityEffect` whose `GainedAbility` is a `StaticAbility` carrying the keyword (mirroring the existing team-pump and modal grant golds — e.g. Flame-Kin Zealot, Savage Alliance). Multiple keywords joined by "and" each become their own grant effect, wrapped in a `CompositeEffect`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TeamGainKeywordTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ThassasOracleRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Recognises the Thassa's Oracle ETB effect: "Look at the top X cards of your library, where X is your devotion to blue. Put up to one of them on top of your library and the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order. If X is greater than or equal to the number of cards in your library, you win the game."

The whole three-sentence fragment is a single coherent game action: the variable X is defined in the first sentence and referenced by both the disposition sentence and the win-condition. Splitting on sentences would break the X-binding, so this rule captures all three sentences as one match and emits them as two structured effects:

`OracleTopLookEffect` — the look-and-reorder action. `ConditionalEffect` — the QuantityComparisonCondition → WinTheGameEffect gate.

CR 700.5 (devotion); CR 701.12 (look); CR 104.3a (you win the game).

Priority 95: must beat generic sentence-bundle dispatch and the plain LookAtTopCards rules.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThassasOracleRule.cs)

### `ThatCreatureDoesntUntapTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Standalone "freeze" back-reference effect on the resolution half of a triggered ability: "that creature doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step." (Cleric of Chill Depths — "Whenever this creature blocks a creature, that creature doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step.").

Unlike `TapAndFreezeBackReferenceTriggeredRule` ("tap that creature and it doesn't untap …", which pairs a tap with the freeze), this covers the lone doesn't-untap instruction with NO tap — the creature the trigger named is simply prevented from untapping. The back-reference "that creature" resolves to `ThatCreature` — the creature identified by the trigger's condition (CR 509.1, the creature this creature blocked), the same convention Inferno Elemental uses for "deals 3 damage to that creature".

CR 502.3 (Untap Step, verbatim): "Third, the active player determines which permanents they control will untap. Then they untap them all simultaneously. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack. Normally, all of a player's permanents untap, but effects can keep one or more of a player's permanents from untapping." The "next untap step" wording is recorded on `WhoseUntapStep` as "its controller's next".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatCreatureDoesntUntapTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ThatCreatureGetsPTTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that creature gets +N/+M [until end of turn]" — triggered P/T modification on the creature named by the trigger condition, not the ability's own source. Primal Forcemage: "Whenever another creature you control enters, that creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn." The subject "that creature" back-references the object the trigger's Filter identified (CR 603.2 — the triggering event names the object), mapping to `ThatCreature`. This is the sibling of the "it"/"this creature"/"target creature" subjects handled by `ModifyPTTriggeredRule`, which does not recognise "that creature".

The P/T buff itself is a continuous effect modifying characteristics (CR 611.1), carried as a `ModifyPTEffect` with an "until end of turn" `UntilTimeDuration` when the clock clause is present.

Anchored on the WHOLE fragment (^…$) so the more-specific siblings in this surface family are never mis-claimed: "…until end of turn instead" (replacement modifier), "…and gains &lt;keyword&gt; until end of turn" (composite pump + grant), "…for each …" (variable modifier), and "…and fights …" all carry trailing text past the P/T clause and therefore fail the anchor, falling through to their own handlers.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatCreatureGetsPTTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ThatCreatureIfEquippedGainsKeywordsInsteadRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"If that creature is equipped, it gains &lt;kw1&gt; and &lt;kw2&gt; until end of turn instead." — the equipped-override sentence of Éowyn, Lady of Rohan, paired with `TargetCreatureGainsChoiceOfKeywordsUntilEndOfTurnRule` (the preceding "your choice of …" default). When the previously-granted target creature ("that creature" / "it") is currently equipped, it instead gains BOTH named keywords for the turn.

Modelled as a `ConditionalEffect` gated on the new `ObjectIsEquippedCondition` (CR 702.6 — a creature with an Equipment attached is "equipped"), whose `Then` is a `CompositeEffect` of one `GainAbilityEffect` per keyword, each targeting the anaphoric "it" (`It`) with an "until end of turn" duration (CR 611.1). "and" (not "or") means both keywords are granted — a `CompositeEffect`, not a `ModalEffect`. The word "instead" is the replacement relationship the preceding default sentence's grant has when this condition holds; the two sentences are decomposed as two sibling effects by the triggered sentence-bundle splitter (functionally the union of the grants equals "both", so the flat decomposition preserves the end state).

Anchored (^…$); the literal "If that creature is equipped … instead" lead-in and tail make it disjoint from every other triggered effect shape.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatCreatureIfEquippedGainsKeywordsInsteadRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerAddsManaOfAnyTypeProducedRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player adds one mana of any type that land produced" — Dictate of Karametra mana-doubler shape. Distinct from the Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy shape handled by `AddManaRule` (bare "add one mana of any type that permanent produced", implicit "you" subject because Kinnan's trigger is "you tap [a nonland permanent]"): Dictate's trigger fires on "a player taps a land for mana" — ANY player, not just Dictate's controller — so its effect names an EXPLICIT "that player" subject to send the doubled mana to whichever player actually tapped the land, not to Dictate's controller. `ThatPlayer` is the pronoun for that back-referenced player (CR 603.2: "that player" refers to the player identified by the trigger event).

The produced-object noun ("land" here, "permanent" on Kinnan) names what was tapped for mana; it doesn't change the effect's shape — `AnyType` already generalizes to "mirrors whatever mana type the triggering tap event produced" regardless of the tapped object's card type, so both nouns are accepted by one pattern.

CR 106.4: "When an effect instructs a player to add mana, that mana goes into a player's mana pool."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatPlayerAddsManaOfAnyTypeProducedRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerDrawsAdditionalCardTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player draws an additional card" — a draw-step trigger effect that makes the player whose draw step is occurring draw one extra card. "That player" is the pronoun for the trigger's named player (CR 603.2: "at the beginning of" fires for the active player; "that player" back-references whoever owns that step). The "additional" qualifier is oracle flavour; mechanically this is identical to drawing one card (CR 121.1: "A player draws a card by putting the top card of their library into their hand.").

Anchored (^…$) to prevent substring matches inside longer clauses. Distinct from `DrawCardsTriggeredRule` (which handles "draw a card" directed at the controller "you", not "that player") and `EachPlayerDrawsTriggeredRule` (which handles "each player draws a card").

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatPlayerDrawsAdditionalCardTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerLifeTotalBecomesRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player's life total becomes [N]" — sets the triggering player's life total to a fixed value.

Rule 119.5: "If an effect sets a player's life total to a specific number, the player gains or loses the necessary amount of life to end up with the new total." "That player" refers to the player identified by the trigger condition (CR 603.2); it maps to `ThatPlayer`.

Canonical use: Master of Cruelties — "Whenever this creature attacks a player and isn't blocked, that player's life total becomes 1." The effect reduces (or in unusual situations raises) the attacked player's life total to exactly 1.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatPlayerLifeTotalBecomesRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerLosesLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player loses N life" — symmetry-drain trigger on an opponent-controlled-ETB trigger (Suture Priest pattern). "That player" is the pronoun for the player whose action fired the trigger (Rule 109.5) and maps to `ThatPlayer`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatPlayerLosesLifeRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerLosesLifeThenSearchesLibraryForCardRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player loses N life, searches their library for a card, puts it into their hand, then shuffles" — Maralen of the Mornsong's each-player's-draw-step trigger. Three conjoined actions taken by "that player" (Rule 603.2 — "that player" resolves to the player identified by the trigger event, here the player about to have their draw step): a life loss (CR 119.3), a library search (CR 701.23a) that puts the found card into that player's hand, and the mandatory post-search shuffle.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatPlayerLosesLifeThenSearchesLibraryForCardRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerLosesLifeYouGainLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player loses N life and you gain N life" — symmetry-drain trigger keyed on a prior "an opponent casts …"/"a player casts …" trigger event, where "that player" is the pronoun for the player whose action fired the trigger (Yawgmoth's Edict pattern).

Distinct from `TargetPlayerLoseAndYouGainLifeRule` (which requires the explicit "target player" wording and maps to `Target`). Here the affected player is a back-reference to the triggering player, encoded as `ThatPlayer` (mirroring `ThatPlayerLosesLifeRule`), so no target is chosen. The trailing "and you gain N life" is what separates this from the bare `ThatPlayerLosesLifeRule` (whose pattern is end-anchored after "life" and therefore never matches this longer surface).

The two effects (lose life, gain life) are wrapped in a `CompositeEffect` because `ITriggeredRule` returns a single `Effect`; the composite preserves both as structured children rather than collapsing to free text.

Representative card: Yawgmoth's Edict — "Whenever an opponent casts a white spell, that player loses 1 life and you gain 1 life." Rule citations: CR 119.3 (an effect that causes a player to gain/lose life adjusts that player's life total), CR 603.2 (triggered ability event matching), CR 109.5 (pronoun back-reference to the player identified by the trigger).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatPlayerLosesLifeYouGainLifeRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerMayPayYouCreateTreasureRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Smothering Tithe pattern: "that player may pay {COST}. If the player doesn't, you create a Treasure token." (CR 603 — triggered on opponent draw; CR 117.7 — the paying player may pay; the IfYouDoNot branch creates for you).

Decomposes as:

`OptionalEffect` — the "may pay" wrapper. `ConditionalPayEffect` as `Inner` — the cost "that player" may pay. `Player` is `ThatPlayer` (the opponent who drew the card, per the trigger condition). `CreateTokenEffect` as `IfYouDoNot` — "you create a Treasure token" when the opponent declines to pay. Player is You (the ability controller), Count = 1, Token = `Treasure()`.

ANCHORED (`^…$`): the full effect clause is matched so that no sibling "that player may pay" text in a different pattern is mis-labelled. Priority 91: must run BEFORE the generic `ConditionalPayTriggeredRule` (priority 80) and after the Rings-of-Brighthearth rule (priority 90), since all three open with a conditional-pay surface but differ in consequent shape.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatPlayerMayPayYouCreateTreasureRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerMillsThatManyRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player mills that many cards" — the Mindcrank family: whenever an opponent loses life, that player mills that many cards.

The antecedent of "that many" is the life lost by the opponent in the triggering event (CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."). The amount is encoded as a `DerivedQuantity` keyed on `LifeLost`. "That player" is a back-reference to the player identified by the `LosesLife` trigger's filter (CR 603.2: the trigger fires whenever the event matches), encoded as `ThatPlayer`.

CR 701.17 defines "mill" as a keyword action: "To mill N cards, a player puts the top N cards of their library into their graveyard." The player mills cards equal to the amount of life lost in the triggering event.

This rule carries NO `[TriggeredRule]` attribute — it must NOT enter the reflection-discovered generic effect pool. The identical surface text "that player mills that many cards" appears on combat-damage triggers (Crosstown Courier, Captain Nghathrod) where "that many" is the damage dealt (`DamageDealt`), not life lost. Dispatching this rule for any trigger event would mislabel those cards. Instead, `TriggeredAbilityParser` dispatches to it directly only when the resolved trigger event is `LosesLife` — mirroring `YouGainThatMuchLifeLostRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatPlayerMillsThatManyRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerSacrificesUnlessPayTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player sacrifices [a|an|one|N] [type] [of their choice] unless they pay {COST}" — the taxing-edict triggered form (Spelltithe Enforcer: "Whenever an opponent casts a spell, that player sacrifices a permanent of their choice unless they pay {1}.").

Rule 701.21 (Sacrifice) — the affected player always chooses which permanent they sacrifice, so "of their choice" is mechanically inert and is matched-and-discarded (mirroring `EachPlayerSacrificesTriggeredRule`). Rule 118.1 — "A cost is an action or payment necessary to take another action or to stop another action from taking place"; the "unless they pay {COST}" clause is the payment the named player ("that player" / "they") may make to stop the sacrifice from happening.

Produces a `PreventableEffect` wrapping a `SacrificeEffect`. The sacrificing player rides on the `Target`'s `ThatPlayer` (the same Target-holds-the-player convention used by `EachPlayerSacrificesTriggeredRule`); the sacrificed-object type rides on that reference's `ObjectFilter`. The `UnlessClause` Player is also `ThatPlayer` ("they" refers back to that player). "a"/"an"/"one" yields no `Count` (singular is the default).

Distinct from `SacrificeUnlessPayTriggeredRule` ("sacrifice it unless you pay …", the controller's own bounce-land sacrifice) by the leading "that player" scope and the "they pay" payer.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatPlayerSacrificesUnlessPayTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ThatPlayerUntapsAControlledTypeTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"that player untaps a land they control" — the resolution half of an each-player time-trigger (paired with the trigger condition handled by `PhaseTriggerConditionRule`) that lets the triggering player untap one permanent of a given type from among the ones they themselves control. Canonical card: Hokori, Dust Drinker ("At the beginning of each player's upkeep, that player untaps a land they control.").

The chosen permanent is not targeted (no "target" keyword in the oracle text), so it is modelled as `Any` — the indefinite controller-choice reference — restricted to objects the triggering player controls via `ThatPlayer` (the player named by the trigger condition, CR 109.5), not the ability's own controller.

Rule 701.20 (Tap and Untap): "To untap a permanent, rotate it back to the upright position from a sideways position. Only tapped permanents can be untapped."

Generalizes over the card-type noun (land / creature / artifact / permanent) rather than a card-literal "a land" regex, so a sibling shape with a different subject type is covered by the same rule. ANCHORED (^…$) to prevent matching a substring of a more specific sibling clause.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThatPlayerUntapsAControlledTypeTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TheyGainKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"They gain [keyword] until end of turn." — grants a keyword ability, for the remainder of the turn, to a plural group of objects named earlier in the same ability (typically the tokens just created by a preceding sentence). Covers Ovika, Enigma Goliath's second sentence: "create X 1/1 red Phyrexian Goblin creature tokens, where X is the mana value of that spell. They gain haste until end of turn."

Plural sibling of `ItGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` (singular "it gains …"). "They" refers anaphorically (CR 113.8b) to the group of objects the previous sentence introduced; MAST records this the same way the singular case does — `It` is the generic anaphoric pronoun regardless of grammatical number (mirrors the "them" → `It` mapping already established for Valley Floodcaller's "Untap them.", and the "they" → `It` mapping on `PoisonCounterDifferenceEffectRule`).

Rule 603: triggered abilities resolve by executing their effects in order. Rule 611.1: continuous effects that grant keyword abilities have a duration; "until end of turn" is the most common one for triggered keyword grants.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TheyGainKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `TheyLoseLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"they lose N life" — triggered life-loss where "they" is the player who performed the triggering action (CR 119.3: if an effect causes a player to lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly; CR 603.2: the trigger fires whenever the event matches). "They" is a pronoun back-reference to the player identified by the trigger's filter (e.g. "an opponent draws a card, they lose N life") — that opponent is `ThatPlayer`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TheyLoseLifeRule.cs)

### `ThisCreatureDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"this creature deals N damage to any target" — self-ping triggered effect that targets any legal target (creature, player, planeswalker, or battle).

Covers cards like Orcish Bowmasters whose compound-trigger effect reads "this creature deals 1 damage to any target." — where the pronoun is "this creature" rather than "it" (the `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` pronoun). The source is the creature itself (CR 109); the target is any legal target (CR 115.4: "any target" — player, creature, planeswalker, or battle).

Rule 120.1–120.2: dealing damage (a source deals damage to a permanent or player). Rule 603.2: triggered abilities (When/Whenever/At).

Distinct from `SelfDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` (which matches the "it deals" pronoun form); both emit the same `DealDamageEffect` with `Self` as the source and `AnyTarget` as the target.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThisCreatureDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ThisCreatureDealsDamageToItTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"this artifact deals N damage to it" — the self-ping resolution of the "whenever a creature attacks/blocks/enters/etc." family whose trigger condition names the affected object with an INDEFINITE pronoun ("a creature") rather than a definite one ("that creature"). Covers Caltrops: "Whenever a creature attacks, this artifact deals 1 damage to it."

The source is the permanent itself (CR 109 — "this artifact" is a self-reference), modelled as `Self`. The target is "it" — the anaphoric pronoun (CR 113.8b) back-referring to the object named by this ability's own trigger event (the attacking creature), modelled as `It`. This mirrors the established "it" convention for trigger-named back-references (see `YouMayCreateTokenCopyOfItTriggeredRule`), and is distinct from `ThisCreatureDealsDamageToThatCreatureTriggeredRule`, whose trigger condition instead names the object definitely ("that creature") via `ThatCreature`.

Rule 120.1–120.2: dealing damage (a source deals damage to a permanent or player). Rule 603.2: triggered abilities (When/Whenever/At). The dealt damage is NONCOMBAT damage (CR 120): a triggered ability resolving and dealing damage is not itself combat damage assigned during the combat damage step (CR 510), so `IsCombat` is left null (≡ noncombat) and omitted from the JSON — mirrors the sibling rule's IsCombat reasoning.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThisCreatureDealsDamageToItTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ThisCreatureDealsDamageToThatCreatureTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"this creature deals N damage to that creature" — the self-ping resolution of the "blocks-or-becomes-blocked" combat-trigger family (Inferno Elemental, Skewer Slinger, Ornery Goblin, …). The source is the creature itself (CR 109 — "this creature" is a self-reference); the target is the creature named by the trigger condition (the blocking/blocked creature), encoded as `ThatCreature` — the creature analogue of "that player" (mirrors Flanking's "the blocking creature" target).

The dealt damage is NONCOMBAT damage (CR 120): this is a triggered ability resolving and dealing damage, not combat damage assigned during the combat damage step (CR 510). The trigger FIRES off combat (a block declaration), but the damage the ability deals is not itself combat damage, so `IsCombat` is left null (≡ noncombat) and omitted from the JSON. This distinction is load-bearing for the interaction layer: the emit must not feed a "deals <em>combat</em> damage" trigger (CR 510), but does feed a bare "deals damage" trigger (CR 120) — see the IsCombat doc-comment on `DealDamageEffect`.

Rule 120.1–120.2: dealing damage (a source deals damage to a permanent or player). Rule 603.2: triggered abilities (When/Whenever/At). Generalises over the type word ("creature"/"permanent"/…) on both the source pronoun and the "that [type]" target so the whole family is covered, not a single exemplar.

Distinct from `ThisCreatureDealsDamageToAnyTargetTriggeredRule` (target = `AnyTarget`): here the target is the trigger-named back-reference `ThatCreature`, not a freely-chosen "any target".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThisCreatureDealsDamageToThatCreatureTriggeredRule.cs)

### `ThisCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"this creature gains [keyword] until end of turn." — grants a keyword ability to the source permanent itself (self-reference, not a chosen target) for the remainder of the turn. Covers Kalastria Nightwatch: "Whenever you gain life, this creature gains flying until end of turn." Rule 603.1: triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect; this rule handles the effect clause. "This creature" is the source permanent naming itself, modelled as `Self` (CR 611.1: continuous effects generated by resolving a one-shot effect have a duration — here, "until end of turn"). Distinct from `TargetCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule`, which grants the keyword to a separately chosen target creature, and `ItGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule`, which grants it to the anaphoric "it" (the object named by the trigger's own filter, e.g. an entering creature) rather than the ability's source.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/ThisCreatureGainsKeywordUntilEndOfTurnRule.cs)

### `TransferCountersOnDeathTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"put its counters on target creature you control" — counter-transfer shape that moves all counters from the dying creature to a target controlled creature. The phrase "its counters" is an anaphoric reference to the triggering creature's current counter set (all types and amounts); MAST describes this as `CounterType = "all"` (the sentinel for "every counter type present on the source") with a `DerivedQuantity` source of "its", meaning the count is whatever is on the dying permanent rather than a fixed number (Rule 122.1 — counters are game objects; their quantity is a game state). Oracle text shape (after trigger/effect split): "put its counters on target creature you control" Example: "When Goobling dies, put its counters on target creature you control." (ONE) Priority 60: more specific than the generic `PutCountersTriggeredRule` (priority 50) which requires an explicit counter type ("a +1/+1 counter", "a charge counter", etc.) and would fall through on "its counters" anyway. The higher priority ensures this rule is tried first for the "its counters" surface without ambiguity.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TransferCountersOnDeathTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TransformTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Matches "transform this creature" / "transform this permanent" effect text. Classic Innistrad werewolves carry explicit transform triggered abilities, e.g.:

"At the beginning of each upkeep, if a player cast two or more spells last turn, transform this creature." (human-to-wolf) "At the beginning of each upkeep, if no spells were cast last turn, transform this creature." (wolf-to-human)

The "if [condition]" intervening-if clause is stripped by `TriggeredAbilityParser` before this rule receives the effect fragment. This rule handles the remaining "transform this creature" / "transform this permanent" text.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TransformTriggeredRule.cs)

### `TransformsIntoConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"As this creature transforms into [Name]" — transform-into trigger condition. CR 603.6: an ability that uses "as [permanent] transforms into [Name]" fires when the permanent transforms; it is functionally a "When" trigger with timing simultaneous to the transformation event.

Produces `Transforms` with Filter carrying the source type and `IsSelf = true` (the object being transformed is the source itself, CR 201.5 — "this [type]" in oracle text is a self-reference). Timing is always `When` (the "As" keyword maps to When by CR 603.6; the caller supplies the timing having already detected the "As" prefix via the raw-text intercept in `TriggeredAbilityParser`).

ANCHORED (`^…`): the guard checks for the exact "As this (creature|permanent) transforms into" prefix so the rule cannot misfire on a sibling trigger.

Priority 999: transform-into triggers are highly specific and must run before any generic `Transforms` rule that might match on "transforms" alone.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TransformsIntoConditionRule.cs)

### `TurnedFaceUpConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"When this creature is turned face up" — Rule 702.37 (Morph/Megamorph) face-up trigger. Fires when the face-down permanent's morph or megamorph cost is paid and the card becomes face up (Rule 702.37e/f). Subject is always "this creature".

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/TurnedFaceUpConditionRule.cs)

### `UntapAllLandsAdditionalCombatLandCreaturesOnlyRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"untap all lands you control. After this phase, there is an additional combat phase. Only land creatures can attack during that combat phase." — the Bumi, Unleashed combat-reset pattern.

Produces a `CompositeEffect` containing:

An `UntapEffect` targeting all lands the controller controls (CR 701.26: untap; CR 305: lands as permanents). An `AdditionalCombatPhaseEffect` with an `OnlyAttackers` filter restricting attackers in the inserted combat phase to land creatures (CR 508.1c: attacker restrictions).

This rule fires BEFORE the sentence-bundle splitter because the third sentence ("Only land creatures can attack during that combat phase") qualifies the <em>specific</em> additional combat phase inserted by the second sentence, making all three sentences a single semantic unit. If processed independently, the third sentence would fail to parse (no standalone rule covers a phase-scoped attacker restriction), causing the entire bundle to fall back to `UnparsedAbility`. Priority 95 places this rule above the generic sentence-bundle path (effectively inline) and above other pre-bundle special-cases.

CR references: CR 500.8 (adding phases to a turn); CR 508.1c (attacker restrictions); CR 701.26 (untap); CR 305 (lands).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/UntapAllLandsAdditionalCombatLandCreaturesOnlyRule.cs)

### `UntapAllTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"untap all [types] you control" — mass-untap triggered effect. Covers patterns such as:

"untap all lands you control" (Bear Umbra) "untap all creatures you control" "untap all permanents you control"

Produces an `UntapEffect` whose Target is `Each` filtered to the named card type with `You` when "you control" is present, or no controller filter otherwise (e.g. "untap all creatures"). Rule 701.26 (Tap and Untap).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/UntapAllTriggeredRule.cs)

### `UntapEachTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"untap each [type] you control" — mass-untap triggered effect using the "each" quantifier (Port Razer: "untap each creature you control").

Sibling of `UntapAllTriggeredRule`, which covers the "all" phrasing ("untap all lands you control", etc.). Kept as a separate, independently anchored rule rather than folding "each" into the shared "all" regex, so this addition cannot alter behaviour for any card already covered by `UntapAllTriggeredRule`'s gold fixtures.

Produces an `UntapEffect` whose Target is `Each` filtered to the named card type with `You` when "you control" is present, or no controller filter otherwise.

Rule 701.26 (Tap and Untap). Pattern anchored (^...$) so it only matches the standalone sentence — used by the sentence-bundle dispatcher to combine with a following sentence (e.g. "After this phase, there is an additional combat phase.", matched independently by `AdditionalCombatPhaseTriggeredRule`) into a flat effects list.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/UntapEachTriggeredRule.cs)

### `UntapSelfAndAllSubtypeTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"untap it and all [Subtype] you control" — the compound untap form that untaps the source permanent (referred to by "it") AND every permanent of a named subtype the controller controls.

Produces a `CompositeEffect` containing two `UntapEffect` instances:

`untap it` — self-reference (`Self`) `untap all [Subtype] you control` — `Each` with `Controller` = `You` and the named subtype on `Subtypes`.

CR 701.26b: "To untap a permanent, rotate it back to the upright position from a sideways position. Only tapped permanents can be untapped."

Priority 55 — above the generic `UntapSelfRule` (Priority 50) and above `UntapAllTriggeredRule` (Priority 50) so this compound form is matched first. The pattern is anchored (^...$) so it cannot silently consume a text that only partially matches (e.g. "untap it" alone).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/UntapSelfAndAllSubtypeTriggeredRule.cs)

### `UntapSelfRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"untap this artifact" / "untap it" with optional gate forms: - "you may pay {X}. If you do, untap this artifact." — Mana Vault style (CR 602) - "you may untap this [type]" — Grinding Station style (CR 117.7 "you may")

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/UntapSelfRule.cs)

### `UntapThemTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"Untap them." — a trailing sentence in a multi-sentence triggered ability resolution that untaps a group of permanents named in the preceding sentence.

The pronoun "them" is a plural anaphoric back-reference (CR 109.2 — game objects) to the set of permanents named by the prior effect clause in the same triggered ability. Because MAST is descriptive, not imperative (ADR-0003), and `TryParseSentenceBundleEffects` dispatches each sentence independently, this rule models the untap target using the `It` pronoun reference — the universal anaphoric stand-in for "the set just named" (the distinction between singular "it" and plural "them" is a linguistic surface form; the reference kind is the same structured back-reference slot).

Rule 701.20 (Tap and Untap): "To untap a permanent, rotate it back to the upright position from a sideways position. Only tapped permanents can be untapped." Rule 109.2 (Objects): an object is a card, token, spell, or ability; pronouns in oracle text refer to objects in the resolution context.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/UntapThemTriggeredRule.cs)

### `UntapUpToNLandsTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"untap up to N lands" — bounded non-targeted land-untap triggered effect.

CR 603.6a: "Enters-the-battlefield abilities trigger when a permanent enters the battlefield. These are written, 'When [this object] enters, …'" — the trigger condition is handled by `EntersConditionRule`; this rule handles only the effect clause.

Examples: "untap up to five lands" (Peregrine Drake). The count "up to N" is an `UpToQuantity` on the target reference — the player-chosen, non-targeted set of lands (no "target" keyword in oracle, so `Any` rather than `Target`). No controller restriction is stated in the text, so none is applied. Rule 701.26 (Tap and Untap).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/UntapUpToNLandsTriggeredRule.cs)

### `VentureIntoTheDungeonTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"venture into the dungeon" — the Venture into the Dungeon keyword action (CR 701.49) on the triggered side (e.g. Clattering Skeletons: "When this creature dies, venture into the dungeon.").

The dispatcher (`TriggeredAbilityParser`) has already split off the trigger condition, stripped the trailing reminder parenthetical (Rule 207.2), and trimmed the trailing period, so the effect fragment reaching this rule is the bare imperative "venture into the dungeon". Anchored to that exact phrase so it never matches the "venture into [quality]" variant (CR 701.49d) as a substring.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/VentureIntoTheDungeonTriggeredRule.cs)

### `WhenThisAuraLeavesSacrificeItDelayedRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Recognises the "When this Aura leaves the battlefield, that creature's controller sacrifices it." delayed-trigger sentence produced by the Animate Dead / Dance of the Dead family.

This sentence appears as the second sentence in the complex ETB ability's effect body, AFTER the composite lose-gain-return-attach sentence. It creates a `CreateDelayedTriggerEffect` whose `DelayedTriggeredAbility` fires when this Aura leaves the battlefield (CR 603.7 — a delayed triggered ability created by a resolving effect).

The sacrifice target is the enchanted creature ("it" — the anaphoric reference to the creature previously returned to the battlefield by the preceding effects). "That creature's controller sacrifices it" — the sacrificer is that creature's controller, not necessarily the Aura's controller. MAST records the sacrifice effect descriptively via `SacrificeEffect` with `It`; the "controller" subject is engine-derived from the triggered ability's implicit actor (CR 603.3 — a triggered ability's controller is the player who controlled the ability's source when it triggered, but here oracle specifies the enchanted creature's controller — the engine resolves this per CR 303.4e). Descriptive, not engine-executable.

CR 702.5a (Enchant); CR 303.4 (Aura); CR 603.7 (delayed triggered abilities); CR 701.21 (Sacrifice).

This rule is tightly anchored (^...$) and keyed on the conjunction of "this Aura leaves the battlefield" + "controller sacrifices it" so it cannot match as a substring of a broader trigger or effect. Priority 95 ensures it fires before the generic `SacrificeTriggeredRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/WhenThisAuraLeavesSacrificeItDelayedRule.cs)

### `WinTheGameTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you win the game." — a triggered ability's effect fragment stating that the controller wins outright (CR 104.2b: "An effect may state that a player wins the game."). Mirrors the spell-context precedent (`ApproachOfTheSecondSunRule`) but as a standalone `ITriggeredRule` so the bare sentence is recognised whenever it appears as the (possibly sole) effect of a triggered ability — e.g. Near-Death Experience: "At the beginning of your upkeep, if you have exactly 1 life, you win the game."

Parameterless beyond the winning player; mirrors `TakeInitiativeRule` doctrine (a fixed, parameter-free idiom recognised by anchored regex rather than decomposed further). Anchored (^…$) so it can never match as a substring of a longer, more specific sibling effect sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/WinTheGameTriggeredRule.cs)

### `YouCreateTokenConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you create a token" — token-creation trigger (CR 111.1; CR 603.2). Fires whenever the ability's controller creates one or more tokens. The filter carries Controller=You so that a "whenever any player creates a token" variant (if ever added) is distinguishable. The anchor is tight: ^you\s+create\s+a\s+token$ to avoid matching "you create a token for each…" compound forms (different shape) or occurrences embedded in a broader trigger body. CR 111.1: "Some effects put tokens onto the battlefield. A token is a marker used to represent any permanent that isn't represented by a card." CR 603.2: "Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability's trigger event, that ability automatically triggers."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouCreateTokenConditionRule.cs)

### `YouCycleThisCardConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"When you cycle this card" — the cycling trigger condition (CR 702.29c).

CR 702.29c (verbatim): "'When you cycle this card' means 'When you discard this card to pay an activation cost of a cycling ability.' These abilities trigger from whatever zone the card winds up in after it's cycled."

The trigger fires on `Cycled` with `IsSelf` = true, identifying that it is THIS card that is being cycled. Anchored check prevents matching broader discard or draw triggers.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouCycleThisCardConditionRule.cs)

### `YouDiscardCardConditionRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggerConditionRule

"Whenever you discard a card" — discard-card trigger (CR 701.9a: "To discard a card, move it from its owner's hand to that player's graveyard.").

Fires whenever the controller discards a card by any means — from cost payment, from a discard effect, from a forced discard, etc. (CR 603.2: the trigger fires on the event, regardless of cause). The controller defaults to You.

CR 603: "Triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect. They are written as '[When/Whenever/At] [trigger condition or event], [effect].'" CR 701.9a defines the discard action. Event = DiscardsCard, Filter.Controller = You.

Anchored check prevents matching "an opponent discards a card" or other subject-prefixed discard forms — those route to `EachOpponentDiscardsRule` or `TargetOpponentDiscardsTriggeredRule`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouDiscardCardConditionRule.cs)

### `YouDrawCardAndLoseLifeTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

Triggered-context effect body "you draw N card(s) and lose M life." — the controller draw-and-drain payoff on a triggered ability (Elegy Acolyte: "…you draw a card and lose 1 life."). ANCHORED (`^…$`) so it beats the unanchored `DrawCardsTriggeredRule` (which matches the bare "draw a card" substring and silently drops the "and lose 1 life" conjunct); this rule's higher priority makes it win the dispatch and emit BOTH effects.

Emits a `CompositeEffect` of the two sibling effects (`DrawCardsEffect` + `LoseLifeEffect`), both scoped to the controller ("you"), mirroring the spell-context `YouDrawCardsAndYouLoseLifeRule`.

CR 121.1 (draw a card); CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouDrawCardAndLoseLifeTriggeredRule.cs)

### `YouDrawThatManyCardsTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you draw that many cards" — draw effect where the count is derived from the triggering event (CR 120: damage dealing; "that many" is an anaphoric reference to the amount of damage dealt). Backed by `DamageDealt`.

Covers Niv-Mizzet, Visionary and similar cards whose trigger fires on damage dealt and whose effect draws cards equal to the damage amount.

CR 121.1: "A player draws a card by putting the top card of their library into their hand." The derived count records <i>how many</i> cards are drawn; the "that many" antecedent is the damage dealt in the triggering event (`DamageDealt`), resolved by the engine (ADR 0004 reference-not-resolution).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouDrawThatManyCardsTriggeredRule.cs)

### `YouGainLifeEqualToThatCreaturesToughnessTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you gain life equal to that creature's toughness" — the derived-lifegain resolution paired with the "destroy that creature" back-reference family (Engulfing Slagwurm). The gained amount is a `DerivedQuantity` keyed on `Toughness` whose `Source` is the anaphoric "that creature" — the object named by this ability's own trigger event (CR 603.2). Mirrors the derived-lifegain shape on Niambi, Esteemed Speaker ("gain life equal to that creature's mana value").

Anchored to the exact toughness surface (`^…$`) so it cannot claim the mana-value / power / literal siblings handled elsewhere. CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouGainLifeEqualToThatCreaturesToughnessTriggeredRule.cs)

### `YouGainLifePerSpellCastThisTurnRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you gain 1 life for each spell you've cast this turn" — triggered effect on Aetherflux Reservoir. The life amount equals the count of spells you have cast in the current turn (CR 601.2 — casting a spell puts it on the stack; the count includes the spell currently being cast when the trigger resolves). The `CountQuantity` carries an `ObjectFilter` with `CastThisTurnPredicate` to express the backward-looking "cast this turn" restriction.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouGainLifePerSpellCastThisTurnRule.cs)

### `YouGainLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you gain N life" — ETB lifegain trigger effect. Rule 701.20: "To gain life, a player adds the indicated amount to their life total."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouGainLifeRule.cs)

### `YouGainThatMuchLifeLostRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you gain that much life" where "that much" is the life a player just LOST — the gain-life half of a `LosesLife` trigger (Exquisite Blood, Bloodthirsty Conqueror).

CR 119.3: "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly." The antecedent of "that much" is the amount of life lost in the triggering event, so the gained amount is a `DerivedQuantity` keyed on `LifeLost`.
