The effect surface ("you gain that much life") is identical to the lifelink/ damage family handled by `YouGainThatMuchLifeRule`, which keys the derived amount on `DamageDealt`. The two differ ONLY by the triggering event — the antecedent of "that much" is the trigger's own event. This rule is therefore NOT reflection-discovered into the generic effect loop (it carries no `[TriggeredRule]`); the `TriggeredAbilityParser` dispatches to it directly only when the resolved trigger event is `LosesLife`, so the two "that much" surfaces never collide.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouGainThatMuchLifeLostRule.cs)

### `YouGainThatMuchLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you gain that much life" — lifelink-analog triggered effect where the amount is derived from the damage dealt by the source in the triggering event. Rule 120 (Damage): a source deals damage; the amount is "that much" referencing the damage dealt in the triggering event. Rule 701.20: "To gain life, a player adds the indicated amount to their life total." Distinct from `YouGainLifeRule` (literal N life) — this rule models a derived amount ("that much") backed by `DamageDealt`.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouGainThatMuchLifeRule.cs)

### `YouGetNamedCounterTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you get a[n]/N [type] counter(s)" — the controller receives a named counter (Kalemne, Disciple of Iroas: "Whenever you cast a creature spell with mana value 5 or greater, you get an experience counter."; the same "you get {E}" shape generalised beyond energy to any named counter, e.g. experience, CR 122.1).

CR 122.1: "A counter is a marker placed on an object or player that modifies its characteristics and/or interacts with a rule or effect." Counters can be placed on players (experience, energy, poison) as well as permanents. This is the "you" (the ability's controller) sibling of the existing "that player gets N [type] counters" shape already recognised by `PutCountersTriggeredRule` — that rule's guard requires "put"/"counter" in the text and its named-player branch is anchored to the literal "that player", so "you get a[n] [type] counter" is not covered there. Modelled identically via `putCounters` (`PutCountersEffect`) targeting `You`.

Priority 60 — above the default-priority (50) reflection-discovered pool so this anchored, more specific "you get" surface is tried before any broader fallback. Fully anchored (^…$) so it cannot substring-match inside a longer or differently-shaped effect sentence.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouGetNamedCounterTriggeredRule.cs)

### `YouLoseLifeIfYouControlFilterRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you lose N life if you [don't ]control a [filter]" — a resolution-time conditional life-loss effect (Takenuma Bleeder: "Whenever this creature attacks or blocks, you lose 1 life if you don't control a Demon."). The trigger half is handled upstream (AttacksOrBlocksConditionRule); this rule structures the effect interior, which otherwise falls through to an `UnstructuredEffect` shell (fidelity L1).

The "if" here does NOT immediately follow the trigger condition (it follows the effect verb "you lose 1 life"), so by CR 603.4 it is NOT an intervening-'if' clause — it "has only its normal English meaning": a within-resolution gate. It is therefore modelled as a `ConditionalEffect` inside the trigger's Effects list, NOT as the trigger's InterveningIf. The condition is a `CountCondition` composing `ObjectFilter` + `Comparison` (ADR 0007), exactly as Gravecrawler encodes "you control a Zombie" — negation ("don't control a") is the same count compared `LessThan` 1 (i.e. you control zero of them). The gated effect is a plain `LoseLifeEffect` (reference-not-resolution, ADR 0004: MAST records the printed if-then; the engine evaluates it).

CR 603.4 (verbatim, in part): "The word 'if' has only its normal English meaning anywhere else in the text of a card; this rule only applies to an 'if' that immediately follows a trigger condition." CR 119.3 (verbatim): "If an effect causes a player to gain life or lose life, that player's life total is adjusted accordingly."

Anchored (^…$) on the full effect fragment, so it cannot match a substring of a longer clause or shadow a sibling shape.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouLoseLifeIfYouControlFilterRule.cs)

### `YouLoseLifeRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you lose N life" — Deadpool's upkeep tax shape.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouLoseLifeRule.cs)

### `YouMayCreateTokenCopyOfItTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may create a token that's a copy of it" — the optional constellation-style token-copy effect found on cards such as Ondu Spiritdancer.

The pronoun "it" is a back-reference to the object named by the trigger condition — the entering enchantment. MAST models this as `It`, consistent with other "copy it" rules such as `CopyTriggeringSpellTriggeredRule`.

The "you may" prefix means the controller may choose not to copy. MAST wraps the `CopyEffect` in an `OptionalEffect` per ADR 0005 (clause-modifier composition). No `IfYouDo` is present (the copy is the sole consequence).

CR 707.1: "Some effects create a token that's a copy of another object." CR 111.2: "The player who creates a token is its owner." CR 603.2h: "A triggered ability may have an instruction followed by 'Do this only once each turn.'" — the restriction is peeled from the effect text by `TriggeredAbilityParser` before this rule is invoked; this rule handles only the single-sentence body.

ANCHORED (^…$): prevents matching inside a more-specific sibling whose text also contains "create a token that's a copy of it" as a substring. Priority 72 — above the generic `CreateCopyOnCombatDamageTriggeredRule` (70) and well above the vanilla token rule (50); specific enough to be tried before any broader "you may create" path.

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouMayCreateTokenCopyOfItTriggeredRule.cs)

### `YouMayExileItTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may exile it" — the optional variant of the CR 701.13a exile action on the triggered side, where the trigger's subject is the object exiled (Norin, Swift Survivalist: "Whenever a creature you control becomes blocked, you may exile it.").

The "you may" is a structured `OptionalEffect` (the codebase's convention, matching `OptionalMillTriggeredRule`) rather than a boolean flag: wrapper presence alone encodes the optionality. Exile is a one-shot action effect, so it composes directly under the wrapper with no further decomposition.

Anchored (^you may exile it$) so it never collides with `ExileSelfTriggeredRule`'s <c>^exile (it|this creature|this permanent)$</c> pattern (no "you may" prefix) — the two patterns are mutually exclusive by construction, so rule priority is irrelevant.

CR 701.13a (verbatim): "To exile an object, move it to the exile zone from wherever it is."

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouMayExileItTriggeredRule.cs)

### `YouMayExileThenCreateModifiedFoodGolemCopyRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may exile it. If you do, create a token that's a copy of that creature, except it's a [P]/[T] [Types…] in addition to its other types and it has \"[activated ability]\"" — Brenard, Ginger Sculptor's dies-trigger consequence.

The whole two-sentence body forms ONE structured `OptionalEffect` (CR 118.12 — "[A player] may [do something]. If [that player] [does], [effect]"): the `Inner` is the optional exile (CR 701.13a) of the triggering creature ("it" → `It`), and the "If you do" consequence (`IfYouDo`) is the copy-token creation. The copy references the dying creature by "that creature" (`ThatCreature` — the object the trigger's filter identified, exiled by the Inner effect).

The copy carries three "except"-clause `CopyModification`s applied in order (CR 707.2 — the copy acquires copiable values except as overridden):

`PowerToughnessOverride` fixes the token at [P]/[T] regardless of the original's stats. `TypeAdder` adds card types (lowercase, e.g. artifact/creature) and subtypes (Capitalised, e.g. Food/Golem) "in addition to its other types" (CR 205.1b — subtype/type addition preserves existing ones). `ActivatedAbilityAdder` adds the quoted activated ability "{2}, {T}, Sacrifice this token: You gain 3 life." as a fully-structured `ActivatedAbility` (CR 602.1 — "[Cost]: [Effect]"; the sacrifice targets the token itself, `IsSelf`).

This rule receives the ENTIRE effect body (both sentences) because the multi-sentence splitter in the dispatcher declines it (the "If you do, create…" second sentence has no standalone rule), falling through to the single-rule dispatch. ANCHORED (^…$) end to end on the exile-then-copy surface so it never claims a substring of any sibling body. Priority 80 — above the generic copy rules (70–76) and the bare "you may exile it" rule (which is anchored to that phrase alone and cannot match this longer body).

Rule citations: CR 118.12 ("you may … if you do"), CR 701.13a (exile), CR 707.2 (copy — copiable values), CR 205.1b (type/subtype addition), CR 602.1 (activated ability form), CR 111.1 (token), CR 119.3 (life gain).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouMayExileThenCreateModifiedFoodGolemCopyRule.cs)

### `YouMayPayReturnAndAttachEquipmentRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"you may pay {COST}. If you do, return that card to the battlefield and attach this Equipment to it." — the conditional-pay reanimation-and-attach pattern.

This is the canonical Nim Deathmantle (SOM) shape: a player may pay a mana cost; if they do, the triggering card (a nontoken creature that just died) is returned to the battlefield AND this Equipment is attached to it. The two consequent actions are a composite one-shot: return + attach are sequential but inseparable per the oracle sentence structure.

AST structure: <c>OptionalEffect { Inner: ConditionalPayEffect { Cost }, IfYouDo: CompositeEffect [ ReturnToBattlefieldEffect { Target: It }, AttachEffect { Target: It } ] }</c> The "that card" pronoun in "return that card to the battlefield" is the creature that triggered the ability — encoded as `It` (CR 113.8b: "it" in an ability refers to the object the trigger is about). "attach this Equipment to it" refers to the same returned creature, also encoded as `It`.

Priority 81 — higher than `ConditionalPayTriggeredRule` (priority 80) so this more-specific rule fires first and the generic handler does not attempt to dispatch the "return and attach" consequence through its limited if-you-do vocabulary.

CR 117.7 ("you may"); CR 701.3 (attach); CR 400.6 (enters under owner's control). CR 113.8b ("it" — the pronoun back-reference).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouMayPayReturnAndAttachEquipmentRule.cs)

### `YouMayPlayThatCardForAsLongAsExiledTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"You may play that card for as long as it remains exiled." — a one-shot permission to play a specific, previously-referenced card while it sits in exile, UNBOUNDED by any turn clock (Savvy Trader: "... exile target permanent card from your graveyard. You may play that card for as long as it remains exiled.").

Sibling of `YouMayPlayThatCardFromExileThisTurnTriggeredRule` (same `MayPlayTargetFromExileEffect`/`OptionalEffect` shape, same "that card" → `It` back-reference, ADR 0004), but the duration differs: "this turn" is a clock-bounded `UntilTimeDuration`, whereas "for as long as it remains exiled" is a zone-membership state (CR 611.2c) — an `AsLongAsDuration` wrapping an `ObjectInZoneCondition` (Reference = It, Zone = Exile). Anchored (^you may play that card for as long as it remains exiled$) so it cannot collide with the "this turn" sibling's distinct anchor.

CR 701.13a (exile) places the card in exile; this permission is what lets the controller play it from there, for as long as it stays there (CR 305.1 "play a land" / CR 601.2 "cast a spell" normally require the hand zone).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouMayPlayThatCardForAsLongAsExiledTriggeredRule.cs)

### `YouMayPlayThatCardFromExileThisTurnTriggeredRule` — *sealed class* : ITriggeredRule

"You may play that card from exile this turn." — a one-shot permission to play a specific, previously-referenced card while it sits in exile, bounded to the current turn (Norin, Swift Survivalist: "Whenever a creature you control becomes blocked, you may exile it. You may play that card from exile this turn.").

"That card" is a pronoun back-reference to the object a sibling effect in the same ability already exiled (typically "you may exile it" — see `YouMayExileItTriggeredRule`), so `Target` carries `It` rather than a filter (ADR 0004 "reference not resolution"). The "you may" is a structured `OptionalEffect` wrapper, matching the codebase's convention.

Anchored (^you may play that card from exile this turn$) so it is specific to this exact composite surface and does not collide with the unrelated filter-based `MayPlayFromExileEffect` static-permission shapes.

CR 701.13a (exile) places the card in exile; this permission is what lets the controller play it from there this turn (CR 305.1 "play a land" / CR 601.2 "cast a spell" normally require the hand zone).

[Source](Parsing/Parsers/Triggered/Rules/YouMayPlayThatCardFromExileThisTurnTriggeredRule.cs)

## `/Parsing/Tokens/`

### `OracleTokenizer` — *sealed class* : Tokenizer<OracleToken>

Tokenizer for Magic: The Gathering oracle text. Transforms character streams into token streams for parsing. Structural keywords are discovered via reflection at startup from classes decorated with `StructuralKeywordAttribute`. To add a new keyword, create a new file under `Parsing/Tokens/Keywords/`; no edits to this file are required.

[Source](Parsing/Tokens/OracleTokenizer.cs)

### `OracleToken` — *enum*

Token types recognized in Magic: The Gathering oracle text. These represent the lexical units that the tokenizer produces.

[Source](Parsing/Tokens/OracleToken.cs)

## `/Parsing/Tokens/Keywords/`

### `StructuralKeywordAttribute` — *sealed class* : Attribute

Marks a class as the registration site for a structural keyword recognized by `OracleTokenizer`. The class body is conventionally empty — the attribute is the entire registration. Each tagged class is discovered at runtime by `StructuralKeywordRegistry`.

[Source](Parsing/Tokens/Keywords/StructuralKeywordAttribute.cs)

### `StructuralKeywordRegistry` — *static class*

Discovers all `StructuralKeywordAttribute`-tagged types in the MagicAST assembly and exposes a case-insensitive text -> token lookup. Discovery runs once on first access and is cached for the process lifetime. Adding a new structural keyword means creating a new file decorated with `StructuralKeywordAttribute` — no edits to this registry or to `OracleTokenizer` are required.

[Source](Parsing/Tokens/Keywords/StructuralKeywordRegistry.cs)

## `/Serialization/`

### `PolymorphicTypeAttribute` — *abstract class* : Attribute

Abstract base for attributes that register a derived concrete type into a polymorphic AST hierarchy. Each polymorphic base has its own concrete subclass (e.g., `OracleAbilityAttribute`, `OracleEffectAttribute`) so that the attribute name signals which hierarchy the type belongs to. Discovered at startup by `PolymorphicReflectionConverter{TBase}`.

[Source](Serialization/PolymorphicTypeAttribute.cs)

### `PolymorphicBaseAttribute` — *sealed class* : Attribute

Marks an abstract record/class as the root of a polymorphic AST hierarchy serialized via `PolymorphicReflectionConverter{TBase}`. The named discriminator property is injected by the converter on write and consumed (then stripped) by the converter on read. The discriminator value itself is supplied per-derived-type by a `PolymorphicTypeAttribute` (or one of its subclasses such as `OracleAbilityAttribute`).

[Source](Serialization/PolymorphicBaseAttribute.cs)

### `PolymorphicConverterFactory` — *sealed class* : JsonConverterFactory

A `JsonConverterFactory` that produces a `PolymorphicReflectionConverter{TBase}` for any type marked with `PolymorphicBaseAttribute`. The set of recognised base types is discovered at startup by scanning the MagicAST assembly. Adding a new polymorphic hierarchy means:

Decorate the abstract base with `PolymorphicBaseAttribute`. Author a per-base `PolymorphicTypeAttribute` subclass (e.g., `OracleAbilityAttribute`). Decorate concrete derived types with that attribute.

No edits to this factory, to `MagicASTJsonOptions`, or to any existing base class are required.

[Source](Serialization/PolymorphicConverterFactory.cs)
